planEntities.description: Strengthening of the Barbados National Ozone Office and technical staff (Ministry of Environment, National Beautification, Blue and Green Economy) to develop and implement its long term management plans.

planEntities.name: Antigua and Barbuda Sustainable Low-Emission Island Mobility Project
planEntities.parentName: MSDCF 6.1: Environmental management institutions strengthened for sustainable natural resource management
planEntities.description: The Project, "Supporting Antigua and Barbuda's Sustainable Low-Emission Island Mobility and transition" (GEF-7 #10281) addresses priorities to transition Antigua and Barbuda's transportation and energy sectors towards a low-carbon trajectory. Total allocation is $3,245,000. As a small island developing state (SIDS), Antigua and Barbuda’s greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions represent just 0.0015% of the world’s total. However, the country’s per capita GHG emissions are higher than those of Spain and France. Antigua and Barbuda’s biggest challenge is the energy sector, which, due to fossil fuel combustion activities, accounts for 76% of the country’s total emissions. These two sectors rely almost entirely on imported petroleum-based fuels. Electricity generation is responsible for close to 40% of total GHG emissions generated from heavy fuel oil thermal power plants and experiences high distribution grid inefficiencies. As a result, the emission intensity per MWh of the electricity consumed is around 1000 kg of CO2 per MWh generated, almost double the global average. The transport sub-sector is similarly problematic, with road transport accounting for more than 20% of total national GHG emissions. Under business as usual (BAU) conditions overall emissions are expected to rise considerably over the next decade, primarily due to increases in electricity demand and growth in individual transport usage. BAU estimations indicate that the private vehicle fleet could grow at an annual rate of 6.5% per year.  Project activities will put in motion the transformation of both the power and transport sectors of Antigua and Barbuda, transitioning these from the current scenario of fossil fuel dependence to a future where low-carbon and climate resilient technologies are predominant. The Project will strengthen and inform political and public support for the uptake of low-carbon and climate-resilient electric transport and power generation systems. Activities include: reducing technological, financial and modal barriers through technical assistance and investment in pilot projects; building local capacity in related areas; and implementing regulations, policies and standards to secure a sustainable transition into the future and avoid potential environmental contamination. The Project has been extended to 30 April 2027

planEntities.name: Improving Environmental Management through Sustainable Land Management in St. Kitts and Nevis
planEntities.parentName: MSDCF 6.1: Environmental management institutions strengthened for sustainable natural resource management
planEntities.description: Improving Environmental Management through Sustainable Land Management practices in St. Kitts and Nevis (GEF-6 #9785). The objective is to transform degraded forest landscapes into biodiversity and climate-friendly areas of sustainable agricultural/agro-forestry production that together can provide economic opportunities for the country’s population while also sustaining ecosystem services and globally significant biodiversity. There are 3 components: 1) Integrated and strengthened environmental planning and management to support island sustainability; 2) Mainstreaming of biodiversity conservation, sustainable land management and climate change mitigation into key development and resources management sectors; 3) Knowledge management and dissemination for Sustainable Land Management, Biodiversity, and Climate Change.  The Project has been extended to June 30, 2027.

planEntities.name: BAH Meeting the Challenge of 2020 in The Bahamas
planEntities.parentName: MSDCF 6.1: Environmental management institutions strengthened for sustainable natural resource management
planEntities.description: National project GEF-6 (#9791) to manage and strengthen Marine Protected Areas in The Bahamas and integrate into broader landscape planning in order to reduce pressures on ecosystem services and biodiversity from competing resource uses. The Project is executed across 5 project sites which includes the MPAs: Andros West Side National Park (AWSNP), Exuma Cays Land and Sea Park (ECLSP), Moriah Harbor Cay National Park (MHCNP), Bonefish Pond National Park (BPNP), & Lucayan National Park (LNP).  Targeted activities include: ecosystem zoning plans; provision of infrastructure, staffing and equipment for all 5 MPAs; species conservation and monitoring plans developed and implemented for AWSNP, ECLSP, LNP, and MHCNP; pilot renewable energy installations and energy efficiency measures at BPNP, ECLSP and LNP; and engagement of farmers in agricultural areas bordering the MPAs. The Project commenced in 2020, was disrupted by COVID-19 and received extensions, with implications for rescheduling of activities and related expenditures in ensuing years. Project was scheduled for closure by May 2026, but has been granted an extension to 30 November 2028.

planEntities.name: Strengthening Resilience of Agricultural Lands and Forests in Dominica
planEntities.parentName: MSDCF 6.1: Environmental management institutions strengthened for sustainable natural resource management
planEntities.description: Strengthening Resilience of Agricultural Lands and Forests in Dominica in the Aftermath of Hurricane Maria (GEF-6 #9978) builds capacity to restore, rehabilitate and sustainably manage forest lands in the vicinity of the Morne Trois Piton National Park. It commenced in 2020 but was disrupted by the COVID-19 Pandemic. It comprises 3 Components: 1) Restoration and rehabilitation of denuded forest areas around Morne Trois Pitons National Park - to reforest and implement supporting measures and initiatives that promote restoration of ecosystem services and reduce land degradation; 2) Promotion of sustainable agriculture in areas around Morne Trois Pitons - promoting behavior change and adoption of sustainable agricultural practices by land users near the National Park; 3) Institutional strengthening, education and training to address land degradation - developing new policies and regulations to address land management practices identified in the wake of Hurricane Maria as contributing to the severity of negative impacts on ecological functioning, livelihoods, and human health and security. The Project has received extensions from delays related to COVID-19 impacts and other implementation challenges and has applied for a further extension. Project expenditures between 2020-2021 = $128,976.

planEntities.name: REG GEF LAC Cities: Reduce marine plastics and plastic pollution in Latin American and Caribbean cities through a circular economy approach
planEntities.parentName: MSDCF 6.2: National capacities strengthened to improve waste management and transition to a greener circular economy
planEntities.description: The GEF LAC Cities project aims to reduce marine plastics and plastic pollution through a circular economy approach and to support city governments and businesses to accelerate the transition to a circular economy. There are xix (6) cities targeted in Jamaica (Kingston, Montego Bay), Colombia (Cartagena & Barranquilla) and Panama (Panama City & Colon) (GEF-7 #10547). The PCAs for specific cities interventions are still under negotiation.

planEntities.name: BAH Integrated Landscape Management for land degradation, food security and climate resilience in the Bahamas
planEntities.parentName: MSDCF 6.1: Environmental management institutions strengthened for sustainable natural resource management
planEntities.description: Integrated Landscape Management for Addressing Land Degradation, Food Security and Climate Resilience Challenges in The Bahamas (GEF-7 #10694). A national, technical assistance project to enhance climate resilient food production across productive agricultural landscapes through sound Integrated Landscape Management and Land Degradation Neutrality approaches in The Bahamas.  The project considers long-term solutions to address problems of land degradation and increase implementation of sustainable land management (SLM) practices through an integrated landscape management planning approach, with restorative measures that reduce the drivers of land degradation and mitigation of loss of productivity within agricultural and natural ecosystems, while enhancing resilience to climate change. The Project has been extended to 30 September 2027 to facilitate completion of activities. Total Budget is $5,717,580. The Project has applied for an extension.

planEntities.name: Support the Shift to Electric Mobility in Saint Lucia
planEntities.parentName: MSDCF 6.1: Environmental management institutions strengthened for sustainable natural resource management
planEntities.description: This SLU National Child Project (GEF-7 #10283) is funded under a Global Support Programme implemented by UNEP to accelerate the introduction of electric mobility in countries. The SLU national Project will accelerate the introduction of electric mobility through capacity-building and electric vehicle demonstration and prepare for scaling-up and replication through the development of electric mobility policies, business models and finance schemes. The total allocation for the St. Lucia national Project is $785,688. The national Project is implemented within 4 Components: 1) Institutionalization of low-carbon electric mobility; 2) Short term barrier removal through low-carbon e-mobility demonstrations; 3) Preparing for scale-up and replication of low-carbon electric mobility; and 4) Long-term environmental sustainability of low-carbon electric mobility.  The Project has suffered COVID-19 related delays and received a 1st approval of extension to 2027-01-31. A total budge of $755,688 is available for the Saint Lucia national project.

planEntities.name: REG CReW+ Promoting integrated water and wastewater management approaches pipeline
planEntities.parentName: MSDCF 6.2: National capacities strengthened to improve waste management and transition to a greener circular economy
planEntities.description: CReW+  is a regional partnership project co-implemented by UNEP and the IDB in 18 countries. It features an integrated approach to water and wastewater management using innovative solutions and promoting financing mechanisms in the Wider Caribbean Region (GEF-6 #9601). The Project is implementing innovative technical small-scale solutions using an integrated water and wastewater management approach and building on sustainable financing mechanisms piloted through the Caribbean Regional Fund for Wastewater Management (CReW). The Project covers watershed and freshwater basin protection, water conservation and efficiency, and water reuse, and prioritizes technologies for treating wastewater in rural and peri-urban areas that are replicable and sustainable. Saint Lucia's allocation in the Project Cooperation Agreement is $260,000.

planEntities.name: REG Prevention of Marine Litter in the Caribbean Sea, PROMAR
planEntities.parentName: MSDCF 6.2: National capacities strengthened to improve waste management and transition to a greener circular economy
planEntities.description: Prevention of Marine Litter in the Caribbean Sea (PROMAR) is a regional project across 5 Caribbean countries which aims to reduce waste streams, i.e. plastic packaging, and single-use plastics, from entering the Caribbean Sea while promoting circular economy solutions and shared learnings, tools and practices in Guyana, St. Kitts & Nevis, Suriname, Trinidad & Tobago and British Virgin Islands. The PROMAR project comprises 4 work packages: 1) mapping waste streams & monitoring systems; 2) piloting circular economy solutions at sites; 3) implementing policy instruments and facilitating (trans)national policy dialogues; 4) raising awareness of stakeholders mapping waste streams, policy dialogues, systems analysis and stakeholder engagement. Regional implementation is through UNEP Cartagena Convention Secretariat in collaboration with Adelphi gmbh (Germany). A no-cost extension was granted to the Project to 30 June 2027.

planEntities.name: REG Advancing Conservation in the Eastern Caribbean
planEntities.parentName: MSDCF 6.1: Environmental management institutions strengthened for sustainable natural resource management
planEntities.description: Regional Project "Advancing Conservation in the Eastern Caribbean" (GEF-6 #9979): supports biodiversity conservation in 4 Organization of Eastern States (OECS) countries through enhanced political will and capacity building for improved management of marine protected areas (MPAs), marine management areas (MMAs) and protected areas (PAs). Activities will also support development of a Regional Conservation Caucus in the OECS. Implemented by UNEP Cartagena Convention Secretariat, with executing agency: Conservation Council of Nations (CCN). Project expenditures between 2019-2021 = $583,723. Project has been extended again to 31/10/2025 to achieve closure. *Note that there are no specific national allocations and expenditures per country are averaged. A No-Cost Extension was granted to 19 November 2024; the Project has been further extended to 30 June 2026.

planEntities.name: REG GEF ISLANDS Child Project 3: Preventing Build up of materials and chemicals in the environment
planEntities.parentName: MSDCF 6.2: National capacities strengthened to improve waste management and transition to a greener circular economy
planEntities.description: Caribbean SIDS have benefited since 2015 from GEF supported interventions to phase out harmful persistent organic pollutants (POPs) under the Basel/Rotterdam/Stockholm Conventions (with FAO and UNEP as implementing partners). The current, regional ISLANDS Caribbean Child Project 3 (GEF-7 #10279) implemented by UNEP is supporting the prevention of a build-up of chemicals and materials in the environment that contain POPs, mercury and other harmful chemicals, to manage and dispose safely. The regional Project covers 9 Caribbean SIDS (ANT & BAR, BAR, BZE, GUY, SKN, SLU, SUR, TTO and the Dominican Republic). The Project partners involve ministries with responsibility for pesticides and chemicals with implementation coordinated by the Basel Convention Regional Centre for Training and Technology Transfer for the Caribbean (BCRC Caribbean) based in Trinidad & Tobago. The Project will be extended to 2028.

planEntities.name: JAM Extension of Institutional Strengthening Project Phase XI (OzonAction)
planEntities.parentName: MSDCF 6.2: National capacities strengthened to improve waste management and transition to a greener circular economy
planEntities.description: OzonAction: Extension of Institutional Strengthening Project Phase XI: Activities will be implemented under the 4th Tranche of the HPMP I: a) Conduct training of RAC technicians on HCFC alternatives; b) Increase awareness of technicians and importers on new technologies and implications of their use; c) Develop and implement a public awareness and education programme to increase awareness related to the HCFC phase-out and the transition to alternative refrigerants that are low GWP and zero ODP; d) Develop and implement project monitoring, evaluation and reporting to ensure the efficient and effective implementation of the HPMP Stage I (HPMP I). Project extended to 31-07-2025.

planEntities.name: Reducing threats from Invasive Alien Species in St. Phillip, Barbados
planEntities.parentName: MSDCF 6.1: Environmental management institutions strengthened for sustainable natural resource management
planEntities.description: Besides landscape and habitat modification, invasive alien species (IAS) are among the biggest threats to biodiversity in Barbados. The Project will reduce threats from habitat loss and Invasive Alien Species (IAS) through enhanced biodiversity governance and strengthened bio-security in Barbados (GEF-7 #10942). Project targets the communities of Ragged Point, St. Phillip Parish. The Project considers key long-term solutions to address the risk of loss of a globally threatened species that occurs only in Barbados from the wider drivers of terrestrial biodiversity loss, emphasizing  IAS and addressing landscape development (and habitat conversion) that does not adequately take into account, the protection of threatened biodiversity.

planEntities.name: Enhancing/Strengthening Land Management, Ecosystem Resilience, and Climate Resilient Food Systems in Carriacou, Grenada
planEntities.parentName: MSDCF 6.1: Environmental management institutions strengthened for sustainable natural resource management
planEntities.description: Enhancing Land Management and Strengthening Ecosystem Resilience for Integrated Landscape Restoration and Climate-Resilient Food Systems in Carriacou, Grenada (GEF-7 # 10980) - addressing land degradation in Carriacou, through demonstration and application of ecosystems-based landscape restoration, sustainable land management and good agricultural practices, using community participatory approaches that expands diversification and sustainability of livelihoods options.  Component 1: Community-Based Landscape Rehabilitation and Protection using EbA approaches - Component 2: Strengthening landscape governance for application of SLM and EbA tools. The Project is extended to 31 August 2027.

planEntities.name: OzonAction in Belize - Hydrofluororcarbons, HCFC, Phase-out (Stage II First Tranche)
planEntities.parentName: MSDCF 6.2: National capacities strengthened to improve waste management and transition to a greener circular economy
planEntities.description: OzonAction to phase out Hydrofluororcarbons, HCFC Stage II, First Tranche: to build the capacity for the National Ozone Unit in Belize to operate and implement the management phase-out plans. Project is scheduled to end June 2027.

planEntities.name: REG EU Zero Waste: Support to the effective and sustainable management of Solid Waste in the Caribbean
planEntities.parentName: MSDCF 6.2: National capacities strengthened to improve waste management and transition to a greener circular economy
planEntities.description: The project started in 2022 under the 11th EU Development Fund and supports 16 Caribbean countries and SIDS (including Cuba, Haiti and Dominican Republic). Through UNEP, the capacity for data-driven decision-making and enhanced accessibility of critical insights for stakeholders have strengthened. This alignment ensures consistency in reporting, promotes harmonising methodologies, and fosters a comprehensive understanding of progress toward sustainable waste management and circular economy goals. (Project extension has now been granted until 30 June 2026. Kindly note that Haiti, Cuba and Dominica Republic are included in the Project)

planEntities.name: BAH Pine Islands: Forest/Mangrove Innovation and Integration (Grand Bahama, New Providence, Abaco and Andros)
planEntities.parentName: MSDCF 6.1: Environmental management institutions strengthened for sustainable natural resource management
planEntities.description:
The Project was commenced in 2015 and the Inception Workshop convened in 2016. It has been much delayed, and disrupted by the COVID-19 pandemic. The total project budget = $1,584,919; total expenditures between 2016-2021 = $1,268,505.
The Project aims to build on recent advancements in the forestry sector by integrating biodiversity values, ecosystem services values and precepts of sustainable forest management and land-use into enhanced land-use planning in The Bahamas. The project addresses a number of environmental priorities through its three components: 1) : The institutional systemic support & associated capacity building; 2) The expansion and improved management of forest and mangrove sector; 3) Sustainable Livelihoods:  Developing the concept of multi-functional conservation by enabling coastal communities thru effective provisioning of forest ecosystem services while promoting sustainable practices and community management. The Project has been extended to 31 March 2026.

planEntities.name: The Path to 2020 - Antigua & Barbuda
planEntities.parentName: MSDCF 6.1: Environmental management institutions strengthened for sustainable natural resource management
planEntities.description: The 2019 GEF-6 (#9402) Project promotes protection and sustainable use of biodiversity and protected areas, under the umbrella of the Environmental Protection and Management Act (EPMA) of 2019. Executing Agency is the Department of the Environment, Ministry of Health, Wellness and the Environment. Main government & other partners include the Ministry of Agriculture, the Caribbean Agricultural Research & Development Institute (CARDI) & the Inter-American Institute for Cooperation on Agriculture (IICA). Project has 3 Components: 1) Strengthening regulations, institutions and financing mechanisms for the national Protected Areas System; 2) Expansion of protected areas in support of species conservation; 3) Pilot livelihood financing mechanisms that support conservation and sustainable use of biodiversity and plant genetic resources in the newly designated Shekerley Mountain Management Area (SMMA). The project was extended to 31 December 2026.

planEntities.name: St. Lucia Southeast Coast Project - Integrated Ecosytem Management and Restoration of Forests
planEntities.parentName: MSDCF 6.1: Environmental management institutions strengthened for sustainable natural resource management
planEntities.description: The GEF-6 (#9406) Project The project enables sustainable economic development of the South East Coast by maintaining healthy ecosystems, sustainable livelihoods and securing global environmental benefits (GEBs). The Project promotes a more cohesive, ecosystem-based approach to development, including interrelated development planning and restoration of ecosystem services, and the establishment of sustainable management and natural resource use best practices. The objectives are change patterns of degradation on SLU's Southeast Coast, reduce impoverishment of local populations and loss of global environmental goods. The Project 3 Components: 1) Ecosystem Management - establishing effective ecosystems management mechanisms; 2) Rehabilitated Landscapes - supported through improved mechanisms for land use planning and collaborative investment decision-making; 3) Sustainable Livelihoods - identifying economic opportunities, incentives and livelihoods for primary natural resources users. Key national IP is the Department of Sustainable Development. The Project has been extended to 31 March 2027 with a total budget of $4,428,145.

planEntities.name: SLU: Strengthening access and benefit-sharing (ABS) policies and institutional frameworks through demonstrable models in Saint Lucia
planEntities.parentName: MSDCF 6.1: Environmental management institutions strengthened for sustainable natural resource management
planEntities.description: The Project (GEF-7, #10840) will enhance the enabling environment in St. Lucia to effectively implement the provisions of the Nagoya Protocol with a harmonized institutional and inter-sectoral approach as well as demonstrate replicable models for equitable and sustainable access and benefit sharing (ABS). The Project has 4 Components: 1) Strengthen national policy and legislative institutional framework for operationalization of the Nagoya Protocol for ABS; 2) Develop an effective permitting and monitoring framework for ABS protocols in accordance with provisions of the Nagoya Protocol; 3) Establish demonstrable commodity pilots to test operationalization of ABS protocol; 4) Enhance knowledge management on ABS to support decision-making, stakeholder engagement and buy-in. The Project is scheduled for completion June 2027.

The GEF-8 #11500 Enabling Activity Global Project is assisting 8 countries including Dominica, Grenada and St. Vincent & the Grenadines in the Caribbean to fulfill essential communication requirements to the Convention and the Paris Agreement and is in conformity with Objective 2.2 of Pillar II under GEF-8 Climate Change Focal Area Strategy, that fosters enabling conditions to mainstream mitigation concerns into sustainable development strategies. The project falls under BTR1 top-up Modality 3, as described in the Information Note on the Update to the Financing of Biennial Transparency Reports for the Developing Country Parties to the Paris Agreement (GEF/C.62/Inf.15). This modality supports countries to access additional (top up) financing to ongoing enabling activity (EA) projects and is only intended to be used for their first BTRs. This option allows country teams that would have been delayed in commencing the BTR work, considering the status of NC/BUR processes, to draft and complete their NCs, BURs and BTRs concurrently.  The Project is scheduled to end 30 April 2028.

The following BTR financing arrangements and projects have been identified for the top-ups as informed by varying technical capacities and country preferences:
i) Dominica BTR1 merged with the Initial Biennial Update Report i.e. BUR1 – GEF ID. 6925
ii) Grenada BTR1 merged with the Third National Communication i.e., NC3 – GEF ID. 4794, which will result in a combined BTR1/NC3 project.
iii) Saint Vincent & the Grenadines BTR1 merged with the Third National Communication i.e., NC3 – GEF ID. 4794, which will result in a combined BTR1/NC3 project.

planEntities.name: Achieving a rapid decarbonization of the energy sector in Saint Kitts and Nevis
planEntities.parentName: MSDCF 6.1: Environmental management institutions strengthened for sustainable natural resource management
planEntities.description:
The GEF-7 (#10856) Project supports the country in accelerating decarbonization by transitioning towards a highly ambitious target of 100% renewable energy generation. To achieve this, the Government of St. Kitts and Nevis intends to harness renewable energy sources, namely geothermal, solar, wind and waste. It also aims to reduce consumption through achieving 100% high energy e\0fficiency in public buildings. The electrical grid accounts for approximately 65% of the country’s emissions and is therefore the target with the highest potential – especially considering that a decarbonized electricity grid is also a pre-condition for the
future decarbonization of the transport sector. Although Saint Kitts & Nevis' overall emissions are minute (203,036 tCO in 2016), its per capita emissions are relatively large. Electricity generation is responsible for close to 65% of total GHG emissions, as the country relies almost entirely on diesel generators.

A key challenge is to build a comprehensive enabling environment, that can support St. Kitts and Nevis to manage and achieve a transition to decarbonization in a controlled and economically, socially and environmentally viable manner. The GEF incremental logic is that through its \0investment, St. Kitts and Nevis will be able to build upon existing investment to address barriers to decarbonization and achieve its ambitious climate targets. The Project budget is $3,318,995 and is scheduled for completion by 31 December 2027.

planEntities.name: REG Advancing a Regional Approach Towards the Green Hydrogen Economy in Latin America and the Caribbean
planEntities.parentName: MSDCF 6.2: National capacities strengthened to improve waste management and transition to a greener circular economy
planEntities.description:
The Project aims to create an enabling environment to foster the development of a regional green hydrogen economy and to build the capacity of participating countries to attract investment, develop policies, and implement strategic projects. Jamaica and Trinidad & Tobago are among seven countries in the Latin America & Caribbean region (including Bolivia, Chile, El Salvador, Honduras and Uruguay) participating in the regional initiative funded by the Green Climate Fund (GCF) and implemented by UNEP. The use of green hydrogen as an energy vector to support countries' decarbonization pathways is a genuinely new vision that was endorsed by many countries at the UNFCCC COP26 meeting.  Total regional Project budget is US$2,049,971.

As a Group A (early stage) country (including El Salvador & Honduras), the Government of Jamaica is advancing the development of a national green hydrogen economy as part of its broader transition toward a low-carbon, resilient, and diversified energy system. Green hydrogen presents a strategic opportunity to reduce dependence on imported fossil fuels, decarbonize hard-to-abate sectors, strengthen energy security, and unlock new areas of industrial development and investment. To support this emerging sector in a coordinated and inclusive manner, the establishment of a National Green Hydrogen Inter-Institutional Working Group is proposed, to serve as a national advisory and coordination mechanism, bringing together key public and private stakeholders to support policy coherence, strategic planning, and informed decision-making related to green hydrogen development in the country. The national partners are the Ministry of Economic Growth and Job Creation (MEGJC), now Ministry of Economic Growth and Infrastructure Development (MEGID); Ministry of Energy, Transport & Telecommunications (METT) and the Ministry of Water, Environment & Climate Change (MWECC).

As a Group B (more advanced) country (including Chile, Bolivia, Uruguay), Trinidad & Tobago is a regional energy leader with a strong foothold in petrochemicals and strategically positioned to spearhead the development of a green hydrogen economy in the LAC region. Leveraging its existing oil and gas infrastructure, operational expertise, and favorable economic conditions, the nation can potentially transform into a green energy superpower. Trinidad & Tobago's competitive advantage includes: its energy sector contribution of 40% of GDP and 80% of export earnings; its strong heritage in oil and gas production and petrochemical exports (ammonia and methanol); its established infrastructure which offers a competitive edge in the emerging hydrogen market; the strategic positioning of the Point Lisas Industrial Estate, poised to be a regional hub for green hydrogen and downstream products; and its thriving energy ecosystem and existing markets with trade relations and export routes. Trinidad & Tobago's lead in existing infrastructure also provides a head start in the green hydrogen market. The national partner is the Ministry of Planning & Development (MPD), now the Ministry of Planning, Economic Affairs & Development (MPEAD).

planEntities.name: Elimination of hazardous chemicals from supply chains Integrated Programme in Trinidad and Tobago
planEntities.parentName: MSDCF 6.2: National capacities strengthened to improve waste management and transition to a greener circular economy
planEntities.description:
The GEF-8 #11176 Project titled, “Elimination of Hazardous Chemicals from Supply Chains Integrated Programme in Trinidad and Tobago” child project is one of the eight child projects of the GEF 8 Integrated Programme (IP) 11 “Eliminating hazardous chemicals from supply chains”. The objective of the IP is to promote transformational change in the fashion and construction sectors by replacing resource-intensive processes and materials with sustainable approaches and alternatives and creating and strengthening circular and transparent supply chains.

The Project is implemented by UNEP and aims to transform the Carnival fashion sector by promoting the use of sustainable, locally sourced materials and eliminating hazardous chemicals from costume production. It addresses environmental and health risks posed by materials such as plastic beads, sequins, and metal wire frames that may contain persistent organic pollutants (POPs) and heavy metals. It also fosters gender equity by increasing women’s participation and leadership in the Carnival industry, and disseminates knowledge and practices to other global Carnival events, contributing to broader environmental and socio-economic benefits. The executing partner is the Trinidad-based, Basel Convention Regional Centre for Training and Technology Transfer for the Caribbean (BCRC-Caribbean). Total project budget is US$2,652,294 over 6 years, and the Project official end date is 31 October 2031

planEntities.name: 2.7.6 BDS Improved capacity of decision makers to leverage ethical artificial intelligence systems in their national decision-making policies and plans to advance safety, social cohesion and benefits across the society
planEntities.parentName: MSDCF 8.1: Government and civil society capacities are strengthened to advocate for, implement and monitor efforts to challenge harmful social norms, and build and maintain safer, fairer, more inclusive, and equitable societies
planEntities.description:
AI Readiness Assessment Methodology (RAM): Artificial Intelligence (AI) is a dynamic technology of the 4th Industrial Revolution. Its effects are forecasted to impact every aspect of society. As the discussions about AI heightens, many SIDS including those in the Caribbean, have yet to develop strategies and national policies to manage the impacts of AI on their society even as the citizens interact with AI in daily life. As an underrepresented stakeholder in the AI ethics debate, Caribbean SIDS must begin to articulate the indigenous knowledge, cultural and ethnic pluralism, and diverse value systems that define the sub-region, in line with global ethical standards.  

AI systems raise new types of ethical issues that include, but are not limited to, their impact on decision-making in employment and labour, social interaction, health care, education, media, freedom of expression, access to information, privacy, democracy, discrimination, and weaponization. Furthermore, new ethical challenges and risks are created by the potential of AI algorithms to reproduce biases, for instance regarding gender, ethnicity, and age, and thus to exacerbate already existing forms of discrimination, identity prejudice and stereotyping. As Caribbean nations expand their adoption of AI tools and other frontier technologies, stakeholders (policymakers, citizens, private sector, academia, and NGOs) must proactively collaborate to create strategies for the humanistic and ethical development and adoption of guidelines, regulations and frameworks.

The present activity aims to subsequently develop a regional roadmap and guidelines for an effective and relevant integration of the UNESCO ICT competency framework in national frameworks in those countries in order to strengthen teachers’ ICT and competencies and skills. In the Natural Sciences sector, UNESCO will conduct a rapid assessment of the island’s major scientific and research infrastructure, provide targeted financial and technical assistance to the Water Resources Authority of Jamaica for the urgent rehabilitation of critical hydrological infrastructure, and support the University of the West Indies (UWI) to implement the Women in Science Emergency (WISE) Initiative, which will provide twenty micro-grants to graduate-level women scientists whose studies and research were disrupted by Hurricane Melissa. planEntities.name: JAM SDG Joint Program: Digital Transformation for Education Jamaica (UNICEF)
planEntities.parentName: MSDCF 4.3: National institutions strengthened to deliver shock-resilient education and learning
planEntities.description:
The objective of this Joint Programme (JP) is to drive the digital transformation of the education system in Jamaica by prioritizing
digitalization of key processes in the education sector that would ultimately contribute to the achievement of better learning outcomes and higher levels of teacher engagement and retention. Focus on digitalization in education around improving data governance and interoperability of existing and newly developed digital systems within the education sector will strengthen data collection, monitoring, and reporting, and will support improved and more informed decision making within the education sector, including around gender responsiveness. Priority will also be placed on stakeholder capacity building, and institutional strengthening towards enabling data-driven decision-making by education ministry staff and teachers, to improve system-wide efficiency, and foster improved learning outcomes of about 240,000 students (girls and boys) in grades 1 through 6 by the end of the 3 years.

planEntities.name: SUR: ASTA - The Accelerator for Agriculture and Agroindustry Development and Innovation Plus for sustainable pineapple value chain development in Suriname
planEntities.parentName: MSDCF 1.1: Support provided to promote inclusive, competitive, and resilient business ecosystems
planEntities.description: The pineapple value chain is a priority value chain in the Government of Suriname's drive to diversify its economy from heavy reliance on the extractive industry. In 2018-2019, in response to a request by the Government of Suriname, FAO, UNIDO and ITC applied the Accelerator for Agriculture and Agroindustry Development and Innovation Plus (3ADI+), a joint value chains and market systems development initiative, to the pineapple sub-sector. Moving from this solid preparatory phase to implementation, the joint programme will foster stakeholder cooperation and engagement and promote SDG-compliant public and private investments in innovation at each value chain stage (i.e. production, processing, and distribution). To assure a long-term sustainability of the action, the technical component will involve a strengthening of the innovative capacities of national institutes and public extension and market promotion services. In sum, the programme represents a unique opportunity to channel investments into productive activities and generate incomes for poor rural communities.

planEntities.parentName: MSDCF 7.2: Governance mechanisms strengthened to protect and advance human rights, combat corruption, reduce crime and curb violence
planEntities.description:
The UNODC Detention Sector Reform Programme in Sint Maarten provides comprehensive technical assistance to the Ministry of Justice to modernize the prison system and support the transition to a new correctional facility in line with the Nelson Mandela Rules, the Bangkok Rules and other international standards. The programme focuses on strengthening prison governance, professionalizing staff through training and operational guidance, and developing sustainable management frameworks to ensure safe, humane and effective detention, as well as broader system reform including non-custodial measures and regional cooperation and knowledge exchange on prison reform.
This programme is carded for completion in August 2029.

planEntities.name: Implementation Support for the Strengthening and Improvement of the Queen Elizabeth Hospital
planEntities.parentName: MSDCF 4.1: National Institutions have improved capacity to provide access and deliver shock resilient and comprehensive health care services
planEntities.description: The project supports the Queen Elizabeth Hospital through project implementation, technical and procurement services aimed at strengthening current capacity and planning for future healthcare needs. UNOPS will support the development of a comprehensive hospital Master Plan informed by an integral assessment of existing infrastructure and projected population health needs. The project also includes rehabilitation and upgrading of existing hospital infrastructure to strengthen service delivery and resilience; procurement of medical equipment and information technology systems to optimize current hospital capabilities; and the identification, design and procurement of additional administrative and laboratory facilities to support future capacity. Together, these interventions aim to strengthen the safety, functionality, efficiency and long-term resilience of Barbados’ principal public referral hospital and its ability to respond to evolving healthcare demands.

planEntities.name: TTO: Detention Sector Reform Program (DSRP) - Sint Maarten Rule of Law Facilities
planEntities.parentName: MSDCF 7.2: Governance mechanisms strengthened to protect and advance human rights, combat corruption, reduce crime and curb violence
planEntities.description: The Sint Maarten Rule of Law Facilities project supports the design, construction and supervision of resilient, sustainable and effective detention infrastructure, including the long-term redevelopment of Point Blanche Prison and the temporary retrofit of the Simpson Bay Immigration Facility to provide additional detention capacity during construction. The project seeks to ensure safe, humane and dignified detention conditions aligned with national and international human rights standards, while supporting rehabilitation, reintegration and stronger correctional infrastructure. It also advances four Priority 1 “soft” components: (1) Point Blanche operations and maintenance, (2) correctional sector strengthening, (3) justice sector strengthening, and (4) implementation advisory support to strengthen institutional readiness, operational planning and delivery.

planEntities.name: TTO: Phase 0: Technical assistance for the strengthening of the Justice Sector in Aruba
planEntities.parentName: MSDCF 8.1: Government and civil society capacities are strengthened to advocate for, implement and monitor efforts to challenge harmful social norms, and build and maintain safer, fairer, more inclusive, and equitable societies
planEntities.description: The Aruba technical assistance for strengthening the justice sector supports the Ministry of Justice in preparing the development of a new detention facility through a pre-feasibility study and the transition toward Phase 1. The project contributes to strengthening the correctional sector and national infrastructure capacity by advancing a resilient, sustainable and effective long-term facility that enables safe and humane detention and supports rehabilitation and reintegration. The four key deliverables are: a consolidated assessment and gap analysis of the existing KIA facility; a high-level prison profile defining the needs and objectives of the future facility; high-level functional programming outlining the required configuration and capacity; and a business case setting out the technical, operational and financial basis for investment. Together, these deliverables provide the Government of Aruba with the foundation to advance decision-making, mobilize resources and move into Phase 1 of the new KIA development.

planEntities.name: Implementation Support for Water, Sanitation and Urban Infrastructure Improvements in Dutch Quarter, Sint Maarten
planEntities.parentName: MSDCF 6.2: National capacities strengthened to improve waste management and transition to a greener circular economy
planEntities.description: The Sint Maarten Dutch Quarter Water and Sanitation project supports the rehabilitation and expansion of critical wastewater and urban infrastructure in a densely populated community. The project focuses on upgrading and completing sewerage infrastructure, including wastewater collection and conveyance systems, pumping infrastructure and connections required to improve sanitation services and reduce environmental and public health risks. Planned works include completion of the pumping station, rationalization of existing intermediate infrastructure, connection of sewerage pressure lines and the progressive establishment of residential house connections. The intervention also incorporates complementary public infrastructure improvements, including sidewalks and streetlighting, to improve accessibility and safety within the project area. Together, these investments aim to provide more reliable and resilient sanitation infrastructure, improve living conditions in Dutch Quarter and support safer, healthier and more sustainable urban development for residents and businesses.

planEntities.name: BDS: Implementation support for the strengthening and improvement of the Queen Elizabeth Hospital
planEntities.parentName: MSDCF 4.1: National Institutions have improved capacity to provide access and deliver shock resilient and comprehensive health care services
planEntities.description:
UNOPS will support the Queen Elizabeth hospital through the provision of project implementation services for the management and procurement of the following components:
1. Development of comprehensive Master Planning for Queen Elizabeth Hospital according to the results of the integral assessment of the Hospital and in coherence with the population health projections data for the hospital growth.
2. Strengthen the existing capacity in the Queen Elizabeth Hospital through the provision of rehabilitation services on existing infrastructures.
3. Support the optimization of the current hospital capabilities through the provision of procurement services for the acquisition of medical equipment and IT equipment.
4. Support the identification and development of future hospital capabilities through the provision of integral design and procurement services for additional administrative and laboratory facilities.

planEntities.name: 22977-001 GUY GCF Grants Management support
planEntities.parentName: MSDCF 2.1: National capacities strengthened to mobilise development financing to support SDG implementation and national development priorites
planEntities.description: GCF has established the Readiness and Preparatory Support Programme (RSRP) and the Project Preparation Facility (PPF) - jointly referred to as the Readiness Programme - designed with the specific aim of promoting country ownership in responding to the challenges to climate change. Since its operationalization in 2014, the Readiness Programme has been providing funding for early support activities to enhance ownership and enable access to the GCF resources. Since 2018, UNOPS has been engaged with the GCF and provided grant management support to selected proposals of the Readiness Programme. On 12 December 2020, the GCF published the RFP 2020/028 on Procurement of Grant Management Services of its RPSP and the PPF. More specifically, the RFP states that the objective of the assignment is to provide high quality GMS to support the GCF Secretariat in ensuring that approved Readiness and PPF projects are implemented in a professional, effective and efficient manner. To provide these services to the GCF Secretariat, a qualified, reputable and experienced firm/consortium is contracted for a period of up to eight years, subject to the results of a Mid-Term Evaluation after year five.

planEntities.name: REG Roadmap for Implementing The Caribbean Priority Actions on the Illicit Proliferation of Firearms and Ammunition across the Caribbean in a Sustainable Manner by 2030
planEntities.parentName: MSDCF 7.2: Governance mechanisms strengthened to protect and advance human rights, combat corruption, reduce crime and curb violence
planEntities.description:
1.	Development of National Action Plan within the framework of the Caribbean Firearms Roadmap and support provided for Reporting via Monitoring and Evaluation Webinars and Workshops on Data Collection, Analysis and Reporting (ALL STATES)

2.	Strengthening institutional capacity via training courses for law enforcement officials, specifically,

I.	Combating Arms and Ammunition Trafficking (CTAM) Course: Bahamas, Guyana, St Lucia, Trinidad and Tobago
II.	National Specialized Interdicting Small Arms, Ammunition, Parts and Components: Trinidad and Tobago
III.	Regional Specialized Interdicting Small Arms, Ammunition, Parts and Components (ALL STATES)
IV.	Firearm Examiner Training: Antigua and Barbuda and St Kitts and Nevis
V.	Firearms identification and classification training workshops: Belize, Guyana, Jamaica, Saint Vincent and the Grenadines 
VI.	Webinar on emerging challenges related to firearms investigations (ALL STATES)

3.	Donation of a Comparison Microscope to support the examination of ballistic evidence at the Trinidad and Tobago Forensic Science Centre to address firearm related crimes: TRINIDAD AND TOBAGO

4.	Annual Meeting of States To ensure continuity and maintain momentum, the Roadmap provides for annual meetings of States, partners, and donors. These meetings are essential for reviewing progress, identifying challenges, and fostering targeted exchanges to strengthen implementation efforts. The 2025 Annual Meeting of States marks a significant milestone: the midpoint of the Roadmap’s implementation period. As outlined in the Joint Statement from the 3rd Annual Meeting of States, the 5th of such meetings is to also provide a platform for CFRM States to discuss the recommendations resulting from the “mid-term review on the implementation of the Roadmap.” The 2026 meeting will be held virtually and will focus on implementing the outcomes of the 2025 Joint Communique and Mid Term Review.

planEntities.name: TTO Support the development and implementation of eco-based solutions (BIOREACH)
planEntities.parentName: MSDCF 6.1: Environmental management institutions strengthened for sustainable natural resource management
planEntities.description:
1. Community mapping exercises; identification of economic/agricultural activities and location, demarcation of residential use from agriculture and development uses; identification of vulnerable areas; identification of current and projected use of land resources and how to manage them sustainably; identification of community level incentives for producing and implementing land use plan 
2. Develop a standardised agroecology curriculum for Lead Farmer Training Programme
3. Identify plots of land where diverse agroforestry can take place, and especially cocoa or coconut plantations that require rehabilitation.
4. Business planning support provided to interested farmers/farming households
5.Collect baseline socioeconomic data disaggregated by sex and age
6. Support ongoing research initiatives and testing resilient palms/trees for diseases.
7. Conduct phased rehabilitation of infected plantations, with agroforestry approach to avoid monoculture
8. Produce land degradation maps
9. Conduct ground truthing mission; determine what species exist at the site, which are at risk, patterns of movement/migration, human factors impacting habitats
10. Identify potential ecotourism/agritourism opportunities in established clusters and/or developing tourism opportunities in agricultural areas and estates
11. Review laws/institutional arrangements and regulations for forest and wildland fire management

planEntities.name: 2.6.8 BDS Government institutions and farmers are equipped with and adopt innovative technologies to improve water management and increase efficiency in the agricultural sector over time.
planEntities.parentName: MSDCF 6.1: Environmental management institutions strengthened for sustainable natural resource management
planEntities.description:
Addressing the water-energy nexus in agriculture, seeking to improve the efficiency of water resources to increase agricultural productivity, using technological innovations, such as (micro)
irrigation systems with solar energy to improve the efficiency and management of water and access to clean and climate-smart energy to increase agricultural water productivity.

planEntities.name: TTO Strengthening Adaptation Planning Processes and Capacity for Successful Implementation of Adaptation Actions in the Agricultural and Water Sectors of Trinidad and Tobago
planEntities.parentName: MSDCF 4.2: Social protection insitiutions have increased capacity and strengthened systems to improve adaptive responses, reduce poverty and enhance resilience, with UN support
planEntities.description:
1. Institutional procedure for effective implementation of Adaptation Pathways planning approach in agriculture and water sectors, involving 240 “Climate Risk Resilience Champions”
2. Capacities strengthened of 240 Climate Risk Resilience Champions on climate risk management backcasting, foresighting, monitoring and evaluation
3. Nine Climate Change Resilience Building Production Units upgraded for research on resilience and future field demonstrations through Farmer Field School programmes. 
4. At least 27 modeling-generated adaptation protocols and procedures designed (a minimum of 3 per Climate Change Resilience Building Production Unit) that can be adopted into farming practices to improve resilience. 
5. Selected mediumterm adaptation solutions for the agriculture and water sectors designed and formalized in a national framework document that builds on the VCA and is aligned with relevant key national documents including the NCCP and NDC
6. At least twelve riverine or watershed protection restoration and maintenance plans prepared for submission to he Adopt a River Programme supported by Climate Risk Resilience Champions
7. Integrated, sustainable business model designed for climate-resilient agricultural and aquaculture value chains in Trinidad and Tobago, based on cost-benefit analyses
8. 60 private sector individuals/entities trained to invest in adaptation-based ventures
9. Concept note for national full-size project, focused on strengthening climate resilience in the agriculture and water sectors, developed and submitted to the GCF.

planEntities.name: TTO Animal Disease Outbreak Response
planEntities.parentName: MSDCF 1.1: Support provided to promote inclusive, competitive, and resilient business ecosystems
planEntities.description: Enhanced capacity of the Ministry of Agriculture, Land and Fisheries (MALF) to respond effectively to animal disease emergencies using planned strategic approaches: The Animal Outbreak Emergency Response in Trinidad and Tobago project strengthens Trinidad and Tobago’s livestock sector by enhancing Ministry of Agriculture and Fisheries (MAF) capacity to rapidly detect and manage animal disease outbreaks, reducing production losses and safeguarding the continuity of agricultural value chains. By upgrading laboratory diagnostics, improving surveillance and field response systems, and modernizing risk‑communication tools, the project creates a more predictable and resilient operating environment for farmers and agri‑businesses. Its gender‑responsive training and procurement ensure equitable participation and access for women, contributing to a more inclusive sector. Overall, the project directly supports MSDCF Outcome 1.1 by reinforcing an enabling, competitive, and shock‑resilient business ecosystem within the national agriculture and livestock industry.

planEntities.name: TTO Ethical Recruitment and Work Permit Support in Aruba
planEntities.parentName: MSDCF 1.2: Strengthened institutions promote social policy for decent work
planEntities.description:
Work Permit Support:
1. IOM Aruba will provide additional capacity and technical support to the Government of Aruba to undocumented migrants with work permit procedures, including for their family members, as allowed in the new policy. Additionally, beneficiaries requiring CBI assistance in order to access permits will receive a small grant. The level of subsidy for the permits will depend on the beneficiaries' vulnerability, assessed using predefined criteria. Importantly, the financial responsibility for these permits will not rest solely on IOM; private sector partners will also contribute to the costs.  
2. IOM Aruba will provide targeted support to the Government of Aruba for the implementation of the new work permit policy, enhancing the government's capacity through technical inputs and assistance. This support aims to streamline processes, improve policy implementation, and ensure that the work permit system effectively addresses the needs of both migrants and the host community. The assistance will include in-kind technical support, such as providing resources, tools, and specialized expertise to facilitate the policy rollout. Additionally, IOM Aruba will offer technical assistance, including capacity-building activities, training sessions, and advisory services to government officials. This collaborative effort is designed to strengthen the government's capacity to manage work permits efficiently, foster economic inclusion, and promote a more organized and responsive labor market in Aruba.

Ethical Recruitment Programme:
The IOM Ethical Recruitment Program aims to promote fair and responsible hiring practices by working closely with employers and recruiters to ensure that labor migration is safe, transparent, and equitable. The program focuses on preventing exploitation and abuse of workers by promoting principles such as no recruitment fees for job seekers, clear employment terms, and respect for workers’ rights. Through training, capacity building, and guidelines, the program helps private sector partners adhere to ethical standards that protect both migrants and employers, fostering a fair and sustainable labor market that benefits all parties involved.

planEntities.name: A detailed report on migrants' needs in Sint Maarten, including recommendations for the implementation of CBI responses is available through the deployment of DTM capacity in targeted locations.
planEntities.parentName: MSDCF 3.1: Increased capacity to produce sustainable development data and use it for evidence-informed policy-making and legislation
planEntities.description:
Building on the capacities of trained partners and to inform an evidence-based understanding of humanitarian and protection needs, IOM will deploy DTM activities in selected locations, in coordination with the Government of Sint Maarten. In parallel, and to support community engagement, limited cash-based assistance may be provided to particularly vulnerable individuals identified during the data collection process. This support is intended to facilitate access to essential services and context-appropriate assistance.

Data collected will be consolidated into an analytical report outlining migrants’ social protection needs in Sint Maarten, accompanied by recommendations for addressing identified gaps through cash-based interventions. The analysis will also explore the applicability of the approach to other areas of migrant assistance, with a view to strengthening protection outcomes for vulnerable groups, including those exposed to exploitation or abuse.

planEntities.name: REG The Smart Seas Toolkit for Disaster Resilience and Digital Inclusion project
planEntities.parentName: MSDCF 3.1: Increased capacity to produce sustainable development data and use it for evidence-informed policy-making and legislation
planEntities.description:
The Smart Seas Toolkit (SST) for Disaster Resilience (“Smart Seas”) project is a joint initiative of the International Telecommunication Union (ITU), Caribbean Telecommunications Union (CTU) and the Telecommunications Authority of Trinidad and Tobago (TATT), supported by the Government of the Republic of Trinidad and Tobago which aims to increase the resilience and ultimately preserve the lives of Caribbean small-scale fishers (SSF) through information and communications technologies (ICTs), with emphasis on the enabling environment.

The project will identify gaps which may exist in the maritime communications enabling environment, from which gap-filling recommendations will be produced under consultation with key stakeholders within the region. These recommendations, along with other resources produced during the project, will form part of an online toolkit to strengthen the enabling environment. The project is initially being implemented in Trinidad and Tobago, which serves as the Maritime Rescue Co-ordination Centre (MRCC) for: Barbados, Grenada, St. Vincent and the Grenadines, as well as Trinidad and Tobago. The project outputs and outcomes are expected to be transferable to other Caribbean countries.

Furthermore, the project aims to facilitate the establishment of an international community to tackle the ongoing challenge of inaccessible communications at sea, through technological, service and market innovations. Subsequent phases of the Smart Seas project will introduce a certification program for marine very high frequency (VHF) radio- operation and increase SSF capacity. Later phases will also feature the utilization of cutting-edge communication technologies to close data gaps in the maritime sector that are essential for boosting resilience across the mitigation, preparation, response, and recovery phases of the disaster risk management cycle.

TTO: Purchase of Very High Frequency (VHF) Coast Station equipment for the Trinidad and Tobago Coast Guard; Digital Skills Training for the Trinidad and Tobago Coast Guard

planEntities.name: 1.10 BDS Quality of Service Review for Fixed Broadband Services in Barbados
planEntities.parentName: MSDCF 8.1: Government and civil society capacities are strengthened to advocate for, implement and monitor efforts to challenge harmful social norms, and build and maintain safer, fairer, more inclusive, and equitable societies
planEntities.description:
ITU and the Ministry of Innovation, Science and Smart Technology of Barbados has signed the partnership agreement on telecommunication and ICT services. The partnership aims to undertake a Quality of Service Review for Fixed Broadband Services in Barbados. 

This project will conduct a review and evaluate the current levels of quality of service (QoS) for Fixed Broadband Services throughout the country with a view to establish baseline of QoS parameters, implementing QoS standards as well as updating its regulatory framework related to Fixed Broadband Services. The review will include an audit of the fixed Broad Band Services (Internet services) being provided by the service providers in Barbados which will determine the current state of play as well as issues and recommendations for improving the level of fixed broadband QoS in Barbados. The Covid-19 pandemic has underscored the need for high quality of service in telecommunications across all sections but especially of significant importance for online education, health and the financial services sector.

planEntities.name: Development of the Human Resources for Health (HRH) Plan for HIV, STI, and TB Integration
planEntities.parentName: TTO-National Health Systems enabled to deliver and expand coverage of key quality services and interventions for HIV, sexually transmitted infections (STIs), tuberculosis (TB), and viral hepatitis (VH), through sustainable policies, up-to-date normative guidance and tools, and generation and use of strategic information
planEntities.description:
The Ministry of Health (MOH), in partnership with the National AIDS Coordinating Committee (NACC), UNAIDS, and the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), is advancing efforts to strengthen Human Resources for Health (HRH) systems to sustain and enhance the HIV response in Trinidad and Tobago. The integration of HIV and STI services requires a robust HRH framework to ensure sufficient, well-trained, and equitably distributed health personnel to meet national needs to end AIDS as a public health threat by 2030. 

This project builds on ongoing MOH processes, including the validation of HRH needs for the Regional Health Authorities (RHAs) and above-site models. The resulting HRH Plan will be guided by the National Strategic Plan for HIV and will inform the broader HIV Sustainability Plan and serve as a strategic guide for workforce planning over the next five years.

planEntities.name: Guidelines for the transition of adolescents and youth living with HIV from Paediatric Sites to Adult services supported by a transitioning plan and peer groups for HIV and STIs
planEntities.parentName: TTO-National Health Systems enabled to deliver and expand coverage of key quality services and interventions for HIV, sexually transmitted infections (STIs), tuberculosis (TB), and viral hepatitis (VH), through sustainable policies, up-to-date normative guidance and tools, and generation and use of strategic information
planEntities.description:
Adolescents continue to be affected by HIV and STIs.  In addition to challenges with new infections, transition of patients, aged 10 to 24 years, is also associated with periods of treatment default. In Trinidad and Tobago, in 2022 there were an estimated 235 adolescents with HIV aged 15–24 years old and 40 adolescents aged 0-14 on ART with viral suppression of 77% and 100% respectively. 

 While significant improvements have been made in treatment access and reduced deaths among PLHIV, certain vulnerabilities of adolescence and youth affect their ability to remain on antiretroviral medication, maintain a suppressed viral load. The evidence informed management of all aspects of transition can significantly decrease the loss to follow up for certain clients.  

In fiscal 2024/2025, the Ministry of Health, through HACU, undertook an assessment, with support from I-TECH, to look at the challenges in adolescent care and inform a standardised mechanism to support the retention in care of the adolescent population at adult HIV treatment and care sites in Trinidad and Tobago. This project being executed by the NACC Secretariat is the follow up to the assessment completed by HACU in order to include some of the social issues and complete the development of a guideline.

planEntities.name: Stronger and Greener Productive Capacities for Just Transitions in Caribbean Small Island Developing States
planEntities.parentName: MSDCF 1.1: Support provided to promote inclusive, competitive, and resilient business ecosystems
planEntities.description:
This initiative, in collaboration with UNDESA, ECLAC and the RC system, supports four Caribbean SIDS to boost statistical capacity, identify productive capacities gaps, and design holistic programmes to address these gaps. Funding is particularly important as SIDS often have less access to external finance and are among the most indebted developing countries in the world. To address the debt problem, UN Trade and Development has advocated for a new development-centered international debt architecture. 

This means:

Scaling up concessional finance and grants from multilateral and regional development banks through greater capitalisation and re-channeling of unused Special Drawing Rights to Multilateral Development Banks.
Enhancing international liquidity through improved access to existing Global Financial Safety Net instruments with a focus on fairness and increased quotas for developing countries.
Implementing standstill rules that provide breathing space during crises to boost resilience to external crises. A good example are climate-resilient debt clauses.
Enhancing debt sustainability analysis by reflecting investments in the SDGs.
And making the Common Framework worthwhile for countries in distress

planEntities.name: REG Harnessing trade policy and transport and logistics to build sustainable and resilient food supply chains in the Caribbean
planEntities.parentName: MSDCF 2.2: National and regional institutions capacity is strengthened to accelerate transition to diversified, resilient and inclusive food systems economies
planEntities.description:
Objective of the Project
To strengthen the capacities of selected countries in the Caribbean and the Arab region to leverage trade policy measures and harness transport and logistic to be better prepared for and respond to supply chain disruptions and build sustainable and resilient food supply chains.

Activities
The project will enhance national actions and policy coordination by supporting the development of policies and plans that promote food security and inclusive and sustainable economic growth through sustainable and resilient food trade and food transport and logistics systems. The project will be deployed across three main phases:

Phase 1 will assess the current state of play regarding food trade and food transport and logistics systems. It will also help to identify needs and gaps as put forward context specific recommendations and solutions.

Phase 2 will focus on implementing the recommendations and solutions identified in Phase 1.

Phase 3 will aim to expand regional cooperation in the field of sustainable and resilient food trading and food transport and logistics system. This will ensure wider dissemination of the project benefits within the target regions and beyond.  Outreach and dissemination activities will include dedicated collaborative platforms, consultation mechanisms, and distance learning.

planEntities.name: TTO: ASYCUDA Extended Digitalisation of Customs Clearance in Trinidad and Tobago
planEntities.parentName: MSDCF 1.1: Support provided to promote inclusive, competitive, and resilient business ecosystems
planEntities.description: In October 2025, the Ministry of Finance and the United Nations Conference on Trade and Development (UNCTAD) signed a new partnership to modernise the country’s customs operations through the Automated System for Customs Data (ASYCUDA) marking a major milestone in efforts to improve trade facilitation, strengthen revenue collection, and create a more transparent, efficient customs environment. Developed by UNCTAD, ASYCUDA is a globally recognised customs management system that automates trade and transport procedures in line with international standards. The 18-month, USD 1.75 million project will deploy the latest ASYCUDA World modules and the ASYHUB data exchange platform at the Customs and Excise Division to expand paperless processing, reduce clearance times and costs, and provide real-time trade data. The systems will enhance risk management, cargo control, and interoperability among port and cargo operators, while enabling pre-arrival and pre-departure processing to expedite legitimate trade. Improved data analytics will also support evidence-based policymaking, strengthen border security, and reduce revenue losses—advancing a more efficient and competitive trade environment.

planEntities.name: Enhancing Smart Sustainable Agriculture and Agro-Processing for Climate Resilience in Dominica: Phase 1
planEntities.parentName: MSDCF 5.4: People vulnerable to food insecurity in the Caribbean benefit from strengthened food systems in a changing climate
planEntities.description:
The project, titled "Enhancing Climate Smart Sustainable Agriculture and Agro-Processing for Climate Resilience in Dominica – Phase 1" ESSAA-1, is Phase 1 of a comprehensive initiative that addresses critical challenges faced by Dominica's agricultural sector. The project seeks during this 1st phase to develop effective gender responsive mitigation and adaptation measures, by enhancing resilience to climate change in supporting sustainable agriculture and strengthening agro-processing. The project follows the UN 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development, supporting specifically the attainment of the following Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) identified as priority for the MASE-CARICOM cooperation: SDG 5, 6,7, 9, 12, 13, 15, 17. The project also aligns with the objectives of the Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD), the UN Convention to Combat Desertification (UNCCD) and the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC).

The project aims to support the sustainable and integrated management of resources; in particular water. The project offers gender responsive capacity-strengthening programs in climate-smart agriculture to empower vegetable farmers in the Morne Prosper community, enabling them to tackle climate-related challenges and improve food and water security. Gender sensitive stakeholder engagement is a core component, ensuring that the project aligns with local needs and priorities.

planEntities.name: Global Biodiversity Framework Early Action Support (GBF-EAS)
planEntities.parentName: MSDCF 6.1: Environmental management institutions strengthened for sustainable natural resource management
planEntities.description:
The recent “Little Book on Investing in Nature” estimates the global annual biodiversity financing gap at US$700 billion. The CBD Panel of Experts on Resource Mobilization highlighted that 
implementation of the new biodiversity targets under the Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF) will require additional financial resources, increased resource efficiency, and a reduction of biodiversity-harmful financial flows. Reducing the biodiversity finance gap can only be achieved through transformative change across 
economies and society.
To develop a clear picture of how to achieve the targets of the CBD’s GBF, a detailed assessment of the policy and institutional national context, a biodiversity expenditures review and financial needs are required as well as development and implementation of finance plans. CBD Parties face the following key barriers to sustainable financing of nature-positive policies and practices: (a) limited awareness, coordination, and capacity among national stakeholders to address gaps in biodiversity financing; (b) insufficient knowledge and systematic (c) lack of systematic measurement and reporting 
of the negative impacts of finance contributing to biodiversity loss; (d) biodiversity finance needs are imprecisely defined and poorly understood; (e) limited knowledge, use and mainstreaming of country-specific biodiversity finance solutions; and (f) limited exchange and uptake of global best practices in the sustainable 
financing of biodiversity.

Given the need for a comprehensive and multi-stakeholder strategic approach to resource mobilization, Target 19 requests all countries to develop national biodiversity finance plans (BFPs). These BFPs should assess the root causes of biodiversity loss, identify national biodiversity finance gaps, and articulate strategies on how to reduce the gaps through a suite of finance solutions aimed at reducing flow of resources that cause harm to biodiversity; generating additional resources; and enhancing the effectiveness and efficiency of resource use. To respond to this need and based on the experience of UNDP’s Biodiversity Finance Initiative (BIOFIN) and other relevant methodologies, this project aims to support a global programme that will establish a transformative 
process for biodiversity finance in all participating eligible countries, involving all relevant stakeholders such as Ministries of Finance and Environment, and the private and financial sectors through a socially and gender-inclusive approach. The project will support countries in baseline diagnostics, capacity and institutional strengthening, and developing finance plans to mobilize resources at scale to implement the GBF.

1.	Autistic Society of Trinidad and Tobago – climate smart agriculture to provide livelihood opportunities for persons with autism
2.	Digicel Foundation – implementation of the first Persons with Disabilities Innovation Challenge
3.	The UWI Life Sciences Department – development of compost and compost tea from sargassum to support agriculture and farmers.
4.	Conserving Habitats and Environmental Organisms (CHAPO) – engaging youth in the design and build of equipment to remove sargassum from the sea as well as in the development of products from the sargassum
5.	Nature Seekers – conversion of sargassum into biogas to fuel jewellery making from waste glass from Matura Beach.
6. Trinidad and Tobago Field Naturalist Club – supporting regional biodiversity conservation
7.  Grande Riviere Tourism Development Organization – solarisation of the community facility building which supports several community activities.
8. Habitat for Humanity Trinidad and Tobago – Rainwater harvesters for 6 community beneficiaries.
9. Tobago Reforestation and Watershed Rehabilitation Programme – Converting bay leaves into teas as an economic driver for reforestation.
10. Buccoo Reef Trust – To support disaster preparedness in Tobago.
11. Future Fishers – To support the development of smoked fish in Trinidad and Tobago as a strategy for addressing bycatch.
12. Art by Creative Design – To develop sustainable knowledge management products which will highlight the 30 years of work of the GEF SGP in Trinidad and Tobago.
13. Rotaract of Arima - to address water conservation, youth development and the realization of green businesses with EcoWash.

These programmes are targetted for completion in 2026 with a new batch of programmes/ grantees under OP8.

planEntities.name: Accelerating the transition to a net-zero, nature-positive economy in Trinidad and Tobago (TT Net-zero)
planEntities.parentName: MSDCF 2.3: National and regional capacities strengthened to accelerate the green energy transition
planEntities.description:
The project’s overall objective is to significantly accelerate the reduction of Trinidad & Tobago’s dependency on oil and gas production while contributing to a national transition towards a net-zero, nature-positive economy. This objective will be achieved through a three-fold approach.
Project activities aim to reform the national policy environment to maximize synergies between climate, biodiversity and human well-being. Hence, the Government of Trinidad and Tobago commits and takes nature-positive action to decarbonize its economy towards a net-zero target.
Also, project activities address barriers to finance such that T&T’s public and private sector will deploy financing mechanisms to mobilize investments for the decarbonization of the economy with a particular focus on the energy sector. This involves the implementation of sectoral and thematic reforms and plans for the energy sector in line with a developed NZNP strategy.
It is further envisaged that interventions will showcase the feasibility of low-carbon, nature-positive technologies by implementing NZNP-aligned demonstration projects on Trinidad as well as on the island of Tobago.
The project is expected to be transformative in supporting T&T in transitioning towards a net-zero, nature-positive economy. The project is expected to achieve greenhouse gas emissions mitigation over the project’s lifetime of 860,699 tCO2e, of which 3,320 tCO2e will be direct and 857,379 tCO2e indirect, to achieve 100 ha of land and ecosystems under restoration, 1000 ha of landscapes under improved practices, and reach 3,260 beneficiaries, with a targeted distribution of 1,630 women and 1,630 men.
