planEntities.name: UNFPA - Local governments strengthened to reduce maternal mortality, promote family planning and reducing GBV (Poderosas da Amazônia)
planEntities.parentName: 2.2.1 Mulheres, jovens, pessoas negras, refugiados, migrantes e apátridas, pessoas com deficiência e de outros grupos que sofrem discriminação e organizações da sociedade civil têm suas capacidades fortalecidas e oportunidades iguais de mobilização social e participação na formulação de leis, políticas, planos e orçamentos, para promover a justiça social, a igualdade de geração, gênero, raça e etnia e o respeito aos direitos humanos.
planEntities.description: The Poderosas da Amzônia project aims to strengthen local governments’ institutional responses to reducing maternal mortality; promoting family planning, especially aimed at reducing teenage pregnancy, and expanding access to modern contraceptives; and reducing gender-based violence in the states of Roraima and Amazonas, in the Legal Amazon region of northern Brazil. The project is structured on two main axes: 1) strengthening public services in the women's health care network and the women's social protection and assistance network, through the training of professionals and the establishment of standard operating procedures; and 2) institutional strengthening of women's NGOs in the Amazon region for women's empowerment, promotion of rights and access of priority populations to public services. The actions will be implemented within the scope of two main government programs at the local level, aiming to strengthen their respective capacities.

planEntities.name: UNFPA (UNICEF, UNESCO, UNHCR, PAHO, IOM, ILO) Comprehensive protection and promotion of the rights of indigenous children, adolescents and young people in the Brazilian Amazon basin
planEntities.parentName: 2.1.1 Capacidades de gestão em políticas públicas de proteção social, erradicação da pobreza, combate à fome e de empoderamento econômico fortalecidas, considerando aspectos demográficos e sociais regionalizados, com foco nos territórios, grupos e pessoas em situação de vulnerabilidade, em especial jovens e mulheres que sofrem discriminações múltiplas, priorizando o desenvolvimento de estratégias de inclusão socioeconômica, incluindo a redução das desigualdades no mercado de trabalho, estimulando níveis de qualificação, empregabilidade e de renda igualitários entre homens e mulheres, abrangendo também trabalhadoras domésticas, o setor de cuidados, trabalhadores rurais e trabalhadores de aplicativos.
planEntities.description:
The project encompass a wide range of areas, including nutrition and food security, protection against various forms of violence (with a particular focus on sexual violence), disease prevention, the production of educational materials in Indigenous languages, economic empowerment, the structuring of an integrated network of indigenous women and youth to support governance in Biosphere Reserves, and the training of youth in ethnic education and leadership.
Additionally, the proposal emphasizes community training and leadership development, as well as the training of health professionals to ensure culturally appropriate and effective healthcare services.

The UNFPA Bahia 2025 Seal aims to recognize and encourage good municipal practices that contribute to the three UNFPA Transformative Outcomes (TOs): Zero unmet need for reproductive planning; Zero preventable maternal deaths; and Zero situations of gender-based violence or harmful practices.

planEntities.name: UNHCR (MPTF SD of Brazilian Legal Amazon) strengthens access to documentation and culturally sensitive services for indigenous refugees and migrants, enabling rights, protection, and inclusion through legal assistance, training, and community-based initiatives
planEntities.parentName: 4.1.3 Capacidades institucionais fortalecidas para políticas públicas e programas para reduzir as múltiplas formas de criminalidade e violência contra públicos mais afetados e em situação de vulnerabilidade, com especial atenção à violência baseada em gênero e à discriminação racial e contra as juventudes, junto com a provisão de serviços de assistência social e acesso à justiça especializados para vítimas, suas famílias e comunidades.
planEntities.description: Sub-output exclusive to MPTF for the Sustainable Development of the Brazilian Legal Amazon). UNHCR works to guarantee the rights and legal identity of indigenous refugees and migrants by promoting access to documentation and culturally sensitive protection services. This includes organizing regular documentation task forces in Pacaraima to issue essential civil documents such as identity cards, birth certificates, and work permits, as well as supporting naturalization processes for indigenous communities affected by displacement. To ensure these services are accessible and culturally appropriate, UNHCR hires indigenous cultural mediators and trains community volunteers to assist in documentation efforts both inside and outside shelters. Complementing these actions, UNHCR conducts workshops and training sessions for local protection networks and shelter teams, in partnership with institutions such as FUNAI, to strengthen their capacity to provide culturally sensitive assistance and uphold the rights of indigenous refugees and migrants.

planEntities.name: UNHCR (MPTF SD of Brazilian Legal Amazon) builds institutional and community resilience through health, education, anti-xenophobia training, livelihoods, and climate initiatives, fostering rights, inclusion, and peaceful coexistence for indigenous refugees and migrants
planEntities.parentName: 5.1.1 Capacidades institucionais fortalecidas para implementar e reforçar políticas, marcos normativos e redes de proteção social e de garantia de direitos, em todos os níveis de governo e junto à sociedade civil, para resposta emergencial, proteção e integração socioeconômica de populações atingidas por crises humanitárias e desastres, pessoas refugiadas, migrantes e apátridas, mulheres, crianças, adolescentes e demais grupos e pessoas em situação de vulnerabilidade, e apoio às comunidades de acolhida.
planEntities.description: Sub-output exclusive to MPTF for the Sustainable Development of the Brazilian Legal Amazon). UNHCR strengthens institutional and community capacities to respond to humanitarian crises and promote socio-economic integration of indigenous refugees and migrants. Activities include reinforcing the indigenous health promoters project and organizing workshops for health professionals on culturally sensitive approaches in urban contexts. UNHCR supports the creation of educational spaces and Portuguese language courses tailored to indigenous communities, alongside literacy programs and youth and adult education initiatives adapted to their cultural specificities. The organization also advances socio-environmental innovation through the establishment of Sustainability Centers, which promote environmental education, traditional knowledge, and productive inclusion linked to the Amazon bioeconomy. To combat racism and xenophobia, UNHCR organizes intersectoral training sessions for local protection networks, involving actors from health, education, justice, and security sectors. Furthermore, UNHCR implements livelihood strengthening programs that combine training in handicrafts, agroecology, entrepreneurship, and digital skills with mentoring in financial management and market access. These efforts are complemented by support for refugee-led organizations through public calls for proposals, fostering community bonds and peaceful coexistence. Finally, UNHCR facilitates indigenous participation in climate-related events such as the Climate Mural pre-COP activity, ensuring their voices are included in global discussions on sustainability.

planEntities.description: The Accelerate-to-Demonstrate (A2D) Facility aims to accelerate the commercialization of innovative clean energy technologies in developing countries. The A2D Facility will include support to innovators, research institutions and related organizations in the thematic areas of: critical minerals, clean hydrogen, smart energy and industrial decarbonization. The programme is funded through GBP 65 million from the UK Government’s Department for Energy Security & Net Zero (DESNZ), which includes the 1% UN coordination levy. It currently runs from 1st April 2023 to 31st March 2029. The programme’s main Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)-of-focus are SDGs 13 (climate action), 1 (no poverty) and 9 (industry, innovation and infrastructure), as well as contributing to a range of co-benefits, including, but not limited to, applying the principles of Leave No One Behind, a human rights-based approach, and gender equality and the empowerment of women that encapsulate the universal values on which the 2030 Agenda is based.

planEntities.description: This project will assist policymakers in evaluating the impacts of Brazil’s transition to a low-carbon economy under New Industry Brazil (NIB), the country’s current industrial policy, and the Ecological Transformation Plan (ETP). NIB is Brazil’s long-term industrial policy launched in 2024 to drive neo-industrialization through innovation, sustainability, and strategic investment. It sets out six missions focused on food security, healthcare resilience, sustainable cities, digital transformation, decarbonization and energy transition, and defense sovereignty A key aspect of this collaboration will be the development and sharing of a common database, including but not limited to the Social Accounting Matrix (SAM), which will serve as the basis for the model, as well as the exploration of synergies and cooperation with other institutions already engaged in ETP modelling.

planEntities.name: UNODC GLOG80 LEAP Law enforcement agencies' capacities strengthened to address illegal deforestation and related crimes in Tropical areas
planEntities.parentName: 3.1.1 Capacidades de gestão e governança fortalecidas para políticas e programas de restauração de zonas degradadas, conservação da biodiversidade e uso sustentável de ecossistemas terrestres, aquáticos e costeiros, com maior participação, inclusive na dimensão territorial, dos povos indígenas, dos povos e comunidades tradicionais e das populações do campo, floresta e águas em geral, respeitando o conhecimento tradicional e valorizando e remunerando, conforme adequado, os serviços ambientais por eles prestados
planEntities.description:
Project: Law Enforcement Assistance Programme to Reduce Tropical Deforestation (LEAP).
Actual start date: 01/07/2018.

LEAP is a partnership between UNODC and INTERPOL that seeks to share expertise and build global networks to fight illegal deforestation and related crimes. The project assists Member States by supporting law enforcement in key countries across Latin America and Southeast Asia, contributing to tackling climate change and achieving the SDGs by assisting in the fight against tropical deforestation. It is implemented under the United Nations Convention against Transnational Organized Crime and in line with the Global Programme on Crimes that Affect the Environment.

planEntities.name: UNODC GLOX99 GMCP Law enforcement agencies' capacities strengthened to address transnational organized crime and illicit trafficking through fluvial means in the Amazon basin and in the tri-border area between Brazil, Paraguay, and Argentina
planEntities.parentName: 4.1.5 Capacidades governamentais fortalecidas para garantir uma abordagem multidimensional para combater crimes transnacionais, em especial durante crises humanitárias, e mitigar seus impactos sobre grupos e pessoas em situação de vulnerabilidade, compartilhando informações e aprimorando políticas orientadas por evidências, voltadas ao respeito aos direitos humanos e baseadas na igualdade de geração, gênero, raça e etnia.
planEntities.description:
#SSC Colombia, Paraguay, Cape Verde, Guinea Bissau, Mozambique, Nigeria, Senegal, South Africa and Tanzania.
Project: Global Maritime Crime Programme (GMCP).
Actual start date: 19/08/2022 | End date: End date: 30/09/2024.

GMCP assists Member States in enhancing and coordinating their efforts against maritime crime. In Brazil, GMCP has three fronts of action. The first aims to strengthen Brazil’s interagency capacity on river and maritime control and the country's prosecutorial capacity to disrupt organized crime in the Amazon basin, including cross-border cooperation with Northern neighbouring countries. The second focuses on the Southern Tri-Border of Brazil (with Paraguay and Argentina), aiming to equip law enforcement agencies and criminal justice sectors with skills to detect, interdict, investigate and prosecute threats in rivers, especially trafficking. Thirdly, GMCP promotes cooperation between Brazil and West African countries. GMCP is implemented under UNODC's mandate of the United Nations Convention against Transnational Organized Crime and the Three International Drug Control Conventions.

planEntities.name: UNODC GLOZ83 CRIMJUST National actors' capacities strengthened to promote transnational investigations, criminal justice actions & cooperation, with a view of disrupting organised crime networks
planEntities.parentName: 4.1.5 Capacidades governamentais fortalecidas para garantir uma abordagem multidimensional para combater crimes transnacionais, em especial durante crises humanitárias, e mitigar seus impactos sobre grupos e pessoas em situação de vulnerabilidade, compartilhando informações e aprimorando políticas orientadas por evidências, voltadas ao respeito aos direitos humanos e baseadas na igualdade de geração, gênero, raça e etnia.
planEntities.description:
#SSC Latin America and West Africa.
Project: Criminal Network Disruption Global Programme (CRIMJUST).

CRIMJUST aims contribute to the reduction of the impact of organised crime and related corruption on the security and rule of law of countries along illicit trafficking routes. In January 2023, a new third phase of CRIMJUST was launched to strengthen transnational investigations, criminal justice actions and criminal justice cooperation along illicit trafficking routes in Africa, Latin America, and the Caribbean. This phase focuses on identifying and disrupting organised crime groups and high-level criminal targets, via a three-tier intervention: (a) investigating and prosecuting transnational illicit trafficking, (b) depriving organized crime groups of illicit proceeds, and (c) fostering institutional integrity and promoting Human Rights Standards. CRIMJUST is implemented under UNODC's mandate of the United Nations Convention against Transnational Organized Crime and the Three International Drug Control Conventions.

planEntities.name: UNODC BRACF23 PRIS-COOP Prison administration organizations' and law enforcement agencies' capacities strengthened to deal with organized crime in prisons in Brazil and Paraguay and with organized crime and illicit trafficking in the Amazon Tri-Border between Brazil, Colombia, and Peru
planEntities.parentName: 4.1.5 Capacidades governamentais fortalecidas para garantir uma abordagem multidimensional para combater crimes transnacionais, em especial durante crises humanitárias, e mitigar seus impactos sobre grupos e pessoas em situação de vulnerabilidade, compartilhando informações e aprimorando políticas orientadas por evidências, voltadas ao respeito aos direitos humanos e baseadas na igualdade de geração, gênero, raça e etnia.
planEntities.description:
#SSC Paraguay, Peru, Colombia.
Project: PRIS-COOP.
Actual start date: 01/06/2021 | End date: 01/02/2024.

This project focuses on addressing the work of Transnational Criminal Organizations (TCOs) in Brazil and bordering countries. To enable so, it divides itself into two main objectives: the first aim is to promote the use, in Brazil and Paraguay, of innovative practices to enhance prison management in line with international minimum standards, with a focus on the challenges posed by organized crime in prisons, promoting cooperation between both countries. The second aim is to promote cooperation between Brazil, Paraguay, Peru and Colombia in implementing prison management best practices. PRIS-COOP is implemented under UNODC's mandate of the United Nations Convention against Transnational Organized Crime and the United Nations Standard Minimum Rules for the Treatment of Prisoners (Nelson Mandela Rules).

planEntities.name: UNODC BRACF23 PEMS Authorities' capacities strengthened to address trafficking in persons for the purpose of forced labour in gold mining in the Tapajós River basin
planEntities.parentName: 4.1.5 Capacidades governamentais fortalecidas para garantir uma abordagem multidimensional para combater crimes transnacionais, em especial durante crises humanitárias, e mitigar seus impactos sobre grupos e pessoas em situação de vulnerabilidade, compartilhando informações e aprimorando políticas orientadas por evidências, voltadas ao respeito aos direitos humanos e baseadas na igualdade de geração, gênero, raça e etnia.
planEntities.description:
Project: TAPAJÓS: A Prevalence-based Project to Reduce Forced Labor (Tapajós).
Actual start date: 01/10/2021.

This project aims to reduce the prevalence of forced labour in the gold mining sector in the State of Pará following evidence-based interventions to prevent trafficking in persons (TiP) and forced labour, protect victims and prosecute traffickers/explorers. Tapajós's Phase I was focused on producing knowledge on (a) the prevalence of TiP and forced labour, (b) the production chain of gold mining in the region, and (c) the convergence of crimes. The project's Phase II now targets applying evidence-based intervention to reach its goal. It is implemented under the United Nations Convention against Transnational Organized Crime's Protocol to Prevent, Suppress and Punish Trafficking in Persons, especially Women and Children and the Protocol against the Smuggling of Migrants by Land, Sea and Air.

planEntities.name: UNODC GLOZ31 CRIMFLO Law enforcement and criminal justice system actors' capacities strengthened to detect and prevent timber trafficking
planEntities.parentName: 3.1.1 Capacidades de gestão e governança fortalecidas para políticas e programas de restauração de zonas degradadas, conservação da biodiversidade e uso sustentável de ecossistemas terrestres, aquáticos e costeiros, com maior participação, inclusive na dimensão territorial, dos povos indígenas, dos povos e comunidades tradicionais e das populações do campo, floresta e águas em geral, respeitando o conhecimento tradicional e valorizando e remunerando, conforme adequado, os serviços ambientais por eles prestados
planEntities.description:
Project: Strengthening the criminal justice system response to illegal deforestation and timber trafficking – from crime scene to court (CRIMFLO).
Actual start date: 26/09/2022.

This project has three main objectives: (a) improved inter-agency cooperation at the state and federal levels, (b) enhanced capacity and knowledge for front-line officers, and (c) increased private-sector cooperation. It focuses on 1) enhancing capacities of investigators, prosecutors, and judiciary to effectively handle a crime scene and case management, ensuring an effective process from crime scene to court, and 2) providing training and capacity building activities for front-line officers on trade supply chain security, law enforcement and customs training to detect and prevent timber trafficking. It is implemented under the United Nations Convention against Transnational Organized Crime and in line with the Global Programme on Crimes that Affect the Environment.

planEntities.name: UNODC (UNDP/UN-HABITAT) BRACF23 PE Pernambuco State's capacities strengthened to adress crime and violence through the Crime and Violence Prevention Programme
planEntities.parentName: 4.1.3 Capacidades institucionais fortalecidas para políticas públicas e programas para reduzir as múltiplas formas de criminalidade e violência contra públicos mais afetados e em situação de vulnerabilidade, com especial atenção à violência baseada em gênero e à discriminação racial e contra as juventudes, junto com a provisão de serviços de assistência social e acesso à justiça especializados para vítimas, suas famílias e comunidades.
planEntities.description:
Project: Technical Support for the Implementation and Monitoring of the 'Crime and Violence Prevention Program' of Pernambuco (Cooperation Pernambuco).
Actual start date: 30/06/2020.

This project aims to offer technical support to the state of Pernambuco in the implementation and monitoring of the 'Crime and Violence Prevention Program', by supporting the promotion of inclusive urban spaces through the improvement of policies on the prevention of crime, violence and drugs. It is a partnership between the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP), the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC), and the United Nations Human Settlements Programme (UN-Habitat) to support the Government of Pernambuco. It is implemented under UNODC's mandate on the United Nations Standards and Norms in Crime Prevention and the Three International Drug Control Conventions.

planEntities.name: UNODC (UNDP) BRACF23 NUPPi National authorities' capacities strengthned to produce evidence-based solutions to drug prevention, treatment, and care via the National System for the Prevention of the Use of Alcohol and Other Drugs
planEntities.parentName: 2.1.4 Capacidades de gestão de políticas públicas de saúde, soberania e segurança alimentar e nutricional fortalecidas, com foco na produção ambientalmente adequada, no acesso igualitário, na qualidade e na ação intersetorial, de forma inclusiva e protetiva para todas as pessoas, em especial as que estão em situação de vulnerabilidade, a partir das perspectivas de geração, gênero, raça e etnia e do respeito aos direitos humanos.
planEntities.description:
Project: Support for the Implementation of the National System for the Prevention of the Use of Alcohol and Other Drugs (SINAP)
Actual start date: 01/02/2022 | End date: 01/04/2024

This project aims to create and implement the National System for the Prevention of the Use of Alcohol and Other Drugs, through (a) a national coordination mechanism, (b) advocacy and communication actions, and (c) strengthening prevention programs already implemented at the national level. It is a partnership between the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP), the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC), and the Ministry of Justice and Public Security. It is implemented under UNODC's mandate on the Three International Drug Control Conventions.

planEntities.name: UNODC (UNDP) BRACF23 CDESC National authorities' capacities strengthened to produce studies and analyses on drug policiy through the Center for Studies on Drug and Social Community Development
planEntities.parentName: 4.2.3 Capacidades das instituições públicas fortalecidas para o planejamento governamental estratégico, integrado e participativo com vistas à convergência das ações de Estado e à integração de suas funções estruturantes, com foco na melhoria do acesso a bens e serviços públicos de qualidade, especialmente por grupos e pessoas em situação de vulnerabilidade.
planEntities.description:
Project: Center for Studies on Drug and Social Community Development (CDESC)

The former Center of Excellence on Illicit Drug Supply Reduction was remodeled into the Center for Studies on Drug and Social Community Development (CDESC) in 2024. CDESC aims to produce evidence and human rights-based studies and analyses on drug policy. It focuses on prevention, innovation, alternative development, human rights, and vulnerable populations.

The project is the result of a partnership between the National Secretariat for Drug Policy and Asset Management of the Ministry of Justice and Public Security (SENAD/MJSP), the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC) and the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP). It is implemented under UNODC's mandate on the Three International Drug Control Conventions.

planEntities.name: UNODC BRACF23 SAR-TI Community-based organizations and public authorities' capacities strenghened to prevent and mitigate the impact of environmental crimes related to illegal gold mining in Indigenous territories
planEntities.parentName: 4.2.2 Gestão pública participativa e fortalecida, baseada em evidências e dados desagregados, com o estabelecimento de estratégias de elaboração, execução, monitoramento e avaliação participativa de políticas públicas, e com atenção aos grupos e pessoas em situação de vulnerabilidade.
planEntities.description:
Project: Strengthening Early Warning Systems and Responses to Environmental Crimes Related to Illegal Gold Mining in Indigenous Territories.

This project seeks to promote a model of preparedness and early warning to respond to risks and impacts caused by environmental crimes related to illegal gold mining in indigenous territories in the Amazon region. It builds upon the results of the evidence-based studies produced by UNODC under the Tapajós Project, implemented in the gold mining area of the Tapajós region in the State of Pará. It aims to promote the interaction of community-based organizations and public authorities in preventing and mitigating impacts. It is implemented under the United Nations Convention against Transnational Organized Crime and in line with the Global Programme on Crimes that Affect the Environment.

planEntities.name: UNODC BRACF23 AURUM Law enforcement and environmental oversight agencies' capacities strenghened to reduce organized criminal activity related to illegal mining and trafficking of mercury in the Brazilian Amazon
planEntities.parentName: 4.1.5 Capacidades governamentais fortalecidas para garantir uma abordagem multidimensional para combater crimes transnacionais, em especial durante crises humanitárias, e mitigar seus impactos sobre grupos e pessoas em situação de vulnerabilidade, compartilhando informações e aprimorando políticas orientadas por evidências, voltadas ao respeito aos direitos humanos e baseadas na igualdade de geração, gênero, raça e etnia.
planEntities.description:
Project: Combating Illegal Mining and Gold and Mercury Trafficking through Law Enforcement Cooperation in the Brazilian Amazon - Project Aurum.

The project aims to reduce organized criminal activity related to illegal mining and trafficking of mercury to promote the rule of law and economic development in the Brazilian Amazon. Its main outcomes include: 

(i) generating better understanding of the criminal networks involved in illegal mining and convergent crimes in the northern region of Brazil amongst law enforcement and the judiciary
(ii) improving operational structure and law enforcement authority response through alignment of internal procedures and regulations
(iii) enhance technical law enforcement capacity to prevent and combat illegal mining and mercury trafficking related to illegal mining
(iv) strengthened regional cooperation among law enforcement agencies through the fostering of effective intelligence sharing and coordinated strategies against illegal mining, and
(v) increased traceability of mercury to ensure follow-up investigations after seizures.

It is implemented under the United Nations Convention against Transnational Organized Crime and in line with the Global Programme on Crimes that Affect the Environment.

planEntities.name: UNODC BRACF23 PETROBRÁS Energy Sector Small and Medium Entreprises' Business Integrity Culture Strenghtened
planEntities.parentName: 4.1.1 Instituições públicas e da sociedade civil com capacidades fortalecidas de participação no controle, desenvolvimento e aplicação do marco legal de transparência, integridade, combate à corrupção, e de inovações tecnológicas no setor público, ampliando a transparência e o acesso a dados e informações sobre a oferta e a qualidade dos serviços prestados à população, e desenvolvendo soluções, baseadas nos direitos humanos e na igualdade de geração, gênero, raça e etnia, para os desafios nacionais e locais.
planEntities.description:
Project: Strengthening the Business Integrity Culture of SMEs in the Energy Supply Chain in Brazil.

This project aims to strengthen the culture of integrity in the energy supply chain in Brazil, with special attention to small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), in the light of the United Nations Convention against Corruption (UNCAC), and national and international best practices.

planEntities.name: UNODC SPORTS Sports Organizations and Governments strenghtened to tackle corruption and economic crime in sport
planEntities.parentName: 4.1.1 Instituições públicas e da sociedade civil com capacidades fortalecidas de participação no controle, desenvolvimento e aplicação do marco legal de transparência, integridade, combate à corrupção, e de inovações tecnológicas no setor público, ampliando a transparência e o acesso a dados e informações sobre a oferta e a qualidade dos serviços prestados à população, e desenvolvendo soluções, baseadas nos direitos humanos e na igualdade de geração, gênero, raça e etnia, para os desafios nacionais e locais.
planEntities.description:
Project: Safeguarding Sports from Corruption and Economic Crime.

The project seeks to support governments, sports organizations, and relevant stakeholders to tackle corruption and economic crime in sport by (a) implementing activities that strengthen legal, policy and institutional frameworks to counter corruption and crime in sport, (b) increasing cooperation among and between governments and sports organizations at national and international level, and (c) enhancing understanding and capacities to tackle corruption and crime in sport through research and analysis. This project is implemented under UNODC's mandate as guardian of the United Nations Convenvention against Corruption.

planEntities.name: #CSS UNODC BRACF23 SYNTHCOOP Brazil and Southern Cone strenghtened to detect and control the emergence of New Psychoactive Substances
planEntities.parentName: 4.1.4 Capacidade do setor público e da sociedade civil fortalecida, com vistas a implementar experiências exitosas, nacional e internacionalmente, inclusive por meio da cooperação sul-sul e trilateral, para otimizar os resultados das políticas públicas.
planEntities.description:
#CSS Southern Cone
Project: Brazil Counter-Synthetics and Southern Cone Cooperation (Synth-Coop)

Under UNODC’s mandate as guardian of the Three International Drug Control Conventions, the project aims to (a) strengthen Brazil and Southern Cone regional and international cooperation to detect and control the emergence of New Psychoactive Substances (NPS) and (b) strengthen the Brazilian Early Warning System (EWS) by promoting the use of reliable and comparable data collection, innovation, and technology to support evidence-based responses to the threats posed by NPS.

planEntities.name: UNODC National capacities strenghtened to address Organized Crime, Corruption, the World Drug Problem and promote Crime Prevention and Criminal Justice
planEntities.parentName: 4.1.4 Capacidade do setor público e da sociedade civil fortalecida, com vistas a implementar experiências exitosas, nacional e internacionalmente, inclusive por meio da cooperação sul-sul e trilateral, para otimizar os resultados das políticas públicas.
planEntities.description: UNODC supports member states to make the world safer from drugs, organized crime, corruption and terrorism.  UNODC offers practical assistance and encourages transnational approaches to action, including via South-South and Trilateral coordination.

planEntities.name: UNODC (UNDP) BRACF23 Vidas Protegidas National Secretariat for the Rights of Children and Adolescents instrumentalized to prevent and respond to intentional lethal violence against children and adolescents at the federal, state and municipal levels
planEntities.parentName: 2.2.2 Capacidades institucionais nacionais e subnacionais fortalecidas para a prevenção e o enfrentamento às múltiplas formas de violências contra grupos e pessoas em situação de vulnerabilidade, em especial as violências baseadas em gênero, no racismo e no território e as que sofrem múltiplas e agravadas formas de discriminação, com atuação, de forma articulada, entre Poderes, Entes da Federação e a sociedade civil.
planEntities.description:
Project Protected Lives: Project to Strengthen the Network for Response and Prevention of Lethal Violence against Children and Adolescents in Brazil.

The project aims to carry out action research and prepare a proposal for a methodology/protocol for the performance of the System of Granted Rights for Children and Adolescents (SGDCA) in the prevention of intentional lethal violence against children and adolescents, as well as in the improvement of care for direct and indirect victims of this type of violence at the municipal, state and federal levels.

planEntities.name: UNODC BRACF23 Environmental UK Law enforcement agencies' and Indigenous peoples' capacities to investigate, denounce and disrupt illegal mining and related environmental crimes in the Brazilian Amazon
planEntities.parentName: 4.1.5 Capacidades governamentais fortalecidas para garantir uma abordagem multidimensional para combater crimes transnacionais, em especial durante crises humanitárias, e mitigar seus impactos sobre grupos e pessoas em situação de vulnerabilidade, compartilhando informações e aprimorando políticas orientadas por evidências, voltadas ao respeito aos direitos humanos e baseadas na igualdade de geração, gênero, raça e etnia.
planEntities.description:
#SSC Peru, Ecuador
Project: Strengthening Financial lnvestigations, Regional Cooperation, and Community Resilience to Counter Environmental Crime in the Amazon

The project aims to enhance the capacity of law enforcement agencies in Brazil and Peru to investigate and disrupt illegal mining and related environmental crimes through targeted training, mentoring, and cross-border cooperation. By integrating institutional strengthening, regional intelligence sharing, and community-based support—especially in indigenous territories—the project will contribute to reducing illicit financial flows, improving environmental protection, and reinforcing the rule of law across the region.

planEntities.name: UNOPS 23894 Social and economic transformation activities related to the work of the Public Prosecution for Labor in Brazil implemented
planEntities.parentName: 1.2.1 Governos nacionais e subnacionais, instituições públicas e setor privado têm suas capacidades reforçadas para formular e implementar políticas e iniciativas para promoção do desenvolvimento econômico local, da geração de renda, da ampliação da empregabilidade e garantia do trabalho decente, com foco em igualdade de oportunidades, na redução da discriminação nas relações econômicas e trabalhistas, das diferenças salariais por sexo, geração, gênero, raça, etnia ou nacionalidade, no fortalecimento dos direitos de trabalhadores, dos usuários e das comunidades afetadas pela atividade econômica, e na promoção da inclusão em condições igualitárias de mulheres, jovens, pessoas com deficiência, migrantes e pessoas refugiadas, de modo a proteger os direitos dos segmentos da população em situação de vulnerabilidade.

planEntities.description: The program aims to implement procurement and grants for the benefit of the population affected by the soil subsidence disaster in Maceió.

planEntities.name: UNOPS 23667 Technical assistance to Codemge in the structuring of partnerships for infrastructure and urban and regional development
planEntities.parentName: 1.1.2 Capacidades institucionais fortalecidas para aprimorar políticas públicas e modelos regulatórios de economia sustentável que favoreçam a descarbonização e a reindustrialização com vistas à agregação de valor por meio de investimentos inovadores, sustentáveis, resilientes e responsivos às questões de geração, gênero, raça e etnia e de novas tecnologias, nos setores público e privado, em especial nos setores de energia renovável, agroindústria e infraestrutura, promovendo padrões sustentáveis de consumo, produção e descarte.
planEntities.description: The project aims to strengthen the capacity of Codemge to develop public-private partnerships by providing advisory services and by structuring up to 5 PPP projects.

planEntities.name: UNOPS 24330 Strengthening education infrastructure management for traditional peoples in Brazil
planEntities.parentName: 2.1.3 Capacidades de gestão de políticas públicas de educação de qualidade, acesso, permanência e aprendizagem fortalecidas, proporcionando, com equidade, proteção e inclusão de grupos e pessoas em situação de vulnerabilidade, e oportunidades de aprendizagem ao longo da vida, a partir da perspectiva de geração, gênero, raça e etnia e respeito aos direitos humanos.

planEntities.description:
OUTCOME 1: PROMOTING PUBLIC POLICIES TO REDUCE MATERNAL AND CHILD MORTALITY AND MALNUTRITION AMONG INDIGENOUS CHILDREN UNDER FIVE YEARS OLD.
Output 1.3: Local capacity strengthened to reduce Maternal and child morbidity and mortality, as well as malnutrition, in priority Special Indigenous Health Districts (DSEI), enhancing indigenous medicine and traditional midwifes activities, through a gender perspective and human rights based approach.

PAHO/WHO Activities:

1.3.1. Identify priority issues through prior community consultations and promote and implement intercultural dialogues to define strategies and culturally appropriate interventions to strengthen comprehensive health care for indigenous women, children, adolescents and young people in priority DSEIs, with gender lenses.

1.3.2. Produce guides and materials appropriate to the context of indigenous health for cultural adaptation and implementation of public policies to reduce maternal mortality in the indigenous territories of priority DSEIs, through gender lenses and knowledge dialogue workshops

1.3.3. Strengthen comprehensive health care for indigenous children, prioritizing the expansion and updating of the Integrated Strategy for the Prevention of Childhood Diseases (AIDPI), including an adapted methodology for indigenous health agents (community AIDPI) in priority DSEIs in alignment with activity 1.1.1.

1.3.4. Train health professionals and vaccinators at the Base Centers to work in a qualified manner in vaccination for the development of microplanning actions in high-quality vaccination activities; and in epidemiological surveillance and surveillance of events supposedly attributable to vaccination or immunization (ESAVI), in the context of the Regional Initiative for the Elimination of Diseases and Health Conditions 30+ and the sustainable development goals with a focus on Indigenous Base Centers and riverside populations in indigenous areas.

1.3.5. Strengthen the cold chain with high-quality equipment and supplies, pre-qualified by the WHO, ensuring efficiency in the conservation and transportation of vaccines and the safety of immunization actions in indigenous areas.

OUTCOME 2: EXPANDING ACCESS TO CONTRACEPTIVE METHODS AND SEXUAL AND REPRODUCTIVE HEALTH SERVICES FOR THE INDIGENOUS POPULATION.


Output 2.1: Four (4) Selected DSEIs in the Legal Amazon strengthened in the promotion of sexual and reproductive health and rights
Output 2.2: Priority DSEIs strengthened for health education, including the promotion of sexual and reproductive health with gender perspective and human rights-based approach.


PAHO/WHO:

2.2.1. Identify priority issues through prior community consultations and promote and implement intercultural dialogues to define strategies and culturally appropriate interventions for the promotion of sexual and reproductive health in priority DSEIs.

2.2.2. Train indigenous health professionals (multidisciplinary indigenous health teams and/or indigenous health workers) in the promotion of sexual and reproductive health, with gender, life-course and intercultural approach, in priority DSEIs.

OUTCOME 3: PROMOTING THE INTEGRAL DEVELOPMENT OF INDIGENOUS ADOLESCENTS AND YOUTH.
Output 3.3: Indigenous adolescents and youth mobilized for actions promoting indigenous health


PAHO/WHO Activities:

3.3.1. Identify priority issues through prior consultations with indigenous adolescents and youth in the communities, and promote and implement intercultural dialogues to define culturally appropriate strategies and interventions to increase social mobilization and participation in promoting indigenous health, including psychosocial care and practices related to alcohol and drug use, sexual and reproductive health.

3.3.2. Conduct workshops to raise awareness and mobilize Indigenous adolescents and youth for community-based actions on Indigenous health, including psychosocial care and practices related to alcohol and drug use, sexual and reproductive health.

OUTCOME 4: PROMOTING INCLUSIVE TERRITORIAL GOVERNANCE AND INDIGENOUS MULTILINGUAL EDUCATION.
Output 4.3: Strengthening the participation of indigenous medicine specialists, especially women, in territorial governance bodies and indigenous multilingual education

PAHO/WHO Activities:

4.3.1. Promote two meetings of indigenous medicine experts, especially indigenous women leaders, from priority DSEIs, in conjunction with indigenous movements and organizations, to encourage participation in territorial governance bodies.

4.3.2. Carry out community-based health education actions to strengthen ancestral practices and knowledge of indigenous medicine on priority topics to be defined in the territorial context.

OUTCOME 5: PREVENTING VIOLENCE AGAINST INDIGENOUS CHILDREN, ADOLESCENTS, AND YOUTH, INCLUDING REFUGEES AND MIGRANTS.
Output 5.3: Training and strengthening of strategies developed by the DSEIs in preventing sexual and gender-based violence against indigenous children, adolescents, and youth.

PAHO/WHO Activities:

5.3.1. Identify priority issues, based on prior consultation with indigenous adolescents and youth from the communities, and promote and implement intercultural dialogues to define culturally appropriate strategies and interventions for violence prevention.

5.3.2. Training of health workers who work in and with priority DSEIs in preventing sexual and gender-based violence against indigenous children, adolescents and youth.

5.3.3. Awareness-raising and mobilization workshops for indigenous adolescents and youth to carry out community-based actions on indigenous health.

planEntities.name: Modernize Bhutan’s border management ecosystem to facilitate the safe trade of agri-food product
planEntities.parentName: 1.1 The Government, in partnership with the private sector and other stakeholders, demonstrates strengthened capacity to foster an enabling economic, institutional, and business environment that generates financing, investments, innovation and jobs in Bhutan’s green and digital economic transformation.
planEntities.description:
This is a three-year project (2025-2027) funded by the Standards and Trade Development Facility (STDF) of the World Trade Organization (WTO). The International Trade Centre (ITC) will serve as the implementing partner, ensuring effective coordination and execution of project activities in close partnership with Bhutan Food and Drug Authority (BFDA).

The project aims to address challenges faced by the Royal Government of Bhutan in ensuring the efficiency and safety of cross-border trade in agricultural and food products, including limited capacity for implementing SPS measures and border inspections, unpredictable trade requirements, lack of coordination among regulatory agencies, delays due to non-recognition of Bhutan’s certificates, and weak infrastructure for testing and certification. This project supports Bhutan in overcoming these challenges by leveraging solutions at the intersection of trade facilitation, border management, and quality compliance.

The Government of Botswana has requested for ILO technical support in facilitating a knowledge sharing and ratification of six instruments that the Government has identified for prioritized ratification, namely the Protocol of 2014 to the Forced Labour Convention, 1930, the Occupational Safety and Health Convention, 1981 (No. 155), Promotional Framework for Occupational Safety and Health Convention, 2006, the Employment Policy Convention, 1964 (No. 122), the Violence and Harassment Convention, 2019 (No. 190), and the Indigenous and Tribal Peoples Convention, 1989 (No. 169).

planEntities.name: Enhanced institutional capacities of national partners to produce, compile and use the tools provided to promote decent work.
planEntities.parentName: Increased availability and use of high-quality, disaggregated data by a more diverse range of stakeholders
planEntities.description: Botswana, through Statistics Botswana, conducted the Household Income and Expenditure Survey named Botswana Multi-Topic Household Survey (BMTHS). The survey takes a year to be completed. Data collection ran from November 2024 to Mid-October 2025. In 2024, the ILO supported Statistics Botswana to incorporate the 19th ICLS in this non-Labour Force Survey (LFS) source, as well as informality. As Botswana has already adhered to the 19th ICLS in the Quarterly Labour Force Survey (QLFS), it was important to ensure that the standard is also applied in the BMTHS, so that the labour market indicators compiled in QLFS are comparable to the labour market indicators compiled in this BMTHS. Furthermore, the BMTHS is used to produce poverty indicators. Given the relationship between employment (or lack of) and poverty, it is essential that employment is well defined in BMTHS, to examine the relationship between poverty and employment in Botswana. Furthermore, this source will allow Botswana to report on SDG 1.1.1 (Working poverty rate), again, highlighting the reason why employment should be well defined in HIES. Statistics Botswana  has requested ILO support for data analysis and report on the labour market indicators from this source. The above is expected to contribute towards improved labour modules in other statistical sources, by introducing the new standards adopted by the International Conference of Labour Statisticians (ICLS). During 2026 the ILO will provided supported Botswana to produce a thematic report on the experience of youth in the labour market. This report is almost ready for dissemination and ILO is expected to provide support for the dissemination of this report.

planEntities.parentName: Policy and legal frameworks and institutional capacities strengthened to address gender inequality and human rights, in line with national and international commitments
planEntities.description: Policy influence. The ILO will provided support towards enhanced institutional, technical, representational and policy impact capacities of workers' organizations in Botswana i.e. the two trade union federations in Botswana namely; Botswana Federation of Trade Unions (BFTU), and Botswana Federation of Public Private Parastatal Unions (BOFEPUSU) towards the development and implementation of labour market policies i.e. operationalization of the Employment and Labour law (2025); Occupational Safety and Health Policy; National Employment Policy etc.

planEntities.description: Support provided to Business Botswana towards their effective involvement in the implementation of various key policy frameworks to create a conducive environment for businesses to thrive through advocacy, stakeholder engagement, representation, and the provision of value-added services to its members. Some of these frameworks inter alia include the recently launched Strategic Plan: 2024-20281; the Botswana Decent Work Country Programme: 2022 - 2024  and the United Nations Strategic Cooperation Framework: 2020 -2026.

planEntities.name: Advancing Social Protection and Employment Opportunities in Botswana
planEntities.parentName: Social protection system strengthened to provide equitable and efficient social protection
planEntities.description:
During 2026 the ILO in collaboration with with UNICEF, UNDP and other agencies  will seek to explore multiple opportunities for improving efficiency of the social protection system, including implementation of the Single Social Registry, improving targeting and data management, more efficient benefit delivery systems, strengthening case management, and reallocating spending to programs that have the greatest impact on reducing poverty. The limited effectiveness of Active Labor Market Programs and youth employment initiatives to promote labor market inclusion is largely due to weaknesses in program design and concept, inadequate training and intermediation support, and persistent implementation challenges. In a context of fiscal constraints, addressing these gaps is a priority.
Therefore, this  Joint Programme will focus on strengthening the SP systems to be more efficient in service delivery, rationalizing of social protection expenditures, and fostering an evidence-based ecosystem initiatives for enhancing economic opportunities for youth and poor.

planEntities.parentName: Improved efficiency, resilience and accountability of government systems
planEntities.description:
Technical Assistance for Botswana’s Voluntary National GCM Review
The UN Network on Migration, with EU-funded support, will assist Botswana in preparing its voluntary national review of the Global Compact for Migration (GCM) ahead of the 2026 International Migration Review Forum. This process will assess progress, identify gaps, and set priorities for safe, orderly, and regular migration. Activities include an inception workshop, targeted questionnaires, progress assessment, multi-stakeholder consultations, drafting and validation of the review, and visibility efforts. The initiative is co-designed with the government to ensure inclusivity and data-driven outcomes within a EUR 10,000 budget.

planEntities.name: GEF-BDLD.10958. Strengthening national-level institutional and professional capacities of country Parties towards enhanced UNCCD monitoring and reporting – GEF 7 EA Umbrella IV
planEntities.parentName: Capacities of government are strengthened to actively manage climate change adaptation and mitigation through policies, guidance and investments that regulate practices of government, private sector and individuals
planEntities.description:
The international community through the UN member states adopted, in September 2015, the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development with 17 Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Among these SDGs, Goal 15 is particularly relevant for the United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification (UNCCD). Through this goal, countries are urged to, Protect, restore and promote sustainable use of terrestrial ecosystems, sustainably manage forests, combat desertification, and halt and reverse land degradation and halt biodiversity loss. The target 15.3 urges countries to combat desertification, restore degraded land and soil, including land affected by desertification, drought and floods, and strive
to achieve a land degradation-neutral world by 2030.
The twelfth session of the Conference of Parties (COP.12) of the UNCCD agreed in October 2015 to integrate the SDGs and related targets into the implementation of the Convention and decided that striving to achieve SDG target 15.3 is a strong vehicle for driving implementation of the UNCCD (decision 3/COP.12). COP.12 also endorsed the definition of land degradation neutrality (LDN) and invited Parties to (i) formulate voluntary targets to achieve LDN, (ii) use the UNCCD monitoring and evaluation framework, including progress indicators, to monitor, evaluate and communicate progress towards achieving the LDN target, (iii) explore options on how to integrate the voluntary LDN targets in their UNCCD National Action Programmes (NAPs), and (iv) promote the use of LDN targets and projects and other SLM initiatives as an effective vehicle for mobilizing additional sustainable financing and investments to address issues related to desertification, land degradation and drought (DLDD). LDN has therefore become an important, while non mandatory, element of UNCCD implementation, while at the same time contributing to other SDGs, including those SDGs relating to climate change mitigation and adaptation, biodiversity conservation, ecosystem restoration, food and
water security, disaster risk reduction, and poverty reduction.
Decision 2/COP.12 invites affected country Parties to establish national baselines and national-level voluntary LDN targets within their National Action Plans (NAPs). The New 10-year strategic plan and framework to enhance the implementation of the Convention paves the way for an enhanced reporting and review process within the UNCCD that considers the SDG framework. As such, UNCCD reporting and review system is based on (i) progress indicators to measure the progress against the future strategic framework of the UNCCD, and (ii) an implementation framework to assess actions at national and sub-national level relevant for UNCCD implementation. The reporting and review system addresses effective monitoring of financing for UNCCD implementation using refined methodologies in accordance with COP decisions.

Through this project, relevant institutions and national focal points will be capacitated to support data collection (default data, spatial mapping, drought status, land-based progress and recovery indicators on LDN targets, LDN, knowledge and technologies inventory, financial flows), undertake comprehensive reviews and detailed analysis and monitoring on progress made towards the implementation of the UNCCD strategic framework and SDG 15.3. The resultant information will be used by the country to prepare and validate the 2026 national report to the UNCCD as well as to support national communication and advocacy on reporting and land degradation neutrality targets achievement at the national level.

The project strengthens institutional governance, develops integrated management and business plans, and builds national and local capacity under the MAB framework. It combines ecosystem restoration, biodiversity monitoring, and climate resilience measures with community-based economic development, targeting women and youth through sustainable value chains and cooperative support. planEntities.name: UNDP-Projet d'appui au leadership national en faveur de solutions durables et de promotion de l'intégration locale, du retour volontaire et de la cohésion sociale en République centrafricaine
planEntities.parentName: Les institutions nationales sont dotées de capacités pour assurer la fourniture de services de qualité et innovants, et favoriser une gouvernance inclusive, redevable et efficace
planEntities.description:
La République Centrafricaine (RCA) fait face à des défis profondément enracinés liés à la fragilité, au conflit et à la violence, résultant de la faible cohésion sociale, d’un contrat social fragile entre l’État et ses citoyens, des déséquilibres régionaux et de l’insuffisance des mesures pour répondre aux risques climatiques. La crise du déplacement, provoquée par les conflits militaires, la peur des abus et les catastrophes naturelles telles que les inondations, a laissé 514 547 personnes déplacées, dont 40 % en situation de déplacement prolongé. Cette crise aggrave les pressions sur l'accès déjà limité aux services de base et aux moyens de subsistance, alimentant souvent les tensions entre les personnes déplacées à l'intérieur du pays (PDI) et les communautés hôtes. Les violences basées sur le genre, en particulier contre les femmes et les filles déplacées, demeurent une préoccupation majeure, soulignant davantage la nécessité de solutions inclusives et holistiques. 

En réponse, le Gouvernement, sous la direction du ministère de l’Action Humanitaire et de la Réconciliation Nationale (MAHRN), a lancé la Stratégie Nationale sur les Solutions Durables (2023–2027), mettant l’accent sur une coordination renforcée, une planification fondée sur des données probantes et l’intégration des personnes déplacées dans les communautés hôtes. Ce projet s’aligne sur cette stratégie à travers trois résultats interconnectés : le renforcement du leadership national et de la coordination des solutions durables, la promotion de l’intégration locale durable des PDI à Bria par l’accès au logement, aux services et aux moyens de subsistance, et la promotion de la cohésion sociale et de la paix entre les PDI et les communautés hôtes. Guidé par des approches sensibles aux conflits et inspiré par des pratiques locales réussies, le projet vise à s’attaquer aux causes profondes, à faire progresser les solutions durables et à soutenir les efforts de consolidation de la paix et de développement en RCA.

planEntities.name: UNDP-Enhancing Stabilization and Strengthening Social Cohesion through the rehabilitation of basic infrastructures provision of livelihood support, and activities to promote peace and social cohesion in the Central African Republic]
planEntities.parentName: Les personnes en situation de vulnérabilité en milieu urbain et rural disposent des capacités en vue de leur autonomisation économique
planEntities.description:
Suite à la cérémonie de lancement du projet en novembre 2023, celui-ci a débuté par la passation de marchés pour les activités de construction. Dès le premier semestre de 2024, le PNUD a réalisé des avancées significatives en posant les bases de son projet à travers l'engagement avec les communautés locales et les parties prenantes. Les processus de passation de marchés essentiels pour la construction ont été achevés, offrant ainsi une assise solide aux objectifs du projet. Des consultations initiales ont été organisées pour définir clairement le périmètre des activités, garantissant que les efforts s'alignent avec ceux des autres partenaires. 

À mesure que l'année avançait, le projet a gagné en élan, lançant avec succès plusieurs activités d'infrastructure. La construction d'un bâtiment administratif public, de deux écoles et d'un centre de dialogue pour les femmes et la communauté a débuté, tous conçus pour répondre aux besoins de la communauté. En avril 2024, le premier déploiement de dix enseignants à Sam-Ouandja a eu lieu, suivi d'un atelier de préparation organisé le 21 mars 2024 en collaboration avec le ministère de l’Éducation pour informer les acteurs sur le projet et ses orientations.  

Le projet a également réalisé une analyse initiale des conflits, engageant la communauté par le biais de séances en octobre 2023 et en mai 2024, en collaboration avec les autorités locales et d'autres partenaires. En mai 2024, une formation de deux jours axés sur la médiation des conflits communautaires et la lutte contre les discours de haine et la violence basée sur le genre (VBG) a rassemblé 115 participants (49 hommes et 66 femmes). Cette formation a sensibilisé sur la VBG et ses formes, permettant aux participants d'aborder ces problématiques efficacement tout en mettant en avant la vulnérabilité des femmes et des filles et en fournissant des conseils pratiques sur la confidentialité et le respect. Dans l'ensemble, l'initiative a favorisé l'appropriation locale et visait à réduire les facteurs de conflit et à renforcer la cohésion sociale. 

À l'approche du dernier trimestre de 2024, le PNUD CAR a intensifié ses efforts d'acquisition, finalisant la plupart des processus et les contrats pour les activités de construction restantes d'ici début décembre. Cette poussée a considérablement amélioré le taux d'dépense du projet, le portant à environ 68 %, y compris les conclusions des contrats pour la construction. En octobre 2024, le PNUD a fait des progrès dans le domaine de l'éducation en déployant 23 enseignants pour l'année scolaire 2024-202. Cette initiative a été accueillie avec enthousiasme par la communauté, les autorités locales exprimant leur gratitude envers KOICA et le PNUD pour leur engagement. 

Le PNUD CAR envisage également de collaborer avec des ONG locales pour mettre en œuvre diverses activités de soutien. Celles-ci comprennent l'aide matérielle aux agriculteurs, la formation professionnelle, des programmes de travaux rémunérés, et des sessions de développement des capacités axées sur la gestion des infrastructures. Le premier processus de recrutement pour ces activités, organisé au cours du deuxième trimestre de 2024, a entraîné une reformulation des termes de référence pour s'aligner sur les normes du PNUD, actuellement en cours de révision au siège. La finalisation du recrutement est prévue pour février 2025, avec des activités qui devraient durer huit mois. 

En conclusion, bien que le projet progresse bien, il est légèrement en retard par rapport au calendrier initial. Des efforts constants sont déployés pour surmonter les défis et assurer la mise en œuvre réussie de toutes les activités prévues, renforçant ainsi l'engagement d'améliorer les communautés locales à l’achèvement du projet. En parallèle, la discussion pour l'extension de la période du projet de 6 mois avec le donateur est en cours.

planEntities.name: UNDP-Modernisation de la Gestion de l’état civil et des services judicaires en faveur de la population locale à Bossangoa
planEntities.parentName: Les collectivités locales disposent de capacités pour promouvoir le développement local
planEntities.description:
Le projet de modernisation de la gestion de l’état civil à Bossangoa intervient dans un contexte marqué par des décennies de conflits ayant gravement affecté les infrastructures et les services publics essentiels, notamment l’état civil.  Les documents d'état civil déterminent l'accès aux services de base, y compris les services de santé, l'éducation, les opportunités économiques, les formalités liées à la mobilité à l'intérieur ou à l'extérieur du pays, l'accès aux services financiers, l'exercice des droits civiques et politiques en tant que candidat ou électeur aux élections locales et nationales, ou la possibilité d'être éligible pour représenter des groupes d'intérêt spécifiques.  

Les documents tels que les actes de naissance permettent également d'accéder à d'autres documents administratifs sans lesquels un Centrafricain ne peut jouir de tous ses droits. Par ailleurs, dans un contexte de fragilité comme en République Centrafricaine, la réintégration socio-économique des retournés, des rapatriés, des personnes déplacés internes, les ex-combattants, des minorités est entravée par le manque de documents d'état civil ; ce qui augmente le sentiment d’exclusion/marginalisation. En définitive, l’absence de l’enregistrement ou de la régularisation d’acte d’état civil demeure une menace au rétablissement de la cohésion sociale et de la paix durable en RCA.  

Les objectifs du projet sont de renforcer l’accès équitable aux documents d’état civil pour les groupes marginalisés, de restaurer la confiance entre l’État et les citoyens, et de promouvoir la cohésion sociale en améliorant la transparence et l’efficacité des services publics. Les résultats attendus incluent la réhabilitation des infrastructures de la mairie et du Tribunal de Grande Instance (TGI), le renforcement des capacités des agents d’état civil, et une augmentation significative des enregistrements d’état civil grâce à des mécanismes inclusifs, des campagnes de sensibilisation et des audiences foraines.

planEntities.name: Appui aux initiatives entrepreneuriales et communautaires de conservation et de tourisme durable autour des sites naturels du patrimoine mondial en RCA
planEntities.parentName: L’exploitation des ressources naturelles est améliorée grâce aux pratiques économiques innovantes et durables
planEntities.description:
Le Parc national du Manovo-Gounda St Floris, inscrit au patrimoine mondial en 1988, est sur la Liste du patrimoine mondial en péril depuis 1997 en raison de menaces telles que le braconnage, l'insécurité, la transhumance, l'exploitation minière artisanale et un manque de gestion. Son état de conservation a été examiné lors de la 45e session élargie du Comité du patrimoine mondial à Riyad en septembre 2023. Ce parc, riche en biodiversité, fait face à des défis liés à l'utilisation non durable et illégale de ses ressources naturelles.

Les initiatives communautaires en matière d'entrepreneuriat axées sur la conservation et le tourisme durable créent des opportunités de revenus alternatifs, renforçant ainsi la résilience des communautés et l'économie locale. Elles possèdent donc un potentiel significatif pour améliorer l'efficacité des efforts de conservation et faire face aux menaces qui pèsent sur l'environnement. Les petites et moyennes entreprises jouent un rôle essentiel dans la promotion de la durabilité environnementale de ces sites, tout en contribuant directement au développement social et économique inclusif et au bien-être des populations locales grâce à l'amélioration de leurs conditions de vie.

Le gouvernement centrafricain, en collaboration avec l'UNESCO, lance un projet pilote pour soutenir les initiatives entrepreneuriales communautaires visant à conserver ses deux sites du patrimoine mondial. Ce projet s'inscrit dans une démarche globale de protection et de conservation du patrimoine, tout en répondant aux besoins environnementaux, sociaux et économiques actuels et futurs. « Accompagnement des initiatives entrepreneuriales et communautaires centrées sur la préservation et le tourisme durable autour du Parc national du Manovo-Gounda St Floris, inscrits au patrimoine mondial en République Centrafricaine ».


Objectifs 

L'objectif principal est de renforcer les initiatives communautaires d'entrepreneuriat en conservation et tourisme durable autour du Parc national du Manovo-Gounda St Floris, inscrits au patrimoine mondial. 
Cela implique de mettre en réseau des associations locales et des entrepreneurs, de renforcer leurs capacités, et de soutenir les efforts communautaires pour la conservation et le développement durable via des subventions, tout en adoptant une approche basée sur les droits.

planEntities.name: « Projet d’appui à la production et à la diffusion des ressources éducatives pour les établissements scolaires et les élèves du primaire et du secondaire en Afrique subsaharienne francophone », mis en œuvre par l’UNESCO et financé par l’Agence française de Développement (AFD)
planEntities.parentName: Les institutions nationales sont dotées de capacités pour assurer la fourniture de services de qualité et innovants, et favoriser une gouvernance inclusive, redevable et efficace
planEntities.description:
Conformément à l’agenda 2030 (ODD4) et à la stratégie 2063 de l’Union Africaine, les pays d’Afrique francophone se sont engagés à transformer l’éducation et à agir sur les différents leviers à leur disposition pour répondre à ce qui est communément désignée comme la « crise de l’apprentissage ». Face aux défis majeurs auxquels la région fait face dans le domaine de l’éducation, la mise à disposition de ressources éducatives de qualité et en nombre suffisant, adaptées aux curricula et aux besoins des apprenants est l’une des réponses pour améliorer la qualité du système éducatif. Les ressources éducatives désignent un ensemble de supports et outils utilisés dans le processus d’apprentissage pour faciliter l’acquisition de connaissances et de compétences, en favorisant l’engagement et l’interaction des apprenants. Elles sont définies selon six catégories : les manuels scolaires, le guide pédagogique, le matériel didactique, les ressources pédagogiques, les ressources pédagogiques numériques et les ressources éducatives libres. 

Bien que le rôle déterminant des ressources éducatives pour la qualité des acquis scolaires soit largement connu, peu de plans sectoriels s’attachent à détailler les ambitions et les moyens mis au service de leur production, leur acquisition, leur acheminement et l’accompagnement de leur utilisation. 

Ainsi, le gouvernement centrafricain a mené, dans le cadre du « Projet d’appui à la production et à la diffusion des ressources éducatives pour les établissements scolaires et les élèves du primaire et du secondaire en Afrique subsaharienne francophone », mis en œuvre par l’UNESCO et financé par l’Agence française de Développement (AFD), une analyse diagnostique de la situation des ressources éducatives en République centrafricaine (RCA). Le rapport de cette analyse a été restitué et validé lors d’un atelier organisé le 14 mars 2025 à Bangui. Le rapport recommande notamment à la RCA de finaliser sa politique du livre et d’étendre son champ aux ressources éducatives.

planEntities.name: Programme d’Appui à la Préservation de la Biodiversité et des Écosystèmes dans les Reserves des Biospheres en République centrafricaine (RCA)
planEntities.parentName: Les capacités nationales sont renforcées pour une meilleure intégration des aspects environnementaux dans les politiques de développement
planEntities.description:
Domaine thématique 1. Des écosystèmes restaurés et protégés pour améliorer la biodiversité et les services écosystémiques, Domaine thématique 2. Intégration effective de la biodiversité dans les politiques, les réglementations, la planification et les stratégies et Domaine thématique 3. Amélioration de l'utilisation durable de la biodiversité
La mise en œuvre des AME est sous la responsabilité du Ministère de l’Environnement et du Développement Durable, représentant la communauté internationale en matière d'environnement. Toutefois, l'élaboration et le début de l'implémentation de la SNPA-DB entre 2000 et 2003 ont été réalisés par le Ministère des Eaux, Forêts, Chasse et Pêche, qui était en charge de l’Environnement avant sa séparation en 2003. À l'époque de la création de la SNPA-DB, ce ministère avait un large champ d'intervention, lui conférant des prérogatives pour atteindre directement certains objectifs stratégiques et opérationnels.
Le Ministère de l’Environnement, axé sur « Environnement et Développement Durable », dépend souvent d'autres ministères pour mettre en œuvre des actions concrètes. La conservation de la biodiversité est encadrée par la politique forestière et la gestion de la faune, tandis que les ressources phytogénétiques et zoogénétiques relèvent des politiques agricoles et d'élevage. De plus, la recherche sur la biodiversité est intégrée dans la Politique Nationale de la Recherche Scientifique et de l’Innovation Technologique.
La conservation en République centrafricaine est réalisée à travers sept types d'Aires Protégées, incluant des Parcs nationaux, des Réserves naturelles intégrales, des Réserves de faune, des Réserves spéciales, des Forêts classées, des Jardins botaniques et des Réserves à usage cynégétique. Ces aires couvrent 18,7% du territoire national depuis 2020, représentant une superficie totale de 112,827 km², soit 18,06% de la zone terrestre totale de 624,568 km². Les différences de superficie proviennent des variations dans les estimations du territoire national.
La diversité biologique est cruciale pour la République Centrafricaine (RCA), contribuant significativement au PIB, notamment à travers le secteur primaire qui inclut la cueillette des produits forestiers non ligneux, la chasse, la pêche, le tourisme cynégétique, le bois énergie, l'agriculture et l'élevage. En 2020, ce secteur, dépendant du climat, représentait plus de 40% du PIB, avec l'agriculture vivrière et l'élevage comme principales activités. Cependant, la diversité biologique de la RCA fait face à des menaces, principalement dues à l'ignorance, à l'extrême pauvreté et à l'incivisme. Les principales menaces sur la diversité biologique en Centrafrique incluent les feux de brousse, les défrichements agricoles, l'exploitation industrielle et artisanale du bois, le braconnage, le non-respect des couloirs de transhumance, l'exploitation minière pour le diamant et l'or, les changements climatiques, ainsi que l'accumulation de déchets solides autour des grandes villes.
Les menaces environnementales entraînent des impacts tels que la fragmentation et la déforestation, la perte de biodiversité et de résilience des écosystèmes, la surexploitation des espèces, ainsi que des fluctuations démographiques et des changements dans la composition des communautés.
L'objectif de ce projet est d'agir ensemble en s'appuyant sur des objectifs et des cibles communs à l'échelle internationale. Cela permettra de suivre efficacement les efforts de chacun dans la mise en œuvre de la Convention sur la Diversité Biologique et de mesurer et comparer les résultats dans un même cadre temporel.

planEntities.name: The Government implements the national DDR program in a coherent and timely approach and alternative disarmament initiatives are discouraged
planEntities.parentName: Les éléments des groupes armés sont désarmés et pris en charge dans les programmes de réintégration socio-économiques et communautaires
planEntities.description: During the reporting period, significant progress was made in the disarmament and reintegration of former armed group members. Individuals identified and disarmed through established procedures were systematically enrolled in socio‑economic and community‑based reintegration programs, including psychosocial support, vocational training, income‑generating activities, and community engagement initiatives that promote social cohesion. At the same time, the Government continued to implement the national DDR program in a coordinated and timely manner, ensuring alignment with national stabilization priorities. Strengthened institutional communication and improved multisectoral coordination helped discourage parallel or informal disarmament initiatives, thereby consolidating efforts within a unified national framework and enhancing the overall effectiveness and sustainability of reintegration interventions.

planEntities.name: Space for spoilers in the peace process is reduced
planEntities.parentName: Les éléments des groupes armés sont désarmés et pris en charge dans les programmes de réintégration socio-économiques et communautaires
planEntities.description: During the reporting period, the space for spoilers in the peace process was significantly reduced as MINUSCA supported the Government in advancing the implementation of the Djamena Agreement and consolidating commitments under the APPR. Through sustained logistical, security, and technical support to UEPNDDRR, disarmament and demobilization operations were successfully conducted in Maloum, Bambari, Koui, and Sanguere‑lim, resulting in the disarmament of 569 combatants—including 3 women—and the collection of more than 400 weapons, while civil‑military activities contributed to rebuilding trust with local populations. By 30 September 2025, a cumulative total of 5,779 combatants, including 350 women, had been disarmed and demobilized since 2018, representing over 80 percent of the DDRR programme’s target. These achievements, combined with the renewed commitment of major armed groups such as 3R and UPC, significantly curtailed the operational space for spoilers, strengthened confidence in the peace process, and accelerated progress toward durable stabilization and reintegration outcomes.

planEntities.name: The Government implements security sector reform and guarantees the professional nature and democratic accountability of internal defence and security forces
planEntities.parentName: Les institutions de l’État sont renforcées pour garantir le déploiement effectif et l’accès aux services de justice de qualité, et d’assurer la promotion et la protection des droits humains
planEntities.description: During the reporting period, the Government advanced key outputs related to security sector reform and institutional strengthening. Progress included the consolidation of the Military Programming Law (2026–2030), reinforced by targeted capacity‑building for 71 officers and NCOs, and inspections that reached 160 FACA personnel to improve discipline and regulatory compliance. Democratic oversight was strengthened through enhanced IGAN capacities and structured engagement with parliamentary committees. The approval of the Border Infrastructure and Equipment Master Plan further contributed to improved governance and operational planning. Complementary coordination with international partners supported defence governance reforms and the deployment of the Chad–CAR Joint Force. Efforts to reactivate the Bouar and Bangui military tribunals also advanced, contributing to improved access to justice and stronger accountability mechanisms. Collectively, these actions contributed to more professional, accountable, and rights‑respecting defence and security institutions.

- Desarrollo de capacidades institucionales y de equipos técnicos para el fortalecimiento de la aplicación del enfoque de género e interseccional en políticas y programas .

- Integración del enfoque de género y vulnerabilidades en instrumentos de gestión climática y promoción del rol de las mujeres como agente de resiliencia y gestión sostenible de la biodiversidad.

planEntities.description: La EDS y la ECC son claves para preparar a las personas para responder a los desafíos de la triple crisis planetaria (cambio climático, pérdida de biodiversidad y contaminación ambiental). En ese contexto, las comunidades que son parte o viven, trabajan en lugares que cuentan con la denominación de Reserva de la Biósfera son clave como espacios de conservación, educación e investigación, dado los enormes impactos que han tenido diversas amenazas naturales y antropogénicas como por ejemplo los incendios estacionales en la Región de Valparaíso. En respuesta a ello, y basado en un piloto implementado por la UNESCO en la RB Archipiélago de Juan Fernández en 2023, se estará trabajando en el desarrollo de una guía metodológica y práctica para el trabajo contextualizado al territorio bajo la premisa de que las personas no protegen lo que no conocen y, por otro, que para transformar la educación, las comunidades tienen que aprender lo que viven y vivir lo que aprenden. Este trabajo además contribuye al establecimiento del SBAP en Chile.
