planEntities.name: 70 MMR staff members received in house and off job training
planEntities.parentName: Capacity of public sector is strengthened to develop strategies and policies for enterprise, job creation and employment.
planEntities.description: A total of 20 staff members have been trained through special international courses, enhancing their skills and expertise. Additionally, 70 staff members from MMR received both in-house and off-job training, focusing on developing their technical capacity in the fish value chain. Furthermore, 50 fishers have been trained in essential skills such as engine mechanics, boat skipping, and refrigeration. These initiatives are complemented by the ongoing digitalization of institutional working systems, which aims to improve efficiency and effectiveness across operations.

planEntities.name: Promotion of agribusiness ventures
planEntities.parentName: Skills and capacity of people, especially women and youth, are improved for increased access to diversified livelihoods and employability
planEntities.description: The promotion of agribusiness ventures is a key focus, alongside efforts to introduce improved stoves in rural households, which aim to enhance energy efficiency and sustainability. Additionally, the procurement of equipment and materials for the ex situ conservation of animal genetic resources is underway, supported by technical assistance for establishing these conservation initiatives. To further support agricultural research, infrastructure for sorting, extraction, curing, and packaging vegetable and fruit seeds is being constructed at a designated research station. A mini-postharvest research laboratory is also being built in Halhale, along with the construction of another new mini laboratory. Furthermore, trials on bio-pesticides and fungicides are being conducted to explore sustainable pest management solutions. These initiatives collectively contribute to the enhancement of agricultural practices and resource conservation.

planEntities.name: Equip Agri Statistics office at HQ and Zobas as well as front line extension officers with essential data collection  tools,
planEntities.parentName: Skills and capacity of people, especially women and youth, are improved for increased access to diversified livelihoods and employability
planEntities.description: Efforts are underway to equip the Agri Statistics office at headquarters and in Zobas, as well as frontline extension officers, with essential data collection tools. This initiative includes conducting surveys, data collection, and analysis, alongside carrying out an agricultural census to gather vital information. To strengthen human resources, staff upgrading opportunities for MSc and PhD programs, as well as short-term training abroad, are being implemented. Additionally, scientific visits to research stations are encouraged to foster knowledge exchange and collaboration development with regional laboratories and research institutions. The procurement of laboratory equipment, general materials, reagents, chemicals, facilities, and consumables is also prioritized to enhance research capabilities. Furthermore, the maintenance of the vaccine production laboratory and laboratory buildings, as well as the service and maintenance of laboratory equipment, are essential for ensuring operational efficiency. Finally, efforts are being made to rehabilitate the Ghinda regional laboratory, further supporting the advancement of agricultural research and statistics.

planEntities.name: Procurement of irrigation infrastructure maintenance supplies and field tools
planEntities.parentName: Skills and capacity of people, especially women and youth, are improved for increased access to diversified livelihoods and employability
planEntities.description: The procurement of irrigation infrastructure maintenance supplies and field tools is essential for ensuring the longevity and efficiency of agricultural operations. This includes the acquisition of spare parts and maintenance supplies, as well as the supply, installation, and commissioning of three automatic weather stations. Additionally, laboratory equipment and chemical reagents are being procured to support various agricultural functions. To ensure high standards, a seed quality control and certification system is being established, along with a national pest surveillance system. Technical assistance is also being provided to develop a registration system for animal drugs and biologics. Furthermore, office facilities are being procured for four existing and eight new animal quarantine stations, accompanied by necessary lab equipment and chemical reagents. Efforts are underway to develop an agro-mapping and agro-geospatial information system, as well as an agriculture market information system. Lastly, the procurement of equipment and materials aimed at expanding the agricultural innovation system will further enhance the sector's overall productivity and resilience.

planEntities.name: Maintenance of seed conditioning and processing plants
planEntities.parentName: Skills and capacity of people, especially women and youth, are improved for increased access to diversified livelihoods and employability
planEntities.description: Efforts are underway to maintain seed conditioning and processing plants, ensuring they operate at optimal efficiency. This includes the procurement of mobile seed conditioning and processing machines, as well as a chips-making machine. Additionally, small-scale fruit peeling, drying, and processing machines are being purchased to support local food production. The procurement of vitro plants will enhance the propagation of high-quality crops, while both expendable and non-expendable items are being acquired to support various agricultural functions. In vitro multiplication is being implemented for seed potatoes, bananas, sweet potatoes, date palms, and aloe vera, promoting diverse agricultural outputs. Furthermore, new materials for various staple crop seeds are being introduced, accompanied by experiments and trials to assess their viability. Foundation seed production is also a priority, along with ongoing trials on bio-pesticides and fungicides to explore sustainable pest management solutions.

planEntities.name: Develop Recipes and complementary foods from aquatic foods
planEntities.parentName: Skills and capacity of people, especially women and youth, are improved for increased access to diversified livelihoods and employability
planEntities.description:
Initiatives are being launched to develop recipes and complementary foods derived from aquatic sources, enhancing nutritional options for communities. A Social Behavior Communication Change (SBCC) strategy is being crafted to encourage increased fish consumption among households and communities. As part of this effort, procurement of aquatic food packaging and labeling materials is essential to promote these products effectively. Nutrition materials and equipment are also being acquired to support these initiatives, alongside a comprehensive fish consumption survey to gather valuable data.

In addition, new parameters are being introduced for research, including analyzing shelf life, assessing seaweed, and cultivating various purpose-driven microbes. To improve local fish distribution, procurement of eight ready-made retail fish shops and five solar-powered refrigerated fish transporting trucks is underway. The construction of ten solar-powered ice-producing facilities will further enhance fish preservation and quality.

Moreover, the procurement of 20 long line drum haulers and complete long line fishing gear for artisanal boats will support local fishermen. Plans include establishing fish drying facilities and renovating existing fish processing facilities to improve operational efficiency. Additional procurement of fishing inputs, the erection of ice plants, and the acquisition of water trucks are all part of a comprehensive approach to enhance the fishing industry. Finally, hatcheries are being established to support sustainable fish production and resource management.

planEntities.name: Introduction of Sexed bull semen and conduct mass insemination
planEntities.parentName: Access to finance, productive assets, technology, infrastructure, and equipment is increased, in support of sustainable livelihood
planEntities.description:
The introduction of sexed bull semen is set to improve breeding efficiency, accompanied by mass insemination efforts to enhance livestock quality. Additionally, the purchase of backyard parent stock chicks will support local poultry production. To bolster veterinary services, equipment and materials are being procured for 73 veterinary clinics across six Zobas, ensuring that these facilities are well-equipped to serve livestock health needs.

Veterinary drugs and vaccines are also being purchased to maintain animal health and prevent disease outbreaks. For beekeepers in two Zobas, two honey processing plants will be acquired to enhance honey production and processing capabilities. Furthermore, procurement of ewes and rams will aid in the improvement of sheep breeding programs. Research will be conducted on breed selection, feeding practices, and health management to optimize livestock productivity.

Supplementary feed purchases are planned to ensure that animals receive adequate nutrition. Additionally, the procurement of Begait cattle and H. Friesian bulls will diversify and improve the genetic stock available to farmers, while the purchase of medicaments will support the overall health and productivity of livestock. These initiatives collectively aim to enhance the resilience and efficiency of the livestock sector.

planEntities.name: Procurement of farm tools and implements procured (Procurement of farm tools and implements procured (line level, rope, range pole, Pick Axe, Crow bar, Sledge hammer)
planEntities.parentName: Capacity of public sector is strengthened to develop strategies and policies for enterprise, job creation and employment.
planEntities.description: This includes the procurement of essential farm tools and implements such as line levels, ropes, range poles, pick axes, crow bars, and sledge hammers. Additionally, the purchase or production of organic fertilizer supports soil health. Key infrastructural projects like the construction of micro dams and the supply, installation, commissioning, and training of solar pumps are vital for efficient water management. The implementation of the Sememo and Merhano irrigation schemes, along with the installation of six additional drip irrigation sites, enhances irrigation capacity. A detailed study of six existing irrigation schemes will provide insights for future improvements. Moreover, the proper disposal of unwanted veterinary drugs and biologics, along with obsolete pesticides and their containers, is essential for environmental safety.

planEntities.name: Introduce fishing boat license number plate
planEntities.parentName: Skills and capacity of people, especially women and youth, are improved for increased access to diversified livelihoods and employability
planEntities.description: To enhance fisheries management, an initiative is underway to introduce fishing boat license number plates, which will help in regulating and tracking fishing activities. In addition, efforts will be made to assess the biological and ecological information of selected Marine Protected Areas (MPAs) and create detailed maps to support conservation efforts. The procurement of an unmanned survey vehicle (USV) will facilitate advanced data collection and monitoring of aquatic environments. Furthermore, comprehensive fish stock assessments will be conducted to evaluate the health and sustainability of fish populations. These initiatives aim to improve the management and conservation of aquatic resources, ensuring long-term viability for fishing communities.

Ethiopia.name: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations
Ethiopia.organizationType: Multilateral - UN organizations excluding pooled funds

planEntities.name: Provide technical assistance for gender-transformative, nutrition-sensitive, adaptive, inclusive, and resilience-building social protection
planEntities.parentName: Strengthen national and sub national capacity of systems and communities including those that are left behind towards accessing gender-transformative, climate-resilient and shock-responsive social protection and social services
planEntities.description: This project provides comprehensive technical assistance to foster the inclusion of refugees and forcibly displaced populations within national social protection systems. It promotes a human rights-based, lifecycle approach to programming that is adaptive, child-sensitive, gender-transformative, disability-inclusive, climate-resilient, and shock-responsive. A core component is the generation of evidence to inform government budgeting for social services and to evaluate Cash Plus programmes, including Child Grant pilots and financial inclusion interventions, while also developing related manuals for national safety net implementation. Furthermore, the project includes UN-led capacity building at national and sub-national levels to strengthen government ownership, institutional systems, and community participation, specifically to scale up and ensure the sustainability of school feeding programmes.

planEntities.name: Increase the proportion of smallholder farmers, agro-pastoralists, and pastoralists accessing and adopting climate-resilient inputs, technology, or good practices across the food supply chain to enhance productivity and competitiveness
planEntities.parentName: Improved access and adoption of inputs, technologies and practices for the production of nutrient dense food and an inclusive and resilient food system
planEntities.description: This sub-output aims to enhance productivity and competitiveness by expanding smallholder, agro-pastoralist and pastoralist access to improved inputs, climate-smart technologies, digital solutions, post-harvest innovations, and One Health–related laboratory and surveillance services. Efforts will focus on strengthening production, storage, processing, and market functions through technologies and practices that improve efficiency, quality, and resilience in the food supply chain. The sub-output will also support initiatives to promote awareness, demand creation and consumption to enhance the 'farm to folk' principle.

planEntities.name: Support effective agri-food system service delivery through strengthened institutional systems and workforce capacities
planEntities.parentName: Improved access and adoption of inputs, technologies and practices for the production of nutrient dense food and an inclusive and resilient food system
planEntities.description: This sub-output focuses on improving capacities across institutions, systems, and value-chain actors to deliver high-quality, inclusive and resilient agri-food services. It includes strengthening surveillance systems, food safety and quality management capacities, and workforce development using a One Health approach, ensuring that public and private actors have the skills, infrastructure and coordination mechanisms needed for effective implementation. The sub-output will also support and strengthen existing structures, especially at lower level to enhance collaboration in delivery of multisectoral nutrition sensitive interventions.

planEntities.name: Produce and implement evidence-based policy reforms and national frameworks for increased public and private sector investments
planEntities.parentName: Improved access and adoption of inputs, technologies and practices for the production of nutrient dense food and an inclusive and resilient food system
planEntities.description: This sub-output supports the implementation of key policy reforms and national food-systems initiatives by generating evidence, developing regional investment plans, conducting investment forums, and promoting regulatory frameworks for food safety, traceability, nutrition, and value addition. It aims to improve public and private sector incentives, strengthen governance structures, and accelerate inclusive and market-oriented agricultural transformation.

planEntities.name: Promote and mobilize innovative financing and de-risking mechanisms to increase access to finance for food systems actors
planEntities.parentName: Improved access and adoption of inputs, technologies and practices for the production of nutrient dense food and an inclusive and resilient food system
planEntities.description: This sub-output seeks to increase the availability of priority commodities—such as those under the Yelimat Tirufat initiative—by expanding access to affordable and inclusive financing options for actors across selected value chains. It promotes the use of blended finance, insurance schemes, credit guarantees, and other de-risking instruments to unlock capital, reduce risk exposure, and stimulate investment by both public and private actors.

planEntities.name: Increase access to market information modalities for producers through reliable, functional and updated information systems
planEntities.parentName: Improved access and adoption of inputs, technologies and practices for the production of nutrient dense food and an inclusive and resilient food system
planEntities.description: This sub-output aims to enhance the availability, quality, and usability of Market Information Systems (MIS) to support better production and marketing decisions by farmers, cooperatives, SMEs, women and youth. It includes strengthening linkages between producers and markets, improving information flow across input and output markets, and promoting digital and inclusive access pathways for underserved groups.

planEntities.name: Monitoring and reporting systems established, and technical capacity strengthened to track biodiversity, land degradation, ecosystems restoration, and land-use changes, and associated CO2 emissions removal/reduction outcomes
planEntities.parentName: Enhanced sustainable natural resources management
planEntities.description: Establish monitoring systems to track biodiversity, land degradation, and restoration outcomes, providing reliable data to guide evidence-based decision-making and natural resource management (NRM) policy implementation; Provide technical support on national REDD+ and MRV capacity consolidation and strengthening as well as enabling biennial transparency reports preparation through Ethiopian Forest Development and MoPD respectively and make national forest monitoring/MRV system fully functional to monitor change of Ethiopian forest cover and reduction in CO2 emission to submit quality reports to UNFCCC.

planEntities.name: Strengthening Resilience of Disaster Affected Communities through Durable Solutions in Oromia and Somali Regions of Ethiopia
planEntities.parentName: Strengthened institutions, systems and mechanisms to promote peace, prevent conflict, effectively address root causes of conflict and implement post-conflict rehabilitation efforts
planEntities.description: The IDSF JP aims to strengthen durable solutions impact in Ethiopia, b  (1) Promoting effective strategies development, coordination, implementation and monitoring of internal displacement solutions at national and regional level including displacement solutions financing; (2)   Strengthening national leadership and building the capacity of key Government Ministries and Departments to promote solutions to internal displacement including through local solutions capacity assessments in line with the new IASC/UNSDG joint Guidance on Solutions to Internal Displacement; (3) Ensuring government, coordination bodies, and partners have improved access to robust data to help inform DS programming and strategy development at the national and sub-national levels.  Above 100,000 individuals will benefit from the programme across the project locations.

planEntities.name: Generate, provide and support the implementation of macroeconomic or fiscal recommendations for policy dialogue and advocacy of improved public investments in human capital
planEntities.parentName: Strengthened economic governance, institutional capacity, and macroeconomic management
planEntities.description:
These recommendations will be generated from different sources: 
- These recommendations will be generated from analyses including budget briefs, medium term revenue and expenditure planning, etc. 
- Technical support provided to the Minitry of Finance on the implementation of the public finance management (PFM) strategy and
- Technical support provided at the sub-national level on domestic resource mobilization
- Through analyses of public agricultural expenditures and price incentives targeting the effective operationalization of national food-security, nutrition, and agricultural-transformation policies

planEntities.name: Advance the empowerment of women, youth, persons with disabilities and marginalized groups through joint program "Strengthen Markets for Agriculture to Build Resilience and Transform  Food Systems in Ethiopia (SMART- Food Systems)
planEntities.parentName: Improved access and adoption of inputs, technologies and practices for the production of nutrient dense food and an inclusive and resilient food system
planEntities.description:
The SMART Food Systems Transformation Project is a joint WFP–FAO initiative funded under the SDG Fund to strengthen regional food systems governance, market integration, and climate-resilient livelihoods in Ethiopia. The project supports regions—especially Somali and Sidama—to operationalize the EFSTN Food System Councils, improve coordination across the 7 Food System Clusters, and link regional work to the national roadmap.

On the ground, the project helps improve production, post-harvest management, value-addition, and market linkages for smallholder farmers, while ensuring stronger engagement of cooperatives, private sector actors, and government bureaus. It also promotes better data, planning, and investment alignment across agriculture, markets, nutrition, and climate adaptation.

planEntities.name: Deliver integrated livelihoods, financial and resilience support for vulnerable communities
planEntities.parentName: Strengthened policy, systems, institutional capacity and access to finance, markets and technology to create decent and inclusive jobs
planEntities.description:
The UN will implement targeted interventions for vulnerable groups, linking immediate livelihood needs with long-term resilience. These include:
- Strengthening the national biodiversity financing framework.
- Deploying e-voucher systems and improving access to livelihood services.
- Providing targeted training and grants for conflict-affected female MSME owners.
- Conducting gender-responsive market assessments and awareness campaigns.
- Developing durable solutions strategies and providing livelihood support to IDPs.
- Expanding finance and insurance for smallholder farmers.
- Strengthening local capacity via training and input provision using e-vouchers.
- Supporting MSMEs with insurance product development and business services.
- Providing grants and training for climate-smart, women-led businesses.

planEntities.parentName: Improved access and adoption of inputs, technologies and practices for the production of nutrient dense food and an inclusive and resilient food system
planEntities.description: People in Ethiopia, especially vulnerable and marginalized groups, benefit from inclusive, resilient, and sustainable economic growth through increased access to financial services for poultry farmers, SMEs, and other value chain actors, and strengthened capacity of local institutions and stakeholders to lead and implement poultry value chain development.

Facilitate the adoption of climate-smart, gender-responsive, and nature-based practices and technologies across households, cooperatives, enterprises, and communities, while engaging families and communities to promote collective climate action and resilience. Build the capacity of local governments to deliver gender-responsive services to farmers and pastoralists and promote private sector–led adoption of climate-smart solutions in SLA-targeted woredas through business appraisals, training, demonstration sites, and support to women’s groups. Complementary support continues being provided to rehabilitate community-based ecosystem and promote regenerative agropastoral practices (sustainable management of natural resources such as rangeland and water).

- Strengthening the national biodiversity financing framework.
- Deploying e-voucher systems and improving access to livelihood services.
- Providing targeted training and grants for conflict-affected female MSME owners.
- Conducting gender-responsive market assessments and awareness campaigns.
- Developing durable solutions strategies and providing livelihood support to IDPs.
- Expanding finance and insurance for smallholder farmers.
- Strengthening local capacity via training and input provision using e-vouchers.
- Supporting MSMEs with insurance product development and business services.
- Providing grants and training for climate-smart, women-led businesses.

planEntities.parentName: Strengthened institutions, systems and mechanisms to promote peace, prevent conflict, effectively address root causes of conflict and implement post-conflict rehabilitation efforts
planEntities.description: The overall goal of the project is to contribute to durable solutions through improved conditions for sustainable socio-economic recovery and peaceful co-existence of DAC with particular attention to most vulnerable groups while strengthening local government capacity in responding to the needs of internal displacement. The project targets seven Woredas and eight kebeles of Somali and Oromia regions and will benefit 54,396 displacement affected peoples. The project is jointly implemented by IOM, FAO, and UN Habitat.

planEntities.name: Leaving No One Behind - The Internal Displacement Solutions Fund (IDS Fund for Ethiopia
planEntities.parentName: Strengthened institutions, systems and mechanisms to promote peace, prevent conflict, effectively address root causes of conflict and implement post-conflict rehabilitation efforts
planEntities.description: The IDSF JP aims to strengthen durable solutions impact in Ethiopia, b  (1) Promoting effective strategies development, coordination, implementation and monitoring of internal displacement solutions at national and regional level including displacement solutions financing; (2)   Strengthening national leadership and building the capacity of key Government Ministries and Departments to promote solutions to internal displacement including through local solutions capacity assessments in line with the new IASC/UNSDG joint Guidance on Solutions to Internal Displacement; (3) Ensuring government, coordination bodies, and partners have improved access to robust data to help inform DS programming and strategy development at the national and sub-national levels.  Above 100,000 individuals will benefit from the programme across the project locations.

planEntities.name: EU IM3 Sustainable support to persons displaced by conflict and natural disasters and their host communities in Afar, Amhara, BSG and Tigray
planEntities.parentName: Strengthened institutions, systems and mechanisms to promote peace, prevent conflict, effectively address root causes of conflict and implement post-conflict rehabilitation efforts
planEntities.description: The overall objective of the Action is to reduce poverty and improve the health and well-being of internally displaced populations (IDPs) and host communities (HC), with an emphasis on man-made disasters and natural and climate hazards in Ethiopia. The proposed Action will enable conflict- and climate-induced IDPs and host communities to move towards recovery and resilience through a comprehensive and multisectoral area-based community development project. This will be achieved through three main objectives: (1)To improve the living conditions of IDPs and host communities through access to livelihoods, and financial support and economic opportunities; (2) To improve access to gender and disability sensitive Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WaSH) infrastructure and services for IDPs and host communities in targeted areas; (3) To strengthen social cohesion and protection services for IDPs and host community (focusing on women and people with disability) through an area-based, community based approach, supported by needs-based data collection and capacity building of relevant stakeholders.

planEntities.name: Support national capacity to implement the transitional justice policy including through the development of subsequent legislations and the establishment of gender responsive and inclusive institutions that meet human rights standards
planEntities.parentName: Strengthened institutions, systems and mechanisms to promote peace, prevent conflict, effectively address root causes of conflict and implement post-conflict rehabilitation efforts
planEntities.description: The overall objective is to ensure the institutions mandated to implement the transitional justice policy can fulfill their mandate and the population (including victims) can meaningfully engage with the process. The thematic focuses include: access to justice; documentation of violations; truth telling; gender equality; victims' empowerment, witness protection, capacity building for investigators and prosecutors. The beneficiaries are: a) institutions at national level (Ministry of Justice, plus new to-be-established institutions such as the Truth Commission, Special Bench etc) as well at selected institutions at regional level (e.g., branch offices of Truth Commission; Somali Truth Commission); b) civil society (victims, women, youth, IDPs etc) include (Continue the support to the witness protection)

planEntities.name: Support enabling environment for rights holders especially victims of SGBV/CRSV to exercise rights through access to justice
planEntities.parentName: Strengthened legal, policy, regulatory and accountability frameworks and institutions at all levels to ensure equitable access to justice and uphold the rule of law
planEntities.description:
The objective is the provision of emergency protection services, including prevention and response of CRSV/SGBV among returns, IDP and (vulnerable) host community women and girls in the Amhara; Tigray, including the contested areas. Specific cluster objectives are: -	
•	Identify the protection needs of women and girls: Through OHCHR’s monitoring, documentation and advocacy, this objective aligns with the humanitarian principle of “accountability to affected populations (AAP) and the broader principles of human rights and humanitarian action. 
•	Provision of emergency protection services: Ensure Support to affected women and girls through provision of emergency protection services including prevention and response of CRSV/GBV among IDP and host community women and girls in Amhara; Tigray, including the contested areas; Oromia and Southern Ethiopia regions.  
•	Raise awareness and build capacity: train service providers, duty bearers, community members, and humanitarian actors to identify and support the most vulnerable, prevent unintended harm and ensure safe, inclusive and accountable service. 
•	Fight impunity and advocate for justice: Focus on accountability efforts to uphold human rights and international humanitarian law committed.

planEntities.name: Strengthen the capacity of the National Human Rights Institution and other independent institutions to effectively undertake their role in the promotion and protection of human rights
planEntities.parentName: Enhanced capacities of institutions, CSOs and Citizens to promote and protect human rights including through strengthened civic engagement and expanded civic space
planEntities.description: The objective is to equip independent institutions with the necessary knowledge, skills and services to enable them to perform their mandates in line with international norms. Key thematic focuses differ depending on the target institution/beneficiary. Namely: for the EHRC, key thematic focuses include civic space, transitional justice, social and economic rights and human rights education. For NEBE: thematic focuses include development of a capable and sustainable electoral management body and strengthening of partnerships and collaboration with key electoral stakeholders; for the Ombudsman, thematic focuses include access to information; and for EMA thematic focuses include media monitoring, regulation and freedom of expression.

planEntities.name: Support the timely submission of state reports to human rights bodies and the implementation of recommendations.
planEntities.parentName: Enhanced capacities of institutions, CSOs and Citizens to promote and protect human rights including through strengthened civic engagement and expanded civic space
planEntities.description: The objective is to strengthen the capacity on one hand of the government (mainly MoJ and the Inter-Ministerial drafting committee called NMRF) to submit sound reports to Treaty Bodies, UPR Working Group etc and on the other hand support the implementation of actual recommendations. Thematic focuses include: justice, economic and social rights; non-discrimination; civic space etc. Beneficiaries are mainly government officials mandated with this tasks including members of the NMRF, Ministry of Justice, Ministry of Women and Social Affairs, Ministry of Education etc.

planEntities.name: Strengthen normative frameworks and institutional capacities to promote freedom of expression, access to information, press freedom, and information integrity
planEntities.parentName: Enhanced capacities of institutions, CSOs and Citizens to promote and protect human rights including through strengthened civic engagement and expanded civic space
planEntities.description: This sub output seeks to reinforce Ethiopia’s legal and institutional environment for freedom of expression, press freedom and access to information. Building on the country’s constitutional guarantees, it supports alignment of national laws and practices with international standards, while enhancing the capacity of key institutions including EMA, EHRC, EIO, and judicial actors, to uphold and implement these standards effectively. The intervention promotes mechanisms to safeguard information integrity and address disinformation through ethical media practices and multi-stakeholder dialogue among government, media, and civil society.

planEntities.name: Strengthen the capacities of the social service workforce and the case management systems to deliver quality child protection services for vulnerable children and populations at risk of GBV in development and humanitarian settings
planEntities.parentName: Strengthen national and sub national capacity of systems and communities including those that are left behind towards accessing gender-transformative, climate-resilient and shock-responsive social protection and social services
planEntities.description: Capacity strengthening will focus on frontline actors and community-based service providers to enhance the delivery of inclusive, shock-responsive social protection, child protection, and GBV prevention and response. This includes training and deployment of social workers and community service personnel, provision of case management services, and support for the implementation of digital case management systems such as CPMIS+. Capacity-building efforts will also target extension workers to improve the delivery of nutrition-sensitive social protection, shock-responsive social protection, child protection and prevention and response to GBV. Community feedback and response mechanisms will be reinforced to promote accountability, service quality, and responsiveness to the needs of vulnerable populations.

planEntities.description:
The overarching goal is to help establish essential foundations and institutional conditions necessary for fostering effective, peaceful, and constructive dialogue in Ethiopia. 
The project focuses on supporting the National Dialogue through ENDC, an initiative widely regarded as essential for addressing Ehtiopia's highly polarized political environment. It aims to foster inclusive discussion, reconcilation and consensus-building among diverse perspectives and interests on critical national issues.
The outcomes of the project benefit all citizens of Ethiopia, including the members of the diaspora communities.

planEntities.description:
The overall objective is to support the demobilization and reinsertion of the Ex-combatants back into their communities as civilians to build a lasting peace, enable reconciliation, and reinforce social cohesion.
The thematic focus of the project is demobilizing the Ex-combatants, ensure their reintegration into the communities through social and economic support , and focus on community recovery and development to support the reintegration.
The direct beneficiaries are 371,971 Ex-combatants.

planEntities.description:
Strengthening criminal justice institutions and judiciary deliver more effective, accountable, and gender-responsive public services. This includes support for legal aid services and targeted interventions to prevent, mitigate, and respond to sexual and gender-based violence (SGBV). Activities will focus on capacity building for justice sector actors, development of gender-sensitive standards and protocols, and institutional support to ensure inclusivity and responsiveness in service delivery, particularly for women and vulnerable groups.

Strengthening public institutions to deliver gender-responsive public policies and services. The initiatives focus on data and innovation advance, as well as social norms, change and prevention of backlashes against women's right.

planEntities.name: Strengthen systems and capacities of the legislative bodies to discharge their key lawmaking and oversight functions at Federal and Regional levels
planEntities.parentName: Democratic institutions and governance structures strengthened to ensure good and democratic governance practices, electoral integrity, and institutional accountability
planEntities.description:
The overall objective of the project is to build on existing enabling environment and opprtunities to further advance good governance and embeded democratic principles within targeted democratic institutions including those at law-making and oversight functions both at federal and regional levels.
The primary focus is to support the country in sustaining its efforts to enhance institutional capacities and frameworks that advance good governance, inclusion, and democratic participation.
The federal parliament and the regional parliaments in three regions such as Amhara, Oromia and Somali.

planEntities.name: Enhance awareness and knowledge of citizens particularly women and other vulnerable groups for understanding & claiming their rights, voicing their concerns, and actively participating in democratic decision-making processes
planEntities.parentName: Democratic institutions and governance structures strengthened to ensure good and democratic governance practices, electoral integrity, and institutional accountability
planEntities.description: The overall objective is to equip rights-holders with the necessary knowledge, skills and services to enable them to enjoy their rights, with a focus on groups who may be in vulnerable situations. Key thematic focuses include: the right to meaningfully participate in decision-making processes, including contributing to policy development, freedom from discrimination and access justice. Beneficiaries are expected to include victims and victims’ associations; women, persons with disability, IDPs.

planEntities.name: Strengthen the electoral frameworks and electoral management bodies and key stakeholders to ensure free, fair, inclusive, and gender responsive electoral processes
planEntities.parentName: Democratic institutions and governance structures strengthened to ensure good and democratic governance practices, electoral integrity, and institutional accountability
planEntities.description:
The primary objective is to enhance Ethiopia's electoral systems and processes by fostering inclusion, gender equality, transparency and accountability.
The project's central theme is the development of a capable and sustainable electoral management body, complemented by strengthened partnerships and collaboration with key electoral stakeholders.
The project primarily benefits citizens, particularly women, youth and other marginalized groups as well as Civil Society Organizations, media and Political Parties.

planEntities.name: Support Federal and Regional ethics and anti-corruption commissions to develop corruption risk assessment tools  and effectively implement it across government sectors
planEntities.parentName: Strengthened legal, policy, regulatory and accountability frameworks and institutions at all levels to ensure equitable access to justice and uphold the rule of law
planEntities.description: Develop standardized corruption risk assessment tools for key government sectors. This includes facilitating stakeholder consultations, delivering targeted training, piloting the tools in selected institutions, and integrating them into planning and monitoring systems to ensure effective and sustainable implementation.

planEntities.name: Strengthen capacities and mechanisms at the national and subnational level for people-centric access to justice including free legal aid service to all especially for the poor and vulnerable members of the society
planEntities.parentName: Strengthened legal, policy, regulatory and accountability frameworks and institutions at all levels to ensure equitable access to justice and uphold the rule of law
planEntities.description: Supporting the development of legal aid legislation and standards, training justice sector actors, establishing mobile legal aid clinics and community justice centers, producing simplified legal information in local languages, conducting awareness campaigns to inform citizens of their rights and available services, and providing financial and technical support to legal aid service providers to enhance their ability to deliver quality legal assistance to indigent populations. Support legislative reform, coordination and technical support to key criminal justice institutions and courts to effectively undertake their mandate.

planEntities.name: Leaving No One Behind - The Internal Displacement Solutions Fund (IDS Fund for Ethiopia
planEntities.parentName: Strengthened institutions, systems and mechanisms to promote peace, prevent conflict, effectively address root causes of conflict and implement post-conflict rehabilitation efforts
planEntities.description: The IDSF JP aims to strengthen durable solutions impact in Ethiopia, b  (1) Promoting effective strategies development, coordination, implementation and monitoring of internal displacement solutions at national and regional level including displacement solutions financing; (2)   Strengthening national leadership and building the capacity of key Government Ministries and Departments to promote solutions to internal displacement including through local solutions capacity assessments in line with the new IASC/UNSDG joint Guidance on Solutions to Internal Displacement; (3) Ensuring government, coordination bodies, and partners have improved access to robust data to help inform DS programming and strategy development at the national and sub-national levels.  Above 100,000 individuals will benefit from the programme across the project locations.

planEntities.name: Operational multi-hazard early warning and action systems strengthened, supported by reliable meteorological observation data, and the Multi-Hazard Early Warning Situation Room at EDRMC
planEntities.parentName: Strengthened disaster risk management systems and capacities at all levels
planEntities.description: Strengthen Ethiopia’s national meteorological observation network through the deployment and operationalization of AWS and upper-air stations. The Multi-Hazard Early Warning Situation Room at EDRMC will be established and operationalized.

planEntities.name: Capacity strengthened and disaster risk reduction and resilience measures implemented, integrated into regional and woreda development planning and budgeting processes
planEntities.parentName: Strengthened disaster risk management systems and capacities at all levels
planEntities.description: Provision of training of trainers and develop a pool of national and sub-national level trainers on integrating disaster risk reduction and climate change adaptation into development planning and budgetary processes. In parallel, implement community-based disaster risk reduction and resilience building activities in 5 selected woredas.

planEntities.name: Government, communities, smallholder farmers, cooperatives supported to benefit from and adopt climate-smart agriculture technologies and nature-based solutions, with a strong emphasis on women’s and youth empowerment
planEntities.parentName: Strengthened capacity of government and communities to respond, adapt and be resilient to climate change and environmental shocks
planEntities.description: Support women and female youth in climate-smart agriculture and agribusiness by strengthening their access to land, resources, and markets, and empowering women’s organizations and leaders. Facilitate the adoption of climate-smart, gender-responsive, and nature-based practices and technologies across households, cooperatives, enterprises, and communities, while engaging families and communities to promote collective climate action and resilience. Build the capacity of local governments to deliver gender-responsive services to farmers and pastoralists and promote private sector–led adoption of climate-smart solutions in SLA-targeted woredas through business appraisals, training, demonstration sites, and support to women’s groups. Provide an integrated package of climate- adaptive livelihood support, anticipatory action, and climate services to smallholder farmers, agro pastoralists and pastoralists especially women, and young people. Complementary support continues being provided to rehabilitate community-based ecosystem and promote regenerative agropastoral practices (sustainable management of natural resources such as rangeland and water).

planEntities.name: Monitoring and reporting systems established, and technical capacity strengthened to track biodiversity, land degradation, ecosystems restoration, and land-use changes, and associated CO2 emissions removal/reduction outcomes
planEntities.parentName: Enhanced sustainable natural resources management
planEntities.description: Establish monitoring systems to track biodiversity, land degradation, and restoration outcomes, providing reliable data to guide evidence-based decision-making and natural resource management (NRM) policy implementation; Provide technical support on national REDD+ and MRV capacity consolidation and strengthening as well as enabling biennial transparency reports preparation through Ethiopian Forest Development and MoPD respectively and make national forest monitoring/MRV system fully functional to monitor change of Ethiopian forest cover and reduction in CO2 emission to submit quality reports to UNFCCC.

planEntities.name: Participatory forest restoration and afforestation campaigns implemented
planEntities.parentName: Enhanced sustainable natural resources management
planEntities.description: Strengthen Participatory Forest restoration and afforestation campaigns through communities and stakeholders' engagement in rehabilitating degraded lands, expanding forest cover, and promoting sustainable ecosystem management.

planEntities.name: Support provided to vulnerable urban households to strengthen livelihoods through income-generating schemes, urban agriculture, and integrated waste management
planEntities.parentName: Strengthened capacity of government and other stakeholder for sustainable management of urbanization and human settlements
planEntities.description: Strengthen the livelihoods of  vulnerable communities and households in towns and cities through the provision of Income generating schemes (IGS) and urban agriculture; Provide technical support to  rehabilitate dumpsites, improve basic services and tenure, and strengthen urban governance for displacement-affected communities.

planEntities.name: Budget mobilized and secured to build resilience to climate change and DRR
planEntities.parentName: Improved Access to Climate Finance for Ethiopia's Long-Term Low Emission and Climate Resilient Development Strategy (2020-2050)
planEntities.description: Participating UN entities will mobilize and allocate resources to ensure delivery of all sub-outputs under Output 4.1, thereby strengthening multi-hazard disaster risk management systems and capacities at national, regional, and local levels;  all sub-outputs under Output 4.2, thereby strengthening capacity of government and communities to respond, adapt and be resilient to climate change and environmental shocks; all sub-outputs under Output 4.3, thereby enhancing sustainable natural resources management;  all sub-outputs under Output 4.4, thereby enhancing sustainable natural resources management.

planEntities.name: Generate, provide and support the implementation of macroeconomic or fiscal recommendations for policy dialogue and advocacy of improved public investments in human capital
planEntities.parentName: Strengthened economic governance, institutional capacity, and macroeconomic management
planEntities.description:
These recommendations will be generated from different sources: 
- These recommendations will be generated from analyses including budget briefs, medium term revenue and expenditure planning, etc. 
- Technical support provided to the Minitry of Finance on the implementation of the public finance management (PFM) strategy and
- Technical support provided at the sub-national level on domestic resource mobilization
- Through analyses of public agricultural expenditures and price incentives targeting the effective operationalization of national food-security, nutrition, and agricultural-transformation policies

planEntities.name: Strengthen the MSME and stratup ecosystem for trade, innovation and formalization
planEntities.parentName: Strengthened policy, systems, institutional capacity and access to finance, markets and technology to create decent and inclusive jobs
planEntities.description:
Under this sub-output, the UN will provide foundational support for businesses, from policy to financing including through the below activities:
- Financial and non-financial support to enterprises including access to finance and BDS
-  Policy harmonization and institutional capacity building for MSMEs and AfCFTA.
- Developing AI strategy and expanding access to innovation infrastructure.
- Implementing the Startup Act and establishing a ManuTech hub with grants and technical assistance.
- Providing entrepreneurship development and support for business formalization.
- Licensing and capitalizing the Enterprise Financing Facility (EFF).
- Developing and piloting credit scoring models.
- Delivering investment readiness and business development services.
- Enhancing regional value chains for AfCFTA access.

planEntities.name: Expansion of decentralized clean energy access for rural households and communities
planEntities.parentName: Enhanced access to affordable and clean energy through increased finance for energy investment, private sector engagement and adoption of diverse new energy technologies
planEntities.description: Support the design and implementation of decentralized renewable energy solutions (minigrids, productive use systems, off-grid solar, etc.) that enable households, particularly in rural and underserved areas, to gain access to affordable and sustainable energy. Improve the livelihoods and food security of vulnerable and fragile communities by promoting the adoption and exchange of renewable energy technologies (RETs) and sustainable practices that enhance water and climate resilience. Pilot integrated delivery models to increase productive use of energy, especially for agriclutral cooperatives,  women-led enterprises and smallholder farmers.

planEntities.name: Provide and advocate for policy recommendations for the debt crisis for Sub Saharan African countries provided
planEntities.parentName: Strengthened economic governance, institutional capacity, and macroeconomic management
planEntities.description: The objectives of the external debt analysis are to broaden understanding about debt and provide evidence-based recommendations. The recommendations of the analysis will be used to advise policymakers in debt management and seeking policy options.

planEntities.name: Conduct macroeconomic monitoring  with the quarterly economic profile of Ethiopia and provide in depth analysis to inform stakeholders
planEntities.parentName: Strengthened economic governance, institutional capacity, and macroeconomic management
planEntities.description: The UN will support the quarterly monitoring of the national economic performance through the simultaneous assessment of four sequential reform pillars: (1) moving to a market-determined currency exchange rate, (2) strengthening the Government's fiscal position through consolidation, (3) reforming public enterprises, and (4) liberalizing interest rate practices.

planEntities.name: Deliver integrated livelihoods, financial and resilience support for vulnerable communities
planEntities.parentName: Strengthened policy, systems, institutional capacity and access to finance, markets and technology to create decent and inclusive jobs
planEntities.description:
The UN will implement targeted interventions for vulnerable groups, linking immediate livelihood needs with long-term resilience. These include:
- Strengthening the national biodiversity financing framework.
- Deploying e-voucher systems and improving access to livelihood services.
- Providing targeted training and grants for conflict-affected female MSME owners.
- Conducting gender-responsive market assessments and awareness campaigns.
- Developing durable solutions strategies and providing livelihood support to IDPs.
- Expanding finance and insurance for smallholder farmers.
- Strengthening local capacity via training and input provision using e-vouchers.
- Supporting MSMEs with insurance product development and business services.
- Providing grants and training for climate-smart, women-led businesses.

planEntities.name: Strengthen private sector engagement in clean energy production, distribution and technology markets
planEntities.parentName: Enhanced access to affordable and clean energy through increased finance for energy investment, private sector engagement and adoption of diverse new energy technologies
planEntities.description: Strengthen entrepreneurship ecosystems for clean energy startups, particularly women- and youth-led enterprises, small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), and innovators through targeted business incubation, technical assistance, and access to de-risking and financing mechanisms, to enhance their capacity, foster innovation, and accelerate market growth for sustainable energy solutions.

planEntities.name: Strengthen financing frameworks and mobilization of public and private investment for clean energy
planEntities.parentName: Enhanced access to affordable and clean energy through increased finance for energy investment, private sector engagement and adoption of diverse new energy technologies
planEntities.description: Mobilize public and private investment through national multi-stakeholder coordination platforms, de-risking instruments for renewable energy investments, innovative financing mechanisms, blended finance, and partnerships to support the scaling up of renewable energy and productive use applications

planEntities.name: Policy, institutional, and technical support provided to national and regional governments to advance energy access and transition
planEntities.parentName: Enhanced access to affordable and clean energy through increased finance for energy investment, private sector engagement and adoption of diverse new energy technologies
planEntities.description: Strengthen the capacity of national and regional institutions to plan, implement, and monitor clean energy access and transition programmes. Support the development of strategies, guidelines, and roadmaps on clean cooking, mini-grids, and the gender–energy nexus to advance inclusive and sustainable energy transitions.

planEntities.name: Enhance capacities of women, youth, and their institutions at federal, regional, and local levels to engage in conflict resolution/management, develop and implement peacebuilding policies and strategies, and promote sustainable peacebuilding efforts
planEntities.parentName: Strengthened institutions, systems and mechanisms to promote peace, prevent conflict, effectively address root causes of conflict and implement post-conflict rehabilitation efforts
planEntities.description: The goal is to empower women and youth as agents of positive peace and security, strengthen institutions, promote innovation, social cohesion, and community resilience in Ethiopia.

planEntities.name: Support maternal health services with wider access to skilled attendance at birth
planEntities.parentName: National health care system capacities are strengthened to ensure equitable access and utilization of integrated, resilient, and shock-responsive high-quality primary health care services, including promotion, prevention and treatment services, particularly for vulnerable and marginalized individuals
planEntities.description: UNICEF and WHO provide policy advice and strategic support to strengthen the national health system, while also supporting PHC facilities to deliver quality maternal, newborn, child, and adolescent health services in both development and humanitarian contexts. UNFPA complements this by building the capacity of health extension workers and community structures to improve awareness and access to maternal health services. In addition, WHO supports the MoH with guidance, standards, and operational tools to reorient service delivery toward people-centred, integrated maternal and child health care, including strengthening SRMNCAYH services across the life course.

planEntities.name: Enhanced reproductive health services with increased availability and uptake of modern contraceptives
planEntities.parentName: National health care system capacities are strengthened to ensure equitable access and utilization of integrated, resilient, and shock-responsive high-quality primary health care services, including promotion, prevention and treatment services, particularly for vulnerable and marginalized individuals
planEntities.description: UNFPA provides technical and financial support to strengthen the availability and accessibility of family planning and broader SRHR services at PHC level. This includes policy and strategy development, capacity building of health workers, provision of supplies, and strengthening supply chain management to ensure contraceptives and life-saving reproductive health commodities reach the last mile. WHO complements this by setting global norms and standards, providing guidance, and supporting the Ministry of Health to adapt SRHR policies and guidelines across the life course.

planEntities.name: 2gether4SRHR (Improving Access to Quality Integrated Sexual and Reproductive Health Services through Strengthening Maternity Waiting Homes in Afar Region
planEntities.parentName: National health care system capacities are strengthened to ensure equitable access and utilization of integrated, resilient, and shock-responsive high-quality primary health care services, including promotion, prevention and treatment services, particularly for vulnerable and marginalized individuals
planEntities.description: This joint initiative, jointly implemented by UNAIDS, UNFPA, UNICEF and WHO, aims to strengthen maternity waiting homes ,expand access to quality sexual and reproductive health (SRH) services and address the social determinants of maternal mortality in Afar region's Wasama District.

planEntities.name: Provide support to government, women rights, youth and disability organizations to improve their system and capacities to draft, design, legislate, and implement gender responsive and inclusive laws, policies, directives, and guidelines
planEntities.parentName: Strengthened mechanisms and capacities of communities and institutions to address discriminatory gender and social norms, to prevent and respond to all forms of gender-based violence including sexual exploitation and abuse
planEntities.description: The support would be trainings, exchange forums, development of guidelines and directives, develop monitoring tools, development of disability inclusion action plan, provision of technical guidance note on inclusion of persons with additional vulnerabilities, close engagement with OPDs, targeting of female-headed households, persons with disabilities, and other vulnerable groups for provision of food security assistance, support printing and dissemination of the Gender Equality and Women Empowerment Policy, monitoring visits for the implementation of GEWE Commitments. Provide technical and financial support for the finalization of the Family Code of Afar and Somali regions.

planEntities.name: Support and mobilize individuals, families, community/religious leaders and local community structures to promote positive and equitable social norms and PSEA
planEntities.parentName: Strengthened mechanisms and capacities of communities and institutions to address discriminatory gender and social norms, to prevent and respond to all forms of gender-based violence including sexual exploitation and abuse
planEntities.description:
Develop/implement structured community mobilization tools, facilitate structured community conversations, awareness raising sessions, capacity building training, facilitate public declarations, media campaigns, uncut girls’ movement, community-based complaint handling mechanisms, establish and strengthen confidential, and accessible reporting channels.
Provision of PSEA and SBCC sensitization sessions and materials within food security programs to beneficiaries and communities, participation in national PSEA in-country network, chairing of two sub-national PSEA networks in Somali and Afar

planEntities.name: Provide technical and financial support to institutions/service providers (health, justice, and social sector) to providing quality, coordinated, accessible, survivor and youth friendly essential services to youth, women and girl survivors of GBV, SEA and harmful practices
planEntities.parentName: Strengthened mechanisms and capacities of communities and institutions to address discriminatory gender and social norms, to prevent and respond to all forms of gender-based violence including sexual exploitation and abuse
planEntities.description: Establish and strengthen safe houses, one stop centers, women and girls friendly spaces, strengthen referral linkages, provide training to service providers, procure equipment and consumables to service providers, raise awareness of community on availability of services, provision of GBV and child protection safe referral trainings  to humanitarian actors, implementation of gender-transformative nutritional sensitive programs, strengthen the national and regional child protection coordination structures including Anti-HTP.

planEntities.name: Support and engage individuals, families, community and religious leaders, and local structures to promote positive social norms, eliminate female genital mutilation, and prevent early, child, and forced marriages
planEntities.parentName: Strengthened mechanisms and capacities of communities and institutions to address discriminatory gender and social norms, to prevent and respond to all forms of gender-based violence including sexual exploitation and abuse
planEntities.description:
Community mobilization campaigns and public declaration events are conducted to eliminate female genital mutilation (FGM) and prevent child marriages. Reflective dialogues, training, and engagement with community and religious leaders strengthen understanding of FGM, Child marriage and support monitoring, advocacy, and community accountability. Engagement of Men and Boys: Implement structured capacity-building and dialogue sessions aimed at promoting positive masculinity and strengthening their role in driving social norm change that supports girls’ empowerment, protection, and gender equality. This will be guided by the Empowering Allies: A Manual for Male Engagement to Promote Gender Equality, End Child Marriage and FGM, targeting boys aged 10–14, 15–19, and men aged 20 and above. 
Mobilization of Women-Led Organizations and Community Structures: Strengthen the capacity and engagement of women-led organizations and community-based structures to build a grassroots movement focused on preventing harmful practices including child marriage, FGM, and other forms of violence while fostering societal change and reinforcing positive social norms. 
Faith-Based Dialogue: Facilitate structured faith dialogues among religious leaders at various levels using communication manuals and theological frameworks to promote understanding and advocacy against harmful practices within religious contexts.                                                                                                         Enhance the agency of adolescent girls: capacitating both in school and out-of-school through life skills education. This will be implemented using the Girls’ Power: Comprehensive Capacity Building Manual for Out-of-School Adolescent Girls and the in-school manual developed by the education sector. The intervention aims to equip girls with the skills, information, and knowledge needed to protect themselves and their peers from child marriage, FGM, and other forms of violence, while also empowering them to lead social change within their communities and contribute to lasting societal transformation.

planEntities.name: Build capacities of Women, Youth and Persons with Disability in decision-making processes across sectors and at all levels
planEntities.parentName: Increased participation and representation of women, young people and other marginalized groups including adolescent girls in the multi-sectoral decision-making process
planEntities.description: Train women from regions and universities on leadership and decision making, Strengthen the capacity of  women development union on basic financial literacy, Capacity building of Organizations of Persons with Disabilities, meaningful engagement with OPDs and linking with food management committees, camp management committees.

planEntities.name: Provide support to institutions and groups working on the rights of women, youth, marginalized groups to influence policies and decision-making processes
planEntities.parentName: Increased participation and representation of women, young people and other marginalized groups including adolescent girls in the multi-sectoral decision-making process
planEntities.description:
Enhance youth engagement through both digital and offline platforms, leveraging U-Report to amplify young voices on key issues such as child rights, education, and employability. Activities will include interactive polls, awareness campaigns, and capacity-building sessions to strengthen life skills and advocacy.
