planEntities.name: National and sub-national authorities develop and coordinate policies that enable early development approaches to respond to the forced displacement from Sudan
planEntities.parentName: Strengthened legal, policy, regulatory and accountability frameworks and institutions at all levels to ensure equitable access to justice and uphold the rule of law
planEntities.description: Rehabilitation and reintegration of refugee returnees from Sudan is an important element of response to the Sudan situation. UNHCR in collaboration with the government provides multi-purpose cash assistance for the returnees to address immediate assistance and protection needs of the returnees. Regular protection monitoring will be conducted to assess protection needs and reintegration challenges including access to livelihoods and self-reliance opportunities. Moreover, UNHCR partners with the EHRC to enhance human rights monitoring and advocacy for forcibly displaced persons.

planEntities.name: EU IM3 Sustainable support to persons displaced by conflict and natural disasters and their host communities in Afar, Amhara, BSG and Tigray
planEntities.parentName: Strengthened institutions, systems and mechanisms to promote peace, prevent conflict, effectively address root causes of conflict and implement post-conflict rehabilitation efforts
planEntities.description: The overall objective of the Action is to reduce poverty and improve the health and well-being of internally displaced populations (IDPs) and host communities (HC), with an emphasis on man-made disasters and natural and climate hazards in Ethiopia. The proposed Action will enable conflict- and climate-induced IDPs and host communities to move towards recovery and resilience through a comprehensive and multisectoral area-based community development project. This will be achieved through three main objectives: (1)To improve the living conditions of IDPs and host communities through access to livelihoods, and financial support and economic opportunities; (2) To improve access to gender and disability sensitive Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WaSH) infrastructure and services for IDPs and host communities in targeted areas; (3) To strengthen social cohesion and protection services for IDPs and host community (focusing on women and people with disability) through an area-based, community based approach, supported by needs-based data collection and capacity building of relevant stakeholders.

Ethiopia.name: United Nations Children's Fund
Ethiopia.organizationType: Multilateral - UN organizations excluding pooled funds

planEntities.name: Support the conduct of scheduled surveys, census and population data and national assessment and analysis
planEntities.parentName: National and regional capacity enhanced for the production, analyses and utilization of high-quality data
planEntities.description: The UN will provide technical support to ESS to conduct the EDHS preparation and dissemination. In addition, other scheduled surveys such as the agricultural survey, integrated household survey/welfare monitoring survey, will be supported. The preparatory work for the Census will also be underway where the focus for the planning period will be on supporting the development of the Census Cartography.

planEntities.name: Enhance capacity of the national statistics system to produce and disseminate timely, quality, comparable and gender responsive data backed by improved sectoral management information systems
planEntities.parentName: National and regional capacity enhanced for the production, analyses and utilization of high-quality data
planEntities.description: The UN will support the GoE to improve its capacity to produce quality data to track SDG and national development indicators. These include strengthening the National & Regional integrated information management systems, improving sectoral information management systems such as EMIS, HMIS, Gender MIS and digital civil registration system; addressing gaps in laws and policies and improving capacity for quality, standardized and accelerated civil registration system. In addition, DTM publications on displaced persons, other migrant populations, and human mobility will be a key component of the programmme.

planEntities.name: Support maternal health services with wider access to skilled attendance at birth
planEntities.parentName: National health care system capacities are strengthened to ensure equitable access and utilization of integrated, resilient, and shock-responsive high-quality primary health care services, including promotion, prevention and treatment services, particularly for vulnerable and marginalized individuals
planEntities.description: UNICEF and WHO provide policy advice and strategic support to strengthen the national health system, while also supporting PHC facilities to deliver quality maternal, newborn, child, and adolescent health services in both development and humanitarian contexts. UNFPA complements this by building the capacity of health extension workers and community structures to improve awareness and access to maternal health services. In addition, WHO supports the MoH with guidance, standards, and operational tools to reorient service delivery toward people-centred, integrated maternal and child health care, including strengthening SRMNCAYH services across the life course.

planEntities.name: Sustained and equitable immunization services ensuring infants receive full protection with DTP vaccines
planEntities.parentName: National health care system capacities are strengthened to ensure equitable access and utilization of integrated, resilient, and shock-responsive high-quality primary health care services, including promotion, prevention and treatment services, particularly for vulnerable and marginalized individuals
planEntities.description: WHO and UNICEF provides technical and financial support to build resilient PHC systems that deliver immunization services, address zero-dose children, and maintain continuity of services during emergencies. UNICEF strengthens community health systems and supports social and behaviour change interventions to increase awareness and demand for vaccines. WHO complements this by building the capacity of national public health institutions, including surveillance, laboratories, emergency preparedness, and workforce development, to sustain immunization programmes and ensure health system resilience in the face of emergencies and disease outbreaks.

planEntities.name: Increased access to equitable and quality education for hardest-to-reach and out-of-school children, including in humanitarian settings
planEntities.parentName: The National education system’s capacities are strengthened to increase access to inclusive and equitable learning opportunities to out of school and hardest to reach children and adolescents and equip them to achieve quality universal foundational literacy and numeracy and develop skills for successful transitions between education levels and from learning to earning
planEntities.description:
UNICEF and UNOPS aim to enhance access to quality formal or non-formal education including early learning in underserved and humanitarian settings. WFP supports Ethiopia’s objective of universal school feeding by 2030, prioritizing food insecure and underserved areas leveraging the Home-Grown School Feeding Programme to connect education with local agricultural development contributing to attendance and nutrition outcome.
The multi-sectoral intervention is aimed at improving health conditions in the woredas of Chifra and Hamer in the Afar and SNNP regions. The project will focus on achieving health milestones through the rehabilitation of the health facilities in both regions and nutrition in education by constructing and rehabilitating the targeted schools. To ensure a holistic approach to the intervention, integration of WASH, energy and biofuel will be weaved into the different components of the project. In strengthening the milestones of the health sector and ensuring progress in achieving universal healthcare, the project will provide technical assistance to the Ministry of Health by enhancing its capacity to provide strategic direction, leadership and coordination of stakeholders to achieve the health transformation plan.

planEntities.name: Adolescent boys and girls have gained gender-responsive learning and skills for life and employment
planEntities.parentName: The National education system’s capacities are strengthened to increase access to inclusive and equitable learning opportunities to out of school and hardest to reach children and adolescents and equip them to achieve quality universal foundational literacy and numeracy and develop skills for successful transitions between education levels and from learning to earning
planEntities.description: Through this sub-output, UNICEF will support adolescents to not only gain foundational and transferable skills but also develop competencies that are sensitive to gender dynamics.

planEntities.name: National WASH systems, policies, and standards are strengthened to improve service delivery and sustainability
planEntities.parentName: Strengthen national and sub national capacity towards equitable access to basic, inclusive and climate-resilient WASH services and show intent to practice WASH behaviours
planEntities.description: National and regional government mechanisms and systems are strengthened to enable legislation, planning and budgeting for resilient and risk-informed, gender-responsive, equitable, inclusive, climate-resilient and energy-efficient basic WASH services and practices in development and humanitarian situations.

planEntities.name: Institutional capacity is enhanced to implement climate-resilient approaches in WASH and health service delivery, including the restoration of essential facilities
planEntities.parentName: Strengthen national and sub national capacity towards equitable access to basic, inclusive and climate-resilient WASH services and show intent to practice WASH behaviours
planEntities.description: Enhancing climate resilience in WASH systems by involving suitable designing of WASH infrastructures to withstand floods and droughts, protecting and diversifying water sources, and integrating climate risks into planning and policies. It also requires engaging communities, improving governance, accessing climate finance, and using innovative technologies for monitoring and early warning. These actions help ensure safe, sustainable water and sanitation services amid increasing climate challenges. In addition, critical health services are restored to improve access to WASH for conflict-communities, focusing on the rehabilitation of health centers and WASH facilities. The project also aims to restore critical health services and improve access to safe water, sanitation, and hygiene for conflict-affected communities, focusing on the rehabilitation of health centres and WASH facilities.

planEntities.name: Strengthen systems for adaptive, integrated, and resilience-building social protection through Cash Plus interventions and infrastructure support
planEntities.parentName: Strengthen national and sub national capacity of systems and communities including those that are left behind towards accessing gender-transformative, climate-resilient and shock-responsive social protection and social services
planEntities.description: Implementation of safety net interventions (cash transfers, voucher assistance, and grants) in humanitarian and development settings through related regional bureau and frontline workers. Interventions also include linkages to essential services (health, education, nutrition, and cash management) and support services for livelihood activities. Activities will also include development of programme implementation manuals and training for subnational governments, including the social service workers, to implement Cash Plus care programmes in both humanitarian and development contexts. Under the programme, the UN also aims to rebuild and improve access to basic services and build climate-resilient community infrastructure in conflict-affected areas of the Tigray region. The project will be operational in 5 Woredas (Abergele, Asgede, Hawzen, Hintalo and Ofla) in Tigray with focus on Health, Education and WASH.UNOPS will undertake the Response - Resilience- recovery activities.

planEntities.name: Provide technical assistance for gender-transformative, nutrition-sensitive, adaptive, inclusive, and resilience-building social protection
planEntities.parentName: Strengthen national and sub national capacity of systems and communities including those that are left behind towards accessing gender-transformative, climate-resilient and shock-responsive social protection and social services
planEntities.description: This project provides comprehensive technical assistance to foster the inclusion of refugees and forcibly displaced populations within national social protection systems. It promotes a human rights-based, lifecycle approach to programming that is adaptive, child-sensitive, gender-transformative, disability-inclusive, climate-resilient, and shock-responsive. A core component is the generation of evidence to inform government budgeting for social services and to evaluate Cash Plus programmes, including Child Grant pilots and financial inclusion interventions, while also developing related manuals for national safety net implementation. Furthermore, the project includes UN-led capacity building at national and sub-national levels to strengthen government ownership, institutional systems, and community participation, specifically to scale up and ensure the sustainability of school feeding programmes.

planEntities.name: Provide support to government, women rights, youth and disability organizations to improve their system and capacities to draft, design, legislate, and implement gender responsive and inclusive laws, policies, directives, and guidelines
planEntities.parentName: Strengthened mechanisms and capacities of communities and institutions to address discriminatory gender and social norms, to prevent and respond to all forms of gender-based violence including sexual exploitation and abuse
planEntities.description: The support would be trainings, exchange forums, development of guidelines and directives, develop monitoring tools, development of disability inclusion action plan, provision of technical guidance note on inclusion of persons with additional vulnerabilities, close engagement with OPDs, targeting of female-headed households, persons with disabilities, and other vulnerable groups for provision of food security assistance, support printing and dissemination of the Gender Equality and Women Empowerment Policy, monitoring visits for the implementation of GEWE Commitments. Provide technical and financial support for the finalization of the Family Code of Afar and Somali regions.

planEntities.name: Support and engage individuals, families, community and religious leaders, and local structures to promote positive social norms, eliminate female genital mutilation, and prevent early, child, and forced marriages
planEntities.parentName: Strengthened mechanisms and capacities of communities and institutions to address discriminatory gender and social norms, to prevent and respond to all forms of gender-based violence including sexual exploitation and abuse
planEntities.description:
Community mobilization campaigns and public declaration events are conducted to eliminate female genital mutilation (FGM) and prevent child marriages. Reflective dialogues, training, and engagement with community and religious leaders strengthen understanding of FGM, Child marriage and support monitoring, advocacy, and community accountability. Engagement of Men and Boys: Implement structured capacity-building and dialogue sessions aimed at promoting positive masculinity and strengthening their role in driving social norm change that supports girls’ empowerment, protection, and gender equality. This will be guided by the Empowering Allies: A Manual for Male Engagement to Promote Gender Equality, End Child Marriage and FGM, targeting boys aged 10–14, 15–19, and men aged 20 and above. 
Mobilization of Women-Led Organizations and Community Structures: Strengthen the capacity and engagement of women-led organizations and community-based structures to build a grassroots movement focused on preventing harmful practices including child marriage, FGM, and other forms of violence while fostering societal change and reinforcing positive social norms. 
Faith-Based Dialogue: Facilitate structured faith dialogues among religious leaders at various levels using communication manuals and theological frameworks to promote understanding and advocacy against harmful practices within religious contexts.                                                                                                         Enhance the agency of adolescent girls: capacitating both in school and out-of-school through life skills education. This will be implemented using the Girls’ Power: Comprehensive Capacity Building Manual for Out-of-School Adolescent Girls and the in-school manual developed by the education sector. The intervention aims to equip girls with the skills, information, and knowledge needed to protect themselves and their peers from child marriage, FGM, and other forms of violence, while also empowering them to lead social change within their communities and contribute to lasting societal transformation.

planEntities.name: Provide support to institutions and groups working on the rights of women, youth, marginalized groups to influence policies and decision-making processes
planEntities.parentName: Increased participation and representation of women, young people and other marginalized groups including adolescent girls in the multi-sectoral decision-making process
planEntities.description:
Enhance youth engagement through both digital and offline platforms, leveraging U-Report to amplify young voices on key issues such as child rights, education, and employability. Activities will include interactive polls, awareness campaigns, and capacity-building sessions to strengthen life skills and advocacy. 
Provide capacity building trainings on advocacy, laws and policies, organize advocacy sessions, support joint call for actions, facilitate joint platforms for policy makers and advocates, women rights organizations, youth and marginalized groups, technical assistance in the development/review of gender responsive laws.

planEntities.name: Provide technical and financial support to government Structures responsible for gender equality, youth empowerment and disability inclusion at federal and regional levels to have strong accountability mechanisms to design, implement, monitor relevant  policies and frameworks
planEntities.parentName: Policy, institutional accountability including financing frameworks strengthened to promote gender equality and the empowerment of women and young people
planEntities.description:
Strengthen the National Gender Information System and support the accountability directive and performance levelling tool, organize trainings on these tools, build capacities of women machineries at federal and regional levels,
Support the implementation of the Monitoring, Evaluation, and Learning (MEL) framework, including the use of data collection tools focused on the prevention of harmful practices specifically child marriage, FGM, and violence against children. These tools are designed to strengthen systems and practices at federal, regional, woreda, and community levels across key institutions such as MoWSA, BoWSA, MoJ, and BoJs. This support includes facilitating cascading trainings by those who received TOT, organizing review and exchange sessions, and providing field-level technical assistance to ensure effective and consistent application of the MEL framework.

planEntities.name: Support multi-stakeholder coordination and platforms functioning at national and regional levels to address harmful gender and social norms
planEntities.parentName: Policy, institutional accountability including financing frameworks strengthened to promote gender equality and the empowerment of women and young people
planEntities.description: Facilitate and strengthen multi-stakeholder coordination platforms at national and regional levels to address harmful practice (FGM and Child marriage). Support collaboration among government, civil society, and community actors to promote positive social change and ensure effective implementation of interventions. Strengthen the National Alliance to End Child Marriage and FGM by providing technical and financial support to convene regular meetings, facilitate learning and exchange sessions, and advance coordinated advocacy efforts.

planEntities.name: Budget mobilized and secured to build resilience to climate change and DRR
planEntities.parentName: Improved Access to Climate Finance for Ethiopia's Long-Term Low Emission and Climate Resilient Development Strategy (2020-2050)
planEntities.description: Participating UN entities will mobilize and allocate resources to ensure delivery of all sub-outputs under Output 4.1, thereby strengthening multi-hazard disaster risk management systems and capacities at national, regional, and local levels;  all sub-outputs under Output 4.2, thereby strengthening capacity of government and communities to respond, adapt and be resilient to climate change and environmental shocks; all sub-outputs under Output 4.3, thereby enhancing sustainable natural resources management;  all sub-outputs under Output 4.4, thereby enhancing sustainable natural resources management.

planEntities.name: Generate, provide and support the implementation of macroeconomic or fiscal recommendations for policy dialogue and advocacy of improved public investments in human capital
planEntities.parentName: Strengthened economic governance, institutional capacity, and macroeconomic management
planEntities.description:
These recommendations will be generated from different sources: 
- These recommendations will be generated from analyses including budget briefs, medium term revenue and expenditure planning, etc. 
- Technical support provided to the Minitry of Finance on the implementation of the public finance management (PFM) strategy and
- Technical support provided at the sub-national level on domestic resource mobilization
- Through analyses of public agricultural expenditures and price incentives targeting the effective operationalization of national food-security, nutrition, and agricultural-transformation policies

planEntities.name: 2gether4SRHR (Improving Access to Quality Integrated Sexual and Reproductive Health Services through Strengthening Maternity Waiting Homes in Afar Region
planEntities.parentName: National health care system capacities are strengthened to ensure equitable access and utilization of integrated, resilient, and shock-responsive high-quality primary health care services, including promotion, prevention and treatment services, particularly for vulnerable and marginalized individuals
planEntities.description:
This joint initiative, jointly implemented by UNAIDS, UNFPA, UNICEF and WHO, aims to strengthen maternity waiting homes ,expand access to quality sexual and reproductive
health (SRH) services and address the social determinants of maternal mortality in Afar region's Wasema Disrict.

planEntities.name: Deliver integrated livelihoods, financial and resilience support for vulnerable communities
planEntities.parentName: Strengthened policy, systems, institutional capacity and access to finance, markets and technology to create decent and inclusive jobs
planEntities.description:
The UN will implement targeted interventions for vulnerable groups, linking immediate livelihood needs with long-term resilience. These include:
- Strengthening the national biodiversity financing framework.
- Deploying e-voucher systems and improving access to livelihood services.
- Providing targeted training and grants for conflict-affected female MSME owners.
- Conducting gender-responsive market assessments and awareness campaigns.
- Developing durable solutions strategies and providing livelihood support to IDPs.
- Expanding finance and insurance for smallholder farmers.
- Strengthening local capacity via training and input provision using e-vouchers.
- Supporting MSMEs with insurance product development and business services.
- Providing grants and training for climate-smart, women-led businesses.

planEntities.name: Strengthen the capacities of the social service workforce and the case management systems to deliver quality child protection services for vulnerable children and populations at risk of GBV in development and humanitarian settings
planEntities.parentName: Strengthen national and sub national capacity of systems and communities including those that are left behind towards accessing gender-transformative, climate-resilient and shock-responsive social protection and social services
planEntities.description: Capacity strengthening will focus on frontline actors and community-based service providers to enhance the delivery of inclusive, shock-responsive social protection, child protection, and GBV prevention and response. This includes training and deployment of social workers and community service personnel, provision of case management services, and support for the implementation of digital case management systems such as CPMIS+. Capacity-building efforts will also target extension workers to improve the delivery of nutrition-sensitive social protection, shock-responsive social protection, child protection and prevention and response to GBV. Community feedback and response mechanisms will be reinforced to promote accountability, service quality, and responsiveness to the needs of vulnerable populations.

planEntities.name: Support effective agri-food system service delivery through strengthened institutional systems and workforce capacities
planEntities.parentName: Improved access and adoption of inputs, technologies and practices for the production of nutrient dense food and an inclusive and resilient food system
planEntities.description: This sub-output focuses on improving capacities across institutions, systems, and value-chain actors to deliver high-quality, inclusive and resilient agri-food services. It includes strengthening surveillance systems, food safety and quality management capacities, and workforce development using a One Health approach, ensuring that public and private actors have the skills, infrastructure and coordination mechanisms needed for effective implementation. The sub-output will also support and strengthen existing structures, especially at lower level to enhance collaboration in delivery of multisectoral nutrition sensitive interventions.

planEntities.name: Increase access to market information modalities for producers through reliable, functional and updated information systems
planEntities.parentName: Improved access and adoption of inputs, technologies and practices for the production of nutrient dense food and an inclusive and resilient food system
planEntities.description: This sub-output aims to enhance the availability, quality, and usability of Market Information Systems (MIS) to support better production and marketing decisions by farmers, cooperatives, SMEs, women and youth. It includes strengthening linkages between producers and markets, improving information flow across input and output markets, and promoting digital and inclusive access pathways for underserved groups.

planEntities.name: Monitoring and reporting systems established, and technical capacity strengthened to track biodiversity, land degradation, ecosystems restoration, and land-use changes, and associated CO2 emissions removal/reduction outcomes
planEntities.parentName: Enhanced sustainable natural resources management
planEntities.description: Establish monitoring systems to track biodiversity, land degradation, and restoration outcomes, providing reliable data to guide evidence-based decision-making and natural resource management (NRM) policy implementation; Provide technical support on national REDD+ and MRV capacity consolidation and strengthening as well as enabling biennial transparency reports preparation through Ethiopian Forest Development and MoPD respectively and make national forest monitoring/MRV system fully functional to monitor change of Ethiopian forest cover and reduction in CO2 emission to submit quality reports to UNFCCC.

planEntities.name: Strengthen the MSME and stratup ecosystem for trade, innovation and formalization
planEntities.parentName: Strengthened policy, systems, institutional capacity and access to finance, markets and technology to create decent and inclusive jobs
planEntities.description:
Under this sub-output, the UN will provide foundational support for businesses, from policy to financing including through the below activities:
- Financial and non-financial support to enterprises including access to finance and BDS
-  Policy harmonization and institutional capacity building for MSMEs and AfCFTA.
- Developing AI strategy and expanding access to innovation infrastructure.
- Implementing the Startup Act and establishing a ManuTech hub with grants and technical assistance.
- Providing entrepreneurship development and support for business formalization.
- Licensing and capitalizing the Enterprise Financing Facility (EFF).
- Developing and piloting credit scoring models.
- Delivering investment readiness and business development services.
- Enhancing regional value chains for AfCFTA access.

planEntities.name: Leveraging Public and Private Sector Investments in Sustainable Food (Poultry) Value Chains
planEntities.parentName: Improved access and adoption of inputs, technologies and practices for the production of nutrient dense food and an inclusive and resilient food system
planEntities.description: The project aims to increase the availability of poultry products by improving access to finance for poultry value-chain actors, thereby enhancing food and nutrition security. It combines technical assistance, capacity development, market linkages and blended-finance instruments to strengthen the poultry value chain.

planEntities.name: Support national capacity to implement the transitional justice policy including through the development of subsequent legislations and the establishment of gender responsive and inclusive institutions that meet human rights standards

planEntities.description: The overall objective is to ensure the institutions mandated to implement the transitional justice policy can fulfill their mandate and the population (including victims) can meaningfully engage with the process. planEntities.name: Strengthen support institutions and systems to ensure greater effectiveness, accountability, transparency,  gender-responsiveness and inclusivity in public services
planEntities.parentName: Democratic institutions and governance structures strengthened to ensure good and democratic governance practices, electoral integrity, and institutional accountability
planEntities.description:
Strengthening criminal justice institutions and judiciary deliver more effective, accountable, and gender-responsive public services. This includes support for legal aid services and targeted interventions to prevent, mitigate, and respond to sexual and gender-based violence (SGBV). Activities will focus on capacity building for justice sector actors, development of gender-sensitive standards and protocols, and institutional support to ensure inclusivity and responsiveness in service delivery, particularly for women and vulnerable groups.

Strengthening public institutions to deliver gender-responsive public policies and services. The initiatives focus on data and innovation advance, as well as social norms, change and prevention of backlashes against women's right.

planEntities.name: Strengthen systems and capacities of the legislative bodies to discharge their key lawmaking and oversight functions at Federal and Regional levels
planEntities.parentName: Democratic institutions and governance structures strengthened to ensure good and democratic governance practices, electoral integrity, and institutional accountability
planEntities.description:
The overall objective of the project is to build on existing enabling environment and opprtunities to further advance good governance and embeded democratic principles within targeted democratic institutions including those at law-making and oversight functions both at federal and regional levels.
The primary focus is to support the country in sustaining its efforts to enhance institutional capacities and frameworks that advance good governance, inclusion, and democratic participation.
The federal parliament and the regional parliaments in three regions such as Amhara, Oromia and Somali.

planEntities.name: Enhance awareness and knowledge of citizens particularly women and other vulnerable groups for understanding & claiming their rights, voicing their concerns, and actively participating in democratic decision-making processes
planEntities.parentName: Democratic institutions and governance structures strengthened to ensure good and democratic governance practices, electoral integrity, and institutional accountability
planEntities.description: The overall objective is to equip rights-holders with the necessary knowledge, skills and services to enable them to enjoy their rights, with a focus on groups who may be in vulnerable situations. Key thematic focuses include: the right to meaningfully participate in decision-making processes, including contributing to policy development, freedom from discrimination and access justice. Beneficiaries are expected to include victims and victims’ associations; women, persons with disability, IDPs.

planEntities.name: Support Federal and Regional ethics and anti-corruption commissions to develop corruption risk assessment tools  and effectively implement it across government sectors
planEntities.parentName: Strengthened legal, policy, regulatory and accountability frameworks and institutions at all levels to ensure equitable access to justice and uphold the rule of law
planEntities.description: Develop standardized corruption risk assessment tools for key government sectors. This includes facilitating stakeholder consultations, delivering targeted training, piloting the tools in selected institutions, and integrating them into planning and monitoring systems to ensure effective and sustainable implementation.

planEntities.name: Strengthen capacities and mechanisms at the national and subnational level for people-centric access to justice including free legal aid service to all especially for the poor and vulnerable members of the society

planEntities.description: Supporting the development of legal aid legislation and standards, training justice sector actors, establishing mobile legal aid clinics and community justice centers, producing simplified legal information in local languages, conducting awareness campaigns to inform citizens of their rights and available services, and providing financial and technical support to legal aid service providers to enhance their ability to deliver quality legal assistance to indigent populations. Support legislative reform, coordination and technical support to key criminal justice institutions and courts to effectively undertake their mandate.

Interventions also include linkages to essential services (health, education, nutrition, and cash management) and support services for livelihood activities. Under the programme, the UN also aims to rebuild and improve access to basic services and build climate-resilient community infrastructure in conflict-affected areas of the Tigray region. The project will be operational in 5 Woredas (Abergele, Asgede, Hawzen, Hintalo and Ofla) in Tigray with focus on Health, Education and WASH.UNOPS will undertake the Response - Resilience- recovery activities.

Ethiopia.name: United Nations World Food Programme
Ethiopia.organizationType: Multilateral - UN organizations excluding pooled funds

planEntities.name: Enhance capacities of women, youth, and their institutions at federal, regional, and local levels to engage in conflict resolution/management, develop and implement peacebuilding policies and strategies, and promote sustainable peacebuilding efforts
planEntities.parentName: Strengthened institutions, systems and mechanisms to promote peace, prevent conflict, effectively address root causes of conflict and implement post-conflict rehabilitation efforts
planEntities.description: The goal is to empower women and youth as agents of positive peace and security, strengthen institutions, promote innovation, social cohesion, and community resilience in Ethiopia.

planEntities.name: Increased access to equitable and quality education for hardest-to-reach and out-of-school children, including in humanitarian settings
planEntities.parentName: The National education system’s capacities are strengthened to increase access to inclusive and equitable learning opportunities to out of school and hardest to reach children and adolescents and equip them to achieve quality universal foundational literacy and numeracy and develop skills for successful transitions between education levels and from learning to earning
planEntities.description:
UNICEF and UNOPS aim to enhance access to quality formal or non-formal education including early learning in underserved and humanitarian settings. WFP supports Ethiopia’s objective of universal school feeding by 2030, prioritizing food insecure and underserved areas leveraging the Home-Grown School Feeding Programme to connect education with local agricultural development contributing to attendance and nutrition outcome.
The multi-sectoral intervention is aimed at improving health conditions in the woredas of Chifra and Hamer in the Afar and SNNP regions. The project will focus on achieving health milestones through the rehabilitation of the health facilities in both regions and nutrition in education by constructing and rehabilitating the targeted schools. To ensure a holistic approach to the intervention, integration of WASH, energy and biofuel will be weaved into the different components of the project. In strengthening the milestones of the health sector and ensuring progress in achieving universal healthcare, the project will provide technical assistance to the Ministry of Health by enhancing its capacity to provide strategic direction, leadership and coordination of stakeholders to achieve the health transformation plan.

planEntities.name: Enhance capacities to mainstream climate change adaptation and environmental sustainability into education sector plans
planEntities.parentName: The National education system’s capacities are strengthened to increase access to inclusive and equitable learning opportunities to out of school and hardest to reach children and adolescents and equip them to achieve quality universal foundational literacy and numeracy and develop skills for successful transitions between education levels and from learning to earning
planEntities.description: The project aims to enhance the capacity of the Ministry of Education to produce and utilize quality data on Climate to provide Evidence for Education Planning and Policy on climate change.

planEntities.name: Provide technical assistance for gender-transformative, nutrition-sensitive, adaptive, inclusive, and resilience-building social protection
planEntities.parentName: Strengthen national and sub national capacity of systems and communities including those that are left behind towards accessing gender-transformative, climate-resilient and shock-responsive social protection and social services
planEntities.description: This project provides comprehensive technical assistance to foster the inclusion of refugees and forcibly displaced populations within national social protection systems. It promotes a human rights-based, lifecycle approach to programming that is adaptive, child-sensitive, gender-transformative, disability-inclusive, climate-resilient, and shock-responsive. A core component is the generation of evidence to inform government budgeting for social services and to evaluate Cash Plus programmes, including Child Grant pilots and financial inclusion interventions, while also developing related manuals for national safety net implementation. Furthermore, the project includes UN-led capacity building at national and sub-national levels to strengthen government ownership, institutional systems, and community participation, specifically to scale up and ensure the sustainability of school feeding programmes.

planEntities.name: Provide support to government, women rights, youth and disability organizations to improve their system and capacities to draft, design, legislate, and implement gender responsive and inclusive laws, policies, directives, and guidelines
planEntities.parentName: Strengthened mechanisms and capacities of communities and institutions to address discriminatory gender and social norms, to prevent and respond to all forms of gender-based violence including sexual exploitation and abuse
planEntities.description: The support would be trainings, exchange forums, development of guidelines and directives, develop monitoring tools, development of disability inclusion action plan, provision of technical guidance note on inclusion of persons with additional vulnerabilities, close engagement with OPDs, targeting of female-headed households, persons with disabilities, and other vulnerable groups for provision of food security assistance, support printing and dissemination of the Gender Equality and Women Empowerment Policy, monitoring visits for the implementation of GEWE Commitments. Provide technical and financial support for the finalization of the Family Code of Afar and Somali regions.

planEntities.name: Support and mobilize individuals, families, community/religious leaders and local community structures to promote positive and equitable social norms and PSEA
planEntities.parentName: Strengthened mechanisms and capacities of communities and institutions to address discriminatory gender and social norms, to prevent and respond to all forms of gender-based violence including sexual exploitation and abuse
planEntities.description:
Develop/implement structured community mobilization tools, facilitate structured community conversations, awareness raising sessions, capacity building training, facilitate public declarations, media campaigns, uncut girls’ movement, community-based complaint handling mechanisms, establish and strengthen confidential, and accessible reporting channels.
Provision of PSEA and SBCC sensitization sessions and materials within food security programs to beneficiaries and communities, participation in national PSEA in-country network, chairing of two sub-national PSEA networks in Somali and Afar

planEntities.name: Provide technical and financial support to institutions/service providers (health, justice, and social sector) to providing quality, coordinated, accessible, survivor and youth friendly essential services to youth, women and girl survivors of GBV, SEA and harmful practices
planEntities.parentName: Strengthened mechanisms and capacities of communities and institutions to address discriminatory gender and social norms, to prevent and respond to all forms of gender-based violence including sexual exploitation and abuse
planEntities.description: Establish and strengthen safe houses, one stop centers, women and girls friendly spaces, strengthen referral linkages, provide training to service providers, procure equipment and consumables to service providers, raise awareness of community on availability of services, provision of GBV and child protection safe referral trainings  to humanitarian actors, implementation of gender-transformative nutritional sensitive programs, strengthen the national and regional child protection coordination structures including Anti-HTP.

planEntities.name: Build capacities of Women, Youth and Persons with Disability in decision-making processes across sectors and at all levels
planEntities.parentName: Increased participation and representation of women, young people and other marginalized groups including adolescent girls in the multi-sectoral decision-making process
planEntities.description: Train women from regions and universities on leadership and decision making, Strengthen the capacity of  women development union on basic financial literacy, Capacity building of Organizations of Persons with Disabilities, meaningful engagement with OPDs and linking with food management committees, camp management committees.

planEntities.name: Increase the proportion of smallholder farmers, agro-pastoralists, and pastoralists accessing and adopting climate-resilient inputs, technology, or good practices across the food supply chain to enhance productivity and competitiveness
planEntities.parentName: Improved access and adoption of inputs, technologies and practices for the production of nutrient dense food and an inclusive and resilient food system
planEntities.description: This sub-output aims to enhance productivity and competitiveness by expanding smallholder, agro-pastoralist and pastoralist access to improved inputs, climate-smart technologies, digital solutions, post-harvest innovations, and One Health–related laboratory and surveillance services. Efforts will focus on strengthening production, storage, processing, and market functions through technologies and practices that improve efficiency, quality, and resilience in the food supply chain. The sub-output will also support initiatives to promote awareness, demand creation and consumption to enhance the 'farm to folk' principle.

planEntities.name: Support effective agri-food system service delivery through strengthened institutional systems and workforce capacities
planEntities.parentName: Improved access and adoption of inputs, technologies and practices for the production of nutrient dense food and an inclusive and resilient food system
planEntities.description: This sub-output focuses on improving capacities across institutions, systems, and value-chain actors to deliver high-quality, inclusive and resilient agri-food services. It includes strengthening surveillance systems, food safety and quality management capacities, and workforce development using a One Health approach, ensuring that public and private actors have the skills, infrastructure and coordination mechanisms needed for effective implementation. The sub-output will also support and strengthen existing structures, especially at lower level to enhance collaboration in delivery of multisectoral nutrition sensitive interventions.

planEntities.name: Produce and implement evidence-based policy reforms and national frameworks for increased public and private sector investments
planEntities.parentName: Improved access and adoption of inputs, technologies and practices for the production of nutrient dense food and an inclusive and resilient food system
planEntities.description: This sub-output supports the implementation of key policy reforms and national food-systems initiatives by generating evidence, developing regional investment plans, conducting investment forums, and promoting regulatory frameworks for food safety, traceability, nutrition, and value addition. It aims to improve public and private sector incentives, strengthen governance structures, and accelerate inclusive and market-oriented agricultural transformation.

planEntities.name: Promote and mobilize innovative financing and de-risking mechanisms to increase access to finance for food systems actors
planEntities.parentName: Improved access and adoption of inputs, technologies and practices for the production of nutrient dense food and an inclusive and resilient food system
planEntities.description: This sub-output seeks to increase the availability of priority commodities—such as those under the Yelimat Tirufat initiative—by expanding access to affordable and inclusive financing options for actors across selected value chains. It promotes the use of blended finance, insurance schemes, credit guarantees, and other de-risking instruments to unlock capital, reduce risk exposure, and stimulate investment by both public and private actors.

planEntities.name: Increase access to market information modalities for producers through reliable, functional and updated information systems
planEntities.parentName: Improved access and adoption of inputs, technologies and practices for the production of nutrient dense food and an inclusive and resilient food system
planEntities.description: This sub-output aims to enhance the availability, quality, and usability of Market Information Systems (MIS) to support better production and marketing decisions by farmers, cooperatives, SMEs, women and youth. It includes strengthening linkages between producers and markets, improving information flow across input and output markets, and promoting digital and inclusive access pathways for underserved groups.

planEntities.name: Advance the empowerment of women, youth, persons with disabilities and marginalized groups through joint program "Strengthen Markets for Agriculture to Build Resilience and Transform Food Systems in Ethiopia (SMART- Food Systems)
planEntities.parentName: Improved access and adoption of inputs, technologies and practices for the production of nutrient dense food and an inclusive and resilient food system
planEntities.description: The SMART Food Systems Transformation Project is a joint WFP–FAO initiative funded under the SDG Fund to strengthen regional food systems governance, market integration, and climate-resilient livelihoods in Ethiopia. The project supports regions—especially Somali and Sidama—to operationalize the EFSTN Food System Councils, improve coordination across the 7 Food System Clusters, and link regional work to the national roadmap. On the ground, the project helps improve production, post-harvest management, value-addition, and market linkages for smallholder farmers, while ensuring stronger engagement of cooperatives, private sector actors, and government bureaus. It also promotes better data, planning, and investment alignment across agriculture, markets, nutrition, and climate adaptation.

planEntities.name: Anticipatory Action Systems developed and activated
planEntities.parentName: Strengthened capacity of government and communities to respond, adapt and be resilient to climate change and environmental shocks
planEntities.description: Maintain current operational anticipatory action implementation and scale-up the development of anticipatory action system in Southern Ethiopia Region to cover the southern pastoral lowlands of Ethiopia.

planEntities.name: Operational multi-hazard early warning and action systems strengthened, supported by reliable meteorological observation data, and the Multi-Hazard Early Warning Situation Room at EDRMC
planEntities.parentName: Strengthened disaster risk management systems and capacities at all levels
planEntities.description: Strengthen Ethiopia’s national meteorological observation network through the deployment and operationalization of AWS and upper-air stations. The Multi-Hazard Early Warning Situation Room at EDRMC will be established and operationalized.

planEntities.name: Children-sensitive INFORM Subnational Risk Model, as well as urban and woreda disaster risk profiles developed and updated
planEntities.parentName: Strengthened disaster risk management systems and capacities at all levels
planEntities.description: Disaster risk profiles will be developed and updated at both the urban and woreda levels. In addition, government will be supported to develop Children-sensitive INFORM Sub-national Risk Mode.

Ethiopia.name: World Health Organization
Ethiopia.organizationType: Multilateral - UN organizations excluding pooled funds

planEntities.name: Support maternal health services with wider access to skilled attendance at birth
planEntities.parentName: National health care system capacities are strengthened to ensure equitable access and utilization of integrated, resilient, and shock-responsive high-quality primary health care services, including promotion, prevention and treatment services, particularly for vulnerable and marginalized individuals
planEntities.description: UNICEF and WHO provide policy advice and strategic support to strengthen the national health system, while also supporting PHC facilities to deliver quality maternal, newborn, child, and adolescent health services in both development and humanitarian contexts. UNFPA complements this by building the capacity of health extension workers and community structures to improve awareness and access to maternal health services. In addition, WHO supports the MoH with guidance, standards, and operational tools to reorient service delivery toward people-centred, integrated maternal and child health care, including strengthening SRMNCAYH services across the life course.

planEntities.name: Sustained and equitable immunization services ensuring infants receive full protection with DTP vaccines
planEntities.parentName: National health care system capacities are strengthened to ensure equitable access and utilization of integrated, resilient, and shock-responsive high-quality primary health care services, including promotion, prevention and treatment services, particularly for vulnerable and marginalized individuals
planEntities.description: WHO and UNICEF provides technical and financial support to build resilient PHC systems that deliver immunization services, address zero-dose children, and maintain continuity of services during emergencies. UNICEF strengthens community health systems and supports social and behaviour change interventions to increase awareness and demand for vaccines. WHO complements this by building the capacity of national public health institutions, including surveillance, laboratories, emergency preparedness, and workforce development, to sustain immunization programmes and ensure health system resilience in the face of emergencies and disease outbreaks.

planEntities.name: Enhance supply and availability of tracer essential medicines at point of care in health facilities
planEntities.parentName: National health care system capacities are strengthened to ensure equitable access and utilization of integrated, resilient, and shock-responsive high-quality primary health care services, including promotion, prevention and treatment services, particularly for vulnerable and marginalized individuals
planEntities.description: WHO supports the Ministry of Health and regulatory authorities to strengthen access to medicines by providing technical assistance on supply chain management, procurement frameworks, forecasting and quantification, pharmacovigilance, and the rational use of medicines. These efforts aim to ensure that tracer essential medicines are consistently available at the point of care.

planEntities.name: Support the use of electronic community health information systems across health posts
planEntities.parentName: National health care system capacities are strengthened to ensure equitable access and utilization of integrated, resilient, and shock-responsive high-quality primary health care services, including promotion, prevention and treatment services, particularly for vulnerable and marginalized individuals
planEntities.description: WHO supports the Ministry of Health in strengthening national digital health systems by advancing DAGU and enhancing DHIS2 for better integration and use of eCHIS. This includes technical and financial support for building and maintaining digital platforms, improving routine data quality, and ensuring interoperability across systems. By reinforcing DAGU and DHIS2, health posts are better equipped to implement eCHIS and generate reliable data to guide planning, monitoring, and equitable service delivery.

planEntities.name: Enhanced reproductive health services with increased availability and uptake of modern contraceptives
planEntities.parentName: National health care system capacities are strengthened to ensure equitable access and utilization of integrated, resilient, and shock-responsive high-quality primary health care services, including promotion, prevention and treatment services, particularly for vulnerable and marginalized individuals
planEntities.description: UNFPA provides technical and financial support to strengthen the availability and accessibility of family planning and broader SRHR services at PHC level. This includes policy and strategy development, capacity building of health workers, provision of supplies, and strengthening supply chain management to ensure contraceptives and life-saving reproductive health commodities reach the last mile. WHO complements this by setting global norms and standards, providing guidance, and supporting the Ministry of Health to adapt SRHR policies and guidelines across the life course.

planEntities.name: National WASH systems, policies, and standards are strengthened to improve service delivery and sustainability
planEntities.parentName: Strengthen national and sub national capacity towards equitable access to basic, inclusive and climate-resilient WASH services and show intent to practice WASH behaviours
planEntities.description: National and regional government mechanisms and systems are strengthened to enable legislation, planning and budgeting for resilient and risk-informed, gender-responsive, equitable, inclusive, climate-resilient and energy-efficient basic WASH services and practices in development and humanitarian situations.

planEntities.name: 2gether4SRHR (Improving Access to Quality Integrated Sexual and Reproductive Health Services through Strengthening Maternity Waiting Homes in Afar Region
planEntities.parentName: National health care system capacities are strengthened to ensure equitable access and utilization of integrated, resilient, and shock-responsive high-quality primary health care services, including promotion, prevention and treatment services, particularly for vulnerable and marginalized individuals
planEntities.description:
This joint initiative, jointly implemented by UNAIDS, UNFPA, UNICEF and WHO, aims to strengthen maternity waiting homes ,expand access to quality sexual and reproductive
health (SRH) services and address the social determinants of maternal mortality in Afar region's Wasema Disrict.

planEntities.name: Etude de marché sur la digitalisation des chaînes de valeur agricole - FAO
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 2.1 Les populations,  notamment les jeunes et les femmes, disposent des compétences renforcées dans l’économie verte et bleue pour s’engager dans l’en- treprenariat et l’innovation (ODD 1, 4, 5, 8, 9, 11, 12).
planEntities.description: Mener une étude sur la digitalisation des chaines de valeur agricoles, notamment le maraichage (spéculation à cycle court et à cycle long d?origine tempéré et non tempéré) et le vivrier (banane et manioc) afin de i) mieux comprendre les opportunités d'impact de la finance numérique sur les chaînes de valeurs agricoles au Gabon, ii) faire un état des lieux des financements des chaînes de valeurs agricoles au Gabon pour pouvoir à terme répondre à la problématique de l'accès au financement par le biais de la finance numérique et iii) établir des recommandations des chaînes de valeurs les plus pertinentes et proposer des scénarios d'implémentation pour digitaliser les paiements au sein de ces chaînes de valeurs et digitaliser également des services non-financiers (les informations).

planEntities.name: Renforcement des capacités des petits producteurs du district de Dienga dans le cadre de l'amélioration de leur production et de leur productivité agro-sylvo-pastorale et la résilience de leurs systèmes culturaux
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 2.1 Les populations,  notamment les jeunes et les femmes, disposent des compétences renforcées dans l’économie verte et bleue pour s’engager dans l’en- treprenariat et l’innovation (ODD 1, 4, 5, 8, 9, 11, 12).
planEntities.description:
Ce projet dont la signature et le lancement sont prévu au cours du premier trimestre 2025 vise à renforcer les capacités techniques (maîtrise  et  application des techniques de gestion d’une exploitation agricole), organisationnelles et structurelles de 300 petits producteurs agricoles du District de Dienga, composés de 60% de femmes et de 40% d'hommes, incluant les populations autochtones. Aussi, le projet appuiera la création de 100 activités génératrices de revenus, dont 60% de celles-ci gérées par les femmes à l'issu des intervention. 
Au cours de l'année 2024, un diagnostic initial de la zone d'implémentation a permis d'identifier les besoins de 500 bénéficiaires  à travers l'organisation d'un entretien d'ensemble - sensibilisation, des focus groups avec les groupes spécifiques (femmes, jeunes, population autochtone) et des entretiens individuels. Mais également de caractériser les besoins spécifiques par spéculation, en fonction des opportunités et des potentialités agroécologiques de la zone. Ainsi, le projet a répertorié neuf (9) opportunités de développement agricole réparties entre la production vivrière, maraichère, séricicole et apicole.
Point focal de l'Intérieur : M. Jovany ILAMBI

planEntities.name: Renforcement de la production et productivité à travers la structuration des filières agricoles porteuses dans l?Estuaire et le Moyen-Ogooué
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 2.2 Les populations sont dotées d’outils et mécanismes pour s’adapter de façon durable aux effets du changement climatique, tout en améliorant leurs moyens d’existence et en promouvant leur savoir-faire endogène (ODD 1, 2, 5, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15).
planEntities.description: L'objectif global du présent projet est d'améliorer durablement la productivité et les revenus des acteurs à travers la structuration des filières agricoles porteuses dans les provinces de l'Estuaire et du Moyen-Ogooué.

planEntities.name: Assistance technique pour l'étude de faisabilité du projet d'autonomie avicole et intégrées au Gabon
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 2.2 Les populations sont dotées d’outils et mécanismes pour s’adapter de façon durable aux effets du changement climatique, tout en améliorant leurs moyens d’existence et en promouvant leur savoir-faire endogène (ODD 1, 2, 5, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15).
planEntities.description: Mettre en place un système national de production locale de poulet de chair, reposant sur six fermes avicoles intégrées et autonomes, réparties dans les provinces de l'Estuaire (Ntoum), du Moyen-Ogooué (Bifoun), de la Ngounié (Mouila), du Haut-ogooué (Franceville), du woleu-Ntem (Oyem) et Ogooué maritime (Port-gentil).

planEntities.name: Appui à l'amélioration de la gouvernance des ressources naturelles (ressources forestières, fauniques, halieutiques) pour leur contribution durable aux économies de la RDC, du Cameroun et du Gabon
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 2.3 Les institutions nationales et locales et les populations locales, notamment les jeunes et les femmes, définissent et appliquent des solutions fondées sur la nature pour gérer et conserver les ressources naturelles, et prennent des décisions à cet égard
planEntities.description: Répondre aux lacunes, insuffisances et faiblesses observées dans la gouvernance des naturelles renouvelables en Afrique centrale afin d'apporter des solutions durables adaptées au contexte et aux capacités de ces pays.

planEntities.name: Promotion de l'Agriculture Urbaine et Péri-urbaine inclusives et innovantes pour une sécurité alimentaire et nutritionnelle durables en Afrique centrale
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 2.1 Les populations,  notamment les jeunes et les femmes, disposent des compétences renforcées dans l’économie verte et bleue pour s’engager dans l’en- treprenariat et l’innovation (ODD 1, 4, 5, 8, 9, 11, 12).
planEntities.description: Mettre en place un mécanisme pour identifier les agripreneurs jeunes ou femmes, qui ont mis en place des solutions innovantes et de soutenir certains d'entre eux dans la consolidation de leurs acquis. Le projet vise également à sensibiliser les municipalités dans leur besoin d'accompagner et de soutenir l'Agriculture urbaine et peri-urbaine (Ag UrPerUb) en développant leurs capacités techniques et communicationnelles autour de l'Ag UrPerUb.

Gabon.organizationType: Multilateral - UN organizations excluding pooled funds

planEntities.name: Appui à l'élaboration du PAN de lutte contre les pires formes de travail des enfants
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 1.1 Le cadre légal et institutionnel et les capacités des  institutions de bonne gouvernance (notam- ment le Parlement, le Commis- sion Nationale de Lutte contre la Corruption et l’Enrichissement Illicite, le Ministère de la bonne gouvernance, l’Initiative pour la Transparence des Industries Ex- tractives, les institutions judiciaires et la société civile) sont renforcés, y compris en matière de lutte contre la corruption, afin de garantir la gestion transparente et orthodoxe des ressources (ODD 5, 13, 16, 17).
planEntities.description: Le Gouvernement du Gabon a adhéré en mai 2025 à l'Alliance 8.7 et a élaboré la feuille de route de l'alliance 8.7. l'une des actions phare est l'élaboration du Plan d'Action National de Lutte contre les pires formes de travail des enfants. L'OIT a appuyé le gouvernement dans le renforcement des capacités des acteurs.

planEntities.name: Appui à l'organisation des élections professionnelles
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 1.1 Le cadre légal et institutionnel et les capacités des  institutions de bonne gouvernance (notam- ment le Parlement, le Commis- sion Nationale de Lutte contre la Corruption et l’Enrichissement Illicite, le Ministère de la bonne gouvernance, l’Initiative pour la Transparence des Industries Ex- tractives, les institutions judiciaires et la société civile) sont renforcés, y compris en matière de lutte contre la corruption, afin de garantir la gestion transparente et orthodoxe des ressources (ODD 5, 13, 16, 17).
planEntities.description: Depuis l’émergence du multipartisme et du pluralisme syndical dans le pays, il apparait que la désignation des organisations syndicales les plus représentatives reste la problématique préoccupante des gouvernants successifs, de l’OIT et des leaders syndicaux eux-mêmes. L'identification des organisations professionnelles des employeurs et des confédérations syndicales des travailleurs au Gabon est un processus complexe. C'est dans ce cadre que le BIT attend appuyer le Gabon dans l'organisation des élections professionnelles.

planEntities.name: Appui à l'observatoire national de l'emploi et de la formation (ONEF)
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 1.4 Le cadre juridique pour la  production des statistiques est  adopté et opérationnel et les capacités nationales dans la production, l’exploitation et la diffusion  des données et statistiques sont  renforcées en vue d’améliorer  l’élaboration et le suivi et l’évaluation des politiques publiques et  des programmes de développement (ODD 16, 17).
planEntities.description: Dans le cadre de la mise en œuvre de cette activité, l’OIT apportera un appui technique à l’ONEF, outil public stratégique d’aide à la décision au Gabon. Cet accompagnement permettra de renforcer ses capacités de collecte, de traitement, d’analyse et de diffusion des données. Ceci contribuera à améliorer la qualité, la fiabilité et l’actualité des statistiques sur l’emploi, la formation et le monde du travail. Les informations produites permettront de suivre le marché du travail, d’anticiper les besoins en compétences et d’identifier les déséquilibres.

planEntities.name: Appui à la formulation de la politique nationale de l'emploi et de la formation professionnelle
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 2.1 Les populations,  notamment les jeunes et les femmes, disposent des compétences renforcées dans l’économie verte et bleue pour s’engager dans l’en- treprenariat et l’innovation (ODD 1, 4, 5, 8, 9, 11, 12).
planEntities.description: A la demande du Gouvernement gabonais, l’OIT apporte un appui technique à la formulation de la Politique nationale de l’emploi et de la formation professionnelle. Cet accompagnement comprend la réalisation d’un diagnostic du marché du travail, le renforcement des capacités des structures de pilotage et l’organisation de consultations avec les partenaires sociaux. L’OIT appuiera également l’élaboration d’un plan d’actions opérationnel chiffré et d’un dispositif de suivi-évaluation. Cette assistance vise à doter le Gabon d’un cadre stratégique cohérent, inclusif et conforme aux normes internationales, favorisant l’emploi décent et une meilleure adéquation entre la formation et les besoins du marché du travail.

planEntities.name: Appui à la protection sociale
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 3.3 Les personnes les plus vulné- rables ont un accès accru à des filets de protection sociale et à la couverture maladie universelle. (ODD 3,5,10).
planEntities.description: A la demande du Gouvernement gabonais, le BIT appuiera la réalisation d’une étude actuarielle de la branche pensions (PVID) de la CNSS du Gabon en vue de soutenir une réforme paramétrique du régime ainsi que l'actualisation de l’Enquête de sécurité sociale pour la mise à jour des indicateurs de couverture de la protection sociale, en particulier l’indicateur ODD 1.3.

planEntities.name: Organisation de l'assistance directe, du retour et de la réintégration des migrants et victimes de traite

planEntities.description:
L’OIM Gabon œuvre à promouvoir une migration humaine, sûre et ordonnée, en plaçant les droits humains, la dignité et le bien-être des migrants au cœur de ses interventions. En étroite collaboration avec les autorités nationales et les partenaires concernés, l’Organisation contribue au renforcement des mécanismes de protection des migrants, à la réduction des vulnérabilités et à l’amélioration de l’accès aux services essentiels pour les populations les plus à risque.
À travers ses programmes d’assistance au retour volontaire et de réintégration, l’OIM Gabon accompagne les migrants de retour dans la reconstruction durable de leurs moyens de subsistance. Ces interventions visent à renforcer leur résilience socio-économique et leur autonomie grâce à la création et au développement d’activités génératrices de revenus, à l’acquisition de compétences professionnelles et au renforcement de leur employabilité. En favorisant l’accès à des opportunités économiques durables, la réintégration contribue à réduire les facteurs de vulnérabilité et à prévenir les risques de migration irrégulière répétée.
Au-delà des bénéfices individuels, les projets de réintégration produisent également un impact positif pour les communautés d’accueil et les économies locales. Ils soutiennent la création d’emplois, stimulent l’entrepreneuriat local, favorisent la circulation des compétences acquises durant le parcours migratoire et renforcent la cohésion sociale entre les migrants de retour et les populations locales. En permettant aux bénéficiaires de retrouver une place active dans leur communauté, ces interventions contribuent au développement local et à la réduction des inégalités.
Dans l’ensemble de ses activités, l’OIM Gabon veille également à promouvoir l’égalité des chances et l’inclusion de tous, en accordant une attention particulière aux besoins spécifiques liés au genre, à l’âge, au handicap ou à d’autres facteurs de vulnérabilité. Cette approche contribue à créer un environnement plus équitable, inclusif et respectueux des droits de toutes les personnes, qu’il s’agisse des migrants, des communautés d’accueil ou du personnel de l’Organisation.​‌

planEntities.description:
PACTE MONDIAL SUR LES MIGRATIONS SURES ORDONNEES ET REGULIERES 
Le Pacte mondial pour des migrations sûres, ordonnées et régulières (PMM) constitue le premier cadre mondial intergouvernemental négocié sous les auspices des Nations Unies pour aborder l’ensemble des dimensions de la migration internationale de manière holistique et intégrée. Adopté à Marrakech en décembre 2018 et entériné par l’Assemblée générale des Nations Unies, il s’agit d’un cadre de coopération non contraignant, fondé sur dix principes directeurs et vingt-trois objectifs, qui promeut une approche pan gouvernementale et pan sociétale.  
Les États Membres ont convenu que le Forum d’examen des migrations internationales (IMRF) constitue la principale plateforme mondiale pour évaluer la mise en œuvre du PMM, y compris sa pertinence pour le Programme de développement durable à l’horizon 2030, avec la participation de l’ensemble des parties prenantes concernées. Convoqué tous les quatre ans sous les auspices de l’Assemblée générale et présidé par son Président, chaque Forum se conclut par une Déclaration de progrès approuvée inter gouvernementalement. Le prochain Forum se tiendra au cours du premier semestre 2026 (mai), conformément à la résolution 73/326 de l’Assemblée générale, les dates exactes devant être confirmées par le Président de la 80e session. Dans ce cadre, des indicateurs sont mis à dispositions des Etats en vue de faciliter l’évaluation des progrès au niveau de chaque objectif de recueillir des informations et des contributions destinées à alimenter le Rapport National Volontaire qui sera utilisé lors de l’examen national volontaire du PMM avant le Forum 2026. En outre, en vue de soutenir les efforts du gouvernement gabonais, l’Union Européenne a mis à disposition des fonds pour le recrutement d’un consultant national en vue du développement du rapport.

planEntities.description:
Cette initiative opérationnalise la stratégie globale de l'OIM (2024-2028) sur l’intégration, la cohésion sociale et la lutte contre les discours de haine au Gabon en transformant la gestion des flux migratoires en un levier de stabilité et de développement local à travers une approche axée sur les résultats.

Face au déficit de données qualitatives nationales, le Bureau Pays se positionne comme un partenaire stratégique clé du gouvernement en produisant des analyses approfondies sur les perceptions intercommunautaires, fournissant ainsi aux décideurs publics une base de connaissances probantes pour moderniser les politiques d'intégration. 

Sur le terrain, l'initiative renforce durablement la paix sociale et la résilience des territoires en combinant la création d'espaces de dialogue inclusifs (impliquant migrants, communautés d'accueil et Gabonais de retour), le renforcement des capacités des acteurs institutionnels et de la société civile, ainsi qu'un engagement continu avec les médias nationaux pour déconstruire les stéréotypes et promouvoir un narratif factuel et apaisé sur la migration.

planEntities.name: Appui au renforcement de la gouvernance migratoire et de la Gestion des Frontières au Gabon
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 1.4 Le cadre juridique pour la  production des statistiques est  adopté et opérationnel et les capacités nationales dans la production, l’exploitation et la diffusion  des données et statistiques sont  renforcées en vue d’améliorer  l’élaboration et le suivi et l’évaluation des politiques publiques et  des programmes de développement (ODD 16, 17).
planEntities.description:
À travers son appui technique, l’Organisation contribue à améliorer les connaissances sur les dynamiques migratoires dans les zones frontalières stratégiques, permettant ainsi aux autorités de disposer de données probantes pour orienter les politiques publiques et renforcer la prise de décision. L’OIM soutient également le renforcement des capacités des acteurs frontaliers afin de promouvoir une gestion des frontières plus coordonnée, efficace, sensible au genre et respectueuse des droits des personnes en mobilité.

Cette intervention contribue à une meilleure prévention des risques liés à la migration irrégulière, à la traite des personnes et à la criminalité transfrontalière, tout en favorisant la protection des groupes les plus vulnérables, notamment les femmes, les enfants et les personnes à risque. En renforçant la coopération entre les institutions nationales, les communautés frontalières et les partenaires locaux, l’OIM participe également à l’amélioration de la cohésion sociale et de la résilience des territoires frontaliers.
À terme, ce soutien permettra au Gabon de disposer de mécanismes de gestion des frontières plus modernes, inclusifs et fondés sur les droits humains, contribuant ainsi à la stabilité, à la sécurité et au développement durable du pays ainsi qu’à une meilleure intégration régionale en Afrique centrale.

planEntities.description:
CLIKPAY Gabon est un établissement de paiement (émetteur de monnaie électronique) agréé auprès de la BEAC. Elle a conçu un modèle économique qui prend en compte les faiblesses de l’écosystème en place et propose un produit sur application mobile et web (CLIKPAY Business) permettant aux entrepreneurs (notamment les MPME) d’émettre et de recevoir des paiements par code QR, d’émettre des factures, de tenir une comptabilité et de payer clients et fournisseurs, d’une part ; aux particuliers d’envoyer et de recevoir de l’argent à distance et par code QR, d’acheter du crédit téléphonique, de payer ou renouveler son abonnement CANAL+, via CLIKPAY Money. CLIKPAY développe un réseau de distribution composé de marchands et d'agents sur tout le territoire du Gabon pour ses produits et services financiers numériques. Pour ce faire, elle a reçu une subvention de la part de l'UNCDF. Au terme de l'appui de l'UNCDF, CLIKPAY doit avoir atteint les objectifs suivants : 
- 340 marchands utilisant activement leurs comptes CLIKPAY Business dont 136 femmes et 136 jeunes de moins de 35 ans
- 1 650 agents utilisant activement leurs comptes CLIKPAY Business dont 660 femmes et 660 jeunes de moins de 35 ans
- 12 500 clients utilisant activement leurs comptes CLIKPAY Money dont 3 750 femmes et 5 000 jeunes de moins de 35 ans
sachant qu'un compte actif est défini comme un compte ayant enregistré au moins 1 transaction sur les 30 jours précédant le reporting.

planEntities.description:
A la suite du changement de régime opéré le 31 Aout 2023 par le Comité pour la Transition et de la Restauration des Institutions (CTRI), le Gouvernement a présenté son Plan National De la Transition (PNDT) et ses piliers dont le pilier 5 axé sur la réforme des Institutions et la transition politique. C’est dans ce contexte que le Gouvernement Japonais dans sa volonté de pouvoir accompagner cette transition à, en collaboration avec le bureau pays, mit en place le projet dénommé “Promouvoir un secteur de la justice responsable, efficace et inclusif au Gabon”.

Il s’agit d’un projet qui a pour objectif de renforcer les institutions du système judiciaire de façon à les rendre plus autonome, indépendantes et transparentes. Ceci par le biais d'une réforme globale axée sur la digitalisation de la chaine pénale et des décisions de justice, le renforcement de capacité des détenteurs du pouvoir judiciaire et sur l’appui aux acteurs de la société civile. Il contribue principalement aux ODDs n° 16, 09 et 05 et est en phase avec le Résultat 1 de notre CPD en lien avec « une bonne gouvernance et des institutions plus responsables, plus efficaces et plus transparente ».
