planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 1.6 Le cadre juridique, institutionnel et opérationnel de la décentralisation est finalisé, mis en oeuvre et financé en partie par des financement durables, pour accélérer le développement local et la réalisation des objectifs de development durable au niveau local
planEntities.description:
La dotation provinciale du chef de l'état pour la province de l'Ogooué Ivindo est un projet issue de la volonté des institutions de transition de contribuer à l’amélioration significative du niveau de vie des populations vivant dans des zones peu ou pas desservi par les infrastructures et services sociaux et économiques de base et à la réduction des inégalités sociale au niveau de la province.

Avec pour chef lieu Makokou, la province de l’Ogooué-Ivindo est divisée en quatre départements (Ivindo, Lopé, Mvoung, Zadié) et s’étend sur une superficie de 46 075Km2. Elle abritait 63 293 habitants lors du dernier recensement, composée de 49,9% de femme et de 58,2% de populations urbaines. 

L’octroi, par le Président de la transition d’une enveloppe de sept milliards de FCFA à répartir entre les villes et villages de l'Ogooué Ivindo pour la réalisation de différents projets de construction, dotation et réhabilitation, est une opportunité pour investir massivement dans des composantes clé du PUDC, dans le cadre d’une phase pilote. Les autres phases à venir du PUDC global viendront compléter les projets amorcés pour in fine offrir un package global devant permettre d’impulser un véritable développement dans la province.

planEntities.name: Skin Lightening Products
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 2.2 Les populations sont dotées d’outils et mécanismes pour s’adapter de façon durable aux effets du changement climatique, tout en améliorant leurs moyens d’existence et en promouvant leur savoir-faire endogène (ODD 1, 2, 5, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15).
planEntities.description:
Mercury-containing skin lightening products are manufactured in many countries and areas including Bangladesh, China, Dominican Republic, Hong Kong SAR (China), Jamaica, Lebanon, Malaysia, Mexico, Pakistan, Philippines, Republic of Korea, Thailand, and the United States of America (USA). Despite having been banned in many countries, mercury-containing SLPs are often easily obtainable, and consumers may be unaware of the harmful effects of the chemicals in these products. Mercury-containing skin lightening products are available for sale over the Internet, promoted online on social media sites, and sold through mobile apps. According to the United States Food and Drug Administration (FDA), these products are often manufactured abroad and sold illegally in the United States, often in small shops and informal markets catering to Latino, Asian, African or Middle Eastern communities. Consumers also purchase them in other countries and bring them back to their country.

With the entry into force of the Minamata Convention on Mercury, Parties to the Convention are required to phase out the manufacture, import, and export of mercury-containing products subject to the provisions of Article 4.   The phase out is also related to other articles, including Article 16 (health aspects), Article 17 (information exchange), and Article 18 (public information, awareness and education). These products include cosmetics with mercury content above 1ppm, including skin lightening creams and soaps. Mercury can be eliminated from SLPs by engaging different parts of society. To protect the public from negative health effects of mercury in SLPs, the proposed project seeks to support Parties implementing the Minamata Convention.

This project also presents an opportunity to educate people to admire and be proud of their natural skin tone and to stop using SLPs. Youth engagement to alter perceptions and misconception of different skin colors will be introduced through the project at both national and global levels.   Support from celebrities and artists will be used as a powerful tool to help resist the peer pressure and society preferences related to skin tone.  The toxic trade of often illegal mercury-added SLPs is a global crisis expected to only worsen with increasing demand, especially in Africa, Asia and the Middle East. Therefore, immediate action is warranted.

planEntities.description:
The funding for Survey of ODS alternatives for Gabon was approved at the 75th meeting of the Executive Committee in the amount of US $110,000 plus agency support costs for UNEP. The objective was to obtain information including data (where available) and estimates of ODS alternatives currently in use by sector and subsector, and forecasts of ODS alternatives most commonly used. The survey was submitted to the 78th Meeting of the Executive Committee. 
The Enabling Activities for HFC phase-down project was approved for Gabon at the 80th meeting of the Executive Committee in the amount of US $150,000 plus agency support costs for UNEP. The aim was to facilitate early ratification (ozone, climate and energy policy/legislation analysis, draft legislation preparation, stakeholder consultations, and cost benefit analysis of the ratification impacts); build capacity for introducing HFC alternatives (training needs assessments in the servicing sector and meetings with technicians on safe handling); develop regulatory framework for import/export licensing systems for HFC and HFC alternatives (review of methodologies for monitoring and recording of individual HFC/alternative imports/exports); prepare a national strategy for implementation (framework, HFC production and consumption information, sector profile and analysis, estimated baseline, growth prediction, alternative technology mapping, HCFC phase out linkage, potential priority areas for phase-down); and raise awareness.

planEntities.name: Improved technical capacities of primary producers and Food Business Operators to reduce food safety risks on targeted value chains
planEntities.parentName: 1.1: Improved enabling environment for inclusive, sustainable and digital economic development, delivering decent jobs, more competitive MSMEs, and fostering women’s economic empowerment.
planEntities.description: Improved technical capacities of primary producers and Food Business Operators across key value chains—including wine, hazelnut, honey, aquaculture, dairy, cereals, fruit, and vegetables—to reduce food safety risks. Sustainable management practices were introduced through EU-funded sub-grant projects, resulting in increased knowledge and enhanced skills, strengthened compliance with national and EU food safety standards, and improved adoption of good agricultural and processing practices along the targeted value chains.

planEntities.name: Land consolidation for Georgia designed and piloted
planEntities.parentName: 1.1: Improved enabling environment for inclusive, sustainable and digital economic development, delivering decent jobs, more competitive MSMEs, and fostering women’s economic empowerment.
planEntities.description: Georgian government will be supported to develop a land consolidation instrument in Georgia and build up a National Land Consolidation Programme to contribute to agricultural development by reducing land fragmentation and facilitating voluntary farm enlargement.

planEntities.name: Improved operational capacities of NFA, Revenue Services (RS) and Scientific Research Centre of Agriculture (SRCA) to implement an effective Sanitary and Phyto-sanitary (SPS) and food safety official control system.
planEntities.parentName: 1.2. Relevant institutions, rural communities and businesses have enhanced capacities to promote and participate in a diversified, green, competitive, and inclusive rural economy, and in sustainable agri-food systems.
planEntities.description: The operational capacities of the National Food Agency (NFA), Revenue Service (RS), and Scientific Research Centre of Agriculture (SRCA) will be strengthened to implement an effective Sanitary and Phyto-sanitary (SPS) and food safety control system. Planned activities include aligning public policies with EU directives, enhancing the TRACES system for traceability, certifying NFA operations under ISO 9001:2015, and supporting the Risk Analysis Coordination Platform to provide evidence-based guidance. These measures will improve institutional capacities, inter-agency coordination, and Georgia’s ability to ensure a robust, EU-aligned SPS and food safety system.

planEntities.name: Enhanced food safety and the competitiveness of the livestock sector through improvement of the National Animal Identification, Registration and Traceability System
planEntities.parentName: 1.2. Relevant institutions, rural communities and businesses have enhanced capacities to promote and participate in a diversified, green, competitive, and inclusive rural economy, and in sustainable agri-food systems.
planEntities.description: Food safety and the competitiveness of the livestock sector will be enhanced through the continued strengthening of the National Animal Identification, Registration and Traceability System (NAITS). FAO will reinforce NAITS and the Farm Management System (FMS) through awareness-raising, targeted capacity building, policy alignment, and technical upgrades to ensure effective animal identification, traceability, and compliance with national and international standards. Information materials and farm-level trainings will be delivered to livestock keepers to improve data recording, animal health management, and responsible production practices, contributing to stronger disease control systems and improved market access.

planEntities.name: Enabled environment for low-emission livestock practices created
planEntities.parentName: 1.3. Capacities of institutions and communities are enhanced for inclusive climate action, disaster risk reduction, and resilient, risk-informed development.
planEntities.description: The objective is to facilitate the reduction of farm-level methane intensity and greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions across the livestock sector in Georgia by supporting the formulation and adoption of enabling policies, standards and regulations to enhance the sector resilience to climate change, contribute to national and international emission reduction targets, and ensure policies are aligned with safeguarding farmers' livelihoods and promoting sustainable livestock practices.

planEntities.name: Farmers and agri-food producers have enhanced lifelong learning and practical capacities through participatory Farmer Field Schools
planEntities.parentName: 2.1. The education system has increased capacities to deliver accessible, inclusive and life-long quality education and training.
planEntities.description: Farmers and agri-food producers will enhance their lifelong learning and practical capacities through participatory Farmer Field Schools (FFS), strengthened extension services, and hands-on training delivered across key value chains. FAO will promote experiential, field-based learning approaches that enable producers to apply improved agricultural practices directly within their farms and communities. Training programmes will focus on good agricultural practices, food safety standards, climate-smart agriculture, integrated pest management, animal health.

planEntities.name: Rural communities have strengthened resilience and reduced vulnerabilities through small-scale socio-economic and rural infrastructure investments
planEntities.parentName: 2.3. The social protection system has improved capacities to identify and respond to population needs and socio-economic changes, including unexpected shocks, thereby reducing life-cycle vulnerabilities for all.
planEntities.description:
Rural communities in Georgia will be supported through small-scale social and infrastructure investments designed to enhance local resilience, improve access to public services, and reduce vulnerabilities throughout the life cycle. Under the Community Support Scheme, selected communities in Martvili and Kaspi municipalities will receive targeted assistance to strengthen water supply and irrigation systems, improve educational infrastructure, and enhance local tourism services.
Gender-responsive, socially inclusive, and participatory rural development will be promoted through these investments, contributing to improved rural livelihoods and greater community resilience.
Local Action Groups (LAGs) and other community-based organizations will be strengthened as community-driven mechanisms for identifying local needs and opportunities and guiding inclusive investments. At least 50 percent of supported investments will prioritize women-led initiatives, while the systematic inclusion of youth in governance and decision-making processes will be promoted.
Gender-responsive, socially inclusive, and youth-focused rural development will also be advanced through targeted policy support to national and municipal authorities, together with the strengthening of participatory planning and governance approaches in selected municipalities, including Martvili and Kaspi. Technical assistance will focus on integrating gender equality, youth engagement, and social inclusion into local development strategies, agricultural policies, and rural investment plans.
Capacity-building activities will enhance the ability of municipal authorities, LAGs, and community stakeholders to apply inclusive planning tools, conduct gender-sensitive analyses, and ensure the meaningful participation of women, youth, and vulnerable groups in decision-making processes.

planEntities.name: Institutions have strengthened capacities to design and implement evidence-based, nutrition-sensitive policies and programs, promote healthy diets
planEntities.parentName: 2.2. Capacities of institutions and service providers are enhanced to deliver inclusive quality health and social services, address key health risks, promote well-being, and reach the most vulnerable.
planEntities.description: FAO will support the strengthening of national capacities to improve food security and nutrition outcomes through evidence-based, inclusive and rights-based policy development. FAO will provide technical assistance to enhance nutrition policies in Georgia, with a particular focus on promoting healthy diets and addressing all forms of malnutrition. FAO will assess the feasibility of organic school gardens in selected municipalities (Kaspi and Martvili) and pilot the programme as an entry point for school health and nutrition.

planEntities.name: Quality of life of small-holder women dairy, fruits and vegetable producers in Abkhazia is improved
planEntities.parentName: 4.2. Conflict-affected people have improved access to essential services, livelihoods and strengthened protection of human rights.
planEntities.description: The economic resilience for small-scale female farmers in Samegrelo-Zemo Svaneti and Abkhazia  will be strengthened  through Farmer Field Schools.

planEntities.name: Strengthening Civic Space through Inclusive Rural Participation in Georgia
planEntities.parentName: 3.2. Civic space, intra-societal dialogue and social cohesion are strengthened.
planEntities.description: The skills, capacities, and resilience of civic actors—particularly youth-led and community-based organizations—to engage effectively in decision-making processes will be strengthened. FAO will ensure strong outreach to rural communities and youth through existing local and national platforms. Implementation will be carried out in close partnership with OHCHR, UNFPA and local CSOs, youth advisory councils, youth-led organizations, and relevant public institutions, local municipalities

planEntities.name: Climate resilient and DRR solutions for pasture rehabilitation and increased productivity promoted
planEntities.parentName: 1.3. Capacities of institutions and communities are enhanced for inclusive climate action, disaster risk reduction, and resilient, risk-informed development.
planEntities.description: This sub-output aims to build capacity and increase the level of awareness about climate change of existing groups of farmers, and supporting them in establishing formal pasture users associations (PUAs). This will be done through demonstrations on collective pasture management approaches and methodologies for improving grassland productivity and on introducing modern, innovative, climate resilient and cost-effective milk production technologies. In particular, PUAs will be trained to design, develop and implement community-based Pasture Management Plans (PMP's) that will integrate Climate Change adaptation resilience and disaster risk reduction measures.

planEntities.name: Supporting the climate resilience of market vulnerable smallholdêrs
planEntities.parentName: 1.1: Improved enabling environment for inclusive, sustainable and digital economic development, delivering decent jobs, more competitive MSMEs, and fostering women’s economic empowerment.
planEntities.description:
This sub-output will target women and youth-headed households and the landless poor to reduce pressures on the ecological services and thereby improve agricultural productivity. This will be
achieved through pilots promoting complementary, non-competitive and non-extractive forms of livelihoods that are not directly dependent on these eco-services. This sub-output will also promote
energy-saving and climate-smart pilots that will build climate change adaptation through mechanisation hereby improving the quality of the dairy produce.

planEntities.parentName: 1.1: Improved enabling environment for inclusive, sustainable and digital economic development, delivering decent jobs, more competitive MSMEs, and fostering women’s economic empowerment.
planEntities.description: National governments, business support organizations, and employers' and workers' organizations will be equipped to design, implement, and monitor evidence-based policies, measures, and services that advance productive employment, enterprise sustainability, and formalization. Technical assistance and capacity development interventions strengthen institutional foundations for sound labour market governance and responsible business practices, including the development and application of minimum wage policies. Gender equality and women's economic empowerment are mainstreamed as cross-cutting priorities across all policy and institutional processes, while dedicated support for green and digital economic transitions ensures that frameworks remain responsive to structural shifts in the world of work.

planEntities.name: Enhanced capacities of enterprises and employment services to support decent work and sustainable enterprise development

planEntities.description: Targeted capacity development interventions support MSMEs, employment service providers (State Employment Support Agency), and skills development and apprenticeship institutions to strengthen service delivery and operational performance. Enterprises are supported to adopt innovative, sustainable, and gender-responsive business practices that generate quality employment and contribute to broader economic resilience. Employment services are strengthened to deliver active labour market programmes that are inclusive, demand-driven, and aligned with national development priorities.

Institutional capacities of training providers and sectoral bodies are enhanced to design and implement gender-responsive curricula, assessment frameworks, and apprenticeship pathways that expand access and improve outcomes for women, youth, and other groups facing barriers to decent work.

planEntities.name: Legislative and regulatory frameworks in the world of work developed to reflect international human rights and labour standards
planEntities.parentName: 3.1. National and local institutions have enhanced capacities for promoting human rights, gender equality, an inclusive and accessible justice system in line with international commitments, and for fostering inclusive governance and effective decentralization.
planEntities.description: Labour legislation and related regulatory instruments are supported to progressively align with international human rights norms and the fundamental principles and rights at work, including freedom of association, collective bargaining, and the elimination of forced labour, child labour, and discrimination. Technical and advisory support strengthens the capacity of national institutions and social partners to lead rights-based legislative reform, ensuring that legal frameworks are coherent, implementable, and reflective of the needs and voices of all workers, including those in vulnerable and underrepresented groups.

planEntities.name: National social protection policies revised and reformed to progressively extend coverage, enhance comprehensiveness, and increase adequacy of benefits
planEntities.parentName: 2.3. The social protection system has improved capacities to identify and respond to population needs and socio-economic changes, including unexpected shocks, thereby reducing life-cycle vulnerabilities for all.
planEntities.description: National governments are equipped to reform social protection policies that expand coverage, improve benefit adequacy, and enhance comprehensiveness across the life cycle. Special emphasis is placed on strengthening unemployment insurance frameworks to deliver accessible and rights-based income protection for workers facing job loss or labour market transitions.

planEntities.name: Strengthened justice systems and dispute resolution mechanisms for improved access to justice in the world of work

planEntities.description: Legal, institutional, and procedural mechanisms that enable workers, employers, and vulnerable groups to seek and obtain justice in the world of work are strengthened. planEntities.name: Extent that policy measures are in place to enable the enhancement and/or implementation of Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) under the Paris Agreement with UN's support

planEntities.description: Policy frameworks integrate Just Transition principles, ensuring that climate mitigation and adaptation actions contribute to decent work, social protection, and inclusive economic transformation. In collaboration with the International Labour Organization, the policies promote labour-market responsive climate strategies, including green job creation, workforce reskilling, social dialogue, and protection of workers and communities affected by the transition to low-carbon economies.

planEntities.name: Capacity building activities to ensure clean energy for all and energy connectivity
planEntities.parentName: 1.4. National and local institutions and communities have adequate capacities and tools to advance environmental governance, protect biodiversity, manage natural resources sustainably, and reduce pollution.
planEntities.description:
1/ To strengthen national capacities in the target countries for the development of comprehensive digital governance policies to better plan and manage integrated power systems for an inclusive and gender-responsive sustainable digital transformation of the energy sector. 
The project is grounded in the understanding that many countries with special needs face fragmented governance systems, outdated and/or damaged infrastructure, and limited technical capacity to integrate digital technologies into power systems. Without structured and inclusive policy frameworks, efforts to deploy smart grids and decentralized renewable energy technologies often remain ad hoc, vulnerable to rebound effects, and unable to ensure interoperability with legacy systems. Additionally, the digital divide, cybersecurity risks, and underrepresentation of women and marginalized groups in energy decision-making processes further hinder the inclusiveness and sustainability of the energy transition. 
To address these challenges, the project will support target countries – Belarus, Tajikistan, Egypt, Jordan, Mongolia, and Georgia – to develop national digital governance frameworks tailored to their energy system contexts (OP1.1). These frameworks will be complemented by capacity-building workshops (OP1.2) and the creation of a harmonized policy toolkit (OP1.3), helping policymakers and regulators apply digital governance principles in planning, managing, and regulating smart grid systems. 
In parallel, the project will facilitate increased cross-country cooperation through the establishment of a regional platform for knowledge exchange on digital energy governance (OP2.1). This platform will foster peer learning, mentorship, and the sharing of best practices among national institutions, regional actors, and the private sector. Policy briefs and country case studies (OP2.2) will summarize key insights and inform ongoing reforms, while national training events (OP2.3) will reinforce technical capacity and promote a responsible and inclusive digital transition.

2/ To enhance energy system resilience through regional cooperation and energy connectivity. Supporting increased energy security and resilience through energy transition. This project aims to help Member States increase their capacity to develop energy transition initiatives that improve energy security, design and implement regionally interconnected, resilient and sustainable energy systems, and develop and mainstream gender-sensitive energy policies[1] to energy access .

planEntities.description: The programme contributes to strengthening national legislative and policy frameworks to better uphold sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR) and to advance health and personal safety education. It supports the development and institutionalization of evidence-based policies, standards, and guidelines, while enhancing the technical and institutional capacities of relevant national stakeholders to effectively implement these frameworks. Through sustained engagement with public institutions and sectoral actors, the programme promotes a coordinated and rights-based approach to SRHR and to the delivery of comprehensive, age-appropriate health and personal safety education. At the same time, the programme places strong emphasis on empowering rights holders by expanding their knowledge, agency, and opportunities for meaningful participation. Particular focus is placed on strengthening youth civic engagement and enabling adolescents and young people to actively contribute to discussions and initiatives related to their health and rights. In partnership with educational institutions and youth-serving organizations, the programme supports the provision of age-appropriate, evidence-based information on sexual and reproductive health and rights, helping adolescents develop the knowledge, skills, and confidence needed to make informed decisions, protect their wellbeing, and advocate for their rights within their communities.

planEntities.name: Supporting the creation of an enabling environment to address gender inequality and contributing to the prevention and elimination of gender-based violence and harmful practices against women and girls.
planEntities.parentName: 3.1. National and local institutions have enhanced capacities for promoting human rights, gender equality, an inclusive and accessible justice system in line with international commitments, and for fostering inclusive governance and effective decentralization.
planEntities.description:
The programme contributes to strengthening policy frameworks aimed at preventing and responding to gender-based violence (GBV) and harmful practices, while promoting a more enabling environment for gender equality. It supports the enhancement of institutional capacities of relevant national stakeholders to design, coordinate, and implement effective prevention and response mechanisms. Through policy dialogue, technical support, and multi-sectoral engagement, the programme promotes the adoption and operationalization of standards, protocols, and coordination mechanisms that enable institutions to respond to GBV in a more systematic, survivor-centred, and accountable manner.
In parallel, the programme seeks to strengthen the capacities and opportunities of rights holders to actively advance women’s rights and contribute to transformative, bottom-up social change toward greater gender equality and respect for human rights. This includes supporting initiatives that enhance the effectiveness of referral pathways and inter-agency coordination mechanisms for the prevention of and response to GBV; promoting family-friendly workplace models through partnerships with the private sector to encourage more equitable work environments; and raising public awareness to challenge harmful gender norms and stereotypes. The programme also contributes to the generation of evidence and knowledge products to inform policy dialogue and decision-making, while supporting the delivery of survivor-centred services for individuals affected by GBV and harmful practices. Through these combined efforts, the programme seeks to strengthen both institutional responses and community engagement in addressing the root causes and consequences of gender inequality and violence

planEntities.name: Ensuring equal rights and opportunities for women and men in family and public life, aiming to reduce gender discriminatory attitudes and practices in institutional and community spheres, including unpaid domestic and care work (EU4GE)
planEntities.parentName: 2.3. The social protection system has improved capacities to identify and respond to population needs and socio-economic changes, including unexpected shocks, thereby reducing life-cycle vulnerabilities for all.
planEntities.description: To ensure equal rights and opportunities for women and men in family and public life, the programme contributes towards the prevention of gender-based violence and has a strong focus on working with men and youth as drivers of change. Building on the successes of the first phase, the programme promotes non-discriminatory relations and roles, with a particular emphasis on shifting stereotypes and strengthening men’s involvement in unpaid care and domestic work. The programme also targets the private sector to strengthen family-friendly policies, including the creation of parent-friendly workplaces, and the promotion of responsible fatherhood and the uptake of parental leave.                                                                                                                                                        Key interventions are based on good examples for reaching out to men and promoting engaged fatherhood through interventions such as Fathers’ Schools, aiming at encouraging more men to become engaged fathers and supportive partners, contributing to transformation and the prevention of violence against women and children. Aiming to educate and engage youth to trigger positive change, the programme reaches out to young persons to strengthen their skills and capacities to promote equality in local communities.

planEntities.name: Transforming negative gender stereotypes, social norms and attitudes that condone violence against women and harmful practices (Gender Equality for Georgia)
planEntities.parentName: 2.3. The social protection system has improved capacities to identify and respond to population needs and socio-economic changes, including unexpected shocks, thereby reducing life-cycle vulnerabilities for all.
planEntities.description: The programme aims to address gender equality gaps by transforming discriminatory stereotypes, social norms, and attitudes that condone violence against women and harmful practices. It supports women’s empowerment and seeks to increase women’s participation in social and community life. A strong focus of the programme is empowering adolescents and youth through the Youth for Social Change initiative, equipping them with the knowledge and skills needed to contribute to building more inclusive and equal societies at the local level. The programme also aims to protect youth, women, and girls from emerging forms of digital violence by promoting digital safety through youth-friendly, non-formal educational resources. Interventions further focus on strengthening engagement and access to essential information on health and rights for ethnic minority youth, while supporting innovative communication approaches that promote social norm change and advance the rights of women and girls. In addition, the programme works with men and boys to promote non-violent, respectful, and caring partnerships, contributing to more harmonious and equitable societies.

planEntities.name: Strengthened the capacity of systems and institutions to respond to demographic change by providing accessible and high-quality SRH information and services and addressing gender-based violence and harmful practices for those furthest left behind
planEntities.parentName: 2.2. Capacities of institutions and service providers are enhanced to deliver inclusive quality health and social services, address key health risks, promote well-being, and reach the most vulnerable.
planEntities.description:
To strengthen institutional capacity to respond to demographic shifts, UNFPA—together with UN partners—works to dismantle structural and behavioral barriers that limit the quality and reach of essential services. Through targeted advocacy and policy dialogue, the UNFPA promotes adequate public investment in resilient health systems capable of delivering integrated sexual and reproductive health (SRH) services. These efforts aim to ensure that women and girls, particularly those in marginalized communities, can access timely and quality care, ultimately reducing maternal health risks.
Key interventions focus on advocacy for integrating family planning into universal health coverage and introducing routine mental health screening for pregnant women. To address maternal mortality, the activity supports the introduction of the National Obstetric Surveillance and Response System (OSRS) for Near-Miss Maternal Morbidities, linking data-driven insights directly to life-saving clinical actions. In parallel, partnerships with professional medical associations help refine clinical protocols that address the needs of women and girls with disabilities and establish professional standards to advance a collaborative, midwifery-led model of care. Also, acceleration of the national rollout of cervical cancer screening through the operationalization of an electronic registry for HPV testing and data analysis.

The project in cooperation with UNDP and OHCHR aims to increase the autonomy and dignity of PwDs in healthcare services by focusing  mainly on informed consent in the health sector in line with the CRPD articles 12 and 25, General Comment #1 (2014). The programme will leverage its partnerships the ministry, experts and underrepresented groups to ensure advancement of services and policies for PwDs.

planEntities.name: Support Increased Access to Basic Quality SRH Services in Abkhazia, Georgia
planEntities.parentName: 4.2. Conflict-affected people have improved access to essential services, livelihoods and strengthened protection of human rights.
planEntities.description: This intervention is designed to ensure the uninterrupted delivery of life-saving services despite significant political and geographic constraints. By focusing on the continuity of essential sexual and reproductive health (SRH) services, the activity provides conflict-affected women with direct access to critical care, including family planning counseling and free cervical cancer screenings. As a primary provider in the region, UNFPA continues to supply modern contraceptives and reproductive health commodities to address the high level of unmet needs. To reach women in remote and underserved communities, mobile medical teams conduct regular outreach missions, offering on-site maternal care consultations and diagnostic services. Parallel to these grassroots efforts, the activity focuses on enhancing health referral mechanisms for high-risk pregnant women, ensuring their safe and timely transfer to Tbilisi-Administered Territories for specialized care. Association for Social Rights will be Implementing Partner, that received the SMR non-objection confirmation.

With this aim, UNFPA will further strengthen the capacities of medical personnel through a cascade training approach, enabling trained professionals to transfer knowledge and skills within their respective facilities. In addition, practical workshops will be organized to facilitate peer learning among representatives of medical institutions, strengthen inter-sectoral coordination, and promote a comprehensive, survivor-centred response to GBV/VAW/DV across the health system. Association for Social Rights will be Implementing Partner, that received the SMR non-objection confirmation

Support will be extended to key national institutions—including the CRC Commission,  High Council of Justice, Ministry of Internal Affairs, Ministry of Justice, Prosecutor’s Office, Legal Aid Service, Forensic Bureau, and State Care Agency—to advance systemic specialization standards and enhance capacities for delivering child sensitive justice services. Additionally, collaboration with the Public Defender’s Office and major actors will facilitate the development of a comprehensive communication strategy and child friendly information materials to strengthen children’s understanding of their rights and available justice mechanisms.

planEntities.description:
The aim of this intervention is to strengthen the capacity of Georgia’s national and local systems to prevent and respond to violence against children (VAC). Support will be provided to relevant authorities to develop a comprehensive policy framework and address legislative gaps. At the municipal level, targeted assistance will help design and introduce evidence‑based prevention services.
The intervention will work with relevant actors to create child‑friendly informational materials on VAC and promote parenting programmes through central agencies and civil society partners. Technical support will be provided to the Inter‑agency Commission on the Implementation of the CRC and all involved institutions to ensure child‑friendly, inter‑agency, and multidisciplinary responses to child victims of all forms of violence, including through the expansion and strengthening of the Barnahus model.

planEntities.description:
This intervention aims to strengthen Georgia’s child protection system by enhancing the capacity, coordination, and professionalism of the social service and child welfare workforce. It will provide advocacy and technical assistance to all relevant central and municipal agencies and other actors to develop a comprehensive conceptual vision for strengthening the social service workforce nationwide. The programme will also reinforce supportive supervision for social workers and other professionals to improve the quality and effectiveness of child protection services.
In parallel, technical assistance will be provided to childcare and judiciary systems, as well as municipalities, to strengthen services that prevent family separation, ensure separation decisions prioritize the child’s best interests, improve the quality of alternative care, and support sustainable reintegration for children returning to their families.

planEntities.description: This focuses on strengthening national human rights monitoring mechanisms to ensure effective and timely collection and analysis of data on children and families. It includes support to the Public Defender’s Office for child rights education and thematic monitoring, technical assistance to municipalities to introduce Child Rights Impact Assessments, and collaboration with GeoStat and the Administration of the Government to integrate child related data into national statistical systems. It also covers capacity building for educators and academic institutions to better interpret and use child focused data.

Efforts will also focus on promoting policy dialogue and advocacy for the adoption and expansion of universal child cash benefits as an effective measure to reduce child poverty and strengthen income security for families. To advance disability‑inclusive reform, UNICEF will support the development of tailored service packages for children with disabilities, fostering their inclusion, autonomy, and independent living. Through dedicated studies, new data and evidence will be generated to identify the barriers families with children face in accessing formal employment, as well as the support systems that children and young people currently have, or lack, within their immediate communities to ensure an adequate standard of living. Findings from these studies will inform policy recommendations for the government and other stakeholders, contributing to the development of a more inclusive and equitable social protection system.

planEntities.name: Enhancing early warning systems by using genomic surveillance and One Health approach in Georgia
planEntities.parentName: 1.3. Capacities of institutions and communities are enhanced for inclusive climate action, disaster risk reduction, and resilient, risk-informed development.
planEntities.description:
The proposed project intends to address the key pandemic prevention, preparedness, and response
(PPR) challenges identified by the JEE 2019 and the 2019 ECDC review, using the One Health
approach to enhance national PPR and strengthen Georgia’s core capacities under the International
Health Regulations (IHR). The project will target gaps identified in the surveillance and the
national laboratory systems and improve regional and local surveillance capacity for both animal
and human health adhering with the one health approach, addressing geographical inequities. As a
cross cutting intervention, under the project will also be conducted a gender gap assessment to
followed by a gender-sensitive data collection and training, with results shared in workshops,
community engagements, and annual reports.

The project objectives focused on building the early warning system (EWS) and AMR surveillance
systems using the One Health approach is fully aligned with the strategic objectives of the National
Action Plan for One Health System Development 2023-2025 and National AMR Strategy
2024-2030 and National AMR Action Plan 2024-2026. The gaps described above will be addressed
by monitoring threats through community and event-based surveillance (EBS) and EWS that
collect, assess, and report potential risks occurring in agricultural settings; implementing sentinel based
surveillance (including for novel influenza strains and AMR) selected industrial and
backyard farms located in vulnerable communities in Georgia; and conducting activities in close
multisectoral collaboration under a unified One Health approach for data collection from farm
animals and poultry, farmers, and the surrounding environment and communities.

planEntities.name: Natural Resources and Biodiversity including protected Areas sustainably Managed for Environmental Protection and Livelihood enhancement
planEntities.parentName: Government institutions and other stakeholders’ capacities are strengthened to mitigate, and adapt to climate change, and respond to disasters in a timely manner
planEntities.description:
Under the Integrated Environment and Climate Resilience Programme (IEMCRP), this outcome aims to conserve and sustainably manage natural resources and biodiversity, including protected areas, while enhancing livelihoods and strengthening ecosystem resilience. The programme recognizes healthy ecosystems as the foundation for environmental protection, climate resilience, and sustainable socio‑economic development.

The programme focuses on strengthening policy, legal, and institutional frameworks for biodiversity conservation, natural resource governance, and protected area management. It supports the implementation of ecosystem‑based approaches to address land degradation, deforestation, habitat loss, and biodiversity decline, while promoting alignment with national development priorities and international biodiversity commitments.

At the landscape and community levels, the programme promotes sustainable land and forest management, biodiversity‑friendly agriculture, ecosystem restoration, and improved protected area management practices. Community‑based natural resource management is central, ensuring that local communities—particularly women and youth—actively participate in conservation efforts and benefit from sustainable livelihoods such as eco‑tourism, non‑timber forest products, sustainable fisheries, and nature‑based enterprises.

The programme also strengthens monitoring systems, data collection, and knowledge management to track biodiversity trends and inform adaptive management and policy decisions. By integrating conservation with livelihood enhancement, the programme reduces pressure on natural resources while increasing resilience to climate change and environmental shocks.

Overall, this IEMCRP outcome contributes to the protection and restoration of ecosystems, improved biodiversity outcomes, enhanced community livelihoods, and long‑term environmental sustainability, supporting climate resilience, food security, and inclusive green growth.

planEntities.name: Improve Chemicals and Waste Management Practices
planEntities.parentName: Government institutions and other stakeholders’ capacities are strengthened to mitigate, and adapt to climate change, and respond to disasters in a timely manner
planEntities.description:
Under the Integrated Environment and Climate Resilience Programme (IEMCRP), the Improved Chemicals and Waste Management Practices component aims to reduce environmental and health risks associated with hazardous chemicals and poorly managed waste while strengthening national capacities for sound chemicals and waste governance. The programme supports the transition towards environmentally sound management (ESM) of chemicals and waste across their life cycle, in line with national priorities and international environmental agreements.

The programme focuses on strengthening policy, regulatory, and institutional frameworks for chemicals and waste management, including the control of persistent organic pollutants (POPs), industrial chemicals, pesticides, plastics, electronic waste, solid waste and other priority waste streams. It enhances coordination among government institutions, improves compliance with international conventions, and supports the development and enforcement of standards, guidelines, and monitoring systems.

At the operational level, the programme promotes best practices in waste segregation, collection, recycling, treatment, and safe disposal, while encouraging the adoption of cleaner production methods and safer chemical alternatives. Capacity-building activities target regulators, local authorities, private sector actors, and communities to improve technical skills, awareness, and accountability. The programme also integrates gender, health, and livelihood considerations, ensuring that vulnerable groups are protected from chemical exposure and that green jobs and circular economy opportunities are promoted.

Overall, this IEMCRP outcome contributes to reduced pollution, improved public health, enhanced ecosystem resilience, and progress towards national sustainability goals, including climate resilience, biodiversity protection, and sustainable consumption and production.

planEntities.name: Climate Change and Disaster Risk Mitigation Actions strengthened for evidence-based policies and decision making
planEntities.parentName: Government institutions and other stakeholders’ capacities are strengthened to mitigate, and adapt to climate change, and respond to disasters in a timely manner
planEntities.description:
Under the Integrated Environment and Climate Resilience Programme (IEMCRP), this outcome focuses on strengthening national and subnational capacities to anticipate, plan for, and respond to climate change impacts and disaster risks through robust data, analysis, and knowledge systems. The programme prioritizes evidence‑based decision‑making to reduce vulnerability, safeguard development gains, and enhance resilience across sectors and communities.
The programme supports the generation, integration, and use of climate, environmental, and disaster risk data, including climate projections, vulnerability and risk assessments, and early warning information. It strengthens institutional frameworks for climate governance, disaster risk reduction (DRR), and climate change adaptation (CCA), enhancing coordination among responsible agencies and improving the mainstreaming of climate and disaster risk considerations into national development plans, sectoral policies, and public investment processes.
At the technical level, the programme builds capacity for climate risk assessment, scenario analysis, impact monitoring, and the application of geospatial and digital tools to support planning and policy formulation. It promotes the development and operationalization of early warning systems, contingency planning, and risk‑informed land use and infrastructure planning. Community‑based approaches are also supported to ensure that local knowledge and priorities inform policy decisions and risk mitigation actions.
Overall, this IEMCRP outcome strengthens the foundation for proactive, informed, and coordinated climate and disaster risk management, enabling more resilient development pathways, reduced losses from climate‑related hazards, and improved alignment with national climate commitments and international frameworks.

planEntities.name: Access to Clean and Renewable Energy
planEntities.parentName: Government institutions and other stakeholders’ capacities are strengthened to mitigate, and adapt to climate change, and respond to disasters in a timely manner
planEntities.description:
The programme focuses on accelerating the deployment of renewable energy technologies such as solar, wind, and hybrid mini-grids, alongside the promotion of clean cooking solutions and energy-efficient appliances. It strengthens enabling policy and regulatory frameworks, supports integrated energy planning, and enhances institutional capacity to scale up decentralized and grid-connected renewable energy systems. Special emphasis is placed on improving energy access for productive uses, including small enterprises, agriculture, health facilities, and social infrastructure.

At the community and household levels, the programme promotes clean cooking and sustainable biomass management to reduce indoor air pollution, deforestation, and health risks—particularly for women and children. Capacity development for public and private sector actors, local technicians, and communities ensures long-term operation, maintenance, and sustainability of clean energy systems. The programme also encourages private sector participation, innovative financing mechanisms, and market-based solutions to increase affordability and uptake.

Overall, this IEMCRP outcome contributes to enhanced energy security, reduced emissions, improved livelihoods, and strengthened climate resilience, while supporting national development priorities and progress towards Sustainable Development Goals on energy access, climate action, and sustainable economic growth.

planEntities.parentName: Small holder farmers and fisher folks particularly in rural and peri-urban areas adopt climate smart resilient, sustainable agricultural and natural resources management practices
planEntities.description: . The objective of the project is consequently to build the climate-resilience of rural Gambian communities and facilitate the development of a sustainable natural resource-based (green) economy by implementing large-scale EbA within and adjacent to agricultural areas, community-managed forest reserves and wildlife conservation areas. This will entail: a) restoring degraded forests and agricultural landscapes with climate-resilient plant species that provide goods for consumption or sale; and b) facilitating the establishment of commercially viable natural resource-based businesses to be managed by community-based organizations.

planEntities.name: Government institutions received technical support to strengthen national social protection systems that integrate adaptative shock responsiveness
planEntities.parentName: Government institutions and other stakeholders’ capacities are strengthened to mitigate, and adapt to climate change, and respond to disasters in a timely manner
planEntities.description:
Under the Global Shield funding, government institutions received targeted technical support to strengthen national social protection systems with a focus on integrating adaptive, shock‑responsive mechanisms. This support enhanced institutional capacity to anticipate, prepare for, and respond effectively to shocks such as climate-related crises, economic disruptions, health emergencies, and food insecurity.
Technical assistance covered key areas including policy and legal frameworks, system design, coordination mechanisms, and operational tools. Governments were supported to improve early warning systems, develop scalable and flexible social protection programmes, and strengthen data and information management systems to enable timely identification of vulnerable populations. This allowed social protection programmes—such as cash transfers, public works, or social insurance schemes—to be rapidly expanded or adapted in response to shocks.
In addition, the support promoted stronger inter‑ministerial coordination between social protection, disaster risk management, climate, health, and finance institutions, ensuring coherent and integrated responses. Capacity building activities, including training and technical guidelines, helped government staff mainstream risk‑informed and climate‑sensitive approaches into planning and budgeting processes.
Overall, this technical support contributed to more resilient, inclusive, and responsive national social protection systems that not only address chronic poverty and vulnerability but also protect households from falling into poverty when shocks occur.

planEntities.name: Comercio Verde, PYMES y Sostenibilidad en África Central
planEntities.parentName: 3.1 Integración económica, clima de negocios y de inversión nacional son mejorados a través del fortalecimiento de los marcos institucionales, legales y regulatorios.
planEntities.description:
El proyecto “Comercio Verde, PYMES y Sostenibilidad en África Central”, liderado por la Comisión Económica para África (CEA/ECA) con el apoyo de DANIDA, apoya a Guinea Ecuatorial en la integración de oportunidades de comercio verde y resiliente al clima dentro de su Estrategia Nacional de Implementación de la ZLECAf (AfCFTA).
La iniciativa, presentada en el lanzamiento virtual del proyecto, tiene como objetivo promover un crecimiento económico sostenible mediante la identificación de cadenas de valor verdes prioritarias, el fortalecimiento de la competitividad de las pequeñas y medianas empresas (PYMES) y la incorporación de medidas de adaptación climática en las políticas comerciales. Un componente central es el desarrollo de un Suplemento Verde (Green Supplement) que complementará la estrategia nacional existente, alineando comercio, sostenibilidad ambiental y diversificación productiva.
El proyecto combina análisis técnico y procesos participativos, incluyendo la revisión de políticas nacionales, marcos regulatorios, estándares ambientales y estrategias sectoriales relevantes. Asimismo, fomenta el diálogo con actores clave del sector público y privado para identificar restricciones, oportunidades de inversión verde y acciones prioritarias que faciliten la inserción sostenible del país en los mercados regionales y continentales.

Se generarán condiciones para fortalecer y consolidar capacidades preventivas, propiciar y facilitar espacios de interlocución inclusivos con un énfasis en la participación de mujeres, jóvenes y pueblos originarios y la reduccción de vulnerabilidades frente a violencia. planEntities.name: Subproducto 3.1.1. Fortalecimiento de capacidades para la gestión integral de incendios en el Corredor Seco Centroamericano.
planEntities.parentName: Producto Conjunto 3.1.1. Gobernanza de los recursos naturales y la biodiversidad
planEntities.description:
The main objective of the project is to improve capacities for integrated fire management, particularly in Guatemala, Honduras and El
Salvador targeting 84 communities across 10 departments.
The project proposes an intervention logic with three key components:
Community level actions to ensure better preparation and response through updated planning protocols, equipped and trained
brigades, early detection and alerts and coordination structures for wildfires response
Institutional action at national, departamental and municipal levels: Aimed at enhancing institutional preparedness and response
through updated protocols, improved early warning systems and historical fire data collection and analysis.
Regional Coordination within the framework of the 2025-2030 Regional Fire Management Strategy. This includes harmonization
among SICA entities, standardization of tools, collaboration with cooperation platforms and actors and regional agreements or
protocols for joint responses to complex scenarios, such as cross-border fires.
A fourth component is included as a Crisis modifier enabling a rapid and effective response to wildfire impacts, when deemed
necessary.

planEntities.name: Subproducto 2.1.2. Apoyo a las acciones post crisis para la recuperación y rehabilitación de los medios de vida y activos de los hogares de las zonas rurales mas afectadas por COVID-19.
planEntities.parentName: Producto Conjunto 2.1.2. Innovación y competitividad empresarial y sistemas alimentarios resilientes
planEntities.description: El proyecto se alinea a los esfuerzos institucionales del Gobierno de Guatemala en especial con la Secretaría de Seguridad Alimentaria y Nutricional (SESAN), el Ministerio de Agricultura, Ganadería y Alimentación (MAGA) y el Ministerio de Economía (MINECO) para atender a las y los agricultores familiares, organizaciones de productoras/es agropecuarias/os, micro y pequeñas empresas agropecuarias, que fueron afectados por la pandemia de COVID-19 en 15 municipios de los departamentos de Huehuetenango, Quiché y Alta Verapaz, municipios en donde el porcentaje de población indígena se estima mayor al promedio del nivel nacional. El proyecto busca alcanzar los siguientes productos: 1) Respuesta temprana a la recuperación y rehabilitación de los medios de vida y activos de los hogares de las zonas rurales más afectadas por COVID-19; 2) fortalecidas las capacidades de los pequeños agricultores para mejorar la calidad de los alimentos, prevenir y reducir su pérdida; 3) se apoyan las herramientas sanitarias y fitosanitarias y de trazabilidad para mejorar la resiliencia climática y la conciencia nutricional; y 4) fortalecidas las capacidades de las instituciones públicas para apoyar a los pequeños agricultores a través de intervenciones sensibles a la nutrición y para responder eficazmente a emergencias y crisis.

planEntities.name: Subproducto 2.2.1. Programa conjunto promoviendo la gestión del entorno social, político e institucional para contribuir a disminuir la conflictividad agraria en el Valle del Polochic
planEntities.parentName: Producto Conjunto 2.2.1. Protección social y sistemas de cuidado
planEntities.description: El proyecto propone mejorar el abordaje desde el rol de dirección que tiene la Comisión Presidencial por la Paz y los Derechos Humanos (COPADEH) de coordinar el cumplimiento de los compromisos internacionales en materia de derechos humanos para el abordaje de la de conflictividad agraria en el Valle del Polochic. Se implementarán estrategias de fortalecimiento de capacidades institucionales y de comunidades indígenas y campesinas, sobre el derecho a la vivienda, la tierra, el territorio y un nivel de vida adecuado, valorando el efecto diferenciado en las mujeres indígenas. En el proceso de reforma institucional llevado a cabo al inicio de 2024, y con la división de funciones entre la Secretaría Privada de la Presidencia y la Comisión Presidencial por la Paz y los Derechos Humanos, esta Comisión tiene a cargo el abordaje de las causas que generan el otorgamiento las medidas cautelares de la Comisión Interamericana de los Derechos Humanos. El objetivo fundamental es fortalecer los conocimientos y capacidades de la institucionalidad pública, a través de herramientas y habilidades, para que puedan atender las causas que generan violaciones de derechos humanos relacionadas a la conflictividad agraria en el Valle de Polochic. En adición, el proyecto fortalecerá los conocimientos y capacidades de los actores locales y las comunidades priorizadas que cuentan con medidas cautelares de la CIDH, sobre todo aquellas que no tienen certeza jurídica sobre las tierras, para que su participación en espacios de diálogo multisectorial contribuya a la gestión de los casos de conflictos agrarios que les afectan y a la prevención de futuros casos. Se espera lograr un cambio positivo en la actitud institucional en términos de querer atender proactivamente la situación de las comunidades que cuentan con medidas cautelares y de las causas estructurales que han generado los conflictos agrarios. Por lo tanto, se espera que esta iniciativa generará buenas prácticas que informarán modelos futuros para la atención de la conflictividad agraria.

planEntities.name: Subproducto 2.2.2. Programa conjunto promoviendo la gestión del entorno social, político e institucional para contribuir a disminuir la conflictividad agraria en el Valle del Polochic
planEntities.parentName: Producto Conjunto 2.2.2. Servicios básicos con acceso universal y enfoque territorial
planEntities.description: El proyecto propone mejorar el abordaje desde el rol de dirección que tiene la Comisión Presidencial por la Paz y los Derechos Humanos (COPADEH) de coordinar el cumplimiento de los compromisos internacionales en materia de derechos humanos para el abordaje de la de conflictividad agraria en el Valle del Polochic. Se implementarán estrategias de fortalecimiento de capacidades institucionales y de comunidades indígenas y campesinas, sobre el derecho a la vivienda, la tierra, el territorio y un nivel de vida adecuado, valorando el efecto diferenciado en las mujeres indígenas. En el proceso de reforma institucional llevado a cabo al inicio de 2024, y con la división de funciones entre la Secretaría Privada de la Presidencia y la Comisión Presidencial por la Paz y los Derechos Humanos, esta Comisión tiene a cargo el abordaje de las causas que generan el otorgamiento las medidas cautelares de la Comisión Interamericana de los Derechos Humanos. El objetivo fundamental es fortalecer los conocimientos y capacidades de la institucionalidad pública, a través de herramientas y habilidades, para que puedan atender las causas que generan violaciones de derechos humanos relacionadas a la conflictividad agraria en el Valle de Polochic. En adición, el proyecto fortalecerá los conocimientos y capacidades de los actores locales y las comunidades priorizadas que cuentan con medidas cautelares de la CIDH, sobre todo aquellas que no tienen certeza jurídica sobre las tierras, para que su participación en espacios de diálogo multisectorial contribuya a la gestión de los casos de conflictos agrarios que les afectan y a la prevención de futuros casos. Se espera lograr un cambio positivo en la actitud institucional en términos de querer atender proactivamente la situación de las comunidades que cuentan con medidas cautelares y de las causas estructurales que han generado los conflictos agrarios. Por lo tanto, se espera que esta iniciativa generará buenas prácticas que informarán modelos futuros para la atención de la conflictividad agraria.

planEntities.name: Subproducto 2.3.1. Fortalecimiento de la acción humanitaria en centroamérica, preparación de alianzas e integración para la seguridad alimentaria y nutricional en contextos de multiamenaza.
planEntities.parentName: Producto Conjunto 2.3.1. Politicas y marcos estratégicos intersectoriales para sistemas alimentarios sostenibles e inclusivos
planEntities.description: el proyecto busca fortalecer las capacidades de los actores clave para reducir la vulnerabilidad de las comunidades centroamericanas a las sequías e inundaciones mediante la integración del enfoque de Acción para la Reducción de Desastres (AA) en los sistemas de gobernanza regionales y nacionales. Esto se logrará mediante el fortalecimiento de la coordinación interinstitucional, la mejora de las capacidades técnicas para la respuesta humanitaria y sectorial, y la promoción de una gestión eficaz del riesgo de desastres. El objetivo también hace hincapié en el apoyo a los gobiernos para el desarrollo o fortalecimiento de los sistemas de Estrategias de Seguridad y Protección de Desastres (SRSP) con el fin de salvaguardar la seguridad alimentaria y nutricional en las comunidades vulnerables, en particular aquellas expuestas a fenómenos meteorológicos extremos. Además, fomentar el intercambio de información, las mejores prácticas y la coordinación entre Honduras, Guatemala, El Salvador y CEPREDENAC contribuirá a integrar la acción anticipatoria y los sistemas de protección social con capacidad de respuesta ante crisis en los marcos regionales y nacionales

planEntities.name: Subproducto 2.3.1. Fortalecimiento e innovación de programas, estratégias y servicios que promueven sistemas agroalimentarios eficientes y sostenibles desde el MAGA.

planEntities.name: Subproducto 2.3.1. Alimentación, Rendición de Cuentas, Derechos y Empoderamiento: fortalecimiento de mecanismos para mejorar la implementación nacional del Derecho a la Alimentación (FARE).

Indonesia, Malawi y Guatemala.
