planEntities.description:
The Promoting SME Enterprises through Improved Entrepreneurs’ Access to Financial Services (PROMISE II IMPACT) project aims to strengthen the enabling environment to drive a more inclusive financial sector for small and medium enterprises (SMEs), generating post-pandemic economic growth and employment opportunities. The project provides technical assistance support, including training, to increase the capacity of Financial Service Providers such as People's Credit Bank (Bank Perkreditan Rakyat/BPR) and Regional Development Bank (Bank Pembangunan Daerah/BPD)) to serve the SMEs in productive sectors in a select location of the project and enhance the capacity of those SMEs to expand their business and create employment.
These objectives are achieved inter alia through promoting digital transformation and strengthening the targeted SMEs' value chain and business ecosystem. In addition, the project will also support the financial service authorities and the national and regional governments to enhance financial inclusion in Indonesia further.

planEntities.name: 3.1.7 Improving OSH and social conditions for women and men in coffee farmer communities in Indonesia (Visin Zero Fund - VZF)
planEntities.parentName: CF Output 3.1 Accelerated inclusive economic transformation through policy support and innovative approaches to expand access to decent work, promote innovative financing, and accelerate sustainable and diversified growth across key sectors such as agriculture, the blue economy, and downstream industries, benefiting women, youth, persons with disabilities, and other vulnerable groups.
planEntities.description:
The project aims to improve workplace safety and health, labour law compliance, social protection and gender equality in the coffee supply chain in Indonesia. End beneficiaries include smallholder farmers and coffee collectors and their workforce: workers cultivating and collecting coffee. Its regional focus is Lampung province, South Sumatra. 

The project will contribute to strengthening workplace safety and health and access to labour rights specifically for informal economy workers in agriculture. It also aims to strengthen coffee supply chain sustainability and farmers’ livelihoods.

planEntities.name: 3.1.8 Global Accelerator on Jobs and Social Protection for Just Transition in Indonesia
planEntities.parentName: CF Output 3.1 Accelerated inclusive economic transformation through policy support and innovative approaches to expand access to decent work, promote innovative financing, and accelerate sustainable and diversified growth across key sectors such as agriculture, the blue economy, and downstream industries, benefiting women, youth, persons with disabilities, and other vulnerable groups.
planEntities.description:
On 7 June 2023, the Government of Indonesia expressed an interest in Joining the Global Accelerator initiative in the letter of the Minister of National Development Planning to the United Nations Resident Coordinator in Indonesia (B-450/D.4/HM.06.01/06/2023). The Government of Indonesia and the United Nations agreed on further collaboration through the initiative to develop and implement inclusive employment and social protection policies and programmes that would contribute to achieving Indonesia's mid- and long-term development goals. The Global Accelerator Roadmap was developed through eight rounds of the drafting committee meetings between the Government and the United Nations between August 2023 and March 2024.
To implement the roadmap two joint SDG funded programmes were developed and financed titled “Modern and adaptive social protection and skills development systems for transforming Indonesia” and “Closing disability inclusion gaps in social protection and labour across the life cycle in Indonesia”.

planEntities.description: PAGE brings together five UN agencies – UN Environment Programme (UNEP), International Labour Organization (ILO), UN Development Programme (UNDP), UN Industrial Development Organization (UNIDO), and UN Institute for Training and Research (UNITAR) – whose mandates, expertise and networks combined can offer integrated and holistic support to countries on inclusive green economy, ensuring coherence and avoiding duplication. planEntities.parentName: CF Output 2.1 Enhanced national capacities and multi-stakeholder partnerships to drive progress toward nature-positive, low-carbon, and climate-resilient development pathways, promoting inclusive environmental governance and equitable climate action for those most affected, including women, youth, persons with disabilities, and other vulnerable groups.
planEntities.description: The Fourth National Communication (NC4) project supports the Government of Indonesia in preparing its official climate reporting to the UNFCCC, including the Fourth National Communication (NC4) and Fourth Biennial Update Report (BUR4). It strengthens national capacity to review sectoral mitigation policies, update GHG emission projections, and prioritize mitigation actions aligned with Indonesia’s NDC and long‑term climate strategies. The project also enhances institutional and local capacities for GHG inventory, adaptation assessments, and monitoring climate actions, while promoting participation from ministries, subnational governments, academia, NGOs, and the private sector.

planEntities.name: 2.1.14 Catalyzing Optimum Management of Natural Heritage for Sustainability of Ecosystem, Resources and Viability  of Endangered Wildlife Species (CONSERVE)
planEntities.parentName: CF Output 2.1 Enhanced national capacities and multi-stakeholder partnerships to drive progress toward nature-positive, low-carbon, and climate-resilient development pathways, promoting inclusive environmental governance and equitable climate action for those most affected, including women, youth, persons with disabilities, and other vulnerable groups.
planEntities.description: The CONSERVE project (Catalyzing Optimum Management of Natural Heritage for Sustainability of Ecosystem, Resources and Viability of Endangered Wildlife Species) aims to strengthen the management of multiple‑use landscapes to enhance biodiversity conservation, promote sustainable land‑use and livelihoods, and combat illegal wildlife trade. Operating across Aceh (Ulu Masen), Bengkulu (Seblat), and West Nusa Tenggara (Moyo Satonda), the project addresses threats such as habitat loss, human–wildlife conflict, and poaching of key species including the Sumatran Tiger, Sumatran Elephant, and Yellow‑crested Cockatoo. Through improved landscape management, community engagement, and enforcement capacities, CONSERVE contributes to safeguarding Indonesia’s critical ecosystems and endangered wildlife.

planEntities.name: 2.1.15 Strengthening sustainability in commodity and food systems, land restoration and land use governance through integrated landscape management for multiple benefits in Indonesia.
planEntities.parentName: CF Output 2.1 Enhanced national capacities and multi-stakeholder partnerships to drive progress toward nature-positive, low-carbon, and climate-resilient development pathways, promoting inclusive environmental governance and equitable climate action for those most affected, including women, youth, persons with disabilities, and other vulnerable groups.
planEntities.description: The FOLUR Project (Strengthening sustainability in commodity and food systems, land restoration and land use governance through integrated landscape management for multiple benefits in Indonesia) aims to transform the sustainability of major commodity value chains—palm oil, coffee, cocoa, and rice—while protecting Indonesia’s high‑value forests and ecosystems. Through integrated landscape management across five key jurisdictions (Aceh, North Sumatera, West Kalimantan, South Sulawesi, and West Papua), the project strengthens policy frameworks, promotes sustainable farming practices, enhances smallholder traceability and market access, and supports conservation and restoration of natural habitats. The initiative connects biodiversity conservation with production systems to ensure long‑term environmental benefits and improved livelihoods for local communities.

planEntities.name: 2.1.9 Enhancing Readiness for the Transition to Electric Vehicles in Indonesia (ENTREV)
planEntities.parentName: CF Output 2.1 Enhanced national capacities and multi-stakeholder partnerships to drive progress toward nature-positive, low-carbon, and climate-resilient development pathways, promoting inclusive environmental governance and equitable climate action for those most affected, including women, youth, persons with disabilities, and other vulnerable groups.
planEntities.description: The ENTREV Project (Enhancing Readiness for the Transition to Electric Vehicles in Indonesia) supports Indonesia’s shift toward sustainable, low‑carbon transportation by strengthening policy, institutional, and technical readiness for Battery Electric Vehicle (BEV) adoption. It helps develop national and sub‑national regulations, innovative financing schemes, and EV charging infrastructure planning, while piloting EV ecosystem solutions across Jakarta, West Java, and Bali. Through awareness building, capacity development, and demonstration projects—including charging stations and battery‑swap systems—ENTREV accelerates market uptake of electric mobility and contributes to long-term emissions reduction.

planEntities.name: 2.1.16 Support Facility for Marine Plastic Litter Reduction Acceleration Secretariat
planEntities.parentName: CF Output 2.1 Enhanced national capacities and multi-stakeholder partnerships to drive progress toward nature-positive, low-carbon, and climate-resilient development pathways, promoting inclusive environmental governance and equitable climate action for those most affected, including women, youth, persons with disabilities, and other vulnerable groups.
planEntities.description: The Marine Debris Project, formally titled Support Facility for Marine Plastic Litter Reduction Acceleration Secretariat, is a national initiative designed to significantly reduce Indonesia’s marine plastic pollution by strengthening governance, coordination, and policy implementation across 18 ministries and key stakeholders. The project supports the Government of Indonesia in accelerating actions under the National Action Plan for Marine Debris Management (RAN PSL), including monitoring progress toward the national target of reducing marine plastic leakage by 70% by 2025. It provides technical assistance, develops integrated monitoring systems, supports regulatory harmonization, and advances innovative waste and riverine plastic management solutions. Its activities also include partnerships with donors (Norway, Danone, UAE), capacity building, and scaling interventions across priority regions to safeguard coastal ecosystems, strengthen institutional frameworks, and contribute to national and global commitments on plastic pollution

planEntities.name: 3.1.14 Seventh Operational Phase of the GEF Small Grants Programme in Indonesia (GEF‑SGP7)
planEntities.parentName: CF Output 3.1 Accelerated inclusive economic transformation through policy support and innovative approaches to expand access to decent work, promote innovative financing, and accelerate sustainable and diversified growth across key sectors such as agriculture, the blue economy, and downstream industries, benefiting women, youth, persons with disabilities, and other vulnerable groups.
planEntities.description: The Seventh Operational Phase of the GEF Small Grants Programme in Indonesia (GEF‑SGP7) empowers community‑based and civil society organizations to protect biodiversity, restore ecosystems, and strengthen climate resilience across four ecologically critical landscapes: Sabu Raijua, Nantu‑Boliyohuto, Balangtieng Watershed, and Bodri Watershed. The programme promotes participatory landscape management, renewable energy adoption, sustainable land use, and livelihood improvement while prioritizing gender equality and inclusion. Implemented from 2022–2026, SGP7 supports local action that generates global environmental benefits, enhances socio‑ecological resilience, and strengthens community leadership in natural resource governance.

planEntities.name: 2.1.17 Investing in the Komodo Dragon and other globally threatened species in Flores (IN‑FLORES)
planEntities.parentName: CF Output 2.1 Enhanced national capacities and multi-stakeholder partnerships to drive progress toward nature-positive, low-carbon, and climate-resilient development pathways, promoting inclusive environmental governance and equitable climate action for those most affected, including women, youth, persons with disabilities, and other vulnerable groups.
planEntities.description: The IN‑FLORES Project (Investing in the Komodo Dragon and other globally threatened species in Flores) focuses on safeguarding Flores Island’s unique biodiversity by protecting endangered species such as the Komodo dragon, Flores eagle, yellow‑crested cockatoo, and other terrestrial and marine wildlife. Operating across the West and North Flores landscape‑seascapes, the project addresses key threats including habitat degradation, over‑exploitation, landscape fragmentation, and pressures from mass tourism. It strengthens cross‑sector governance, supports community‑based ecosystem restoration, enhances sustainable livelihoods, and develops innovative conservation financing mechanisms. By combining conservation and sustainable development, IN‑FLORES aims to secure long‑term ecological resilience and improve community well‑being in one of Indonesia’s most critical biodiversity hotspots.

planEntities.name: 2.1.18 Hydrochlorofluorocarbons (HCFC) Phase‑out Management Plan (HPMP) III
planEntities.parentName: CF Output 2.1 Enhanced national capacities and multi-stakeholder partnerships to drive progress toward nature-positive, low-carbon, and climate-resilient development pathways, promoting inclusive environmental governance and equitable climate action for those most affected, including women, youth, persons with disabilities, and other vulnerable groups.
planEntities.description: The Hydrochlorofluorocarbons (HCFC) Phase‑out Management Plan Stage‑III (HPMP‑III) supports Indonesia in meeting its 2025 and 2030 Montreal Protocol compliance targets by completely phasing out HCFC consumption. Approved at the 91st Meeting of the Multilateral Fund (ExCom), HPMP‑III (2023–2030) focuses on transitioning 64 manufacturing enterprises—across refrigeration and air‑conditioning sectors—from HCFC‑22 to non‑HCFC, low‑GWP alternative technologies. As the lead implementing agency, UNDP oversees major investment components, including large‑scale technology conversion, technician training, and sector transformation. With coordinated support from UNEP and GIZ, the project strengthens regulatory enforcement, enhances HCFC import licensing and quota systems, and integrates gender equality across implementation. Ultimately, HPMP‑III accelerates Indonesia’s shift toward ozone‑friendly and climate‑friendly cooling technologies, contributing to global ozone protection and national climate mitigation goals.

planEntities.name: 3.1.15 Forest, Agriculture and Sustainable Trade (FAST)
planEntities.parentName: CF Output 3.1 Accelerated inclusive economic transformation through policy support and innovative approaches to expand access to decent work, promote innovative financing, and accelerate sustainable and diversified growth across key sectors such as agriculture, the blue economy, and downstream industries, benefiting women, youth, persons with disabilities, and other vulnerable groups.
planEntities.description: The Forest, Agriculture and Sustainable Trade (FAST) Project strengthens Indonesia’s governance and trade systems for key agricultural commodities—especially palm oil and cocoa—to make them more sustainable, transparent, and globally competitive. The project helps integrate sustainability into national regulations, supports policy reform, enhances certification and digital traceability systems, and promotes inclusive, multi‑stakeholder collaboration across government, private sector, and smallholder communities. By reducing environmental and social impacts from commodity production while improving market access, FAST positions Indonesia as a leader in sustainable commodity trade and ensures that farmers, women, and youth benefit equitably from cleaner, more resilient value chains.

planEntities.name: 2.1.19 Institutional Strengthening for the Phase 14
planEntities.parentName: CF Output 2.1 Enhanced national capacities and multi-stakeholder partnerships to drive progress toward nature-positive, low-carbon, and climate-resilient development pathways, promoting inclusive environmental governance and equitable climate action for those most affected, including women, youth, persons with disabilities, and other vulnerable groups.
planEntities.description: The Institutional Strengthening for the Implementation of the Montreal Protocol in Indonesia (IS Phase XIV) project supports the Government of Indonesia—through the Ministry of Environment—to maintain and strengthen its national systems for controlling and monitoring ozone‑depleting substances (ODS) and HFCs. The project ensures continued compliance with the Montreal Protocol by enhancing regulatory enforcement, improving ODS/HFC data collection and reporting, coordinating national implementation of HPMP Stage III and preparation for upcoming KIP Stage I, and sustaining public awareness and stakeholder engagement. IS‑14 also enables Indonesia’s National Ozone Unit to carry out oversight, institutional coordination, monitoring, and participation in regional and global Montreal Protocol meetings, ensuring long‑term sustainability of ODS phase‑out achievements.

planEntities.name: 2.1.20 Management of Plastics Waste and Circular Interventions on Plastics in South, Southeast Asia, and the Pacific
planEntities.parentName: CF Output 2.1 Enhanced national capacities and multi-stakeholder partnerships to drive progress toward nature-positive, low-carbon, and climate-resilient development pathways, promoting inclusive environmental governance and equitable climate action for those most affected, including women, youth, persons with disabilities, and other vulnerable groups.
planEntities.description: In Indonesia, the TCCF Plastics Circularity Project supports the country’s transition toward a circular plastic economy by strengthening waste collection, segregation, and recycling systems; improving policy and institutional frameworks; and empowering waste workers through capacity building and gender‑responsive approaches. The project is implemented across priority locations including Jabodetabek, Medan, East Java, South Kalimantan, Bali, Makassar, Labuan Bajo, and Bandung—areas selected for their significant plastic waste challenges. It also promotes digital tools, public engagement, and multi‑stakeholder cooperation to reduce plastic leakage and enhance sustainable, inclusive waste management practices nationwide.

planEntities.name: 2.1.22 Boosting Renewable Innovation for Green and Inclusive Transition (BRIGHT)
planEntities.parentName: CF Output 2.1 Enhanced national capacities and multi-stakeholder partnerships to drive progress toward nature-positive, low-carbon, and climate-resilient development pathways, promoting inclusive environmental governance and equitable climate action for those most affected, including women, youth, persons with disabilities, and other vulnerable groups.
planEntities.description: The Boosting Renewable Innovation for Green and Inclusive Transition (BRIGHT) project supports Indonesia’s just and inclusive energy transition by integrating national‑level transition finance frameworks with community‑level renewable energy solutions. The project works with partners such as UNDP, ERIA, PLN, and GEAPP to expand access to clean energy, introduce innovations like battery-powered boats and solar PV systems, and strengthen local livelihoods—especially in remote and underserved areas. Through its dual focus on policy and community action, BRIGHT aims to accelerate progress toward Indonesia’s Net Zero vision while ensuring that the benefits of renewable energy reach vulnerable groups and promote equitable development.

planEntities.name: 2.1.23 Climate & REDD+ Indonesia (CREDDIN)
planEntities.parentName: CF Output 2.1 Enhanced national capacities and multi-stakeholder partnerships to drive progress toward nature-positive, low-carbon, and climate-resilient development pathways, promoting inclusive environmental governance and equitable climate action for those most affected, including women, youth, persons with disabilities, and other vulnerable groups.
planEntities.description: The Climate & REDD+ Indonesia (CREDDIN) project strengthens Indonesia’s ability to implement its climate commitments by enhancing policies, institutions, and financing mechanisms for reducing emissions from deforestation and forest degradation. The project supports evidence-based climate planning, REDD+ readiness, and the operationalization of robust Monitoring, Reporting, and Verification (MRV) systems. It also helps align national and subnational actions with Indonesia’s NDC and FOLU Net Sink 2030 targets, while integrating gender-responsive approaches and improving safeguards, transparency, and the credibility of REDD+ implementation.

planEntities.name: 1.2.16 Strengthening women’s civil society and women environmental human rights defenders' political participation and influence for a just, green future
planEntities.parentName: CF Output 1.2 Strengthened national institutions, policy and approaches to enhance social inclusion, social protection, and ensure equitable access to services, and opportunities for all, including migrants, refugees, women, children, youth, persons with disabilities, and vulnerable groups.
planEntities.description: The project “Strengthening women’s civil society and women environmental human rights defenders’ (WEHRDs) political participation and influence for a just, green future” empowers women‑led civil society organizations and WEHRDs to engage safely and effectively in civic space. It strengthens their advocacy, leadership, digital and physical security, and evidence‑based policy influence—particularly on gender‑responsive environmental governance and climate action. The initiative also fosters collective action, creates platforms for dialogue with policymakers, and enhances protection mechanisms to ensure women defenders can participate meaningfully in shaping a more inclusive and sustainable future.

planEntities.name: 2.1.24 Institutional Strengthening for the Indonesian Environment Fund (IEF) Governance and Oversight (INSIGHT)
planEntities.parentName: CF Output 2.1 Enhanced national capacities and multi-stakeholder partnerships to drive progress toward nature-positive, low-carbon, and climate-resilient development pathways, promoting inclusive environmental governance and equitable climate action for those most affected, including women, youth, persons with disabilities, and other vulnerable groups.
planEntities.description: The Institutional Strengthening for the Indonesian Environment Fund (IEF) Governance and Oversight (INSIGHT) project enhances the institutional capacity, governance systems, and operational effectiveness of BPDLH. Through UNDP‑supported technical assistance, the project strengthens core functions such as financial management, safeguards, transparency, accountability, and data‑driven decision‑making. INSIGHT focuses on improving organizational structures, operational procedures, MIS systems, and the development of a digital transparency dashboard—aiming to transform BPDLH into a credible, efficient, and internationally recognized fund manager for environmental and climate financing in Indonesia.

planEntities.name: 1.2.19 Strengthening Police Capacities to Prevent and Respond to Technology‑facilitated Gender‑Based Violence (TF‑GBV)
planEntities.parentName: CF Output 1.2 Strengthened national institutions, policy and approaches to enhance social inclusion, social protection, and ensure equitable access to services, and opportunities for all, including migrants, refugees, women, children, youth, persons with disabilities, and vulnerable groups.
planEntities.description: The project Strengthening Police Capacities to Prevent and Respond to Technology‑facilitated Gender‑Based Violence (TF‑GBV) aims to enhance the ability of the Indonesian National Police and relevant stakeholders to prevent, investigate, and respond to digital forms of GBV. Through a survivor‑centered and rights‑based approach, the project strengthens institutional mechanisms, builds specialized skills among police officers and cadets, and integrates TF‑GBV modules into national police training. It also promotes coordinated, whole‑of‑society responses by improving collaboration between law enforcement agencies, ministries, and civil society organizations.

planEntities.name: 3.1.1 Strengthening Livelihood of Small-scale Fishers and Promoting Sustainable Local Economic Development through the Blue Economy
planEntities.parentName: CF Output 3.1 Accelerated inclusive economic transformation through policy support and innovative approaches to expand access to decent work, promote innovative financing, and accelerate sustainable and diversified growth across key sectors such as agriculture, the blue economy, and downstream industries, benefiting women, youth, persons with disabilities, and other vulnerable groups.
planEntities.description: The project supports small‑scale fishers in Morotai and Tanimbar by improving livelihoods, strengthening fisheries governance, and introducing solar‑powered technologies to enhance supply chains and reduce emissions. It empowers 1,600 beneficiaries—including at least 30% women—through training, alternative income opportunities, data system integration, and traceability tools. These interventions boost food security, raise incomes, and advance Indonesia’s sustainable blue economy and SDG commitments.

planEntities.name: 2.1.25 Amplifying Blue Economy Growth through Enhanced Blue Carbon and Financing Profiling
planEntities.parentName: CF Output 2.1 Enhanced national capacities and multi-stakeholder partnerships to drive progress toward nature-positive, low-carbon, and climate-resilient development pathways, promoting inclusive environmental governance and equitable climate action for those most affected, including women, youth, persons with disabilities, and other vulnerable groups.
planEntities.description: The project supports ASEAN Member States and Timor‑Leste in strengthening blue economy action by developing national and regional Blue Carbon and Blue Finance Profiles. These profiles provide robust scientific data, financing pathways, and policy recommendations to advance climate mitigation through mangrove, seagrass, and peatland ecosystems. The initiative enhances technical capacity, harmonizes methodologies, and promotes innovative financing instruments such as blue bonds and blended finance. Implemented by UNDP Indonesia with support from the Government of Japan, the project improves evidence‑based policymaking and mobilizes sustainable investments to scale blue carbon solutions across the region.

planEntities.name: 3.1.16 The Biodiversity Finance Initiative – Phase II (BIOFIN INDONESIA)
planEntities.parentName: CF Output 3.1 Accelerated inclusive economic transformation through policy support and innovative approaches to expand access to decent work, promote innovative financing, and accelerate sustainable and diversified growth across key sectors such as agriculture, the blue economy, and downstream industries, benefiting women, youth, persons with disabilities, and other vulnerable groups.
planEntities.description: National programme to strengthen biodiversity financing by closing the funding gap for conservation and sustainable use of biological diversity. It builds on BIOFIN’s global methodology to assess current biodiversity spending, estimate finance needs, and design innovative financing solutions , such as biodiversity-focused sukuk, faith-based funds, and private sector mechanisms,  to support Indonesia’s biodiversity goals and integrate finance into planning and policy processes. The initiative promotes institutional capacity, national dialogue, and implementation of financial solutions that help mobilize sustainable resources for biodiversity conservation in line with national strategies and international commitments.

planEntities.name: 3.1.17 The Indonesia Insurance and Risk Finance Facility (IRFF) - Implementation
planEntities.parentName: CF Output 3.1 Accelerated inclusive economic transformation through policy support and innovative approaches to expand access to decent work, promote innovative financing, and accelerate sustainable and diversified growth across key sectors such as agriculture, the blue economy, and downstream industries, benefiting women, youth, persons with disabilities, and other vulnerable groups.
planEntities.description: The Insurance and Risk Finance Facility aims to engage the insurance industry and the investment side of industry, providing capital to deliver on the monumental task of financing the SDGs. IRFF implementation in Indonesia to carry out diagnostic and readiness support to shape a programmatic workplan for insurance and risk finance development in the country. A country diagnostic is being conducted which will identify gaps, opportunities and lessons learned in the various aspects of insurance and risk finance experiences of Indonesia. The results and recommendations from the diagnostic report will be translated into a country implementation workplan.

planEntities.name: 2.1.26 Cimate Finance Network Indonesia
planEntities.parentName: CF Output 2.1 Enhanced national capacities and multi-stakeholder partnerships to drive progress toward nature-positive, low-carbon, and climate-resilient development pathways, promoting inclusive environmental governance and equitable climate action for those most affected, including women, youth, persons with disabilities, and other vulnerable groups.
planEntities.description: Climate Finance Network Indonesia is a peer-to-peer network and technical assistance facility that aims to assist the ministry of finance sector ministries and subnational government as well as engage with private sector and development partners.

planEntities.name: 3.1.18 Leveraging Finance to Scale Up Climate-Resilient Food System
planEntities.parentName: CF Output 3.1 Accelerated inclusive economic transformation through policy support and innovative approaches to expand access to decent work, promote innovative financing, and accelerate sustainable and diversified growth across key sectors such as agriculture, the blue economy, and downstream industries, benefiting women, youth, persons with disabilities, and other vulnerable groups.
planEntities.description: The Joint Program provides technical support for the adoption of climate-smart and innovative practices across multiple crops with a focus on drought-resilient crops, solar irrigation, synthetic fertilizers reduction, water-saving rice paddies and guidelines and standards for climate-smart innovative practices.  Enhancing the existing Government rice insurance mechanism, the Joint Program will derisk and integrate sustainable agricultural practices for farmers into the insurance mechanism in East Java.  Leverage proceeds from Indonesia’s annual SDG Bond, Green Sukuk and project-based Green Sukuk issuances , the Joint Programme will facilitate investments in sustainable agriculture and biofortification of rice. The JP will also support MSMEs and farmers group to prepare bankable staple food projects to access the revolving fund of the Indonesia Environment Fund (BPDLH) with a capitalization of $2.5 million.

planEntities.name: 1.1.33 HEALTH GOVERNANCE INITIATIVE
planEntities.parentName: CF Output 1.1: Inclusive and resilient systems deliver equitable and improved access to quality health, education, nutrition, and WASH services, particularly for women, children, youth, persons with disabilities, and vulnerable groups.
planEntities.description:
The Technical Assistance for Implementation (TAA) HIV programme under the Global Fund to Fight AIDS, Tuberculosis and Malaria and UNDP in Indonesia is designed to strengthen the effective delivery of HIV-related grants supported by the Global Fund. As the Global Fund operates primarily as a financing mechanism, UNDP plays a critical role as an interim Principal Recipient, providing programmatic, financial, and operational management support while working closely with the Ministry of Health and national stakeholders. This includes technical assistance in procurement, supply chain systems, monitoring, and coordination to ensure that HIV prevention, testing, treatment, and care services reach targeted populations efficiently and equitably. UNDP in partnership with the Global Fund, supporting about 20 countries to manage resources for actions on SDG 3 which include the following inter-connected areas of action:
(i) reducing inequalities and social exclusion that drive HIV and poor health; ii) promoting effective and inclusive governance for health; and (iti) building resilient and sustainable systems for health.

planEntities.name: 1.1.34 SMILE Project for Digital Transformation in Health Development
planEntities.parentName: CF Output 1.1: Inclusive and resilient systems deliver equitable and improved access to quality health, education, nutrition, and WASH services, particularly for women, children, youth, persons with disabilities, and vulnerable groups.
planEntities.description:
The Ministry of Health with GAVI funding has invested in the scale-up of the SMILE system for routine immunisation with UNDP Indonesia as the implementing agency under the Health Governance Initiative Project (HEART). Originally, the intervention was involving 600 community health centres, but then switched to the improvement of the SMILE system for COVID-19 in January 2021, covering a total of 12,000 community health centres and hospitals. The support from GAVI further supported the improvement of vaccine quality to the last mile by installing 4,000 remote temperature loggers with sensors inside the vaccine chillers. The device also collects temperature data across the vaccine cold-chain and sends the notifications to the SMILE app when the storage temperature breach occurs.
UNDP Indonesia with MoH will shape the action framework on Digital Health Solution for Health Commodities Services, Waste in Health Care Facilities and other related health programs under this project.

planEntities.name: 2.1.35 AIS Forum Phase II-UNDP-IDN-00133979
planEntities.parentName: CF Output 2.1 Enhanced national capacities and multi-stakeholder partnerships to drive progress toward nature-positive, low-carbon, and climate-resilient development pathways, promoting inclusive environmental governance and equitable climate action for those most affected, including women, youth, persons with disabilities, and other vulnerable groups.
planEntities.description:
Archipelagic and Island States (AIS) around the globe face common development challenges that inhibit their ability to live prosperously and grow sustainably. Many are facing existential threats that include climate change, natural disasters, marine pollution, marine plastic debris, unsustainable fisheries, and ocean unsustainability. 
AIS project aims to establish the Archipelagic and Island States (AIS) Forum's Support Facility to ensure its ability to operate effectively and enable effective implementation of its key services. Serving multiple stakeholders, the AIS Forum will be responsible for directing the Forum's programs, managing the AIS Fund Facility and other finances, maintaining relationships with Participants, and developing stakeholder networks. 
The Forum is designed to include all island states and archipelagic countries regardless of their location, size, and level of development. There are regional initiatives that allow island states to connect with and aid one another.

planEntities.name: 2.1.47 UN PAGE
planEntities.parentName: CF Output 2.1 Enhanced national capacities and multi-stakeholder partnerships to drive progress toward nature-positive, low-carbon, and climate-resilient development pathways, promoting inclusive environmental governance and equitable climate action for those most affected, including women, youth, persons with disabilities, and other vulnerable groups.
planEntities.description: The Project embodies the UNDP component of the multi-agency Partnership for Action on Green Economy (PAGE). The project includes global and country level intervention on SDGs- aligned national development planning, and sectoral thematic reform.

planEntities.name: 2.1.46 LEVERAGE
planEntities.parentName: CF Output 2.1 Enhanced national capacities and multi-stakeholder partnerships to drive progress toward nature-positive, low-carbon, and climate-resilient development pathways, promoting inclusive environmental governance and equitable climate action for those most affected, including women, youth, persons with disabilities, and other vulnerable groups.
planEntities.description: As part of the Global Wildlife Program (GWP) under GEF-8, the project builds on earlier GEF-financed and government investments to strengthen combatting the illegal wildlife trade through more effective law enforcement agency collaboration and enhanced engagement with local communities. By integrating conservation of globally significant biodiversity with human health and climate resilience, the project delivers multiple, synergistic benefits that extend beyond national borders.

planEntities.name: 2.1.48 Sustainable Infrastructure Programme in Asia (SIPA)
planEntities.parentName: CF Output 2.1 Enhanced national capacities and multi-stakeholder partnerships to drive progress toward nature-positive, low-carbon, and climate-resilient development pathways, promoting inclusive environmental governance and equitable climate action for those most affected, including women, youth, persons with disabilities, and other vulnerable groups.
planEntities.description: The Sustainable Infrastructure Programme in Asia (SIPA) Project is a collaborative initiative led by the Organization for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) and its consortium partners, including WWF. SIPA aims to support countries in Central and Southeast Asia in transitioning their infrastructure systems to meet the Paris Agreement and Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). The program provides guidance for various stages of the infrastructure investment cycle, including strategic planning, project evaluation, policy alignment, and green finance.

planEntities.name: 3.1.27. The Youth Digitalization for Employability and Entrepreneurship Program (YDEEP)
planEntities.parentName: CF Output 3.1 Accelerated inclusive economic transformation through policy support and innovative approaches to expand access to decent work, promote innovative financing, and accelerate sustainable and diversified growth across key sectors such as agriculture, the blue economy, and downstream industries, benefiting women, youth, persons with disabilities, and other vulnerable groups.
planEntities.description: The Youth Digitalization for Employability and Entrepreneurship Program (YDEEP) by UNDP Indonesia aims to empower underserved youth by building digital and 21st-century skills, improving employability, and fostering entrepreneurship for inclusive economic participation.

planEntities.name: 1.1.35 Management and Technical Cooperation for the AIDS,   Tuberculosis, Malaria Prevention and Control (MTC ATM)   Project
planEntities.parentName: CF Output 1.1: Inclusive and resilient systems deliver equitable and improved access to quality health, education, nutrition, and WASH services, particularly for women, children, youth, persons with disabilities, and vulnerable groups.
planEntities.description:
UNDP supports countries through three directions of change: structural  transformation, leaving no one behind, and resilience. Considering the target of eliminating AIDS, TB, and malaria in 2030, UNDP work closely with Government of Indonesia and development partners to strengthen the implementation  of the National Strategy Plan for AIDS, Tuberculosis and Malaria in Indonesia. Support will be provided through the implementation of the Management and Technical Cooperation for the AIDS, Tuberculosis, Malaria Prevention and Control project which is critical for progress towards the SDGs, especially SDG 3 on healthy lives and well-being for all, 
and the pledge to leave no one behind. The objective of this MTC ATM Project is to strengthened national and subnational level capacities to promote inclusive local development and service delivery for AIDS, Tuberculosis, and Malaria.

planEntities.name: 1.3.33 Modern and adaptive social protection and skills development systems for transforming Indonesia
planEntities.parentName: CF Output 1.2 Strengthened national institutions, policy and approaches to enhance social inclusion, social protection, and ensure equitable access to services, and opportunities for all, including migrants, refugees, women, children, youth, persons with disabilities, and vulnerable groups.
planEntities.description:
The Joint Programme will enhance educational  responsiveness to private sector needs through sectoral skills 
councils and upgrade apprenticeship programs by revising practices and enhancing design. It will refine vocational training financing through innovative modalities like skills development funds and assess skills needs in climate-affected regions, developing programs for vulnerable populations. The Joint Programme will also build capacity 
for just transitions, strengthening policymakers and MSMEs, and pilot innovative financing schemes such as social impact investments. The Joint Programme is designed to support acceleration of the achievement of 
SDGs 1, 4, 8 and aim to directly benefit 1,400 people and indirectly benefit 58 million people in Indonesia, notably those currently  benefitting from the PKH (family hope) and the Sembako (food voucher) programmes. The Joint Programme will leverage the USD 5 billion government financing for implementing the GA Roadmap on social 
protection and jobs.

planEntities.name: 1.2.49 Supporting Asian countries’ resilience to violent extremism in the digital space
planEntities.parentName: CF Output 1.2 Strengthened national institutions, policy and approaches to enhance social inclusion, social protection, and ensure equitable access to services, and opportunities for all, including migrants, refugees, women, children, youth, persons with disabilities, and vulnerable groups.
planEntities.description:
This new regional initiative is a collaboration between UNDP and United Nations Office of Drugs and Crime (UNODC) funded by the European Union, aims to support countries in Asia in strengthening community
mechanisms, building partnerships to promote digital peacebuilding and enhancing knowledge and capacities to build resilience against violent
extremism in digital space.

planEntities.name: Climate Finance Network Indonesia
planEntities.parentName: CF Output 2.1 Enhanced national capacities and multi-stakeholder partnerships to drive progress toward nature-positive, low-carbon, and climate-resilient development pathways, promoting inclusive environmental governance and equitable climate action for those most affected, including women, youth, persons with disabilities, and other vulnerable groups.
planEntities.description:
The Project will serve as a peer-to-peer network and as a knowledge management and technical support 
facility to support Ministries of Finance with the engagement of sector ministries and sub-national 
governments to identify and scale up climate finance innovations in the region. In collaboration with 
stakeholders and partners the CFN will harness the momentum in climate finance reforms in ways that will 
allow knowledge to be shared in real-time across countries to facilitate acceleration and adoption/replication 
of climate budget planning and finance across governments as well as mobilization of public, private and 
blended climate finance. 
The CFN will work across the following six inter-related workstreams which are based on our climate change finance programming experience :1) Climate change aligned budgeting and planning; 2) Direct access to international climate change finance;  3) Tax and use of innovative climate change financing instruments; 4) Gender and social inclusion and climate change finance; and 5) Transparency and accountability of climate change finance; and 6) Modelling climate change impacts on economic growth, sectors and consideration of distributional impacts.

planEntities.name: Accelerating Climate Resilience through (CARA)
planEntities.parentName: CF Output 2.1 Enhanced national capacities and multi-stakeholder partnerships to drive progress toward nature-positive, low-carbon, and climate-resilient development pathways, promoting inclusive environmental governance and equitable climate action for those most affected, including women, youth, persons with disabilities, and other vulnerable groups.
planEntities.description: The CARA Project will build the resilience of economies and vulnerable communities to climate change, conserve the natural environment and promote low carbon growth. The CARA project, supported by the UK government and the UNFCDO, aims to enhance climate resilience in Indonesia and other regions in the Indo-Pacific. The project focuses on several key areas to address the impacts of climate change and promote sustainable development

planEntities.name: 2.1.7 InTex Indonesia (Innovative Business Practices and Economic Models in the Textile Value Chain)
planEntities.parentName: CF Output 2.1 Enhanced national capacities and multi-stakeholder partnerships to drive progress toward nature-positive, low-carbon, and climate-resilient development pathways, promoting inclusive environmental governance and equitable climate action for those most affected, including women, youth, persons with disabilities, and other vulnerable groups.
planEntities.description:
InTex Indonesia works with the Government of Indonesia and the textile industry to accelerate the sector’s transition towards a circular economy.

InTex Indonesia is a UNEP project funded by the Government of Denmark and implemented in collaboration with the Ministry of National Development Planning (BAPPENAS), other line ministries, and key stakeholders. The project aims to support the implementation of Indonesia’s Circular Economy Roadmap and Action Plan, launched in July 2024.

As part of the global InTex Programme, InTex Indonesia contributes to UNEP's goal of transforming the textile value chain towards circularity through policy support, financial measures, advocacy, and industry practices.

planEntities.name: 2.1.27 Strengthening forest and ecosystem connectivity in RIMBA landscape of central Sumatra through investing in natural capital, biodiversity conservation, and land-based emission reductions
planEntities.parentName: CF Output 2.1 Enhanced national capacities and multi-stakeholder partnerships to drive progress toward nature-positive, low-carbon, and climate-resilient development pathways, promoting inclusive environmental governance and equitable climate action for those most affected, including women, youth, persons with disabilities, and other vulnerable groups.
planEntities.description: It is a partnership of seven national ministries (both those concerned with forests and peatlands, economic development, infrastructure, energy, natural resources management, and village and community development), three provinces and six districts in central Sumatra, as well as the extractive mining- and forest plantation sectors. The project will enable the integration of Green Economy principles in 'routine' planning and operations of both the local government as well as key corporate sectors depending or affecting on natural resources, and importantly their annual budgets and investment portfolios; this to protect, restore and expand forests and peatlands, water resources, carbon stocks, as well as enhancing landscape connectivity for biodiversity conservation.

planEntities.name: 2.1.33 UN-REDD Program : TA for Indonesia
planEntities.parentName: CF Output 2.1 Enhanced national capacities and multi-stakeholder partnerships to drive progress toward nature-positive, low-carbon, and climate-resilient development pathways, promoting inclusive environmental governance and equitable climate action for those most affected, including women, youth, persons with disabilities, and other vulnerable groups.
planEntities.description: The UN-REDD Programme is the UN knowledge and advisory platform on forests and climate, with a focus on advancing Articles 5 and 6 of the Paris Agreement. Our long-term goal (2030) is to realize the climate change mitigation potential of forests solutions by avoiding carbon emissions and fostering carbon sequestration for at least 5 GtCO2e per year.

planEntities.name: 2.1.34 UN Partnership for Action on Inclusive Green Economy (PAGE) II
planEntities.parentName: CF Output 2.1 Enhanced national capacities and multi-stakeholder partnerships to drive progress toward nature-positive, low-carbon, and climate-resilient development pathways, promoting inclusive environmental governance and equitable climate action for those most affected, including women, youth, persons with disabilities, and other vulnerable groups.
planEntities.description: This project is the UNEP component of the multi-agency the Partnership for Action on Green Economy (PAGE) initiative. Since the start of its activities in 2013, PAGE has evolved from a small, coordinated effort  involving five United Nations agencies into a growing partnership supported by eight funding partners. UN PAGE brings together the expertise of ILO, UNDP, UNEP, UNIDO and UNITAR who work jointly in supporting countries to reframe macroeconomic and sectoral policies around sustainability. To date, PAGE has been active in 20 partner countries, and inspired action in a further 90 countries. In the decade 2020-2030, UN PAGE plans to build on this momentum by expanding and deepening its engagement with 10 additional countries and with regional organizations.

planEntities.description: UNESCO, through its Social Media 4 Peace initiative, worked with ELSAM and the Damai Coalition to assess how digital governance during the August–September 2025 crisis affected digital rights in Indonesia, particularly freedom of expression and access to information. The project involves collecting and analyzing data on actions taken by the government, digital platforms, and civil society, and identifying issues such as internet disruptions, content moderation, and digital threats. Based on the findings, the Contractor will prepare an analytical report with recommendations, develop advocacy and communication materials, and support the Coalition’s efforts to promote transparent, rights‑respecting digital governance. The activity started on December 2025.

planEntities.name: 1.1.2 Accreditation of government and private midwifery schools as per national pre-service midwifery education standards that are aligned with the International Confederation of Midwives (ICM) standards.
planEntities.parentName: CF Output 1.1: Inclusive and resilient systems deliver equitable and improved access to quality health, education, nutrition, and WASH services, particularly for women, children, youth, persons with disabilities, and vulnerable groups.
planEntities.description:
The International Confederation of Midwives developed the Global Standards in Midwifery Education in response to calls to standardise and improve midwifery education and training across the world. The ICM has a clear definition of midwife to support both education and regulation standardisation. 
The Global Standards for Midwifery Education provide a benchmark for programmes leading to registration/ recognition as a midwife. This indicator counts the cumulative total of government and private midwifery schools that comply with national pre-service midwifery education standards.
 There are six ICM Standards that provide a benchmark for midwifery education and training programmes: ● Organisation and Administration ● Midwifery Faculty ● Student Body ● Curriculum ● Resources, Facilities and Services ● Assessment Strategies/Quality Improvement The Standards were developed using a recognised consensus research methodology (Modified Delphi Process) with midwifery education experts from across low, middle and high-income countries. They are the minimum standards expected of a midwifery programme. A crucial element of the implementation of the standards is through deep approaches to learning. Deep approaches to learning relies on learners having the time to integrate new knowledge and to apply this new knowledge in supported practice settings. If graduates are expected to be able to practice in a way that meets the essential competencies of the midwife then they require time to gain the necessary skills, knowledge and behaviours.  Midwifery schools in this context refer to midwifery study programs, both Diploma 3 (D3) and professional programs, with priority given to professional programs, in both public and private universities.

planEntities.name: 1.1.4 Midwives that are re-licensed based on the newly developed and institutionalized continuing professional development.
planEntities.parentName: CF Output 1.1: Inclusive and resilient systems deliver equitable and improved access to quality health, education, nutrition, and WASH services, particularly for women, children, youth, persons with disabilities, and vulnerable groups.
planEntities.description:
Mandatory training has been introduced in Indonesia to improve the standard of midwifery services, address the risks associated with midwives’ underperformance or incompetence, and to protect the public from unsafe midwifery care. The new Omnibus Health Law in Indonesia offers a new opportunity for strengthening Continuing Professional Development (CPD). The new laws mandates that midwives need at a minimum 50 CPD credits for relicensure. The indicator measures the percentage of registered midwives who have completed this mandatory 50 credit requirement and obtains relicensing from the Midwifery Collegium according to the new CPD framework.   
Re-licensed refers to the renewal of a midwife’s professional license through the fulfillment of the required CPD credits, in accordance with the national CPD framework that has been developed and institutionalized. This process is mandatory not only for independent practice but also for obtaining and maintaining licenses to practice in primary health care facilities (FKTP) and referral health care facilities (FKRTL).

planEntities.name: 1.1.6 Adoption of new basic emergency obstetric and new born care standards and monitored its signal functions in districts with high maternal mortality
planEntities.parentName: CF Output 1.1: Inclusive and resilient systems deliver equitable and improved access to quality health, education, nutrition, and WASH services, particularly for women, children, youth, persons with disabilities, and vulnerable groups.
planEntities.description: The capacity of a health facility to provide Basic Emergency Obstetric and Newborn Care (BEmONC) is monitored by thirteen signal functions. BEmONC facilities are first line referral facilities that should: ● ensure a positive experience of care for all pregnant women and their accompanying family members;  ● respectful and people-centered care; ● safely attend to mothers and newborns for births without complications; ● safely attend to mothers and newborns experiencing basic non-surgical complications and stabilizing complications that require surgical intervention or others requiring referral to a Comprehensive Emergency Obstetric and Newborn Care (CEmONC) health facility; ● coordinate antenatal and postnatal care (including postpartum family planning).

planEntities.name: 1.1.7 Implementation an acceleration programme on family planning in districts with low modern contraceptive prevalence rates
planEntities.parentName: CF Output 1.1: Inclusive and resilient systems deliver equitable and improved access to quality health, education, nutrition, and WASH services, particularly for women, children, youth, persons with disabilities, and vulnerable groups.
planEntities.description: Sub-output measures the number of administrative districts within Indonesia that: have been identified as having a low modern Contraceptive Prevalence Rate (mCPR) based on a defined threshold (below national benchmark) and are actively implementing an acceleration program specifically designed to improve family planning (FP) access and uptake. Modern Contraceptive Prevalence Rate (mCPR): mCPR refers to the percentage of women of reproductive age (typically 15-49) who are currently using a modern method of contraception. Modern methods typically include (but are not limited to) oral contraceptive pills, injectables, implants, intrauterine devices (IUDs), condoms, and sterilization. The specific definition of "modern methods" used should be consistent with national definitions and clearly documented. Low mCPR: This signifies that the district's mCPR is below national benchmark, indicating a need for targeted interventions to improve access to and uptake of modern contraception.  Acceleration Programme: This refers to a focused and intensified set of activities designed to rapidly increase mCPR in the targeted districts. This focus set of activities are tailored based on evidence and data of the district.  Family Planning: This emphasizes that family planning services are provided in a way that respects, protects, and fulfills the reproductive rights of individuals. This includes ensuring informed choice, voluntary participation, accessibility, availability, acceptability, and quality of services. Selection of targeted districts: the targeted districts are those having mCPR below national benchmark as stipulated in Head of BKKBN Decree No. 141/KEP/E3/2024 Year 2024 concerning Priority Location for Family Planning and Reproductive Health and MOH regulation No. 2 Year 2025 on implementation of reproductive health efforts. Final selection of the districts will be discussed with Kemendukbangga/BKKBN, MoH, and Bappenas.

planEntities.name: 1.1.14 Implementation of newly developed and institutionalized reproductive health education in the national curriculum
planEntities.parentName: CF Output 1.1: Inclusive and resilient systems deliver equitable and improved access to quality health, education, nutrition, and WASH services, particularly for women, children, youth, persons with disabilities, and vulnerable groups.
planEntities.description: This indicator tracks the progress of integrating comprehensive reproductive health (RH) education into the school national curriculum system, thereby  empowering school-aged children and youth with the knowledge and skills necessary for reproductive health and contributing to the prevention of VAWG and harmful practices. Institutionalization in the national curriculum refers to the integration of the RH education  into intra-curricular, intracurricular, co-curricular, or extracurricular according to the Indonesian regulation on the national curriculum structure.  The reproductive health curriculum will be developed based on two primary references: first, the reproductive health education module—approved by the Ministry of Primary and Secondary Education and the Ministry of Health, and set to be adapted according to Indonesian social and cultural norms and children and youth aged 7-18 year development—and second, the current curriculum assessment led by UNFPA, UGM, the Ministry of Education, and the Ministry of Health, which will serve as the foundation for the new curriculum's implementation. This indicator measures the number of schools (both government and private, including those managed by non-governmental and faith-based organizations) that have officially adopted and demonstrably implemented the newly developed and institutionalized RH education curriculum. Schools implement RH education curriculum when  1)  the RH education content must be demonstrably integrated into the school’s regular educational activities. This integration can take various forms, including incorporation into existing subject curricula, dedicated counseling sessions, character education programs, or locally tailored subjects designed to address specific community needs;  2)  the teachers responsible for delivering this RH education must have successfully completed the training for teachers’ programme approved by the Ministry of Primary and Secondary Education. This ensures that educators are equipped with the necessary knowledge, skills, and pedagogical approaches to effectively impart RH education in a manner consistent with national standards and best practices.

planEntities.name: 1.2.36 Implementation of integrated planning and budgeting to increase domestic financing for VAWG and harmful practices reduction.
planEntities.parentName: CF Output 1.2 Strengthened national institutions, policy and approaches to enhance social inclusion, social protection, and ensure equitable access to services, and opportunities for all, including migrants, refugees, women, children, youth, persons with disabilities, and vulnerable groups.
planEntities.description: 2.2 UNFPA  sub-output measures the number of districts that have successfully integrated planning and budgeting processes for VAWG prevention and response  and harmful practices. Integrated Planning and Budgeting for VAWG aims to synchronize cross-sectoral activities to increase domestic budget allocations through efficient and high-impact programming, with the goal of increasing reporting and response to cases of violence against women and girls (VAWG) and reducing cases related to child marriage and female genital mutilation/cutting (FGM/C). The allocation and mobilization of financial resources from national and subnational government budgets are critical to address VAWG, which contributes to poor maternal health outcomes, including child marriage and unintended pregnancies resulting from sexual violence. Increasing domestic financing helps ensure that essential VAWG-related services are accessible and less dependent on external donor funding.

planEntities.description: Sub-output tracks the number of government technical unit for managing VAWG case  (UPTD-PPA) in the district level that has adopted standardized VAWG case management system and established referral mechanisms with multisectoral institutions, including with healthcare facilities, those are required to effectively response to the VAWG cases. This response capacity should also be in place during humanitarian crises situations. Institutional capacity building of UPTD-PPA will focus on the use of established protocols and tools for VAWG case management and reporting according to Sexual Violence Crime Law. The minimum requirements for this indicator include the availability of district regulations, infrastructure, budget sources, Case Management SOPs, and a minimum number of human resources, including the Head of UPTD-PPA, Case Managers, Social Service Workforce, and Administrative staff, as well as the operational functions of UPTD-PPA. The indicator is measured by the number of cases reported, managed by UPTD-PPA, and referred to sectoral services (health, law enforcement, etc.).

planEntities.description: 2.4_UNFPA. Disaster Preparedness Plan focuses on identifying potential hazards (like earthquakes, floods, and fires), establishing clear communication channels, and having emergency kits readily available, while also practicing evacuation procedures. In this situation the assistance in the Plan development at the provincial and/or district levels will include availability and accessibility of reproductive health and VAWG prevention/response service package and cost estimate for its implementation. The standard for service package will follow the Minister of Health Regulation no. 6/2024 on Technical Standard for Minimum Health Service Standards; the MOH Regulation no 75/2019 on Health Crises Management; and the Minister  of Women Empowerment and Child Protection Regulation No. 8/2024 on Protection of Women and Children from VAWG in Disaster Management. Sex, Age, Disability Disaggregated Data (SADDD) method should be applied in the Disaster Preparedness Plan.

planEntities.description:
The Global Eco-Industrial Parks Programme II—Indonesia country-level intervention project (GEIPP II—Indonesia) will address the development of Eco-Industrial Parks (EIPs) in Indonesia under the framework of Phase II of the Global Eco-Industrial Parks Programme (GEIPP II) in developing and transition countries. It will be implemented by UNIDO and funded by the Government of Switzerland through its State Secretariat for Economic Affairs.
The development objective of the country-level intervention for Indonesia is in line with that of GEIPP II: to promote circular economy approaches, mitigate the climate impact of industries, and help industrial parks adapt to the negative consequences of climate change. The GEIPP II -Indonesia country-level intervention will achieve this by continuing to facilitate the uptake of eco-industrial Park approaches in scaling up resource productivity, minimizing waste, promoting recycling, and improving the economic, environmental, and social performance of businesses, thereby contributing to inclusive and sustainable industrial development (ISID) in a circular economy in Indonesia

At the same time, it will support the strengthening of regulatory and institutional frameworks to enhance the capacity of relevant authorities to detect, investigate, adjudicate, and prosecute corruption offences in line with international standards, including the United Nations Convention against Corruption (UNCAC). Recognizing corruption as a cross-cutting enabler of other forms of crime. planEntities.name: 1.2.34 Combatting Online Scams
planEntities.parentName: CF Output 1.2 Strengthened national institutions, policy and approaches to enhance social inclusion, social protection, and ensure equitable access to services, and opportunities for all, including migrants, refugees, women, children, youth, persons with disabilities, and vulnerable groups.
planEntities.description: The United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC) is actively collaborating with a wide range of national stakeholders—including law enforcement agencies, financial intelligence units, financial regulatory authorities, and relevant government ministries—to strengthen efforts in combating the growing threat of online scams and related financial crimes. This collaboration includes the development of analytical and threat assessment reports to better understand emerging scam typologies, the delivery of specialized capacity-building programmes to enhance investigative skills, and technical training on digital forensic extraction and analysis to support evidence collection. In addition, UNODC works with these partners to develop and promote standard operating procedures (SOPs) that facilitate effective coordination among authorities and enable more efficient mechanisms for tracing, freezing, and ultimately returning funds to victims of scams.

planEntities.name: 1.2.35 Law Enforcement Assistance Programme
planEntities.parentName: CF Output 2.1 Enhanced national capacities and multi-stakeholder partnerships to drive progress toward nature-positive, low-carbon, and climate-resilient development pathways, promoting inclusive environmental governance and equitable climate action for those most affected, including women, youth, persons with disabilities, and other vulnerable groups.
planEntities.description:
The United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC) works closely with law enforcement agencies, financial intelligence units, financial regulatory authorities, and relevant government ministries to strengthen the investigation and prosecution of money laundering linked to environmental and forestry crimes. Through this collaboration, UNODC supports efforts to enhance investigative capacities, promote financial investigation techniques, and improve inter-agency coordination in addressing illicit financial flows generated from activities such as illegal logging, wildlife trafficking, and other forms of environmental crime.

In addition, UNODC assists national authorities in identifying and mitigating emerging risks associated with carbon trading mechanisms that may be vulnerable to financial crime, including fraud, money laundering, and market manipulation. By strengthening financial investigations and institutional capacities, these efforts ultimately contribute to protecting forests and the broader environment while ensuring that environmental protection mechanisms are not exploited for illicit financial gain.

planEntities.parentName: CF Output 2.1 Enhanced national capacities and multi-stakeholder partnerships to drive progress toward nature-positive, low-carbon, and climate-resilient development pathways, promoting inclusive environmental governance and equitable climate action for those most affected, including women, youth, persons with disabilities, and other vulnerable groups.
planEntities.description: WasteNet: EU–Southeast Asia Partnership in Waste Shipment Management ("WasteNet") is a regional action funded by the European Union and implemented by the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC), in cooperation with relevant United Nations entities and partners. The overall objective of the project is to assist major waste-importing countries in ASEAN in transitioning smoothly towards effective management of imported waste, while combating illegal waste shipments from the EU. The project aims to achieve two main outcomes: (i) enhancing the capabilities of major waste-importing ASEAN countries to manage imported waste, including through strengthened enforcement cooperation; and (ii) strengthening the EU–ASEAN partnership by working towards better-aligned waste shipment policies and procedures. The project will be implemented in the four focus countries in Southeast Asia, i.e., Indonesia, Malaysia, Thailand, and Viet Nam, and involving the other countries member of ASEAN.

planEntities.name: 3.2.5 Data Insights for Social and Humanitarian Action (Phase 2)
planEntities.parentName: CF Output 3.2 Strengthened digital transformation and data innovation to foster greater inclusion, drive policy innovation, and enhance evidence-based decision-making, enabling more equitable access to services and opportunities, especially for vulnerable groups.
planEntities.description:
Global Data Access Initiative (GDAI) is an initiative managed by UNOPS and the Executive Office of the Secretary General (EOSG) across UN Global Pulse (UNGP) in collaboration with UN agencies (World Food Program (WFP), the UN Development Program (UNDP), private sector partners, and foundations. GDAI aspires to catalyst the formation of a connected and cohesive ecosystem of “plug-and-play” data and AI products and services including the responsible access to, use, and reuse of data thereby accelerating the attainment of the SDGs. 

GDAI will build and deploy two scalable, productionized solutions to problems faced by frontline organizations focusing on natural disaster response and recovery in close collaboration with, and informed by the needs of WFP and UNDP: Vulnerability mapping and population assessment and; Disaster damage assessment. In building these solutions, the team will take an approach that aims at scalable products for these use cases and beyond. This will result in a collection of “plug-and-play” data and AI products and services that can be used to accelerate the delivery of solutions in pursuit of the SDGs whilst generating insights into how to best evolve and, over time, realise the vision of GDAI beyond natural disaster response and recovery.

UNOPS is tasked for the provision of operational services to the UN Global Pulse to operationalize SDG specific use cases leveraging data from private sector and other entities across countries in Asia. 

In 2023, GDAI was renamed DISHA (Data Insights for Social and Humanitarian Action) to better reflect the goal of the initiative and to show what the personnel wants to achieve with the data. DISHA keeps being a unique partnership between the UN and private firms and foundations, working day to day in different regions on the same goal. The partners are UN Global Pulse, McKinsey & Company, Google.org, the Patrick J. McGovern Foundation and the Jain Family Institute.

planEntities.name: 3.2.6 UN Global Pulse Asia Pacific (Phase 2)
planEntities.parentName: CF Output 3.2 Strengthened digital transformation and data innovation to foster greater inclusion, drive policy innovation, and enhance evidence-based decision-making, enabling more equitable access to services and opportunities, especially for vulnerable groups.
planEntities.description:
UN Global Pulse serves as the United Nations Secretary-General's flagship innovation initiative, established in 2009 to harness the power of big data and technology for sustainable development. Functioning as the UN's innovation laboratory, Global Pulse operates at the intersection of data science, technology, and development to generate insights that inform evidence-based policy-making. The initiative originated in response to the recognition that traditional methods of data collection and analysis were insufficient to address the rapidly evolving challenges faced by the international community.

The core mandate of UN Global Pulse revolves around leveraging emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence and big data analytics, to unlock real-time, actionable insights. By doing so, Global Pulse aims to enhance the UN system's ability to respond effectively to global crises, accelerate progress towards the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), and address complex socio-economic challenges. Over the years, UN Global Pulse has pioneered innovative approaches to data analysis, experimentation, and collaboration. The initiative has actively engaged with governments, the private sector, academia, and civil society to build a network of Pulse Labs worldwide. These labs serve as localized hubs, exploring how data innovation can contribute to more effective and targeted development interventions at the country level.

The initiative to transition Pulse Lab Jakarta (PLJ) into the UN Global Pulse Asia-Pacific Hub marks a pivotal phase for the UN Global Pulse in the Asia Pacific region. Shifting from country-level activities, the Regional Hub will now assume a broader regional role, focusing on convening stakeholders, sharing information, knowledge management, advocacy, and standard-setting. UN Global Pulse Asia-Pacific aims to enhance efficiency in digital innovation efforts, contribute to policy-making, and address issues of exclusion and bias. 

The project is activated through a grant from the UN Foundation and aims at leveraging big data and artificial intelligence to achieve Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) in the Asia-Pacific region. The expanded scope includes emphasizing successful scaling, scanning regional gaps and challenges, and fostering broader innovation capabilities. The project design aligns with UN Global Pulse Core Functions, encompassing digital innovation programs, strategic foresight, and support for inclusive digital innovation policies. 

The project's theory of change outlines three impact channels: Innovation Solutions, Innovation Services & Capability Building, and Advocacy & Thought Leadership. These channels collectively aim to accelerate delivery, induce policy transformations, and generate social impact across the Asia-Pacific region. The project's programmatic considerations include stakeholder and communication management, partnership engagement, sustainable results management, gender mainstreaming, capacity building, and risk management.

The governance mechanism involves a Regional Steering Committee comprising the Government of Indonesia, multilateral, and philanthropic donors, responsible for providing strategic direction, advocacy, and overseeing program performance. The project team structure is designed for flexibility and efficiency, leveraging UNOPS support services and recruiting specialists to deliver on program objectives. 

UNOPS and UNGP-AP

The UNOPS team managing the UNGP-AP project brings its extensive expertise in project management, procurement, and operational support to ensure the successful establishment and functioning of the Regional Hub. UNOPS, known for its commitment to excellence in project delivery and adherence to the highest standards of transparency, efficiency, and accountability, will have to play a crucial role in overseeing the day-to-day operations of the Asia-Pacific initiative.

UNOPS will provide comprehensive support in the areas of fund management, administration, human resource management, procurement, and legal arrangements for strategic partnerships, including data partnerships and technical collaborations. Leveraging its vast experience in managing complex, multi-stakeholder projects, UNOPS will have to facilitate the smooth transition of Pulse Lab Jakarta into the UN Global Pulse Asia-Pacific Hub.

In addition to operational support, UNOPS will contribute to risk management, ensuring that the project adheres to UNOPS risk management strategy and engages in continuous evaluation and mitigation of potential challenges. The organization's commitment to sustainability will be integral to the project's success, with a focus on mainstreaming gender considerations, promoting diversity, and addressing climate impacts throughout the implementation.

planEntities.description:
The United Nations strengthened institutional capacities — with a strong gender mainstreaming lens — to improve the implementation of flagship public skilling and entrepreneurship schemes and enhance education-to-work transitions.
In Jharkhand, technical support to the State Skill Development Mission strengthened planning, market alignment and implementation of flagship programmes, enabling over 116,000 youth (77% women; 33% SC/ST; 40% OBC) to access market-relevant skills, with nearly 64,000 transitioning into formal employment across emerging sectors, reflecting improved inclusive livelihood outcomes. Through outcome-based financing partnerships and ecosystem strengthening, the UN enhanced accountability for enterprise sustainability, income generation and employment outcomes, contributing to more inclusive, gender-responsive pathways from education to decent work and livelihoods.
