planEntities.parentName: Equitable Opportunities for Skilling and Decent Work: All employable persons have equitable opportunities to enhance 21st century and life skills, vocational training, and access to decent work.
planEntities.description:
The United Nations supported the adoption of fair, safe and gender-responsive labour migration frameworks by strengthening social dialogue, policy advocacy and state-level engagement.
Technical inputs and advocacy by workers’ organizations contributed to consolidated recommendations on the draft Overseas Mobility Bill, calling for alignment with International Labour Standards and global migration governance frameworks to uphold migrant workers’ rights and decent work principles. At the state level, dialogue was initiated in Mizoram on bridging skills for migration and promoting safe migration and entrepreneurship pathways.
Focused engagement on migrant care workers — the majority of whom are women — advanced discussions on improving working conditions, rights protection and gender-responsive labour standards. By engaging both women and men trade union leaders, the UN fostered inclusive social dialogue to promote ethical recruitment practices, strengthened labour protections and improved reintegration and support mechanisms for migrant workers, particularly women.

planEntities.parentName: Equitable Opportunities for Skilling and Decent Work: All employable persons have equitable opportunities to enhance 21st century and life skills, vocational training, and access to decent work.
planEntities.description:
The United Nations strengthened institutional, statistical and service delivery capacities to advance universal and inclusive social protection coverage, including health, while modernising systems and reducing digital and access gaps.
Technical assistance to the Ministry of Labour and Employment improved governance, data collection and SDG 1.3–aligned measurement of social protection, strengthening national data systems and increasing reported coverage of at least one social protection branch from 24.4 per cent (2020–22) to 48.8 per cent (2024–26), with further expansion to 64.3 per cent through enhanced data pooling at central and state levels.
At the delivery level, UN support expanded last-mile access for marginalised and informal economy workers — including sanitation workers, migrant workers, platform workers, domestic workers, construction workers and people living with HIV. Nearly 11,000 sanitation workers were linked to government schemes, supported by the institutionalisation of the NAMASTE National Helpline, which reached over 25,000 beneficiaries in 2025. Integrated outreach also enrolled informal and migrant workers in social protection schemes and linked vulnerable groups to health services, skills development and employment opportunities.
Through policy advisory and advocacy, the UN supported labour protection reforms, strengthened grievance and institutional mechanisms, and promoted gender-responsive and non-discriminatory access to social security.
Overall, UN interventions reinforced systems, institutions and inclusive delivery mechanisms to accelerate progress towards universal social protection.

planEntities.description:
The United Nations strengthened policies, institutions and community systems to improve Female Labour Force Participation (FLFPR), advance gender parity and uphold rights at work.
Evidence-based advisory and financing analysis informed gender-responsive childcare models and revisions to national schemes, alongside pilot childcare centres that demonstrated affordable solutions to support women’s economic participation. Regional technical assistance built the capacities of over 390 stakeholders to design sustainable and inclusive care systems, while community skilling initiatives enabled women from low-income communities to access income-generating roles in the care economy.
Technical inputs to national and state task forces supported gender-responsive labour and employment policies, integrating care economy approaches to increase women’s workforce participation. The UN also supported the adoption of a State Plan of Action on child labour and integrated Fundamental Principles and Rights at Work — including elimination of child and forced labour — into industry training systems, promoting safer, more equitable employment across sectors.

planEntities.parentName: Improved Productivity and Decent Working Conditions: All enterprises, particularly MSMEs, cooperatives and self help groups, have access to appropriate business development services and innovation, to enhance productivity and working conditions.
planEntities.description:
The United Nations strengthened institutional and financing mechanisms to improve women-led MSMEs’ access to affordable finance, digital capabilities and business support services.
Through the Fund for Women Entrepreneurs, an innovative blended financing model mobilised USD 1.3 million in low-cost, collateral-free credit from over 2,100 social investors, expanding access to capital for underserved women entrepreneurs. The initiative supported 2,619 women-led enterprises — 80% from SC, ST and OBC communities — with finance, mentoring and digital literacy, enhancing their capacity to improve business operations, adopt new models and scale sustainably.
With a 96% repayment rate and 4,071 jobs created, the model demonstrated a scalable and inclusive approach to strengthening women-led MSMEs and promoting equitable enterprise growth.

planEntities.parentName: Improved Productivity and Decent Working Conditions: All enterprises, particularly MSMEs, cooperatives and self help groups, have access to appropriate business development services and innovation, to enhance productivity and working conditions.
planEntities.description:
The United Nations strengthened capacities of businesses, MSMEs and industry bodies to promote responsible business conduct, good corporate governance and compliance with human and labour rights standards.
Over 360 business representatives enhanced their human rights due diligence capacities, improving compliance with global and domestic frameworks, while SMEs strengthened awareness on disability inclusion and accessible workplaces. A landmark bipartite Roadmap on Responsible Business Conduct, jointly developed by workers’ and employers’ organizations, advanced social dialogue, fair employment and alignment with Fundamental Principles and Rights at Work.
Private sector engagement deepened through 69 new Women’s Empowerment Principles (WEPs) signatories, expansion of gender data reporting, and reforms in gender-responsive procurement policies. Capacity building supported gender-inclusive hiring, workplace mental health policies and strengthened implementation of POSH across textile supply chains, with trade unions and civil society enhancing oversight mechanisms to prevent violence and harassment.
In parallel, support to artisans and handicraft clusters improved production standards and working conditions, contributing to safer, more equitable and decent work in both formal and informal sectors.

The United Nations strengthened institutional, statistical and service delivery capacities to advance universal and inclusive social protection coverage, including health, while modernising systems and reducing digital and access gaps.
Technical assistance to the Ministry of Labour and Employment improved governance, data collection and SDG 1.3–aligned measurement of social protection, strengthening national data systems and increasing reported coverage of at least one social protection branch from 24.4 per cent (2020–22) to 48.8 per cent (2024–26), with further expansion to 64.3 per cent through enhanced data pooling at central and state levels.
At the delivery level, UN support expanded last-mile access for marginalised and informal economy workers — including sanitation workers, migrant workers, platform workers, domestic workers, construction workers and people living with HIV. Nearly 11,000 sanitation workers were linked to government schemes, supported by the institutionalisation of the NAMASTE National Helpline, which reached over 25,000 beneficiaries in 2025. Integrated outreach also enrolled informal and migrant workers in social protection schemes and linked vulnerable groups to health services, skills development and employment opportunities.
Through policy advisory and advocacy, the UN supported labour protection reforms, strengthened grievance and institutional mechanisms, and promoted gender-responsive and non-discriminatory access to social security.
Overall, UN interventions reinforced systems, institutions and inclusive delivery mechanisms to accelerate progress towards universal social protection.

planEntities.name: Support in improving Female Labour Force Participation Rate (FLFPR), facilitate gender parity across sectors, including through development of the care economy, promotion of rights at work and elimination of child labour and forced labour (ILO, UN Women, UNFPA, UNIDO, UNDP, IOM)
planEntities.parentName: Equitable Opportunities for Skilling and Decent Work: All employable persons have equitable opportunities to enhance 21st century and life skills, vocational training, and access to decent work.
planEntities.description:
The United Nations strengthened policies, institutions and community systems to improve Female Labour Force Participation (FLFPR), advance gender parity and uphold rights at work.
Evidence-based advisory and financing analysis informed gender-responsive childcare models and revisions to national schemes, alongside pilot childcare centres that demonstrated affordable solutions to support women’s economic participation. Regional technical assistance built the capacities of over 390 stakeholders to design sustainable and inclusive care systems, while community skilling initiatives enabled women from low-income communities to access income-generating roles in the care economy.
Technical inputs to national and state task forces supported gender-responsive labour and employment policies, integrating care economy approaches to increase women’s workforce participation. The UN also supported the adoption of a State Plan of Action on child labour and integrated Fundamental Principles and Rights at Work — including elimination of child and forced labour — into industry training systems, promoting safer, more equitable employment across sectors.

planEntities.description:
The United Nations strengthened capacities of MSMEs, micro producers, cooperatives and women-led enterprises to expand market linkages and integrate into value chains.
Cultural entrepreneurs and artisans were supported to participate in multi-city events, national fairs and festivals, enhancing market visibility and regional linkages. In Taj Ganj, 100 artisans and youth were trained in cultural entrepreneurship to build sustainable tourism-linked enterprises.
Digital and institutional innovations advanced business mentoring and market access. The COMPASS digital platform connected women entrepreneurs with private-sector mentors, while a partnership with the Government e-Marketplace (GeM) promoted gender-responsive public procurement and expanded sourcing from women-led enterprises.
At the community level, 3,500 women smallholder farmers strengthened their capacities through rights awareness and cooperative-based livelihood models, supporting collective enterprise development and improved access to markets.

planEntities.parentName: Improved Productivity and Decent Working Conditions: All enterprises, particularly MSMEs, cooperatives and self help groups, have access to appropriate business development services and innovation, to enhance productivity and working conditions.
planEntities.description:
The United Nations strengthened capacities of businesses, MSMEs and industry bodies to promote responsible business conduct, good corporate governance and compliance with human and labour rights standards.
Over 360 business representatives enhanced their human rights due diligence capacities, improving compliance with global and domestic frameworks, while SMEs strengthened awareness on disability inclusion and accessible workplaces. A landmark bipartite Roadmap on Responsible Business Conduct, jointly developed by workers’ and employers’ organizations, advanced social dialogue, fair employment and alignment with Fundamental Principles and Rights at Work.
Private sector engagement deepened through 69 new Women’s Empowerment Principles (WEPs) signatories, expansion of gender data reporting, and reforms in gender-responsive procurement policies. Capacity building supported gender-inclusive hiring, workplace mental health policies and strengthened implementation of POSH across textile supply chains, with trade unions and civil society enhancing oversight mechanisms to prevent violence and harassment.
In parallel, support to artisans and handicraft clusters improved production standards and working conditions, contributing to safer, more equitable and decent work in both formal and informal sectors.

planEntities.parentName: Equitable Opportunities for Skilling and Decent Work: All employable persons have equitable opportunities to enhance 21st century and life skills, vocational training, and access to decent work.
planEntities.description:
The United Nations strengthened institutional capacities — with a strong gender mainstreaming lens — to improve the implementation of flagship public skilling and entrepreneurship schemes and enhance education-to-work transitions.
In Jharkhand, technical support to the State Skill Development Mission strengthened planning, market alignment and implementation of flagship programmes, enabling over 116,000 youth (77% women; 33% SC/ST; 40% OBC) to access market-relevant skills, with nearly 64,000 transitioning into formal employment across emerging sectors, reflecting improved inclusive livelihood outcomes. At the national and state levels, UN support advanced entrepreneurship and innovation ecosystems, reaching 2.7 million young people — 52% young women — through awareness, school and higher education initiatives. Innovation and entrepreneurship education were embedded within government school, technical and higher education systems, reaching over 2.8 million students nationwide. Through outcome-based financing partnerships and ecosystem strengthening, the UN enhanced accountability for enterprise sustainability, income generation and employment outcomes, contributing to more inclusive, gender-responsive pathways from education to decent work and livelihoods.

planEntities.name: Support in improving Female Labour Force Participation Rate (FLFPR), facilitate gender parity across sectors, including through development of the care economy, promotion of rights at work and elimination of child labour and forced labour (ILO, UN Women, UNFPA, UNIDO, UNDP, IOM)
planEntities.parentName: Equitable Opportunities for Skilling and Decent Work: All employable persons have equitable opportunities to enhance 21st century and life skills, vocational training, and access to decent work.
planEntities.description:
The United Nations strengthened policies, institutions and community systems to improve Female Labour Force Participation (FLFPR), advance gender parity and uphold rights at work.
Evidence-based advisory and financing analysis informed gender-responsive childcare models and revisions to national schemes, alongside pilot childcare centres that demonstrated affordable solutions to support women’s economic participation. Regional technical assistance built the capacities of over 390 stakeholders to design sustainable and inclusive care systems, while community skilling initiatives enabled women from low-income communities to access income-generating roles in the care economy.
Technical inputs to national and state task forces supported gender-responsive labour and employment policies, integrating care economy approaches to increase women’s workforce participation. The UN also supported the adoption of a State Plan of Action on child labour and integrated Fundamental Principles and Rights at Work — including elimination of child and forced labour — into industry training systems, promoting safer, more equitable employment across sectors.

planEntities.description:
The United Nations strengthened institutional and financing mechanisms to improve women-led MSMEs’ access to affordable finance, digital capabilities and business support services.
Through the Fund for Women Entrepreneurs, an innovative blended financing model mobilised USD 1.3 million in low-cost, collateral-free credit from over 2,100 social investors, expanding access to capital for underserved women entrepreneurs. The initiative supported 2,619 women-led enterprises — 80% from SC, ST and OBC communities — with finance, mentoring and digital literacy, enhancing their capacity to improve business operations, adopt new models and scale sustainably.
With a 96% repayment rate and 4,071 jobs created, the model demonstrated a scalable and inclusive approach to strengthening women-led MSMEs and promoting equitable enterprise growth.

planEntities.name: Addressing marine litter and marine plastic – a systemic approach in the Caspian Sea
planEntities.parentName: Fragile ecosystems of Iran are managed sustainably through application of sustainable land and water resource management approach
planEntities.description:
Under this project implemented jointly by UNDP and UNEP through the Tehran Convention Secretariat, with funding from the Russian Federation's ODA programme, the following results are anticipated in 2027:
•	Strengthening the evidence base on land-based sources of pollution, including marine litter, affecting Iran's Caspian coast.
•	Developing regionally harmonized marine litter monitoring guidelines in support of the Moscow Protocol under the Tehran Convention.
•	Reviewing relevant national legislation and initiating preparatory work on Iran's National Action Plan for pollution control.
•	Supporting integrated coastal zone management through the development of national inputs to regional guidelines.

planEntities.name: Improving Disaster Risk Management to Strengthen Climate and Disaster Resilience in Iran
planEntities.parentName: National and provincial government organizations have strengthened policy and institutional mechanisms to effectively plan, implement, and monitor disaster risk reduction, disaster response and disaster recovery.
planEntities.description:
Iran is grappling with a multitude of severe climate-related issues. These include floods, droughts, desertification, dust storms, and declining biodiversity. The economic impact of natural disasters in Iran is predominantly from hydro-meteorological hazards, such as floods and droughts, accounting for about 70% of long-term damages, with the remaining 30% attributed to earthquakes and other disasters. Floods regularly afflict different parts of the country, placing Iran among the top 20 nations worldwide in terms of flood damage. 
This project consists of two components:  
Component 1: Flood Inundation Mapping and Risk Assessment in a Selected Basin for Early Warning System Development
Component 2: Agricultural Drought Risk Assessment in the Selected Basin

planEntities.parentName: Fragile ecosystems of Iran are managed sustainably through application of sustainable land and water resource management approach
planEntities.description: UNESCO Tehran Office, in line with its mandate to promote sustainable development, environmental awareness, and youth engagement, is supporting the Implementation of the Mohit-Yar environmental education programme ln cooperation with the Department of Environment of the Islamic Republic of Iran. This Initiative aligns with UNESCO's strategic objectives in Education for Sustainable Development (ESD), Global Citizenship Education, youth empowerment, biodiversity conservation, and community participation. The programme aims to enhance environmental literacy, foster responsibility among children and youth, and integrate environmental education across formal and informal learning spaces in Iran.

planEntities.name: Hyrcanian Forest Wildfire Recovery and Preparedness Initiative
planEntities.parentName: Capacities developed to mitigate and adapt to climate emergencies (e.g. SDS), education and awareness raising
planEntities.description:
In early November, the wildfire erupted in the village of Elit, Mazandaran Province, spreading rapidly across steep and inaccessible terrain that threatened the Hyrcanian forests and nearby communities. Although the fire has largely been contained, continued monitoring is required to prevent re-ignition. In response to a request from the Government, the UNESCO Tehran Office (UTO) applied for support under the Extrabudgetary Emergency Fund. 
In this context, the UTO will support the National Environment Fund (NEF), affiliated with the Department of Environment of the Islamic Republic of Iran, in implementing the project entitled "Hyrcanian Forest Wildfire Recovery and Preparedness Initiative."

planEntities.name: Efficient sewage management to enhance government capacities on climate change adaptation
planEntities.parentName: Capacities developed to mitigate and adapt to climate emergencies (e.g. SDS), education and awareness raising
planEntities.description:
Based on a partnership with the provincial Water and wastewater Company, the construction of a comprehensive sewage collection network in Kohak was committed by this company, while UNICEF committed to construct the treatment package. Construction of this Sewage Treatment Plant in Kohak village, in Zahak county of Sistan and Baluchestan province, preserves water resources form contamination, benefiting 10,000 local population in Kohak. In collaboration with the project consulting company, the engineering services were successfully completed, encompassing design, calculations, technical specifications, and necessary documentation across structural, mechanical, electrical, and civil disciplines. These deliverables were handed over to the relevant stakeholders, ensuring alignment with project standards and requirements. The design of the system is such that the quality of the treated wastewater would meet the environmental standards set by the Iranian Department of Environmental for the nutrients, heavy metals and microbiological parameters, allowing its outlet to be used for green space irrigation.

A leading company from the Iranian private sector was selected as the contractor for the construction, transportation, installation, and utilization of the sewage treatment plant. The construction of the plant started in the company’s workshop in Isfahan and was completed by September 2024, including all 6 sewage reservoirs, and the package was ready to be transferred to Kohak. 

Following the initial phases, site preparation in Kohak was carried out, ensuring the area was fully prepared for the installation of the treatment package. The workshop mobilization in Kohak was successfully completed in September 2024, including the installation and commissioning of essential machinery, tools, and materials at the project site. This involved setting up prefabricated rooms, pumps, lights, electric panels, and tachometers to support the construction and operation of the facility.

The construction of a concrete platform for the sewage treatment package was the next stage. The platform was successfully completed in October 2024, and the treatment system was transferred from Isfahan to Kohak and installed over it. The contractor utilized the capacity of local concrete delivery companies to facilitate the construction process.

.Day-to-day resident technical supervision during the execution process was carried out by a qualified consulting company from the private sector, contracted by the provincial WWC. UNICEF, in collaboration with the provincial WWC, also provided high-level technical oversight of the project in coordination with the consulting company.

As a result of this support, the water quality of aquifers (Chahnimes) will be improved, leading to improved water quality for the Niatak Refugee settlement which is supplied through this wate rresource and environmental sanitation in areas will be improved, leading to the advanced well-being of the refugees and the people from the host communities living in this area. This project was completed by the end of December 2024. The commissioning and utilization was followed in 2025. This is the last component of the joint initiative between the Republic of Korea and UNICEF Iran with the current funding.

planEntities.name: Strengthening national capacity on implementing Water and Sanitation for Health Facility Improvement (WASH FIT) to improve quality of care in health care facilities (WHO and UNICEF)
planEntities.parentName: Capacities in Government strengthened to develop and implement climate action including National Adaptation Plan (NAP)
planEntities.description:
"This programme intervention strengthens the capacity of experts of Ministry of Health and Medical Education (MOHME), universities of Medical Education and environmental health technicians of healthcare facilities in a training for trainers (TOT) workshop run jointly by UNICEF (regional and national), WHO (regional and national), and MOHME staff for implementing and coordinating WASH in Healthcare Facilities programmes/initiatives. The workshop enhanced the participants' skills and knowledge in supporting their countries in implementing the WASH FIT approach, gaining practical insights from regional and international experts, and sharing past experiences and lessons learned. Through this intervention, MoHME was further supported to institutionalize the WASH-FIT approach within the national health system, ensuring its systematic integration into policies, standards, and routine practices across healthcare facilities."
Between 11 and 15 October, environmental health experts from 40 universities of medical sciences across 25 provinces participated in a national training of trainers (ToT), organized jointly by the Ministry of Health and Medical Education (MoHME), the World Health Organization (WHO) and the United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF).

The workshop strengthened the capacity of participants to lead improvements in water supply, sanitation and hygiene (WASH), waste management and cleaning services in health facilities, essential elements of infection prevention, patient safety and quality care.
The training combined classroom learning with field visits and practical group exercises, allowing participants to apply the WASH FIT methodology in real-world settings. Facilitators from WHO and UNICEF noted the high level of professionalism and engagement, describing it as one of the most successful WASH FIT trainings conducted in the Region.

WASH FIT is a risk-based, iterative management tool developed by WHO and UNICEF to help health facilities identify hazards, prioritize improvements and monitor progress. Its adoption can reduce health care-associated infections, improve maternal and newborn care and build resilience against climate and health threats. In use in more than 50 countries, it enables health facilities to identify risks, plan and prioritize low-cost improvements and monitor progress over time.

The initiative builds on the Islamic Republic of Iran’s ongoing efforts to improve WASH in health care, including a 2021 baseline assessment of 742 facilities and a costed national roadmap developed with WHO support. It aligns with the WHO–MoHME 5-year strategic framework on environmental and occupational health and the UN Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework for Iran.

The workshop concluded with a high-level ceremony at Shahid Rajaei Heart Hospital attended by senior officials from MoHME, the Ministry of Energy, Presidential Department of Environment, WHO, UNICEF and the United Nations.

Based on the final report, here's a concise paragraph that omits the names of the individual locations:

The project successfully completed the assessment, design, and installation of seven hybrid solar power systems for 7 remote rural health houses in Chabahar rural areas, providing a reliable renewable energy solution to support essential health services during frequent power outages. Each facility was equipped with a 5 kW hybrid solar PV system, a 5 kW hybrid inverter, and a 4.8–5.0 kWh lithium battery storage system, designed to ensure uninterrupted operation of critical equipment such as vaccine refrigerators, lighting, and ventilation during grid interruptions. The systems also enable surplus electricity to be exported to the national grid, generating additional income for the health facilities while reducing greenhouse gas emissions and strengthening the resilience of primary healthcare services in underserved areas. This pilot and pattern is documented by UNICEF and negotiations are ongoing with MoHME to adopt this in similar health care facilities.

planEntities.name: Rolling out Young Water Guardians Initiative
planEntities.parentName: Capacities developed to mitigate and adapt to climate emergencies (e.g. SDS), education and awareness raising
planEntities.description:
The “Water-Guardians” initiative aims to empower students to take an active role in water conservation. Through training sessions with WWC experts and educational materials, children learn how to advocate for responsible water use, both in school and at home. 
Young Water Guardians: How Students in Birjand Are Leading the Way in Water Conservation

When my colleague and I arrived in Birjand on a crisp December morning, we were welcomed by a team of experts from the Water and Water waste Company (WWC), eager to take us to a special event - the “Water Celebration.” This UNICEF-supported initiative builds on long-standing educational programs about water conservation, implemented jointly by the Ministry of Energy and the Ministry of Education. As we drove through the dry landscape of Birjand, it was clear why such efforts were essential: every drop of water mattered.
In the car, WWC experts explained that renovating old water facilities and raising awareness about responsible water use were top priorities. That’s why UNICEF, through its WASH and Social and Behavior Change (SBC) programmes, had stepped in not only to upgrade water taps, drinking fountains, and restroom facilities in schools but also to launch an educational campaign called “Water for all, all for Water”. This campaign reached 700 students across three primary schools, engaging them as active participants in water conservation through the “Water-Guardians” initiative.

A Celebration of Water Awareness
Upon arrival at Sanderos School in Birjand, we stepped were welcomed into a vibrant celebration hall filled with energy and enthusiasm. More than 340 Iranian and Afghan students, all wearing colorful caps adorned with water drop symbols, held educational pamphlets about responsible water use. Around the hall, students’ artwork lined the walls, showcasing creative expressions of the importance of water. A lively water-themed song played in the background, setting the tone for an engaging event.
The celebration featured a variety of activities, students shared traditional stories about water conservation, animated characters highlighted the consequences of water waste, and winners of a water themed painting competition were announced. The event ended with a powerful call to action from school authorities, encouraging students to become agents of change in their families and communities.
After the event, we toured the newly renovated water facilities, including modernized drinking fountains, upgraded taps, and repaired restrooms facilities - supported by UNICEF. It was heartwarming to see children excited about these improvements. “Upgrading the taps and water facilities has made a big difference. Now, there’s no more leaking water!” shared Ahmad, a third-grade student. “Some of us used to worry about the old taps wasting water,” added Pooya, another student. Their words reaffirmed the impact of UNICEF’s support—not just in improving infrastructure but in fostering a sense of responsibility among students.

Students as Water Ambassadors[MN1.1]
The “Water-Guardians” initiative aims to empower students to take an active role in water conservation. Through training sessions with WWC experts and educational materials, children learn how to advocate for responsible water use, both in school and at home. Recognizing the potential of this initiative, school authorities and government officials expressed their commitment to expanding it. “Students are the best ambassadors for water conservation. Their engagement will not only shape their behavior but also influence their families and communities,” said Mr. Asemani, the school principal.

Looking Ahead: A Student-Led Water Movement; Closing ceremony 
UNICEF with the cooperation of the Ministry of Energy and WWC plans to support strengthening and[MN2.1] expanding the “Water-Guardians” initiative across more schools in 2025, creating a network of student volunteers who receive educational briefings from WWC and committed to water preservation. The closing ceremony for the “Water for All, All for Water” campaign that was planned to reach 5000 students in primary school across the province,  happened in early February with high level participation from Ministry of Energy, UNICEF and national WWC representatives, Member of Parliament for South Khorasan and Governor General of the town and most importantly 400 school boys and girls students in Nehbandan town. The ceremony was an opportunity to underscore the crucial role of children in water conservation efforts, the importance of water education and awareness raising in the communities by students, connecting schools to WWC and calling for expanding this successful campaign to other provinces. An exhibition of hand-made crafts and paintings by students with the theme of not wasting water was an eye-catching part of the event that was well planned and displayed conjointly with the music singing, role playing, interactive questions and answers with the students by authorities, hands-on guidance for appropriate behaviours that leads to saving water at home and school, and many more engaging activities. Students were fully engaged and attentive to the ceremony while exchanging and playing with one another in the hall. The event was followed by a planning meeting between UNICEF and WWC on how to take forward the initiative and involve more sectors. This has been the first time that UNICEF’s contribution in awareness raising for water conservation programmes among the students in schools occurred.  
As our visit came to an end, I was convinced that investing in young people as water stewards can create lasting change. With the right education and support, students can be the driving force behind a more sustainable future for Iran’s water resources.

planEntities.name: Improvement of water consumption habits and management
planEntities.parentName: Capacities developed to mitigate and adapt to climate emergencies (e.g. SDS), education and awareness raising
planEntities.description:
Identification of household water consumption behaviors and practices, and development of a community-based action plan (to promote improved habits and water consumption management in urban and rural households of Yasuj) was the primary purpose of this project.
Project proceedings: The project adopted a **concurrent mixed-methods approach**, combining quantitative and qualitative research to develop evidence-based and context-specific recommendations for reducing household water consumption. The quantitative component consisted of a structured household survey of **100 urban and rural residents aged 15 years and above**, selected through multi-stage cluster sampling to ensure representation across gender, age groups, place of residence, and persons with disabilities. The qualitative component included **40 in-depth interviews** (20 community members and 20 water experts and key informants), followed by **two two-day participatory consultation workshops** involving **20 participants** (10 community representatives and 10 water experts) to validate findings and co-develop practical behaviour change interventions. Quantitative data were analysed using statistical methods, while qualitative data underwent grounded theory analysis. The combined findings informed the development of a community-based behavioural intervention package and an operational action plan for sustainable water demand management.   

Summary of Results

The study found that excessive household water consumption is driven primarily by deeply rooted daily habits and social norms rather than a lack of awareness alone. High-consumption practices—such as prolonged showers, leaving taps running, washing courtyards and vehicles with hoses, inefficient irrigation of home gardens, and improper use of household appliances—are reinforced by cultural perceptions of cleanliness, comfort, and convenience, as well as by climatic conditions, housing characteristics, and economic factors.

The findings also showed that knowledge alone is insufficient to achieve sustained behaviour change. Participants emphasized the need for practical, locally relevant communication, family-based interventions, and school-based education, with children serving as effective agents of change within households. Positive incentives, such as rewards for low water consumption, were perceived as more motivating than punitive measures alone.

Clear differences were identified between urban and rural communities. Urban households reported higher sensitivity to water shortages due to pressure reductions and service interruptions, while rural households, with greater access to natural water sources, often perceived water as abundant and showed lower sensitivity to conservation. Water use patterns also differed, highlighting the need for context-specific interventions rather than a one-size-fits-all approach.

Overall, the results indicate that effective water demand management requires integrated behaviour change strategies that combine awareness raising with practical guidance, social norm change, incentives, improved access to water-saving technologies, and interventions tailored to local socio-cultural and environmental contexts.

planEntities.name: Improving climate resilience in schools
planEntities.parentName: Capacities developed to mitigate and adapt to climate emergencies (e.g. SDS), education and awareness raising
planEntities.description:
Improving climate resilience in schools of 2 provinces hit by climate change, namely Sistan and Baluchestan and Khorasan Razavi
WASH rehabilitation:  

At the beginning of the project, UNICEF worked with regional experts from MoE and the Organization for Development, Renovation and Equipping of Schools (ODRES) to identify schools requiring support in sanitation facilities and water hygiene in the provinces of Khorasan Razavi and Sistan and Baluchestan, which host significant numbers of Afghan students. 

The Tabadkan educational region in Khorasan Razavi Province, one of UNICEF’s target areas, is among the most important educational areas hosting refugee students. According to available statistics, 29,000 Afghan students out of a total student population of 165,000 benefit from MoE educational services in this region. Some schools in the area have student populations that are up to 80 per cent Afghan. These areas, which also host internal migrants from eastern parts of the country, other parts of the province and the city of Mashhad, face substantial infrastructural challenges and are considered deprived areas based on relevant deprivation indices. 

In Khorasan Razavi Province, rehabilitation of WASH facilities was implemented in Mashhad’s Tabadkan and District No. 5, covering a total of 15 schools. Through these interventions, 3,104 refugee students, including 1,847 girls and 1,257 boys, and 7,162 Iranian students, including 3,393 girls and 3,769 boys, benefited from improved WASH infrastructure. Overall, 10,266 students gained access to safer and more functional water, sanitation and hygiene facilities. The activities focused on restoring and upgrading school WASH systems to ensure safer water access and improved sanitation conditions. 

In Sistan and Baluchestan Province, rehabilitation activities were carried out in the cities of Zahedan and Zabol, reaching 18 schools. These interventions benefited 1,720 refugee students, including 1,268 girls and 452 boys, and 11,031 Iranian students, including 7,342 girls and 3,689 boys. In total, 12,751 students were supported through the rehabilitation of WASH facilities. The works significantly improved water supply systems, sanitation facilities and overall hygiene conditions in the targeted schools. 

Based on the results of ongoing needs assessments during implementation, UNICEF complemented this project through other funding sources by procuring and installing essential WASH items in both provinces. This support covered 87 schools, including 14 in Khorasan Razavi and 73 in Sistan and Baluchestan. A total of 4,041 refugee students, including 1,872 girls and 2,169 boys, and 43,562 Iranian students, including 19,509 girls and 24,053 boys, benefited from the provision of water pumps, water tanks, water purifiers and water coolers. Overall, these procurement activities supported 47,603 students, strengthening access to safe drinking water and enhancing the functionality and sustainability of school WASH facilities in both provinces. 

Through the combined implementation of WASH rehabilitation and the procurement and installation of essential WASH items, the project reached a total of 120 schools across Khorasan Razavi and Sistan and Baluchestan provinces. In total, 70,620 students benefited from improved WASH services, including 8,865 refugee students, of whom 4,987 were girls and 3,878 were boys, and 61,755 Iranian students, of whom 30,244 were girls and 31,511 were boys. These interventions significantly enhanced access to safe water and sanitation facilities, contributing to healthier and more supportive learning environments in the targeted schools.

planEntities.name: Consumption of ODS reduced (Joint programme HPMP Stage II)
planEntities.parentName: Capacities in government and private sector enhanced through provision of technical support and technological solutions to reduce carbon emissions
planEntities.description: Iran`s HPMP was approved in the 63rd Meeting of the Executive Committee. HPMP included investment activities in RAC sector as well as foam sector and project management component. Total funding that was approved was US $10.39 million. Over the last three years, Iran has implemented a range of activities including investment projects, awareness and information outreach activities and regulations for facilitating HCFC phase-out. Agreements were signed with the manufacturing companies covered under HPMP in RAC applications and foam sector including continuous and discontinuous sandwich panels and domestic refrigerators. In addition to the above, the Government has enacted policies and regulations to control growth of HCFC consumption in the manufacturing sector; implemented licensing and quota system to restrict import of HCFCs to limits specified in the agreement, and carried out training program for service technicians and enforcement officials. The above measures have helped the country in constraining the growth of HCFC-22 and HCFC-141b consumption in Iran.

planEntities.description: The Nutrition Joint Programme aims at ensuring national and county government institutions and non-state actors have enhanced governance frameworks and strengthened capacities to deliver equitable, quality, and integrated nutrition services through a systems approach, including in humanitarian settings. This is in light with the constitution of Kenya that acknowledges nutrition as a constitutional right as per article 43 (1) (c) - the right of every Kenyan to be free from hunger and a right to adequate food of acceptable quality, and article 53 (l) (c) - the right of every child to basic nutrition, shelter, and health care. The JP was developed through a highly consultative process with the participation of the 5 PUNOs (UNICEF, WFP, FAO, WHO and UNHCR), various Government Ministries, Departments & Agencies, CSOs, Youth, LNOB Groups, SUN Movement, and private sector. The nutrition JP is Led by UNICEF and will be implemented over three years starting from July 2023 with an overall estimated budget of USD 52.6 Million.

Priority will be placed on youth between the ages of 15-34 years with the main focus being youth traditionally left behind such as young women, youth with disability, and those in ASAL counties and informal urban settlements.

planEntities.parentName: Output 1.2.2. planEntities.description: This sub-output focuses on building the technical, institutional, and community-level capacities necessary to deliver inclusive and sustainable child protection and social protection services. It involves strengthening the ability of national and county governments, as well as non-state actors such as civil society organizations, faith-based groups, and community-based institutions to design, implement, monitor, and expand integrated and inclusive protection systems. Particular emphasis is placed on ensuring that these programmes are responsive to the needs of vulnerable populations, and are anchored in rights-based, gender-sensitive, and resilience-oriented approaches. Through targeted training, policy and legislative support, resource mobilization, and community engagement, the initiative aims to promote coordination, efficiency, and accountability in the delivery of protective and preventive services across the country.

planEntities.description: This sub-output aims to strengthen coordination mechanisms, data systems, and the use of evidence in policymaking, planning, and budgeting to improve child protection and social protection outcomes. It supports the establishment and operationalization of multi-sectoral coordination frameworks at national and county levels, enabling aligned and efficient delivery of services. It also focuses on enhancing data collection, analysis, and management systems such as Management Information Systems (MIS) and registries to ensure timely, disaggregated, and reliable information is available for decision-making. By promoting evidence-based approaches, this sub-output contributes to more responsive, equitable, and resource-efficient policies and programmes that address the needs of vulnerable populations.

planEntities.description: This intervention is aimed at including voices of youth in the project interventions, by ensuring that youth actively participate hence ensures that programmes stay relevant and responsive to their needs. This will be realized through partnerships with youth in intervention design, development, implementation and monitoring as well as supporting youth-led initiatives. This entails;  1. Strengthening the capacities of Youth-Led Organisations (YLOs) as partners for interventions, developing an action-oriented programme that targets YLO to strengthen their capacities towards different pillars of the programme and supporting the development of their strategic plans and pilot specific interventions that the YLO can implement after the training, 2. Youth Innovation Challenge - Design youth innovation challenges targeting organizations rather than specific individuals. 3. Rights at Work - This includes collaboration with the Central Organization of Trade Unions (COTU) to sensitize youth to join trade unions and promote their active participation and engagement in trade union activities. 4. Youth in Sports and Orange Economy Initiatives - Understanding that sports enhance social cohesion as well as the creative economy. Work closely with TVETS and existing youth centres to amplify sports activities for youth. Linkages of creatives to mainstream media, recording labels and mentors for coaching and mentorships. 5. Youth employment and leadership forums: Support youth employment and leadership forums. This will be structured as blended webinars with various thematic discussions on trends in the labour market, skills development, orange and green economy, and youth meaningful participation structures by partnering with various YLO or Youth Advisory Council (YAC) in the country.

planEntities.description: This sub-output underpins the development and realization of inclusive, evidence-based policies, regulatory, and institutional frameworks that enable green and blue economic transition, sustainable business development, and green finance. It is designed to enhance skills development systems through continuous professional development policies, standards, and guidelines, built through engagements between industries and training institutions. It further promotes institutionalization of Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) among the youth, facilitates the implementation of the harmonised regional TVET Qualifications Framework, and revitalizes the Kenya Labour Market Information System to improve labour market linkages. It also strengthens mechanisms to expand youth employment in foreign labour markets, scale ICT and innovation in training, and facilitates opportunities for youth in emerging sectors (i.e. the green, blue, creative, digital, and care economies), aligned to the national strategy for green skills and jobs.

planEntities.description:
This Joint Programme on Peace and PVE therefore draws on the conclusions of the PBA Review, the experience of a wide range of Kenyan government and civil society actors, and of the UN system in Kenya and globally, to focus on three strategic areas of change:
Strengthening and supporting an effective National Peacebuilding Architecture as a necessary precondition for effective responses to peacebuilding and PVE challenges in Kenya, including creating a new PeaceBuilding Fund
Building effective sub-national and county-level responses to conflict and peacebuilding challenges that are attuned to the context as conflict dynamics manifest themselves very differently in different parts of Kenya.
Supporting the empowerment and inclusion in peacebuilding of key LNOB groups, most notably youth & women, as peacebuilding is most effective when it is inclusive.

planEntities.description: The project will support the development, review, and implementation of national and county-level policy, legal, institutional, and regulatory frameworks to ensure gender-responsive climate action and disaster risk management (DRM). Building on capacity needs assessments (e.g., CADRI), the initiative will strengthen institutional capacities for policy formulation, implementation, monitoring, and reporting on DRR and resilience strategies. A multi-agency and participatory approach will be employed to formulate or review DRM-related bills and policies, incorporating gender considerations at every stage. Additionally, the project will promote awareness creation, training, and capacity building for both government and non-state actors to institutionalize gender-responsive approaches across all climate and DRM interventions.

planEntities.name: Sub Output 2.1.2.2. Support technical and institutional capacities at national and county levels to implement gender-responsive climate action and disaster risk management using innovative technologies and other solutions.
planEntities.parentName: OUTPUT 2.1.2: Strengthened capacities and policies/ strategies of institutions and communities for climate action, disaster risk management and justice for the benefit of youth, women, PWDs, people in ASALs and urban informal settlements
planEntities.description: The project will strengthen technical and institutional capacities at both national and county levels to implement gender-responsive climate action and disaster risk management (DRM) through the use of innovative technologies and inclusive solutions. This will include establishing and/or enhancing structured DRM coordination mechanisms, such as national platforms and county DRM committees, to improve multi-sectoral collaboration and policy implementation. The initiative will also support targeted capacity development for government institutions tasked with DRM and climate policy, informed by comprehensive national and county-level needs assessments (e.g., CADRI). Further, it will promote resource mobilization and investment in disaster risk reduction, including the review and operationalization of the Disaster Risk Financing Strategy. Emphasis will be placed on integrating gender considerations and leveraging technology-driven tools for risk-informed planning, early warning, and community-based resilience building.

planEntities.description: The project seeks to enhance community resilience by promoting sustainable, climate-smart, and diversified livelihoods that reduce vulnerability to climate shocks and crises. This will be achieved through the integration of disaster risk reduction (DRR) approaches into skills development, entrepreneurship, social protection systems, and livelihood initiatives, particularly within priority value chains and urban informal sectors. Emphasis will be placed on innovative, climate-resilient housing and secure land tenure to foster inclusive, sustainable urbanization and infrastructure. In parallel, the project will strengthen county government capacities to develop, implement, and enforce legal and policy frameworks that advance food and nutrition security, ensuring no one is left behind.

planEntities.description: This project aims to scale up the zKe: Youth Voices digital platform as a trusted civic engagement tool that empowers Kenyan youth to actively participate in governance and national dialogue. Building on the successful 2024 pilot, the project responds to the urgency revealed by youth-led protests, which highlighted deep frustrations over exclusion and lack of trust in institutions. By combining digital tools with grassroots engagement, zKe seeks to institutionalize youth participation, counter misinformation and hate speech, and promote inclusive, peaceful dialogue ahead of the 2027 elections. Anchored on four pillars—Talk, Track, Act, and Transform—the initiative fosters accountability, gender inclusion, and policy influence, particularly for young women and marginalized groups. It is implemented through a UN-led consortium and aligned with the UN Kenya Joint Programme on Youth, contributing to Vision 2030 and the Bottom-Up Economic Transformation Agenda.

planEntities.description: This project promotes inclusive governance, human rights, and accountability in Kenya by supporting peaceful and participatory elections, advancing political and electoral reforms, and strengthening early warning systems. It safeguards freedom of expression, enhances human rights institutions, and addresses violence against vulnerable groups—especially women, children, and youth—with a focus on femicide prevention. planEntities.description: This Joint Programme (JP) a is a concerted effort by several UN agencies, notably UNESCO, UNFPA, UN WOMEN, ILO, UNICEF, UNDP, and WFP to provide a consolidated support to youth empowerment particularly in the dimensions of decent employment, voice and agency as well as increasing their skills. Building on the existing reform agenda set by UN member states, which asks the UN development system to accelerate its efforts to increase coherence and effectiveness of its operations in the field, the UN agencies will deliver this JP as one UN by leveraging on their core areas of competencies. This will be done though mainstreaming in national programmes and policy frameworks; strengthening institutional capacities and capabilities among the youth; and creating fundamental linkages to integrate interventions with local value chains, among others. Successful initiatives will be adopted by the government as well as collaborating partners and incorporated into exiting national programmes. Through a catalytic fund from the Government of Canada, the JP aims at incentivizing innovative and transformative gender interventions aiming at reaching 60 per cent young women and 40 per cent young men in Nairobi, Mombasa, Kisumu, Isiolo, and Turkana Counties.

planEntities.description: The JP      RMNCAH will focus on three pillars namely, Newborn and Child health, Adolescent health, and Reproductive & Maternal health. The program will address challenges in these pillars by focusing on five strategies: 1) Strengthening partnerships and coordination 2) Enhancing continuous quality improvement and accountability for results 3) Supporting innovative and cost-efficient approaches to capacity and skills enhancement of healthcare workers, 4) Empowering communities to co-design and plan for RMNCA health services to ensure no one is left behind 5) Advocate for increased domestic financing for RMNCAH. The expected outcome of the programme is Outcome 1.2 as given in the UN Sustainable Development Cooperative Framework: By 2026, all people in Kenya at risk of being left behind - particularly all women and girls, all youth, and children, all in the ASALS counties and all in the informal urban settlements - have improved, inclusive and equitable social and protection services. planEntities.description: The Nutrition Joint Programme aims at ensuring national and county government institutions and non-state actors have enhanced governance frameworks and strengthened capacities to deliver equitable, quality, and integrated nutrition services through a systems approach, including in humanitarian settings. This is in light with the constitution of Kenya that acknowledges nutrition as a constitutional right as per article 43 (1) (c) - the right of every Kenyan to be free from hunger and a right to adequate food of acceptable quality, and article 53 (l) (c) - the right of every child to basic nutrition, shelter, and health care. The JP was developed through a highly consultative process with the participation of the 5 PUNOs (UNICEF, WFP, FAO, WHO and UNHCR), various Government Ministries, Departments & Agencies, CSOs, Youth, LNOB Groups, SUN Movement, and private sector. The nutrition JP is Led by UNICEF and will be implemented over three years starting from July 2023 with an overall estimated budget of USD 52.6 Million.

planEntities.description:
The programme seeks to transform Kenya’s coffee sector into a catalytic driver of inclusive, green, and resilient economic development. Anchored in the principles of the 2030 Agenda and Kenya’s own development frameworks—such as Vision 2030, the Bottom-Up Economic Transformation Agenda (BETA), and the Agricultural Sector Transformation and Growth Strategy (ASTGS)—this Joint Programme brings together multiple UN agencies, government actors, and private sector partners under a shared ambition: to unlock sustainable development through value chain transformation.
The programme is led by UNDP as the convening agency and implemented jointly with FAO, UN Women, UNIDO, and UNEP, in partnership with the Ministry of Agriculture and Livestock Development and county governments in key coffee-growing regions. It is supported through the UN SDG Multi-Partner Trust Fund (MPTF), with co-financing expected from public and private sources.
At its core, the programme aims to reposition the coffee value chain as a strategic lever for achieving the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), especially those related to poverty reduction, gender equality, decent work, responsible production, and climate action. It recognizes that despite its historical and economic significance, Kenya’s coffee sector has been constrained by policy bottlenecks, limited value addition, environmental degradation, and exclusion of women and youth.
To address these challenges, the programme is structured around three mutually reinforcing outcomes:
1.	An Enabling Policy and Investment Environment: The programme will support ongoing policy and regulatory reforms in the coffee sector to enhance transparency, attract investment, and promote quality standards. It will also establish a blended finance facility to de-risk private investment and develop bankable investment cases that align with SDG priorities.
2.	Sustainable Coffee Production and Climate Action: Farmers will be supported to adopt climate-smart, regenerative agricultural practices, including intercropping, agroforestry, and organic soil management. The programme will contribute to land restoration, improved soil health, and biodiversity protection while reducing emissions from agricultural practices. Eco-certification and climate adaptation will be central pillars of resilience building within farming communities.
3.	Inclusive Coffee Value Chain Development: The programme will focus on expanding market access through digital traceability systems, product differentiation, and branding of Kenyan coffee. The programme seeks to transform Kenya’s coffee sector into a catalytic driver of inclusive, green, and resilient economic development. Anchored in the principles of the 2030 Agenda and Kenya’s own development frameworks—such as Vision 2030, the Bottom-Up Economic Transformation Agenda (BETA), and the Agricultural Sector Transformation and Growth Strategy (ASTGS)—this Joint Programme brings together multiple UN agencies, government actors, and private sector partners under a shared ambition: to unlock sustainable development through value chain transformation.
The programme is led by UNDP as the convening agency and implemented jointly with FAO, UN Women, UNIDO, and UNEP, in partnership with the Ministry of Agriculture and Livestock Development and county governments in key coffee-growing regions. It is supported through the UN SDG Multi-Partner Trust Fund (MPTF), with co-financing expected from public and private sources.
At its core, the programme aims to reposition the coffee value chain as a strategic lever for achieving the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), especially those related to poverty reduction, gender equality, decent work, responsible production, and climate action. It recognizes that despite its historical and economic significance, Kenya’s coffee sector has been constrained by policy bottlenecks, limited value addition, environmental degradation, and exclusion of women and youth.
To address these challenges, the programme is structured around three mutually reinforcing outcomes:
1.	An Enabling Policy and Investment Environment: The programme will support ongoing policy and regulatory reforms in the coffee sector to enhance transparency, attract investment, and promote quality standards. It will also establish a blended finance facility to de-risk private investment and develop bankable investment cases that align with SDG priorities.
2.	Sustainable Coffee Production and Climate Action: Farmers will be supported to adopt climate-smart, regenerative agricultural practices, including intercropping, agroforestry, and organic soil management. The programme will contribute to land restoration, improved soil health, and biodiversity protection while reducing emissions from agricultural practices. Eco-certification and climate adaptation will be central pillars of resilience building within farming communities.
3.	Inclusive Coffee Value Chain Development: The programme will focus on expanding market access through digital traceability systems, product differentiation, and branding of Kenyan coffee. Special emphasis will be placed on supporting women and youth to access opportunities in coffee production, processing, and entrepreneurship. Training, financial inclusion, and cooperatives will be leveraged to drive equitable participation and benefits.
By embedding environmental sustainability, gender responsiveness, and inclusive finance into all stages of the value chain, the programme seeks to create decent livelihoods, strengthen Kenya’s global positioning as a producer of premium, sustainable coffee, and contribute meaningfully to the SDGs. It reflects a systems approach that bridges climate action, economic empowerment, and sustainable trade.
In doing so, this initiative not only aligns with UNSDCF 2022–2026 Pillar II: Prosperity and Planet but also serves as a replicable model for how green value chains can unlock blended finance, deliver climate co-benefits, and enable locally led sustainable development.

planEntities.name: Integrated Community-based Management of High Value Mountain Ecosystems in Southern Kyrgyzstan for Multiple Benefits
planEntities.parentName: Critical ecosystems are better protected throughout the country, and the rational and sustainable use of natural resources, including water and land, is improved through gender-responsive, participatory and conflict-sensitive systems at all levels
planEntities.description: The objective of the project is to secure high value mountain ecosystem biodiversity and associated ecosystem services, while ensuring resilient and sustainable livelihoods in Kyrgyzstan’s Pamir-Alai landscape. The project’s components have been designed to address key threats and corresponding barriers to sustainable land management and biodiversity conservation within mountain forest and pasture ecosystems including Key Biodiversity Areas (KBAs) found in Kyrgyzstan’s Pamir-Alai Mountain landscape. The project will deliver Global Environmental Benefits using a participatory approach that ensures promotion of women, youth and vulnerable groups and equitable participation opportunities. The project’s approach is closely linked with the Land Degradation Neutrality (LDN) conceptual framework, and the project applies the avoid-reduce-reverse principle. The “avoid” principle is applied through the strengthening management of PAs, and improved spatial land use planning. The reduce principle is applied through improved forest and pasture management. The expected project results will be improved management and biodiversity conservation within 6 KBAs that cover 866,000 ha. The project will contribute to the establishment of 4 new national-level PAs covering 281,083.79 ha. Additionally, the project will support the improved management effectiveness of 5 national-level protected areas covering 153,250 ha. The project will improve the management of 563,949 hectares of high conservation value forest (HCVF) lands, including 500 hectares of degraded forest. The project will improve the management of 621,905 hectares of pastures, including 19,500 ha of degraded pastures. The project will improve livelihood benefits for 94,883 people, while improving the conservation status of globally significant biodiversity, and supporting Kyrgyzstan’s progress toward LDN.

planEntities.parentName: Accountable, participatory, transparent, and effective governance systems at all levels ensure the provision of quality services for all and inclusive spaces and promote social cohesion gender transformative systems of relations, and a violence free society.
planEntities.description: The project aims to enhance trust and enable a conducive environment on the Kyrgyz side of border areas with Uzbekistan for collaboration between both sides. Border areas between Kyrgyzstan and Uzbekistan have been marked by social tensions and conflict for many years. In recent years, both countries considerably increased their political and diplomatic relations at the strategic level, which gives a new impetus and presents significant opportunities for collaboration. However, border communities and relevant government agencies still have disproportionate capacities to effectively tackle the sudden upsurge in socio-economic, trade, cultural and humanitarian relationships. In the context of growing relations between Kyrgyzstan and Uzbekistan, the project aims to enable border communities and relevant government agencies to mitigate the risk and leverage the opportunities of increased cooperation and border mobility to promote a more peaceful and safer borderland environment. The project will be strengthening cooperation capacities across multiple sectors, improving safe and orderly genderresponsive border management and enhancing opportunities for positive interactions with their Uzbek counterparts. The project focuses on confidence and trust building between local authorities and communities living on the borderlands of Kyrgyzstan - Uzbekistan. Through enhanced capacities of border officials and local authorities, local communities, private sector and civil society actors, including those led by youth and women, the project will mitigate the negative consequences of increased mobility across the border and harness the potential trade and economic ties by creating socio-economic development and livelihood opportunities for better cross-border cooperation and relationships.

planEntities.parentName: Critical ecosystems are better protected throughout the country, and the rational and sustainable use of natural resources, including water and land, is improved through gender-responsive, participatory and conflict-sensitive systems at all levels
planEntities.description: A new ecological corridor of around 800,000 hectares, or 8,000 km², has been announced by the Kyrgyz Republic on 22 May 2025. The corridor is set to link up existing conservation areas and complete a protected area spanning a total of over 1,2 million hectares, in a landmark move for biodiversity. As the largest protected area of its kind in the country, it will enable snow leopards and their prey to better adapt to climate change. Also, grazing density will be reduced by almost one quarter, in agreement with local herders, to help restore pastures and allow wildlife to graze. This ecological corridor could become a model for Central Asia. The UN Environment Programme (UNEP) supported the Kyrgyz government by providing ecological modelling to help define the corridor’s borders. The area will connect the Khan-Tengri National Park and Naryn Nature Reserve, passing through several other conservation areas along the way. The corridor aims to safeguard migration and dispersal routes for key mountain wildlife species under pressure from changing habitat conditions due to overgrazing and climate change. Link: https://www.unep.org/news-and-stories/press-release/kyrgyz-republic-unveils-800000-hectare-ecological-corridor

planEntities.name: Climate knowledge of communities and institutions is strengthened to improve their capacity to respond to climate change at local level
planEntities.parentName: Climate policy, financing, and awareness mechanisms are designed and implemented that support climate actions, with the full participation of women and men at all decision-making levels
planEntities.description: The headwaters of main river systems in Central Asia heavily depend on the seasonal melting of cryosphere, with little additional precipitation input in their lower reaches. These rivers sustain the lives and livelihoods of the people and the economic development in the region, including Kyrgyzstan. However, glaciers in Kyrgyzstan are experiencing a rapid decline in mass. Changes in glaciers will have significant effects on the large populations of the region. It is therefore necessary to understand the impact of climate change on the cryosphere in the region and Kyrgyzstan, in particular. Activities under this sub-output aim to strengthen climate knowledge of communities and institutions in Kyrgyzstan to improve their capacity to respond to climate change. The sub-output will support evidence-based adaptation measures through scientific assessment of snow, glaciers, permafrost and water availability, while also fostering cooperation with regional and international partners to share knowledge and best practices relevant to Kyrgyzstan’s climate adaptation priorities.

planEntities.name: Enhanced responses to local and national water management challenges through improved water education, scientific research and awareness raising
planEntities.parentName: Critical ecosystems are better protected throughout the country, and the rational and sustainable use of natural resources, including water and land, is improved through gender-responsive, participatory and conflict-sensitive systems at all levels
planEntities.description: Kyrgyzstan is facing growing water management challenges driven by climate change, population growth and the need to ensure food and energy security. Changes in glacier melt and seasonal water availability are affecting both rural and urban communities, while shared river systems add further complexity to water governance. Water plays a central role in Kyrgyzstan’s sustainable development and is essential for achieving SDG 6, as well as other interlinked SDGs. This sub-output will strengthen national and local responses to water security challenges in Kyrgyzstan through enhanced water education, scientific research, capacity building and awareness raising. It will promote cooperation among water experts, policy makers, communities and youth, supporting more informed decision-making and sustainable water management practices aligned with national development priorities.

planEntities.name: Building capacities of national entities to conserve biodiversity and manage geological natural resources to support local sustainable development through UNESCO Man and the Biosphere (MAB) and the International Geosciences and Geoparks (IGGP) Programmes
planEntities.parentName: Critical ecosystems are better protected throughout the country, and the rational and sustainable use of natural resources, including water and land, is improved through gender-responsive, participatory and conflict-sensitive systems at all levels
planEntities.description: Kyrgyzstan is characterized by rich biodiversity and geodiversity. This sub-output will support national efforts to conserve biodiversity and sustainably manage geological resources by strengthening capacities of relevant institutions, local authorities and communities. Knowledge transfer from the scientific community to policy makers and local stakeholders will be promoted, with particular emphasis on youth as agents of change. Building on the principles of UNESCO’s Man and the Biosphere (MAB) Programme and the International Geosciences and Geoparks Programme (IGGP), the sub-output will strengthen existing cooperative networks and establish new partnerships. These platforms will facilitate exchange of knowledge and experience among stakeholders, contributing to resilient and green societies in Kyrgyzstan.

planEntities.name: Strengthening science-policy interface for DRR and providing scientific advice related to geohazards mitigation
planEntities.parentName: Capacity of disaster management systems is strengthened, and community resilience to multiple shocks is increased at all levels through enhanced participation of women in DRR planning, as well as effective investments, policies, mechanisms, and tools
planEntities.description: Kyrgyzstan is highly exposed and vulnerable to a wide range of natural hazards, including earthquakes, landslides, mudflows and floods, which are increasingly exacerbated by climate change. Glacier melting and formation of glacial lakes have significantly increased the risk of Glacier Lake Outburst Floods (GLOFs), posing serious threats to mountain communities, infrastructure, livelihoods and ecosystems. This sub-output focuses on strengthening the science-policy interface for disaster risk reduction (DRR) in Kyrgyzstan by improving risk knowledge, enhancing monitoring and analytical capacities, and providing scientific advice to national and local authorities. It will build capacities of government officials, young professionals and technical institutions involved in DRR and climate change adaptation, while directly engaging communities at risk. Cooperative networks will be further strengthened to facilitate knowledge exchange and coordinated action, contributing to reduced vulnerabilities and increased resilience to climate-related and geological hazards.

planEntities.name: Social Media 4 Peace (SM4P) - building resilience to online harmful content—including disinformation and hate speech—while safeguarding freedom of expression and fostering peace through social media
planEntities.parentName: Accountable, participatory, transparent, and effective governance systems at all levels ensure the provision of quality services for all and inclusive spaces and promote social cohesion gender transformative systems of relations, and a violence free society.
planEntities.description:
Social Media 4 Peace (SM4P - https://www.unesco.org/en/social-media4peace) is a global initiative implemented by UNESCO to build societies’ resilience to online harmful content—including disinformation and hate speech—while safeguarding freedom of expression and fostering peace through social media.  

In the digital world, harmful online content can deepen social divisions and even trigger offline violence, which is particularly true in conflict-prone and polarised societies. At the same time, efforts to address the harms of online content must respect and protect human rights, in particular freedom of expression and access to information.  SM4P works to strike this balance between addressing the spread and impact of harmful content while protecting freedom of expression. Importantly, the project aims to capture social, cultural, and linguistic nuances of the geographical areas where it operates to develop locally informed strategies that contribute to peace narratives and advance human rights for all.

Since 2021, the project has been implemented in four pilot countries: Bosnia and Herzegovina, Colombia, Indonesia, and Kenya. In 2025, building on the knowledge and lessons learned in that initial phase, the project has expanded its efforts to Iraq, Kyrgyzstan, and South Africa, bringing its approach to other countries facing similar challenges.
