planEntities.name: Strengthening the justice system through provision of essential legal aid services to  refugees, asylum – seekers and stateless persons, improving due process and justice mechanisms, capacitating state authorities
planEntities.parentName: The system of justice and out-of-court dispute resolution, as well as human rights institutions, ensure the full application of the rule of law, justice, equality, and the fight against corruption
planEntities.description:
UNHCR’s interventions during the reporting period contributed to strengthening the justice system and improving access to fair and effective legal remedies for refugees, asylum-seekers, and stateless persons in the Kyrgyz Republic. Through the provision of direct legal assistance, capacity development of national institutions, and community-focused awareness activities, UNHCR supported national efforts to advance the rule of law, uphold equality before the law, and prevent discrimination and rights violations affecting vulnerable groups.
UNHCR’s implementing partner delivered legal aid services and legal counselling to 932 refugees and asylum-seekers, ensuring that individuals at risk of rights infringements received timely, professional support to navigate administrative and judicial procedures. These services improved the ability of persons of concern to understand and claim their rights, access documentation, and address barriers linked to their legal status. In cases where individuals faced unjust or incorrect decisions in asylum procedures, UNHCR’s partner represented 121 asylum-seekers in courts to appeal rejections of refugee status. This direct legal representation strengthened procedural fairness and contributed to the integrity of national asylum systems.
To enhance the capacity of justice-sector institutions, UNHCR supported seven training activities for 185 representatives of law enforcement agencies, the General Prosecutor’s Office, national human rights institutions, and the judiciary. These sessions increased institutional understanding of international protection principles, refugee rights, and citizenship-related issues, thereby improving the ability of state authorities to apply standards of due process, prevent discrimination, and ensure equitable treatment of all individuals under their jurisdiction. This work contributes to strengthening the responsiveness, professionalism, and human rights compliance of justice mechanisms.
Complementing these system-level interventions, UNHCR’s implementing partner organized fourteen information and outreach events for refugees and asylum-seekers on their rights, obligations, and procedures necessary for integration. Through these events, community members gained essential knowledge about legal protections, available grievance mechanisms, and pathways to lawful residence and participation in society. This supported their ability to engage confidently and independently with public institutions, reducing vulnerability to exploitation, discrimination, and rights violations.
Together, these actions contributed to strengthening due process guarantees, improving access to justice, and promoting equal treatment before the law. They supported national efforts to eliminate discrimination and violence against women and girls, promote rule-of-law–based governance, and reinforce institutions responsible for protecting and promoting human rights. Through this combination of legal aid, institutional capacity building, and community empowerment, UNHCR helped advance a justice system that is more accessible, accountable, and inclusive for all.

planEntities.name: The Programme for Country Partnership for the Kyrgyz Republic is operationalized
planEntities.parentName: Green economic growth is accelerated through increased equitable entrepreneurship and employment opportunities, including through the sustainable use of natural resources.
planEntities.description:
Through the Programme for Country Partnership for the Kyrgyz Republic 2025–2029, UNIDO, in cooperation with the Cabinet of Ministers of the Kyrgyz Republic and national and international partners, will support the Government in advancing inclusive and sustainable industrial development. Anchored in a multi-stakeholder partnership led by the Cabinet of Ministers and key ministries and government institutions, the Programme for Country Partnership sets out a programmatic vision to accelerate sustainable industrial development and unlock investment potential.

The Programme delivers an integrated package of services that combines UNIDO’s advisory and normative functions, technical cooperation and convening role, thereby facilitating the mobilisation of partners and resources to achieve enhanced development impact. Building on strong national ownership, the Programme will support the Government in modernising selected priority industrial sectors, including agro-industrial processing, textiles and garments, construction materials, energy, the pharmaceutical industry and tourism. This support will focus on enhancing market access and strengthening integration into regional and global value chains.

planEntities.name: Improve quality of family planning services through capacity building of healthcare providers in rights-based family planning services and expanding adolescent and youth friendly health services, coupled with community engagement and schools and school health rooms to improve positive attitude and address social norms
planEntities.parentName: Universal Health Coverage is advanced through resilient people-centered health system.
planEntities.description:
Key focuses will be on equipping newly recruited healthcare providers with human-rights based family planning, reaching out the furthest left behind combined with the utilization of evidence from secondary data and  in-depth analyses in order to address bottlenecks, including harmful social norms, from both sides: supply side and and rights-holders . The interventions will be multi-pronged approaches: in-service and pre-services capacity building and the community and school engagement including the school health rooms. For the pre-service education,  the new curriculum for midwives as well as will be implemented and monitored and for the in-service capacity development, the focus will be on equipping human-rights based family planning to newly recruited healthcare providers and expanding of newly introduced method - Jadelle . The engagement with community, local authorities, schools, particularly the school health rooms, adolescent and youth aim to address misperceptions, myths, and perceived side-effects. 

In partnership with a CSO, the intervention will also reach out the furthest left behind populations such as FEWs and other populations (subject to other resources available); and
Ensure secured commodity supplies to the public sector. Engage with community-led distribution network to enhance reach and accessibility of family planning services for hard-to-reach populations and conduct supportive supervision.

planEntities.name: Improve quality and scale up maternal health services and life saving interventions [Emergency Obstetric and Newborn Care (EmONC), pre-service midwifery programme; Maternal and Perinatal Death Response and Surveillance]. Generate evidence and data to address critical sexual reproductive and maternal health bottlenecks including harmful social norms.
planEntities.parentName: Universal Health Coverage is advanced through resilient people-centered health system.
planEntities.description: In line with the global recommended health interventions to address preventable maternal death of 1) EmONC and MPDSR , 2) Skilled Birth Attendance/Midwifery Programme, and 3) Family Planning, and 4) social determinants and community engagement, the focus is on these three interventions to ensure quality maternal health services and life-saving interventions to women and the furthest left behind, coupled data and evidence of in-depth analyses to identify root causes of maternal deaths, including to address any harmful social norms. These interventions will be delivered along with Strategic Behavior Change and Communications (SBCC) through social media platforms and influencers. Maternal health interventions are parts of the Social Protection, Universal Health Coverage, and Primary Health Care.

planEntities.name: Develop capacity and scale up of health sector response to Gender-Based Violence (GBV)/Violence Against Women (VAW) as an integral intervention of the essential service package for GBV/VAW.
planEntities.parentName: Universal Health Coverage is advanced through resilient people-centered health system.
planEntities.description: The intervention will focus on the capacity development to healthcare providers to be women-centred approaches to enhance the quality of and to scale up the health sector response to GBV/VAW as a key sector of the multi-sectoral approaches in addressing GBV/VAW in Cambodia and to contribute to addressing harmful social norms toward women and girls. This health sector contribution is an integral part of the essential service packages for GBV/VAW under the Outcome 4 of the UNSDCF 2024 - 2028.

planEntities.name: Enhance positive attitude among healthcare providers to be human-centered approaches, and among service users towards utilization of sexual reproductive maternal health services and information including family planning throuugh evidenced-based Strategic Behavior Change Communication (SBCC) which will also contribute to addressing harmful social norms.
planEntities.parentName: Universal Health Coverage is advanced through resilient people-centered health system.
planEntities.description: The key communications objectives for long-term advocacy and strategic communications for strategic behavior change interventions relating to sexual reproductive health and rights, including maternal mortality and family planning are 1) To reduce unmet need for family planning among the furthest left behind focusing on “Women’s health seeking behavior in family planning”, 2) To raise awareness of harmful practices or risky behavior in birth preparedness, including transport, companion, family and community support, health facility readiness, as well as individual and family decisions, and 3) To improve providers’ positive behavior on youth and women-centred healthcare, and increase women’s healthcare seeking behaviors on the continuum of care, including SRHR, mental/emotional health and respectful SRHR services. Key communications interventions include social media campaigns, community outreach,  awareness raising through couples counselling, client satisfaction feedback, entertainment and knowledge products for women centered healthcare.

planEntities.name: Strengthen capacity to implement Health Education and Comprehensive Sexuality Education (CSE) to address SRH, gender equality, GBV, child marriage and other harmful social and gender norms
planEntities.parentName: Better quality and accessible education, skills development and life-long learning.
planEntities.description: Comprehensive Sexuality Education (CSE) is crucial for young people, empowering them with knowledge and skills to navigate their sexual and reproductive health responsibly. It shifts social norms by challenging taboos, promoting respect for diversity, and fostering open conversations. CSE promote gender equality and prevents gender-based violence and harassment by educating about consent and healthy relationships, while also promoting informed family planning decisions, strengthening HIV/STIs prevention, and addressing child early and forced marriage and teen pregnancy. By encouraging health-seeking behavior and providing accurate information, CSE empowers young people to make informed choices and decisions, leading to healthier relationships and a more equitable society.

planEntities.description: Adolescents and youth actively enhanced their knowledge and advocacy skills by leading policy dialogues and participating in programmes focused on SRHR, gender equality, and GBV prevention. Key interventions included: utilising digital platforms for sexuality education; delivering peer education in school & school health rooms; developing life skills education and leadership through national and community programmes (youth debate and youth volunteering, ... etc); accessing youth-friendly health services and safe spaces; engaging communities in supportive dialogues; challenging harmful gender norms; and leading advocacy campaigns for SRH/CSE, GBV prevention, and CEFM.

planEntities.description:
*Note: This is a joint programme with UNICEF, but I could not drop down the list for selection. Please support. 
UNICEF and UNFPA are implementing a joint programme to address CEFM in Cambodia, with support from the Government of Australia. The programme titled “Hidden in Plain Sight: UNICEF-UNFPA Joint Programme to End Child, Early and Forced Marriage in Southeast Asia (HIP)”, under the Towards Universal Sexual Reproductive Health and Rights in the Indo-Pacific (TUSIP), will be implemented 4 years from June 2024 to June 2028, and with three tiers of intervention: Policy and system level (Outcome 1); Individual and community level (Outcome 2); and Regional level (Outcome 3). Activities under Outcomes 1 and 2 will focus on three priority countries: Lao PDR, the Philippines and Cambodia, whereas Outcome 3 will be implemented at the regional level in Southeast Asia.

planEntities.name: Basic social services for women and children are climate resilient
planEntities.parentName: The adaptive capacity of systems & communities to climate change & disasters is strengthened.
planEntities.description:
as part of its climate strategy for children, UNICEF focus on ensuring that basic social services are:
1.	Resilient to the impacts of climate change and environmental degradation. This approach entails being guided by a climate and environment risk assessment to comprehend the hazards children face and their degree of vulnerability, utilizing sub-national CCRI analysis and sector-specific climate and environmental risk assessments. It also involves ensuring the continuity of social services, with minimal disruptions, even during extreme weather events.
2.	Low Environmental Footprint. This encompasses adopting suitable technologies and sustainable systems to minimize greenhouse gas emissions, advocate for the 3Rs (Reduce, Recycle, and Reuse), and mitigate exposure to environmental hazards.
3.	Transformative. This entails building upon national ownership and capacity while integrating into national systems to achieve scalability and sustainability.

planEntities.name: National immunization programme strengthened
planEntities.parentName: Universal Health Coverage is advanced through resilient people-centered health system.
planEntities.description:
Expected deliverables 2025:
•	Full implementation of the National Immunization Policy across all 25 provinces and 103 operational districts.
•	Maintenance of high routine immunization coverage, with implementation of the National Immunization Policy (NIP) following the National Guideline on Immunization in Practice and strengthening of the zero-dose strategy. Monitoring and support for the implementation of Gavi Health System Strengthening and Equity Accelerator Funding activities.
•	High-quality NIP surveillance maintained according to the National Guideline on Vaccine-Preventable Diseases (VPD) surveillance, with data analysis and regular monitoring of immunization, VPD surveillance, and Adverse Events Following Immunization (AEFI), including performance indicator monitoring at subnational levels.
•	Nationwide implementation of the evidence-based rotavirus vaccine introduction.
•	Comprehensive re-investigation of VPD cases, contact tracing, routine immunization coverage and surveillance assessment, and local vaccination responses supported.
•	Data analysis of measles outbreaks, close monitoring, technical advice, and coordination with the Ministry of Health (MOH), NIP, National Laboratory of Measles and Rubella, and subnational levels in surveillance implementation and outbreak response activities.
•	Support for the introduction of digital tools, including the development of an e-learning course for the immunization program and support for supportive supervision.
•	Support for program review and assessment, including NIP review, Effective Vaccine Management Assessment, coverage surveys, and DQA/RCA.
•	Regular monitoring of program activities across all areas.

planEntities.name: National HIV/AIDS programme is strengthened

•	Continuation of drug resistance monitoring for Gonorrhea, with analysis of results to guide treatment strategies.
•	Establishment and functioning of the eMTCT National Validation Committee to monitor progress.

planEntities.name: Accelerating the Implementation of the ASEAN Sustainable Urbanisation Strategy
planEntities.parentName: 2.6 Urban Development
planEntities.description:
The “Accelerating the Implementation of the ASEAN Sustainable Urbanisation Strategy (ASUS) – Phase II” aims to provide strategic and technical support to ASEAN cities in implementing ASUS, while supporting collection, documentation and dissemination of lessons learned at the local level to encourage other cities to adopt ASUS into their urban development plans. A key component of Phase II, strengthened from Phase I, is the element of capacity building for cities and national key actors, and expanding the outreach and engagement of local and regional stakeholders to promote sustainable urbanisation in ASEAN. 

The project is led by the Lead Implementing Body for the Master Plan on ASEAN Connectivity (MPAC) 2025 Strategic Area of Sustainable Infrastructure (LIB-SI) and the ASEAN Smart Cities Network (ASCN). The ASEAN Secretariat and the UN-Habitat Regional Office for Asia and the Pacific supports the implementation of the project’s activities and ensures a close collaboration between local, national, and regional stakeholders.

planEntities.name: EC - Strengthening Disaster Preparedness through the Establishment of Evacuation Centers - 01003142
planEntities.parentName: 4.2 Natural Resources Management
planEntities.description: The project's objective is to safeguard the lives of vulnerable communities impacted by seasonal flooding by ensuring access to safe evacuation centers and updating the National Evacuation Center guidelines based on practical feedback. The Lao People's Democratic Republic (Lao PDR) is significantly susceptible to flooding due to its geographical characteristics, with approximately 39.7% of the population exposed to flood risks, rendering it the sixth most flood-prone country in terms of population exposure. Ongoing financial constraints have impeded the government's capacity to respond to disasters, resulting in the isolation of remote communities during flood events, with women, children, the elderly, and individuals with disabilities being disproportionately affected. Prior to the crisis in 2022, the government had made advancements in disaster risk governance, which included the enactment of disaster management legislation and the adoption of the National Strategy on Disaster Risk Reduction for 2021-2030. Nonetheless, challenges such as inadequate funding, limited inter-agency coordination, and accessibility issues for non-governmental organizations continue to obstruct the effective implementation of policies. The project aims to enhance human security in flood-prone communities in the provinces of Khammouane, Saravane, and Champasack through inclusive designs that prioritize safety and privacy. Insights gained from this project will contribute to developing national guidelines, thereby improving their relevance and practicality. The Ministry of Labour and Social Welfare will collaborate with other ministries to ensure the effectiveness of the project implementation. In order to achieve the said outcomes, the project focuses on two main outputs: 1. Analysing risk knowledge and community needs to develop detailed implementation plans, & 2. Enhancing human security by establishing and sustainably operating 12 inclusive evacuation centers.

planEntities.parentName: 4.2 Natural Resources Management
planEntities.description: Brief Description The UNDP Climate Promise 2025 aims to support the UN system's coordinated efforts toward advancing NDC 3.0. The project's primary purpose is to assist the Government of Lao PDR in revising its NDC with a high level of ambition, integrating nature-climate linkages, gender inclusion, and other critical considerations. The main project goal is based on 3 pillars: 1.) Scale and Speed: Utilize the NDC as a gateway to deliver and monitor ambitious climate actions across sectors and thematic areas, enabling the achievement of bold targets outlined in the revised and enhanced NDCs. 2.) Amplifying Ambition: Link robust, integrated NDCs to long-term net-zero and climate-resilient pathways, as well as the next NDC cycle, to chart a path toward climate neutrality. 3.) Lasting Inclusivity: Systematically engage and empower key societal actors to accelerate NDC implementation and establish long-term net-zero and climate-resilient development pathways. The engagement facility will be implemented over 1.5 years, from January 2025 to June 2026.

planEntities.name: LEAP-UNDP-LAO-LAO PDR Efficiency and Accessibility of Public Services  - 01003550
planEntities.parentName: 3.5 Public Administration Reform and Data Driven Governance
planEntities.description: The LAO PDR Efficiency and Accessibility of Public Services (LEAP) Project aims to improve the efficiency, effectiveness, accessibility, and inclusivity of public services, ultimately improving the quality of service delivery and development outcomes for the public. The project is delivered in a context characterised by societal change, including rapid digital transformation, and various challenges, including macroeconomic instability and ongoing recovery from the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic. The overall aim of the project is to improve governance outcomes and people’s involvement and satisfaction with them. This will be done by partnering with the Ministry of Home Affairs to strengthen public service delivery, and with Lao PDR citizens and their organisations. The project will strengthen the One Door Service Centers (ODSCs), a modality of delivering different public services in one place at the local level, including supporting the standardization of operational procedures and the digital transformation of ODSC functions. ODSCs face sustainability challenges, such as closures and resource shortages, thus the project will also focus on supporting local authorities to improve ODSCs’ financial stability. Well-functioning local government is pivotal in ensuring effective and equitable service access, particularly in remote areas. However, ODSCs’ effectiveness is currently impacted by high regulatory burdens, excessive fees, and limited government capacity. Thus, the implementation of this strategy presents a key opportunity for modernizing, improving, and making more inclusive service delivery nationwide. Non-profit organisations have played a vital role in contributing to the development of the government’s public services agenda, promoting citizen participation, and helping improve clarity of national and local governance. The project will also work with some non-profit organizations in promoting improved and more equitable public service delivery.

planEntities.name: Strengthen gender-transformative education in Lao PDR: Gender-Transformative Education sector planning and programming and Capacity Building of Education Personnel
planEntities.parentName: 1.3 Education
planEntities.description:
GEM 3: Gender equality/women's empowerment is the principal objective
This sub-output aims to strengthen gender-transformative education in Lao PDR by addressing gender stereotypes, discriminatory practices and systemic barriers to gender equality through two key interventions:

(i) Mainstreaming Gender-responsive pedagogy (GRP) in teacher education institutions: Supporting the Ministry of Education and Sports (MoES) to institutionalize GRP in pre-service teacher education through curriculum integration, capacity development of teacher educators, institutional mentoring and promotion of gender-equitable, violence-free learning environments.
(ii) Evidence-informed sector planning: Strengthening the evidence base and institutional capacity for gender-responsive education planning through a sector-wide gender assessment, review of the 4th Five-Year Action Plan on Gender Equality and Mothers and Children Issues (2021–2025), and support for the development of the 5th Action Plan (2026–2030).
Gender-responsive monitoring
UNESCO monitors progress towards this sub-output through the following gender-responsive indicators. Participant data are disaggregated by sex and, where feasible, by ethnicity, disability and province. Monitoring also captures changes in gender-related attitudes and teaching practices, beyond participation alone:
(a) Number of teacher educators and master trainers trained in GRP, disaggregated by sex: 69 trained to date (39 female), comprising 50 (33 female) in 2024 and 19 (6 female) in 2026. In addition, 16 TEI leaders (3 female) received GRP orientation.
(b) Number of TEIs that have integrated GRP content into approved pre-service curricula: 3 of 16 TEIs are piloting the integration of GRP into five compulsory subjects.
(c) Number of TEIs with designated GRP mentors and focal points: All 16 TEIs have designated two GRP mentors and focal points each.
(d) Number of evidence informed the development and implementation of the 5th Five-Year Action Plan on Gender Equality and Mothers and Children in the Education, Science and Sports Sector (2026–2030): Two targeted outputs – a rapid gender assessment report and a review of the 4th Action Plan.
Data are collected through training attendance records, pre- and post-training surveys, classroom observations and TEI monitoring reports. UNESCO reviews the results with the DTE and the Division for the Advancement of Women, Mothers and Children to inform adjustments to training content and approaches, as well as to provide evidence for the development of the 5th Action Plan.

planEntities.description: WFP aims to reduce all forms of malnutrition among vulnerable groups in rural areas by providing universally accessible nutrition support services for targeted populations and nutrition-related technical assistance, advocacy and evidence-based advice to the Government and other stakeholders, including in the private sector. Activities under this strategic outcome will also serve the population overall through strengthened government capacity to design, implement and partner for multisectoral nutrition programmes that contribute to the achievement of national targets by 2026.

planEntities.name: 4.3.18 Vulnerable people in disaster-affected or at risk areas have enhanced food and nutrition security all year (WFP CSP SO 3)
planEntities.parentName: 4.3 Resilience
planEntities.description: Vulnerable people in disaster-affected or at-risk areas have enhanced food and nutrition security all year round and increased capacity to mitigate and manage risks associated with climate and other shocks by 2026. This will be achieved by improving community capacities in managing climate shocks and risks through i) access to climate /weather information; ii) use of climate resilient livelihoods practices; iii) climate resilient assets protecting the community against climate related shocks; iv) access to risk transfer transfer mechanisms and contingency funding. v) strengthening the capacity of local authorities and communities to prepare for, respond to and recover from disasters.

Supporting Lao PDR to provide affordable health care for all. This also means ensuring that the care provided is people-centred, of high-quality and efficient.

planEntities.name: People1.2.1 ESCWA: Support in finalizing and launching the national action plan to implement Lebanon's older persons' strategy 2020-2030
planEntities.parentName: People1.2: Local and national capacities and frameworks for social protection are enhanced
planEntities.description: Following its technical support in developing Lebanon’s National Strategy for Older Persons (2020–2030), ESCWA provided advisory services to finalize and launch the accompanying national action plan. After extensive national consultations, the plan was finalized in late 2024 based on inputs from the Ministry of Social Affairs. At the Minister’s request, ESCWA supported the plan’s refinement and official launch, which took place on 30 January 2025. The launch marked a significant step toward mobilizing resources and operationalizing the strategy, aimed at advancing the rights and well-being of older persons in Lebanon.

planEntities.name: Peace and Gov1.1.3 ESCWA: Advisory and technical support for deploying the ESCWA Monitoring Application for Reporting on the SDGs (MARS) in Lebanon
planEntities.parentName: Peace and Gov1.1: Capacities to promote accountability, transparency, and effectiveness of public institutions are strengthened at the national and local levels
planEntities.description: In 2025, ESCWA provided advisory and technical support to initiate the deployment of the Monitoring Application for Reporting on the SDGs (MARS) in Lebanon. Preparatory meetings were held to lay the groundwork for establishing the national network of data providers. A key coordination meeting took place on 20 May 2025 to present the requirements and structure for the national MARS setup, with participation from relevant stakeholders. The process of setting up the system is underway, with national engagement progressing through ESCWA’s continued support.

planEntities.name: Project 1.2.1.4.1 Developing Juvenile justice in Libya II
planEntities.parentName: Non-discriminatory, enforceable, harmonized, and monitorable legal and policy frameworks are developed by legitimate authorities to promote rule of law in Libya in line with international human rights norms and standards.
planEntities.description:
Guided by the principles of the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child (CRC) and other relevant international and national legal frameworks, the Project builds on the achievements and lessons learned from the first Phase of this joint project “developing juvenile justice in Libya”.Building on the accomplishments of Phase I and informed by the recommendations and lessons learned identified during its final evaluation, Phase II of the project is designed to address emerging needs and leverage strategic opportunities for greater impact. This phase aims to support Libyan authorities in aligning the national legal framework with international laws, norms, and standards, while strengthening the juvenile justice system to ensure a more effective, child-centered approach.

Key priorities for Phase II include the institutionalization of child-friendly legal aid, the implementation of alternatives to detention, and the enhancement of detention conditions to better meet international standards. The project will also focus on raising awareness about children’s rights through targeted campaigns, establishing specialized procedures, and improving institutional capacities. Phase II seeks to contribute to a more peaceful, secure, and equitable society in Libya by fostering a rehabilitative and rights-based juvenile justice system.

Phase II effort directly supports the United Nations Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (UNSDCF) Outcome 1.2: “By 2025, people in Libya participate in and benefit from a more peaceful, safe, and secure society, free from armed conflict and underpinned by unified and strengthened security, justice, rule of law, and human rights institutions.” Through this initiative, the project seeks to foster a more inclusive and protective environment for children in Libya, ensuring their rights are safeguarded and their development is nurtured.

planEntities.parentName: Government institutions and social partners have improved capacities to formulate, implement, and monitor inclusive and comprehensive national and sectoral policies and strategies for promoting decent work.
planEntities.description: The project focuses on upgrading research infrastructure by procuring and installing modern laboratory equipment to strengthen biotechnology research, while ensuring the regular maintenance of instruments to support sustainable, long-term scientific activities. It will also prioritize training and capacity building through both long-term and short-term programs. The long-term training will include support for postgraduate studies, international research exchanges, and partnerships with leading global institutions. The short-term training will involve organizing workshops, seminars, and hands-on sessions for students, technicians, and researchers to enhance practical skills and technical expertise. In addition, the project will encourage innovation and research excellence by promoting collaboration among universities, industry, and research institutions to advance scientific discovery and practical applications, while supporting research projects that contribute to Libya’s socio-economic development.

planEntities.name: Technical Support to Libya in the Monitoring and Maintenance of Dams
planEntities.parentName: Government institutions and other stakeholders are better able to sustainably manage water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) systems, and provide equitable access to safe, climate resilient, sustainable WASH and waste management services, including for productive needs.
planEntities.description: The project aims to assess the post-disaster condition of the Derna and Mansour dams and develop the failure modes scenarios, while strengthening national capacity in the monitoring and maintenance of resilient dams. It will include a comprehensive vulnerability assessment of Libyan dams, the development of maintenance standards and criteria, and the conduct of flood risk analysis and mapping. The project will develop a national flood risk management strategy and action plan. It will also establish a national flood Early Warning Modelling and simulation in anticipation for future flash floods to improve preparedness and response to high-intensity rainfall events. In addition, it will support training for journalists and media professionals on flood early warning and disaster risk reduction reporting, alongside the production of awareness-raising materials, including videos in local languages, to promote risk prevention and reduction measures.

planEntities.name: Project 1.2.1.4.1 Developing Juvenile justice in Libya II
planEntities.parentName: Non-discriminatory, enforceable, harmonized, and monitorable legal and policy frameworks are developed by legitimate authorities to promote rule of law in Libya in line with international human rights norms and standards.
planEntities.description:
Guided by the principles of the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child (CRC) and other relevant international and national legal frameworks, the Project builds on the achievements and lessons learned from the first Phase of this joint project “developing juvenile justice in Libya”.Building on the accomplishments of Phase I and informed by the recommendations and lessons learned identified during its final evaluation, Phase II of the project is designed to address emerging needs and leverage strategic opportunities for greater impact. This phase aims to support Libyan authorities in aligning the national legal framework with international laws, norms, and standards, while strengthening the juvenile justice system to ensure a more effective, child-centered approach.

Key priorities for Phase II include the institutionalization of child-friendly legal aid, the implementation of alternatives to detention, and the enhancement of detention conditions to better meet international standards. The project will also focus on raising awareness about children’s rights through targeted campaigns, establishing specialized procedures, and improving institutional capacities. Phase II seeks to contribute to a more peaceful, secure, and equitable society in Libya by fostering a rehabilitative and rights-based juvenile justice system.

Phase II effort directly supports the United Nations Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (UNSDCF) Outcome 1.2: “By 2025, people in Libya participate in and benefit from a more peaceful, safe, and secure society, free from armed conflict and underpinned by unified and strengthened security, justice, rule of law, and human rights institutions.” Through this initiative, the project seeks to foster a more inclusive and protective environment for children in Libya, ensuring their rights are safeguarded and their development is nurtured.

planEntities.name: Enhancing Maritime Safety and Security in Libya
planEntities.parentName: Security sector institutions, operating under civilian oversight, are more unified, resourced, capable, and functional, including professional, unified, and accountable defence and security forces.
planEntities.description:
UNODC GMCP project aims at strengthening Libya maritime institutions capacities and capabilities to enhance the delivery of maritime operations, having a robust accountability mechanism in place, promoting cooperation and coordination -interoperability- to bridge existing gaps between the Libyan maritime authorities in the West and East. A particular focus will be placed on aligning the incoming subnational coordination centre in Benghazi (sub-MRCC) with the established structures in Tripoli (MRCC). 
The proposed project (two-year) is centred on three objectives: 
1.          Through the deployment of full-time subject matter experts -Arabic speakers- institutionalize the use of SOPs developed by UNODC for Libya I both Tripoli and Benghazi sub-centre.
2.          Through practical trainings courses and exercises, promote maritime inter-agency cooperation across and among East and West Libya.
3.          Produce a needs assessment and later procure critical equipment to ensure safe and secure operations at sea.
A unified approach to MLE and SAR operations will ensure that a rescue operation off the coast of Tobruk in the far East is managed with the same procedures and standards as one off Tripoli in the West, improving operational effectiveness, strengthening rule of law at sea, and ensuring that all Libyan maritime operations meet international standards for safety, accountability, and respect for human rights. By harmonizing protocols and training, the project seeks to eliminate miscommunication and procedural incompatibilities, laying a foundation for eventual integration of Command & Control structures. 
All activities will strengthen Libya’s capacity to manage its maritime domain more effectively and in line with international standards, in close partnership with UK counterparts where appropriate.

planEntities.description:
Presently the capacity of DFC for assessment and designing measures for sustainable
management and value addition of NTFP to benefit local livelihoods and their food security remains
limited. In the above context, the project aims to support the DFC to build the national capacity to ensure
sustainable management, value addition and use of NTFP, that in turn will enhance the contribution of
NTFP to the livelihoods and food security of the rural people. Specific objectives are to: (i) improve
knowledge and skills of NWFP users on sustainable extraction and resource assessments (ii) prepare
assessment reports focusing on selected NTFP that will include both economically and nutritionally
viable species (iii) design and pilot a selected NTFP resource improvement program and (iv) design and apply conservation measures for selected threatened NTFP species. A proposal for resource mobilization
will also be prepared to conserve and sustainably use NTFP.

planEntities.name: Support to promoting investment in agri-food system transformation in Sri Lanka under the framework of Hand-in-Hand Initiative
planEntities.parentName: The government in partnership with the private sector, trade unions/producers’ organizations, women, youth, and other stakeholders demonstrate strengthened capacity and commitment to implement transformational economic strategies that support sustainable, green and gender-responsive economic recovery, growth and decent work.
planEntities.description:
The Hand-in-Hand Initiative (HIH), launched in 2019 by the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO), is a targeted intervention aimed at supporting the transformation of agri-food systems, food security, and rural development in countries facing significant challenges. It can provide solutions to a lower-middle-income country like Sri Lanka that seeks to mobilize resources available most-efficiently. 
The HIH is designed to address poverty reduction and is intrinsically linked to agri-food investment in several ways: 
•	Territorial approach: By identifying specific geographic and sectoral areas where the impact can be maximized, the initiative helps direct investments to where they are most needed. 
•	Enhancing Productivity: Investments under this initiative aim to modernize agriculture through technology and innovation, thus enhancing productivity and sustainability. 
•	Market Access: Improving infrastructure and logistics to provide farmers better access to markets is a key component, thus increasing their potential revenue and investment returns. 
•	Capacity Building: The initiative invests in training and equipping local communities and governments to manage agricultural projects effectively, ensuring long-term sustainability.

planEntities.name: Strengthening Risk-based Approaches to Border Security in Sri Lanka
planEntities.parentName: Governance and State institutions, systems and mechanisms at all levels demonstrate strengthened commitment to people-centric, independent, inclusive and transparent democratic governance and administration.
planEntities.description:
Since 2016, the International Organization for Migration (IOM) has been supporting the Government of Sri Lanka (GoSL) to transition to a risk-based, intelligence-driven, well-coordinated approach to border management under an Integrated Border Management (IBM) model.  This project aims to consolidate these efforts by strengthening application of risk-based approaches to border security, thereby improving the capacities to facilitate legitimate travel and trade through Sri Lanka’s borders and mitigate vulnerabilities to transnational organized crime.  Towards this end, the project is structured around four critical components: improving risk-assessment capacities of the Sri Lanka border control authorities, enhancing screening of passengers and passenger goods at points of entry (PoE), improving border data management and analysis, and strengthening inter-agency coordination mechanisms through the Sri Lanka Border Risk Assessment Centre (BRAC).   
The project aims to enhance Sri Lanka Customs' capacity to screen passengers, goods, and courier packages in line with the Customs Ordinance[2]  by assessing current screening technologies at points of entry, identifying critical gaps, and procuring necessary screening equipment. Technical support to BRAC will focus on refining their data schema and revising system workflows with a view to enhancing data accuracy, process-efficiency, and monitoring, evaluating and reporting capabilities. To complement these efforts, a capacity building program will be implemented to strengthen the application of risk assessment principles within Sri Lanka Customs and BRAC and improve coordination among relevant risk management divisions. Collectively, these interventions aim to foster a culture of risk-based, coordinated approach to border security.
The capacity building programmes under the project will integrate human rights, diversity and gender considerations in the context of immigration and border governance in line with IOM values.
The anticipated outputs—enhanced screening capabilities at PoE, improved risk assessment capacities, and refined border data management practices—are expected to substantially contribute to the project's broader outcome of strengthened border security and the facilitation of legitimate travel and trade.

Funding partner: United States - Bureau of International Security and Nonproliferation.

The UNDP Climate Finance Network (CFN) programme is a 7-year project supported by FCDO active in 14 countries across the Asia-Pacific Region.  

Asia and Pacific countries are amongst the most vulnerable to climate change. The impacts of climate change are increasingly disrupting national economies and affecting livelihoods, water, energy, transportation, agriculture and ecosystems at an unprecedented scale. It is usually the poorest and the most vulnerable who are most at risk of the storms, floods, droughts, wildfires and rising sea levels, while lacking protections and resources to adapt. At the same time, here is growing recognition that affordable, scalable solutions are possible both for mitigation of greenhouse gas emissions and adaptation – and that these solutions can enable all of us to leapfrog to cleaner, more resilient economies. However, these call for policy and financing shifts away from business as usual to actively factor in climate change as well as ensure co-benefits and a focus on the needs of the most vulnerable.   

Over the past five years there has been an increase in the interest and capacity of Ministries of Finance, who are the main programme counterparts, to respond to climate change as well as take more integrated approaches to addressing and financing the social, environmental and economic objectives of the 2030 Agenda and take forward commitments under the Paris Agreement. This area of work is likely to acquire even further importance in light of the Sixth Assessment Report (AR6) of the IPCC and the momentum that has built on the in the wake of COVID-19 to recover forward better. The DFID-supported Climate Proofing Growth and Development (CPGD) programme (2013-2019) and the Government of Sweden supported Strengthening the Governance of Climate Change Finance to Enhance Gender Equality (GCCF) programmes (2017-22; previous phase 2012-16) have hitherto sought to respond to this demand by providing technical support for policy and technical policy reforms and interventions across the budget cycle ; as well as supporting the a promotion of sharing of knowledge and innovative ways to tap into expertise and offer peer-to-peer technical assistance across the region.  

Based on the success of the CPGD and GCCF programmes, a Climate Finance Network (CFN) is being proposed. It will serve as a peer-to-peer network and as a knowledge management and technical support facility to support Ministries of Finance with the engagement of sector ministries and sub-national governments to identify and scale up climate finance innovations in the region. planEntities.parentName: The private sector, other non-state actors and the people in Sri Lanka have improved knowledge and capacities to demand for, adopt and use environmentally friendly, gender-responsive and climate-smart environmental protection, natural resource management, and sustainable consumption and production practices.
planEntities.description:
The objective of this global project is to fast-track readiness and early actions to implement the post-2020 Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF) by providing financial and technical support to GEF-eligible Parties to the United Nations Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD) in their work to align their National Biodiversity Strategies and Action Plans (NBSAPs) including national biodiversity targets, monitoring, policy, and finance frameworks with the Global Biodiversity Framework of the CBD. Financial and technical support is provided through two pathways: first, grants made to Parties to undertake early actions at the national level, and second, a global technical support grant that will make it possible to provide technical guidance to Parties to ensure these early actions are effective, efficient, inclusive, and of the highest technical standards.

Each of the participating countries, based on their current planning status, will use the grant to undertake 
activities from the following menu: 
a) Rapid review of NBSAP for alignment with the post-2020 GBF; 
b) assessment of monitoring systems; c) policy and institutional alignment and review of policies for coherence with the GBF; and 
d) biodiversity finance activities. The rapid review of the NBSAP and national targets will focus 
on identifying gaps required to align the national targets, goals, objectives and action plans within the existing NBSAP to the new GBF; the assessment of monitoring systems will focus on identifying gaps and promoting alignment between the NBSAP-related monitoring system and the GBF; the policy and institutional review will focus on identifying policy gaps and inconsistencies within the existing NBSAP and the GBF; and the biodiversity finance activities will focus on preparedness for developing and/or implementing a finance plan for implementing a GBF-aligned NBSAP.

planEntities.name: Development of the First Biennial Transparency Report, the Second Biennial Transparency  Report and Fourth National Communication of Sri Lanka to UNFCCC (Sri Lanka: BTR1+ BTR2/NC4) (1000404)
planEntities.parentName: The government, non-state institutions and the people in Sri Lanka, particularly the most vulnerable, have strengthened resilience and improved capacities to anticipate, adapt, respond to and recover better from crises including climate-related shocks, food insecurity, epidemics, and natural hazards.
planEntities.description:
The Project objective is to strengthen technical and institutional capacity to assist Sri Lanka to fulfill the 
climate change reporting commitments under the UNFCCC and Paris Agreement. As such, the Project 
will enable Sri Lanka to prepare and submit its First Biennial Transparency Report (BTR1), the Second 
Biennial Transparency Report (BTR2) and Fourth National Communication (NC4). The Project will build 
on the findings and recommendations of previous NCs, Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs).

Project is continuing till 05 Aug 2028.

planEntities.name: Management of Plastics Waste and Circular Interventions on Plastics in South, Southeast Asia, and the Pacific (Sri Lanka Component) (1003436)
planEntities.parentName: The private sector, other non-state actors and the people in Sri Lanka have improved knowledge and capacities to demand for, adopt and use environmentally friendly, gender-responsive and climate-smart environmental protection, natural resource management, and sustainable consumption and production practices.
planEntities.description:
The TCCF Plastics Circularity Project aims to address the critical issue of plastic waste 
management in nine countries across Asia. This initiative targets countries with varying levels of 
waste management infrastructure and plastic waste challenges, including India, Bangladesh, 
Bhutan, Nepal, Maldives, Sri Lanka, Philippines, Cambodia, and Vietnam. The project is designed 
to support the transition to a circular economy by improving plastic waste management, promoting 
recycling, and reducing plastic leakage into the environment. By focusing on these targeted areas, 
the project will contribute to better public health, environmental protection, and the development 
of sustainable waste management practices. The project is expected to contribute to collect at 
least 55,610 tons of plastics and support 72,100 direct beneficiaries during the implementation 
period across all nine participating countries. There are four components under the Project, 
namely:

1. Stakeholder Engagement and Strategy Development.
2. Implementation of Best Environmental Practices (BEP) and Best Available Technologies (BAT).
3. Strengthening National Capacities and Guidelines
4. Information Outreach and Knowledge Management.

Sri Lanka project interventions will reduce plastic pollution and mitigates aggravation of disaster impacts (i.e., intensified floods in urban areas due to clogging of drainage systems), as well as reducing threats to environment such as biodiversity, especially fauna, contamination of environment with microplastics etc. By developing and implementing gender-sensitive, pro-poor strategies for plastic waste management, the project ensures that vulnerable communities benefit from strengthened livelihoods and increased incomes. The dissemination of lessons learned and best practices across all local authorities in Sri Lanka further supports sustainable natural 
resource management and biodiversity conservation.

planEntities.name: Enabling Implementation of Climate and Environmental Commitments of Sri Lanka (01003546)
planEntities.parentName: The government demonstrates improved commitment to gender-responsive and climate-smart environmental protection, natural resource management, and sustainable consumption and production practices.
planEntities.description:
Sri Lanka, a biodiversity hotspot in the Indian Ocean, faces increasing environmental challenges due to climate change, biodiversity loss, and land degradation. As a signatory to international agreements like the Paris Agreement, the Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD), and the United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification (UNCCD), Sri Lanka has committed to a path of sustainable development and environmental conservation. 
The overall objective of this Initiation Plan (IP) is to support the Government of Sri Lanka to update and enhance their environmental commitments under these conventions. This IP will cover the following specific interventions:
•	Output 1: NDC 3.0 is updated through an inclusive and participatory process 
•	Output 2: Preparatory elements to enable the implementation of Loss & Damage (L&D) in Sri Lanka
•	Output 3: LDN TSP 2.0 is revised through a participatory and stakeholder-driven process

planEntities.name: Promoting Participation Pathways for Human Development (01003844)
planEntities.parentName: Governance and State institutions, systems and mechanisms at all levels demonstrate strengthened commitment to people-centric, independent, inclusive and transparent democratic governance and administration.
planEntities.description:
This project in Sri Lanka builds on ongoing efforts within the Sri Lankan Parliament and lessons from UNDP’s recently concluded initiative on strengthening local government capacities for inclusive development. It emphasizes creating stronger connections between national and sub-national engagement spaces to foster inclusive, participatory governance. Key interventions include strengthening public engagement in parliamentary oversight committees, optimizing the Parliament's Public Outreach and Media Departments, and developing tools and strategies for citizen participation in legislative impact assessment processes, both pre- and post-enactment.

The project will enhance the capacity of the Right to Information Commission, promoting public oversight, awareness, and access to parliamentary oversight functions. A critical component is the development of an online citizen engagement platform to enable dialogue between Parliament and the public, fostering participatory policymaking. Additionally, the initiative supports the creation of a civil society network, including the revival of Youth Peace and Security Coalitions, to advance dialogue on the regulatory framework for civic engagement. It will also develop mentorship initiatives and a comprehensive network of young and seasoned women leaders, creating an enabling environment for women aspiring to enter politics through skills development and resource support.

Globally, the initiative is designed to go beyond country-specific results by promoting cross-country knowledge exchange and collaboration, distilling national insights into global knowledge products, and leveraging interventions into global partnerships. Through the 3P4D initiative, the project will generate evidence on effective strategies for nurturing civic space, offering insights into technically sound and politically viable approaches. These lessons will be positioned and showcased to regional and global audiences, contributing to knowledge generation and advancing civic engagement as a strategic global objective.

planEntities.name: Support toward Selected Anti-Corruption Initiatives (01003869)
planEntities.parentName: Governance and State institutions, systems and mechanisms at all levels demonstrate strengthened commitment to people-centric, independent, inclusive and transparent democratic governance and administration.
planEntities.description:
The project aims to enhance Sri Lanka's anti-corruption mechanisms through three strategic interventions. First, the development of an E-Asset Declaration System will transition the existing manual system to a digital platform, ensuring greater transparency, accessibility, and efficiency in compliance with the Right to Information Act (2016) and the Personal Data Protection Act (2022). This system will modernize asset declarations, making them more effective in detecting conflicts of interest and illicit wealth accumulation.

Moreover, a knowledge exchange visit to the Independent Commission Against Corruption (ICAC) in Hong Kong will provide CIABOC prosecutors and investigators with exposure to international best practices in corruption prevention, investigation, and prosecution. This initiative aims to strengthen institutional capacities by integrating successful strategies from ICAC into Sri Lanka’s anti-corruption framework.

Lastly, the project will conduct a Corruption Risk Assessment in Revenue Institutions, focusing on the Inland Revenue Department (IRD) and the Excise Department. This assessment will identify corruption vulnerabilities and recommend mitigation strategies to strengthen governance and institutional integrity in these key revenue-generating bodies.

Sri Lanka’s new anti-corruption law (2023) mandates the modernization of asset declaration processes and strengthens CIABOC's role in investigating and preventing corruption. The project directly supports these legal requirements while addressing persistent challenges such as inefficiencies in the manual asset declaration system and corruption risks within revenue institutions. Additionally, the knowledge exchange with ICAC ensures that CIABOC aligns its investigative and preventive approaches with international best practices.

The project will be implemented through a phased approach. The E-Asset Declaration System is expected to be developed by January 2025, with regulatory guidelines and user training incorporated into the rollout. The ICAC Knowledge Exchange Visit is scheduled for August 2025, focusing on hands-on training and strategic learning. The Corruption Risk Assessment and Mitigation Plans for revenue institutions will be conducted between January and March 2026, leading to the development of targeted action plans for corruption risk management.

By implementing these strategic interventions, UNDP aims to strengthen Sri Lanka’s anti-corruption framework, enhance transparency, and improve governance in revenue administration and public sector accountability.

planEntities.name: support the Data, statistics and knowledge for peaceful, just and inclusive societies: strengthening the measuring and monitoring of SDG 16 in conflict and fragility affected countries Flagship Initiative in Sri Lanka (1003929)
planEntities.parentName: Government demonstrates strengthened capacities to plan, resource, deliver and monitor, evidence-led, SDG-driven sustainable national and sub-national development which is responsive to people’s needs in an inclusive, agile, transparent and accountable manner.

planEntities.name: Support Security 4 Peace Global Flagship In Sri Lanka (1004215)
planEntities.parentName: Justice sector institutions and stakeholders have enhanced capacity and demonstrate commitment to ensure equal access to affordable, non-discriminatory justice and rule of law in a transparent and accountable manner.
planEntities.description: The "Security 4 Peace Global Flagship" funding window support in this second round aims to deliver safety and security for people in crisis and fragile contexts, addressing urgent needs in countries like Libya, Ethiopia, Mauritania, Burundi, Sri Lanka and Pakistan. This initiative focuses on human rights and business and human rights for prevention and risk anticipation/management, including dealing with past human rights violations and transitional justice and addressing new violations and conflicts, as well as enhancing justice and security systems and fostering community resilience. Delivered through the Global Programme for the Rule of Law, Security and Human Rights, this support strengthens national and local capacities, enables development approaches in fragile settings and enables people-centred approaches. It seeks to build inclusive, effective institutions that respond to the human rights and security and justice needs of all, particularly those most impacted by the crises and left behind. The funding window aligns with global development priorities, including SDG 16 (Peace, Justice, and Strong Institutions) and SDG 5 (Gender Equality), aiming to create stable environments where communities can thrive.

planEntities.name: Kigali Implementation Plan - Stage I (1006010)
planEntities.parentName: The government, non-state institutions and the people in Sri Lanka, particularly the most vulnerable, have strengthened resilience and improved capacities to anticipate, adapt, respond to and recover better from crises including climate-related shocks, food insecurity, epidemics, and natural hazards.
planEntities.description:
Sri Lanka, as a Party to the Montreal Protocol and all its amendments including the Kigali Amendment (2018), is committed to reducing the consumption of hydrofluorocarbons (HFCs), which are potent greenhouse gases used primarily in refrigeration and air-conditioning equipment. Under the Kigali Amendment, Sri Lanka is required to freeze HFC consumption at its baseline level and progressively reduce consumption by 80 per cent by 2045.

To support compliance with these obligations, Sri Lanka developed Stage I of its Kigali Implementation Plan (KIP) for the period 2025–2029. The plan aims to achieve a 10 per cent reduction in HFC consumption from the national baseline by 2029, equivalent to phasing down 117,023 tonnes of CO₂ equivalent HFCs. Key interventions focus on promoting low-global-warming-potential (GWP) alternatives in the refrigeration and air-conditioning (RAC) sector, strengthening policy and regulatory frameworks, enhancing technical capacity, and ensuring the safe adoption of alternative technologies while maintaining energy efficiency.

On behalf of the Government of Sri Lanka, the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP), as the lead implementing agency, submitted the Stage I KIP proposal to the 96th Meeting of the Executive Committee of the Multilateral Fund (MLF) held in Montreal from 26–30 May 2025. The Executive Committee approved, in principle, Stage I of the KIP for Sri Lanka with total funding of US$455,677, comprising US$325,307 for UNDP (including agency support costs) and US$130,370 for UNEP (including agency support costs), under Decision 96/45.
