planEntities.name: Scale-up and Sustain the Low Carbon Municipal Solid Waste Management (1004813)
planEntities.parentName: The government demonstrates improved commitment to gender-responsive and climate-smart environmental protection, natural resource management, and sustainable consumption and production practices.
planEntities.description:
Improving Municipal Solid Waste Management (MSWM) is a priority to achieve inclusive sustainable 
development in Sri Lanka. This project presents an opportunity to consolidate past efforts, scale up proven 
practices, and introduce sustainable, system-wide approaches that go beyond isolated interventions, 
ensuring long-term environmental, social, and economic benefits. The project interventions introduce 
integrated MSWM solutions that address the entire chain from waste generation to final disposal. 
The objectives of this project are to: 
1. Review, strengthen and develop inclusive policy, regulatory, institutional, and green financing 
frameworks on municipal solid waste management (MSWM) at provincial and local levels. 
2. Demonstrate viable, sustainable Public Private Partnership (PPP) options for total MSWM 
solutions and a system for GHG emission reduction management in the selected Local Authorities 
(LAs). 
3. Gather and share knowledge, support training, replication, and scalability of project results, and 
manage, monitor, and evaluate the project performance including GHG emission reduction.

planEntities.name: Project for Promoting Prosecution of Corrupt Practices through the Establishment of Anti-corruption Mechanism
planEntities.parentName: Justice sector institutions and stakeholders have enhanced capacity and demonstrate commitment to ensure equal access to affordable, non-discriminatory justice and rule of law in a transparent and accountable manner.
planEntities.description:
The overall objective of this Project is to ensure the effective implementation of the activities proposed in the National Anti-Corruption Action Plan 2025-2029 (NACAP), which will contribute to a more transparent, accountable, and resilient society, ultimately leading to a significant reduction in corruption and an enhancement of public trust in institutions. The project seeks to support the whole of-society approach adopted in the NACAP to respond to corruption engendered barriers which hinder progress and development. Through targeted interventions, the project seeks to support the dismantling of these barriers, facilitating positive change and empowering communities to thrive. 

 Accordingly, the project has three (3) Specific Objectives or Outcomes in the broad areas of prevention, institutional strengthening, and community engagement which broadly correspond to the pillars of intervention identified in the NACAP and seven (07) Output level results contributing to the three specific objectives. The specific objectives are as follows:

Objective 1: Effective and Institutionalized preventive mechanisms in the public sector promote transparency, accountability, and integrity in governance and business practices.  

Objective 2: Strengthened institutions have enhanced investigative processes, improved coordination with stakeholders, and ensured quality of prosecutions. 

Objective 3: Empowered citizens enhance social accountability and effectively mobilize against corruption.  


Project end date - 30 June 2028.

planEntities.name: Ditwah: Early Recovery Support for people impacted by Cyclone Ditwah (01005285)
planEntities.parentName: The government, non-state institutions and the people in Sri Lanka, particularly the most vulnerable, have strengthened resilience and improved capacities to anticipate, adapt, respond to and recover better from crises including climate-related shocks, food insecurity, epidemics, and natural hazards.
planEntities.description:
Cyclone Ditwah has rapidly evolved into one of Sri Lanka’s most devastating flood disasters in two decades, 
with new information revealing a deepening humanitarian and early recovery crisis. Since making landfall on 
28 November, the cyclone has affected over one million people (455,405 families) across all 25 districts, with 
639 lives lost and 203 still missing. Over 180,000 people remain displaced in 1,094 government-run safety 
centres, while access to affected communities continues to be disrupted by persistent flooding. The heaviest 
impacts are concentrated in Gampaha, Colombo, Puttalam, Mannar, Trincomalee and Batticaloa, with severe 
landslides in Kandy, Badulla and Matale causing extensive loss of life and long-term livelihood damage. More 
than 15,000 homes have been destroyed, and widespread damage to roads, bridges, rail lines, and power 
infrastructure, including a flooded substation, continues to hinder mobility, communications, and relief 
operations—particularly around the Kelani River basin. 
 
The project is to support early recovery sector related activities in support of national partner capacity 
strengthening, cash for work and other mechanisms to build back better. UNDP’s key interventions in this 
sector include Debris management, Livelihoods recovery, Community Infrastructure Rehabilitation, 
Community Security, Restoring Local Governance Functions, Advancing Gender Equality, Energy Services 
in Crisis, and Health Services in Crisis.

planEntities.name: Promoting sustainable economic benefits through the conservation of critical biodiversity and ecosystem services in the Eastern and Southern Coastal Regions of Sri Lanka - (1003617)
planEntities.parentName: The government, non-state institutions and the people in Sri Lanka, particularly the most vulnerable, have strengthened resilience and improved capacities to anticipate, adapt, respond to and recover better from crises including climate-related shocks, food insecurity, epidemics, and natural hazards.
planEntities.description:
The project aims to address the current and future development pressures on the biologically rich terrestrial, coastal, and marine ecosystems in the Southern and Eastern regions of Sri Lanka. Emerging economic pathways are expected to accelerate habitat encroachment, promote destructive harvesting practices, increase pollution and invasive species proliferation, and exacerbate the impacts of climate change. These pressures threaten critical ecosystem services that support livelihoods, biodiversity, and disaster resilience.

To address these challenges, the project adopts a holistic, multi-disciplinary, and multi-sectoral approach that integrates biodiversity conservation with sustainable development. It will promote an integrated and coordinated framework for planning and managing ecosystems, engaging all sectors and local communities that impact or depend on these ecosystems. The intervention pathways include strengthening governance, policies, and institutional capacities for integrated landscape and seascape management, fostering financing and incentives for nature-positive practices, and demonstrating ecosystem-based management and nature-based solutions with potential for replication and scaling.

The project is structured around five interlinked components:

1: Enabling framework for safeguarding biodiversity, combating coastal and marine degradation, and securing a nature-based economic pathway.

2: Improved financing and incentives for nature-based solutions in the Eastern coastal and marine regions.

3: Piloting ecosystem and nature-based solutions to enhance environmental and economic benefits in selected coastal landscapes and seascapes.

4: Awareness raising, knowledge management, and gender mainstreaming to promote replication and scale-up of integrated approaches to resource management.

5: Monitoring and Evaluation.
Through these interventions, the project aims to strengthen ecosystem resilience, mitigate environmental threats, and promote sustainable economic pathways while ensuring inclusivity and long-term sustainability.

- Total Project Budget - USD 4,507,534.00
- Expected project end date: 31 Jan 2032.

planEntities.name: Inclusive Climate-Smart Dairy Value Chains: Accelerating Renewable Energy Adoption, Nature-Based Solutions, and Smallholder Resilience (1005671)
planEntities.parentName: The government, non-state institutions and the people in Sri Lanka, particularly the most vulnerable, have strengthened resilience and improved capacities to anticipate, adapt, respond to and recover better from crises including climate-related shocks, food insecurity, epidemics, and natural hazards.
planEntities.description:
Sri Lanka’s dairy sector is at a critical juncture, facing cascading climate shocks, economic hardship, and deepening rural inequality—challenges that disproportionately affect women, youth, and marginalized estate communities. Rural poverty has more than doubled since 2019, and women—who make up a significant share of the agricultural workforce—are especially vulnerable due to limited access to resources, technology, and decision-making platforms. In climate-vulnerable districts like Kilinochchi and Nuwara Eliya, smallholder dairy farmers, including women-headed households and aspiring youth agri-entrepreneurs, struggle with declining productivity, input shortages, and nutrition insecurity. The destabilization of the dairy sector threatens household food security, 
particularly for children and women in estate areas where dairy is often the only accessible protein source.

This intervention builds on and represents a continuation of earlier phases under the Climate Promise, as well as UNDP’s ongoing portfolio on renewable energy, climate-resilient agriculture, and just transition pathways. It draws on established models and lessons from prior initiatives that have focused on strengthening energy security, promoting renewable energy-based green technologies, and integrating smallholder farmers into resilient agricultural value chains particularly in vulnerable districts such as Kilinochchi and Nuwara Eliya. By scaling and deepening these proven approaches, the project is positioned within a broader, programmatic framework that 
supports Sri Lanka’s NDC implementation and long-term net-zero ambitions. As such, the Climate-Smart Dairy intervention is not a standalone effort but part of a coherent continuum of support, reinforcing inclusive, gender-responsive, and climate-resilient agricultural transformation while contributing to a just transition for rural communities. By establishing a Climate-Smart Dairy ecosystem, the intervention will reduce emissions, enhance dairy yields, and build adaptive capacity, supporting a just and inclusive transition toward a sustainable, climate-resilient dairy sector in Sri Lanka. 

Project expects to support, 
- Direct beneficiaries (number, men/women): 750 smallholder famers (400 women/350 men) and 100 government officers. 
- Indirect Beneficiaries: 5,000 (including family members, aspiring youth agri-entrepreneurs, veterinary officers, animal health professionals, local milk collectors & other community members)

planEntities.name: Blue Economy Pipeline Development with a focus on Marine Tourism
planEntities.parentName: The government demonstrates improved commitment to gender-responsive and climate-smart environmental protection, natural resource management, and sustainable consumption and production practices.
planEntities.description:
For Sri Lanka, the Blue Economy offers a diverse range of opportunities for sustainable, clean, and fair growth in both traditional and emerging sectors, but it also requires innovation to meet these sustainability objectives. Leveraging the country’s vast ocean resources to advance ‘blue industries’ that supply goods and services to ‘blue value chains’ offer an innovative pathway to improve Sri Lanka’s external and trade balances. The pathway also provides an entry point to strengthen the equitable access of livelihood and economic opportunities for women and girls.

Adopting an integrated ‘blue economy’ approach – balancing both economic and conservation objectives - is aligned with UNDP’s Strategic Plan 2022-2025 and with the current Sri Lanka Country Programme. UNDP’s ambition is to support a blue economy that sustainably utilizes ocean resources for inclusive and sustainable development in Sri Lanka. This is also detailed in UNDP’s Ocean Promise and the integrated offer to Small Island Developing States (SIDS) – Rising Up for SIDS - which prioritizes climate action, blue economy acceleration, and digital transformation. 

Amongst other key priority areas within the blue economy, Sri Lanka’s marine tourism industry can evolve and unlock further opportunities for economic development and creation of ‘blue jobs’. By capitalizing on its natural resources, Sri Lanka can further drive economic growth and ensure the preservation of its marine environments for future generations.  

Against this backdrop, there are opportunities to put in place certain foundations to develop a pipeline of bankable 
projects focused on Sri Lanka’s blue economy.  

In this regard, UNDP Sri Lanka’s integrated service offer on blue tourism consists of 1) a blue economy development approach with a Marine Spatial Plan as the central governance framework, 2) collaboration with partners such as the Asian Development Bank (ADB) on marine tourism business models, 3) Northern and Eastern province tourism development, and other activities that are central to innovation in blue economy for sustainable growth.

planEntities.name: Supporting Asian countries’ resilience to violent extremism in the digital space
planEntities.parentName: The government, state and other institutional duty bearers, demonstrate increased capacities and commitment to uphold standards, practices and norms that promote human rights, non-discrimination, social dialogue, social cohesion and the empowerment of women and vulnerable populations.
planEntities.description:
The project supports countries in Asia to build resilience against violent extremism in the digital space, especially 
among youth by strengthening community mechanisms, knowledge and capacities specifically in Bangladesh, Indonesia, Malaysia, Maldives, Pakistan, Philippines, Thailand and Sri Lanka. 
 
It will strengthen the capacity of relevant stakeholders including youth-focused/youth-led organizations, women, educators, and CSOs at the national, regional, and cross-regional levels, to jointly formulate and implement prevention efforts with pro-active youth participation. The project aims to encourage behavioural change in opportunities for gender-responsive PVE and digital harm work. It also aims to encourage tech-based peacebuilding initiatives and provide support to young social media influencers with online start-up platforms (blogs, channels, Tik Tok etc.) to engage youth on issues of peace and social cohesion, manage hate speech, misinformation and online abuse, and facilitate online dialogue and trustbuilding, including with the use of AI.  
 
In addition to the above-described efforts, which will be led by UNDP, UNODC will undertake efforts to foster trust-based multi-stakeholders’ partnership against online radicalisation in Central, South and Southeast Asia, activities which will be implemented in parallel to UNDP’s project. Dedicated governance bodies, as described below, will assure complementarity and collaboration. However, for the purpose of this Project Document, focus will be solely on UNDP’s work. 

Project end date: 31 July 2028

planEntities.name: Governance, Rule of Law and Peacebuilding for Sustainable Development (AAA 2) - (01005340)
planEntities.parentName: People of all ages in Sri Lanka have enhanced knowledge, skills, and capacities to demand for and exercise their rights, and engage in constructive dialogue and actions that promote social cohesion, and peaceful coexistence.
planEntities.description:
The project adopts a social cohesion perspective with a gender lens, prioritizing community resilience, constructive dialogue, and responsive, rights‑based mechanisms that connect early signals to coordinated action 
particularly in the aftermath of the natural disaster. The project will (A) strengthen community‑based early warning/response (EWER) mechanisms with a Youth Peace and Security (YPS) lens; and (B) build cross‑ministerial capacities to prevent and respond to gendered information harms and TFGBV. All actions begin with rapid reviews of existing systems and practices to optimize before design or scale‑up. 

The project focus on strengthening the community‑based early warning/response (EWER) mechanism that identifies, reports, and engages stakeholders on conflict drivers and threat multipliers, by optimizing an existing CSO data pipeline through a diagnostic of indicators, gender‑disaggregation, privacy, analytics, and escalation, followed by upgrades to SOPs, dashboards, and feedback loops to improve data quality, timeliness, and safety; mobilizing and capacitating a provincial network of at least nine CBOs (including women‑led) with standardized tools, training, refresher clinics, and peer learning to monitor and report provincial indicators, ensuring coverage, comparability, and reliable trend detection under the YPS lens; and institutionalizing state–civil society dialogue platforms to conduct regular, solution‑oriented reviews of alerts with documented actions, translating data into coordinated, rights‑based mitigation,

Strengthening the capacities of state and non‑state institutions to respond to gendered hate speech, dis/misinformation/mal-information, and TFGBV by establishing cross‑ministerial coordination and protocols such as mapping mandates and workflows across the Ministries of Health & Mass Media, Women & Child Affairs, and Digital Economy, and co‑creating role clarity, referral SOPs, escalation pathways, joint communications, and an action calendar, to convert fragmented efforts into survivor‑centred, coherent responses; developing and maintaining a consolidated knowledge repository that curates prior and ongoing UNDP products and adds Sri Lanka‑specific guidance, templates, and measurement tools—to standardize and accelerate good practice; and initiating a national media awareness campaign—co‑designing and pre‑testing messaging with media partners, women leaders, and human rights defenders to counter harmful narratives, signpost services, and monitor reach and sentiment—to shift norms and increase help‑seeking and institutional responsiveness

Sri Lanka is expected to demonstrate:
• Stronger community mechanisms for conflict prevention and resilience, aligned with the YPS agenda. 
• Improved institutional capacity for inclusive governance and gender-responsive service delivery. 
• Enhanced protection and participation of women and marginalized groups in governance and peacebuilding processes.

planEntities.name: Gender Responsive Advancement and Operational Enhancement for Women Deminers in the Northern and Eastern Provinces of Sri Lanka (1005680)
planEntities.parentName: The government, state and other institutional duty bearers, demonstrate increased capacities and commitment to uphold standards, practices and norms that promote human rights, non-discrimination, social dialogue, social cohesion and the empowerment of women and vulnerable populations.
planEntities.description:
Sri Lanka continues to face a significant landmine and unexploded ordnance (UXO) challenge in its Northern and 
Eastern Provinces, where contamination remains concentrated near communities, infrastructure, and productive 
land. The National Mine Action Centre (NMAC), established with UNDP support, leads national coordination and 
implementation under the Mine Action Strategy (2023–2027) in order to meet Sri Lanka’s obligations under the Anti-Personnel Mine Ban Convention. While notable progress has been achieved, newly identified hazardous areas, 
funding constraints, and increasingly complex operating conditions continue to place pressure on national clearance timelines and operational capacity. 
 
Women comprise approximately 30 percent of Sri Lanka’s demining workforce, one of the highest proportions 
globally, and play a critical role in sustaining mine action operations. Many women deminers are heads of households or primary income earners in conflict-affected communities. Despite their contribution, women deminers continue to face structural and operational challenges, including demanding field conditions, limited access to gender responsive equipment, and constraints on technical advancement within mine action operations. Ensuring safe, inclusive, and enabling working environments for women deminers is therefore essential to sustaining clearance progress and protecting livelihoods dependent on the sector. 
 
In addition, recent extreme weather events, including Cyclone Ditwah and associated flooding, have further complicated the mine action operating environment in parts of the Northern and Eastern Provinces. Heavy rainfall, 
flooding, and soil erosion have disrupted access to previously surveyed area, and increased the risk of mine and UXO re-exposure in areas thought to be safe. These climate-related impacts have introduced new operational 
uncertainties and intensified safety risks for deminers working in already challenging conditions.  
 
Against this backdrop, the National Mine Action Centre (NMAC) and its partners are prioritising rapid non-technical 
surveys, re-marking hazardous zones, and restoring damaged demining facilities, alongside Explosive Ordnance Risk Education (EORE) campaigns to protect affected communities. These efforts are vital to achieving Sri Lanka’s 2027 mine-free goal under the National Mine Action Completion Strategy, which is now facing delays due to climate induced recontamination and operational disruptions. 
 
In response to these efforts, the project will engage in (1) Identifying and deploying advanced demining technologies to support remapping of contaminated areas, increase clearance speed, precision and safety, (2) Supporting immediate operational needs through non-technical surveys to identify new hazardous areas, and Explosive Ordnance Risk Education (EORE) for at-risk communities to safeguard people in the post-disaster context. In the process, it will directly benefit approximately 2500 demining workers including 750 women deminers and indirectly benefit 10,000 people including families of the deminers. As such, it will enhance community resilience in post disaster, mine-affected environments through inclusive, safe, and dignified living and working conditions. 
 
While adopting an enabling approach to gender equality and social inclusion, the project focuses on physical systems, equipment, and facilities that allow deminers—especially women—to operate safely and efficiently in challenging conditions. Through these investments in tangible assets and field improvements, the project will strengthen national mine action capacity, support timely progress towards the 2028 clearance deadline, and contribute to safer, more inclusive, and climate-resilient mine action operations across Sri Lanka’s most affected regions.

planEntities.name: Support to the implementation of Sri Lanka's nationally determined contributions in the industry sector
planEntities.parentName: The private sector, other non-state actors and the people in Sri Lanka have improved knowledge and capacities to demand for, adopt and use environmentally friendly, gender-responsive and climate-smart environmental protection, natural resource management, and sustainable consumption and production practices.
planEntities.description:
This is a 5-year project funded by the European Union under GCCA+ initiative. The main government counterparts are the Ministry of Industry, Ministry of Environment and the Ministry of Energy and the Ministry of Power.

The overall objective of the Project is to contribute to climate change mitigation through supporting the implementation of Sri Lanka's Nationally Determined Contributions (NDC) for the industrial sector. The specific Project objective is to scale-up the climate change response of Sri Lanka’s industrial sector through the design and implementation of technical, policy, regulatory and financial tools and mechanisms to accelerate the deployment of renewable energy, energy and resource efficiency technologies and best practices.
 
The Project aims to achieve greenhouse gas emission reductions through accelerating the uptake of innovative technologies, established best practices and methods for reducing carbon intensity and improving energy and resource efficiency performance of Sri Lanka’s industrial sector. Furthermore, this project is envisioned to contribute to long-term development gains such as capacity building of the government counterparts and empowerment of the project beneficiaries.
 
 
 
Expected Outcomes:
• EO1: A Monitoring, Review and Verification (MRV) system for the industry sector is developed and implemented and baseline for the industrial sector established
• EO2: An industrial sector plan for implementing NDCs has been validated and activities prioritized according to agreed criteria
• EO3: Policy and regulatory frameworks are improved and related awareness and capacity building of stakeholders to implement these frameworks have been built
• EO4: Capacity related to climate change mitigation practices in the area of industry is built
• EO5: Pilot technologies and methodologies leading to improved energy efficiency and reduction in GHG emissions are tested to be then replicated
 
The Project is implemented with the support of EU GCCA+ initiative, which aims to assist the world’s most vulnerable countries to respond to climate change. The project corresponds with the following priorities: to contribute to enhancing Sri Lanka's resilience to climate change while enabling the engagement in low-carbon development processes via the implementation of the NDCs.

*Actual project start date is 1 January 2022.

planEntities.parentName: Output 3.5: Private sector development: Enhanced multi-stakeholder capacity and improved business environment for a resilient,  productive, competitive, and innovative private sector including MSMEs
planEntities.description:
The project “Africa-Europe Partnerships for Culture: Promoting Culture and Heritage-based Sustainable Tourism in Southern Africa”, a European Union project implemented by UNESCO, will contribute to strengthening the contribution of culture and heritage to sustainable development, notably through enhancing culture and heritage-based tourism development, diversifying tourism products and delivering high-quality visitor experiences at selected UNESCO-designated sites and cities. These activities aim to contribute to improving livelihoods of the communities in the region, including youth, women and indigenous peoples, through capacity building and the creation of opportunities for income-generation and jobs.

Through innovative partnerships, the project will invest in the development of engaging storytelling, the production of meaningful digital content and authentic, relevant products incorporating new narratives. It will enhance cultural production capacities to develop community-based programming and tourism offers at the participating UNESCO-designated sites and cities. At the same time, the project presents a unique occasion to promote international cooperation and peer-to-peer learning opportunities among the six target Southern African countries, namely Botswana, Eswatini, Lesotho, Namibia, South Africa and Zimbabwe, as well as with European Union countries, to foster regional integration and social cohesion.

planEntities.parentName: CF output 2.4: Resilience and Climate Action - Strengthened institutional and community capacities for disaster preparedness, anticipatory  action and response with climate change mitigation measures.
planEntities.description:
OBJECTIVE: Strengthening the transition to people-centred, action-based warnings, formalising coordination and roles, embedding GEDSI considerations, and establishing learning processes that enhance the effectiveness and usability of forecasting and warning services in Lesotho.

TIMEFRAME: February 2026 to March 2027

Contributing Partners: FCDO through UK Met Office: 80 000 USD, WMO: 25 000 USD and SAWS: 15 000 USD.

Sub Activities

Sub Activity 1: Identify and prioritise user needs for Action-Based Forecasting by engaging at least four key user groups (disaster management, agriculture, health, and local government) for each priority hazard.

Sub Activity 2: Co-produce and validate impact tables and risk matrices for Heavy Rainfall and Cold Waves, endorsed by LMS, DMA, and relevant line departments.

Sub Activity 3: Strengthen coordination and clarify institutional roles by jointly developing draft inter-agency Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) that define responsibilities, decision thresholds, and response actions.

Sub Activity 4: Improve communication and accessibility of warnings by testing at least three dissemination channels (e.g. radio, mobile messaging, community networks) and incorporating GEDSI-responsive communication approaches.

Sub Activity 5: Advance implementation of Action-Based Forecasts and Warnings by conducting at least one validation or simulation exercise per hazard to test usability and trigger early action.

Sub Activity 6: Generate learning to inform future scale-up, with documented lessons and recommendations feeding into a national Action-Based Forecasting roadmap.

Required Budget: USD 1 million, Available: USD 120 000.00

planEntities.name: Provide technical and policy support to the implementation of the National Programme on Childcare Services for Children up to the Age of Three for the years 2023-2026
planEntities.parentName: OU 3.2_Regulatory framework and institutions promote economic empowerment of women and their equal access to decent work
planEntities.description: The Ministry of Labor and Social Protection is implementing the National Program on Childcare Services for Children up to Three Years Old (2023–2026), aimed at expanding access to quality childcare services and supporting parents in their caregiving and educational roles, while enabling their active participation in the labour market. The initiative provides technical and policy support to develop the necessary bylaws, strengthen the social protection of care workers, and create an enabling environment for the development of alternative childcare services. These include home-based nurseries, individual nanny services, and on-site childcare facilities, including their expansion at the regional level in six designated growth poles.

planEntities.name: Enhancing the effectiveness of labour market institutions in the Republic of Moldova to design and implement inclusive policies that generate quality jobs, promote fair working conditions, and safeguard workers’ rights.
planEntities.parentName: OU 3.1_Policy and institutional frameworks create an empowering environment for inclusive and sustainable economic development that promotes creation of productive and decent work
planEntities.description:
The overall objective of the project is to improve access to more and better employment opportunities in the Republic of Moldova.
Specific Objectives / Outcomes: 
- Strengthened capacity of the Ministry of Labour and Social Protection (MoLSP) and the National Employment Agency (NEA) to prevent and address labour market exclusion.
-Enhanced capacity of the Ministry of Labour and Social Protection (MoLSP) and the State Labour Inspectorate (SLI) to improve working conditions and ensure the protection of workers’ rights.
Objective 1: focuses on improving the institutional capacity of the MoLSP and NEA to deliver on the objectives of the national employment policy framework. This will be achieved through diversifying employment services and programmes expanding individualized service delivery, strengthening the performance management system, improving the in-house training system for NEA staff, including modernization of a new office for NEA staff in Cimislia.
Objective 2: aims to reinforce the capacity of the SLI to fulfil its state control mandate. This will be achieved by reviewing and updating legal frameworks and internal policies, planning inspection visits more strategically, improving the training system for SLI staff, modernizing procedures and upgrading the SLI information system, strengthening collaboration with social partners, providing necessary material and logistical support, including modernization of a new office for SLI staff in MoLSP premises.

planEntities.name: Development of skills to facilitate the green transition in the Republic of Moldova
planEntities.parentName: OU 3.4_People of Moldova, in particular those left behind, have improved access to adequate protection and safe working conditions, knowledge, in-demand skills and resources to foster employability, competitiveness and entrepreneurship culture
planEntities.description:
The specific activities focus on developing new occupational and qualification standards, curricula, and training programmes to prepare young and adult learners for emerging green job opportunities in the renewable energy sector. In particular, it aims at preparing young people and adult learners for three types of technologies, for which employers are currently looking for trained staff:
Electrician in Construction - Solar Photovoltaic Systems Installer
Technician for Renewable Energy Installations
Shallow Geothermal Systems and Heat Pump Installer
In addition, this project also seeks to aim higher: It will examine the skills needs in the Renewable Energy sector in general, to analyse systematically the skills that are needed for the green transition. To create opportunities for all in this sector, it will also advocate for a stronger participation of women, persons with disabilities and adult learners in this sector, to engender a National Dialogue on the importance of skills for the green transition and create awareness about career opportunities and green skills among young people.

planEntities.parentName: OU 1.5_State institutions and CSOs ensure effective prevention and improved multisectoral response to address all forms of violence against women and girls, including harmful practices and discriminatory gender norms and stereotypes
planEntities.description: Strengthened capacity of tripartite constituents to design and implement policies promoting gender equality in the world of work, including equal pay for work of equal value, improved work–life balance, and a more balanced sharing of family responsibilities. The initiatives also contribute to addressing discrimination, as well as violence and harassment in the world of work

planEntities.name: National institutions have increased capacity to strengthen and implement regulatory frameworks, policies and institutions to promote the economic empowerment of women and their equal access to decent work (UNWomen&ILO SDC Joint Programme)
planEntities.parentName: OU 3.2_Regulatory framework and institutions promote economic empowerment of women and their equal access to decent work
planEntities.description: At the policy level, the interventions focus on promoting gender mainstreaming, equal pay and improved childcare services to be integrated into the policies, programs and budgets of national institutions. The activities contribute to the development of an improved social protection system for care workers and advocate for decent working conditions in this female-dominated sector. Second, at the institutional level, the initiative supports various organizations, such as childcare service providers and social partners, to strengthen their capacity to provide quality services in the area of working conditions for care workers, gender pay gap and workplace policies.

planEntities.name: Enabling environment for women to enter into the labour market and enjoy decent working conditions, inclusive in the care sector
planEntities.parentName: OU 3.2_Regulatory framework and institutions promote economic empowerment of women and their equal access to decent work
planEntities.description: The government, in consultation with the social partners, takes steps towards ratification of the Workers with Family Responsibilities Convention, 1981 (No. 156) and Convention Domestic Workers Convention, 2011 (No. 189) to improve labour rights or working conditions of care workers, including domestic workers and to promote non-discrimination and support for workers with family responsibilities, including through: implementing campaigns to improve compliance with a law, policy or regulation to improve worker protection or quality of care services. Another activity is envisaged in view of the implementation of the Programme to Activate Women (PAW): specialized support services will be piloted within the Ungheni employment office, targeting mothers returning to work and those entering the labour market for the first time (uninsured persons without work experience).

planEntities.name: A more conducive environment for women’s entrepreneurship development and resilience
planEntities.parentName: OU 3.3_Enterprises are more resilient to crises and have strengthened capacities to efficiently utilize resources, generate decent employment and integrate innovations to enhance productivity and competitiveness
planEntities.description: In line with Moldova’s new Programme on women’s entrepreneurship and other relevant policies, the ILO provides targeted support to established women entrepreneurs operating in different sectors in Moldova. The proposed interventions support women entrepreneurs by connecting them with available care services and providing assistance to them in managing work-life balance and care responsibilities while also facilitating access to other gender-responsive support services. Within this context,  a pilot initiative will be launched to establish a peer and technical support group for 12 women entrepreneurs planning to start home-based crèches in the Municipality of Ungheni. The initiative will offer guidance, networking opportunities, and technical assistance to enhance their capacities in business start-up, management, and sustainable operations, ultimately contributing to more resilient, competitive, and inclusive enterprises.

planEntities.name: Advocacy for increased access to human rights by older persons, based on identified needs and challenges
planEntities.parentName: OU 1.1_Regulatory and policy framework that is evidence-informed and takes into account demographic trends promotes gender-responsive and human rights-based social protection and equal access to basic services
planEntities.description:
Activity planned for 2024
Needs assessment on human rights of older persons will be conducted by OHCHR etc. Human rights-based approach will be applied in identification of needs and human rights situation of older persons in Moldova in their full diversity to comprehensively identify the existing gaps and address them efficiently. The needs assessment will be conducted, in close coordination with the Ministry of Labor and Social Protection. The outcome will inform the ex-ante analysis for the development of a national law on older persons, foreseen in the National Programme on Active Ageing for the period 2023 – 2027.
Activity planned in 2025 
- Finalization of the report; 
- Consultation and validation of the results of the situational analysis;
- Publication and dissemination of the report.
Activities for 2026
- Advocacy for the implementation of the recommendations of the study on older persons.

planEntities.description:
2023 - 2025
"1. Strengthening the institutional capacity, motivation, and work resilience for 6 CSO's team and their members to respond efficiently and promptly to the humanitarian crisis (expected beneficiaries: at least 279 CSOs' staff member, board members, volunteers; representatives of Romni population and Ukrainian displaced women). 
2.	 Supporting women both local and refugees from Ukraine to remain/ become financially independent, and be economically and socially empowered but also involved into political life: 
2.1	 At least 1955 women will benefit of entrepreneurial training sessions, leadership programs, pre – accelerator programs, start -up Academy, capacity building activities, financial entrepreneurial camps.
2.2	120 women will be supported through a newly developed infrastructure for socio-professional integration.
2.3	200 refugee women are expected to be enrolled in retraining courses.
2.4	At least 245 of forcibly displaced women and local women will be employed or will benefit from financial support for starting own businesses/ developing active once or will be offered with paid placements. 
2.5	500 women will be receiving caregivers’ support.
2.6	104 of local enterprises involved in job fairs that can potentially provide the forced displaced women and young women with a job.
2.7	At least 125 women will strengthen their capacity and be more resilient in the situation of humanitarian crisis.
2.8	Creation of the Ukrainian Refugee Women's Network Association dedicated to protecting women's refugee rights.
3.	Supporting Local Public Authorities in providing a localized humanitarian response
3.1	At least 5 LPA will benefit from capacity building but also financial support to develop local plans for providing assistance to refugee women and children.
3.2	At least 10 representatives of LPAs (from 3 districts) are expected to get knowledge on correct identification of needs of people with disabilities. 
2024
1. Strengthening the institutional capacity, motivation, and work resilience for at least 21 CSO’s team members to respond efficiently and promptly to the humanitarian crisis. Focused areas: Gender Equality Programming, Women Economic Empowerment, Women, Peace and Security, Youth Engagement, Sex, Age and Disability Disaggregated Data and Gender Analysis, Gender-Sensitive Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning, Innovative and Creative Thinking, Project Cycle Management, Use of Generative Artificial Intelligence Tools for Project Management, Data Protection according to Local Legislation, Feminist Leadership and Leadership in Crisis, Wellbeing and Resilience, Public Speaking, Negotiation, Advocacy, Conflict Management.
Expected beneficiaries around 450, including CSOs' staff members, board members, volunteers, representatives of Romni population and Ukrainian displaced women. 
Implementing partners: KATALYST, ROMNI, WPC - 50/50, UEH, Motivatie,  NIKA - Generation, Consiliul National al Tineretului din Moldova (CNTM), Gender Centru, Institutum Virtutis Civilis, Institute for Democracy and Development, Casa Budesti, Women's Democracy Network, The Moldova Project Association (MPA), Agency for Innovation and Development (AID), European Abilities without Limits (AEFL), Copil Comunitate Familie (CCF), Public Association HELP,  Faclia, Women for Women (W4W), I4DD, WDN, Casa-Budesti", PISA, AO "Female Support Force".

planEntities.name: Increasing awareness of country specific norms and stereotypes to reduce the impact of stereotypes and challenge the roles of men and women
planEntities.parentName: OU 1.5_State institutions and CSOs ensure effective prevention and improved multisectoral response to address all forms of violence against women and girls, including harmful practices and discriminatory gender norms and stereotypes
planEntities.description:
The second phase of the regional programme “EU 4 Gender Equality: Together Against Gender Stereotypes and Gender-Based Violence” funded by the European Union (EU) and implemented jointly by UN Women and UNFPA in six Eastern Partnership countries: Armenia, Azerbaijan, Belarus, Georgia, Moldova, and Ukraine.

2025:
- Up to 50 women with disabilities have benefited from cohesion activities, psychological counseling, and other support services. (PA with NGO Motivatie)
- Up to 240 personal assistants, including members of the families in which persons with disabilities live, have improved their knowledge and capacities to support prevention and combating violence and discrimination against persons with disabilities in their families. (PA with NGO Motivatie)
- At least 60 members of the district multidisciplinary and mobile teams in the target regions have increased knowledge on the stereotypes, violence faced by women with disabilities and the ways of preventing/combating (PA with NGO Motivatie)
- Up to 100 women and men, girls and boys received transformative messages combating stigma and discrimination and/or gender-related information through the awareness raising activities. (PA with NGO Motivatie)
- Up to 70 young people from Stefan Voda and Causeni, with increased awareness on GE, gender stereotypes, VAW, engaged in a competition on the subject of gender equality (PA with IVC)
- 10 priests from the Bessarabia Metropolis from different regions of the country have increased knowledge on prevention and combating domestic violence, due to a Train of Trainers workshop and mentoring process (PA with Social Mission Diaconia). 
- 10 communities reached on promotion of healthy relationships and prevention of domestic violence, through raising awareness activities, with involvement of trained priests from these regions, and other stakeholders (NGO Diaconia)

planEntities.name: Women and girls, including those who are most often left behind( women with disabilities, living with HIV?AIDS, Roma, elderly and survivors of domestic violence) understand their rights to access and claim quality essential services
planEntities.parentName: OU 1.4_Rights holders, in particular from vulnerable groups, are empowered to access and claim for quality public services
planEntities.description:
Strengthen capacity and knowledge of women and girls to exercise their rights, access and claim qualitative essential services and to equally participate in the design of innovative solutions to VAWG prevention and response. Undertake public awareness and advocacy campaigns on EVAW area with participation of women survivors of violence, to promote positive social norms. Support women survivors of violence to access employment and entrepreneurial opportunities through vocational capacity building, mentoring programs, financial literacy and incentives.

2026:
- Up to 100 women survivors of violence from 5 regions of the country (Rîșcani, Ungheni, Drochia, UTA Găgăuzia, and one additional region to be confirmed) strengthened their economic empowerment capacities through tailored training and mentoring interventions. 
- Up to 20 women survivors of violence accessed support for vocational training, entrepreneurship, or income-generating activities 
- 7–8 women and approximately 10 dependent children provided with safe accommodation and protection services, according to individual risk and needs assessments
- Up to 55 women strengthened their confidence, communication and decision-making skills through thematic capacity-building workshops
- Up to 60 adolescent girls increased their knowledge of healthy relationships, consent, personal safety and available protection mechanisms through participatory prevention sessions.
- 129 students from five higher education institutions enhanced their knowledge and capacities to prevent, identify and respond to gender-based violence and sexual harassment in academic settings through targeted awareness-raising and capacity-building sessions
 -  Up to 200 women survivors of violence and women at risk access information sessions, primary legal aid, legal information through three partner organizations: Biaz Gul (Gagauzia, Basarabeasca, Taraclia), Dacia (Soroca), and Ophelia (Cahul)
- Up to 40 women survivors of violence receive professional legal aid and accompaniment to court services.

planEntities.name: State institutions and CSOs increase the quality of prevention and multisectoral response services to address all forms of VAWG including harmful practices and discriminatory gender norms and stereotypes
planEntities.parentName: OU 1.1_Regulatory and policy framework that is evidence-informed and takes into account demographic trends promotes gender-responsive and human rights-based social protection and equal access to basic services
planEntities.description:
Strengthen capacity of duty bearers, service providers, to ensure coordinated multi-sectoral and survivor-centered response for all women and girls by applying innovative solutions and "what works" principle. Increase capacity of WRO, survivors networks, CSOs to co-design women and girl-led innovative solutions to VAWG prevention and response in partnership with private sector, FBOs, men and boys, etc, incl. in online settings. Equip educational specialists, teachers, and relevant institutions to implement and promote comprehensive gender sensitive curricula, initiatives, strategies by applying innovative tools. Establish and/or strengthen integrated services for VAWG/GBV and sexual violence at local level. Support laws/policy reforms on VAWG based on international standards (Istanbul Convention, CEDAW, UPR) through consultancy, capacity building. Strengthen administrative data collection and analysis to inform VAWG prevention policies and programmes (based on approved multisectoral protocol) including support on the development of new VAW survey. Promote gender-sensitivity in media and journalism.

2026:
 - Up to 100 service providers and local stakeholders from 5 regions of the country (Rîșcani, Ungheni, Drochia, UTA Găgăuzia, and one additional region to be confirmed) strengthened their capacity to support the economic reintegration of women survivors of violence.
-  Up to 300 members of multidisciplinary teams (MDTs) from Nisporeni, Călărași and Taraclia, representing social assistance, law enforcement, health, education and local public authorities, strengthened their knowledge and practical skills in applying survivor-centred approaches, coordinated case management and effective interinstitutional cooperation across the identification, referral, protection and assistance continuum, in line with the National MDT Training Programme and Curriculum.
- 40 managers from Territorial Social Assistance Agencies and Structures and 25 specialists from specialized social services enhanced their capacities in institutional planning, strategic leadership, resource management, interinstitutional coordination and the provision of quality, survivor-centred services.
-  Six pilot communities (Tîrnova, Vălcineț, Botanica district of Chișinău, Taraclia, Congaz, and Bălți) advanced the localization of the National Programme on the Prevention and Combating of Violence against Women and Domestic Violence through inclusive and participatory planning processes, strengthening local ownership and coordinated community-based mechanisms for the prevention of and response to violence against women and domestic violence.
- up to 3 state institutions and CSOs will increase capacities to address discriminatory gender norms and violence against women and girls. (E.G. work with Superior Council of Magistrates, Superior Council of Prosecutors and the General Prosecutor's Office on developing policies on prevention of sexual harassment at workplace). 
- Up to 80 data collection operators strengthened their capacities to safely and ethically conduct the national “Women’s Well-being and Safety” survey using internationally aligned research methodologies.
- Seven local organizations have strengthened capacities to design and lead community initiatives to prevent and combat VAW and DV.
- Seven LPAs demonstrate strengthened capacities to develop and implement VAW and DV prevention initiatives based on participatory and inclusive
Community Safety Mapping.
-  At least 25 NGO representatives strengthened their capacities to develop and review PSEA policies in line with international standards.
- At least 7 higher education institutions strengthened their capacity to educate future professionals on preventing and responding to violence against women and domestic violence through the assessment and revision of relevant curricula and learning modules.
- Approval of the Framework Regulation on the Prevention, Reporting and Response to Sexual Harassment in Higher Education Institutions (Order No. 350 of 27 February 2026), providing higher education institutions with standardized procedures and mechanisms to prevent, identify, report and respond to sexual harassment, while strengthening institutional accountability and survivor-centred responses. 
- At least five higher education institutions adopted their own internal regulations, operationalizing the provisions of the Framework Regulation at the institutional level and strengthening mechanisms for the prevention, reporting and response to sexual harassment.
- The first specialist service for survivors of sexual violence in Ungheni piloted and consolidated. Outreach in communities on availability of the service and breaking stigma on reporting.
- Two CSOs (NGOs Onoarea și Drepturile Femeii Contemporane (Bălți) and BIAZ GUL (Comrat), with strengthened capacities for delivering specialized, trauma healing and rehabilitation services, for survivors of GBV within the sub-partner program with RCTV Memoria. 
-Up to 100 service providers and local stakeholders from 5 regions of the country (Rîșcani, Ungheni, Drochia, UTA Găgăuzia, and one additional region to be confirmed) strengthened their capacity to support the economic reintegration of women survivors of violence.
- The Mid-Term Evaluation of the National Programme on Preventing and Combating Violence against Women and Domestic Violence (2023–2027) developed for ANPCV, with support from UN Women, UNFPA and the Council of Europe, providing evidence-based recommendations to strengthen the national response to violence against women and domestic violence.
- Support the development of amendments to several laws to strengthen the legal protection of women and children from violence, improve the enforcement of family law decisions, and enhance access to justice for survivors.
- A capacity-building programme on gender-sensitive media practices initiated, with media outlets selected to receive tailored support for promoting inclusive and stereotype-free media coverage.

planEntities.name: HIV prevention and response services are provided for refugees and host communities, focusing on key populations
planEntities.parentName: OU 1.2_Health, education and food systems are strengthened and become more resilient to ensure universal access and quality of services and respond to humanitarian needs
planEntities.description:
Activities focused on HIV prevention and response services are provided for refugees and host communities in the 4 regions of the country: North, Center, South, East. Through collaboration with UNAIDS in 2024: 
• Provision of community-based HIV prevention, TB screening, care, and support services for 1600 refugees living with and affected by HIV, focusing on key populations such as sex workers, LGBTIQ+ individuals and refugees who use drugs.  This includes informational and educational sessions (individually or in groups) for key topics such as prevention, detection and treatment of HIV, hepatitis, STIs and TB. Participants will also learn about accessing available humanitarian aid and vital services like GBV support, Sexual and Reproductive health services, and psychological help.                                                                   
• Provision of Prevention Services for 400 individuals: The project will focus on providing HIV, TB, STIs, and Viral hepatitis prevention services for 400 individuals, primarily high-risk groups among refugees from Ukraine.
 - Referral of 400 Refugees to Specialized Support Services: This aspect of the project aims to refer 400 refugees to partner organizations and specialized institutions for essential medical and non-medical support.   
- Continuity of Treatment Support Services: The project will prioritize the continuity of OAT, ART, and TB services, promoting treatment and medication adherence. Regular medication supply will be provided through the National HIV/AIDS and TB Programmes. 
- The project aims to distribute 1360 Incentive/Dignity Kits, which contain hygiene, sanitary, beauty items, and other local necessities. These kits will also include basic information on sexual and reproductive health, GBV, and mental health.        
• Community-based Operational Research (OR) to provide a comprehensive, evidence-based understanding of the priority needs or barriers faced by refugees, particularly those at risk, in accessing health and social services, including social inclusion and human rights, since their arrival in the Republic of Moldova.

planEntities.name: Promote social-cohesion through youth engagement (UNDP)
planEntities.parentName: OU 2.4_Government and non-government actors have strengthened capacities and resources to address the humanitarian crisis, sustain peace and security at the national and regional level and ensure access to justice for all
planEntities.description: Multiple dividing lines between people and communities in Moldova weaken social cohesion and hinder the development of a consolidated, resilient society, in turn undermining political stability and sustainable peace. Community dialogue platforms and inter-regional and intersectional cooperation platforms play a pivotal role in fostering resilience and promoting social cohesion. By facilitating open dialogue and collaboration among diverse community members and between communities, the project interventions will create opportunities for people to interact, express their concerns, share opinions and ideas, and cooperate towards common goals. The project interventions are expected to empower target communities and their residents from both banks of the Nistru river to take an active role in addressing the needs of the people (older people, youth, women, under-represented groups and refugees), address local tensions and strengthen social cohesion. The project will contribute to increased collaboration with civil society organizations (CSOs), local stakeholders, private sector as well as local public authorities. The project also aims to empower communities to initiate local programs such as intergenerational support arrangements, intergenerational activities, discussion platforms for youth etc. Through these efforts, community members will be actively involved in decision-making processes and community life, fostering a deeper sense of connection and solidarity among them. This engagement will result in the cultivation of stronger social bonds and the establishment of robust mutual support networks within the community.

planEntities.name: From Risk to Resilience Finance in Moldova and Beyond
planEntities.parentName: OU 4.2_Public and private institutions have increased capacities to ensure effective sustainable management, protection and use of natural resources, improved energy resources efficiency and climate, emergency and disaster resilience that benefit most vulnerable and poor
planEntities.description:
The project aims to strengthen the integration of disaster risk reduction (DRR) and climate change adaptation (CCA) considerations into public and private financing, budgeting, investment, and decision-making processes, contributing to more risk-informed, resilient, and sustainable development at national, sectoral and local levels. The identified areas of cooperation are designed to respond to identified needs and align with Moldova’s evolving national crisis management architecture, the National Program for Natural Disaster Risk Reduction (NPDRR) for 2026-2030, the National Adaptation Plan, the forthcoming National Programme on Resilience in Agriculture 2027–2030, and other relevant sectoral, public finance, and investment frameworks.
The project is expected to contribute to:
1. Improved evidence and analysis on DRR and CCA financing, public expenditure, and the economic and fiscal benefits of investing in prevention and resilience in Moldova
2. Strengthened dialogue and collaboration among government, financial institutions, development partners and the private sector on financing resilience;
3. Improved consideration of DRR and resilience in post-disaster recovery planning;
4. Enhanced evidence and analysis on resilience-related public expenditure through the pilot application of DRR and CCA Budget Tagging (DCBT) in the agriculture sector, generating lessons for programme design and broader application.
5. Increased awareness, capacities and policy recommendations for MSMEs and business support organisations to prepare for and manage disruptions; and
6. Enhanced regional knowledge exchange and cooperation on DRR, recovery and resilience financing through Moldova's participation in the Europe and Central Asia Regional Platform for Disaster Risk Reduction in 2027.

This project under the UNESCO-KFIT initiative “Digital Creative Lab II”, aims to support developing countries in addressing the digital skills shortages in the cultural and creative industries. This will be done by supporting the establishment of training programmes that strengthen the digital skills and competencies of the cultural and creative sectors in developing countries, and to support their full participation in the ongoing changes to the cultural value chain.
As such, the UNESCO Office in Venice shall:
Enhance the capacity of the cultural and creative sectors to promote inclusive, fair and sustainable economic development in the Republic of Moldova. Through the proposed activities, creative and cultural industries will be empowered to better face socio-economic challenges. In the long run, the project will create synergies to promote the diversity of cultural expressions in the digital environment.
Inform policy in culture and creative sectors through high quality data and information especially related to digital environment (Thematic Indicators for Culture in 2030 Agenda, and Creative Industries Festival)
Improve the digital skills and competencies of professionals in the cultural and creative sectors by providing capacity building for professionals and managers in the cultural and creative sectors, by providing digital tools and equipment to universities teaching subjects related to the creative industries, and by establishing formal cooperation and exchange of experiences with CCIs in other countries.

planEntities.name: (UNFPA) Strengthened capacity of the General Education system to deliver quality health education and create an enabling environment for students’ wellbeing and healthy development.
planEntities.parentName: OU 1.2_Health, education and food systems are strengthened and become more resilient to ensure universal access and quality of services and respond to humanitarian needs
planEntities.description:
As part of its ongoing commitment to the Ministry of Education and Research (MER), UNFPA continues to enhance national capacity and policy in the education sector, empowering pupils and youth through life-skills development and supporting their safe transition to adulthood. UNFPA will provide sustained technical expertise to advance national priorities related to adolescent and youth well-being, comprehensive sexuality education (CSE), and safe and healthy development. Additionally, it will support MER in strengthening communication and promoting the roles of schools and families in education. 
In 2023, is formalising its collaboration with the Ministry of Education and Research by signing a Memorandum of Understanding for the 2023-2027 period. 
Following the International Technical Guidance on Sexuality Education and addressing national needs, UNFPA will support the Ministry in developing a health education school club for grades V-VII. In 2023, the curriculum and didactic resources will be developed, with pilot implementation and finalization planned for 2024. 
Additionally, UNFPA will piloted the EduLIFE School Program: friendly environment, access to health education, and menstrual hygiene products. This concept embodies a multidimensional approach to strengthening the educational institutions’ ability to contribute to students' well-being and life skills, encouraging healthy and non-violent behaviour, promoting equal learning opportunities for both girls and boy
In 2024, UNFPA is expanding the "EduLIFE School" model to four new schools, including two designated as Model Schools. This initiative will promote a student-friendly environment, comprehensive sexuality education, and access to menstrual hygiene products. The selection of schools will be carried out in collaboration with the Ministry of Education, with two institutions being reorganized to accommodate refugee students from Ukraine. Key implementing partners will include the NGO “Youth Media Center” and the platform “suntparinte.md.”
In 2025, alongside with other UN agencies, UNFPA is assisting MER in conducting a national school survey among pupils, parents, and teachers. The survey will assess education quality, student participation, informal payments, rights awareness, gender equality, bullying, well-being, and include dedicated questions on CSE. 
As one of the key partners in the National Curriculum reform, UNFPA is building the capacities of curriculum authors to evaluate the existing curriculum and develop a new one. International standards and assessment tools in CSE will guide this process, ensuring the integration of CSE and life-skills topics into the new mandatory national curriculum. 

UNFPA will also support MER in organizing Education Week in May 2025, contributing to organization of a national conference with local and regional education experts and organizing a side event on Dual Education in the Vocational Education and Training (VET) system. 
Building on 2024 achievements, UNFPA will pilot a curriculum-based school club on health education, providing training and continuous support to 30 teachers from various schools. 

In 2026, UNFPA will continue to support the integration of health education, including comprehensive sexuality education (CSE), into the formal curriculum as part of the national curriculum reform. The working group responsible for the subject Me and Society will receive technical support to integrate these topics while developing the key curricular products, including the conceptual framework, the curriculum, and the methodological guide for teachers. Once these materials are finalized, UNFPA will begin delivering a long-term in-service capacity-building programme for the first cohort of Me and Society teachers who will start implementing the curriculum in September 2027.

Additionally, UNFPA will continue to provide technical support to MER in the process of institutionalizing the menstrual health and hygiene programme. As part of this process, UNFPA will conduct an assessment of the use of public funds by schools during the 2026–2027 school year and the actual access of girls to menstrual pads. The findings will inform the design of the fund disbursement process for the resources already allocated by MER for the 2027–2028 school year.

Building on the experience of previous years in supporting parents of adolescents to strengthen their knowledge of health and sexuality education topics—enabling them to better support the healthy development of their children—and in line with MER’s initiative to develop an ecosystem of parenting programmes, UNFPA will provide technical support for the development of a legal framework on parenting and will pilot a parenting programme.

Following the School Barometer research conducted last year, UNFPA will support a communication campaign to disseminate the findings. The organization will also support the National Pupils’ Council to share the results with their peers, consult them on recommendations and solutions, and present these during Education Week.

Finally, UNFPA will contribute to the collection of data on health behaviours among school-aged children through the HBSC study, in order to inform evidence-based decision-making in the education and health sectors.

planEntities.name: (UNFPA) Strengthened capacity of the Vocational Education and Training system/schools to deliver quality life skills education and create an enabling environment for students’ wellbeing and job readiness.
planEntities.parentName: OU 1.3_Public institutions and CSOs/CBOs have enhanced capacities to ensure quality sustainable people-centered service delivery that is responsive to social, economic and environmental shocks and emergencies
planEntities.description:
Over the last few years, UNFPA has been supporting Vocational Education and Training (VET) to increase the quality-of-life skills-based health education and create safe and friendly school spaces so young people can develop healthy behaviors and increase their job readiness. 

In 2023, UNFPA will continue its work in this area and will invest in developing a continuous training programme for teachers in VET on health education; developing the teachers' handbook for the ‘Decisions for a Healthy Lifestyle’, based on the recently revised curriculum; support the functionality and capacity building of the Network of Peer Educators in VET to reach out to 2000 VET students with informative activities on healthy behaviors, mental health, sexuality, and reproductive health and rights, etc.; analyze knowledge, attitudes, and practices related to sexual and reproductive health among students in VET.

During the period 2024–2025, the focus will be on strengthening the capacity of teachers delivering the Decisions for a Healthy Lifestyle course across all VET institutions by accrediting the continuous training program. Additionally, efforts will be made to equip schools with edutainment materials and menstrual hygiene products, as well as create a youth friendly learning classroom in 20 targeted VET institutions endowed with IT equipment.

Furthermore, support will be provided to strengthen the Peer Educators Network in promoting life skills education and increase the capacity of business companies from dual VET in creating a youth-friendly workplace. 

During 2025–2026, a dedicated training programme was also organized for nurses, psychologists and social pedagogues working in VET institutions to strengthen their capacity to support students’ well-being and healthy development.

During 2026–2027, a parenting programme will be developed and implemented to engage parents of VET students in supporting their children’s education and development. At the same time, Youth Centres will receive support in designing and implementing career guidance and employability skills programmes, helping young people strengthen the skills needed for their transition to the labour market.

The support will continue through 2027, with other strategic and system-wide interventions with support from the Austrian Development Agency.

planEntities.name: Out-of-school comprehensive sexuality education for youth, including young people with disabilities, is operationalized following international standards.
planEntities.parentName: OU 1.4_Rights holders, in particular from vulnerable groups, are empowered to access and claim for quality public services
planEntities.description:
To complement the formal/school-based comprehensive sexuality education and reach out to adolescents and youth from vulnerable groups and remote areas, UNFPA has been supporting for many years the out-of-school programs. 
In 2023 UNFPA will continue implementing the out-of-school comprehensive sexuality education (CSE) program. This initiative will follow UNFPA’s International Technical and Programmatic Guidance on Out-of-School CSE and will focus on reaching adolescents and young people in rural areas, those with disabilities, and youth from the left bank of the Nistru River.
In 2024, the initiative aims to foster a more inclusive and supportive environment where all young people, regardless of their background, have access to comprehensive sexuality education and essential resources for a healthy and informed future. To achieve this, several institutions and organizations working with youth will be equipped with dedicated spaces for non-formal sexuality education activities.
Additionally, civil society organizations, particularly those in underserved regions, will receive support to enhance their capacity in promoting young people’s sexual and reproductive health and rights. Specialists from various organizations will be trained to deliver accurate, age-appropriate education on these topics, ensuring that young people are well-informed and empowered.
Furthermore, parents and caregivers of adolescents with disabilities will be provided with the necessary knowledge and resources to support their children’s development and smooth transition into adulthood.
In 2025, UNFPA will continue strengthening civil society organizations and youth networks across Moldova, including those on the left bank of the Nistru River, to develop and implement programs on sexual and reproductive health and rights tailored to diverse youth groups. To support these efforts, UNFPA will create guidelines for delivering youth-friendly health services for vulnerable youth, aligned with international out-of-school comprehensive sexuality education (OOS CSE) standards.
A digital training program will be introduced for facilitators working in CSE, ensuring they are well-equipped to provide accurate and effective education. Additionally, new educational and interactive materials, such as the Diary of an Adolescent Boy/Girl, will be developed to make information on sexual and reproductive health and rights more accessible and relevant to young people. 
Building on UNFPA Moldova’s expertise in youth well-being and global best practices, and in partnership with the Ministry of Education and Research (MER) and the Youth National Agency, UNFPA will establish the Future-Ready Hub—a pioneering space dedicated to life skills development, innovation, and modern technologies. Bringing together adolescents, youth educators, youth workers, NGOs, and the private sector, the Hub will foster a collaborative, forward-looking environment. 

In 2026, UNFPA will continue supporting NGOs to deliver out-of-school comprehensive sexuality education (CSE) programmes for adolescents and young people. Organizations trained in previous years will receive further support to reach adolescents with disabilities and those from rural areas or families affected by poverty, violence, and other vulnerabilities. NGOs will also be supported to integrate the Adolescent Diary into their programmes, both as a complementary resource and as a stand-alone CSE tool.
Healthcare providers from the left bank of the Nistru River will receive continuous supervision on specific health and CSE topics to strengthen their capacity to provide accurate, evidence-based, and youth-friendly medical and psychological services. In addition, they will be empowered and supported to act as trainers for local school staff.
As part of the operationalisation of the EduLIFE Hub, planned for launch this year, a regionally co-created curriculum and handbook on life skills will be developed. These resources will support educators in strengthening adolescents’ competencies in sexuality education and in developing the skills necessary to navigate modern societies.
Additionally, UNFPA will conduct a national youth-centered campaign to promote healthy and safe adolescent development, including targeted messages on the prevention of teenage pregnancy.

planEntities.parentName: OU 3.2_Regulatory framework and institutions promote economic empowerment of women and their equal access to decent work
planEntities.description: The project aims to enhance shared prosperity in Moldova by 2028, ensuring that women and girls, especially the most vulnerable, including NEET (Not in Education, Employment, or Training) women, will benefit from family friendly opportunities and sustainable economic development, including access to gender-responsive workplaces and employment. It targets local government institutions, professional training providers, and private sector representatives. The project will target women and girls from 5 rayons, including Chisinau, and the number of beneficiaries is estimated from the average demographic statistics, as the exact rayons of work will be determined later during the assessment.  An average rayon population (excluding Chisinau and UTA Gagauzia) is about  50,000 people, with women above 50%, and out of these, less than 20% are women and girls 15-64 years old. It will encompass study assessments, capacity building, developing and piloting inclusive employment measures, extending childcare services, and promoting FFP. The project will also raise awareness and share best practices to ensure sustainable impact. This holistic approach addresses socio-economic challenges, aiming to create a more inclusive and equitable labour market in Moldova, ultimately contributing to the country's sustainable economic development and the well-being of its diverse population.
