The programme is funded by the European Union (EU) and implemented jointly by UN Women and UNFPA in six Eastern Partnership countries: Armenia, Azerbaijan, Belarus, Georgia, Moldova, and Ukraine.

Overall, the programme provides a unique opportunity to change the social discourse, perceptions and harmful practices on gender equality in the region, and to empower women and girls to fully access their rights and develop their potential.

planEntities.name: (UNFPA) Preventing and responding to GBV by transforming harmful gender norms, strengthening parenting programmes, combating TFGBV, and enhancing inclusive, survivor-centred response services and coordination.
planEntities.parentName: OU 1.5_State institutions and CSOs ensure effective prevention and improved multisectoral response to address all forms of violence against women and girls, including harmful practices and discriminatory gender norms and stereotypes
planEntities.description: Under the Joint Programme, UNFPA leads efforts to prevent and respond to gender-based violence by transforming harmful gender norms, engaging men and boys, and strengthening survivor-centred services for women and adolescents from refugee and host communities. UNFPA enhances gender-transformative parenting programmes through a dedicated GBV toolkit, combats technology-facilitated GBV through awareness raising in Safe Spaces and nationwide campaigns, and supports the national eViolenta platform and specialised women’s helpline. It strengthens the national GBV case management, builds the capacity of service providers — including those working with refugees — promotes disability inclusion, and improves coordination across GBV, child protection, and social protection systems. UNFPA also supports the development of the VioData national GBV register and contributes to research and evidence generation to inform stronger national policies and interventions.

planEntities.name: Strengthened national capacity to expand access to life-saving, survivor-centered, and integrated GBV prevention and response services, as well as comprehensive SRH care, counseling, and information for refugees from Ukraine and vulnerable host communities within the humanitarian response context.
planEntities.parentName: OU 1.5_State institutions and CSOs ensure effective prevention and improved multisectoral response to address all forms of violence against women and girls, including harmful practices and discriminatory gender norms and stereotypes
planEntities.description:
UNFPA will continue strengthening national capacity to expand access to life-saving, survivor-centered, and integrated GBV prevention and response services, as well as comprehensive SRH care, counseling, and information for refugees from Ukraine and vulnerable host communities within the humanitarian response context.
The main activities will be:
- Running of 22 Women and Girls Safe Spaces nationwide (16 static, 6 mobile), providing inclusive, survivor-centered GBV prevention and response services for refugee and host-community women. Safe Spaces offer psychosocial and legal support, enable safe disclosure, and extend access to underserved rural areas.
- UNFPA will continue supporting the operation of 2 shelters - MAGNOLIA shelter and SALVIA, the Cross-Border Crisis Center, addressing the urgent needs of refugee women and women from hosting communities who have experienced violence. The Centers have been revitalized and prepared to accommodate up to 45 beneficiaries. 
- UNFPA Moldova, through its IP, AO Artemida and in close coordination with the Ministry of Labour and Social Protection, continues to scale survivor-centred GBV case management linked to targeted cash assistance as part of a carefully managed refugee and host-community response. The model integrates emergency and recurring cash support through bank transfers into individual case action plans, enabling survivors to access protection services, legal aid, psychosocial support and basic needs while reducing economic barriers to safety and recovery and avoiding dependency. Operational coverage spans multiple northern districts.
- UNFPA Moldova continues winter and contingency preparedness through pre-positioning dignity and menstrual hygiene kits and sustaining case-management and PSS capacity via safe spaces, but severe funding cuts have reduced the scale of distributions and surge readiness. In line with the GBViE Minimum Standards, dignity kits remain a core, non-specialized component of coordinated, survivor-centred GBV programming in emergencies, contributing to protection, risk mitigation, and dignity when implemented alongside referral pathways, service information, and community engagement.
- As part of WGSS empowerment programming, UNFPA supports women at risk, including GBV survivors, to access vocational training and skills development through structured referral pathways, complementing psychosocial support and case management to strengthen resilience and self-sufficiency. Building on a 2025 pilot, UNFPA Moldova—with PRO DIDACTICA and vocational institutions—implements a VET-based pathway offering accredited micro-qualification courses, alongside financial-literacy support and links to employment or self-employment, enabling transition from short-term assistance to sustainable livelihoods.
- UNFPA will support the psychologists working with GBV victims and tghe newly established National College of Psychologists, as mandated by the Law on the Exercise of the Psychology Profession, as part of its programme to support frontline social services who provide psychosocial support and conduct court-mandated evaluations for women and survivors of GBV.
- UNFPA will support the National Bureau of Statistics to conduct a nationally representative GBV prevalence study, generating high-quality, ethically collected data on the scale, forms, and drivers of violence against women and girls, including in crisis-affected and displaced populations. The study will inform evidence-based policy, humanitarian planning, and service delivery, while strengthening national capacity for GBV data collection in line with international standards.
- UNFPA will support the Ministry of Labour and Social Protection (MLSP)  - Currently, state care institutions for persons with disabilities in Moldova face poor living conditions, including overcrowding, inadequate infrastructure, limited accessibility, and insufficient specialized staff. Many residents experience restricted autonomy, lack of individualized care, and heightened risk of neglect or abuse, undermining their dignity and well-being. These challenges are compounded by limited resources, outdated practices, and gaps in staff training on rights-based, inclusive care. Urgent action is needed to improve quality of life, ensure accessibility, and establish safe, supportive, and empowering environments for all residents. 
-  Supporting the outreach activity of the Mobile Youth Clinic in the South Region, which increases access of young people from rural communities to youth-friendly health information and services, including SRH care.
-  Strengthening Primary Healthcare facilities for provision of quality SRH services (antenatal and postnatal healthcare, cervical screening etc.) through endowment of 12 additional PHC facilities with standardized set of modern medical equipment
-  Capacity building for 250 non-health professionals on MISP for SRH in Refugee Crisis context (staff of the National Crisis Management Center, General Inspectorate for Emergency Situations, Police and Border Police, Agency for Material Reserves/Management Center of State Material Reserves, Refugee Accommodation Centers)
- Cross-sectoral simulation exercise on MISP for SRH in a refugee crisis context
-  Supporting winterization efforts by procuring and distributing 2000 Mama Kits through Perinatal Centers to pregnant women and new mothers—including refugee women and vulnerable women of host communities
-  Capacity Building for 100 healthcare professionals, staff of Pre-hospital Emergency Healthcare Service on Clinical Management of Obstetrical Emergencies / 8 Training Workshops to be organized and conducted.
-  Support will be provided for the development and production of visibility and communication materials related to cervical cancer prevention during Cervical Cancer Prevention Awareness Week and Cancer Control Awareness Month 2026
-  Support for development of 3 National Clinical Protocols (Clinical Emergency Protocols): NCP “Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation in Pregnant Women”; NCP “Preterm Birth”; NCP “Fetal Growth Restriction”

planEntities.name: Creation of an Enabling Environment to Prevent GBV and Provision of Survivor-Centred GBV and SRH Response Services for Refugees from Ukraine and Vulnerable Host Communities
planEntities.parentName: OU 1.5_State institutions and CSOs ensure effective prevention and improved multisectoral response to address all forms of violence against women and girls, including harmful practices and discriminatory gender norms and stereotypes
planEntities.description:
Actions:
Women and Girls Safe Spaces (WGSS):
Establishment and operationalization of 22 Women and Girls Safe Spaces nationwide (16 static and 6 mobile), delivering inclusive, survivor-centred GBV prevention and response services to refugee and host-community women and girls. WGSS provide psychosocial and legal support, facilitate safe disclosure and referrals, and extend outreach to underserved and rural areas through mobile modalities.
Strengthening Cross-Border and Shelter Response Capacity:
Enhancement of institutional capacities and cross-border referral mechanisms for the Cross-Border Crisis Center and the MAGNOLIA Shelter to address the urgent protection and assistance needs of refugee women survivors of violence, ensuring coordinated, timely, and survivor-centred support.
GBV Case Management and Cash Assistance:
Scale-up of survivor-centred GBV case management integrated with targeted cash assistance as part of a coordinated refugee and host-community response. The model incorporates emergency and recurring cash transfers (via bank transfers) into individualized case action plans, enabling survivors to safely access protection services, legal aid, MHPSS, and essential goods, while reducing economic barriers to safety and recovery and mitigating risks of dependency.
Safe@Home Modality:
Provision of tailored outreach services for persons with limited mobility, ensuring access to MHPSS and referrals to specialized protection and support services through home-based interventions.
WGSS Empowerment Programming:
Support to women at risk, including GBV survivors, to access vocational education and skills development through structured referral pathways that complement psychosocial support and case management. Building on a 2025 pilot, UNFPA Moldova, in partnership with PRO DIDACTICA and accredited vocational institutions, implements a VET-based pathway offering certified micro-qualification courses to strengthen resilience, economic empowerment, and self-sufficiency.
Disability Inclusion:
Mainstreaming of disability inclusion across all interventions to ensure accessibility, reasonable accommodation, and equitable participation of women and girls with disabilities in GBV prevention, response, and empowerment programming.
-	Supporting the expansion of the network of Hospital GBV/CMR Units to 5 additional hospital emergency departments – equipping psychosocial support offices with the non-medical equipment and furniture necessary to provide safe, confidential counseling and prevent the re-victimization of sexual violence survivors
-	Supporting the development of an advanced training module for nurses in higher education, focused on the specialized collection of forensic evidence within the Clinical Management of Rape (CMR) & its integration into the curricula of the State University of Medicine and Pharmacy “Nicolae Testemitanu” (adapting international best practices such as the Sexual Assault Nurse Examiner (SANE) model).  
-	Strengthening capacity of 60 nurses with higher education on the specialized collection of forensic evidence within the Clinical Management of Rape (CMR) / 4 Training Workshops to be organized and conducted
-	Capacity building of 100 healthcare professionals from Perinatal Healthcare Centers  (obstetricians-gynecologists) on human-rights based approach to disability and on disability-sensitive intranatal care
-	Capacity building of 200 healthcare professionals from Primary Healthcare facilities (family doctors) on HRBA to disability and on disability-sensitive SHR care
-	Support will be provided for the development and production of visibility and communication materials related to cervical cancer prevention during Cervical Cancer Prevention Awareness Week and Cancer Control Awareness Month 2026
-	Support will be provided to design and produce an outdoor thematic photo exhibition showcasing key achievements over the past few years in the area of SRHR.
-	Support for content development and production of communication materials to be disseminated via social media channels used by people with disabilities and NGOs working with PwDs  - 10 videos on inclusive safe maternity adapted for sign language to meet the needs of women with disabilities
-	Support in conducting the HPV testing pilot within cervical screening (mentorship for participating healthcare institutions within HPV testing pilot, field monitoring visits to assess quality, and the collection and synthesis of data collected)
-	Support in performing an Economic Analysis based on HPV testing pilot data (the findings will serve as an evidence base for policy decisions to shift the primary cervical screening modality from the Papanicolaou (Pap) test to HPV testing)

planEntities.name: Refugee and vulnerable Moldovan children, including Roma children and children with disabilities, have improved access to inclusive and quality formal education through targeted support, strengthened coordination, and capacity-building initiatives.
planEntities.parentName: OU 1.2_Health, education and food systems are strengthened and become more resilient to ensure universal access and quality of services and respond to humanitarian needs
planEntities.description:
UNHCR will continue collaborating with the Ministry of Education and Research (MER) and UNICEF to ensure that refugee and vulnerable Moldovan children, adolescents, and youth have access to inclusive and quality formal education. Key efforts will focus on increasing enrollment rates in Moldovan schools, expanding access to preschool education, and ensuring that all refugee families are informed about school enrollment procedures. UNHCR will also support the endorsement and fundraising efforts for the costed roadmap on educational inclusion, ensuring that financial and technical assistance is available to sustain refugee education efforts.

To facilitate effective learning and integration, UNHCR will support targeted Romanian language classes, literacy programs, and catch-up education, particularly for Roma children and other marginalized groups facing barriers to school enrollment and retention. Schools will receive technical support and additional resources, and teacher training programs will be expanded to improve inclusive education methodologies. Furthermore, UNHCR will promote in-person education, mitigating risks associated with prolonged online learning and ensuring that refugee children can fully participate in classroom environments​.

Strengthening child protection and psychosocial support within the education system will remain a priority. UNHCR will work to enhance school-based protection mechanisms, ensuring that refugee and vulnerable Moldovan children have access to safe learning environments free from bullying and discrimination. In line with the new Temporary Protection Directive, and in coordination with UNICEF, UNHCR will support the MER to develop and implement the monitoring system to track refugee children access to education, including its modalities. Additionally, UNHCR will continue advocating for higher education opportunities for refugees, including exploring the potential rollout of the DAFI scholarship program in Moldova. Through these interventions, UNHCR aims to foster sustainable inclusion, ensuring that education serves as a pathway to protection, resilience, and future self-reliance for all refugee children, particularly those from marginalized backgrounds.

planEntities.name: Access to private housing for refugees is expanded through rental subsidies, small-scale housing rehabilitation combined with tenure security guarantees, and inclusion in Moldova’s national affordable housing schemes, supporting long-term, sustainable living arrangements.
planEntities.parentName: OU 1.4_Rights holders, in particular from vulnerable groups, are empowered to access and claim for quality public services
planEntities.description:
Access to stable, adequate housing is a catalyst for all other aspects of refugees’ self-reliance—enabling people to settle, seek employment, enrol their children in school, and fully participate in community life.

UNHCR will promote access to private housing solutions through rental assistance programs, small-scale repairs, and advocacy for refugee inclusion in Moldova’s affordable housing schemes. These efforts will primarily target economically active refugees who are able to progressively assume responsibility for their housing costs, ensuring that rental assistance remains a transitional and sustainable form of support.

Rental subsidies will act as a stabilizing measure—helping refugees move out of temporary arrangements, focus on livelihoods, and build the foundations for independent living. Small-scale rehabilitation will target property owners hosting refugees, with improvements offered in exchange for hosting arrangements that include tenure security guarantees. This supports more vulnerable refugees, reinforces community-based coping mechanisms, and offers a pathway toward affordable, longer-term housing.

In parallel, UNHCR will advocate for refugees’ inclusion in national affordable housing schemes, including favourable loan conditions and first-time homeownership programs.

planEntities.name: Inclusion of refugees in national social protection and housing systems is supported through the maintenance, transformation, and phased decommissioning of collective accommodation, with pathways to specialized and community-based housing solutions for individuals with heightened vulnerabilities.
planEntities.parentName: OU 1.4_Rights holders, in particular from vulnerable groups, are empowered to access and claim for quality public services
planEntities.description:
UNHCR will continue to work closely with the MLSP and local public authorities to maintain a limited number of RACs, ensuring that they provide safe, dignified, and protection-sensitive conditions for individuals with heightened vulnerabilities. These include older persons, persons with disabilities, Roma refugees, and others who are unable to live independently due to physical, psychosocial, or social support needs.

Support will be provided for the ongoing maintenance and rehabilitation of these RACs, including essential repairs, accessibility improvements, and the provision of equipment to meet minimum living standards. UNHCR will also strengthen site management and coordination, with an emphasis on inclusive practices, accountability, and capacity-building of RAC staff. This will include training on protection-sensitive service delivery, inclusive communication, and referral mechanisms for specialized support.

As part of the broader RAC transition and decommissioning strategy, UNHCR will support the progressive consolidation of temporary RACs and facilitate the transition of residents to more sustainable, long-term solutions. In coordination with the MLSP and development partners, UNHCR will advocate for and support the inclusion of vulnerable refugees in Moldova’s existing institutional care systems, residential services, and social housing stock, in line with the government’s deinstitutionalization and community integration policies. UNHCR will also collaborate with MLSP to strengthen case management and referral systems for highly vulnerable individuals, ensuring that their needs are adequately assessed and that transitions out of RACs are voluntary, informed, and protection-sensitive. Special attention will be given to Roma communities and others at risk of exclusion from mainstream services.

To promote long-term solutions, UNHCR will engage in strategic advocacy and resource mobilization to expand Moldova’s inclusive housing and care infrastructure. This includes promoting investments in specialized and community-based accommodation, with a focus on persons with disabilities, older persons, and Roma refugees.

planEntities.name: Child protection mechanisms are strengthened to ensure the identification, referral, and support of refugee children at risk, including survivors of violence, gender-based violence (GBV), and unaccompanied and separated children (UASC).
planEntities.parentName: OU 1.5_State institutions and CSOs ensure effective prevention and improved multisectoral response to address all forms of violence against women and girls, including harmful practices and discriminatory gender norms and stereotypes
planEntities.description:
UNHCR will work closely with the Ministry of Labor and Social Protection (MLSP), UNICEF, and key partners to enhance the capacity of Moldova’s national child protection system, ensuring that refugee and vulnerable Moldovan children have continuous and equitable access to essential services. This will involve capacity-building initiatives for child protection professionals, social workers, and local authorities to improve case management, referral mechanisms, and inter-agency coordination. Special attention will be given to the integration of refugee children and unaccompanied and separated children (UASC) into national child protection programs, ensuring they receive the same standard of care and protection as Moldovan children. Throughout this work, gender and disability mainstreaming will be systematically applied to ensure that girls and boys, including those with disabilities, are equally protected and supported.

UNHCR will support community-based child-friendly spaces, providing psychosocial support, safe spaces, and tailored services for children at risk of violence, neglect, exploitation, or family separation.Through protection desks, UNHCR and partners will support the identification of children at risk and ensure their referral to the national child protection system and access to child protection services, including systematic Best Interests Assessments (BIAs) for UASC. Additionally, UNHCR will assist in harmonizing legal and procedural frameworks to ensure that refugee children continue to be systematically included in Moldova’s national child protection policies and legal structures. Training for frontline service providers will emphasize inclusive and gender-sensitive approaches, focusing on mandatory reporting procedures, child protection case management, and the specific needs of children with disabilities, Roma children, survivors of abuse, and those at risk violence, neglect and/or abuse.

To guarantee long-term sustainability and equitable access to services, UNHCR will support the decentralization of protection services, ensuring that refugee and Moldovan children can receive support in urban and rural areas alike. Efforts will also focus on strengthening disaggregated data collection and monitoring systems, enabling authorities to track service delivery, identify protection gaps across population groups, and improve timely and inclusive responses. Through these interventions, UNHCR aims to contribute to a resilient, inclusive, and rights-based child protection system that meets the needs of all children.

planEntities.name: Access to quality health services for refugees and vulnerable host populations is reinforced through strengthened national health systems and coordinated multi-sectoral interventions, ensuring continuity of care.
planEntities.parentName: OU 1.2_Health, education and food systems are strengthened and become more resilient to ensure universal access and quality of services and respond to humanitarian needs
planEntities.description:
UNHCR will continue working with the Ministry of Health, WHO, UNAIDS, UNFPA, and health partners to ensure that refugees and vulnerable Moldovan populations (including Roma communities, persons with disabilities and older persons) have equitable access to essential health services. In 2025, UNHCR will support access to primary healthcare, emergency and trauma care, sexual and reproductive health (including clinical management of rape), immunization, perinatal care, mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS), and services related to gender-based violence (GBV). Support will also focus on HIV and STI prevention and harm reduction through community outreach activities, including peer support and information dissemination, particularly targeting hard-to-reach populations and groups at increased risk, such as LGBTIQ+ individuals, persons living with HIV, sex workers, and Roma refugees​. UNHCR, UNAIDS and local partners will continue supporting access to HIV-related services for key affected populations within the refugee community along with case management and psychosocial support. Also through local partners and in coordination with local public authorities, UNHCR will provide gynecological consultations for refugees.

To strengthen access to care, UNHCR, in close coordination with WHO, UNFPA and IOM, will continue supporting the inclusion of refugees in national health systems, including access to public health insurance through advocacy and technical support. UNHCR will also contribute to improved access to essential medicines, specialist consultations, rehabilitative and palliative care, and ensure that referral pathways to public services are functional and accessible. Outreach interventions, including mobile health teams and information sessions, will be reach underserved regions and populations with mobility challenges or barriers to health access, such as older persons and persons with disabilities​.

planEntities.name: Access to quality and specialized GBV services is enhanced through a survivor-centered and coordinated referral system, ensuring case management, legal aid, and psychological support across all regions of Moldova.
planEntities.parentName: OU 1.5_State institutions and CSOs ensure effective prevention and improved multisectoral response to address all forms of violence against women and girls, including harmful practices and discriminatory gender norms and stereotypes
planEntities.description:
UNHCR will continue to strengthen gender-based violence (GBV) prevention, response, and risk mitigation efforts by ensuring that refugees and other vulnerable populations, including Roma women, LGBTIQ+ persons, sex workers and persons with disabilities, have access to specialized and survivor-centered GBV services. This includes safe shelter, GBV case management, legal assistance, and mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS), delivered in coordination with government authorities, UN agencies, and civil society actors​. UNHCR will continue supporting the MLSP through technical capacity aiming at meeting the standards of the Istanbul Convention for service provision.

GBV services will be provided in four key locations across Moldova, including through support centers offering case management, gynecological consultations, legal aid, and psychosocial support. Mobile and community-based teams will enhance outreach, particularly to underserved areas and groups facing compounded barriers, such as Roma women and sex workers. UNHCR’s Roma-led partner will work to connect Roma GBV survivors to available services, recognizing the systemic discrimination and structural obstacles they may face. Legal services for GBV cases will be provided.

UNHCR will replicate good practices such as support to women-led organizations (WLOs) and the localization of the Girl Shine curriculum, which will be implemented with adolescent girls and their caregivers. The office will work on tailored communication materials on GBV and gender equality for Roma women, based on a 2024 study conducted with a WLO. Additionally, group psychosocial support and skills development workshops will continue, integrating content on mental health, sexual and reproductive health, and online safety, and creating safe spaces for survivors to seek help. UNHCR's Roma-led partner will carry out group activities with Roma women to provide them with life skills and information, empowering them to make decisions about their own lives.

planEntities.name: Social cohesion and refugee inclusion are enhanced through Participatory Community Projects (PCPs), Community Support Initiatives (CSIs), and the Cities of Solidarity initiative, fostering mutual understanding and resilience among refugees and host communities.
planEntities.parentName: OU 2.4_Government and non-government actors have strengthened capacities and resources to address the humanitarian crisis, sustain peace and security at the national and regional level and ensure access to justice for all
planEntities.description:
UNHCR will continue to promote social cohesion and community resilience by implementing Participatory Community Projects (PCPs) and Community Support Initiatives (CSIs) that foster engagement between refugees and host communities. These initiatives will include joint community-led projects, improvement of shared infrastructure, and rehabilitation of locally managed public spaces, ensuring that both communities collaborate to address shared needs. Projects will prioritize inclusive design and participation, with specific outreach to persons with disabilities, Roma community members, older persons, youth, women, boys and girls, in line with UNHCR’s commitment to age, gender, and diversity (AGD) inclusive programming​. UNHCR will continue to support Community Service Centers in key locations hosting refugees. 

Under the Cities of Solidarity initiative, UNHCR will continue working with municipalities to develop and implement local action plans that enhance refugee inclusion in social protection, employment, and local development programmes. These plans will be developed through participatory assessments and dialogue between local authorities, civil society, refugees, and vulnerable host community members, and will promote long-term urban resilience. UNHCR will provide technical assistance, financial support, and policy guidance to ensure that local action plans are inclusive of marginalized groups, including Roma and persons with disabilities, and reflect their specific needs and contributions​.

To further strengthen refugee participation in local decision-making, UNHCR will support the establishment of Refugee Committees in key locations and promote their formal inclusion in municipal structures and coordination mechanisms. These bodies will represent the diverse refugee population, including older persons, Roma, persons with disabilities, LGBTIQ+ individuals, and youth, ensuring their voices are reflected in local governance. UNHCR will also invest in capacity-building for refugee leaders, enabling them to engage in advocacy and community planning in a meaningful and sustained manner. These efforts will help build inclusive, cohesive, and accountable communities, in line with Moldova’s commitment to refugee protection and social inclusion.

planEntities.name: Access to employment, entrepreneurship, and financial services for refugees and stateless persons is improved through strengthened public-private partnerships, targeted skills development, and inclusive labor market support.
planEntities.parentName: OU 3.4_People of Moldova, in particular those left behind, have improved access to adequate protection and safe working conditions, knowledge, in-demand skills and resources to foster employability, competitiveness and entrepreneurship culture
planEntities.description:
UNHCR will promote the economic inclusion of refugees and stateless persons by supporting access to formal employment, entrepreneurship, and financial services. In coordination with the National Employment Agency (NEA), the Ministry of Labour and Social Protection (MLSP), and development actors, UNHCR will facilitate job placement, Romanian language classes, vocational training, and job counselling, with an emphasis on overcoming specific barriers faced by women, older persons, and persons with disabilities. Efforts will include expanding access to childcare options to better support the participation of female-headed households in the labor market.

To address broader structural barriers, UNHCR will support the recognition of qualifications, raise awareness among employers on refugee rights to work, and promote inclusive labor market policies. Collaboration with private sector stakeholders and financial institutions (such as the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development) will support entrepreneurship training and access to business development services, particularly for refugees with limited financial resources or who face intersectional discrimination, including Roma refugees and persons with disabilities​.

Economic inclusion initiatives will be embedded in broader inclusion strategies, including the Cities of Solidarity initiative, and implemented in partnership with local authorities. UNHCR will promote gathering evidence on the socio-economic indicators and area-based approaches that extend support to both refugees and host communities. These efforts will prioritize equity, ensuring that refugees of all ages, genders, and backgrounds are empowered to achieve self-reliance and contribute to Moldova’s socio-economic development​.

planEntities.description: Support to the Child Rights Ombudsperson office to raise awareness on children's rights, including gender-specific concerns, regularly producing comprehensive reports on key emerging issues affecting children, with a specific focus on gender-related matters (how it affects girls and boys), and monitoring the implementation of Convention on the Rights of the Child (CRC) recommendations to ensure independent  child rights monitoring.

planEntities.description: UNICEF works with the Ministry of Finance, local governments, and other line ministries to enhance the management of child-sensitive public finance management by increasing efficiency, transparency and equity and improving the impact of public spending on children. The technical support on budget analyses and advice will reflect the country’s demographics and, in particular, identify any systemic bias that disadvantages women and girls. A key advocacy objective will be protecting social spending in the context of economic contraction.

planEntities.name: ( UNICEF - NEW) Social Protection: an equitable, responsive, and adequately funded social protection system will address socioeconomic vulnerabilities and includes the most vulnerable families with children, including refugees.
planEntities.parentName: OU 1.1_Regulatory and policy framework that is evidence-informed and takes into account demographic trends promotes gender-responsive and human rights-based social protection and equal access to basic services
planEntities.description: Provide technical assistance to reform the social protection system by improving targeting, coverage and effectiveness in reducing child poverty. Opportunities for sustainable child grant schemes will be explored. It will be essential to ensure that any measures reduce the push factors for emigration and avoid damaging the country’s fragile economic model, which has been strongly affected by the global economic recession and the Ukraine crisis. Well-defined social protection approaches will be needed to mitigate the effects on children, on girls and boys, from environmental and climate change risks. Adequate child- and gender-responsive social services provision at the local level will be promoted through enhanced decentralized service planning and improved budgeting, financing, and delivering capacities for government entities and other stakeholders.

planEntities.name: (UNICEF - NEW) Nurturing care: Capacities of the primary health-care system, parents and communities strengthened to ensure continuing equitable nurturing care for all young children, including those facing risks to their survival and development.
planEntities.parentName: OU 1.2_Health, education and food systems are strengthened and become more resilient to ensure universal access and quality of services and respond to humanitarian needs
planEntities.description: Technical assistance to the Ministry of Health (MoH) in implementing routine and COVID-19 vaccination including integrating gender-sensitive approaches, conducting a behavioral insights research to identify gender-specific barriers and motivations, providing training for healthcare providers, ensuring inclusive information materials and addressing contraindications, and designing vaccination campaigns. Provided assistance includes assessing the implementation of Health Standards for Monitoring the Growth and Development of children and parenting skills, integrating BFHI indicators into accreditation standards for perinatal care, capacity building perinatal care providers in applying BFHI standards, conducting  building activities for perinatal care and primary healthcare professionals on identifying danger signs, promoting child development, breastfeeding, and encouraging shared responsibilities (engaging fathers and male caregivers) in Infant and Young Child Feeding (IYCF) and child care practices. Ensure mapping and establishment of inclusive, accessible, and cost-effective "Early Intervention services" that promote equitable access, address gender disparities, and support optimal development and well-being for both host and refugee children with developmental delays.

planEntities.description: Provision of technical assistance to the Ministry of Education and Research (MER) in the implementation of the Education Sector Plan (ESP) 2030, with a particular emphasis on increasing equitable access of adolescent girls and boys fostering inclusiveness, gender equality, resilience, WASH, digital transformation, and financial efficiency within the education sector, addressing the needs and rights of all women/girls, men/boys, and encompassing both development and humanitarian contexts

planEntities.name: (UNICEF - NEW) Justice for Children: Justice system will have the capacity and functional mechanisms to protect the rights of all children in contact with the law, shaping age - appropriate intersectoral mechanisms for prevention, response and rehabilitation.
planEntities.parentName: OU 2.4_Government and non-government actors have strengthened capacities and resources to address the humanitarian crisis, sustain peace and security at the national and regional level and ensure access to justice for all
planEntities.description:

•	Conduct public outreach and media campaign promoting positive use of the Internet and the role of the school community in support of a safer internet for children 
•	Support law enforcement, justice sector, and child protection specialists in preventing and responding to the needs of children victims and witnesses of crime and VNET as well as to child offenders

planEntities.name: (UNICEF - NEW) Child Protection: National authorities and families will have strengthened mechanisms and capacities to identify and deliver prompt, integrated and gender and age -responsive child protection services to address violence against children, prevent child - family separation and safeguard all children’s chances to grow up in a caring family environment.
planEntities.parentName: OU 1.5_State institutions and CSOs ensure effective prevention and improved multisectoral response to address all forms of violence against women and girls, including harmful practices and discriminatory gender norms and stereotypes
planEntities.description:
The program supports reform efforts to strengthen the child protection system to meet the challenges and provide care and protection for children and families, including refugees, by ensuring children's increased access to social services including: identification, evaluation, assistance, monitoring of unaccompanied/at risk refugee children, protection from violence, exploitation and abuse, social protection, and adequate family support. lt further strengthens children and youth empowerment and participation in decision-making processes and provides support to parents and families in caring for their children. The programme focuses on the most deprived and excluded children and address urban-rural issues and gender related disparities. The program also provides technical support towards enhanced local and national planning processes, strengthened data collection, evidence based policy making and enhanced monitoring of children needs and includes provision of gender-responsive support and social assistance transfers to eligible refugee households tailored to the specific needs and vulnerabilities of refugee women/girls, men/boys.
Main outputs refer to 
•	Ensuring sustainability of the "Family Support" social service and other services for families with children 
•	Strengthening the Social Service "Personal Assistance"  
•	Financial support for social services „Foster care”, „Family type homes for Children” and guardianship service			
•	Funding foster care families specialized in assisting of children at risk situation, including refugee 			
•	Financial support for the specialists in the social assistance system at the district/community level 
•	Strengthen the Barnahus type, integrated services for children victims and witnesses of crime
•	Develop and strengthen family support and parenting programmes and raising for and building gender-responsive parental practices and skills 
•	Building the knowledge and generate evidence to better understand specific needs, perceptions and experiences of parents and caregivers of children with disabilities
•	Increase leadership skills and knowledge of adolescent girls and women, dismantle negative gender social norms and improve access to GBV services

planEntities.name: (UNICEF - NEW) Adolescents Participation: Policies and gender-responsive mechanisms and social investments will be in place for adolescent empowerment, meaningful engagement and effective participation in relevant decision-making processes.
planEntities.parentName: OU 2.3_People of Moldova, in particular most vulnerable and marginalized, are empowered to claim and exercise their human rights and meaningfully participate in public and civic life, governance and decision-making processes
planEntities.description:
UNICEF in cooperation with the Ministry of Education and Research developed and costed the National Strategy on Youth 2030 inducing its action plan and key implementation programs. In line with the national strategic priorities, UNICEF and Cahul, Ungheni and Chisinau Municipalities developed and adopted local youth strategies and action plans. UNICEF supported development of youth-friendly guidelines for participation in school life and in community and trained district youth council and pupils’ councils on strategic planning and implementation, efficient participation in school committees and in LPAs decision making process. UNICEF built capacity of school management committees in 20 localities in Cahul and Ungheni rayons. The schools were provided with necessary policies and instructions on establishing pupils’ councils and managing pupils’ engagement and participation in decision making processes. 
UNICEF supported establishment of 9 local Youth Centres and two mobile teams of youth workers that are providing the full range of seven youth friendly services mandated by the application of the Minimum Quality Standards adopted by the Ministry of Education and Research.  UNICEF engaged and ensured that adolescents are empowered to claim for and shape youth friendly services and programs and have access to decision making processes. 2500 young volunteers’ members of pupils’ councils and centers were capacitated on peer-to-peer education, social innovation and civic engagement. This was possible as UNICEF organized two editions of the social innovation program UPSHIFT. During USPHIFT activities, 1400 adolescents benefited from a full cycle training on local mobilization, business development, startup management and implementation.  Working directly with 9 youth centers, UNICEF engaged 1,000 young volunteers in capacity building, outreach and peer to peer to 35,000 Moldovan and refugee adolescents and youth.

planEntities.name: Joint Action to Strengthen Human Rights in the Transnistrian Region
planEntities.parentName: OU 2.4_Government and non-government actors have strengthened capacities and resources to address the humanitarian crisis, sustain peace and security at the national and regional level and ensure access to justice for all
planEntities.description:
The programme will work on reducing inequalities for women and men, youth and children in the Transnistrian region, by ensuring that vulnerable right-holders are empowered to exercise their human rights and human rights defenders are able to claim and advocate for human rights. Under Output 1. Increased capacities of vulnerable right-holders to exercise their human rights the Programme is expected to achieve the following results: enhanced human rights skills and knowledge of vulnerable rights holders, strengthened institutional capacity of CSOs and informal groups, and improved service delivery of CSOs; Under Output 2. Improved systems and mechanisms for the respect, protection and fulfilment of human rights of vulnerable groups - enhanced human rights compliant regulatory framework, strengthened human rights institutions and improved service delivery as a result of advocacy actions from CSOs and human rights defenders; and under Output 3. Enhanced human rights culture in the Transnistrian region - enhanced human rights capacity of the media and raised human rights awareness.  
The current programme builds on the results of the previous phase of the One UN Joint Action, finalized in June 2022 and will consolidate and expand the results achieved in the area of awareness raising and development of social community-based services.

The Overall Objective of the project is to contribute to human capital development in the Republic of Moldova, improving quality and relevance of education and lifelong learning opportunities for all, for better matching the labor market demands. planEntities.description:
1. Collecte et diffusion de données fiables:
Rassembler et diffuser des données claires sur le nombre d'entreprises détenues par des femmes.
Identifier les secteurs dans lesquels elles sont représentées.
Déterminer les obstacles qui entravent leur croissance.

2. Soutien à GEM:
Permettre à GEM d'utiliser ces informations et la visibilité qu'elle développe pour soutenir son programme de plaidoyer politique (concernant les obstacles aux entreprises détenues par des femmes).
Établir des partenariats stratégiques avec des associations de femmes entrepreneurs.
3. Mobilisation de donateurs et développement de projets techniques:
Identifier des bailleurs de fonds (tels que la GIZ) et développer des propositions de projets techniques dans ce domaine.
Ces projets devront s'attaquer aux obstacles auxquels sont confrontées les entreprises détenues par des femmes tout en renforçant parallèlement les capacités des organisations d'employeurs et d'entreprises représentatives opérant dans ce secteur (GEM et ses associations membres).
Appui à l'établissement de la monographie du FHORM

Le projet vise à renforcer la participation civique et politique des jeunes et des femmes malagasy pour une consolidation de la démocratie et de la paix à Madagascar à travers une démarche de renforcement de capacités et réseautage ainsi que la promotion d’un environnement institutionnel, social et légal favorable à leur implication effective dans les processus décisionnels et de la gestion des affaires publiques à tous les niveaux dans un contexte electoral et de renouvellement de  mandats pour des institutions clés au niveau national (exécutif et parlement) et locale (Communes); ce qui constitue une opportunité pour soutenir l’engagement des femmes et des jeunes, et contribuer ainsi à un changement transformationnel vers une société plus inclusive, résiliente et stable.

Programme conjoint: Renforcement d’une paix inclusive et durable dans le massif d’Andriry

Le projet vise à renforcer les acquis des interventions du PBF dans la zone située autour de la chaine de montagne de l’Andriry dans le sud de Madagascar, mais allant dans les communes encore plus éloignées, marginalisées et vulnérables aux conflits et aux tensions en mettant l’accent sur l’inclusion des communautés marginalisées vivant à l’intérieur du massif, qui ont jusqu’à maintenant eu très peu d’opportunité d’inclusion, de manière à promouvoir de manière durable la cohésion sociale dans l’ensemble de la zone d’intervention.

planEntities.description:
a) Renforcement et amélioration du cadre légal, réglementaire et institutionnel du secteur de l’énergie favorable à la réalisation de l’ODD-7 ; sensibles au genre et informés par les risques de catastrophes naturelles
b) Renforcement de capacité des acteurs étatiques en matière de réduction des dépenses publiques liées à l’énergie
c) Promotion de la cuisson propre et de l’efficacité énergétique dans la production et l’utilisation de l’électricité en milieu rural et péri-urbain
d) Électrification des infrastructures sociocommunautaires et établissements publiques pour assurer la continuité du service publique et la performance de l’administration
e) Renforcement du MIX Energétique par le pilotage de solutions innovantes d’exploitation du potentiel en énergie du pays : Hydroélectricité ; Biomasse, Hydrogène vert au service du développement
f) Investissements en solaire photovoltaïque ; Mini centrales éoliennes ; Centrales à biomasse etc.
g) Développement de l’industrie, de l’utilisation productive de l’énergie (UPE) par les groupements de femmes, associations ONGs et PME et augmenter leur résilience face aux chocs exogènes et aux changements climatiques
h) Le suivi et la réduction des émission de GES et la digitalisation du secteur de l’énergie
i) Mise en place des outils et mécanismes de sauvregardes environnementales et sociales
j) Mécanismes de Financement Innovants
k) Valorisation énergétique des déchets

planEntities.name: Strengthening the Implementation of National Biosafety Frameworks in Southern Africa
planEntities.parentName: Produit 4.2 - Tous les acteurs locaux et nationaux ont la capacité de produire, de coordonner les collectes, de gérer et d’utiliser efficacement les données, les recherches et les innovations favorisant la valorisation des ressources naturelles et des écosystèmes et leur gestion durable, inclusive et résiliente aux risques et au changement climatique tenant en compte des besoins spécifiques des hommes, des femmes, jeunes et personnes handicapées
planEntities.description:
"Global concerns about the risks of LMOs led to adoption in 2000 of the Cartagena Protocol on Biosafety, which came into force in 2003. Since the ratifications of the Protocol, there have been many interventions particularly from the GEF to assist Parties develop and implement their National Biosafety Frameworks to enable them meet their obligations under the international framework.
The overall goal of the project, “Strengthening the Implementation of National Biosafety Frameworks in Southern Africa (SINBF)” is to assist the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), Madagascar and Namibia to enhance and strengthen their national capacities through cooperative facilitative mechanisms for the implementation of the Cartagena Protocol on Biosafety and have functional, workable and transparent national biosafety frameworks by 2026.
In its preparatory phase, the project reviewed the biosafety related policies and legislation in each of the participating countries and analyzed each participating country’s strategic focus on biosafety. The analysis highlighted the strategic importance that biosafety issues are assuming in each country’s National Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP), other strategic policies and development plans. 
The project is designed to help the participating countries to enhance and strengthen their national capacities through cooperative and facilitative mechanisms for the implementation of the Cartagena Protocol on Biosafety  and to: a) Integrate biosafety into the national biotechnology strategies; b) Put in place a fully operational and responsive regulatory regime in line with their existing national laws and other international obligations is in place; c) Establish an efficient national system for handling requests on LMOs and decision-making; d) Put in place an effective national system for follow-up activities, namely monitoring, inspections and enforcement; e) Establish an active national system for public awareness and participation.
The project consists of three components. The first two, A and B are technical components whilst the third Component C is for project administration. The three components are as follows: 
Component A - Biosafety Regulatory Regimes and Policy 
Component B - Biosafety institutional systems
Component C - Project Administration, Monitoring and Evaluation 
The envisaged results of the project in the three participating countries are enhanced, strengthened and operational National Biosafety Frameworks."

planEntities.parentName: Produit 4.2 - Tous les acteurs locaux et nationaux ont la capacité de produire, de coordonner les collectes, de gérer et d’utiliser efficacement les données, les recherches et les innovations favorisant la valorisation des ressources naturelles et des écosystèmes et leur gestion durable, inclusive et résiliente aux risques et au changement climatique tenant en compte des besoins spécifiques des hommes, des femmes, jeunes et personnes handicapées
planEntities.description: This project aims to support the Government of Madagascar and development partners in designing a comprehensive National Clean Cooking and Reforestation Programme to be supported by the OPEC Fund and other partners. This initiative is expected to improve the living and health conditions of the Malagasy population by stimulating the development and adoption of innovative clean cooking solutions and revitalizing the degraded ecosystem as well as reducing the climate change effects in the country. The project leverages UNIDO's innovative Market Enabling Framework (MEF) to stimulate private sector investments in the clean cooking sector and its value chain for switching households from traditional fuels to clean and affordable cooking solutions at scale. The project will undertake necessary baseline studies and feasibility studies and propose pilot projects to demonstrate various technologies and business models as part of the National Clean Cooking Transition Program

planEntities.parentName: Produit 1.1 - Le pays dispose et met en œuvre une vision et des plans/stratégies nationaux et sectoriels valorisant et développant durablement les capitaux institutionnel, humain, économique et naturel, en faveur de tous et en particulier des plus vulnérables, des jeunes, des femmes et des personnes handicapées
planEntities.description: Dans le cadre de son mandat, le GMCP s'engage à aider les États membres à promouvoir la coopération aux niveaux régional et international et à renforcer les capacités de lutte contre la grande criminalité organisée dans le domaine maritime. Il s'agit d'apporter un soutien technique, matériel et infrastructurel aux autorités chargées de l'application de la loi, des poursuites et de la détention. Comme les crimes maritimes dépassent presque toujours les frontières internationales, toutes les interventions mettent fortement l'accent sur la coopération régionale et sont menées dans le cadre du Forum de l'océan Indien sur la criminalité maritime (IOFMC).

planEntities.name: La capacité des agences d'application de la loi maritime est améliorée en vue de renforcer l'action de l'Etat en mer
planEntities.parentName: Produit 1.3 - Les institutions au niveau central et déconcentré/décentralisé sont outillées pour fournir des services publics de qualité, équitables et accessibles à tous ; en particulier aux femmes, aux jeunes, aux personnes handicapées et aux groupes marginalisés
planEntities.description: Le GMCP renforce les capacités d'application du droit maritime (MLE) par le biais de cours de formation et d'un encadrement à temps plein. Il s'agit notamment d'une formation sur la connaissance du domaine maritime (MDA), nécessaire pour détecter et localiser les navires suspects, ainsi que sur des sujets fondamentaux de l'application du droit maritime, tels que la création d'une culture de la maintenance et les compétences en matière de matelotage. Ces fondements servent de base à la formation régionale avancée, à une série de cours de formation de qualification et à la formation continue des instructeurs au niveau national. Les formations sur l'application de la législation portuaire se poursuivent dans toute la région afin de garantir que les délits commis dans les ports fassent l'objet de poursuites efficaces. Compte tenu de la nature internationale des crimes maritimes, les interventions comprennent la coordination du Partenariat de la Route du Sud dans le cadre de l'IOFMC, la fourniture d'une plateforme de coordination entre les agences nationales de lutte contre la drogue, les agences MLE et les partenaires internationaux, ainsi que la formation et le soutien à l'équipement du Centre régional de fusion de l'information maritime.
