planEntities.description:
El Centro de Excelencia UNODC–INEGI tiene como objetivo contribuir a la generación, el desarrollo y la homologación de información estadística de calidad sobre el delito y la justicia penal en los países de América Latina y el Caribe. A través de este esfuerzo, el Centro busca fortalecer la manera en que las instituciones de seguridad pública, procuración y acceso a la justicia toman decisiones, diseñan estrategias e implementan acciones orientadas a la prevención del delito, la construcción de paz y la defensa del Estado de Derecho.
Este proyecto es un referente regional para la producción de evidencia estadística y analítica oportuna, promoviendo el uso de metodologías armonizadas, estándares internacionales y marcos conceptuales comparables. Mediante asistencia técnica, orientación metodológica y desarrollo de productos de conocimiento, UNODC apoya a las oficinas nacionales de estadística y a las instituciones de justicia penal para mejorar la calidad, consistencia y utilidad de los datos administrativos, encuestas de victimización y otros instrumentos estadísticos.
Asimismo, el Centro impulsa la innovación metodológica y el fortalecimiento de capacidades en temas prioritarios como la trata de personas, los homicidios y feminicidios, la violencia de género, el crimen organizado, los flujos ilícitos y el uso de nuevas tecnologías para el análisis estadístico. De esta manera, el proyecto contribuye a una toma de decisiones más informada y basada en evidencia, alineada con el mandato de UNODC y los compromisos internacionales de los países de la región.

planEntities.name: Agentes de Cambio
planEntities.parentName: Producto 1.3. Organizaciones de la sociedad civil, colectivos de víctimas, periodistas, personas defensoras y personasen situación de movilidad han fortalecido sus capacidades de incidencia, exigibilidad y acceso a mecanismos de justicia.
planEntities.description:
El proyecto Agentes de Cambio busca reducir la vulnerabilidad que representa la trata de personas en comunidades indígenas y afromexicanas de México, mediante el fortalecimiento de capacidades comunitarias y el empoderamiento de las mujeres como agentes clave de prevención, detección temprana y acompañamiento. La iniciativa parte del reconocimiento de que los contextos de exclusión estructural, desigualdad de género, barreras lingüísticas y limitado acceso a servicios incrementan los riesgos de trata de personas en estos territorios.
El proyecto promueve un enfoque comunitario, intercultural y basado en derechos humanos, que articula la prevención del delito con el fortalecimiento de liderazgos locales y la mejora de los mecanismos de atención y canalización de casos. A través del trabajo con Casas de la Mujer Indígena y Afromexicana (CAMIAs), autoridades locales y organizaciones comunitarias, se busca consolidar capacidades sostenibles para la identificación, documentación, denuncia y seguimiento de casos de trata de personas.

planEntities.name: ALERT: Acceso a Laboratorios, Evidencia, Respuesta y Trazabilidad
planEntities.parentName: Producto 2.1. Instituciones de seguridad pública han fortalecido sus políticas, protocolos operativos, herramientas de gestión y metodologías de medición para la prevención y atención del delito, con enfoques de derechos humanos, género, seguridad humana, territoriales y de curso de vida.
planEntities.description: El proyecto ALERT busca colaborar con las instituciones mexicanas para hacer más eficiente el desmantelamiento de laboratorios clandestinos, un paso crucial para construir investigaciones penales en materia de fabricación ilícita de drogas sintéticas.  A través de los siguientes ejes de acción, ALERT busca ser una respuesta al problema de la fabricación y tráfico ilícito de drogas sintéticas al: a) estandarizar procedimientos para reducir riesgos químicos y biológicos en el personal de primera línea; b) impulsar la coordinación interinstitucional; y c) reforzar la adecuada detección, manipulación y registro de indicios de modo que cada intervención contribuya de manera efectiva a la judicialización de los delitos correspondientes.

planEntities.name: Disrupción de las Redes Delictivas de la Trata de Personas con el Lavado de Activos
planEntities.parentName: Producto 2.1. Instituciones de seguridad pública han fortalecido sus políticas, protocolos operativos, herramientas de gestión y metodologías de medición para la prevención y atención del delito, con enfoques de derechos humanos, género, seguridad humana, territoriales y de curso de vida.
planEntities.description:
El proyecto Disrupción impulsa la coordinación nacional y regional para la investigación de la trata de personas, mediante la integración sistemática del enfoque de inteligencia financiera y la vinculación de este delito con el lavado de activos. La iniciativa parte del reconocimiento de que la trata de personas es un delito altamente lucrativo, operado por redes criminales complejas cuya identificación y desmantelamiento requiere el análisis de flujos financieros, esquemas de ocultamiento y mecanismos de legitimación de recursos ilícitos.
El proyecto convoca a fiscalías, unidades de inteligencia financiera, instituciones bancarias y sector privado, para cerrar brechas operativas en la investigación integral de ambos delitos. A través del desarrollo de procedimientos estandarizados, guías técnicas y espacios de coordinación, se busca mejorar la detección de tipologías financieras asociadas a la trata de personas y fortalecer el uso de la información financiera en los procesos de investigación penal.

planEntities.name: GRIDS: Programa Global de Interdicción Rápida de Sustancias Peligrosas (JIFE)
planEntities.parentName: Producto 2.1. Instituciones de seguridad pública han fortalecido sus políticas, protocolos operativos, herramientas de gestión y metodologías de medición para la prevención y atención del delito, con enfoques de derechos humanos, género, seguridad humana, territoriales y de curso de vida.
planEntities.description: El Programa Global de Interdicción Rápida de Sustancias Peligrosas (GRIDS), una iniciativa de la Junta Internacional de Fiscalización de Estupefacientes (JIFE), que brinda asistencia técnica a los Estados Miembros para reducir de manera medible el tráfico de sustancias peligrosas, con énfasis en nuevas sustancias psicoactivas y opioides sintéticos de uso no médico. El Programa apoya a los países mediante el fortalecimiento de capacidades, el intercambio oportuno de información y la cooperación operativa entre Gobiernos. Asimismo, GRIDS promueve la articulación entre autoridades competentes y el sector privado para mejorar la detección, el análisis y la respuesta frente a amenazas emergentes asociadas al uso indebido y desvío de precursores químicos.

planEntities.name: Monitoreo de Cultivos Ilícitos en Territorio Mexicano
planEntities.parentName: Producto 2.1. Instituciones de seguridad pública han fortalecido sus políticas, protocolos operativos, herramientas de gestión y metodologías de medición para la prevención y atención del delito, con enfoques de derechos humanos, género, seguridad humana, territoriales y de curso de vida.
planEntities.description:
El proyecto de Monitoreo de Cultivos Ilícitos complementa las capacidades del Gobierno de México para generar información confiable, sistemática y basada en evidencia sobre la ubicación, extensión y rendimiento de los cultivos ilícitos de amapola y la producción de goma de opio. Esta información constituye un insumo estratégico para el diseño, implementación y evaluación de políticas públicas integrales orientadas a combatir tanto la oferta como la demanda de drogas.
El proyecto se basa en una metodología científica y validada por la Sección de Investigación y Análisis de Tendencias de UNODC a nivel global, que combina trabajo de campo, análisis geoespacial y cooperación interinstitucional, permitiendo al Estado mexicano contar con datos objetivos y comparables a lo largo del tiempo. Además, las cifras obtenidas como parte del trabajo de campo y el análisis correspondiente, son reportadas para la elaboración del Informe Mundial sobre Drogas de UNODC.

planEntities.name: AIRCOP: Programa de Comunicación Aeroportuaria
planEntities.parentName: Producto 2.1. Instituciones de seguridad pública han fortalecido sus políticas, protocolos operativos, herramientas de gestión y metodologías de medición para la prevención y atención del delito, con enfoques de derechos humanos, género, seguridad humana, territoriales y de curso de vida.
planEntities.description:
El Programa de Comunicación Aeroportuaria (AIRCOP) busca reforzar la capacidad nacional para prevenir, detectar e investigar el tráfico ilícito de drogas y otras mercancías ilícitas en el transporte aéreo, mediante el fortalecimiento de la cooperación interinstitucional y el intercambio oportuno de información operativa. El programa se enfoca en mejorar la comunicación y coordinación entre las autoridades aeroportuarias, de seguridad y de control fronterizo.
El programa promoverá el uso de herramientas de comunicación segura y el establecimiento de canales permanentes de cooperación entre instituciones nacionales e internacionales, además de diversas capacitaciones especializadas. De esta manera, AIRCOP contribuye a una respuesta más ágil y eficaz frente a las amenazas asociadas al tráfico ilícito en el transporte aéreo, fortaleciendo la seguridad aeroportuaria y la cooperación internacional.

planEntities.name: CCP: Programa Global de Control de Contenedores
planEntities.parentName: Producto 2.1. Instituciones de seguridad pública han fortalecido sus políticas, protocolos operativos, herramientas de gestión y metodologías de medición para la prevención y atención del delito, con enfoques de derechos humanos, género, seguridad humana, territoriales y de curso de vida.
planEntities.description:
El Programa Mundial de Control de Contenedores tiene como objetivo mejorar las capacidades de perfilamiento, análisis de riesgo e inspección de contenedores en puertos estratégicos de México, con el fin de combatir el tráfico de drogas sintéticas, precursores químicos y otras mercancías ilícitas, así como fortalecer la cooperación interinstitucional entre autoridades responsables del control portuario. El programa parte del reconocimiento de que los puertos marítimos constituyen nodos críticos para el comercio internacional y, al mismo tiempo, puntos de alto riesgo para la operación de redes de delincuencia organizada transnacional.
A través del establecimiento y fortalecimiento de Unidades de Control Portuario, se busca mejorar la coordinación entre autoridades aduaneras, fuerzas de seguridad y otras instituciones relevantes, incrementando la eficacia de las inspecciones y la calidad de la información utilizada para la toma de decisiones basadas en inteligencia.
Asimismo, el programa impulsa el intercambio de información a nivel regional e internacional, contribuyendo a una respuesta más integrada frente a las dinámicas cambiantes del tráfico ilícito y al fortalecimiento de la seguridad de las cadenas de suministro

planEntities.name: Programa Global de Delincuencia Marítima
planEntities.parentName: Producto 2.1. Instituciones de seguridad pública han fortalecido sus políticas, protocolos operativos, herramientas de gestión y metodologías de medición para la prevención y atención del delito, con enfoques de derechos humanos, género, seguridad humana, territoriales y de curso de vida.
planEntities.description:
El programa tiene como objetivo cooperar con los Estados Miembros para identificar y analizar las tendencias emergentes en delitos marítimos y sus vínculos con diversas manifestaciones de la delincuencia organizada transnacional, así como fortalecer las capacidades de las autoridades competentes para prevenir, detectar e investigar estos delitos. 
En México, el Programa se implementa a través de su componente de formación especializada en fronteras marítimas y puertos, en estrecha coordinación con la Secretaría de Marina, priorizando las acciones en los puertos de Salina Cruz y Coatzacoalcos, los dos ejes principales del Corredor Interoceánico del Istmo de Tehuantepec. Las acciones se orientan a reforzar las capacidades técnicas y operativas del personal naval para la identificación, manejo y mitigación de riesgos asociados a sustancias peligrosas, materiales de doble uso y otros elementos vinculados a delitos marítimos complejos

planEntities.name: Desarticulación de Redes Delictivas vinculadas al Comercio Estratégico
planEntities.parentName: Producto 2.2. Instituciones responsables de la seguridad han diseñado e implementado estrategias integrales e intersectoriales de prevención del delito y construcción de paz.
planEntities.description:
El Programa busca complementar y reforzar las capacidades técnicas de actores nacionales para mejorar la prevención y disrupción de redes criminales vinculadas al comercio estratégico. Reconoce que estas redes aprovechan las cadenas de suministro y los flujos comerciales para facilitar actividades ilícitas, lo que requiere respuestas especializadas y coordinadas.
El proyecto tiene un enfoque integral que combina la detección de redes delictivas, el fortalecimiento de capacidades técnicas y la promoción de la cooperación interinstitucional. En conjunto con actores clave de industrias estratégicas, busca la identificación de riesgos asociados al comercio estratégico y en el diseño de respuestas para prevenir el uso indebido de bienes, tecnologías y materiales sensibles.
Asimismo, impulsa el intercambio de buenas prácticas internacionales, contribuyendo a una respuesta más eficaz frente a las redes delictivas transnacionales, protegiendo la seguridad nacional y la integridad del comercio legítimo.

planEntities.name: Mujeres Imparables: libres y seguras contra la Trata
planEntities.parentName: Producto 2.2. Instituciones responsables de la seguridad han diseñado e implementado estrategias integrales e intersectoriales de prevención del delito y construcción de paz.
planEntities.description:
El proyecto Mujeres Imparables: libres y seguras contra la Trata implementa una estrategia integral de capacitación y sensibilización en materia de trata de personas en sus múltiples modalidades en el municipio de Puebla. A través de distintas actividades, se brindarán conocimientos para identificar los distintos tipos y modalidades de la trata de personas, brindar una atención inicial adecuada a víctimas mujeres, adolescentes y niñas, y promover su participación en acciones de prevención y adopción de la campaña Corazón Azul contra la Trata de Personas.
A través de procesos formativos teóricos y vivenciales, se sensibilizó a liderazgos comunitarios y actores locales sobre la importancia de la detección temprana, la canalización oportuna y la corresponsabilidad social en la erradicación de la violencia contra mujeres, adolescentes y niñas.

planEntities.name: Prevención de la delincuencia organizada en el sector de la aviación
planEntities.parentName: Producto 2.2. Instituciones responsables de la seguridad han diseñado e implementado estrategias integrales e intersectoriales de prevención del delito y construcción de paz.
planEntities.description:
La alianza entre UNODC México y Aeroméxico integra los criterios ESG (ambiental, social y gobernanza) con la misión institucional de promover la justicia y la protección de los derechos humanos. Esta colaboración fortalece la integridad del sector aeronáutico y turístico a través de dos ejes prioritarios: 
Prevención de la trata de personas en el sector turístico - El eje tiene como objetivo generar una caracterización integral de las fuentes de información disponibles sobre la trata de personas en el sector turístico en México, con el fin de identificar patrones, riesgos y modalidades específicas del delito en este ámbito. A través de un estudio integral y el uso de inteligencia de datos, la iniciativa desarrolla herramientas preventivas y de política pública bajo un enfoque de derechos humanos, fortaleciendo la capacidad de respuesta de todos los actores de la cadena turística. 
Prevención del tráfico de vida silvestre - Este eje extiende la colaboración hacia la seguridad ambiental mediante el diseño de un protocolo técnico para la detección del tráfico ilícito de especies. La iniciativa dota al personal de mecanismos de actuación inmediata y capacitación especializada, asegurando que las rutas aéreas cuenten con blindajes efectivos para proteger la biodiversidad y prevenir el uso del sector para el tráfico de flora y fauna silvestre.

planEntities.name: QALAT: Garantía de Calidad en el Tratamiento de los Trastornos por Uso de Drogas en América Latina y el Caribe
planEntities.parentName: Producto 2.2. Instituciones responsables de la seguridad han diseñado e implementado estrategias integrales e intersectoriales de prevención del delito y construcción de paz.
planEntities.description:
El proyecto de QALAT busca fortalecer las capacidades de los Estados Miembros para establecer sistemas que aseguren servicios de tratamiento basados en evidencia científica, principios éticos y estándares de calidad. Promueve la aplicación de los Estándares Internacionales para el Tratamiento de los Trastornos por Uso de Drogas y de herramientas para la evaluación de los servicios, con el fin de garantizar una atención integral, accesible y equivalente a la ofrecida para otras condiciones de salud.
Sus actividades se centran en Morelia, Michoacán, buscando fortalecer la atención del uso problemático de sustancias psicoactivas en la región Purépecha. Se espera favorecer la adaptación de los modelos de atención a la cosmovisión y las prácticas comunitarias locales, fortaleciendo la participación de liderazgos comunitarios.

planEntities.name: RASTROS: Acción Regional para apoyar a los países en la lucha contra la trata de personas perpetrada a través de operaciones de estafa en línea
planEntities.parentName: Producto 2.2. Instituciones responsables de la seguridad han diseñado e implementado estrategias integrales e intersectoriales de prevención del delito y construcción de paz.
planEntities.description: El proyecto RASTROS busca fortalecer la capacidad de las autoridades policiales y fiscales de los países beneficiarios para detectar, investigar y enjuiciar, a nivel nacional y regional, casos de trata de personas vinculados a la criminalidad forzada en operaciones de estafas en línea. El proyecto busca desarrollar indicadores específicos de trata de personas vinculada a la criminalidad forzada en operaciones de estafas en línea, incorporando aportaciones de sobrevivientes y otros actores clave, con el fin de identificar patrones y dinámicas en las fases de reclutamiento, coacción y explotación. Con esto, se impartirá formación práctica basada en casos reales para fuerzas del orden, incluidas unidades cibernéticas, expertos forenses y fiscales, orientada a la recopilación efectiva de pruebas y a la construcción de casos sólidos de trata de personas con fines de criminalidad forzada.

planEntities.name: Viaje Seguro
planEntities.parentName: Producto 2.2. Instituciones responsables de la seguridad han diseñado e implementado estrategias integrales e intersectoriales de prevención del delito y construcción de paz.
planEntities.description:
El proyecto tiene como objetivo contribuir a una industria turística más segura y sostenible en Quintana Roo y en ciudades sede de la Copa Mundial de la FIFA 2026, mediante la prevención y detección de la trata de personas en contextos turísticos. La iniciativa trabaja con actores clave del sector, particularmente anfitriones/as de Airbnb y empresas prestadoras de servicios turísticos para identificar señales de alerta, comprender los riesgos asociados a la trata de personas y actuar de manera oportuna y responsable.
El proyecto promueve un enfoque de corresponsabilidad y alianzas público-privadas, reconociendo el papel estratégico del sector de alojamiento y plataformas digitales en la protección de visitantes y residentes. A través de espacios de diálogo, capacitación y desarrollo de herramientas prácticas, se busca generar una cultura de prevención que integre la seguridad, los derechos humanos y la sostenibilidad como ejes centrales de la actividad turística.

planEntities.name: Estrategia de Implementación de Sistema de Transporte por Cable — Tuxtla Gutiérrez, Chiapas
planEntities.parentName: Producto 5.3. Instituciones responsables del desarrollo urbano, la vivienda y el ordenamiento territorial han fortalecido sus capacidades para implementar políticas públicas que mejoran el acceso a vivienda adecuada y promueven ciudades inclusivas, resilientes y con protección del patrimonio cultural, particularmente en territorios y poblaciones en situación de vulnerabilidad.
planEntities.description: Asesorar al Ayuntamiento de Tuxtla Gutiérrez, en el Estado de Chiapas, en la definición de la estrategia de implementación de un sistema de transporte por cable para la Zona Metropolitana de Tuxtla Gutiérrez. La asesoría comprende la definición del mecanismo contractual y de los contratos a incluir en cada fase, la determinación de los mecanismos de financiamiento potenciales y el análisis de los actores involucrados, así como la conformación de una matriz de riesgos y la elaboración de una hoja de ruta crítica con los hitos principales del proyecto.

planEntities.name: Asistencia Técnica al Gobierno de la Ciudad de México, en la Implementación del Proyecto para la Modernización de la Línea 1 y la Estructuración de una Línea del Sistema de Transporte Colectivo
planEntities.parentName: Producto 5.3. Instituciones responsables del desarrollo urbano, la vivienda y el ordenamiento territorial han fortalecido sus capacidades para implementar políticas públicas que mejoran el acceso a vivienda adecuada y promueven ciudades inclusivas, resilientes y con protección del patrimonio cultural, particularmente en territorios y poblaciones en situación de vulnerabilidad.
planEntities.description: El proyecto consiste en la asistencia técnica y el acompañamiento especializado al Gobierno de la Ciudad de México y al Sistema de Transporte Colectivo (STC). Su intervención se estructura a través de componentes estratégicos que abarcan el fortalecimiento y la transferencia de capacidades de gestión a la Oficina de Gestión de Proyectos (PMO) del STC, el asesoramiento continuo de gestión y mitigación de riesgos bajo esquemas de contratos de niveles de servicio, el monitoreo y diseño de estrategias de comunicación institucional, la consolidación de la memoria técnica y sistematización de lecciones aprendidas de la Línea 1, y el soporte técnico, económico y financiero para la estructuración de la licitación de la Línea 3. El propósito final es fortalecer la capacidad institucional del STC para que la modernización integral de la Línea 1, que comprende la renovación de vías, la puesta en servicio de trenes nuevos y modernizados y la migración tecnológica del sistema de control, se ejecute bajo estándares internacionales de calidad, transparencia y sostenibilidad, contribuyendo a un transporte público más seguro, accesible y eficiente y a una ciudad más inclusiva y resiliente.

planEntities.name: Asistencia Técnica para la Licitación de los Nuevos Trenes de Pasajeros para el Sistema Ferroviario Mexicano
planEntities.parentName: Producto 5.3. Instituciones responsables del desarrollo urbano, la vivienda y el ordenamiento territorial han fortalecido sus capacidades para implementar políticas públicas que mejoran el acceso a vivienda adecuada y promueven ciudades inclusivas, resilientes y con protección del patrimonio cultural, particularmente en territorios y poblaciones en situación de vulnerabilidad.
planEntities.description: El proyecto brinda asesoría y acompañamiento técnico al Gobierno de México para la estructuración, diseño y evaluación de las licitaciones públicas internacionales de la primera flota de trenes de pasajeros de las nuevas líneas del sistema ferroviario nacional, en los tramos AIFA a Pachuca, México a Nuevo Laredo y México a Nogales. Comprende el análisis de interoperabilidad con la infraestructura existente, la redacción de términos de referencia técnicos y de mantenimiento, la definición de niveles de servicio, indicadores de desempeño y penalizaciones, y la creación de herramientas de evaluación de ofertas con acompañamiento a los comités. La asistencia es técnica y no vinculante, sin gestión directa de las licitaciones ni intervención en la firma de contratos ni en la obra física.

planEntities.name: Implementación del Programa de Acción Estratégica del Gran Ecosistema Marino del Golfo de México
planEntities.parentName: 10.3. Instituciones públicas, gobiernos subnacionales, actores productivos y comunidades locales han fortalecido sus modelos, capacidades y mecanismos de gobernanza territorial para la gestión sostenible de ecosistemas y la transición hacia esquemas resilientes, bajos en carbono y circulares.
planEntities.description: Implementar el Programa de Acción Estratégica del Gran Ecosistema Marino del Golfo de México para la gestión sostenible y la conservación de sus recursos, estableciendo mecanismos de sostenibilidad y gobernanza que permitan mantener y escalar los impactos del proyecto a nivel regional.

planEntities.name: STBP IH Diagnostics 2
planEntities.parentName: Producto 5.1. Instituciones del sector salud han fortalecido sus capacidades para ampliar el acceso equitativo y de calidad a servicios integrales de salud, nutrición y bienestar, con enfoque de curso de vida, particularmente para poblaciones en situación de vulnerabilidad.
planEntities.description: Adquisición y entrega de equipos médicos de medición, observación y pruebas, así como diagnósticos IH.

planEntities.name: Centros Multiservicios de Inclusión y Desarrollo de Movilidad Humana y Desarrollo Territorial.
planEntities.parentName: Producto 5.4. Instituciones del sector social, económico y de desarrollo han fortalecido sus capacidades y la articulación intersectorial para implementar intervenciones orientadas a la disminución de la pobreza y las desigualdades.
planEntities.description: El Proyecto Centros Multiservicios de Inclusión y Desarrollo busca ampliar la capacidad instalada para atender las necesidades relacionadas con la movilidad humana en México, aprovechando las áreas de experiencia del Sistema de las Naciones Unidas para complementar y apoyar las iniciativas del Estado mexicano en la promoción de derechos, el acceso a servicios esenciales y la integración socioeconómica de personas refugiadas y migrantes. De igual manera, se buscará implementar iniciativas de la estrategia sobre el retorno de personas migrantes mexicanas, México TEABRAZA, principalmente en los componentes de reintegración, vinculación laboral y acceso a los servicios disponibles. Esta contribución representa la puesta en marcha de un nuevo modelo de movilidad humana en México, respaldado por la visión y la experiencia del Sistema de las Naciones Unidas. UNOPS liderará la implementación general junto con la SRE y la Coordinación Residente, y estará a cargo de la implementación de los servicios de adquisiciones, así como de la contratación con las agencias de la ONU y de la coordinación programática general, el monitoreo y la evaluación del proyecto.

Montenegro.name: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations

planEntities.name: Support to smallholder livestock farmers through FFSs and development of the national cattle breeding strategy
planEntities.parentName: 1.1.Private sector growth, economic transformation and decent jobs
planEntities.description: One of the objectives of this project is increased local capacity for cattle breeding through the development of a national cattle breeding strategy. This project will also strengthen community ties and foster collaborative efforts among farmers and local advisory services through Farmer Field School (FFS) approach aiming at creating a more resilient and supportive farming community where knowledge and resources are shared for mutual benefit.

planEntities.name: Support to creating preconditions for implementation of the LEADER approach
planEntities.parentName: 1.1.Private sector growth, economic transformation and decent jobs
planEntities.description:
The National Program for the Development of Agriculture and Rural Areas in Montenegro under IPARD III, along with the expected adaptation in 2024 of the amendment of the Law on Agriculture and Rural Development, lays the path for the full introduction of the EU LEADER approach and should prepare the grounds for future registration of LAGs in Montenegro. However, as the country is taking the first steps towards the implementation of LEADER in accordance with the EU policy and legislation, there is a lack of technical and administrative capacity to implement it. Thus, it is necessary to strengthen capacity and knowledge on national and local levels in order to make Montenegro ready for the implementation of the EU LEADER approach. 

FAO Action aims to strengthen capacities and enabling environment at national and local levels to implement the LEADER approach and establish Local Action Groups for the benefit of increased competitiveness and economic development in rural areas of Montenegro. The project is designed to prepare the Montenegrin rural actors for implementation of LEADER approach both at the national and local levels, specifically through capacity building for LAGs creation and functioning.

planEntities.name: Enhance strategic frameworks for the AFOLU sectors and support the initiation of the second National Forest Inventory of Montenegro
planEntities.parentName: 1.2 Mitigation and adaptation for DRR
planEntities.description:
Despite progress in resilience building, Montenegro faces data deficits and lacks specific baseline information and monitoring systems for effective climate planning. This gap hinders the integration of AFOLU sectors into the NDC update and future climate strategies. Without enhanced data collection and inter-sectoral cooperation, Montenegro risks failing to meet its climate targets and commitments.
The Readiness Proposal aims to address these gaps by improving data collection and institutional capacities. Key barriers include limited multi-stakeholder dialogue, insufficient specific data and monitoring systems, lack of awareness among national institutions, outdated forest inventory methodologies, and limited private sector engagement in climate investment. This initiative seeks to improve Montenegro’s ability to respond to climate challenges by enhancing data collection, fostering multi-stakeholder cooperation, and building institutional capacities. These efforts are crucial for achieving the country’s climate goals and ensuring sustainable development in the face of increasing climate impacts.

planEntities.name: Support with the integration of an ecosystem approach to fisheries management in Skadar Lake
planEntities.parentName: 1.3 Management of  infrastructure, cultural and natural resources
planEntities.description:
As EU candidate countries, both Albania and Montenegro are required to align with the EU Water Framework Directive, which mandates maintaining or restoring good ecological status in the lake. 
Efforts to implement modern and sustainable management of fisheries resources are hindered by administrative, technical, and financial constraints. These challenges are further complicated by the lake's cross-border status, as effective management requires cooperation between Montenegrin and Albanian authorities to align environmental standards and regulatory measures.
The requested assistance would address these gaps by strengthening transboundary cooperation and supporting the development of a simplified framework for a fishery monitoring system. This initiative aligns with national objectives facilitating Montenegro's and Albanian’s commitment to environmental sustainability and rural economic development which will in turn support the countries in their accession to EU by aligning with EU standards and practices. The project would integrate gender-sensitive practices by involving local communities, including women, in decision-making processes. The Blue Transformation roadmap recognizes the importance of aquatic food systems as drivers of employment, economic growth, social development and environmental recovery, which all underpin the SDGs.
Overall, the FAO's support in strengthening bilateral institutional collaboration under the Cooperation agreement in the fields of maintenance and joint management of fisheries in Lake Skadar and the river Bojana, and establishment of simplified monitoring system would provide the necessary technical support for the sustainable management of Skadar Lake’s fisheries, directly contributing to the long-term socio-economic resilience of local communities and environmental preservation in the region. The project thus serves the objectives of FAO Blue Transformation efforts aiming at promoting sustainable and resilient aquatic food systems.

Montenegro.name: International Organization for Migration

planEntities.name: Assisted Voluntary Return and Reintegration (AVRR)
planEntities.parentName: 2.3  Mixed migrations
planEntities.description: Within the Assisted Voluntary Return and Reintegration (AVRR) programme, IOM works with national and international partners in both, the host country and the country of origin, to ensure that beneficiaries willing to return to their countries of origin are able to travel in a safe and dignified manner - from host country to their final destination in country of origin.  Beneficiaries will be supported to return to their country of origin by organizing all travel arrangements including flight bookings, facilitating the issuance of travel documents when required in cooperation with the authorities of origin and/or host countries, carrying out airport clearance and other procedures as necessary, making transit and reception arrangements, facilitating pre-migration health checks, informing migrants of their travel schedules and entitlements (return allowances, luggage allowances). Additionally, upon their return to the country of origin, based on criteria associated with reintegration needs and vulnerability, beneficiaries are provided with tailored reintegration assistance in an individualized, timely and effective manner. Those not provided with reintegration assistance will continue to receive counselling and onward referral where feasible.

planEntities.name: Enhancing Migration Response and Service Delivery in Montenegro

planEntities.name: Strengthening the national response to combat trafficking in persons and smuggling of migrants in Montenegro
planEntities.parentName: 4.6. Combating corruption and organized crime
planEntities.description: This initiative aims to strengthen Montenegro’s national response to trafficking in persons and smuggling of migrants by enhancing institutional capacities, fostering multi-sectoral coordination, and utilizing technology to address emerging challenges. It includes capacity-building activities for different responders, development of tool for victim identification, and public awareness campaigns on online recruitment methods and labor exploatation. Additionally, emphasis is placed on improving policy frameworks and operational procedures to ensure a victim-centered and proactive approach to combating TIP and smuggling.

planEntities.description: The objective of this project is to contribute to the effective operationalisation of return systems in the WB  and strengthened institutional capacities to lead rights-based return management operations, in line with international and EU standards. Namely, the project is to establish an effective return mechanism compliant to EU standards, at both legislative and operational levels.

planEntities.name: REGIONAL MIGRATION GOVERNANCE PROGRAMME (RMGP)
planEntities.parentName: 2.3  Mixed migrations
planEntities.description:
The overall objective of the proposed programme is to enhance safe, orderly, and rights-based migration and border management in Türkiye and the Western Balkans.
The programme aims to strengthen institutional capacities, improve legal frameworks, and promote cooperation among key stakeholders to address migration challenges effectively. It also emphasizes the protection of vulnerable migrants, including victims of trafficking, by enhancing identification, referral pathways, and access to protection services. The project supports the development of regular mobility pathways to facilitate economic growth and integration of migrants. Overall, RMGP aims to create a sustainable and coordinated approach to migration management, aligning with international standards and best practices.

The project has a particular focus on women journalists. Convening representatives of UN Member States, civil society, NHRI, UN and government pre-UPR review and after treaty body reviews to advocate for implementation of human rights standards and of recommendations.

planEntities.name: Strengthening knowledge of the UNCT and partners on developments and incidents of hate speech and advocacy to tackle the phenomenon

Provide technical assistance in the implementation of activities supported by the 2024-2025 PBF project to strengthen social cohesion, particularly to strengthen the capacity of the Protector of Human and Minority Rights and Freedoms and civil society to monitor the implementation of human rights instruments for prevention, analysis and early warning; technical advice on prevention of hate speech with full respect for the freedom of expression; support for the design and implementation of human rights education; and technical advice for strategic use of UN human rights mechanisms for monitoring, analysis and advocacy to increase respect for rights and enhance social cohesion.

planEntities.name: Ending the Denial of Legal Capacity of Persons with Disabilities in Montenegro
planEntities.parentName: 4.1. Rule of law and justice for all
planEntities.description: The programme seeks to facilitate system-level change in Montenegro by proposing amendments to a legal framework that violates rights and by establishing a system that supports persons with disabilities to exercise their rights. It seeks to address harmful practices and significantly reduce cases of legal capacity denial for persons with disabilities. Thereby, it will end the discrimination persons with disabilities face and empower them to exercise their human rights. A new service for supported decision-making will be designed and piloted to drive system-level change. The project will establish a scalable model to enable persons with disabilities, particularly those with intellectual and psychosocial disabilities, to access structured, sustainable support mechanisms that enable them to make decisions on an equal basis with others.

planEntities.name: Improving capacities for integrated climate-resilient flood risk management (FRM) and enhancing resilience of vulnerable communities in Drin River Basin in Montenegro, Albania and North Macedonia

planEntities.name: E-Social: Leveraging Digital Solutions to Enable Efficient Social Protection of the Vulnerable
planEntities.parentName: 2.1 Social and child protection
planEntities.description:
UNDP has supported the Government of Montenegro in establishing the national Integrated Social Welfare Information System (e-Social IS), which has been in operation since January 2015. Being the backbone of the country's social protection system, e-Social is in charge of processing nearly all social protection entitlements. 

To provide timely and efficiently cash transfers and social services and to ensure that new legislative solutions are duly enforced, it is necessary to continuously invest in the e-Social IS. To that end, the project envisages key components, including the development of new and upgraded functionalities (including its e-services for citizens), IS refactoring, capacity-building support for IS administrators and end-users, as well as its maintenance to ensure medium-term sustainability. The project will also provide, until 31 December 2027, procurement of additional server capacities as well as regular hardware supply replacement and maintenance in 36 remote locations.

Not least, the project will better equip grassroots actors to raise public awareness of past crimes, including dialogue and exchanges amongst and between a wide range of stakeholders, especially youth and future opinion leaders in order to contribute to increasing a shared understanding of the crimes committed during the 1990s conflicts on the territory of the former Yugoslavia.

public sectors; supporting and accelerating women’s entrepreneurship; investing in the care economy and promoting more equitable distribution of
unpaid care work; bridging the digital gender divide and promoting participation of women
in STEM careers.

planEntities.name: Enhancing capacities for gender mainstreaming in the work of the Government - United in Gender Equality
planEntities.parentName: 4.2. Public administration, data and digitalisation
planEntities.description: This upcoming Action has been designed to contribute to the enhance capacities to promote gender equality and introduce gender mainstreaming in the work of the Government offering technical assistance and addressing specific needs. Action is designed to collect evidence, analyze perceptions, policies and practices, including the role and position of existing gender equality infrastructure. Action will enhance capacities for gender mainstreaming in strategic framework and state programmes and development plans, offering technical gender expertise and gender mainstreaming support, that will be informed by gender analyses, guided by tools, methods and knowledge products, assuring dialogue and boosting political will and commitment of the highest-ranking public officials to assure gender mainstreamed approach.

planEntities.name: More efficient people-centred public administration
planEntities.parentName: 4.2. Public administration, data and digitalisation
planEntities.description:
In order to create an environment for efficient communication between citizens and public administration, the Project will build capacities of the Ministry of Public Administration (MPA) as the key institution in coordinating the public administration reform. The Project will focus on two outputs: 
1) standardizing functioning of public institutions, which is a part of the administration lacking normative framework, and upgrading institutional capacities of the MPA, as a coordinating body of public administration reform, reflected in the Output 1 - Increased efficiency through standardized functioning of public administration.
2) standardization of human-centered e-services and further development of digital skills of the citizens and businesses, reflected in the Output 2 - Increased digital efficiency of public administration serving citizens and businesses.

planEntities.name: Enhancing citizens’ trust in institutions and building resilient communities (Joint PBF project)
planEntities.parentName: 4.5. Countering hate speech
planEntities.description:
The UNDP component of the Joint UN Programme aims to foster trust in institutions and build resilient communities by enhancing social cohesion and promoting gender equality. It emphasizes the empowerment of both women and men, particularly younger generations, to engage in meaningful civic activities that protect human rights and advance social cohesion. Key activities include organizing local dialogues in five communities to address trust issues, divisive narratives, and social cohesion, and designing actionable recommendations.

A Social Cohesion Innovation Lab will pilot solutions developed during these dialogues, working with civil society and local governments. Institutional capacities at local and national levels will be strengthened to develop, adopt, and implement pledges for social cohesion, informed by local dialogue outcomes. The initiative also supports parliaments at both the national and local levels to enhance oversight and promote dialogue on social cohesion.

The program aims to monitor hate speech, violence, and divisive narratives, building capacity for evidence-based policymaking using behavioral insights and public perception surveys. It includes advocacy to counter hate speech and foster trust and collaboration. Additionally, the program empowers women politicians and decision-makers with skills and knowledge to advance gender equality and address gender-based challenges effectively.

planEntities.description: This project aims to strengthen the Human Resource Management Authority  in gender mainstreaming and establish gender equality standards within the public sector. It focuses on enhancing HRMA’s capacity to integrate gender equality through consultations, providing guidance and tools to create an Action Plan addressing gender gaps, and fostering ongoing dialogue on gender issues within public administration. The goal is to position HRMA as a leader in promoting gender inclusivity and equality across the public sector, contributing to a more equitable and inclusive work environment. planEntities.description: The overall objective of the UNDP project “Support to HIV and building resilient and sustainable systems for health (RSSH) in Montenegro” is to maintain low HIV prevalence in Montenegro by supporting prevention services to key populations and support services and strengthening health system resilience and sustainability. Its specific objective/outcome is to foster a safe, supportive, and inclusive environment for people living with HIV and those at increased risk, reduce gender inequality in the HIV response, establish an effective prevention system for high-risk groups, institutions, and the general population, ensure equitable access to affordable treatment and care, and implement robust monitoring, coordination, and partnership mechanisms for a sustainable response to HIV/AIDS.

It aims to empower civil society and youth to actively engage in decision-making and citizen oversight, while stimulating governments to create a supportive policy, legal and financial environment for civil society and youth. The specific objective of the Action: Strengthened coordination between governments and CSOs in the Western Balkans contributes to a more conducive environment for CSOs and youth, upheld by transparent public financing, a supportive legal framework, and increased civic engagement in policy design, delivery, and monitoring.

planEntities.name: Capacity Development of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs

The Engagement Facility 2024-2027 will be implemented under the Direct Implementation Modality, through an agreed set of initiatives agreed by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Montenegro and UNDP and in line with the committed strategic priorities in the UNDP’s Country Programme for 2023-2027.

The Engagement Facility 2023-2027 will be implemented under the Direct Implementation Modality, through an agreed set of initiatives agreed by the Office of the President of Montenegro and UNDP and in line with the committed strategic priorities in the UNDP’s Country Programme for 2023-2027.

planEntities.name: Public and Private Finance for Development (PPFD) program - ReWaste – Reducing Waste and Rethinking Waste Management in Montenegro
planEntities.parentName: 1.1.Private sector growth, economic transformation and decent jobs
planEntities.description:
In 2025, UNDP Montenegro launched the ReWaste Project under the regional Public and Private Finance for Development (PPFD) initiative, focusing on sustainable waste management. Waste management remains a critical issue for Montenegro, particularly under Chapter 27 of its EU accession process, which mandates improved waste separation, recycling, and infrastructure modernization. Despite progress, the country faces challenges, including low recycling rates, financial constraints, and inefficient landfill dependency. The ReWaste Project directly addresses these issues by modernizing waste infrastructure, enhancing institutional capacity, and fostering private and public investments to accelerate Montenegro’s transition towards a circular economy.
OBJECTIVES
The ReWaste Project seeks to transform Podgorica’s waste management system into a sustainable, modern, and EU-compliant model. The project focuses on three key areas:
•	Optimizing Waste Management Operations: Enhancing institutional efficiency, financial sustainability, and knowledge exchange with Slovak experts.
•	Attracting Investments for Infrastructure: Developing feasibility studies and investment plans to modernize waste processing facilities.
•	Promoting Public Awareness & Participation: Engaging citizens and businesses in waste separation and recycling through digital incentives and behavioural change campaigns.

planEntities.name: Circular Transition and Responsible Business Conduct in Montenegro (UNDP part)
planEntities.parentName: 1.1.Private sector growth, economic transformation and decent jobs
planEntities.description:
The overarching goal of the project is to enhance Montenegro’s circular economy by fostering the application of responsible business conduct at the enterprise level, encouraging industrial symbiosis, a collaborative approach where businesses utilize waste and by-products from their processes. This approach seeks to address critical challenges of decent work at the enterprise level, including inefficient resource use, high waste generation, and limited awareness of circular economy principles among stakeholders. By promoting resource-sharing, reducing environmental impacts, and improving economic efficiency, the project directly aligns with Montenegro’s national development priorities, EU accession goals (particularly Chapter 27 on environmental protection), and global commitments under the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and the Paris Agreement.  
The envisaged Outcome is an increased adoption of industrial symbiosis practices and RBC/HRDD frameworks across selected clusters and MSMEs in Montenegro, ensuring gender-responsive benefits
This project will drive industrial symbiosis and circular supply chain integration by equipping MSMEs with digital tools, capacity-building programs, and policy support to enhance better working conditions for workers, resource efficiency, and MSME productivity.  
The outcome is envisaged to be achieved through three complementary project outputs that will be implemented in close collaboration between UNDP and ILO.

planEntities.parentName: 2.1 Social and child protection
planEntities.description: In Montenegro, persons with disabilities continue to face systemic barriers that limit their full participation in social, economic, and public life. The project aims to consolidate and operationalize Montenegro’s transition to a unified, human-rights–based disability assessment and social protection system. Building on the achievements of Phase I (2020–2025), the project will move from legal and policy formulation to implementation—translating the newly adopted Law on Unified Disability Assessment into practice and introducing the Inclusive Allowance as a single, needs-based cash benefit for persons with disabilities. By combining legal reform, institutional capacity development, and digital innovation, the project will complete Montenegro’s transition to a modern, inclusive, and rights-based disability determination and social protection system. It will enable more than 60,000 persons with disabilities to access their rights more easily and equitably, while enhancing the efficiency, transparency, and accountability of public institutions in line with the UN CRPD, EU accession commitments, and the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development. Project specifically supports implementation of Reform Agenda measure 3.1.3 Reforming social and child protection system for more effective, efficient, and transparent use of public funds specifically step 3: One single inclusive and unified disability-related cash transfer covering all rights of a given beneficiary and processed through an electronic system in place.

planEntities.name: Support to UNEP/MAP-GEF-Funded MedProgramme for Removal of PCB and Mercury Wastes in Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Montenegro and Tunisia (UNEP/MAP-GEF-Funded MedProgramme)
planEntities.parentName: 1.3 Management of  infrastructure, cultural and natural resources
planEntities.description:
Under the GEF-funded MedProgramme, two complementary activities were implemented for Montenegro during the 2025–2026 period, addressing priority chemical pollution hotspots and supporting the environmentally sound management of persistent organic pollutants.

The first activity concerns the implementation of a Small-Scale Funding Agreement focused on the environmental assessment of contamination at the Port of Bar. This SSFA represents a continuation of earlier assessment work conducted in Montenegro, which examined contamination levels in harbour sediments at Tivat Bay and Risan Harbour. The previous SSFA included the analysis of PCBs, mercury, other heavy metals and organic substances, and revealed contaminant concentrations exceeding threshold values at specific sampling points in Tivat Bay. These findings highlighted the need for further site-specific assessment and potential remediation measures. Building on this evidence base, the current SSFA aims to further characterize contamination at the Port of Bar while also supporting the development of an environmental sound management plan for monitoring and remediation actions in Tivat Bay. Through this activity, Montenegro contributes to Component 1, Output 1.1 of the GEF MedProgramme Child Project 1.1, which targets the management of persistent organic pollutants in identified Mediterranean hotspots, in line with the UNEP/MAP Programme of Work and Budget.

The second activity is implemented through an Implementing Partner Services Agreement between UNEP/MAP and UNOPS and focuses on the environmentally sound management and disposal of PCB waste in Montenegro. Under this regional agreement, approximately 77 tons of PCB-contaminated equipment and oils from Montenegro are being safeguarded, collected, transported and exported for environmentally sound disposal in compliance with international standards, including the Basel Convention. This activity forms part of a wider regional effort covering Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Montenegro and Tunisia, contributing to the phase-out and elimination of PCBs by March 2026 under Child Project 1.1. The agreement supports Montenegro’s obligations under the Stockholm Convention, where PCBs are listed as persistent organic pollutants due to their severe impacts on human health and the environment.

Implementation of the IPS Agreement follows a coordinated approach between UNEP/MAP and UNOPS. UNEP/MAP facilitates communication with national authorities, provides assessment results, inventories and environmental management planning outputs developed under the MedProgramme, and supports the follow-up of critical approvals such as HSSE plans and Basel Notifications. UNOPS leads on technical validation, development of specifications for waste collection and disposal, procurement of contractors, and operational coordination on the ground. During the implementation phase, UNEP/MAP supports monitoring through a national expert in Montenegro, ensuring close coordination with government authorities and timely resolution of any challenges that may affect project delivery.

Together, these two activities strengthen Montenegro’s capacity to assess, manage and remediate chemical pollution hotspots, contribute to the environmentally sound management of PCBs, and support the achievement of Sustainable Development Goals related to chemicals and waste management, human health, water quality and marine protection.

planEntities.name: Enabling labor market access to persons under the Law on International and Temporary Protection of Foreigners
planEntities.parentName: 2.2. School to work transition and employability
planEntities.description:
In 2024/25, UNHCR sustained its efforts to facilitate labor market access for asylum seekers. A significant advocacy focus was on reducing the waiting period for asylum seekers to gain employment rights from nine months post-application. The authorities have acknowledged the validity of this proposal, and it is anticipated that the legislative framework will be amended accordingly in 2026.
UNHCR also intensified its collaboration with the Employment Agency, resulting in the creation of joint informational materials to be disseminated to all individuals under UNHCR's mandate, thereby enhancing their awareness of employment process and opportunities. Additionally, UNHCR addressed fundamental issues such as the recognition of foreign diplomas in partnership with the Ministry of Education and funded small-scale language learning initiatives.

planEntities.parentName: 2.3  Mixed migrations
planEntities.description: By the end of 2025, the Ministry for Human and Minority Rights prepared draft new Strategy for Social Inclusion of Roma and Egyptians, to replace previous 2021-2025 Strategy, whose validity expired. All UNHCR inputs are fairly incorporated in the draft Strategy and UNHCR will support line institutions to implement Strategy activities that are UNHCR's mandate.

planEntities.name: Support Ministry of the Interior to amend the Law on Foreigners, and harmonize other legislation accordingly
planEntities.parentName: 2.3  Mixed migrations
planEntities.description: In 2022 Montenegro started to amend its Law on Foreigners to strengthen the statelessness determination procedure, as well as other issues relevant for persons of concern to UNHCR, such as: issuing of visas for a person in family reunification procedure; access to labor market for persons granted international protection; etc. In addition, number of laws needs to be harmonized with the Law on Foreigners, to recognize stateless persons as beneficiaries of that law, thus creating condition for effective access to rights for persons granted stateless status. The draft amendments to the law has been prepared by the MoI, through cooperation with UNHCR. The draft Law is expected to be adopted in early 2026.

planEntities.name: Support line institutions to improve the standards in access to territory and asylum procedure in line with the UNHCR's and Montenegrin Ombudsman's findings from the 2022/23 partnership projects
planEntities.parentName: 2.3  Mixed migrations
planEntities.description: While Montenegro is a positive example in the region in relation to access to territory, the Ombudsman/UNHCR projects implemented in 2022 and 2023 provided clear indicators on where the focus should be put in the following period. As the outcome, the Border Police of Montenegro and UNHCR posted a 6-languages poster (Montenegrin, English, Arabic, Farsi, Russian and Spanish) in all sea/land/air border crossings, with information to interested persons on possibility to apply for asylum in Montenegro. The poster contains QR code that leads to UNHCR hotline and HELP page, containing additional information on asylum system of Montenegro and assistance that a person can get if s/he decides to apply for asylum. In addition, the Border Police opened possibility for registration of asylum intention in all police stations in Montenegro, in line with the 2018 asylum law. Other Ombudsman's recommendations, related to capacity building of Border Police, will be included in UNHCR's training and advocacy activities.

planEntities.name: Facilitate the certificate recognition for refugees to ensure that their prior learning was recognized and valorized in education and employment
planEntities.parentName: 3.2. Quality education
planEntities.description:
Following UNHCR's advocacy efforts, the Ministry of Education, Science, and Innovation prepared amendments to the Law on Recognition of Foreign Diplomas and Qualifications, adopted by the Parliament in 2025. These amendments are opening possibility for adoption of by-law to the amended Law, to secure that refugees cannot always obtain all the documents necessary for the recognition of foreign diplomas as required by regular procedures. During 2026, UNHCR expects to work with the education ministry on the above mentioned by-law.
Consequently, the Ministry of Education has started collaborating with the Council of Europe to determine the manner of establishing qualifications and skills for refugees who do not possess the respective educational certificates (prior test). UNHCR will continue to make significant effort to contribute to the adoption of this procedure.

planEntities.name: Technical and expert support to the Administrative Court of Montenegro, Bar Association and Ombudsperson to work with asylum seekers, refugees and stateless persons/persons at risk of statelessness
planEntities.parentName: 4.1. Rule of law and justice for all
planEntities.description: The Administrative Court of Montenegro is the 2nd instance institution in the asylum procedures and the 3rd instance institution in the statelessness determination procedure. Work with asylum seekers, refugees and stateless persons/persons at risk of statelessness pose different challenges to the court: from interpretation services, to more specific knowledge on different topics (country of origin information, unaccompanied and separated children, family reunification cases, credibility assessment, etc.). During 2023-2025, UNHCR organized several workshops for judges of the Administrative Court and the Bar Association, to facilitate discussion on several asylum related topics. The Ombudsperson is the main national human rights institution whose role in access to territory and detention facilities is of utmost importance for asylum seekers, refugees and stateless persons/persons at risk of statelessness. In 2024, UNHCR and the Ombudsperson renewed Memorandum of Understanding to define cooperation in the area of joint interest, such as border monitoring.

planEntities.name: Technical and expert support to the Ministry of Justice to secure access to state funded free legal aid scheme for vulnerable persons and group of persons
planEntities.parentName: 4.1. Rule of law and justice for all
planEntities.description: As per the 2011 Law on Free Legal Aid, state funded free legal aid covers a number of court procedures for socially vulnerable persons, but it does not cover judicial procedure for determination of date and place of birth of persons born at home, as well as all administrative procedures, including refugee status determination procedure and statelessness determination procedure. Refugees and persons missing birth registration are among the most vulnerable groups of persons in Montenegro, who often does not speak Montenegrin language and live on margins of society. Due to that reason, the Law on Free Legal Aid needs to be amended to introduce above mentioned specific procedures in the state funded free legal aid scheme. In addition, a tailor made information material needs to be produced to introduce these categories of persons with the benefits and possibilities of the state funded free legal aid scheme in procedures that they need to initiate. On that way Montenegro will implement recommendations of the UN Committee against torture, issued in the 2022 report on Montenegro. In 2025, the UN Human Rights Committee recommended to Montenegro to amend the Law on Free Legal Aid to introduce birth registration, statelessness determination and refugee status determination procedures in the state funded free legal aid system. Also, the Law should be amended to enable state funding to NGOs registered for provision of free legal aid.

planEntities.description: Provided capacity building support to the Curriculum Revision Team for Pre-Primary and Primary Education with particular focus on ESD policy, climate change education and sustainability. UNESCO supported Mongolia in strengthening institutional capacity for Education for Sustainable Development (ESD), climate change education, and sustainability to align Mongolia’s educational policies with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Key initiatives include preparing ESD Roadmap, enhancing policy dialogue, integrating climate change education into curricula, and promoting sustainable practices. By fostering intersectoral collaboration and capacity-building, UNESCO helps Mongolia address environmental challenges and build a sustainable future. This partnership is part of UNESCO’s broader strategy to support national priorities and sustainable development in Mongolia.

planEntities.name: 1.2.6 Strengthened Institutional capacity in education policy, planning statistics and monitoring of SDG4 progress and national benchmarks
planEntities.parentName: Output 1.2 - Education system and institutions have the capacity to offer inclusive learning, including early childhood education, to all children and young people, life skills, comprehensive sexuality education and smooth transition from education to labour market, especially to the vulnerable, including in emergency situations
planEntities.description:
UNESCO-UIS provided technical support to Ministry of Education to prepare SDG4 bench-mark value for 2025 and 2030. UNESCO has been instrumental in supporting the Mongolian government to set benchmark values for the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). This collaboration focuses on aligning national priorities with the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development. UNESCO provided technical assistance, data collection, and analysis to help Mongolia monitor progress on SDG4 indicators. By strengthening Mongolia’s capacity to track and achieve these goals, UNESCO ensured that the country can make informed policy decisions and effectively mobilize resources to meet its development objectives.

UNESCO and Ministry of Education jointly launched the Global Education Monitoring Report (GEMR) 2023 in Mongolia on 20 September 2024. The event gathered over 70 participants (female 30) from Mongolian Government, research institutes, universities, international agencies, private sector, civil society organizations, NGOs and other education stakeholders. The joint launch event provided a platform for showcasing Mongolia’s innovative strategies while fostering dialogue and cooperation among regional and international stakeholders. The event fostered a shared understanding of the strategic priorities for education technology, emphasizing the need for inclusivity, teacher empowerment, and alignment with global education goals, particularly SDG 4. These initiatives are expected to significantly enhance educational outcomes, bridge the digital divide, and contribute to both national and global education goals.

planEntities.description:
UNESCO-UIL organized the “Capacity-Building Workshop: Empowering Cities to Become Key Players for Lifelong Learning Advancement” from 21 to 25 October 2024 in Shanghai, People’s Republic of China. 
The workshop was designed for selected UNESCO Member States from Asia and the Pacific and Africa. A high-level team from Mongolia joined the workshop. During the workshop, nine country teams comprising national and municipal policymakers will engage with in-depth learning materials and collaborate with other participants and experts to develop learning city strategies. Activities covered all strategic areas of learning city development, as outlined in the Key Features of Learning Cities publication and addressed key thematic areas such as sustainable development and climate action, where learning cities play a leading role.

planEntities.description: Conducted a Regional Study on “Digitalization of Higher Education”. The has explored the good practices and challenges as well. Based on the research results, students are moderately prepared for the digital transition in higher education. The self-assessment scores indicate that while students have developed a solid foundation in essential digital skills such as Technology Proficiency, Social Media Usage, and Internet Awareness, there is still room for improvement, particularly in areas like Content Creation and Management. Additionally, the current levels of proficiency suggest that to fully capitalize on the benefits of digital education, students need to be further empowered, particularly in refining their skills in content creation, data management, and critical evaluation of online resources. Strengthening these areas will ensure that students are not just participants in the digital transition but are also well-equipped to thrive in a fully digital academic environment.

To respond to the increasing risks of online sexual exploitation, abuse and bullying, jointly with relevant authorities and with information and communication technology companies, UNICEF will pursue a holistic approach from the policy level to capacity-building on digital literacy among boys, girls, adolescents, caregivers, professionals and policymakers. 
Child protection will closely work with the education sector. Safe schools approach to ending violence will be promoted. UNICEF will support capacity building of teachers to apply positive discipline practices and promote a culture of zero-tolerance against any forms of corporal punishment. Mandatory reporting of child protection concerns will be promoted as well.

planEntities.parentName: Output 4.2 - Improved mechanisms and processes in place to effectively prevent and remedy violence and harassment against women and children, persons with disabilities, and human trafficking and promote gender equality, through frequent policy reviews, rigorous advocacy and outreach
planEntities.description:
UNICEF will support legislative reform and policy dialogue and influence the alignment of national laws and policies with international norms and standards as well as their enforcement. UNICEF will work with MLSP in strengthening cross sectoral linkages and enhance inter-ministerial and inter-sectoral dialogue and collaboration in both humanitarian and development contexts. 
UNICEF will also support the development and implementation of standards and oversight mechanisms and the monitoring of, and accountability for, child protection-related child rights violations. There will be a strong focus on supporting national and local authorities to improve their own skills in budgeting, monitoring, and tracking of the expenditure for child protection services. 
UNICEF will also support integration of disaggregated administrative data as part of broader national statistical systems and its use for policymaking and will build the capacity of relevant stakeholders to collect data in ethnical and responsible manner for the best interests of children. This will help child protection actors manage data for case management, incident monitoring and programming monitoring. 
Modelling, testing and expansion of child protection services will be supported with a focus on preventive approaches including parenting. It will further the roll-out of case management, information management through IMS and referral systems and foster a coherent continuum of services across Social Welfare, Justice, Health and Education sectors, as well as strengthening coordination mechanisms. 
Following the reimagine justice agenda, UNICEF will focus on justice for children adapting the interconnected and mutually reinforcing six actions to achieve just, peaceful and inclusive societies (SDG 16) for all children. UNICEF will support legal empowerment for children to effectively claim their rights, promote free legal aid for children, support the integration of social work and child specialization within the justice sector, and intersectoral coordination and collaboration. Prevention and early intervention in child offending, diversion and the use of alternatives to detention will be prioritized. 
UNICEF will work with Government and the ICT sector to ensure all child survivor of sexual violence, abuse or exploitation receive justice, and continue its support in the development of comprehensive legal frameworks to protect children from all forms of online or technology-facilitated sexual abuse and exploitation. UNICEF will support development and implementation of standards and oversight mechanisms of supervision and accountability. Strengthening of child protection workforce will be equally supported with a focus on preventive approaches and in monitoring the function of the workforces for quality assurance purposes.

Il vise à renforcer les capacités institutionnelles en matière de gouvernance éthique de l’IA, et dresser un diagnostic à 360° de l’écosystème national de l’IA, notamment dans les axes économique, éducatif, juridique, et infrastructurel.
L’initiative soutient un processus multipartite associant institutions publiques, experts nationaux, société civile et secteur académique, et contribue à structurer un cadre national de gouvernance responsable de l’IA (ODD 9.5; 16.6;  16.7).

planEntities.description:
HCR (1.	Former les services sociaux nationaux et régionaux (MASEF/DRASEF, Taazour, acteurs locaux) sur l’identification des réfugiés vulnérabilités, et l’orientation vers les filets sociaux existants.
2.	Accompagner l’intégration des réfugiés dans le Registre Social national, en poursuivant l’appui méthodologique, technique et digital au processus de collecte, d’actualisation et d’interopérabilité des données.)
3.	Développer des outils digitaux de suivi et de gestion des cas sociaux, compatibles avec les systèmes nationaux, afin d’assurer la traçabilité et le référencement harmonisé des réfugiés vulnérables.
4.	Appuyer la formation des OSC et structures communautaires sur les référencements, la gestion des cas de vulnérabilité extrême, et le rôle du communautaire dans la prévention des risques sociaux.
5.	Soutenir la transition vers des filets sociaux adaptatifs, en intégrant les besoins des réfugiés dans les analyses du Cadre Harmonisé, les mécanismes chocs et les réponses anticipatoires nationales.
PAM: Mise en place et/ou redynamisation des CoPil/CT de la SNPS au niveau régional (2 à 3 ateliers), sponsoriser un voyage d’échange d’expérience en Inde, appuyer l'elaboration de la loi-cadre de la PS, appuyer le PNLM pour le fonctionnement des CNC/CNP pour la prévention de la malnutrition, appuyer le RS à moderniser la plateforme de suivi de paiement digital, Appuyer un pilote MàJC à Kankossa, Appuyer l'integration des refugiés dans la BD du RS (enquetes, mission terrain), appuiyer le fonctionnement du DCAN par la redynamiser des CRSAN et l'operationalisation de son SSE, Actualiser et valider la strategie SBC du MASEF - National - ODD2
PNUD : Organisation des formations de renforcement de capacités des acteurs impliqués dans l'egalité du genre. ODD5.5
OIM: Mise en oeuvre de la feuille de route pour favoriser l'inclusion des migrants dans le systeme de protection sociale (Couverture nationale).
OIT: 
- Capitalisation de l'expérience d'accès à l'assurance maladie au profit des travailleurs 
indépendants.
- Renforcement de capacités actuarielle des cadres de la CNAS et de la CNSS 
- Appui à la mise en œuvre de la Strategie nationale d la Protection sociale (mobilisation expertise technique)
