planEntities.name: Develop and implement gender sensitive roadmap to reduce obesity
planEntities.parentName: Food security is enhanced for all – especially children, youth, women and other vulnerable groups – ensuring the transition of food, water and energy systems towards sustainability.
planEntities.description:
Mauritius with the support of the World Health Organization conducted three-day multisectoral consultative roundtable in April 2024 with participation of cross-section of stakeholders from government, the private sector, civil society and academia to come up with concrete actions to combat the obesity epidemic which affects 36.2% of the population. Using an evidence-based approach, the Obesity Roadmap prescribes a broad range of policy tools – political, fiscal and legal - aimed at tackling the obesogenic environment which encourages unhealthy lifestyles. The Mauritius Acceleration Plan to Stop Obesity 2024-2030 will address obesity which represents a significant public health burden in a country where NCDs account for 80% of the disease burden and 85% of mortalities.  Factors addressed in the Roadmap include the marketing of unhealthy foods and beverages, access to affordable and sustainable alternatives, fiscal policies, food labelling, early food environments, public food procurement, physical activity, health service delivery, public education and awareness, and country specific solutions.  the three major objectives of the Roadmap are as follows:(i) to reduce the prevalence of insufficient physical activity by 8% (57.6% to 49.6%) in children and adolescents (74.8% to 66.8%) from 2021 to 2030; (ii)to decrease consumption of unhealthy and ultra-processed foods and sugar sweetened beverages; and (iii) to increase coverage of obesity clinics to 50% through primary health centres and community based program to provide obesity prevention and management services.

The Roadmap will be implemented through a set of 5 priority actions and interventions:
•	Priority 1:Integrate obesity prevention and management in primary healthcare services and community outreach services.
•	Priority 2: Promote and create enabling environments to facilitate physical activity appropriate for all ages in different settings. 
•	Priority 3: Restrict the marketing of unhealthy, ultra-processed foods and sugar sweetened beverages.
•	Priority 4: Conduct behaviour change communication campaigns related to healthy diets, physical activity, and demand for health services.
•	Priority 5: Increase local agricultural production and accessibility to healthy foods to ensure availability and affordability of safe and quality agricultural products.  

The implementation of the specific activities under the five priorities as delineated in the Roadmap will further strengthen the interventions already in place through a multi-sectoral and coordinated approach to achieve the goal of reducing the obesity prevalence by 5% by 2030.  

Under Priority 1 and Priority 4 of the Obesity Roadmap, WHO provided technical support to conduct training of trainers and roll out of child growth assessment over a five-day intensive training.  The training empowered 90 health workers (Mauritius and Rodrigues) on appropriate child growth monitoring to enable the detection of wasting and stunting among children.  25 Health workers were empowered as trainers including 10 facilitators for training roll out across the five health regions in Mauritius.  The training of trainers further contributed to in-country capacity building (pool of trainers and facilitators) .  In the same vein, an assessment of the national nutrition information system was conducted in view of strengthening the national nutrition surveillance system in the Republic of Mauritius.  The findings of the assessment will help in standardizing and normalizing nutrition data for informed evidence-based decisions on national policies and improved nutrition programmes outcomes. Additionally, it will help to the country to report and monitor the global nutrition targets .

Under Priority 3, WHO has contributed to capacity building of key technical persons at the level of the Ministry of Health and Wellness and the Ministry of Finance on Sugar Sweetened Beverages (SSB) Taxation  during a global meeting with 14 front runner countries and others.  The Mauritian Health and Finance experts learned from other countries on SSB as well as shared Mauritius' experiences on SSB taxation.

Further, under Priority 4, WHO supported the roll out of the Behavioural Insights training in Mauritius and Rodrigues.  Some 75 multi-sectoral stakeholders (Mauritius and Rodrigues) were trained on the principles, use and application of  Behavioural insights to improve communications to tackle NCDs and risk factors; communicable diseases (dengue, chikungunya,etc) and other health issues.  Rodrigues island have prioritized a list of programmes/projects that would need further support for application of behavioural sights.

planEntities.name: Elaboration of the Decent Work Country Programme 2024-2028 (2nd Generation)
planEntities.parentName: Enhanced, innovation driven blue, green, circular, and digital economies that provides opportunities for all, in particular youth, women, persons living with disabilities and other vulnerable groups.
planEntities.description:
The First Generation of the Mauritius Decent Work Country Programme  (MDWCP I) was signed by the national tripartite constituents on 30 November 2012. The programme was initially meant to cover the period 2012-2014. However, after a mid-term review exercise that took place in October 2014, the tripartite constituents requested additional time to implement and complete their respective remaining activities. MDWCP I was subsequently extended to 31 December 2015. Another recommendation of the Mid-Term Review  was to focus on activities that were of relevance and priority to the tripartite constituents and “ensure that these are in tune with realistically achievable outputs, outcomes and constituents’ capacity”.

To ensure continued guidance and prioritisation of the International Labour Organisation’s (ILO) development support, the Republic of Mauritius embarked on the formulation of the Second Generation of the Mauritius Decent Work Country Programme (MDWCP II). The process started by the development of the country context analysis validated by the national tripartite constituents. The report gathered evidence on the work of the ILO as well as the constituents and other partners on employment and labour issues prevailing in the country and provided a strategic description of the main labour and social issues as well as national policies pertaining to the Republic of Mauritius in the year 2024. 

The document will be validated during the month of November of this year 2026. The related costs will be borne by the Government.

planEntities.name: Technical Assistance in the drafting of the Domestic Abuse Bill to incorpate international recommendations and align Mauritius to its international commitments and engagements to effectively and comprehensively address GBV in an inclusive manner.
planEntities.parentName: Social protection and health systems are better able to deliver timely, equitable and innovative services to all, especially youth, women, and migrants.
planEntities.description:
UNFPA provided techical expertise and input into the draft of the Domestic Abuse Bill, ensuring coherence to international recommendations as related to the national context and legal framework. Consequently, the Ministry of Gender Equality and Family Welfare, with support from UNFPA, convened stakeholders to a 3-day consultation workshop to review and dicuss the draft Domestic Abuse Bill.

THe 3-day consultation marked a pivotal moment in Mauritius's collective efforts to create a society where every individual is safe and respected within their own home. The draft document represents a significant milestone in the journey towards ending gender-based violence  providing a basis for a basis for a comprehensive legal framework that addresses the specific needs and vulnerabilities of victims and survivors - in its majority women and girls.

At the heart of the Domestic Abuse Bill is the recognition of domestic violence as a violation of fundamental human rights. Every individual has the right to live free from fear, violence, and discrimination, and this legislation sends a powerful message that domestic violence is unacceptable and will not be tolerated. By incorporating international benchmarks, best practices and recommendations, the bill intends to intends to set a high standard for the protection of victims' rights and the promotion of gender equality.

Quality and gender-responsive legislation and policies are critical grounds for progress. The draft Domestic Abuse Bill will fulfil its transformative potential when it is accompanied by adequate policies, strategic frameworks and budgetary allocations from relevant sectors, with clear guidelines for law enforcement agencies, health and social service providers, and other stakeholders on how to respond to cases of domestic violence in a sensitive and victim-centred  manner, including including mechanisms for coordination and accountability.

planEntities.description:
WHO supported the MOHW to develop the National strategy for adolescent health 2024-2029. Adolescence is a critical period of growth and development, marked by physical, emotional, and social changes. 
The Objectives of the National Strategy for Adolescent health 2024-2029 are multi-folds: 
1.	Promote Health Education:
o	Equip adolescents with knowledge about physical, mental, and reproductive health.
o	Foster informed decision-making and resilience.
2.	Enhance Access to Services:
o	Provide age-appropriate, accessible, and confidential health services.
o	Ensure equitable access to healthcare, especially for marginalized adolescents.
3.	Prevent Risky Behaviors:
o	Reduce substance use, early pregnancies, and unsafe sexual practices.
o	Promote interventions addressing violence, injury, and mental health challenges.
4.	Strengthen Support Systems:
o	Engage families, schools, and communities in fostering a supportive environment.
o	Build partnerships with stakeholders, including non-governmental organizations (NGOs).
5.	Empower Adolescents:
o	Encourage participation in health-related decision-making.
o	Promote life skills development, leadership, and advocacy for healthy living.
6.	Address Social Determinants:
o	Tackle poverty, education gaps, and gender inequalities that influence adolescent health outcomes.
The strategy has already been approved by the cabinet on 16 August 2024. WHO will continue to provide support to implement the recommendation of the adolescent health strategic plan.
 2026-The Ministry is in the process of reviewing the strategy.

planEntities.name: National Health Sector Strategic Plan costed and developed, in a gender sensitive way
planEntities.parentName: Social protection and health systems are better able to deliver timely, equitable and innovative services to all, especially youth, women, and migrants.
planEntities.description:
Following the Government Programme 2025–2029, A Bridge to the Future, the Ministry of Health and Wellness has developed the Health Sector Strategic Plan (HSSP) 2026–2030 to translate the Government’s vision into a coherent, actionable strategy for transforming Mauritius’ health sector over the next five years.
The draft HSSP has been completed and is currently awaiting final approval. The plan sets out the national roadmap for modernising the health system, advancing Universal Health Coverage (UHC), strengthening health security, and improving population health and well-being.
The draft HSSP builds on a strong foundation, with a UHC Service Coverage Index of 75, rising life expectancy, and immunisation coverage above 95%, while responding to emerging pressures, including an ageing population, declining fertility, and a rising burden of non-communicable diseases (approximately 80% of deaths).
The draft is structured around four strategic transformations:
      1.    Shifting focus from treating illness to promoting lifelong health, anchored in Primary Health Care
      2.    Moving from fragmented services to integrated, people-centred care across the life course
      3.    Strengthening system foundations — governance, financing, workforce, medicines and technologies, infrastructure, digital health/AI, and research
      4.    Building national resilience to future health threats, including outbreaks, antimicrobial resistance, and climate-related risks
These transformations are consolidated into two strategic goals: strengthening the foundations of the health system, and improving population health through integrated, high-quality service delivery and stronger health security.
The draft HSSP is with Ministry of Health and Wellness for final review and approval. Once approved, the Ministry of Health and Wellness will proceed to finalise implementation arrangements in coordination with Government institutions, healthcare professionals, academic and research institutions, the private sector, civil society, and development partners.
It is recommended that the final approval process be expedited to enable timely rollout of the Plan’s priority actions, given the alignment required with the 2026/27 budget cycle and ongoing health system reforms

planEntities.name: Develop and implement gender sensitive roadmap to reduce obesity
planEntities.parentName: Food security is enhanced for all – especially children, youth, women and other vulnerable groups – ensuring the transition of food, water and energy systems towards sustainability.
planEntities.description:
Mauritius with the support of the World Health Organization conducted three-day multisectoral consultative roundtable in April 2024 with participation of cross-section of stakeholders from government, the private sector, civil society and academia to come up with concrete actions to combat the obesity epidemic which affects 36.2% of the population. Using an evidence-based approach, the Obesity Roadmap prescribes a broad range of policy tools – political, fiscal and legal - aimed at tackling the obesogenic environment which encourages unhealthy lifestyles. The Mauritius Acceleration Plan to Stop Obesity 2024-2030 will address obesity which represents a significant public health burden in a country where NCDs account for 80% of the disease burden and 85% of mortalities.  Factors addressed in the Roadmap include the marketing of unhealthy foods and beverages, access to affordable and sustainable alternatives, fiscal policies, food labelling, early food environments, public food procurement, physical activity, health service delivery, public education and awareness, and country specific solutions.  the three major objectives of the Roadmap are as follows:(i) to reduce the prevalence of insufficient physical activity by 8% (57.6% to 49.6%) in children and adolescents (74.8% to 66.8%) from 2021 to 2030; (ii)to decrease consumption of unhealthy and ultra-processed foods and sugar sweetened beverages; and (iii) to increase coverage of obesity clinics to 50% through primary health centres and community based program to provide obesity prevention and management services.

The Roadmap will be implemented through a set of 5 priority actions and interventions:
•	Priority 1:Integrate obesity prevention and management in primary healthcare services and community outreach services.
•	Priority 2: Promote and create enabling environments to facilitate physical activity appropriate for all ages in different settings. 
•	Priority 3: Restrict the marketing of unhealthy, ultra-processed foods and sugar sweetened beverages.
•	Priority 4: Conduct behaviour change communication campaigns related to healthy diets, physical activity, and demand for health services.
•	Priority 5: Increase local agricultural production and accessibility to healthy foods to ensure availability and affordability of safe and quality agricultural products.  

The implementation of the specific activities under the five priorities as delineated in the Roadmap will further strengthen the interventions already in place through a multi-sectoral and coordinated approach to achieve the goal of reducing the obesity prevalence by 5% by 2030.  

Under Priority 1 and Priority 4 of the Obesity Roadmap, WHO provided technical support to conduct training of trainers and roll out of child growth assessment over a five-day intensive training.  The training empowered 90 health workers (Mauritius and Rodrigues) on appropriate child growth monitoring to enable the detection of wasting and stunting among children.  25 Health workers were empowered as trainers including 10 facilitators for training roll out across the five health regions in Mauritius.  The training of trainers further contributed to in-country capacity building (pool of trainers and facilitators) .  In the same vein, an assessment of the national nutrition information system was conducted in view of strengthening the national nutrition surveillance system in the Republic of Mauritius.  The findings of the assessment will help in standardizing and normalizing nutrition data for informed evidence-based decisions on national policies and improved nutrition programmes outcomes. Additionally, it will help to the country to report and monitor the global nutrition targets .

Under Priority 3, WHO has contributed to capacity building of key technical persons at the level of the Ministry of Health and Wellness and the Ministry of Finance on Sugar Sweetened Beverages (SSB) Taxation  during a global meeting with 14 front runner countries and others.  The Mauritian Health and Finance experts learned from other countries on SSB as well as shared Mauritius' experiences on SSB taxation.

planEntities.name: Development and implementation of  a gender sensitive Capacity Building Plan to enhance knowledge of climate change and health risks and integration into health programming for key stakeholders
planEntities.parentName: Policy and regulatory framework strengthened and innovative technologies are leveraged to accelerate climate change actions through the promotion of naturebased solutions, access to climate finance and disaster risk reduction.
planEntities.description:
The Capacity Building Plan on climate change and health has been developed and progressively rolled out in Mauritius through a phased, evidence-based approach, strengthening MoHW and partner stakeholders' knowledge and preparedness.

Key milestones:
- November 2024: A three-day V&A Assessment Training Workshop built foundational knowledge on climate-health impacts and assessment methodology, with a June 2025 refresher to share preliminary V&A findings.
 - Jan–Feb 2026: A KAP Survey (369 targeted respondents, 70% response rate) identified capacity gaps and training needs, directly shaping the Health Sector Capacity Assessment, HNAP, and subsequent training design.
- April 2026: A three-day workshop trained MoHW staff across five priority areas (NCD management, heat illness, mental health, disease surveillance, RCCE), producing measurable knowledge gains, most notably heat-illness cooling response rising from 33% to 100%. A few areas (heat-exhaustion red flags, a cooling-cessation misconception, two RCCE points) were flagged for reinforcement.
Medium/long-term plan: A separate multi-year plan, "Building Climate Resilient Health Systems in Mauritius," was developed, spanning 9 thematic pillars and 19 training modules with defined cadres, formats, timelines, and indicators. Five of its modules were prioritized and already delivered via the 2026 workshop, showing the plan is being implemented in line with its own roadmap.

planEntities.name: Technical support to develop the health component of the National Adaptation Plan (HNAP) to identify adaptation solutions for reducing the  health risks of CC, including implementation road map, monitoring and evaluation framework, and sustainable health adaptation financing  strategies
planEntities.parentName: Policy and regulatory framework strengthened and innovative technologies are leveraged to accelerate climate change actions through the promotion of naturebased solutions, access to climate finance and disaster risk reduction.
planEntities.description:
This sub-output involved providing technical support to develop the Health National Adaptation Plan (HNAP) 2026-2030 for Mauritius, a strategic framework identifying priority adaptation solutions to reduce climate-related health risks, together with an implementation roadmap, a Monitoring, Evaluation and Reporting (MER) framework, and a sustainable, multi-tiered health adaptation financing strategy.

The HNAP was grounded in two evidence-generating exercises: a Climate and Health Vulnerability and Adaptation (V&A) Assessment identifying priority climate-sensitive health risks and vulnerability hotspots, and a Health Sector Capacity Report (March 2026) assessing the health system's institutional readiness. Fourteen multi-sectoral thematic panels translated this evidence into context-specific adaptation strategies across the ten components of the WHO Operational Framework for Climate-Resilient Health Systems. These were consolidated into a validated set of Flagship Adaptation Strategies, grouped into seven investment packages and reviewed at a national stakeholder validation workshop, of which the three highest-priority packages were selected for further costing and development into standalone concept notes. The HNAP also establishes a phased implementation roadmap (short, medium, and long-term), an MER framework aligned with WHO Quality Criteria, and a layered financing strategy combining domestic budget tagging, international climate finance (GCF, Adaptation Fund, GEF), and private sector and blended finance mechanisms, anchored by the Climate & Health Technical Unit (CHTU) under joint MoHW-Ministry of Environment leadership.

planEntities.description: Evidence on the health impacts of climate change, vulnerable and at-risk populations, adaptation options, and the capacity of the health system to effectively deal with climate-related shocks and stresses has been generated. This was achieved through three sequenced activities: building the technical capacity of MoHW staff and key stakeholders in Vulnerability and Adaptation (V&A) assessment methodology; conducting Mauritius's first national, gender-responsive Climate Change and Health V&A Assessment (finalized September 2025) to establish the evidence base and identify prioritized adaptation options across eleven health system components; and developing an Early Warning and Alert Response System for Climate-Sensitive Diseases (EWARS-csd) through a phased implementation roadmap, directly informed by the V&A Assessment's findings.

planEntities.name: All-hazards emergency preparedness capacities assessed, including risk mapaping, and reported as per International Health Regulations(2005)
planEntities.parentName: Policy and regulatory framework strengthened and innovative technologies are leveraged to accelerate climate change actions through the promotion of naturebased solutions, access to climate finance and disaster risk reduction.
planEntities.description:
The Republic of Mauritius continues to strengthen its health emergency preparedness and response capacities in line with the International Health Regulations (IHR 2005) and the WHO 
Health Emergency Preparedness, Response and Resilience (HEPR) Framework. The assessment and reporting of national emergency preparedness capacities in line with the International Health Regulations (IHR) in order to identify and address critical gaps, document strengths and build on best practices for health security. WHO has supported Mauritius in the implementation of the IHR Monitoring and Evaluation Framework through improved methodological approach to conducting the State Party Annual Reporting (SPAR) and ensuring timely submission of the report. The MOHW has led this intervention by ensuring follow up of the gaps and developing and implementing actions to enhance the health security. WHO also supported an intra-action review following the dengue outbreak as per the IHR as well as an Early Action Review for dengue. Mauritius is also considering the next Joint External Evaluation (JEE) in a view to get a more precise view of the progress made since the last JEE.

In 2023, the Ministry of Health and Wellness (MOHW), with technical support from the World Health Organization (WHO), conducted a Strategic Tool for Assessing Risks (STAR) workshop to 
develop an evidence-based national health emergency risk profile. The workshop identified priority biological, natural, technological and societal hazards and proposed strategic actions to 
strengthen national preparedness and response capacities. The STAR 2023 assessment established a comprehensive national risk profile that guided preparedness planning and highlighted priority areas for strengthening health security. Since then, Mauritius has experienced evolving public health threats and changes in its emergency 
preparedness landscape that warrants a review of the previous assessment. 
For the period 2025-2027, the following additional activities are planned: 
Provide evidence-based guidance for implementation of specific technical areas
- Strengthening the functionality and operationalization of the Public Health Emergency Operation Centre (PHEOC) 
- Conduct TTX, SimEx, IAR/AAR as part of the ongoing efforts of IHR Monitoring and Evaluation - 
- Conduct participatory eSPAR annually
-conduct a JEE 
- Review the STAR 2023 assessment.

planEntities.name: First National Action Plan on Health Security ( 2023-2024) implemented and evaluation to inform development of the second generation of NAPHS conducted
planEntities.parentName: Policy and regulatory framework strengthened and innovative technologies are leveraged to accelerate climate change actions through the promotion of naturebased solutions, access to climate finance and disaster risk reduction.
planEntities.description:
The International Health Regulations (IHR 2005) require all Member States to develop and maintain core capacities for the prevention, detection and response to public health emergencies. As part of the IHR Monitoring and Evaluation Framework (IHR-MEF), Mauritius successfully completed the Joint External Evaluation (JEE) in November 2025, providing a comprehensive assessment of national capacities across all technical areas of health security.
Following the completion of the JEE, the findings and recommendations of the JEE will inform the next NAPHS. Mauritius is now embarking on the development of its second-generation National Action Plan for Health Security (NAPHS) 2027–2032, which will serve as the country’s strategic framework for strengthening health security capacities over the next five years. The development of the NAPHS follows WHO guidance and the national roadmap for NAPHS development and implementation.

The development of the Five-Year NAPHS 2027-2032, represents a critical step towards strengthening Mauritius’ national health security architecture.

planEntities.parentName: Policy and regulatory framework strengthened and innovative technologies are leveraged to accelerate climate change actions through the promotion of naturebased solutions, access to climate finance and disaster risk reduction.
planEntities.description: Mauritius  is a Small Island Development State which  is vulnerable to climate changes and associated implications. The recent years have demonstrated the impact of climate change on countries like Mauritius, with cyclones, flash floods, heavy rainfall and outbreaks of vector borne diseases. In 2023/2024, Mauritius and Rodrigues experienced one of the worst outbreaks of dengue with more than 9000 cases of dengue. The outbreak of dengue provided an opportunity for the country to further consolidate the Risk Communications and Community Engagement practices. A consultancy on developing the RCCE strategy for dengue during the outbreak of dengue was fruitful. The Ministry of Health and Wellness led the development of the strategy with the support of the World Health Organisation. A situational analysis showed some gaps in the understanding of the concepts of RCCE and how to enhance the delivery of communication products to the general population and high risk population.  The consultant recruited by WHO compiled a list a of key strategic objectives relevant to dengue that can be transferrable to other priority diseases. The objectives were further unpacked into specific actions and activities, which were prioritized for implementation by the Ministry of Health and Wellness. An RCCE strategic plan was adapted to address vector-borned diseases including chikungungya and yellow fever, among others.  The RCCE strategic plan for vector-borne diseases was scrupulously implemented by the MOHW during the outbreak of chikungunya early this year.

planEntities.parentName: Policy and regulatory framework strengthened and innovative technologies are leveraged to accelerate climate change actions through the promotion of naturebased solutions, access to climate finance and disaster risk reduction.
planEntities.description:
Mauritius and Rodrigues are Small Island Development States with heightened vulnerabilities to the effects of climate change. The Ministry of Health and Wellness in collaboration with WHO, who provided the technical assistance in strategically assessing the risks to the respective countries through the STAR (Strategic Toolkit for Assessing Risks). Following the STAR, the key recommendations were to assess risks at the Port of Entries and develop the National Health Emergency Response Operational Plan. The PoE risk assessment has been conducted in 2023, with a view to conduct the NHEROP in 2024. The project has been strongly advocated, however financial constraints and the human resource factors at the Ministry of Health and Wellness can impede the implementation of this project. Ongoing advocacy with root cause analysis are being conducted to discuss way forward.

To build on this work, a STAR 2023 Review Workshop was conducted from 9–11 September 2026, bringing together key stakeholders to reassess the evolving risk landscape, validate priorities and identify preparedness and response actions. The findings will directly inform the development of the second-generation NAPHS (2027–2032), scheduled for 19–23 October 2026, ensuring that identified risks and vulnerabilities are translated into prioritized, costed and actionable measures to strengthen national emergency preparedness, operational readiness and response capacity.

planEntities.name: Provide guidance, and build country capacity to strengthen and sustain quality immunization services across the life course, and focusing on  under-vaccinated persons and communities
planEntities.parentName: Social protection and health systems are better able to deliver timely, equitable and innovative services to all, especially youth, women, and migrants.
planEntities.description:
1.1 Technical support to develop National Immunization Strategy for Mauritius and Rodrigues Island starting with the conduct Situational Analysis and Review of EPI ( CmYP 20218-23)I.  
Mauritius is fully committed to achieving the goals set under the Immunization Agenda 2030 (IA2030) namely reducing mortality and morbidity from vaccine-preventable diseases across the life course, Increase equitable access to new and existing vaccines, and strengthening  immunization within primary health care (PHC) to support universal health coverage (UHC) and sustainable development.

Mauritius has demonstrated strong performance in vaccination coverage across both routine immunizations, with Coverage has consistently been above 90% since 2015, indicating strong routine immunization systems. 

In response to evolving global health priorities, the National Immunization Strategy (NIS) replaces the previous comprehensive Multi-Year Plan (cMYP). The NIS is a strategic, streamlined, and country-owned document that guides immunization efforts over a five-year period, ensuring alignment with national health sector plans and resource realities.
Mauritius has no National Immunization Strategy and the last cMYP expired in 2023. Furthermore, the last review of the EPI was conducted in 2018, and which was used to inform the latest cMYP. 

Scope and purpose of the support requested:
To develop a comprehensive, evidence-based, and costed National Immunization Strategy that:
•	Aligns with IA2030 strategic priorities and core principles.
•	Integrates immunization within the broader health system and PHC. 
•	Addresses equity, gender-related barriers, and zero-dose children.
•	Feasible within the expected domestic and external resource envelope. 
•	Serves as a guiding framework for annual operational planning, monitoring, and evaluation.

Specific Objectives
a. Conduct a situational analysis of the immunization programme, including performance  review, equity gaps, and health system linkages.
b. Define a long-term vision and strategic goals for immunization aligned with IA2030 and  national health priorities.
c. Design a monitoring, evaluation, and action (ME&A) framework with clear indicators,  baselines, and targets.
d.  Estimate resource requirements using the NIS.COST tool and conduct budget dialogue with key stakeholders.
e.  Ensure integration of immunization priorities into the national health sector strategic plan and budget.
f.  Facilitate stakeholder engagement and consensus-building throughout the strategy development process.
g.   Produce a concise, strategic NIS document for endorsement and implementation

2.  Technical support to strengthen the National Immunization Technical Advisory Group (NITAG) through - virtual capacity building of the Mauritius NITAG ( MAUNITAG) and an internal evaluation of the MAUNITAG (based on the Action Plan developed in 2025)
The external assessment and the EtR training of the Mauritius National Immunisation Technical Advisory Group (MAUNITAG), was conducted in February 2025 by WHO/AFRO and the NITAG Support Hub at the University of Cape Town, aimed to evaluate the maturity and functionality of MAUNITAG using the NITAG Maturity Assessment Tool (NMAT). The assessment revealed that MAUNITAG met 41% of the NMAT criteria, with relatively strong performance in establishment and composition (69%), resources and secretariat support (50%), and operations (50%). However, significant gaps were identified in stakeholder recognition (0%), integration into policymaking (25%), and the recommendation-making process (25%). 

Despite these challenges, MAUNITAG is officially recognised by the Ministry of Health and Wellness and benefits from a committed and diverse membership. Key challenges include the absence of a dedicated secretariat, limited funding, weak documentation and digital access, and insufficient integration into national policy processes. WHO played a central role in facilitating the assessment, providing
technical expertise, and supporting capacity building. The report recommends strengthening MAUNITAG through expanded membership, improved transparency, institutionalised procedures, and a costed annual work plan. A detailed improvement roadmap was validated by stakeholders to guide future actions and elevate MAUNITAG’s maturity and impact.

planEntities.name: Technical Assistance to build capacity to understand, adapt and Implement WHO Data collection tools, including Data Systems stengthening
planEntities.parentName: Social protection and health systems are better able to deliver timely, equitable and innovative services to all, especially youth, women, and migrants.
planEntities.description:
1. Background

A Data Quality Review (DQR) and a Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) System Assessment conducted in January–February 2025, using the WHO DQR toolkit, identified significant data quality and system performance issues at the health‑facility level. Key gaps include:

- Inaccurate and inconsistent reporting across key health indicators
- Missing or incomplete tracking of critical indicators (e.g., viral suppression, HIV‑positive test results)
- Lack of standardized data capture tools, including registers and reporting forms
- Sub‑optimal filing and weak mechanisms for retrieval of client records
- Inadequate safeguards to ensure data confidentiality, privacy, and security

The M&E System Assessment further highlighted:

- Absence of indicator definitions, data management guidelines, and user instructions within existing tools
- Limited data management and M\&E capacity at both central and facility levels
- Lack of data quality assurance mechanisms, including SOPs and supportive supervision
- Insufficient use of available data for evidence‑based decision-making

These findings underscore the critical need to strengthen national data systems by adopting standardized, interoperable approaches. This includes aligning national tools and practices with WHO‑recommended standards to ensure accuracy, consistency, and readiness for DHIS2 rollout.

In this context, technical assistance from WHO is requested to support the adaptation, operationalization, and institutionalization of WHO data collection and reporting tools, alongside capacity-building for sustainable national ownership.

2. Objectives of the Technical Assistance

Overall Objective
To strengthen Mauritius’ national health information system through the adaptation, standardization, and implementation of WHO-recommended data collection tools and guidance, in preparation for the transition to the DHIS2 platform.

Specific Objectives

1.  Facilitate national understanding of WHO-recommended data collection tools, their purpose, and application across service delivery points.
2.  Adapt WHO tools and guidelines to Mauritius’ epidemiological, programmatic, and service delivery context.
3.  Develop and validate national protocols and operational guidelines for data collection, reporting, and data management.
4.  Strengthen capacity of health personnel at central, regional, and facility levels through targeted training, mentoring, and supportive supervision.
5.  Provide technical assistance for data reconstruction and validation, ensuring cleaned, accurate, and interoperable datasets prior to DHIS2 implementation.

Technical Assistance has been cancelled s this would be provided through the current grant from Global Fund AIDS, TB and Malaria (GFATM)

planEntities.name: Re-invigorating and re-establishing culture at the heart of Seychelles economic and social development
planEntities.parentName: Improved access to justice, particularly for vulnerable and marginalized groups within a governance framework characterized by strong, efficient and accountable institutions.
planEntities.description: Conceived by the Seychelles National Institute for Culture, Heritage and the Arts (SNICHA) and funded through the International Fund for Cultural Diversity (IFCD), this project seeks to identify and advance key cultural policy reforms aimed at reinvigorating and repositioning culture at the heart of Seychellois society. The initiative focuses on strengthening a sustainable and coherent governance framework for culture, while critically reviewing existing mechanisms for the creation, promotion, and dissemination of cultural content. In parallel, the project explores methodologies to enhance the visibility of cultural expressions and to ensure more equitable, inclusive, and balanced access to cultural content for diverse audiences, in line with the principles and objectives of the 2005 Convention on the Protection and Promotion of the Diversity of Cultural Expressions.

planEntities.name: Strengthening Sea Level Monitoring and Data Management in East Africa for Coastal Resilience and Community Safety
planEntities.parentName: Institutions and communities are better prepared and collaborating to adapt to climate change and manage risks.
planEntities.description: SEAMARCS is a regional initiative to strengthen sea-level monitoring and improve data collection and management in East Africa, with a focus on Kenya, Madagascar, Mozambique, and Seychelles. The project aims to deploy affordable 'Sea Level Station in a Box' units to enhance monitoring infrastructure and build a regional network of data operators. By integrating collected data into global systems such as GLOSS and the IOC/VLIZ Sea Level Station Monitoring Facility (SLSMF), the initiative supports international oceanographic research and enhances coastal resilience and disaster preparedness. Furthermore, the project aligns with global agreements such as the Paris Agreement and the Sendai Framework, as well as regional frameworks such as the African Union's Agenda 2063.

planEntities.parentName: Health and social protection systems are increasingly inclusive and resilient.
planEntities.description: The Republic of Seychelles is facing a pivotal demographic juncture, experiencing a unique "High-Income Paradox" in Africa. Following its transition to high-income status in 2015, the country achieved significant progress driven by strong human development and a booming tourism industry.  Today, however, that demographic window is closing. With birth rates falling below replacement levels and the population structure shifting into a mature, "stationary" phase, Seychelles faces a new challenge. To sustain its prosperity, the country must now pivot from relying on rapid workforce expansion to preparing for the looming economic pressures of a rapidly aging society. UNFPA partners with national counterparts to leverage demographic intelligence and demographic foresight to inform and capacitate key national stakeholders for evidence-informed poliy making and programming.

planEntities.parentName: Strengthened productive capacities of institutions to implement sustainable, diversified economic value addition, with community shared ownership.
planEntities.description: Contribute to improved evidence generation, and food security and livelihood diversification of El-Nino affected farming households - As more than 43% of the population was reported to be food insecure, Government availed NAD 829 million (USD 46 million) for the drought relief support program, leaving a funding gap of approximately NAD 482 million (USD 26 million). More than 70% of the drought relief support program is earmarked for food assistance. In light of the funding gap, and as expressed by OPM, there is an urgent need to avail fodder (hydroponic) for core breeding herds as well as small scale irrigation systems and vegetable seeds, and to support diversification of livelihoods through provision of low-maintenance livestock such as chickens and rabbits. Through this assistance, FAO Namibia aims to reach 1200 households (4,800 people) in Erongo, Hardap, Kunene, Omaheke and Otjozondjupa regions to improve livelihoods through enhanced agricultural production while contributing to strengthened capacity for resilience building.

planEntities.name: Appuyer la mise en œuvre de la Budgétisation sensible au dividende démographique (BSDD)
planEntities.parentName: Produit 1.6 : Les institutions et organes aux niveaux nationaux, locaux, disposent de capacités techniques et financières renforcées pour le suivi, l’analyse et l’évaluation de la mise en œuvre des politiques publiques en lien avec le PDES, les recommandations des EPU (Examens Périodiques Universels) et les ODD, y compris la production, la gestion et l’utilisation des statistiques fiables, désagrégées et harmonisées
planEntities.description: L'outil BSDD vise une allocation efficace des ressources dans les secteurs clés favorisant le dividende démographique tels que le développement du capital humain (éducation, santé), l'entrepreneuriat et l'emploi, comme stipulé dans la feuille de route de l'Union Africaine de 2017 sur l’exploitation du dividende démographique grâce à des investissements massifs dans la jeunesse. L'intégration de l'approche BSDD dans les processus de planification et de programmation budgétaire favorise également les conditions favorables à la réalisation des Objectifs de Développement Durable (ODD). Il s’agit en particulier de l'ODD 3 (Bonne santé et bien-être), l'ODD 4 (Éducation de qualité) et l'ODD 8 (Travail décent et croissance économique), qui ont des effets d'entraînement et de retombées significatifs sur d'autres ODD.

planEntities.name: Urban Eco-system Based Adaptation for Climate-resilient Development in the Kathmandu Valley, Nepal
planEntities.parentName: Rural and urban development is increasingly sustainable and climate resilient
planEntities.description:
The project “Urban Ecosystem-based Adaptation for Climate-resilient Development in the Kathmandu Valley, Nepal” (Urban EbA) was approved by the Global Environment Facility (GEF) in 2019. The project is planned to be implemented targeting five municipalities, namely Kathmandu and Lalitpur Metropolitan Cities, Tokha, Madhyapur Thimi and Budhanilkantha Municipalities in Kathmandu Valley. The project is executed by the Kathmandu Valley Development Authority (KVDA) with the oversight of the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP).
The overarching objective of this project is to build the resilience of the local communities in Kathmandu Valley amidst increased impacts of climate change, such as flooding, landslides, erosion, heat and drought. The project interventions aim to mainstream EbA into planning frameworks, budgeting and implementation mechanisms of the KVDA and five target municipalities, as a demonstration to decrease the climate-induced impacts, particularly urban flood, pollution, drought, and heat. Project interventions directly benefit 82,400 people in the selected wards of the target five municipalities, where EbA interventions will be demonstrated, while the entire municipal population will be the indirect beneficiaries of the project, through institutionalization and mainstreaming of the EbA in the municipal and KVDA’s annual planning process.
Moreover, the project adopts a demonstration approach as a proof of concept to i) enhance groundwater recharge; ii) improve soil stability; iii) check urban flooding surge; iv) reduce urban heat effect, and v) build the resilience capacity of urban households. At the same time, the entire Kathmandu population will benefit indirectly through institutionalization and mainstreaming of the EbA in the municipalities and KVDA’s decision-making and annual planning process.

planEntities.description: UNCDF's Local Transformative Finance helps  local and provincial governments to lead local transformation. The programme combines finance and investment instruments with sector expertise across all aspects of subnational public and private finance for urban, green and productive transition.  The urban transition aims to implement the New Urban Agenda that transforms cities into inclusive, sustainable and resilient places with everyone benefiting from growth, access to transport, housing, water and sanitation, green space and the “right to the city”. The green transition aims to implement the Rio Conventions through sustainable city planning and zoning, urban food systems land-use management, circular water management and clean and smart energy solutions. The productive transition aims to implement the priorities of the Doha programme of action for the Least Developed Countries (2022-2031): increasing productive capacities through a territorial approach to local economic development and the creation of value-added urban/rural linkages leading to structural transformation.

A standard, internationally recognized mechanism designed and hosted by the UN Capital Development Fund (UNCDF), LoCAL promotes climate change– resilient communities and local economies. LoCAL combines performance-based climate resilience grants (PBCRGs) – which ensure programming and verification of climate change expenditures at the local level while offering strong incentives for performance improvements in enhanced resilience – with technical and capacity-building support.

Through this Project, UNDP Nepal aims to support the Ministry of Health and Population, Government
of Nepal by strengthening its capacity to combat TB and HIV cases and equipping the relevant entities
with health and non-health drugs, diagnostics, and equipment. The Project is specifically focused
to support the transition of procurement of drugs, diagnostics, and equipment under the costed extension
of Global Fund Grant Cycle 6, to be implemented by Save the Children and funded by the Global Fund.
By implementing this Plan, UNDP Nepal intends to make an efficient transition of due procurement plan
at Save The Children to allow the continuation of stocks of essential drugs at warehouses in respective
entities in Nepal. UNDP Nepal will coordinate with UNDP teams with health and procurement expertise
to procure identified and listed drugs, diagnostics and equipment and deliver to government entities like
National Tuberculosis Control Center (NTCC) and National Center for AIDS and STD Control (NCASC) in
Nepal. It is expected that with this transitional procurement, the supplies and basic health service delivery
in the various health entities will continue to be delivered to patients and remain unaffected.

planEntities.name: Management of Plastics Waste and Circular Interventions on Plastics in South, Southeast Asia, and the Pacific
planEntities.parentName: More people have skills, assests and access to services for better employment and sustainable livelihoods
planEntities.description:
The TCCF Plastics Circularity Project aims to address the critical issue of plastic waste management in nine countries across Asia. This initiative targets countries with varying levels of waste management infrastructure and plastic waste challenges, including India, Bangladesh, Bhutan, Nepal, Maldives, Sri Lanka, Philippines, Cambodia, and Vietnam. The project is designed to support the transition to a circular economy by improving plastic waste management, promoting recycling, and reducing plastic leakage into the environment. By focusing on these targeted areas, the project will contribute to better public health, environmental protection, and the development of sustainable waste management practices. The project is expected to contribute to collect at least 55,610 tons of plastics and support 72,100 direct beneficiaries during the implementation period across all nine participating countries. There are four components under the Project, namely:

1. Stakeholder Engagement and Strategy Development. The project will engage stakeholders to develop strategies and roadmaps for replicating and scaling up successful plastic waste management interventions. This includes the establishment of multi-stakeholder platforms to ensure gender-sensitive and inclusive participation. At the end of the project, 23 business models and/or Management Systems will be created or strengthened.
2. Implementation of Best Environmental Practices (BEP) and Best Available Technologies (BAT). The project will assist countries in deploying BEP/BAT for plastic waste management, including the establishment of Material Recovery Facilities (MRFs) and other processing units to improve the recycling and repurposing of plastics. At the end of project, 23 MRFs facilities will be implemented and/or strengthened.
3. Strengthening National Capacities and Guidelines. The project will enhance the capacities of national and subnational governments to implement plastic waste management strategies, develop guidelines, and strengthen regulatory frameworks. This includes integrating the informal sector into formal recycling systems and promoting gender-sensitive approaches. The project will generate direct benefits to72,100 people (of which 34,560 women) and contribute to strengthening national legal framework to support the plastic waste management transformation toward clean, sustainable and resilient system.
4. Information Outreach and Knowledge Management. Finally, the project will develop and implement comprehensive knowledge management strategies, including the documentation of best practices, capacity-building initiatives, and the dissemination of information through training, workshops, and awareness campaigns. At the end of project, 23 awareness /training programs will be delivered and a specific knowledge management platform on circular economy will be deployed and fully used.

planEntities.name: Strengthening Urban Preparedness and Earthquake Response in Western region of Nepal (SUPER-II)
planEntities.parentName: Communities have increased resilience and capacity to adapt to the impacts of climate change and disasters
planEntities.description: Building on past urban preparedness and drawing learnings from recent disasters, the action aims to institutionalize operational urban and earthquake preparedness and response in targeted provinces and municipalities and link it with federal mechanism. With inclusion at the heart of the action, addressing specific needs of vulnerable groups especially women, children and persons with disabilities, it also intends to upscale interventions in project area and beyond. The key result areas: i)Government-led operational system for urban and earthquake preparedness institutionalized at provincial and local level for effective response ii) Coordination and information management strengthened at provincial and municipal levels, aligned with national framework, for disaster risk governance; iii) Enhanced policy engagement for scalability of disaster preparedness and response mechanism at federal, provincial, and local levels.It has been identified based on deeper risk analysis, consultation with federal, provincial, and municipal governments and development partners engaged in similar interventions, lessons learned from the recent earthquakes including Jajarkot earthquake & learnings from SUPER. Under the leadership of the NDRRMA, provincial government and municipalities, the project will be implemented by a UNDP led partnership with UNICEF and UN WOMEN and HI, and in close coordination with RCO, WHO, PIN, NRCS, CSOs and other development partners and will engage parliamentarians, various association of municipalities, government training institutions, media and private sector. In the ongoing federalization context, the Action aims to institutionalize urban preparedness including continuity of essential services such as ambulance, fire service, water supply, electricity, access for relief etc. through policy and procedures, knowledge transfer and capacity development, financing arrangement and partnership and will contribute to create environment for upscaling.

planEntities.parentName: Communities have increased resilience and capacity to adapt to the impacts of climate change and disasters
planEntities.description:
Livelihoods Improvement and Disaster Resilience Enhancement in the Areas Affected by the Jajarkot Earthquake - 

Through The Project, UNDP will utilize its long-standing experience in supporting Nepal’s disaster risk preparedness, response, and recovery to support early recovery and reconstruction in the areas most affected by the Jajarkot earthquake. The proposed interventions will help communities recovering from the earthquake, and the facilities built for local governments will facilitate the smooth implementation of long-term reconstruction. The permanent housing reconstruction and long-term recovery measures need to be led by local governments and governance support will help in strengthening their capacity to coordinate, implement and monitor the long-term reconstruction. In close collaboration with local governments and other ongoing initiatives in the areas, the Project will provide direct support to: 1) strengthen governance capacity for delivery of basic services and enabling environment for long-term reconstruction and resilience; 2) promote community-led reconstruction of damaged small infrastructures for livelihoods opportunities, coupled with psychosocial support; and 3) strengthen capacities and mechanisms for emergency preparedness and response (EPR) to enhance resilience against future disasters.

planEntities.name: Advancing Civic Engagement for Democratic Participation
planEntities.parentName: Increased participation and inclusion of more people, especially women, youth and most marginalised and poor, in development and decision-making at all levels
planEntities.description: UNDP’s governance and civic engagement initiatives are grounded in the belief that sustainable peace and inclusive development depend on effective, accountable, and participatory institutions. A key condition for such governance is the ability of citizens, especially young people, women, and marginalized groups, to actively and meaningfully participate in public affairs, hold institutions accountable, and co-create solutions that strengthen trust and cohesion between citizens and the state. In this regard, to translate civic engagement in practice, the project focuses on strengthening inclusive, participatory, and accountable governance in Nepal by advancing political literacy and civic education, empowering young people as informed, responsible, and engaged citizens, and fostering trust and cohesion between citizens and the state. Through civic learning, digital literacy, and critical engagement with information, the initiative seeks to transform civic awareness into active participation, ensuring that governance processes are transparent, responsive, and reflective of the voices of all citizens, particularly youth, women, and marginalized groups. The goal of the project is to ensure that youth, including young women and youth from marginalized communities, hold more leadership roles and influence governance reforms, supported by safer civic spaces. The project focuses on strengthening the capacities of youth networks, partnering with civil society, academic institutions, and government to foster meaningful youth participation in governance. It envisions a series of civic and political literacy initiatives; the establishment and strengthening of youth councils and participatory mechanisms; building their capacity for evidence generation to support policymaking and advocacy and engagement with youth-led groups and marginalized communities to empower them to participate safely, counter misinformation, and drive civic-tech innovations that expand access to credible information and strengthen democratic accountability.

planEntities.name: Strengthening Inclusive Democratic Governance and Electoral Process in Nepal
planEntities.parentName: Increased participation and inclusion of more people, especially women, youth and most marginalised and poor, in development and decision-making at all levels
planEntities.description:
Nepal is entering a critical phase in its democratic trajectory as preparations intensify for the House of Representatives election on 5 March 2026. The political landscape has shifted following the youth-led Gen Z movement of September 2025, which mobilized tens of thousands of young citizens demanding transparency, accountability, better governance, inclusion, and renewed political leadership. This awakening has elevated public expectations and placed strong pressure on electoral institutions to deliver a credible, transparent, and inclusive process.
As Nepal moves toward the March polls, it is essential to respond to Gen Z expectations, ensure meaningful participation of political parties, rebuild public trust and strengthen both the operational and institutional readiness of the ECN. The ECN must urgently advance procurement of essential electoral materials, effectively enforce the Election Code of Conduct, counter misinformation, disinformation and hate speech, advance voter education targeting youth, women and marginalized groups and reinforce cybersecurity and data protection safeguards. Its ability to maintain public confidence will depend on timely action in these areas, supported by coordinated technical, operational, and security measures. 
The primary goal of the project is to strengthen democratic governance in Nepal by ensuring elections that are credible, inclusive, transparent, and secure, thereby building public trust and enabling meaningful participation for all citizens.

It aims to enhance the country's climate resilience and sustainability by focusing on finalization and implementation of the third Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC 3.0), gender-responsive local adaptation planning, empowering youth leaders to drive community-specific environmental changes, and promoting innovations and voluntary carbon markets. The project is part of a broader effort to support Nepal's vision of net-zero carbon by 2045 and becoming a risk-resilient society by 2030. It integrates efforts across various initiatives such as Climate Promise, HCFC Phase out Management Plan, SCALA, Climate Finance Network, and Early Action Support.

planEntities.name: Inclusive Energy Access for Accelerating Economic Growth in Karnali corridor (TA SASEC/ETDSP)
planEntities.parentName: Rural and urban development is increasingly sustainable and climate resilient
planEntities.description: Nepal's electricity access remains uneven due to deep-rooted social norms and structural inequalities, limiting economic opportunities for marginalized communities. Many remote villages struggle to leverage electricity for entrepreneurial activities due to a lack of skills, knowledge, and financial resources. Additionally, poor infrastructure for last-mile electrification and weak interconnections, particularly between micro- (and decentralized) hydropower projects (MHPs) and the national grid, result in supply-demand gaps, affecting trade and overall development. The proposed technical assistance (TA) under the Asian Development Banks’ (ADB’s) South Asia Subregional Economic Cooperation (SASEC) Electricity Transmission and Distribution Project (ETDSP) seeks to address these challenges by embedding gender equality and social inclusion (GESI) principles into electricity infrastructure projects to create a more inclusive and sustainable energy sector in Nepal. The Project broadly aims to enhance the impact of ADB’s project towards ensuring reliable and efficient electricity access, while also contributing to improved energy infrastructure for potential trade between SASEC nations. The project aims to strengthen the Nepal Electricity Authority’s (NEA’s) capacity on integrating GESI and on project implementation. The technical assistance (TA) will broaden NEA’s institutional outreach services for safe electricity utilization, local skills development, and promotion of energy efficient technologies. ‘Last mile’ connectivity to national grid by disadvantaged groups and women-headed households will be enhanced with the rehabilitation and interconnection of micro-hydropower projects to the national grid for stable and reliable energy access by the most rural communities. The project will be implemented in select municipalities of Dailekh, Kalikot and Jumla.

planEntities.name: Smart buildings and green infrastructure for improved human security and sustainable development in Nepal
planEntities.parentName: Rural and urban development is increasingly sustainable and climate resilient
planEntities.description:
Nepal is warming at nearly twice the global average, with urban areas facing severe heat stress. In the southern 
Terai, extreme heat and humidity are driving rapid growth in energy demand for cooling, increasing emissions and 
placing significant stress on energy infrastructure. Dhangadhi Sub-Metropolitan City (DSMC) in Sudurpaschim 
Province experiences recurrent heatwaves during May–August, with temperatures frequently exceeding 40°C. 
Climate variability, rapid and unplanned urbanization, loss of green spaces, and limited energy-efficient 
infrastructure exacerbate risks to public health, livelihoods, and essential services, disproportionately affecting low
income households, outdoor workers, and residents of poorly insulated housing. Impacts include heat-related illness and mortality, school disruptions, and reduced functionality of public facilities.  
In response, DSMC has adopted a Heat Action Plan. Building on this, the project will pilot scalable nature-based 
and energy-efficient cooling solutions in public buildings and small urban infrastructure, while strengthening 
evidence-based urban heat management. Interventions include wetland restoration, protection of green open 
spaces, and retrofitting public facilities to improve thermal comfort and energy efficiency. The project will directly 
benefit around 4,000 people and indirectly benefit DSMC’s entire population of approximately 198,792 people. The 
Project will be implemented under UNDP’s Direct Implementation Modality, with cost sharing with the Green Transition Portfolio for management and operations.

planEntities.description: Systemic Observations Financing Facility (SOFF) was co-founded by WMO, UNEP and UNDP to close critical weather and climate data gaps, predominantly in LDCs and SIDS. SOFF supports the sustained collection and international exchange of essential surface-based weather and climate observations according to the internationally agreed Global Basic Observing Network (GBON) regulations. The implementation of GBON will significantly strengthen the provision of high-quality weather forecasts, early warning systems, and climate services at global, regional, and national levels. GBON data are essential for effective, resilient development and climate adaptation action that results in saved lives, improved livelihoods, and protected property (SOFF Operational Manual 2022). planEntities.name: Creating Safe and Inclusive Learning Environment in Schools
planEntities.parentName: (multi/inter-agency): Strengthened inclusive and equitable educational institutions and systems at all levels of government promoting quality education for all children and young people
planEntities.description: Psychological and physical violence in and around schools, such as bullying, cyberbullying, gender-based violence, and sexual harassment, hinder learning and harm the physical and mental health of children and adolescents. Globally, approximately 246 million students experience such violence annually, with girls being particularly vulnerable. School-related gender-based violence (SRGBV) is a significant issue, driven by unequal power dynamics and gender stereotypes. Girls in Nepal face challenges in completing secondary education due to gender norms and societal structures, including menstruation restrictions and child marriage. Factors like patriarchal mindsets and school-related violence contribute to girls dropping out. Addressing this requires implementing strategies from education sector plans and national policies, mobilizing communities, and providing practical guidance. It's crucial to build the capacity of local education stakeholders and teachers to prevent and respond to SRGBV, leveraging UNESCO's resources and focusing on provinces with high child abuse cases and low literacy rates. These efforts align with UNESCO's strategy for Education for Health and Well-being and contribute to achieving SDG goals 4 and 5.

planEntities.name: School Health and Nutrition Programme (SHNP)
planEntities.parentName: (multi/inter-agency): Strengthened Government and non-governmental institutions at all levels to develop and implement multi-sectoral policies, strategies, use of evidence and investment programs for food and nutrition security, and increase knowledge among families on nutritious foods, healthy diets and optimal young child feeding, care and hygiene practices
planEntities.description:
With UNICEF’s support, the number of adolescents receiving Iron Folic Acid (IFA) supplementation doubled, increasing from 0.4 million in 2023 to 1 million in 2024 across six provinces: Lumbini, Gandaki, Madhesh, Bagmati, Karnali, and Sudurpaschim. Similarly, the proportion of mothers receiving 180 or more IFA tablets increased from 60 per cent in 2023 to 63 per cent in 2024.
To achieve these results, UNICEF enhanced coordination and communication between the health and education sectors by strengthening the skills and capacities of school health nurses and health coordinators under the School Health and Nutrition (SHN) programme. This included capacity-building efforts for 126 school health nurses in Lumbini, Gandaki, and Madhesh provinces, and 140 health coordinators in Bagmati, Lumbini, Karnali, and Sudurpaschim provinces. As a result, coverage of Weekly Iron Folic Acid Supplementation (WIFS) and deworming prophylaxis increased, and the quality of nutrition education and counseling for adolescents in schools saw significant improvements.

Empowered Women, Prosperous Nepal (EWPN) is a European Union (EU) and United Nations Joint programme, implemented by ILO, UNFPA, UNICEF, and UN Women, under the overall leadership of the UN Resident Coordinator in partnership with the Government of Nepal, including the provincial and local governments, as well as civil society and the private sector. Its objective is to advance gender equality and empowerment of women and girls for the realization of the national vision of a prosperous and developed Nepal (Vision 2030). 
UNICEF related activities in the EWPN programme are:-
1 ) Engagement with men and boys on gender transformation, including Rupantaran sessions
2) Engagement with the family and communities using gender transformative approaches. Develop girls as mentors or leaders to continue to reach more people. The model for scale up – Rupantaran (life skill) / Youth Volunteer at all levels, across institutions (government, schools, workplace). 
3) Roll out of gender equitable parenting and early childhood development curricula through community networks, in coordination with health, nutrition and education sectors (Early Childhood Development and Rupantaran Parenting module)
4) Youth, women, sexual / gender / ethnic minorities and women with disabilities outreach - existing networks identified and oriented on gender transformative approaches, sexual and reproductive health and human rights for further cascading and support to develop campaigns in coordination with other social justice advocates
5) Strengthen essential multi-sectoral gender and child sensitive GBV response services including  through OCMCs (psychosocial and case management support; community psychosocial workers (CPSWs); capacity building of front-line workers, health service providers, police, lawyers, safe house staff). Linkages will be made to the GBV in Emergencies programming and GBV Essential Service Package. 
6) Strengthen gender-equitable and inclusive access to justice / effective legal remedies / civic documentation and equitable CRVS services including for those who are gender non-conforming
7) Design and disseminate referral pathways information to communities and service providers 
8) Technical assistance to the strengthening of GBV service delivery to women, children / adolescents. Also includes development of technical guidelines, linkages between GBV and child welfare services.
9) Support the sustainable functioning of new or exisiting shelter and safe house at district level, including during emergencies 
10) Technical assistance to the planned scale up of Child helplines incl. strengthened linkages with services and crisis-response capacities 
11) Vulnerability assessment training and identification of at risk children. 
12) Technical and capacity strengthening support (training) for NWC (GBV network), Ministry of Women Children and Senior Citizens, Ministry of Social Development - Social Development Section, municipal women and children section, judicial committees, women and youth--led organisations

planEntities.parentName: (multi/inter-agency): Strengthened capacities of federal, provincial, and local health systems in Nepal to deliver inclusive, resilient, equitable, gender-responsive and quality health services for people, especially the most vulnerable groups, by developing and implementing evidence-based health policies, strategies, and plans, in line with the international health standard and regulations within the framework of Universal Health Coverage
planEntities.description: The rice fortification initiative has been embraced as a crucial approach in Nepal's National Health Policy 2019 and Nutrition Strategy 2020 to combat micronutrient deficiencies. This initiative actively collaborates  with federal and provincial health ministries, aiming to establish a policy framework that supports fortification efforts. It also engages with local authorities, health facilities and health care providers to enhance their conselling skills, promote awareness and generate demand for fortified rice. Additionally, the initiative seeks to integrate fortification efforts to existing health and nutrition services as well as other social safety net programme implemented through the health sector. In response to the GFC, fortified rice will provide increased nutrition to vulnerable populations living in remote areas of Nepal which are struggling to access nutritious food due to increased food prices. WFP will provide strategic technical assistance and financial support to the Government to initiate food fortification through procurement, blending and delivery of fortified rice in social assistance programs for the farthest left behind populations found in Karnali.
