planEntities.name: Enhanced capacities and mechanisms for gender-disaggregated data collection, analysis, validation and usage to inform policy-making and approaches for gender equality and women empowerment.
planEntities.parentName: Output 2.1: National and international commitments to gender equity and rights-based approaches that inform policy making are realized, through support to government institutions in monitoring implementation of commitments, the production, analysis, and use of sex/gender disaggregated statistics, SDG data and knowledge advocacy and accountability.
planEntities.description:
ILO's strategy to implement this suboutput rests on strengthening the capacity for data collection and analysis in the informal economy which employs women in large numbers and tihs is also an area where formalisation is required so women and men can move to more secure and decent jobs. This involves providing technical assistance and training to national statistical agencies, government institutions, and relevant stakeholders to improve their skills in collecting and disaggregating data by gender in informal economy sectors. The ILO also supports the development of standardized methodologies and tools for data collection to ensure consistency and comparability across different regions and countries.

Secondly, the ILO emphasizes the validation and quality assurance of gender-disaggregated data. This involves establishing mechanisms to ensure the accuracy and reliability of the collected data through rigorous validation processes. The ILO promotes the use of internationally recognized standards and methodologies, including peer review, to validate the data and ensure its credibility. By enhancing the quality of gender-disaggregated data, policymakers can have confidence in the information and make informed decisions to promote gender equality and women's empowerment in the informal economy. Ongoing support to provincial governments in collecting data on home based workers and domestic workers is an example of work to be carried out under this suboutput.

Additionally, the ILO focuses on facilitating the usage of gender-disaggregated data for policy-making and program development. This includes promoting the integration of gender analysis into policy formulation processes, using the data to identify gender-specific challenges and opportunities in the informal economy.

UN Women will support the mainstreaming of gender perspectives in national data collection tools, mechanisms and analysis: Building on its current efforts jointly with national and provincial stake holders, UN Women will develop a comprehensive indicator framework to respond to the data gaps for missing indicators under Pakistan’s national commitments and international reporting requirements. There will be continued focus on the mainstreaming of gender perspective in the SDG data production, analysis and utilization, including gender-disaggregated data and gender statistics at all levels (federal, provincial, local) in civil registration and vital statistics, and building the capacity of various departments to use and analyze available data. This will strengthen the mechanisms for collection, compilation, and use of standardized cross-thematic data to inform evidence-based reforms and interventions and report on the country’s national and international commitments on gender. UN Women will work with the Planning Commission, the National Commission on the Status of Women (NCSW), and the Pakistan Bureau of Statistics to build capacities to collect data and strengthen the indicator framework for gender equality, in order to plug gaps in national surveys. The agency will continue to work with NCSW to build on and strengthen the National Gender Data Portal (NGDP) and link it with sub-national databases and gender management information systems (GMIS), for it to serve as a one-stop repository of gender-disaggregated data and knowledge products. The NGDP will also be leveraged as a platform for linkages with academia, primarily providing direction in the potential areas of research for students and experts.
UNESCO has allocated funds from regular programme to contribute to this sub-output.

planEntities.name: Strengthened government capacities and systems to implement, monitor and report on national and international commitments on Gender Equality and Women Empowerment.
planEntities.parentName: Output 2.1: National and international commitments to gender equity and rights-based approaches that inform policy making are realized, through support to government institutions in monitoring implementation of commitments, the production, analysis, and use of sex/gender disaggregated statistics, SDG data and knowledge advocacy and accountability.
planEntities.description:
The ILO is providing support to governments in addressing concerns raised by the ILO supervisory mechanism regarding the conventions on equal pay for equal value of work and equal training and empowerment opportunities for women. Firstly, the ILO extends support in reviewing and aligning their national legislation and policies with the provisions of these conventions. This includes analyzing existing laws, regulations, and practices to identify gaps and inconsistencies, and providing guidance on legal reforms and policy development to ensure compliance with the principles of equal pay and equal training opportunities. 

Secondly, the ILO supports the government in implementing programs and initiatives that promote equal pay for equal value of work and equal training and empowerment opportunities for women. This involves capacity-building programs to enhance the skills and knowledge of employers, workers, and relevant stakeholders on the principles of equal pay and equal training. The ILO provides technical expertise in designing and implementing gender-responsive wage policies, including the establishment of transparent and fair wage-setting mechanisms. Additionally, the ILOassists the government in developing and implementing training programs and strategies that target the specific needs and barriers faced by women, ensuring they have equal access to training opportunities and support for career advancement. The ILO also facilitates knowledge-sharing and peer learning among governments to exchange best practices and successful strategies in promoting equal pay and equal training opportunities for women.

For strengthening gender data, during reporting period UN Women supported Federal Ministry of Human Rights for preparation of 6th periodic state report on CEDAW. An indicator matrix was developed which carries 97 indicators and trainings were conducted for provincial and  federal departments responsible for collection and provision of relevant data. A total of 5 training sessions were conducted in which 185 officials (100 Men and 85 Women) were trained. Presently data is being collected for writing of the report by MoHR.  

The interplay of climate and gender equality, especially in the context of the Glasgow Climate Change Conference and session 52-55 of COP 26, will also be an area of focus. UN Women will also support linkages and stronger coordination  between oversight institutions such as the National Commission of Human Rights, National Commission for Status of Women (NCSW) and CSO alliances to mobilize support for recommended actions and legislative reforms. Linkages between provincial CSWs and the NCSW will be strengthened including with the CSW of Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK). This will be supplemented by concrete support to women machineries across the country to institutionalize policies on gender equality and empowerment.

UNSCO allocated funds for this sub-put through the support to Ministry of Japan.

planEntities.name: Enhanced advococy and support for formulation of women-related laws and policies, and their implementation.
planEntities.parentName: Output 2.1: National and international commitments to gender equity and rights-based approaches that inform policy making are realized, through support to government institutions in monitoring implementation of commitments, the production, analysis, and use of sex/gender disaggregated statistics, SDG data and knowledge advocacy and accountability.
planEntities.description:
The ILO has a strategic approach to support Pakistan in formulating and advocating for laws that promote the rights of women in the workforce, including those in informal economy sectors. Firstly, the ILO provides technical assistance to the Pakistani government in conducting comprehensive assessments of existing legal frameworks, identifying gaps, and proposing necessary legislative reforms to ensure gender equality, non-discrimination, and decent work for women. This involves engaging with relevant stakeholders, including employers' and workers' organizations, civil society, and policymakers, to facilitate dialogue, raise awareness, and build consensus on the need for legal reforms. Additionally, the ILO advocates for the adoption and implementation of these laws through policy briefs, research reports, and international conventions, while also providing capacity-building support to strengthen the enforcement and monitoring mechanisms necessary to ensure effective implementation of the laws.

UN Women will support finalization and implementation of a National Gender Policy Framework (NGPF). This will be based on the priorities and recommendations received in periodic reviews. and will correlate reporting between the Beijing Platform for Action Areas of Priority, CEDAW and SDG 5 to put the recommendations into action. The NGPF will provide a comprehensive plan of action to measure the progress against the National Plan of Action for Women’s Development, 1998, and the National Gender Policy of the Planning Commission. UN Women will also continue to engage with provincial Planning & Development Departments to ensure that gender-related policies, including gender tools, are implemented.

planEntities.parentName: Output 2.1: National and international commitments to gender equity and rights-based approaches that inform policy making are realized, through support to government institutions in monitoring implementation of commitments, the production, analysis, and use of sex/gender disaggregated statistics, SDG data and knowledge advocacy and accountability.
planEntities.description:
The International Labour Organization (ILO) employs a comprehensive strategy to strengthen coordination, oversight, and accountability mechanisms of government institutions, civil society organizations (CSOs), and other relevant stakeholders for gender equality and women's empowerment. This strategy includes fostering multi-stakeholder partnerships and collaboration, facilitating dialogue and knowledge-sharing platforms, providing technical assistance and capacity-building support, and promoting the integration of gender equality and women's empowerment considerations into policies, programs, and practices. By enhancing coordination and oversight among these stakeholders, the ILO aims to ensure effective implementation of gender equality initiatives, monitor progress, and hold institutions accountable for their commitments, ultimately advancing gender equality and women's empowerment across various sectors.
UN Women will support linkages and stronger coordination  between oversight institutions such as the National Commission of Human Rights, National Commission for Status of Women (NCSW) and CSO alliances to mobilize support for recommended actions and legislative reforms. Linkages between provincial CSWs and the NCSW will be strengthened including with the CSW of Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK). This will be supplemented by concrete support to women machineries across the country to institutionalize policies on gender equality and empowerment.

planEntities.name: Increased awareness and advocacy for the prevention, protection and response to VAWG and harmful practices (including the effects of irregular migration) against women, girls, persons with disabilities and other vulnerable groups.
planEntities.parentName: Output 2.3: Vulnerable and marginalized women, girls, and transgender persons, actively contribute to resilient and empowered communities, and are able to operate in safe spaces and harassment-free environments, protected from gender based violence and violence against women and other harmful practices and have equitable access to services and information.
planEntities.description:
ILO employs a comprehensive strategy to increase awareness and advocacy for the prevention, protection, and response to violence against women and girls (VAWG) and harmful practices, including the effects of irregular migration, against women, girls, persons with disabilities, and other vulnerable groups. The ILO focuses on multiple fronts, including conducting research and data collection to better understand the magnitude and impact of VAWG and harmful practices, raising awareness through targeted campaigns and awareness-raising activities, advocating for policy and legal reforms to strengthen protections and support services, promoting workplace policies that prevent and respond to VAWG, collaborating with governments, civil society organizations, and other stakeholders to develop and implement prevention and response programs, and providing technical assistance and capacity building to enhance the capacity of governments and relevant institutions in preventing and addressing VAWG and harmful practices. By combining these efforts, the ILO aims to foster a safe and inclusive environment that upholds the rights and dignity of women, girls, persons with disabilities, and other vulnerable groups, while combating VAWG and harmful practices effectively.

UN Women will strengthen evidence-based advocacy as a cross-cutting theme to address harmful social norms and attitudes in workplaces, public spaces, and transportation, including engagement of families, matriarchs and men and boys, and support the implementation of social and behavior change strategies, including engagement with the formal education sector. UN Women’s approach involves moving forward is to integrate behavioural change related to social norms as a cross-cutting theme in all projects to address the issue from multiple dimensions. Emphases will be laid on strengthening UN Women’s engagement with communities, CSOs and academics to bridge the gap between interventions and impact. Innovative solutions to address the issue of mobility will be identified, and collaborations with non-traditional partners like the aviation industry and transport companies will be explored to support women’s access to safe public spaces and transport systems for increased mobility. UN Women will also play its part in connecting law enforcement agencies with the community in a more empathetic manner through advocacy campaigns to increase trust, promote a positive and friendly image of police, improve access to justice without any fear or stigma; promote female recruitment in justice sector institutions; and engage men and boys as advocates and HeforShe champions to promote gender equality to challenge patriarchal mindsets.

the ILO's strategy to strengthen the policy environment, capacities, and accountability mechanisms for gender inclusion and gender parity in public and private organizations involves promoting gender-responsive policies, enhancing organizational capacities, and establishing monitoring and accountability mechanisms. Through these efforts, the ILO aims to create an enabling environment where gender equality is prioritized, organizations have the necessary tools and knowledge to implement gender inclusion initiatives, and mechanisms are in place to track progress and ensure accountability towards achieving gender parity in the workplace.
the ILO emphasizes the establishment of accountability mechanisms to monitor progress and ensure gender parity in public and private organizations. The organization also encourages the establishment of gender equality committees or focal points within organizations to oversee progress, promote accountability, and address gender-related issues.

planEntities.description:
Gender Responsive Budgeting (GRB) has been identified as an important tool for advancing gender equality in key national documents, in accordance with existing national policy documents on social inclusion and gender equality. UN Women plans to support government efforts in using GRB as a tool to advance gender equality and ensure that women’s needs are incorporated in policies and related budgets. UN Women will also expand the purview of GRB, so that it is applied to annual development plans (ADPs) and public sector development programmes (PSDP). The expected long-term result of these initiatives is the incorporation of gender equality principles, perspectives and priorities not only in policy making, but also in budgeting at the national and provincial levels, leading to greater accountability and transparency of public finances.

Additionally, UN Women plans to engage Pakistan’s apex institutions and financial regulators, including the State Bank of Pakistan and the Securities and Exchange Commission. This work will holistically and strategically tackle women’s financial inclusion. Part of this engagement will include guiding regulators’ policies – such as the Banking on Equality Policy of the SBP – towards high-quality implementation. Commercial banks and other private organizations in the financial sector will also be engaged for capacity building, including but not limited to, gender-responsive procurement, budgeting and women-friendly HR policies.

planEntities.name: Supporting the development of evidence-based social protection policy, governance and legislative frameworks
planEntities.parentName: Output 1.5: Social protection systems and measures are strengthened to provide well-coordinated responses, in an inclusive and shock-responsive manner, to the most deprived and vulnerable populations.
planEntities.description:
The International Labour Organization (ILO) has a specific strategy to facilitate provincial legislative reforms aimed at extending social security to excluded groups. This strategy recognizes the importance of ensuring that vulnerable segments of the population have access to comprehensive social protection. The ILO works closely with provincial governments to develop and implement legislative changes that enable the expansion of social security coverage.

In addition to legislative reforms, the ILO also focuses on developing gender and disability-responsive policy initiatives. These initiatives aim to ensure that social protection schemes are designed and implemented in a manner that addresses the specific needs and challenges faced by women and persons with disabilities. The ILO engages in consultation with social partners, including employers' and workers' organizations, to develop policies that are mutually aligned and promote inclusivity.

To increase the effectiveness and quality of existing social protection schemes, the ILO pays attention to various aspects, including implementation frameworks, planning and coordination mechanisms, and exploring options to review existing fiscal space. This approach helps to streamline the implementation of social protection programs and improve their overall impact.

Furthermore, the ILO, in collaboration with provincial authorities, develops Social Protection (SP) roadmaps for provinces and territories. These roadmaps serve as strategic plans for the gradual implementation of universal social protection. They outline the necessary steps, timelines, and actions required to achieve comprehensive social security coverage for all individuals, including vulnerable segments of the population.

The development of SP roadmaps involves engaging with provincial stakeholders, including government representatives, employers, workers' organizations, and civil society. This participatory process ensures that the roadmaps reflect the specific needs and contexts of each province or territory. The ILO provides technical expertise, guidance, and support throughout the roadmap development process.

planEntities.name: Supporting data collection and analysis of social protection policies and programmes
planEntities.parentName: Output 1.5: Social protection systems and measures are strengthened to provide well-coordinated responses, in an inclusive and shock-responsive manner, to the most deprived and vulnerable populations.
planEntities.description:
The ILO places emphasis on collecting accurate and up-to-date data on social protection programs. This involves collaborating with national statistical agencies, government institutions, and other relevant stakeholders to establish robust data collection systems. The ILO supports the development and implementation of surveys, monitoring mechanisms, and data management tools to capture comprehensive information on social protection coverage, benefits, and impact. The ILO recognizes the importance of building the capacity of governments, researchers, and practitioners to effectively collect and analyze social protection data and for the country to be ultimately be able to report on its obligations such as SDG 1.3. The organization provides technical assistance, training, and knowledge-sharing platforms to enhance the skills and expertise of stakeholders involved in data collection and analysis. Capacity-building efforts focus on areas such as survey design, data management, statistical analysis, and utilization of data for policy formulation.

The ILO conducts sectoral analysis to identify social protection gaps and prioritize interventions. This involves analyzing data on specific sectors of the economy, such as agriculture, informal employment, and vulnerable groups, to understand the specific challenges they face regarding social protection coverage. Sectoral analysis helps in identifying target areas for policy interventions and tailoring social protection programs to meet the unique needs of different sectors.

Through data collection and analysis, the ILO aims to identify gaps in social protection coverage and benefits. This includes understanding the extent of exclusion faced by certain population groups, such as informal workers, women, persons with disabilities, and marginalized communities. By identifying these gaps, the ILO can advocate for policy reforms, program expansions, and targeted interventions to address the specific needs of excluded groups.The data collected and analyzed by the ILO serves as a basis for evidence-based policy formulation. The organization uses the insights gained from data analysis to develop policy recommendations, guidelines, and frameworks that promote the extension and improvement of social protection programs. Evidence-based policymaking ensures that interventions are targeted, effective, and responsive to the identified social protection gaps.

planEntities.name: Enhanced capacities and mechanisms for gender-disaggregated data collection, analysis, validation and usage to inform policy-making and approaches for gender equality and women empowerment.
planEntities.parentName: Output 2.1: National and international commitments to gender equity and rights-based approaches that inform policy making are realized, through support to government institutions in monitoring implementation of commitments, the production, analysis, and use of sex/gender disaggregated statistics, SDG data and knowledge advocacy and accountability.
planEntities.description:
ILO's strategy to implement this suboutput rests on strengthening the capacity for data collection and analysis in the informal economy which employs women in large numbers and tihs is also an area where formalisation is required so women and men can move to more secure and decent jobs. This involves providing technical assistance and training to national statistical agencies, government institutions, and relevant stakeholders to improve their skills in collecting and disaggregating data by gender in informal economy sectors. The ILO also supports the development of standardized methodologies and tools for data collection to ensure consistency and comparability across different regions and countries.

Secondly, the ILO emphasizes the validation and quality assurance of gender-disaggregated data. This involves establishing mechanisms to ensure the accuracy and reliability of the collected data through rigorous validation processes. The ILO promotes the use of internationally recognized standards and methodologies, including peer review, to validate the data and ensure its credibility. By enhancing the quality of gender-disaggregated data, policymakers can have confidence in the information and make informed decisions to promote gender equality and women's empowerment in the informal economy. Ongoing support to provincial governments in collecting data on home based workers and domestic workers is an example of work to be carried out under this suboutput.

Additionally, the ILO focuses on facilitating the usage of gender-disaggregated data for policy-making and program development. This includes promoting the integration of gender analysis into policy formulation processes, using the data to identify gender-specific challenges and opportunities in the informal economy.

UN Women will support the mainstreaming of gender perspectives in national data collection tools, mechanisms and analysis: Building on its current efforts jointly with national and provincial stake holders, UN Women will develop a comprehensive indicator framework to respond to the data gaps for missing indicators under Pakistan’s national commitments and international reporting requirements. There will be continued focus on the mainstreaming of gender perspective in the SDG data production, analysis and utilization, including gender-disaggregated data and gender statistics at all levels (federal, provincial, local) in civil registration and vital statistics, and building the capacity of various departments to use and analyze available data. This will strengthen the mechanisms for collection, compilation, and use of standardized cross-thematic data to inform evidence-based reforms and interventions and report on the country’s national and international commitments on gender. UN Women will work with the Planning Commission, the National Commission on the Status of Women (NCSW), and the Pakistan Bureau of Statistics to build capacities to collect data and strengthen the indicator framework for gender equality, in order to plug gaps in national surveys. The agency will continue to work with NCSW to build on and strengthen the National Gender Data Portal (NGDP) and link it with sub-national databases and gender management information systems (GMIS), for it to serve as a one-stop repository of gender-disaggregated data and knowledge products. The NGDP will also be leveraged as a platform for linkages with academia, primarily providing direction in the potential areas of research for students and experts.
UNESCO has allocated funds from regular programme to contribute to this sub-output.

planEntities.name: Strengthened government capacities and systems to implement, monitor and report on national and international commitments on Gender Equality and Women Empowerment.
planEntities.parentName: Output 2.1: National and international commitments to gender equity and rights-based approaches that inform policy making are realized, through support to government institutions in monitoring implementation of commitments, the production, analysis, and use of sex/gender disaggregated statistics, SDG data and knowledge advocacy and accountability.
planEntities.description:
The ILO is providing support to governments in addressing concerns raised by the ILO supervisory mechanism regarding the conventions on equal pay for equal value of work and equal training and empowerment opportunities for women. Firstly, the ILO extends support in reviewing and aligning their national legislation and policies with the provisions of these conventions. This includes analyzing existing laws, regulations, and practices to identify gaps and inconsistencies, and providing guidance on legal reforms and policy development to ensure compliance with the principles of equal pay and equal training opportunities. 

Secondly, the ILO supports the government in implementing programs and initiatives that promote equal pay for equal value of work and equal training and empowerment opportunities for women. This involves capacity-building programs to enhance the skills and knowledge of employers, workers, and relevant stakeholders on the principles of equal pay and equal training. The ILO provides technical expertise in designing and implementing gender-responsive wage policies, including the establishment of transparent and fair wage-setting mechanisms. Additionally, the ILOassists the government in developing and implementing training programs and strategies that target the specific needs and barriers faced by women, ensuring they have equal access to training opportunities and support for career advancement. The ILO also facilitates knowledge-sharing and peer learning among governments to exchange best practices and successful strategies in promoting equal pay and equal training opportunities for women.

For strengthening gender data, during reporting period UN Women supported Federal Ministry of Human Rights for preparation of 6th periodic state report on CEDAW. An indicator matrix was developed which carries 97 indicators and trainings were conducted for provincial and  federal departments responsible for collection and provision of relevant data. A total of 5 training sessions were conducted in which 185 officials (100 Men and 85 Women) were trained. Presently data is being collected for writing of the report by MoHR.  

The interplay of climate and gender equality, especially in the context of the Glasgow Climate Change Conference and session 52-55 of COP 26, will also be an area of focus. UN Women will also support linkages and stronger coordination  between oversight institutions such as the National Commission of Human Rights, National Commission for Status of Women (NCSW) and CSO alliances to mobilize support for recommended actions and legislative reforms. Linkages between provincial CSWs and the NCSW will be strengthened including with the CSW of Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK). This will be supplemented by concrete support to women machineries across the country to institutionalize policies on gender equality and empowerment.

UNSCO allocated funds for this sub-put through the support to Ministry of Japan.

planEntities.name: Promoting social protection floors (universal health care and basic income security) including through to birth registration, Computerized National Identity Cards (CNICs) and cash transfer
planEntities.parentName: Output 1.5: Social protection systems and measures are strengthened to provide well-coordinated responses, in an inclusive and shock-responsive manner, to the most deprived and vulnerable populations.
planEntities.description:
ILO's strategy to promote SPFs is based on both conventional and unconventional support. Foremost is the support for Global Accelerator and SPF Design.  This involves developing comprehensive frameworks that outline minimum levels of social protection, including income security, access to essential services, and social transfers for vulnerable populations.

THe ILO is also supporting the Government with  Conducting actuarial analysis of existing health schemes like Sehat Sahulat to evaluate their financial sustainability, efficiency, and coverage effectiveness. And identify gaps and areas for improvement in health schemes based on actuarial findings. The ILO is also providing recommendations to the government for enhancing the design and implementation of health schemes, including adjustments to premiums, benefit packages, and coverage expansion.
The ILO is also collaborating with the government and stakeholders to design income insurance or unemployment benefit schemes that provide financial support to workers during job loss or economic downturns. This includes conducting feasibility studies and actuarial analysis to determine the financial viability and sustainability of these schemes. Developing eligibility criteria, benefit levels, and duration of support in consultation with relevant stakeholders to ensure adequacy and inclusivity.
And finally, the ILO also advocates for and support the implementation of initiatives that facilitate access to social protection, such as the issuance of National Identity Cards (NIC) and birth certification for all individuals. We work with government agencies to streamline the registration process for enterprises, ensuring that businesses are formalized and eligible for social protection benefits.
And strengthen collaboration with the National Insurance Corporation (NIC) and other relevant entities to integrate social protection initiatives and promote accessibility and efficiency in service delivery.

planEntities.name: Fostering innovative solutions for the delivery of existing social protection schemes (including use of IT, service providers etc)
planEntities.parentName: Output 1.5: Social protection systems and measures are strengthened to provide well-coordinated responses, in an inclusive and shock-responsive manner, to the most deprived and vulnerable populations.
planEntities.description:
The ILO recognizes the importance of fostering innovative solutions for the delivery of existing social protection schemes. These innovative approaches leverage technology, service providers, coordinated management information systems (MIS), and universal registries to enhance the effectiveness and efficiency of social protection programs. Here's an explanation and expansion of the ILO's strategy in this regard:
    a. Promote the adoption of information technology solutions, such as digital platforms, mobile applications, and online portals, to streamline the delivery of social protection services.
    b. Facilitate the digitization of processes like registration, enrollment, benefit claims, and payments to reduce administrative burdens, improve accessibility, and enhance transparency.
    c. Develop user-friendly interfaces and secure IT systems that ensure data privacy and protection.
d. collaborate with public and private service providers, including financial institutions, telecom companies, and other relevant entities, to facilitate the delivery of social protection benefits.
    e. Explore partnerships to leverage existing infrastructure and service networks for efficient disbursement of payments, access to healthcare services, and provision of other social protection components.
    f. Establish clear guidelines and standards for service providers to ensure the quality, reliability, and affordability of services provided to beneficiaries.
  g. Promote the establishment of single window service centers where individuals can access multiple social protection schemes and services in a streamlined manner.
    h. These service centers serve as one-stop shops, facilitating simplified processes for registration, information dissemination, and benefit claims.
   i. Coordinate with relevant stakeholders to integrate services and ensure seamless service delivery at these single window centers.
j. Advocate for the development and implementation of coordinated MIS for social protection programs.
    k. These systems enable the collection, storage, and analysis of data related to beneficiaries, coverage, and program performance.
    l. Coordinated MIS help improve monitoring, evaluation, and policy formulation by providing accurate and up-to-date information on the implementation and impact of social protection schemes.
  m. Facilitate the establishment of a universal registry for informal economy workers, ensuring comprehensive coverage and inclusion in social protection programs.
    n. This registry helps identify and enroll informal workers, enabling them to access benefits and services tailored to their needs.
    o. Collaborate with relevant stakeholders, including employers' and workers' organizations, to develop mechanisms for the registration and maintenance of the universal registry.

By fostering innovative solutions for the delivery of social protection schemes, including the use of IT, engagement of service providers, single window services, coordinated MIS, and universal registries for the informal economy, the ILO aims to improve the accessibility, efficiency, and coverage of social protection programs. These approaches contribute to the goal of achieving comprehensive and universal social protection, ensuring that all individuals, including those in vulnerable employment, can access the benefits and support they need.

planEntities.name: Promoting integrated approaches for progressive expansion of coverage (including range of benefits and adequacy - health insurance, social security and protection against violence)
planEntities.parentName: Output 1.5: Social protection systems and measures are strengthened to provide well-coordinated responses, in an inclusive and shock-responsive manner, to the most deprived and vulnerable populations.
planEntities.description:
ILO's strategy to implement this suboutput is to focus on  capacity Building for Coordinating and Expanding Coverage, improving governance and improving integration of different labour market programmes with SP schemes. The following activities will be carried out in 2023-2024 towards this suboutput.
a. Provide training and technical assistance to institutions responsible for coordinating social, economic, and labor protection programs.
b. Enhance their capacity to effectively coordinate and integrate various social protection schemes and services.
c. Offer guidance on expanding coverage to reach marginalized and vulnerable groups, including informal economy workers, women, youth, and persons with disabilities.
d. Support the development of governance frameworks that facilitate effective coordination among departments and agencies responsible for social, economic, and labor protection.
e. Establish mechanisms for interdepartmental collaboration, information sharing, and joint decision-making.
f. Strengthen institutional capacities to monitor and evaluate the implementation and impact of integrated social protection approaches.
g. Promote the adoption of Active Labor Market Programs (ALMPs) to enhance access to social protection and employment opportunities.
h. Provide training and resources to institutions responsible for implementing ALMPs, including employment services, skills development agencies, and vocational training institutions.
i. Raise awareness among jobseekers and employers about the availability and benefits of ALMPs, emphasizing their role in supporting decent work, skills upgrading, and social protection.
j. Conduct awareness-raising campaigns and training programs on key International Labor Standards, such as Forced Labor, Occupational Safety and Health (C190), and protection against violence in the workplace.
k. Work closely with governments, employers' organizations, and workers' organizations to promote the ratification and effective implementation of relevant international conventions and standards.
l. Support the development of policies, guidelines, and mechanisms to ensure compliance with international labor standards, fostering a culture of safety, non-discrimination, and social protection.

m. Encourage the adoption of integrated approaches to expand coverage and ensure the adequacy of social protection programs.
n. Promote the progressive expansion of benefits and coverage, encompassing health insurance, social security, and protection against violence and discrimination.
o. Support research, data collection, and analysis to inform evidence-based decision-making and policy formulation for the expansion and improvement of social protection coverage.

planEntities.name: Facilitating shock responsive livelihoods programmes focusing food security (including through livestock protection and management interventions)
planEntities.parentName: Output 1.5: Social protection systems and measures are strengthened to provide well-coordinated responses, in an inclusive and shock-responsive manner, to the most deprived and vulnerable populations.
planEntities.description:
Facilitating shock-responsive livelihoods programs that focus on food security involves a comprehensive strategy that addresses various aspects of livelihoods and social protection. One key component is livestock protection and management interventions. This involves implementing measures to safeguard the health and well-being of livestock, such as providing vaccinations, improving animal husbandry practices, and establishing early warning systems for disease outbreaks. Additionally, support is given to farmers in managing their livestock effectively, including guidance on breeding, feeding, and ensuring proper shelter.

Another crucial element of the strategy is skills training and entrepreneurship development. This is where ILO will focus on equipping individuals with the necessary skills and knowledge, they can enhance their capacity to earn a sustainable income. Skills training programs can focus on a range of sectors, such as agriculture, handicrafts, or small-scale manufacturing. Additionally, entrepreneurship development initiatives can empower individuals to start their own businesses, providing them with opportunities for income generation and economic resilience.

Furthermore, ILO's strategy will emphasizes the creation of labour-intensive employment opportunities. This involves promoting sectors that have the potential to absorb a large number of workers, such as infrastructure development, construction, or public works projects. By providing employment opportunities, especially during times of shocks or crises, individuals can access income to meet their immediate needs, reducing their vulnerability to food insecurity.

Lastly, the strategy incorporates shock-responsive social protection frameworks. These frameworks aim to provide a safety net for individuals and communities affected by shocks, such as natural disasters or economic downturns. They include mechanisms such as cash transfers, food assistance programs, and social insurance schemes. These social protection measures can help individuals cope with the impacts of shocks, maintain their food security, and mitigate the negative consequences on their livelihoods.

In summary, facilitating shock-responsive livelihoods programs for food security requires a multi-faceted approach. Livestock protection and management interventions ensure the well-being of animals and support farmers in effectively managing their livestock. Skills training and entrepreneurship development equip individuals with the necessary tools to earn a sustainable income. Labor-intensive employment opportunities provide immediate income generation during shocks or crises, while shock-responsive social protection frameworks offer a safety net to mitigate the impacts of shocks on livelihoods. By integrating these strategies, communities can enhance their resilience, ensuring sustainable food security and promoting long-term economic well-being.

planEntities.name: Enhanced capacities and mechanisms for gender-disaggregated data collection, analysis, validation and usage to inform policy-making and approaches for gender equality and women empowerment.
planEntities.parentName: Output 2.1: National and international commitments to gender equity and rights-based approaches that inform policy making are realized, through support to government institutions in monitoring implementation of commitments, the production, analysis, and use of sex/gender disaggregated statistics, SDG data and knowledge advocacy and accountability.
planEntities.description:
ILO's strategy to implement this suboutput rests on strengthening the capacity for data collection and analysis in the informal economy which employs women in large numbers and tihs is also an area where formalisation is required so women and men can move to more secure and decent jobs. This involves providing technical assistance and training to national statistical agencies, government institutions, and relevant stakeholders to improve their skills in collecting and disaggregating data by gender in informal economy sectors. The ILO also supports the development of standardized methodologies and tools for data collection to ensure consistency and comparability across different regions and countries.

Secondly, the ILO emphasizes the validation and quality assurance of gender-disaggregated data. This involves establishing mechanisms to ensure the accuracy and reliability of the collected data through rigorous validation processes. The ILO promotes the use of internationally recognized standards and methodologies, including peer review, to validate the data and ensure its credibility. By enhancing the quality of gender-disaggregated data, policymakers can have confidence in the information and make informed decisions to promote gender equality and women's empowerment in the informal economy. Ongoing support to provincial governments in collecting data on home based workers and domestic workers is an example of work to be carried out under this suboutput.

Additionally, the ILO focuses on facilitating the usage of gender-disaggregated data for policy-making and program development. This includes promoting the integration of gender analysis into policy formulation processes, using the data to identify gender-specific challenges and opportunities in the informal economy.

UN Women will support the mainstreaming of gender perspectives in national data collection tools, mechanisms and analysis: Building on its current efforts jointly with national and provincial stake holders, UN Women will develop a comprehensive indicator framework to respond to the data gaps for missing indicators under Pakistan’s national commitments and international reporting requirements. There will be continued focus on the mainstreaming of gender perspective in the SDG data production, analysis and utilization, including gender-disaggregated data and gender statistics at all levels (federal, provincial, local) in civil registration and vital statistics, and building the capacity of various departments to use and analyze available data. This will strengthen the mechanisms for collection, compilation, and use of standardized cross-thematic data to inform evidence-based reforms and interventions and report on the country’s national and international commitments on gender. UN Women will work with the Planning Commission, the National Commission on the Status of Women (NCSW), and the Pakistan Bureau of Statistics to build capacities to collect data and strengthen the indicator framework for gender equality, in order to plug gaps in national surveys. The agency will continue to work with NCSW to build on and strengthen the National Gender Data Portal (NGDP) and link it with sub-national databases and gender management information systems (GMIS), for it to serve as a one-stop repository of gender-disaggregated data and knowledge products. The NGDP will also be leveraged as a platform for linkages with academia, primarily providing direction in the potential areas of research for students and experts.
UNESCO has allocated funds from regular programme to contribute to this sub-output.

planEntities.name: Enhanced advococy and support for formulation of women-related laws and policies, and their implementation.
planEntities.parentName: Output 2.1: National and international commitments to gender equity and rights-based approaches that inform policy making are realized, through support to government institutions in monitoring implementation of commitments, the production, analysis, and use of sex/gender disaggregated statistics, SDG data and knowledge advocacy and accountability.
planEntities.description:
The ILO has a strategic approach to support Pakistan in formulating and advocating for laws that promote the rights of women in the workforce, including those in informal economy sectors. Firstly, the ILO provides technical assistance to the Pakistani government in conducting comprehensive assessments of existing legal frameworks, identifying gaps, and proposing necessary legislative reforms to ensure gender equality, non-discrimination, and decent work for women. This involves engaging with relevant stakeholders, including employers' and workers' organizations, civil society, and policymakers, to facilitate dialogue, raise awareness, and build consensus on the need for legal reforms. Additionally, the ILO advocates for the adoption and implementation of these laws through policy briefs, research reports, and international conventions, while also providing capacity-building support to strengthen the enforcement and monitoring mechanisms necessary to ensure effective implementation of the laws.

UN Women will support finalization and implementation of a National Gender Policy Framework (NGPF). This will be based on the priorities and recommendations received in periodic reviews. and will correlate reporting between the Beijing Platform for Action Areas of Priority, CEDAW and SDG 5 to put the recommendations into action. The NGPF will provide a comprehensive plan of action to measure the progress against the National Plan of Action for Women’s Development, 1998, and the National Gender Policy of the Planning Commission. UN Women will also continue to engage with provincial Planning & Development Departments to ensure that gender-related policies, including gender tools, are implemented.

planEntities.description:
the ILO's strategy to strengthen the policy environment, capacities, and accountability mechanisms for gender inclusion and gender parity in public and private organizations involves promoting gender-responsive policies, enhancing organizational capacities, and establishing monitoring and accountability mechanisms. Through these efforts, the ILO aims to create an enabling environment where gender equality is prioritized, organizations have the necessary tools and knowledge to implement gender inclusion initiatives, and mechanisms are in place to track progress and ensure accountability towards achieving gender parity in the workplace.
the ILO emphasizes the establishment of accountability mechanisms to monitor progress and ensure gender parity in public and private organizations. This includes supporting the implementation of gender-disaggregated data collection and analysis systems to track indicators of gender equality, such as workforce composition, pay gaps, and career advancement opportunities. The ILO assists organizations in setting targets and benchmarks for gender parity and provides guidance on designing and implementing effective monitoring and evaluation frameworks. The organization also encourages the establishment of gender equality committees or focal points within organizations to oversee progress, promote accountability, and address gender-related issues.

planEntities.name: Enhanced capacities and mechanisms for gender-disaggregated data collection, analysis, validation and usage to inform policy-making and approaches for gender equality and women empowerment.
planEntities.parentName: Output 2.1: National and international commitments to gender equity and rights-based approaches that inform policy making are realized, through support to government institutions in monitoring implementation of commitments, the production, analysis, and use of sex/gender disaggregated statistics, SDG data and knowledge advocacy and accountability.
planEntities.description:
ILO's strategy to implement this suboutput rests on strengthening the capacity for data collection and analysis in the informal economy which employs women in large numbers and tihs is also an area where formalisation is required so women and men can move to more secure and decent jobs. This involves providing technical assistance and training to national statistical agencies, government institutions, and relevant stakeholders to improve their skills in collecting and disaggregating data by gender in informal economy sectors. The ILO also supports the development of standardized methodologies and tools for data collection to ensure consistency and comparability across different regions and countries.

Secondly, the ILO emphasizes the validation and quality assurance of gender-disaggregated data. This involves establishing mechanisms to ensure the accuracy and reliability of the collected data through rigorous validation processes. The ILO promotes the use of internationally recognized standards and methodologies, including peer review, to validate the data and ensure its credibility. By enhancing the quality of gender-disaggregated data, policymakers can have confidence in the information and make informed decisions to promote gender equality and women's empowerment in the informal economy. Ongoing support to provincial governments in collecting data on home based workers and domestic workers is an example of work to be carried out under this suboutput.

Additionally, the ILO focuses on facilitating the usage of gender-disaggregated data for policy-making and program development. This includes promoting the integration of gender analysis into policy formulation processes, using the data to identify gender-specific challenges and opportunities in the informal economy.

UN Women will support the mainstreaming of gender perspectives in national data collection tools, mechanisms and analysis: Building on its current efforts jointly with national and provincial stake holders, UN Women will develop a comprehensive indicator framework to respond to the data gaps for missing indicators under Pakistan’s national commitments and international reporting requirements. There will be continued focus on the mainstreaming of gender perspective in the SDG data production, analysis and utilization, including gender-disaggregated data and gender statistics at all levels (federal, provincial, local) in civil registration and vital statistics, and building the capacity of various departments to use and analyze available data. This will strengthen the mechanisms for collection, compilation, and use of standardized cross-thematic data to inform evidence-based reforms and interventions and report on the country’s national and international commitments on gender. UN Women will work with the Planning Commission, the National Commission on the Status of Women (NCSW), and the Pakistan Bureau of Statistics to build capacities to collect data and strengthen the indicator framework for gender equality, in order to plug gaps in national surveys. The agency will continue to work with NCSW to build on and strengthen the National Gender Data Portal (NGDP) and link it with sub-national databases and gender management information systems (GMIS), for it to serve as a one-stop repository of gender-disaggregated data and knowledge products. The NGDP will also be leveraged as a platform for linkages with academia, primarily providing direction in the potential areas of research for students and experts.
UNESCO has allocated funds from regular programme to contribute to this sub-output.

planEntities.name: Promoting social protection floors (universal health care and basic income security) including through to birth registration, Computerized National Identity Cards (CNICs) and cash transfer
planEntities.parentName: Output 1.5: Social protection systems and measures are strengthened to provide well-coordinated responses, in an inclusive and shock-responsive manner, to the most deprived and vulnerable populations.
planEntities.description:
ILO's strategy to promote SPFs is based on both conventional and unconventional support. Foremost is the support for Global Accelerator and SPF Design.  This involves developing comprehensive frameworks that outline minimum levels of social protection, including income security, access to essential services, and social transfers for vulnerable populations.

THe ILO is also supporting the Government with  Conducting actuarial analysis of existing health schemes like Sehat Sahulat to evaluate their financial sustainability, efficiency, and coverage effectiveness. And identify gaps and areas for improvement in health schemes based on actuarial findings. The ILO is also providing recommendations to the government for enhancing the design and implementation of health schemes, including adjustments to premiums, benefit packages, and coverage expansion.
The ILO is also collaborating with the government and stakeholders to design income insurance or unemployment benefit schemes that provide financial support to workers during job loss or economic downturns. This includes conducting feasibility studies and actuarial analysis to determine the financial viability and sustainability of these schemes. Developing eligibility criteria, benefit levels, and duration of support in consultation with relevant stakeholders to ensure adequacy and inclusivity.
And finally, the ILO also advocates for and support the implementation of initiatives that facilitate access to social protection, such as the issuance of National Identity Cards (NIC) and birth certification for all individuals. We work with government agencies to streamline the registration process for enterprises, ensuring that businesses are formalized and eligible for social protection benefits.
And strengthen collaboration with the National Insurance Corporation (NIC) and other relevant entities to integrate social protection initiatives and promote accessibility and efficiency in service delivery.

planEntities.name: Promoting integrated approaches for progressive expansion of coverage (including range of benefits and adequacy - health insurance, social security and protection against violence)
planEntities.parentName: Output 1.5: Social protection systems and measures are strengthened to provide well-coordinated responses, in an inclusive and shock-responsive manner, to the most deprived and vulnerable populations.
planEntities.description:
ILO's strategy to implement this suboutput is to focus on  capacity Building for Coordinating and Expanding Coverage, improving governance and improving integration of different labour market programmes with SP schemes. The following activities will be carried out in 2023-2024 towards this suboutput.
a. Provide training and technical assistance to institutions responsible for coordinating social, economic, and labor protection programs.
b. Enhance their capacity to effectively coordinate and integrate various social protection schemes and services.
c. Offer guidance on expanding coverage to reach marginalized and vulnerable groups, including informal economy workers, women, youth, and persons with disabilities.
d. Support the development of governance frameworks that facilitate effective coordination among departments and agencies responsible for social, economic, and labor protection.
e. Establish mechanisms for interdepartmental collaboration, information sharing, and joint decision-making.
f. Strengthen institutional capacities to monitor and evaluate the implementation and impact of integrated social protection approaches.
g. Promote the adoption of Active Labor Market Programs (ALMPs) to enhance access to social protection and employment opportunities.
h. Provide training and resources to institutions responsible for implementing ALMPs, including employment services, skills development agencies, and vocational training institutions.
i. Raise awareness among jobseekers and employers about the availability and benefits of ALMPs, emphasizing their role in supporting decent work, skills upgrading, and social protection.
j. Conduct awareness-raising campaigns and training programs on key International Labor Standards, such as Forced Labor, Occupational Safety and Health (C190), and protection against violence in the workplace.
k. Work closely with governments, employers' organizations, and workers' organizations to promote the ratification and effective implementation of relevant international conventions and standards.
l. Support the development of policies, guidelines, and mechanisms to ensure compliance with international labor standards, fostering a culture of safety, non-discrimination, and social protection.

m. Encourage the adoption of integrated approaches to expand coverage and ensure the adequacy of social protection programs.
n. Promote the progressive expansion of benefits and coverage, encompassing health insurance, social security, and protection against violence and discrimination.
o. Support research, data collection, and analysis to inform evidence-based decision-making and policy formulation for the expansion and improvement of social protection coverage.

planEntities.name: Facilitating shock responsive livelihoods programmes focusing food security (including through livestock protection and management interventions)
planEntities.parentName: Output 1.5: Social protection systems and measures are strengthened to provide well-coordinated responses, in an inclusive and shock-responsive manner, to the most deprived and vulnerable populations.
planEntities.description:
Facilitating shock-responsive livelihoods programs that focus on food security involves a comprehensive strategy that addresses various aspects of livelihoods and social protection. One key component is livestock protection and management interventions. This involves implementing measures to safeguard the health and well-being of livestock, such as providing vaccinations, improving animal husbandry practices, and establishing early warning systems for disease outbreaks. Additionally, support is given to farmers in managing their livestock effectively, including guidance on breeding, feeding, and ensuring proper shelter.

Another crucial element of the strategy is skills training and entrepreneurship development. This is where ILO will focus on equipping individuals with the necessary skills and knowledge, they can enhance their capacity to earn a sustainable income. Skills training programs can focus on a range of sectors, such as agriculture, handicrafts, or small-scale manufacturing. Additionally, entrepreneurship development initiatives can empower individuals to start their own businesses, providing them with opportunities for income generation and economic resilience.

Furthermore, ILO's strategy will emphasizes the creation of labour-intensive employment opportunities. This involves promoting sectors that have the potential to absorb a large number of workers, such as infrastructure development, construction, or public works projects. By providing employment opportunities, especially during times of shocks or crises, individuals can access income to meet their immediate needs, reducing their vulnerability to food insecurity.

Lastly, the strategy incorporates shock-responsive social protection frameworks. These frameworks aim to provide a safety net for individuals and communities affected by shocks, such as natural disasters or economic downturns. They include mechanisms such as cash transfers, food assistance programs, and social insurance schemes. These social protection measures can help individuals cope with the impacts of shocks, maintain their food security, and mitigate the negative consequences on their livelihoods.

In summary, facilitating shock-responsive livelihoods programs for food security requires a multi-faceted approach. Livestock protection and management interventions ensure the well-being of animals and support farmers in effectively managing their livestock. Skills training and entrepreneurship development equip individuals with the necessary tools to earn a sustainable income. Labor-intensive employment opportunities provide immediate income generation during shocks or crises, while shock-responsive social protection frameworks offer a safety net to mitigate the impacts of shocks on livelihoods. By integrating these strategies, communities can enhance their resilience, ensuring sustainable food security and promoting long-term economic well-being.

planEntities.name: Enhanced capacities and mechanisms for gender-disaggregated data collection, analysis, validation and usage to inform policy-making and approaches for gender equality and women empowerment.
planEntities.parentName: Output 2.1: National and international commitments to gender equity and rights-based approaches that inform policy making are realized, through support to government institutions in monitoring implementation of commitments, the production, analysis, and use of sex/gender disaggregated statistics, SDG data and knowledge advocacy and accountability.
planEntities.description:
ILO's strategy to implement this suboutput rests on strengthening the capacity for data collection and analysis in the informal economy which employs women in large numbers and tihs is also an area where formalisation is required so women and men can move to more secure and decent jobs. This involves providing technical assistance and training to national statistical agencies, government institutions, and relevant stakeholders to improve their skills in collecting and disaggregating data by gender in informal economy sectors. The ILO also supports the development of standardized methodologies and tools for data collection to ensure consistency and comparability across different regions and countries.

Secondly, the ILO emphasizes the validation and quality assurance of gender-disaggregated data. This involves establishing mechanisms to ensure the accuracy and reliability of the collected data through rigorous validation processes. The ILO promotes the use of internationally recognized standards and methodologies, including peer review, to validate the data and ensure its credibility. By enhancing the quality of gender-disaggregated data, policymakers can have confidence in the information and make informed decisions to promote gender equality and women's empowerment in the informal economy. Ongoing support to provincial governments in collecting data on home based workers and domestic workers is an example of work to be carried out under this suboutput.

Additionally, the ILO focuses on facilitating the usage of gender-disaggregated data for policy-making and program development. This includes promoting the integration of gender analysis into policy formulation processes, using the data to identify gender-specific challenges and opportunities in the informal economy.

UN Women will support the mainstreaming of gender perspectives in national data collection tools, mechanisms and analysis: Building on its current efforts jointly with national and provincial stake holders, UN Women will develop a comprehensive indicator framework to respond to the data gaps for missing indicators under Pakistan’s national commitments and international reporting requirements. There will be continued focus on the mainstreaming of gender perspective in the SDG data production, analysis and utilization, including gender-disaggregated data and gender statistics at all levels (federal, provincial, local) in civil registration and vital statistics, and building the capacity of various departments to use and analyze available data. This will strengthen the mechanisms for collection, compilation, and use of standardized cross-thematic data to inform evidence-based reforms and interventions and report on the country’s national and international commitments on gender. UN Women will work with the Planning Commission, the National Commission on the Status of Women (NCSW), and the Pakistan Bureau of Statistics to build capacities to collect data and strengthen the indicator framework for gender equality, in order to plug gaps in national surveys. The agency will continue to work with NCSW to build on and strengthen the National Gender Data Portal (NGDP) and link it with sub-national databases and gender management information systems (GMIS), for it to serve as a one-stop repository of gender-disaggregated data and knowledge products. The NGDP will also be leveraged as a platform for linkages with academia, primarily providing direction in the potential areas of research for students and experts.
UNESCO has allocated funds from regular programme to contribute to this sub-output.

planEntities.name: Fortalecimiento de capacidades institucionales, de comunidades locales y alianzas publico-privadas para la recopilación, monitoreo y gestión de datos del jaguar y sus presas en áreas protegidas - Proyecto GEF Jaguares.
planEntities.parentName: Socios claves implementan mecanismos para la gestión integral equitativa, transparente y sostenible de los recursos naturales, biodiversidad y los ecosistemas estratégicos.
planEntities.description: El Proyecto GEF - 10285 busca principalmente la conservación de los jaguares a través de la promoción de la conectividad entre el punto de vulnerabilidad y el hábitat más grande del jaguar; medidas a nivel de paisaje para reducir los conflictos entre los seres humanos y la vida silvestre causados por la pérdida y fragmentación del hábitat; una gestión mejor informada de las áreas protegidas que integre información sólida sobre el estado de los gatos monteses y sus presas; y un centro institucionalizado de investigación e información sobre el jaguar al servicio de las poblaciones de jaguares en América Central y del Sur. EL proyecto está compuesto por tres componentes que buscan de manera puntual: 1. La conservación de Jaguares y sus presas a través de la promoción de la conectividad y el manejo del conflicto humano-vida silvestre; y 2. Mediante la generación de conocimiento científico, construcción de capacidades nacionales y la promoción de compromisos nacionales orientados a la conservación de los jaguares.

planEntities.description: El objetivo de la subvención de Preparación propuesta es apoyar a Panamá para movilizar financiamiento privado para la implementación de sus objetivos nacionales de clima, tal como se articula en su Estrategia Nacional de Cambio Climático 2030-2050 y su NDC actualizada, a través del desarrollo de una taxonomía nacional de finanzas sostenibles bien definida y metodologías relacionadas para el sector financiero – bancos y aseguradoras – para identificar, evaluar y divulgar su exposición a riesgos financieros relacionados con el clima, así como recomendaciones dirigidas a autoridades reguladoras y de supervisión financiera para evaluar los riesgos relacionados con el clima. Específicamente, las recomendaciones incluirán medidas políticas dentro del marco regulatorio que deberían ser adoptadas por las autoridades reguladoras y de supervisión para mejorar la resiliencia del sistema financiero frente a los riesgos financieros relacionados con el clima.

planEntities.description: Mediante el Proyecto GCF, se busca construcción de capacidades sostenibles al igual que el fortalecimiento de la participación de las distintas partes interesadas para planificar, financiar, implementar, monitorear y reportar respecto de los procesos de adaptación estratégicos y comunicación sobre la adaptación al cambio climático. El proceso NAP cubrir 10 temas de adaptación en total, los cuales están planteadas en case a las NDC de Panamá ya actualizadas, asegurando su alineación con las estrategias y prioridades de cambio climático.

planEntities.name: Fortalecer de capacidades nacionales el sistema nacional de transparencia para el cambio climático mediante la mejora de la Plataforma de Transparencia, así como el Sistema de Monitoreo, Reporte y Verificación (MRV) subyacente de Panamá - Proyecto CBIT II.
planEntities.parentName: Instituciones y socios claves formulan e implementan políticas que impulsan la productividad, el acceso a mercados, economía sostenible y creativa, así como la innovación en sectores estratégico para facilitar la transición digital y ambiental de manera inclusiva.
planEntities.description: Este proyecto CBIT fase 2 busca construir sobre los logros de la CBIT fase 1 que se finalizó en 2022. Como tal, el objetivo general es fortalecer aún más el sistema nacional de transparencia para el cambio climático mediante la mejora de la Plataforma de Transparencia, así como del Sistema subyacente de Monitoreo, Reporte y Verificación (MRV) de Panamá. Por lo tanto, el proyecto CBIT responde a la necesidad de Panamá, como país signatario del Acuerdo de París, de establecer sistemas funcionales que permitan la presentación de informes sobre información del cambio climático bajo las directrices internacionales de reporte según lo estipulado por el Marco de Transparencia Mejorado.

planEntities.name: Desarrollo de capacidades a nivel de MiAmbiente y herramientas nacionales y regionales para preparar la implementación de los Mercados de Carbono y el Artículo 6 en América Latina. - Carbon Mkts Regional Project.
planEntities.parentName: Instituciones y socios claves formulan e implementan políticas que impulsan la productividad, el acceso a mercados, economía sostenible y creativa, así como la innovación en sectores estratégico para facilitar la transición digital y ambiental de manera inclusiva.
planEntities.description: Según el Banco Mundial, la fijación de precios del carbono es una forma eficaz de reducir las emisiones y todas las jurisdicciones deben ir más allá y con mayor rapidez en el uso de políticas de fijación de precios del carbono como parte de sus paquetes de políticas climáticas. Si está bien diseñada y es suficientemente ambiciosa, la fijación de precios del carbono puede crear fuertes incentivos económicos para los cambios necesarios en los patrones de inversión, producción y consumo, e inducir avances tecnológicos, reduciendo la magnitud de la inversión pública adicional necesaria. Por lo tanto, la fijación de precios del carbono a través de los mercados de carbono y el Artículo 6 del Acuerdo de París desempeña un papel crucial para que los gobiernos y el sector privado puedan cumplir los compromisos de cero emisiones o neutralidad de carbono para 2050, como propone el Panel Intergubernamental sobre el Cambio Climático (IPCC).

planEntities.description: Este subproducto se enfoca en la modernización y adecuación de las sedes de formación del INADEH bajo estrictos estándares de construcción sostenible. Las acciones aseguran que la nueva infraestructura sea resiliente frente al cambio climático, garantice la accesibilidad universal (inclusión) y cuente con espacios diseñados con perspectiva de género. De esta manera, se promueve la alineación de la inversión pública con los marcos normativos ambientales y sociales, optimizando el entorno para la formación técnica profesional y fomentando la igualdad de oportunidades y la gestión eficiente de los recursos.

planEntities.name: Asistencia técnica a SENACYT, en la dotación de infraestructura sostenible de la Fase A de la Estación Científica Coiba en el Parque Nacional de Coiba.

planEntities.description: Este sub-output proporciona acompañamiento técnico especializado para la materialización física de la Estación Científica Coiba. Dada su ubicación estratégica en un área protegida y Patrimonio de la Humanidad, la asistencia garantiza el cumplimiento riguroso de los acuerdos ambientales multilaterales y la normativa del Parque Nacional. El proyecto implementa soluciones de infraestructura de bajo impacto, incluyendo la gestión eficiente del agua, energía y tratamiento de residuos. El resultado fortalecerá la capacidad institucional para la investigación científica y la conservación de la biodiversidad, consolidando un modelo de infraestructura resiliente y ecológicamente responsable.

planEntities.name: Fortalecimiento al INADEH en un Modelo de Gestión Institucional integral para fortalecer su capacidad operativa y sostenibilidad, articulando la modernización de su estructura organizacional y marco legal con la adopción de nuevos sistemas tecnológicos y el desarrollo de capacidades de su capital humano.

planEntities.description: Este sub-output impulsa una transformación profunda en la gobernanza del INADEH, alineada con la innovación y la toma de decisiones basada en evidencia. Mediante la actualización de su marco legal y estructura organizativa, junto con la implementación de nuevos sistemas tecnológicos (ERP/Plataformas de Formación), se optimiza la interoperabilidad institucional y la gestión de datos. Esto fortalece la capacidad del Estado para administrar los recursos de manera eficiente y transparente, garantizando que el desarrollo del capital humano responda ágilmente a las demandas del mercado laboral bajo principios de inclusión y sostenibilidad institucional.

planEntities.name: Fortalecimiento a la Unidad Coordinadora de Infraestructura Pública (UCIP) del Ministerio de Obras Públicas, proporcionando las herramientas, metodologías y acompañamiento necesario para la puesta en marcha efectiva de la Unidad.

Mediante la transferencia de metodologías ágiles, herramientas de gestión de proyectos y acompañamiento técnico especializado, se dota a la institución de capacidades para el uso estratégico de datos y la toma de decisiones informadas. Esto permite una planificación, adjudicación y supervisión de la infraestructura pública más transparente, eficiente y resiliente, fortaleciendo el rol del Estado en la provisión de servicios y obras que benefician a la población.

planEntities.name: Initiative for Climate Action Transparency
planEntities.parentName: Socios claves implementan mecanismos para la gestión integral equitativa, transparente y sostenible de los recursos naturales, biodiversidad y los ecosistemas estratégicos.
planEntities.description: The Initiative for Climate Action Transparency (ICAT) is partnering with Fundación Natura to strengthen Panama's Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) systems for climate change adaptation and the registration of losses and damages. In collaboration with the Ministry of Environment's Climate Change Directorate, this project aims to systematize data for Panama’s Biennial Transparency Reports and Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs). The initiative will analyze economic and non-economic losses, build capacities to integrate subnational and non-state actors into M&E frameworks, and enhance the M&E Module within the Panama Climate Transparency Platform. Ultimately, this effort will guarantee the continuity of national planning instruments, increase climate data transparency, and improve the implementation of the M&E system.
