planEntities.name: Aumento de las capacidades de las instituciones para reducir la carga de enfermedades no transmisibles y salud mental basadas en APS de manera intersectorial.
planEntities.parentName: Instituciones proveedoras de servicios sociales están fortalecidas y cuentan con las capacidades humanas, financieras, y los sistemas para ofrecer bienes y servicios de calidad, basados en derechos, con enfoque de género, con sensibilidad y pertinencia cultural.
planEntities.description: Se busca fortalecer el sistema de salud en Panamá mediante el fortalecimiento de la integración de la prevención y atención de enfermedades no transmisibles y de salud mental en la Atención Primaria de Salud (APS). Esto implica mejorar la capacidad institucional, la gestión de recursos y la acción intersectorial para reducir la carga de enfermedades y garantizar un acceso equitativo. Implica, además, capacitar al personal de salud no especializado para gestionar problemas de salud mental y enfermedades crónicas (cardiovasculares, diabetes, cáncer) a nivel comunitario. La cooperación en este tema responde a la necesidad de disminuir la fragmentación del sistema y asegurar que la atención llegue a las comunidades más vulnerables.

planEntities.name: Aumento de las capacidades de las instituciones para reducir el impacto en la salud pública de las enfermedades transmisibles de manera intersectorial.
planEntities.parentName: Instituciones proveedoras de servicios sociales están fortalecidas y cuentan con las capacidades humanas, financieras, y los sistemas para ofrecer bienes y servicios de calidad, basados en derechos, con enfoque de género, con sensibilidad y pertinencia cultural.
planEntities.description: La acción en este subproducto se centra en la lucha contra las enfermedades transmisibles de manera intersectorial que implica articular acciones entre el sector de la salud, organismos públicos, privados y la comunidad para abordar los determinantes sociales, ambientales y económicos, yendo más allá de la atención clínica, que también será fortalecida, con el fin de mejorar la equidad y reducir la morbilidad y mortalidad. Se fortalecerá el enfoque de Una Salud (coordinación entre salud humana, sanidad animal y medio ambiente para prevenir brotes (ej. dengue, zoonosis); mejorar la vigilancia epidemiológica, laboratorios, y respuesta rápida ante emergencias sanitarias; incorporar a la sociedad civil en la prevención y promoción de la salud para lograr cobertura universal, entre otras acciones.

planEntities.name: Fortalecimiento de las capacidades de los sistemas nacionales de provisión de salud integrados para garantizar acceso equitativo a servicios de calidad, centrados en las personas y comunidades.
planEntities.parentName: Instituciones proveedoras de servicios sociales están fortalecidas y cuentan con las capacidades humanas, financieras, y los sistemas para ofrecer bienes y servicios de calidad, basados en derechos, con enfoque de género, con sensibilidad y pertinencia cultural.
planEntities.description: Se busca contribuir a garantizar la salud universal, eliminando barreras de acceso y mejorando la equidad mediante la Atención Primaria de Salud (APS). Implica transitar de modelos fragmentados a Redes Integradas de Servicios de Salud (RISS), centrados en las personas y comunidades, con financiamiento sostenible y gobernanza robusta para asegurar calidad. Esto permite ampliar el acceso a servicios integrales y de calidad sin que el pago sea una barrera; asegurar que los servicios respondan a las necesidades contextuales, familiares y sociales, no solo a la enfermedad; y a reducir desigualdades en salud y fortalecer la capacidad de respuesta de los sistemas ante crisis.

planEntities.name: Fortalecimiento de las capacidades de la Autoridad Sanitaria Nacional para la implementación y diseño de políticas públicas, coordinadas de manera intersectorial y con enfoque territorial, avanzando hacia el acceso universal de la salud.
planEntities.parentName: Instituciones y socios clave diseñan, implementan y evalúan políticas sociales, planes y programas intersectoriales que promuevan el piso de protección social con enfoque territorial, de derechos humanos, de género y ciclo de vida.
planEntities.description: Las acciones potenciarán la capacidad rectora del Ministerio de Salud (Autoridad Sanitaria Nacional) para diseñar e implementar políticas públicas. Implica coordinar acciones entre diversos sectores (educación, vivienda, economía) con un enfoque en el territorio local, buscando superar brechas de equidad y asegurar el acceso y cobertura universal a la salud. Se potenciará la capacidad del MINSA para ejercer su función rectora, asegurando la gobernanza, el financiamiento y la regulación efectiva del sistema de salud.

planEntities.name: Estudio Actuarial que tiene por objeto estimar el porcentaje del credito de la seguridad social para financiar el Plan Esencial de Aseguramiento en salud (PEAS) por parte de las Entidades Prestadoras de Salud (EPS)
planEntities.parentName: Las instituciones y actores nacionales y subnacionales fortalecen sus capacidades para diseñar e implementar políticas públicas – incluyendo marcos legales y de financiamiento, sistemas de gestión e información, y seguimiento y rendición de cuentas – orientadas a mejorar el acceso al trabajo decente, a la vivienda digna y espacios públicos adecuados, y a un sistema integral de protección social, incluyendo un piso de protección social, que garantice seguridad económica, cobertura de salud y acceso a un sistema nacional de cuidados a lo largo de todo el ciclo vital, con énfasis en las poblaciones y territorios en situación de especial protección, o en situación de vulnerabilidad y/o precariedad, atendiendo las brechas de género, generacionales y por nacionalidad.
planEntities.description: Este proyecto elabora un estudio actuarial con el proposito de estimar el porcentaje del credito de la seguridad social para financiar el Plan Esencial de Aseguramiento en Salud (PEAS) por parte de las Entidades Prestadoras de Salud - EPA. Este estudio sirve como insumo para la elaboracion del Estudio Tecnico del Cálculo del Crédito (ETCC) por parte de las autoridades e instituciones respectivas. Para ello, la OIT debe: Primero, realizar el análisis exhaustivo de los beneficios de salud pagados por EPS, así como los ingresos del crédito complementario de la seguridad social, para el período 2016 a 2021 (sujeto a disponibilidad de datos). Segundo, basándose en el análisis de la evolución de los factores macroeconómicos relevantes, así como de los indicadores específicos de la población asegurada, se desarrolla supuestos actuariales sobre la evolución futura de estos factores e indicadores. Tercero, proyectar los gastos de beneficios de salud, así como los ingresos asegurables futuros para evaluar el porcentaje de ingresos asegurables requeridos para la cobertura del PEAS y, en consecuencia, la parte de la contribución de la seguridad social que se acredite a EPS para el financiamiento del PEAS. Finalmente, evalua la sostenibilidad financiera de la propuesta a través de escenarios y análisis de sensibilidad

planEntities.parentName: Las instituciones y actores nacionales y subnacionales fortalecen sus capacidades para diseñar e implementar políticas públicas – incluyendo marcos legales y de financiamiento, sistemas de gestión e información, y seguimiento y rendición de cuentas – orientadas a mejorar el acceso a mercados internos e internacionales, la inclusión económica y medios de vida sostenibles y resilientes para las poblaciones en situación de mayor vulnerabilidad, en particular los pequeños productores y empresarios,  tomando en cuenta un enfoque territorial, intergeneracional e intercultural y en condiciones de igualdad de género.
planEntities.description: El objetivo del proyecto es reforzar la capacidad del Gobierno, las organizaciones de trabajadores y de empleadores y los actores de la sociedad civil para mejorar la integración socioeconómica de las mujeres refugiadas y migrantes procedentes de Venezuela en Colombia, Ecuador y Perú. Asimismo, mejorará el acceso de los migrantes a los Servicios Públicos de Empleo (SPE) mediante un enfoque inclusivo y no discriminatorio, junto con servicios de desarrollo empresarial, con el fin de facilitar la integración laboral y productiva de los refugiados y migrantes, especialmente de las mujeres y las personas con experiencia de vida transgénero. El proyecto mejorará las capacidades de las organizaciones de empleadores y de trabajadores, así como de las organizaciones de la sociedad civil, para prestar servicios y orientación a las mujeres refugiadas y migrantes y a las personas con experiencia de vida transgénero, en particular a aquellas que sufren violencia y discriminación, con miras a una integración socioeconómica sostenible. También mejorará los mecanismos de integración regional y la agenda institucional de los procesos consultivos en lo que respecta a la integración socioeconómica de los refugiados y migrantes, especialmente de las mujeres.

planEntities.name: Transformando las economías. Hacia el Reconocimiento, reducción y redistribución del trabajo doméstico y de cuidados no remunerado en América Latina y el Caribe - Fase II
planEntities.parentName: Las instituciones y actores nacionales y subnacionales fortalecen sus capacidades para diseñar e implementar políticas públicas – incluyendo marcos legales y de financiamiento, sistemas de gestión e información, y seguimiento y rendición de cuentas – orientadas a mejorar el acceso al trabajo decente, a la vivienda digna y espacios públicos adecuados, y a un sistema integral de protección social, incluyendo un piso de protección social, que garantice seguridad económica, cobertura de salud y acceso a un sistema nacional de cuidados a lo largo de todo el ciclo vital, con énfasis en las poblaciones y territorios en situación de especial protección, o en situación de vulnerabilidad y/o precariedad, atendiendo las brechas de género, generacionales y por nacionalidad.
planEntities.description:
El proyecto “Transformando las economías” busca promover la autonomía económica y el bienestar de las mujeres en América Latina y el Caribe mediante el acceso a políticas y sistemas integrales de cuidado. En esta tercera fase, se desarrollarán políticas y sistemas integrales de cuidados en el nivel local a partir de un modelo escalable y metodologías de implementación, que permitan su replicabilidad. Este enfoque también busca fortalecer la cooperación birregional entre América Latina, el Caribe y Europa, impulsando el desarrollo de sistemas integrales de cuidados en ambas regiones.
El presente proyecto abarca tanto el ámbito regional como nacional, enfocándose en Ecuador, México, Panamá, Perú y República Dominicana, bajo la coordinación de ONU Mujeres y con el apoyo financiero de la Agencia Española de Cooperación Internacional para el Desarrollo (AECID) y fondos adicionales propios. La duración del proyecto es hasta junio2026

planEntities.name: Acelerar el cumplimiento del Convenio de Minamata mediante una mejor comprensión y control del comercio de mercurio en América Latina (Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador, Honduras, Mexico, Peru)
planEntities.parentName: Las instituciones y actores nacionales y subnacionales fortalecen sus capacidades para diseñar e implementar políticas públicas – incluyendo marcos legales y de financiamiento, sistemas de gestión e información, y seguimiento y rendición de cuentas – orientadas a mejorar la gestión ambiental, la gestión, protección y conservación  de la biodiversidad y la naturaleza y la mitigación del cambio climático, desde un enfoque integrado y multiactor.
planEntities.description: El proyecto apoyará específicamente la redacción o adaptación de instrumentos jurídicos (disposiciones para controlar la importación/exportación y las transferencias internas) de los seis países participantes en consonancia con sus obligaciones en virtud del artículo 3 del Convenio. También creará un consenso nacional para su respaldo. Paralelamente, elaborará estrategias para hacer frente al comercio ilícito dentro de los países y entre ellos. El proyecto impartirá capacitación a nivel nacional a los funcionarios de comercio, aduanas y control fronterizo de todos los países destinatarios a fin de garantizar la coherencia de los procedimientos y las medidas para una aplicación eficaz a nivel nacional y regional. Finalmente, la participación del Observatorio Andino de Mercurio como red regional promoverá la articulación regional y la complementariedad de esfuerzos durante la ejecución del proyecto. También garantizará la sostenibilidad de las intervenciones del proyecto y seguirá vigilando y rastreando los flujos de mercurio una vez finalizado el proyecto..

planEntities.parentName: Las instituciones y actores nacionales y subnacionales fortalecen sus capacidades para diseñar e implementar políticas públicas – incluyendo marcos legales y de financiamiento, sistemas de gestión e información, y seguimiento y rendición de cuentas – orientadas a mejorar la gestión ambiental, la gestión, protección y conservación  de la biodiversidad y la naturaleza y la mitigación del cambio climático, desde un enfoque integrado y multiactor.
planEntities.description: El proyecto tiene como objetivo catalizar un despliegue más amplio del enfoque IAA6 a nivel regional y mundial. Al aprovechar los progresos existentes y adaptarse al contexto específico de cada país, la aplicación del Enfoque es valiosa, incluso si el artículo 6 no se utiliza ampliamente después de la evaluación. La aplicación del artículo 6 puede ayudar a facilitar flujos financieros adicionales de los países de ingresos altos a los de ingresos bajos. El enfoque ayudará a llenar las brechas identificadas (por ejemplo, la gestión de datos climáticos o la planificación de políticas nacionales) para mejorar la toma de decisiones.

planEntities.description: Fortalecer las capacidades de las instituciones y los actores nacionales y subnacionales para transformar las normas sociales y de género discriminatorias, abordando los vínculos entre las masculinidades hegemónicas y el embarazo adolescente, los matrimonios infantiles/uniones tempranas y la violencia sexual. El programa utilizará una combinación de rutas destinadas a promover las masculinidades positivas, avanzar en la implementación de programas de educación sexual integral dentro y fuera de la escuela, y crear conciencia sobre el derecho a la autonomía corporal y a una vida libre de violencia mediante campañas de comunicación.

planEntities.description: Fortalecer las capacidades de las instituciones nacionales y subnacionales para implementar marcos legales, de políticas y de rendición de cuentas que prioricen al acceso universal a la planificación familiar y la anticoncepción de calidad, como parte del paquete integral de servicios de salud sexual y reproductiva, en contextos de desarrollo y humanitarios. Se enfatizará la ampliación del acceso a la gama de anticonceptivos desde un enfoque basado en los derechos humanos, en particular anticonceptivos modernos (incluidos los anticonceptivos reversibles de acción prolongada o LARC, por sus siglas en inglés), para las mujeres y las adolescentes más rezagadas (de bajos ingresos, zonas rurales, indígenas, afroperuanas, migrantes y personas con discapacidad).

Se prestará especial atención a la mejora de la calidad de los servicios de salud materna, incluyendo el acceso a la atención obstétrica integral de emergencia para las mujeres, niñas y adolescentes de los grupos y territorios más rezagados.

planEntities.name: Políticas y servicios - violencia basada en género y prácticas nocivas

Se utilizarán enfoques de derechos humanos, género, interseccionalidad e interculturalidad, alcanzando a las mujeres y adolescentes (particularmente menores de 15 años) que pertenecen a los territorios y poblaciones más rezagadas (indígenas, afroperuanos, LGBTIQ+, personas con discapacidad y migrantes).

planEntities.parentName: Las instituciones y actores nacionales y subnacionales fortalecen sus capacidades para diseñar e implementar políticas públicas – incluyendo marcos legales y de financiamiento, sistemas de gestión e información, y seguimiento y rendición de cuentas – orientadas a promover una gestión, administración y gasto público eficiente, efectivo,  descentralizado y orientado a las personas, articulado,  con un enfoque de desarrollo sostenible,  así como el gobierno abierto y la cohesión social vertical.
planEntities.description: El proyecto SIMCI busca brindar apoyo técnico al Estado peruano enfocado en 7 componentes: (i) Información actualizada sobre el área de cultivos de coca a nivel nacional, (ii) Información actualizada sobre la productividad/rendimiento de la hoja de coca en las principales zonas cocaleras. iii) Información actualizada sobre la eficiencia de la producción clandestina de derivados de la cocaína, iv) Información actualizada sobre la pureza de los derivados de la cocaína, v) Información actualizada sobre los precios de la hoja de coca y sus derivados, (vi) información confiable sobre las transformaciones multidimensionales de los territorios afectados por los cultivos de coca y el TID y (vii) herramientas de registro estandarizado, análisis de información y alerta temprana.

planEntities.description: Mejorar la calidad de vida de los caficultores en zonas afectadas o vulnerables a los cultivos ilícitos. En paralelo, abordar la probelmática de los flujos ilícitos vinculados al crimen organizado transnacional mediante la articulación entre entidades nacionales.

planEntities.description: Fase II del proyecto "Respuestas de la Justicia Penal a Delitos Forestales" tiene como objetivo reforzar la asistencia técnica para la protección de los bosques de Perú mediante el fortalecimiento de la colaboración interinstitucional, el desarrollo de capacidades y la implementación de herramientas para abordar los delitos forestales y delitos conexos a nivel local. Los resultados del proyecto incluyen: 1) Fortalecimiento de las autoridades nacionales y locales a través de redes interinstitucionales, intercambio de información y coordinación; 2) Fortalecimiento de las capacidades del sector justicia en la prevención, investigación y enjuiciamiento de los delitos forestales; 3) Mejora del conocimiento y la conciencia de las autoridades nacionales para mitigar la corrupción y los delitos económicos en el sector forestal.

planEntities.name: Zero Hunger Accelerator – Catalysing Local Investments for Agrifood System Transformation and Green Transition
planEntities.parentName: OU2.2 Institutions and systems are strengthened to mobilize public and private sector investments and increase access to traditional and innovative financing to transform infrastructure facilities, agriculture and fisheries sector, and service sectors to becoming more sustainable, integrated, resilient, and modernized.
planEntities.description: The Zero Hunger Accelerator is a joint programme in the Philippines that strengthens inclusive, climate‑resilient food systems by mobilizing blended financing solutions aligned with national priorities and institutional markets such as school meals and social protection. By combining public funding, concessional capital, de‑risking instruments, and tailored nano‑credit bundled with climate‑responsive insurance, it expands financial inclusion for smallholder farmers, fisherfolk, cooperatives, and women‑led enterprises. Through the Zero Hunger Facility, first‑loss guarantees attract investors to local food systems, while national platforms like EPAHP and BARMM’s BFSTF enable policy coordination and LGU‑led investment pipelines in post‑harvest infrastructure, food fortification, cold storage, and women‑led enterprise development. Expected to mobilize at least US$24 million over three years, with half channelled through subnational systems, the initiative supports the Philippines Development Plan, National Adaptation Plan, and local climate strategies, creating a replicable model to localize the SDGs, stimulate equitable markets, and scale green and gender‑responsive food system transformation.

planEntities.name: Technical Assistance and support to the Mindanao Development Authority in localizing a quadruple humanitarian-peace-climate-development (HPCD) nexus approach to increase resilience of local communities and strengthen local value chains, fair production, and economic opportunities for target communities.

planEntities.description:
The overall objective of the project is to foster an enabling environment for sustainable peace and development in Mindanao.
It champions a two-pronged approach:
• Local communities’ resiliency is increased and
• Local value chains and value addition, fair production and economic opportunities for target communities are strengthened.

To operationalize the HPCD nexus, the human security approach  and conflict-sensitive programming across the two outcomes of the Action will be applied, ensuring programmatic coherence and cost-effectiveness that maximize lasting impact."

JPSTs will also be supported to include gender-sensitive approaches to conflict mapping and management, to contribute and better align with the BARMM RAP-WPS. Harnessing the gains of key and cross-cutting reforms in health systems, the project will further seek to improve the availability, accessibility, and efficiency of health service delivery across the region and promote community engagement capacity of health actors with specific focus on priority health programs for Safe Motherhood (SM), Adolescent Reproductive Health (ARH), and Global Health Security (GHS).

planEntities.name: Resilience, Innovation and Sustainability for Empowered Youth (RISE) in the Philippines
planEntities.parentName: OU3.1 Capacities of institutions at all levels and those of the communities, strengthened for improved disaster risk reduction and management, climate resilience, water and sanitation systems, through evidence and risk-informed planning and implementation.
planEntities.description: Resilience, Innovation and Sustainability for Empowered Youth (RISE) is IOM Philippines' contribution to climate justice. It is IOM's pilot initiative to demonstrate the gains that could be achieved by investing in youth for long-term solutions to climate-induced human mobility. Bicol youth ages 18-30 are the primary stakeholders of this project, recognizing their vulnerability to the long-term effects of the climate crisis, while simultaneously acknowledging their capacity to develop and mobilize impactful solutions to these challenges. RISE's Theory of Change is as follows: If the youth are equipped with the relevant information, skills, and have access to resources, then they will be empowered to innovate and provide context-based localized solutions mainstreaming climate change mitigation and adaptation for the most vulnerable communities, because they are the demographic most invested in tackling the climate crisis coming from their first-hand experiences on the direct impacts of climate and environmental change.

planEntities.name: Increasing Community Resilience by Maximizing Diaspora's Impact
planEntities.parentName: OU1.5 The people have improved resilience to and protection from multidimensional risks through the provision of adequate housing, improved environmental quality, and enhanced social environment, including social cohesion.
planEntities.description: Endemic poverty in the Philippines is regularly exacerbated by frequent disasters, as it is one of the world's most disaster-prone countries. Diaspora engagement initiatives have been shown to promote disaster risk reduction and communities' resilience and self-reliance across the humanitarian-development nexus. In light of the above, the objective of this project is to contribute to development of the Philippines and enhanced resilience of communities to shocks, through strengthening diaspora engagement.  It will focus on allowing selected affected communities to access safe shelters through diasporas’ contributions towards greening and environmentally friendly housing solutions in the Philippines by expanding the Diaspora Fundraising Model, taking into account gender considerations; revising and scaling up the micro-finance institution (MFI) loan model; making available and allocating loans to vulnerable community members, especially women and girls; and developing and disseminating an external assessment report of the MFI loan model for replicability and buy-in.

planEntities.name: Generating Renewable and Innovative Designs for Displacement (GRID)

The project will ensure that evacuation centres, which often serve as the first line of protection during displacement, are equipped with sustainable energy systems that provide reliable power both during normal times and emergencies.

planEntities.parentName: OU1.1 The Philippine healthcare system has accelerated progress on key health-related SDG targets and implementation of the UHC Act by enabling healthy choices of individuals, ensuring access to improved quality, efficiency, equitable and gender-responsive health services and systems, while preparing for and responding to health emergencies, and addressing key social determinants and risk factors across the life course.
planEntities.description:
IOM aims to enhance service utilization and improve the Maternal, Neonatal, and Child Health (MNCH) outcomes amongst vulnerable, underserved individuals in Geographically Isolated and Disadvantaged Areas (GIDAs), as well as mobile populations.  In alignment with the Universal Health Care (UHC) agenda and national health standards, IOM seeks to contribute to long-term improvements in MNCH service equity and quality by addressing systemic gaps in health facilities, workforce capacity, and community awareness.

The project responds to persistent health inequities in the Bangsamoro region, where decades of conflict, geographic isolation, and socio-economic challenges have resulted in some of the country’s poorest MNCH outcomes. High rates of adolescent pregnancy, malnutrition, and limited access to skilled birth attendance and antenatal care are compounded by a lack of well-equipped health facilities and trained personnel. These challenges are particularly acute in BaSulTa, where mobility trends—such as displacement and irregular migration—further restrict access to essential health services.

planEntities.name: Durable Solutions for Displacement and Strengthened Resilience of Communities Affected by Conflict and Disasters
planEntities.parentName: OU1.5 The people have improved resilience to and protection from multidimensional risks through the provision of adequate housing, improved environmental quality, and enhanced social environment, including social cohesion.
planEntities.description: IOM aims to deliver durable solutions for displacement and strengthen resilience among communities affected by conflict and disasters in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM). Since April 2025, compounded crises—natural hazards and armed conflict—have deepened vulnerabilities of internally displaced persons (IDPs), particularly Marawi Siege survivors, and created new waves of displacement. Despite ongoing government and development efforts, critical gaps persist in shelter recovery, site management, and Housing, Land, and Property (HLP) security, leaving thousands of families at risk of prolonged displacement and exposure to protection risks. IOM's interventions will contribute to measurable improvements in living conditions, reduction of HLP issues and potential for conflict, and reinforce institutional capacities.

planEntities.parentName: OU1.1 The Philippine healthcare system has accelerated progress on key health-related SDG targets and implementation of the UHC Act by enabling healthy choices of individuals, ensuring access to improved quality, efficiency, equitable and gender-responsive health services and systems, while preparing for and responding to health emergencies, and addressing key social determinants and risk factors across the life course.
planEntities.description:
The persistent rise in HIV infections in the country underscores significant gaps in HIV program delivery among key populations, particularly among the youth. An empowered youth sector, through platforms such as the Sangguniang Kabataan (SK), can play a critical role in bridging the gap between sexual initiation and the consistent practice of HIV preventive behaviors. At the same time, adolescent girls and young women remain underserved by existing HIV messaging and services, contributing to low uptake of prevention, testing, and treatment, including among women living with HIV (WLHIV). Addressing these gaps requires targeted assessment of their needs and concerns, alongside strengthened capacity of service providers to engage people who use drugs and others facing intersecting risks related to sexual and injecting practices.

In response, this sub-output focuses on reducing new HIV infections by improving the coverage, inclusiveness, and responsiveness of HIV programs across all settings, particularly for youth aged 10–24 years and adolescent girls and young women. It emphasizes meaningful participation of community-based organizations and youth-led networks, supported by the strategic use of evidence and data for improved information dissemination, surveillance, and community-led feedback. Leveraging the convening role of UNAIDS to coordinate UNJTA members, development partners, and national stakeholders will maximize available resources, strengthen community-led monitoring systems, and support increased domestic financing for HIV programs. Key activities include the validation workshop and Training of Trainers (TOT) for the Youth Health Learning Package (YHLP), implemented in collaboration with the National YKP Network Philippines, to strengthen youth engagement and expand effective HIV prevention and service delivery.

planEntities.parentName: OU1.7 Peace and unity are further strengthened through support to government efforts to implement peace agreements and deliver peace dividends.
planEntities.description:
The programme is designed to promote the decommissioning and normalization aspects of the Bangsamoro peace process by addressing the challenge of personal firearms of both former MILF combatants as well as members of the private armed groups. 

Effective SALW programme, with accelerated provision of socio-economic support, will help move decommissioning and the wider normalization process forward urgently and effectively. The programme can be the first model case, which embodies the concept of “a new generation of human security” by systematically operationalizing a set of human-centred policy measures in post-conflict peacebuilding. The programme outcome aims at integrating comprehensive human security policy initiatives, raising from the ones that capture former combatants’ socio-economic needs to those that promote climate action and disaster risk reduction, which contributes to advancing the local implementation of SDGs among all the people in Mindanao who share the common future. (ASPIRE)

planEntities.name: Reduction in the number of new HIV infections by improving the coverage of HIV programs coverage among  key populations including the youth aged 10 - 24 years, adolescent girls and young women through the provision of inclusive, responsive, and well-funded services across all settings and guided by increased participation of community-based organizations, leveraging the use of evidence and data for strategic information dissemination and community-led feedback.
planEntities.parentName: OU1.1 The Philippine healthcare system has accelerated progress on key health-related SDG targets and implementation of the UHC Act by enabling healthy choices of individuals, ensuring access to improved quality, efficiency, equitable and gender-responsive health services and systems, while preparing for and responding to health emergencies, and addressing key social determinants and risk factors across the life course.
planEntities.description:
The persistent rise in HIV infections in the country underscores significant gaps in HIV program delivery among key populations, particularly among the youth. An empowered youth sector, through platforms such as the Sangguniang Kabataan (SK), can play a critical role in bridging the gap between sexual initiation and the consistent practice of HIV preventive behaviors. At the same time, adolescent girls and young women remain underserved by existing HIV messaging and services, contributing to low uptake of prevention, testing, and treatment, including among women living with HIV (WLHIV). Addressing these gaps requires targeted assessment of their needs and concerns, alongside strengthened capacity of service providers to engage people who use drugs and others facing intersecting risks related to sexual and injecting practices.

In response, this sub-output focuses on reducing new HIV infections by improving the coverage, inclusiveness, and responsiveness of HIV programs across all settings, particularly for youth aged 10–24 years and adolescent girls and young women. It emphasizes meaningful participation of community-based organizations and youth-led networks, supported by the strategic use of evidence and data for improved information dissemination, surveillance, and community-led feedback. Leveraging the convening role of UNAIDS to coordinate UNJTA members, development partners, and national stakeholders will maximize available resources, strengthen community-led monitoring systems, and support increased domestic financing for HIV programs. Key activities include the validation workshop and Training of Trainers (TOT) for the Youth Health Learning Package (YHLP), implemented in collaboration with the National YKP Network Philippines, to strengthen youth engagement and expand effective HIV prevention and service delivery.

planEntities.name: Reduction in the number of new HIV infections by improving the coverage of HIV programs coverage among  key populations including the youth aged 10 - 24 years, adolescent girls and young women through the provision of inclusive, responsive, and well-funded services across all settings and guided by increased participation of community-based organizations, leveraging the use of evidence and data for strategic information dissemination and community-led feedback.
planEntities.parentName: OU1.1 The Philippine healthcare system has accelerated progress on key health-related SDG targets and implementation of the UHC Act by enabling healthy choices of individuals, ensuring access to improved quality, efficiency, equitable and gender-responsive health services and systems, while preparing for and responding to health emergencies, and addressing key social determinants and risk factors across the life course.
planEntities.description:
The persistent rise in HIV infections in the country underscores significant gaps in HIV program delivery among key populations, particularly among the youth. An empowered youth sector, through platforms such as the Sangguniang Kabataan (SK), can play a critical role in bridging the gap between sexual initiation and the consistent practice of HIV preventive behaviors. At the same time, adolescent girls and young women remain underserved by existing HIV messaging and services, contributing to low uptake of prevention, testing, and treatment, including among women living with HIV (WLHIV). Addressing these gaps requires targeted assessment of their needs and concerns, alongside strengthened capacity of service providers to engage people who use drugs and others facing intersecting risks related to sexual and injecting practices.

In response, this sub-output focuses on reducing new HIV infections by improving the coverage, inclusiveness, and responsiveness of HIV programs across all settings, particularly for youth aged 10–24 years and adolescent girls and young women. It emphasizes meaningful participation of community-based organizations and youth-led networks, supported by the strategic use of evidence and data for improved information dissemination, surveillance, and community-led feedback. Leveraging the convening role of UNAIDS to coordinate UNJTA members, development partners, and national stakeholders will maximize available resources, strengthen community-led monitoring systems, and support increased domestic financing for HIV programs. Key activities include the validation workshop and Training of Trainers (TOT) for the Youth Health Learning Package (YHLP), implemented in collaboration with the National YKP Network Philippines, to strengthen youth engagement and expand effective HIV prevention and service delivery.

planEntities.parentName: OU1.1 The Philippine healthcare system has accelerated progress on key health-related SDG targets and implementation of the UHC Act by enabling healthy choices of individuals, ensuring access to improved quality, efficiency, equitable and gender-responsive health services and systems, while preparing for and responding to health emergencies, and addressing key social determinants and risk factors across the life course.
planEntities.description:
In 2021, WHO and UNICEF entered into a partnership agreement with the Australian Government Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT) to support the expansion of the cold chain capacity, improve information management systems, and risk communication/community engagement with a funding of AU$10.6 million from May 2021 to June 2023. WHO and UNICEF implemented the programme in priority areas of the Philippines in close collaboration with the National Government Agencies (NGAs) including Department of Health (DOH), Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT) and local government units (LGUs) to address the gaps in cold chain capacity, vaccine information management system, and demand generation among others.  

For Phase 2, DFAT approved an additional $9.4 million to 1) improve the health information system, laboratory network, and surveillance system for COVID-19 vaccination and routine immunization, and 2) increase demand and acceptance for COVID-19 vaccination and routine immunization among the remaining unvaccinated priority groups, men, women, girls, and boys.

planEntities.name: Technical Assistance and support to the Department of Science and Technology to implement clean hydrogen programme in the Philippines
planEntities.parentName: OU3.1 Capacities of institutions at all levels and those of the communities, strengthened for improved disaster risk reduction and management, climate resilience, water and sanitation systems, through evidence and risk-informed planning and implementation.
planEntities.description:
The Child Project of Philippines is part of the Global Clean Hydrogen Programme (GEF-8). This project aims to enhancing national institutional capacities, enabling policy frameworks, improving technological readiness at industrial level, and financial mechanisms for the successful uptake of clean hydrogen in Philippines, to ensure its net zero development with social considerations and benefits. The Project expects to generate the following outcomes:

- Address the limited appropriateness of policy, regulatory and standards frameworks by developing a Clean Hydrogen Roadmap and Strategy to lead the long-term development of clean hydrogen in the Philippines, improve market conditions and foster private sector investments.

- Support the development of studies and assessments to improve technical readiness and enable the implementation of clean hydrogen projects that would bring Global Environmental Benefits (GEBs) in the form of total GHG emissions reduction, estimated at 929,665 tCO₂eq, thus contributing to national and international mitigation targets.

- Address knowledge and capacity gaps at institutional and technical levels to identify opportunities and develop green hydrogen projects, through capacity building and knowledge sharing activities and raising awareness in key sectors.

planEntities.name: Reduction in the number of new HIV infections by improving the coverage of HIV programs coverage among  key populations including the youth aged 10 - 24 years, adolescent girls and young women through the provision of inclusive, responsive, and well-funded services across all settings and guided by increased participation of community-based organizations, leveraging the use of evidence and data for strategic information dissemination and community-led feedback.
planEntities.parentName: OU1.1 The Philippine healthcare system has accelerated progress on key health-related SDG targets and implementation of the UHC Act by enabling healthy choices of individuals, ensuring access to improved quality, efficiency, equitable and gender-responsive health services and systems, while preparing for and responding to health emergencies, and addressing key social determinants and risk factors across the life course.
planEntities.description:
The persistent rise in HIV infections in the country underscores significant gaps in HIV program delivery among key populations, particularly among the youth. An empowered youth sector, through platforms such as the Sangguniang Kabataan (SK), can play a critical role in bridging the gap between sexual initiation and the consistent practice of HIV preventive behaviors. At the same time, adolescent girls and young women remain underserved by existing HIV messaging and services, contributing to low uptake of prevention, testing, and treatment, including among women living with HIV (WLHIV). Addressing these gaps requires targeted assessment of their needs and concerns, alongside strengthened capacity of service providers to engage people who use drugs and others facing intersecting risks related to sexual and injecting practices.

In response, this sub-output focuses on reducing new HIV infections by improving the coverage, inclusiveness, and responsiveness of HIV programs across all settings, particularly for youth aged 10–24 years and adolescent girls and young women. It emphasizes meaningful participation of community-based organizations and youth-led networks, supported by the strategic use of evidence and data for improved information dissemination, surveillance, and community-led feedback. Leveraging the convening role of UNAIDS to coordinate UNJTA members, development partners, and national stakeholders will maximize available resources, strengthen community-led monitoring systems, and support increased domestic financing for HIV programs. Key activities include the validation workshop and Training of Trainers (TOT) for the Youth Health Learning Package (YHLP), implemented in collaboration with the National YKP Network Philippines, to strengthen youth engagement and expand effective HIV prevention and service delivery.

planEntities.name: Zero Hunger Accelerator – Catalysing Local Investments for Agrifood System Transformation and Green Transition
planEntities.parentName: OU2.2 Institutions and systems are strengthened to mobilize public and private sector investments and increase access to traditional and innovative financing to transform infrastructure facilities, agriculture and fisheries sector, and service sectors to becoming more sustainable, integrated, resilient, and modernized.
planEntities.description: The Zero Hunger Accelerator is a joint programme in the Philippines that strengthens inclusive, climate‑resilient food systems by mobilizing blended financing solutions aligned with national priorities and institutional markets such as school meals and social protection. By combining public funding, concessional capital, de‑risking instruments, and tailored nano‑credit bundled with climate‑responsive insurance, it expands financial inclusion for smallholder farmers, fisherfolk, cooperatives, and women‑led enterprises. Through the Zero Hunger Facility, first‑loss guarantees attract investors to local food systems, while national platforms like EPAHP and BARMM’s BFSTF enable policy coordination and LGU‑led investment pipelines in post‑harvest infrastructure, food fortification, cold storage, and women‑led enterprise development. Expected to mobilize at least US$24 million over three years, with half channelled through subnational systems, the initiative supports the Philippines Development Plan, National Adaptation Plan, and local climate strategies, creating a replicable model to localize the SDGs, stimulate equitable markets, and scale green and gender‑responsive food system transformation.

planEntities.description:
In 2021, WHO and UNICEF entered into a partnership agreement with the Australian Government Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT) to support the expansion of the cold chain capacity, improve information management systems, and risk communication/community engagement with a funding of AU$10.6 million from May 2021 to June 2023. WHO and UNICEF implemented the programme in priority areas of the Philippines in close collaboration with the National Government Agencies (NGAs) including Department of Health (DOH), Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT) and local government units (LGUs) to address the gaps in cold chain capacity, vaccine information management system, and demand generation among others.  

For Phase 2, DFAT approved an additional $9.4 million to 1) improve the health information system, laboratory network, and surveillance system for COVID-19 vaccination and routine immunization, and 2) increase demand and acceptance for COVID-19 vaccination and routine immunization among the remaining unvaccinated priority groups, men, women, girls, and boys.

Papua New Guinea.organizationType: Multilateral - UN organizations excluding pooled funds

planEntities.name: IFAD’s Maket Bilong Vilis Fama (MVF) aims at improving the livelihoods of village farming households in the target provinces, by facilitating their transition from semi-subsistence agriculture to market-oriented production and farming as a business. The project’s development goal is to achieve sustainable increased returns to village farming households from increased marketed production
planEntities.parentName: Enterprise Development: Enhanced growth of Micro Small Medium Enterprise (MSME) and value chain development in agriculture, manufacturing, and services
planEntities.description:
The MVF project started in 2018 and was originally expected to end in 2024. The project recently received additional financing and was extended, with new expected completion date in September 2029.

The project will predominately focus on the fresh produce sub-sector which involves approximately 94% of village farmers across PNG. In addition, the project provide limited investment to pilot activities focused on stimulating the development of the galip nut value chain as this has potential to be become a new export cash crop for village farmers in PNG. 

The project was recently expanded to target seven provinces of PNG. Activities related to the fresh produce sub-sector will be implemented in four provinces in the Highlands Region (Western Highlands, Jiwaka, Simbu and Eastern Highlands) and one province in the Momase Region, Morobe. Galip nut related activities will be implemented in East New Britain, Madang and Morobe. Building on its initial success, the MVF was scaled up and now targets around 40,000 farming households, benefiting approximately 200,000 people.

planEntities.parentName: Enterprise Development: Enhanced growth of Micro Small Medium Enterprise (MSME) and value chain development in agriculture, manufacturing, and services
planEntities.description:
The EU-ACP Business-Friendly: Supporting value chains through inclusive policies, investment promotion and alliances is an Intra-ACP action funded by the European Union and the Organisation of African, Caribbean and Pacific States (OACPS). It seeks to improve the ability of agribusiness firms in ACP countries to compete, grow and prosper in domestic, regional and international markets, ultimately generating inclusive, sustainable jobs and economic growth. Micro-level interventions are led by ITC through its Alliances for Action approach that promotes inclusive and sustainable agricultural value chains. Interventions aim to enhance value chain operators individual and collective competitiveness with specific attention to family farmers, agri-entrepreneurs and processors. In Papua New Guinea the programme is focusing on the coconut value chain.

planEntities.description:
This component focuses on testing, piloting, demonstrating and learning – specifically testing mechanisms to deliver funds from the Biodiversity  Fund to selected protected areas (Output 3.1); piloting mechanisms that will catalyse (or consolidate) revenue in a small number of sites such that that revenue will be re-invested into the management of those sites and possibly other sites (Output 3.2); and learning from the diverse practices that are being implemented by various partner organisations across the country (Output 3.3).
National and international stakeholders will participate in the project M&E, and lessons learned from the implementation will be systemized (Output 3.4)

planEntities.name: Advanced  foundational building blocks of the  Integrated National Financing  Framework (INFF)
planEntities.parentName: Innovative Financing and partnerships: Expanded public/private partnerships for increased innovative financing instruments.
planEntities.description:
The project aims to support the implementation of the MTDP IV with a key focus on identify financingoptions using the Integrated National Financing Framework and creating a platform for a multi
stakeholder partnership involving civil society, the private sector, and other partners in decision making.  
The expected results of the project are as follows:  
• Ensuring adequate financing for the national development priorities (MTDP IV) through the Integrated National Financing Framework: This outcome aims to ensure that the development plan is sufficiently funded by leveraging the Integrated National Financing Framework. The immediate focal area will be mobilizing much-needed resources to finance PNG’s transition to a sustainable and inclusive economy grounded in the 10th SPA of the MTDP IV and the sixth transition area identified by the Joint SDG Fund: climate change, biodiversity loss, and pollution.

planEntities.name: Integrated land management, restoration of degraded landscapes and natural capital assessment in the mountains of Papua New Guinea
planEntities.parentName: Natural Resource Management: Natural resources are better managed to the benefit of Papua New Guineans through improved biodiversity conservation, environmental governance and partnerships at all levels.
planEntities.description: The Project (GEF 10580) will contribute to the sustained flow of ecosystem services in PNG Highlands that will provide a solid basis for sustainable livelihoods and to the achievement of Land Degradation Neutrality (LDN). At the global scale, the Project will contribute to the achievement of GEF Global Environmental Benefits, including the conservation and sustainable use of globally significant biodiversity, the improved provision of ecosystem services, and to carbon sequestration benefits. In total, 84,409 ha of land will benefit from restoration and improved management and 22,000 people will benefit from Sustainable Land Management (SLM) and Sustainable Forest Management (SFM) technologies, livelihood and value chain development and strengthened SMEs, along with assocated capacity development. The Project will also contribute to the achievement of global development objectives structured along the Sustainable Development Goals, particularly SDG 15 “Life on Land”, SDG 2 “Zero Hunger” and SDG 13 “Climate Change”.

planEntities.name: Support to the Papua New Guinea National Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WaSH) Policy 2015–2030 - Part 2
planEntities.parentName: Water Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH): WASH systems strengthened to ensure people have equitable access to affordable, gender sensitive, environmentally and climate friendly safe drinking water and sanitation
planEntities.description:
The proposed Action will directly support the implementation of the Papua New Guinea National Water, Sanitation and Hygiene Policy 2015 - 2030, as well as other targets, as stated in the Vision 50, the Development Strategic Plan 2010 - 2030, the Water Papua New Guinea Master Plan 2012 - 2030, the Medium Term Development Plan III 2018 - 2022, and ultimately contribute to the following Sustainable Development Goals: SDG 3, SDG 4, SDG 5, SD6, SDG 11, SDG 13.

3.1 The Action (project) objectives

In line with the Papua New Guinea National Water, Sanitation and Hygiene Policy (WaSH) 2015 - 2030, the proposed Action aims to contribute towards improving the quality of life of Papua New Guineans through increased access to and utilization of a safe, adequate and sustainable water supply, sanitation and improved hygiene practices.

General objective: The general objective of the Action is to improve the quality of life of women, children and men through contributing to increased access to safe, adequate and sustainable water supply and sanitation in locations of higher human concentration (schools, healthcare facilities, and major market places).

The project aims to achieve increased equitable access to safe, convenient and sustainable water supply and sanitation and improved hygiene practices and long-term hygiene behavior change at the personal, household, community and institutional level, particularly to urban areas that are currently under-served, in- line with the National WaSH policy. Hence, the specific objectives of the action are:

Specific Objective 1: Improved equitable access to safe and affordable drinking water in selected urban areas, focusing on vulnerable groups and locations of higher human concentration (schools, healthcare facilities, markets).

Specific Objective 2: Improved adequate and equitable sanitation and hygiene in selected urban areas, with a special focus on locations of higher human concentrations (schools, healthcare facilities, markets) and paying special attention to the needs of women and girls and those in vulnerable situations, including improved nutrition for children in schools.

This reiterates the interventions' work towards increasing equity of services in urban towns/areas, and to disadvantaged groups, as well as reducing economic and financial losses related to accessing safe and sustainable water supply.

planEntities.name: Provision of ICT equipment and solar energy systems in Bougainville
planEntities.parentName: Service Delivery: Strengthened national and sub-national planning, monitoring, data, and public finance management systems for improved effectiveness and efficiency in service delivery.
planEntities.description:
UNOPS proposes a series of actions for the provision of ICT equipment and the development of a functionally enhanced Financial Management Information System (FMIS) for the Department of Treasury & Finance in Bougainville.

For the ICT equipment, UNOPS outlines steps such as finalizing technical specifications, collaborating with stakeholders for input, launching a tender, evaluating submissions, and awarding contracts to economically viable suppliers. The organization will ensure transparency in the procurement process, administer contracts, and oversee the delivery of goods to Bougainville. UNOPS also commits to minimizing delivery delays, providing installation support, and offering training, including digital literacy, to beneficiary offices.

Regarding the development of the FMIS, UNOPS plans to create solicitation documents to procure competent suppliers. The goal is to enhance the existing Provincial Government Accounting System (PGAS) by introducing a system that addresses its limitations, including the lack of graphical user interface, absence of management information reports, and inability to reflect Assets and Liabilities values. The new FMIS aims to transform bookkeeping and accounting processes from manual to electronic, providing comprehensive financial data and supporting decision-making.

planEntities.name: Buka Electricity Grid Solar Upgrade - MFAT Funded Project
planEntities.parentName: Climate Action: Enhanced climate adaptation and mitigation measures are delivered to strengthen the capacity of Papua New Guinea to mitigate the impacts of climate change on ecosystems, communities, livelihoods and the economy.
planEntities.description:
UNOPS initiated the Sustainable Energy Project for Buka as part of the Strengthening Infrastructure System in PNG. The Buka Electricity Grid Solar Upgrade aims to strengthen energy access for the Buka population through providing practical solar PV energy systems and upgrading the distribution systems, thereby enhancing the access to basic services and fostering economic development. The proposed project is expected to reduce reliance on expensive diesel generation by 90% and significantly improve the reliability and resilience of the Buka Island
electrical grid by meeting the existing and anticipated ten-year future demand.
The project outputs include:
An energy generation system comprising solar PV subsystem, BESS subsystem, backup generators, protection panel systems, communication control and energy management systems to manage the various power generation units and battery storage system to balance supply and demand; and An upgraded distribution system comprising step-up and step-down transformers, and other components necessary to rehabilitate the existing medium voltage (MV) distribution system and provide smart energy meters.

planEntities.name: National Health Facility Assessment Tool and related Capacity Development (#24589-0010
planEntities.parentName: Health: Strengthened health systems to improve the well-being and access to quality, integrated, people-centred health services including TB, HIV/AIDS and Sexual and Reproductive Health; and provide protection from health emergencies for people at national and sub-national levels, particularly those in hard-to-reach areas.
planEntities.description:
UNOPS with its expertise in construction implementation, condition assessment and development of infrastructure solutions is well placed to offer support to the NDoH and provincial and district levels in the development of capacity to carry out infrastructure audits and field assessments. Further, UNOPS holds expertise in the area of institutional capacity development, training and knowledge transfer and data management, analysis and visualization.
The main objective of the proposed project is to develop a rapid assessment tool for use at district level to capture information on the status of health facilities focusing on human resources, services and infrastructure and support the development of capacity in the use and application of this tool. The assessment tool will focus initially on Provincial Hospitals (Level 5), Rural and District Hospitals (Level 4)  and a selected number of Urban and Rural Health Centre (Level 3), capturing concise foundational data commensurate with the assigned level and facility type. 
The project will be implemented in a duration of 3 years commencing June 2024, with a proposed budget of AUD 9,217,223.

planEntities.parentName: Women and violence: Women and girls are free from discrimination, violence, and torture through a whole-of-society approach to the promotion of gender-equitable socio-cultural attitudes, norms, and behaviours
planEntities.description:
Soim Wokabout project is being implemented in NCD and Eastern Highlands provincies with the aim of preventing GBV and SARV as well as providing services to survivors of GBV and SARV. This will be achieved through three outcome areas listed below.  
- To increase access of women, men, girls and boys in all their diversity, experiencing gender-based violence, to essential quality services, protection and justice. 
- To improve advocacy and agency of civil society organisations, women’s rights organisations, social movements, and communities to end gender-based violence; and 
- To make more effective the engagement of community leaders, male advocates and influential groups and actors in society in changing discriminatory social norms, gender stereotypes, GBV and harmful practices. 

The project will be implemented by three UN Agencies (UN Women, UNFPA and UNOPS) in partnership with the Government of Papua New Guinea.  The project is financed under the EU Neighbourhood, Development and International Cooperation Instrument (NDICI-Global Europe) and contributes to Multiannual Indicative Programme (MIP) for Papua New Guinea 2021-2027 priority area 3, “Transparent and accountable governance,” and more precisely to the second part: addressing gender-based violence and promoting peaceful conflict resolution and human rights.

planEntities.name: Youth entrepreneurs trained on advanced business management and digitalization, financial literacy and productivity
planEntities.parentName: Output 1.1: Strengthened public and private systems that foster creation of decent jobs that are inclusive and productive within a resilient, green and diversified economy.
planEntities.description:
Under this sub-output, significant progress was achieved in expanding access to quality Business Development Services (BDS). 

The ILO's Start and Improve Your Business (SIYB) and Digitalise Your Business (DYB) training materials were fully adapted to the Rwandan context and translated into Kinyarwanda to ensure inclusivity and accessibility at the district level. 

All nine manuals (in English and Kinyarwanda) were digitized to be integrated into national e-learning platforms, contributing to the long-term sustainability of training delivery. The first integration was as part of the Rwanda Polytechnic Innovation Hub e-learning platform. These efforts are ongoing to reach more e-learning platforms across the country.

A total of 44 trainers from government and social partner institutions completed the Training of Trainers (ToT) , with 50 per cent now certified to deliver SIYB and DYB independently. The remainder expected to finalize their certification in early 2026. 

To strengthen outreach, the ILO established partnerships with three BDS providers—Hanga Hubs, Kina Rwanda, and Imanzi Business Institute—who have roll out the SIYB/DYB training at the district level. Through these partnerships, over 450 youth-owned businesses have already benefited from enhanced capacities in business planning, financial management, marketing, and digitalization.

The output remains on schedule, with further expansion of partnerships and roll-out of digital learning modules planned for 2026, targeting an additional 550 youth entrepreneurs.

planEntities.name: Support the digital skills development through curricula development and work-based learning for transition to jobs
planEntities.parentName: Output 1.2: People in Rwanda, especially the most vulnerable groups, are equipped with employable skills and have access to and utilise sustainable productive resources, innovation, and financing to improve their livelihoods and build resilience
planEntities.description:
1- Under this output, the ILO, Rwanda TVET Board, and the National Cyber Security Authority are jointly developing a competency-based cybersecurity curriculum aligned with national accreditation standards. The curriculum targets Level 3 qualifications, with selected modules at Levels 4 and 5, and aims to strengthen the supply Rwandan cyber security experts at the high school level. 
The activity includes a 20-day Training of Teachers (ToT) to build their instructional capacity. The programme will be piloted in two TVET schools, reaching 60 students. 
A dedicated delivery team, comprising ILO experts, national consultants, and staff from RTB and NCSA, is currently overseeing the curriculum design and accreditation process. The pilot is expected to conclude in March 2026, after which findings will inform national scale-up.

2- Through the Innovate4DigiJobs initiative, the ILO and the ICT Chamber partnered with five implementing institutions to sustainably expand access to digital skills development to collectively reach over 300 direct beneficiaries through structured training, mentorship, and job linkages.
Each partner is implementing a tailored programme that leads to an integrated approach to respond to specific local needs at the district level and different target groups. The Code and Design Alliance is providing intensive training and mentorship enabling 60 young Rwandans to access digital freelancing and online employment opportunities. The Rwanda Organization of Persons with Physical Disabilities and Wheelchair Users is delivering the Digital Empowerment for Youth with Physical Disabilities (DEYPD) programme, equipping 60 young persons with disabilities with digital literacy and employability skills. The College Baptiste Gacuba II TVET School is establishing a Digital Agri-Innovation and Youth Empowerment Hub to train 60 youth in using digital tools to improve agricultural productivity and rural enterprise creation. The Rwanda Polytechnic – Kigali College is implementing the Smart Skills Hub for Youth Employment in Digital-Economy Transformation, linking 60 TVET graduates to demand-driven training and job placement opportunities. Finally, Igire Rwanda is delivering the She Can Code programme, advancing 60 women’s participation in coding and technology careers.

Through these partnerships, the ILO ensures a balanced coverage across priority districts, combining technical training, employability coaching, and exposure to digital work opportunities. The initiatives reinforce national efforts to promote digital inclusion and contribute to the project’s broader objective of creating decent jobs for young people in Rwanda’s digital economy.

planEntities.description: OHCHR contributed to national efforts to promote unity and inclusive governance by supporting the Government, the National Commission for Human Rights (NCHR) and civil society before, during and after Rwanda’s fourth-cycle UPR. Technical assistance and consultative processes, including validation meetings with government, civil society, development partners and the media, supported the finalisation of Rwanda’s State report. Rwanda was reviewed on 21 January 2026 and supported 249 of the 286 recommendations received when the Human Rights Council adopted the outcome on 30 June 2026. OHCHR is now supporting implementation, which strengthens institutional coordination and the mainstreaming of human rights into development planning. A UNCT roadmap and implementation matrix is under validation, and validation of the government-led national implementation roadmap is scheduled for November 2026. OHCHR also supported the drafting of the National Human Rights Action Plan, led by the Ministry of Justice, including its Business and Human Rights chapter finalised in December 2025. These are key milestones in advancing national integration and rights-based peacebuilding.

planEntities.description: Technical assistance provided to; and collaborated with NAEB, RICA and other agencies / National Trade Facilitation Committee in Simplifying trade and reducing export costs. The USD 100 coffee export licence fee was abolished, and export licence validity extended from one to five years for coffee, tea and horticultural products. planEntities.name: Deliver capacity-building programs, technical assistance, and knowledge tools to enable government institutions and civil society organizations to effectively engage with international and regional human rights mechanisms.
planEntities.parentName: Output 3.1: Strengthened capacities of national and sub-national institutions and systems to deliver inclusive, rights-based, gender-transformative, resilient quality services for all people while promoting unity, peace and security.
planEntities.description: During 2026, OHCHR in partnership with national institutions, civil society organisations and the media, strengthened the capacity of government institutions and civil society to engage effectively with international and regional human rights mechanisms, including the Universal Periodic Review (UPR). National Commission for Human Rights commissioners and staff, parliamentary human rights committee members and staff, civil society organisations and journalists benefited from targeted capacity-building, technical assistance and dialogue as core strategies to improve reporting, monitoring and oversight of human rights commitments. Specifically, training for the National Commission and the parliamentary committee strengthened reporting, monitoring and oversight skills and produced draft UPR action plans and evaluation reports. Journalists were trained, with PAX PRESS, on human rights reporting and UPR dissemination. With NUDOR, 30 participants from government, UN agencies, civil society, grassroots groups and development partners discussed implementation of UPR recommendations on the rights of persons with disabilities. A workshop with Coalition Umwana ku Isonga and UNICEF brought together government institutions, civil society, the National Commission and UN agencies on implementing child rights-related UPR recommendations. In September, a high-level meeting with GLIHD on civil society engagement with human rights mechanisms produced practical recommendations to strengthen government–civil society dialogue and coordinated monitoring and reporting. These interventions improved the knowledge and skills of national actors, strengthened coordination between government and civil society, and supported national ownership of follow-up to UPR recommendations.

planEntities.parentName: Output 3.1: Strengthened capacities of national and sub-national institutions and systems to deliver inclusive, rights-based, gender-transformative, resilient quality services for all people while promoting unity, peace and security.
planEntities.description: In 2026, OHCHR provided technical assistance to the legislative reform process concerning the National Commission for Human Rights, through legal advice, workshops and engagement with the Commission and national stakeholders. The adoption of a new law in June 2026, governing the Commission strengthened its legal framework, including its mandate and preventive role against torture. OHCHR’s support contributed to this reform process, providing an enhanced legal basis for human rights monitoring and the protection of rights holders, including persons deprived of liberty.

planEntities.description: During the reporting period, OHCHR in partnership with Action pour le Développement du Peuple (ADEPE), organised training for 34 community paralegals in Rubavu District. The training strengthened skills in legal aid, case management and referral systems, with a focus on access to justice, gender-based violence, child protection and the rights of persons with disabilities and other vulnerable groups. This support equipped community paralegals with practical knowledge and skills relevant to identifying legal needs and facilitating access to assistance and referral services.

planEntities.name: Facilitate initiatives that promote national and regional integration, unity, peace and security
planEntities.parentName: Output 3.2: By 2029, people in Rwanda, especially the most vulnerable, live in a united, peaceful, secure and inclusive environment with equitable access to gender-responsive and resilient quality services
planEntities.description: OHCHR contributed to national efforts to promote unity and inclusive governance by supporting the Government, the National Commission for Human Rights (NCHR) and civil society before, during and after Rwanda’s fourth-cycle UPR. Technical assistance and consultative processes, including validation meetings with government, civil society, development partners and the media, supported the finalisation of Rwanda’s State report. Rwanda was reviewed on 21 January 2026 and supported 249 of the 286 recommendations received when the Human Rights Council adopted the outcome on 30 June 2026. OHCHR is now supporting implementation, which strengthens institutional coordination and the mainstreaming of human rights into development planning. A UNCT roadmap and implementation matrix is under validation, and validation of the government-led national implementation roadmap is scheduled for November 2026. OHCHR also supported the drafting of the National Human Rights Action Plan, led by the Ministry of Justice, including its Business and Human Rights chapter finalised in December 2025. These are key milestones in advancing national integration and rights-based peacebuilding.

planEntities.name: Support to laws, decrees, strategies, policies and guidelines to reinforce the enabling and inclusive environment for Social sectors
planEntities.parentName: Output 2.1: Strengthened systems that provide inclusive, resilient, and gender-transformative quality social services.
planEntities.description:
During 2026, OHCHR provided technical and policy support to promote the integration of international human rights standards, non-discrimination and inclusion into national employment and social protection policies.
In October, OHCHR contributed to consultations on the National Employment Policy 2026–2036, providing specific recommendations on incorporating a human rights-based definition of decent work, strengthening accessible reporting and remedy mechanisms for labour rights violations, and addressing barriers to employment faced by persons in vulnerable situations.
OHCHR also participated in national consultations on extending social protection coverage and contributed to the development of the joint programme Financing Just Transitions in Rwanda: Scaling Formalization, Decent Jobs and Social Protection, in collaboration with UN agencies and national stakeholders. The programme document was signed by the Government and submitted to the SDG Fund in September 2026.

UN WOMEN: Addressing the underrepresentation of women in leadership particularly at the local level, in executive roles, and across key sectors is crucial for fostering inclusive decision-making and strengthening accountability for gender equality. Promoting women’s leadership is also essential for achieving equality in governance, driving sustainable development, and ensuring that policies and decisions reflect the needs of all members of society. To this end, UN Women will strengthen the capacity of National Gender Machinery institutions,  strenthen gender accountability platforms, and policy dialogues. The progress achieved under the Gender Seal program, along with efforts to meaningfully engage men and boys in advancing gender equality, will be scaled up and sustained.

Additionally, to further enhance women’s leadership, UN Women will invest in capacity building, mentorship, and advocacy. Leadership skills will be nurtured through initiatives such as intergenerational dialogues, women’s networking, and the African Women Leaders Network (AWLN), with a strong focus on institutionalizing mentorship and transformational leadership programs across sectors.

planEntities.parentName: Output 2.1: Strengthened systems that provide inclusive, resilient, and gender-transformative quality social services.
planEntities.description:
During 2026, OHCHR provided technical and policy support to promote the integration of international human rights standards, non-discrimination and inclusion into national employment and social protection policies.
In October, OHCHR contributed to consultations on the National Employment Policy 2026–2036, providing specific recommendations on incorporating a human rights-based definition of decent work, strengthening accessible reporting and remedy mechanisms for labour rights violations, and addressing barriers to employment faced by persons in vulnerable situations.
OHCHR also participated in national consultations on extending social protection coverage and contributed to the development of the joint programme Financing Just Transitions in Rwanda: Scaling Formalization, Decent Jobs and Social Protection, in collaboration with UN agencies and national stakeholders. The programme document was signed by the Government and submitted to the SDG Fund in September 2026.

planEntities.parentName: Output 3.2: By 2029, people in Rwanda, especially the most vulnerable, live in a united, peaceful, secure and inclusive environment with equitable access to gender-responsive and resilient quality services
planEntities.description:
UNDP:  facilitate strategic partnerships and initiatives with state and non-state actors, women-led CSOs, networks, and advocacy groups to enhance women’s leadership and participation in decision-making including advocacy through high level events; Conduct leadership and governance training programs for women at sub-national levels to increase representation in policy formulation and implementation and Support private companies and public institutions in achieving certification under national gender standards (RS/560:2023) through tailored technical assistance and compliance monitoring. UNDP will facilitate the institutionalisation of gender equality principles with the CSOs

UNHCR: continue to empower more refugee women and host community through different capacity building sessions, to boost their confidence in taking up leadership roles.
UNHCR: engage men and boys in efforts to prevent and respond to GBV which is critical to transforming harmful social norms that perpetuate gender inequality and promote the health and safety of women and girls. 
UNHCR: address the gaps on gender equality notably by addressing the social gender stereotyping through champions of change projects with men and boys and provision of sustainable day care for women entrepreneurs.
UNHCR: enhance gender inclusion into digital transformation through Coding Courses, Female Digital Career Counselor and creation of Digital Centre by women's group in camp 

UN WOMEN: Addressing the underrepresentation of women in leadership particularly at the local level, in executive roles, and across key sectors is crucial for fostering inclusive decision-making and strengthening accountability for gender equality. Promoting women’s leadership is also essential for achieving equality in governance, driving sustainable development, and ensuring that policies and decisions reflect the needs of all members of society. To this end, UN Women will strengthen the capacity of National Gender Machinery institutions,  strenthen gender accountability platforms, and policy dialogues. The progress achieved under the Gender Seal program, along with efforts to meaningfully engage men and boys in advancing gender equality, will be scaled up and sustained.

Additionally, to further enhance women’s leadership, UN Women will invest in capacity building, mentorship, and advocacy. Leadership skills will be nurtured through initiatives such as intergenerational dialogues, women’s networking, and the African Women Leaders Network (AWLN), with a strong focus on institutionalizing mentorship and transformational leadership programs across sectors.
