planEntities.parentName: Output 3.2: By 2029, people in Rwanda, especially the most vulnerable, live in a united, peaceful, secure and inclusive environment with equitable access to gender-responsive and resilient quality services
planEntities.description: OHCHR contributed to national efforts to promote unity and inclusive governance by supporting the Government, the National Commission for Human Rights (NCHR) and civil society before, during and after Rwanda’s fourth-cycle UPR. Technical assistance and consultative processes, including validation meetings with government, civil society, development partners and the media, supported the finalisation of Rwanda’s State report. Rwanda was reviewed on 21 January 2026 and supported 249 of the 286 recommendations received when the Human Rights Council adopted the outcome on 30 June 2026. OHCHR is now supporting implementation, which strengthens institutional coordination and the mainstreaming of human rights into development planning. A UNCT roadmap and implementation matrix is under validation, and validation of the government-led national implementation roadmap is scheduled for November 2026. OHCHR also supported the drafting of the National Human Rights Action Plan, led by the Ministry of Justice, including its Business and Human Rights chapter finalised in December 2025. These are key milestones in advancing national integration and rights-based peacebuilding.

planEntities.description:
UNDP:  facilitate strategic partnerships and initiatives with state and non-state actors, women-led CSOs, networks, and advocacy groups to enhance women’s leadership and participation in decision-making including advocacy through high level events; Conduct leadership and governance training programs for women at sub-national levels to increase representation in policy formulation and implementation and Support private companies and public institutions in achieving certification under national gender standards (RS/560:2023) through tailored technical assistance and compliance monitoring. UNDP will facilitate the institutionalisation of gender equality principles with the CSOs

UNHCR: continue to empower more refugee women and host community through different capacity building sessions, to boost their confidence in taking up leadership roles.
UNHCR: engage men and boys in efforts to prevent and respond to GBV which is critical to transforming harmful social norms that perpetuate gender inequality and promote the health and safety of women and girls. 
UNHCR: address the gaps on gender equality notably by addressing the social gender stereotyping through champions of change projects with men and boys and provision of sustainable day care for women entrepreneurs.
UNHCR: enhance gender inclusion into digital transformation through Coding Courses, Female Digital Career Counselor and creation of Digital Centre by women's group in camp 

UN WOMEN: Addressing the underrepresentation of women in leadership particularly at the local level, in executive roles, and across key sectors is crucial for fostering inclusive decision-making and strengthening accountability for gender equality. Promoting women’s leadership is also essential for achieving equality in governance, driving sustainable development, and ensuring that policies and decisions reflect the needs of all members of society. To this end, UN Women will strengthen the capacity of National Gender Machinery institutions,  strenthen gender accountability platforms, and policy dialogues. The progress achieved under the Gender Seal program, along with efforts to meaningfully engage men and boys in advancing gender equality, will be scaled up and sustained.

Additionally, to further enhance women’s leadership, UN Women will invest in capacity building, mentorship, and advocacy. Leadership skills will be nurtured through initiatives such as intergenerational dialogues, women’s networking, and the African Women Leaders Network (AWLN), with a strong focus on institutionalizing mentorship and transformational leadership programs across sectors.

During 2026, OHCHR provided technical and policy support to promote the integration of international human rights standards, non-discrimination and inclusion into national employment and social protection policies.
In October, OHCHR contributed to consultations on the National Employment Policy 2026–2036, providing specific recommendations on incorporating a human rights-based definition of decent work, strengthening accessible reporting and remedy mechanisms for labour rights violations, and addressing barriers to employment faced by persons in vulnerable situations.
OHCHR also participated in national consultations on extending social protection coverage and contributed to the development of the joint programme Financing Just Transitions in Rwanda: Scaling Formalization, Decent Jobs and Social Protection, in collaboration with UN agencies and national stakeholders. The programme document was signed by the Government and submitted to the SDG Fund in September 2026.

planEntities.name: Strengthen skills development systems and improve skills governance in KSA through assessment, capacity building activities, policy development and techncial support
planEntities.parentName: Increased knowledge and skills of population, especially women, girls and the most vulnerable groups, to enable them to participate in labor market, civic engagement and decision making
planEntities.description: The ILO is supporting Saudi Arabia in strengthening its national skills development system by establishing effective sectoral and national skills governance mechanisms. This includes setting up National Sector Skills Councils (NSSCs) to align workforce skills with labor market demands, improving competency standards, and enhancing skills policy coordination. The initiative aims to bridge the gap between education and employment, ensuring a demand-driven approach to skills development that supports economic growth and job creation. Additionally, the ILO will provide strategic guidance for developing a national skills policy, institutional frameworks, and action plans while embedding expertise within the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Development (MHRSD) to drive sustainable implementation. Through these efforts, the ILO aims to enhance workforce competitiveness, productivity, and alignment with Saudi Arabia’s Vision 2030 goals.

planEntities.name: Promote improved application of ILS, including on forced labour, through capacity building activities
planEntities.parentName: Strenghtened policy and legal frameworks in the labor sector to protect workers' rights and support equitable employment opportunities and safer labour migration
planEntities.description: The ILO is working to enhance awareness and implementation of International Labour Standards (ILS) in Saudi Arabia by organizing capacity-building workshops for key national stakeholders, including officials from the MHRSD, labor courts, and other relevant institutions. These workshops will strengthen understanding of ILO conventions and recommendations, improve compliance with international labor norms, and promote best practices in areas such as child labor, forced labor, and workplace equality. By fostering greater awareness and technical expertise, this initiative supports Saudi Arabia’s commitment to aligning its labor policies with global standards, ensuring fair and equitable working conditions while reinforcing the country’s broader labor market reforms.

planEntities.name: Support implementation of child labour (CL) policy through improved evidence and capacity building support
planEntities.parentName: Strenghtened policy and legal frameworks in the labor sector to protect workers' rights and support equitable employment opportunities and safer labour migration
planEntities.description: The ILO is supporting Saudi Arabia’s efforts to eliminate child labour by providing technical assistance and capacity building to align legislation and practice with international labour standards. Building on the National Child Labour Policy, the ILO is helping to ensure its effective implementation by strengthening the knowledge base, improving enforcement mechanisms, and promoting decent work alternatives for adults and youth of legal working age. This includes conducting sectoral studies on decent work in agriculture and the informal urban economy to assess employment conditions and their link to child labour. Additionally, the ILO is enhancing the capacity of labour inspectors, law enforcers, and child protection officials to better detect, report, and prevent child labour. These efforts support Saudi Arabia’s broader commitment, as reflected in its G20 leadership, to eradicating child labour and ensuring safe, fair, and sustainable employment conditions for all.

planEntities.name: Improve Occupational Safety and Health in line with international labour standards, through policy and systems' development as well as techncial and capacity building support.
planEntities.parentName: Strenghtened policy and legal frameworks in the labor sector to protect workers' rights and support equitable employment opportunities and safer labour migration
planEntities.description: The ILO is supporting Saudi Arabia in strengthening occupational safety and health (OSH) governance to ensure safer and healthier workplaces. Building on the National OSH Policy adopted in 2021, the ILO is working with the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Development (MHRSD) to develop and implement a comprehensive national OSH strategy, improve systems for reporting and recording workplace injuries and diseases, and transition OSH inspections towards a strategic compliance model. Additionally, the ILO is facilitating the development of sector-specific OSH guidance manuals to address work-related hazards, particularly in high-risk industries. These efforts aim to align Saudi Arabia’s workplace safety framework with international labor standards, enhance compliance, and foster a culture of prevention, ultimately improving working conditions and reducing occupational risks in line with the Kingdom’s broader labor market reforms.

planEntities.name: Foster cooperative development in KSA through policy development, and techncial and capacity building support
planEntities.parentName: Strenghtened policy and legal frameworks in the labor sector to protect workers' rights and support equitable employment opportunities and safer labour migration
planEntities.description: The ILO is supporting Saudi Arabia’s cooperative sector by enhancing its policy, regulatory framework, governance, and capacity-building efforts. This includes reviewing the National Cooperative Strategy and the Executive Regulation of the Cooperative Law to align them with international labor standards and best practices. The ILO is also working to strengthen the Cooperative Societies Council (CSC), refining its role as an Apex organization to better support cooperatives across the Kingdom. To build technical expertise, the ILO is providing training programs for cooperatives, government officials, and educators, including a Training of Trainers (ToT) initiative and workshops on cooperative management. Additionally, efforts are being made to improve national statistics on cooperatives and increase awareness of innovative cooperative models worldwide through study tours, webinars, and multimedia content. These initiatives aim to create an enabling environment for cooperative growth, promote financial and organizational sustainability, and enhance the cooperative sector’s contribution to Saudi Arabia’s economic and social development.

planEntities.name: Technical and capacity building support for effective functioning of the labour market information system in KSA
planEntities.parentName: Enhanced collection, provision, and dissemination of reliable and transparent data in accordance with International standard to support evidence-based decision and policy making
planEntities.description: The International Labour Organization (ILO) is working closely with the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Development (MHRSD) in Saudi Arabia to strengthen and fully operationalize the Labour Market Information System (LMIS). This system provides up-to-date data and indicators essential for analyzing the labour market and monitoring and evaluating employment programmes. Additionally, the ILO is building the capacity of MHRSD staff by providing technical support and training on operating the system and analyzing data, enabling them to develop evidence-based policies. Activities include updating the system, training staff on managing and analyzing labour market data, and enhancing institutional capacities to ensure sustainability and effectiveness.

planEntities.name: Support improved policy development and implementation through placement of international advisers in the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Development
planEntities.parentName: Strengthened capacity of government institutions at all levels to increase accountability, transparency and reliability towards people of KSA, especially from vulnerable groups in line with international standards to combat corruption and bribery, and foster an environment of integrity and responsible governance
planEntities.description: The ILO is strengthening Saudi Arabia’s employment and skills governance by positioning Technical Advisors on Employment and Skills within the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Development (MHRSD). These advisors will provide high-level technical expertise and on-the-job capacity building to support the development of national employment strategies, labor market analysis, skills policies, and impact assessment frameworks. Their role is to ensure that Saudi Arabia's labor policies and skills initiatives are data-driven, responsive to economic challenges, and aligned with international labor standards. This initiative reinforces the Ministry’s ability to address structural employment challenges, including youth employment and skills mismatches, while enhancing policy adaptation in times of crisis, such as post-pandemic recovery. Through this embedded advisory support, the ILO aims to strengthen Saudi Arabia’s workforce development and labor market governance in line with Vision 2030.

planEntities.name: Increased capacities of MHRSD staff on policy development, implementation and monitoring and evaluation
planEntities.parentName: Strengthened capacity of government institutions at all levels to increase accountability, transparency and reliability towards people of KSA, especially from vulnerable groups in line with international standards to combat corruption and bribery, and foster an environment of integrity and responsible governance
planEntities.description: The ILO is supporting Saudi Arabia’s Ministry of Human Resources and Social Development (MHRSD) in strengthening its policy development, monitoring, and impact assessment capacities to enhance labor and employment-related policymaking. This initiative aims to equip ministry staff with the necessary skills to develop and implement evidence-based policies that improve employment outcomes. Through specialized training courses and on-the-job capacity building, the ILO is enhancing MHRSD’s ability to formulate, evaluate, and refine labor market policies using robust data and impact assessment methods. By fostering a more strategic and analytical approach to employment policy, this effort contributes to more effective labor market governance and alignment with Saudi Arabia’s broader workforce development goals.

planEntities.name: Establishment of Social Dialogue institutions with UN support
planEntities.parentName: Strengthened capacity of government institutions and multi-stakeholder partnerships promoting improved services and social dialogue to advance a peaceful, just, and inclusive society for all
planEntities.description: The ILO is supporting Saudi Arabia in strengthening its social dialogue framework by assisting in the establishment of a dedicated Social Dialogue Unit within the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Development (MHRSD) and facilitating the creation of a national tripartite social dialogue council. These initiatives aim to institutionalize structured dialogue between the government, employers, and workers to enhance labor relations and policy-making. Additionally, the ILO is working with Saudi authorities to support the ratification of key international labor conventions related to social dialogue and tripartism. Through these efforts, the ILO seeks to create a more inclusive and participatory labor governance system, in line with international standards and Saudi Arabia’s broader labor market reforms.

planEntities.parentName: Strengthened capacity of government institutions and multi-stakeholder partnerships promoting improved services and social dialogue to advance a peaceful, just, and inclusive society for all
planEntities.description:
The ITU Arab Regional Office partnered with the Communications Space & Technology Commission (CST) of Saudi Arabia since 2019 to support the dissemination of digital regulation trainings throughout the various ITU regions, while benefit the Digital Regulation capacity of Saudi Arabia as well. The project is being implemented in three phases of two years each. While the first phases ended in 2022, the first addendum added a third phase to the project that ended in 2024. Currently, the third addendum is being finalized and ready to sign with Saudi Arabia CST in order to implement a third phase for the project that will extend implementation to the end of 2026. The latest regional event supported by the project was a regional digital regulation training for Africa, that took part in 12-22 Nov 2024. The project has played a pivotal role in advancing digital regulation and transformation and strengthening national expertise in Saudi Arabia, which can be regarded currently as a Digital Regulator, especially after Saudi's creation of a National Digital Regulations Committee as part of the impact of this project on the Kingdom. 
Please note that financial contribution from the ITU to this project is assessed based on in kind contribution.

planEntities.name: Developing a national model for trade and shock simulations (ATSI)
planEntities.parentName: Strengthened capacity of government institutions at all levels to increase accountability, transparency and reliability towards people of KSA, especially from vulnerable groups in line with international standards to combat corruption and bribery, and foster an environment of integrity and responsible governance
planEntities.description:
Upon receiving the technical assistance request from the Ministry of Economy and Planning in Saudi Arabia, ESCWA presented Economic Tools for trade analysis and the panel of Arab countries to simulate alternative national, regional and global trade policies and economic shocks on the national economy. During the various meetings organized at the ministry, other tools and potential developments were also presented and discussed including carbon tax on trade, and trade simulations at product level using modified versions of TASTE software.  The aim of the project is to introduce the major features of the existing interfaces and models and how they can be used by the Ministry for their daily work. The Ministry’s focal point expressed high interest to undertake a technical cooperation with ESCWA on developing tailored national versions of the GETSI and TASTI programs to timely assess the new trade agreements under negotiations between Saudi Arabia and its major trade partners in coordination with the rest of the GCC. The ministry expressed interest also to use GETSI To update its forecast for the kingdom and assess global changes on its economy. 
Capacity building workshops were thus organized:
1) Preparatory workshop in Saudi Arabia
2) training workshop on GETSI SA once finalized
3) Training workshop on linking GETSI-SA to simulation at products level using TASTE and GETSI

planEntities.name: Development of Makkah Region Authority
planEntities.parentName: Enhanced collection, provision, and dissemination of reliable and transparent data in accordance with International standard to support evidence-based decision and policy making
planEntities.description: ESCWA held an online coordination meeting with the Makkah Region Development Authority (MRDA) on 26 May 2025 to clarify needs and define the scope of support for the Makkah Urban Observatory. Following the meeting, MRDA shared three core indicator documents, enabling ESCWA’s urban development team to begin the technical review. The team conducted a comprehensive compatibility assessment between the Saudi indicator set and ESCWA’s Urban Monitoring Framework (UMF), introducing a refined compatibility scale and completing a full indicator-by-indicator mapping. The analysis also incorporated SDG linkages and visualized areas of alignment, synergies, and measurement gaps. These outputs were consolidated into a compatibility matrix, which ESCWA presented to MRDA on 29 September 2025.

planEntities.description: This project is entitled: “Spatial Planning Reform and Visual Appeal Program in Saudi Arabia” is implemented by UNDP and UN-Habitat to support MOMAH. Over the course of four years, this initiative aims to enable systemic municipal and planning reforms and provide essential implementation and capacity-building support for the sustainable urbanization of Saudi cities. The project's overarching goal is to reinforce the Spatial Planning Reform and Visual Appeal Program in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia. This ambitious endeavor seeks to achieve six main outcomes, each designed to enhance the efficiency and effectiveness of urban development and planning practices within the nation: 1. Delivering International Best Practices: The project aims to ensure that regional plans, local plans, and urban codes adhere to international best practices, setting a high standard for Saudi Arabia's urban development. 2. National Urban Policy: By developing a National Urban Policy to help govern and cascade urban governance and management at all levels, will help contribute to enhancing Saudi cities to develop sustainably and holistically. 3. Empowering Local Planning Departments: Through a new Operating Model for Planning Departments, the initiative empowers and enables local planning departments to better serve their communities. 4. Enhancing the Municipal System: The project seeks to improve and restructure the municipal system, updating settlement boundaries, revising classification, and optimizing service delivery for greater efficiency and sustainability. 5. Restructuring the Planning Framework: The Saudi planning framework will undergo a significant overhaul, with planning tools redefined, updated, and improved in alignment with new classification and categorization standards. Additionally, new tools will be introduced to support implementation and capacity-building efforts. 6. Upscaling the MOMAH Urban Design Studio: The existing MOMAH Urban Design Studio will evolve into a fully-fledged Urban Lab, equipped to spearhead innovative projects and serve as a hub for satellite labs supporting MOMAH’s mission.

planEntities.name: Supporting the localization of SDGs in Saudi Arabia (Madinah and Qassim)
planEntities.parentName: Enhanced implementation of strategies and policies to safeguard cultural and natural heritage,and promote sustainable urbanizition, prioritizing the needs of vulnerable populations
planEntities.description: As part of UN-Habitat's global mandate to support countries advance on the implementation of the SDGs at the local level, UN-Habitat has developed a comprehensive approach to enable local action in the UN system, by providing assistance through all stages of planning, policymaking, project development and monitoring. One of the five main components of SDG localization, includes support to cities in completing Voluntary Local Reviews (VLRs). In Saudi Arabia, UN-Habitat has supported Madinah and Buraydah (Al-Qassim) in undertaking and completing a VLR each. In Madinah, the technical assistance was geared towards supporting the Madinah Development Authority in reaching its SDG targets and adopting a people-centred urban planning approach towards becoming a dynamic, smart and sustainable city, delivering enriching experience for its communities and visitors. Next steps following the strategic plan and its impact will hopefully materialize during the course of 2025 and beyond. The VLR for Buraydah (Al-Qassim) was implemented in partnership with ESCWA with the view to support this authority enhance their existing approach to urban planning through evidence-based decision-making, leveraging high-quality data collection supported by the Qassim Urban Observatory. The Buraydah VLR focused on a structure approach to mainstreaming SDGs, promoting several stakeholder engagement activities and empowering local sustainable development aligned with national and global agendas. More than 60 indicators tracking the city’s performance were constructed, providing insights on the progress, limits and potential for 7 of the 17 SDGs – namely, SDG 1, 3, 4, 5, 6 11 and 17. The results aim to guide Buraydah urban development trajectory.

planEntities.name: National Urban Policy for the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia
planEntities.parentName: Enhanced implementation of strategies and policies to safeguard cultural and natural heritage,and promote sustainable urbanizition, prioritizing the needs of vulnerable populations
planEntities.description:
The National Urban Policy (NUP) initiative provides a national framework to guide how cities and settlements grow and function. It brings together spatial planning, economic development, housing, infrastructure, and social inclusion into one coherent direction. The aim is to support balanced development across regions, improve quality of life, and align urban growth with national priorities and long-term sustainability goals.

The initiative focuses on clarifying roles and responsibilities across institutions, reducing fragmentation, and strengthening coordination between national, regional, and local levels. Through analysis, stakeholder engagement, and policy development, the NUP helps translate high-level national objectives into practical guidance for urban planning and decision-making. It also supports consistency across sectoral policies that affect cities, such as transport, housing, land management, and environmental protection.

A core part of the NUP is building an evidence base to understand urban trends, challenges, and gaps. This includes reviewing existing policies, assessing governance and legal frameworks, and identifying priority issues that affect cities and municipalities. The process emphasizes inclusive engagement, ensuring that public entities and relevant stakeholders contribute to shaping a shared vision for urban development.

Overall, the NUP serves as a strategic reference for future reforms, investments, and implementation tools. It does not replace existing plans or laws, but provides a common policy umbrella to guide them. By doing so, it supports more coordinated, efficient, and resilient urban development over time.

planEntities.description: The AlUla Walkable Neighbourhood Programme (AWNP), proposed by the Royal Commission for AlUla (RCU) and the French Agency for AlUla Development (AfAlUla) and supported by UN‑Habitat, aims to transform AlUla from a car‑oriented to a leading pedestrian‑friendly city. It focuses on delivering practical, operational outputs: review and refinement of a Walkability KPI framework and baseline assessments, a roadmap and implementation plan, a Complete Streets design manual, and a Walkable Neighbourhood Design & Policy Report. Alongside these technical outputs, UN‑Habitat will design and develop an AlUla Urban Lab as a strategic institutional platform to translate frameworks into policies and pilots, test innovations, coordinate cross‑sectoral stakeholders, and build local capacity and knowledge products for scaling.

planEntities.description: The project objective is to enhance water use efficiency in irrigation in Saudi Arabia through the implementation of a capacity building initiative. Staff of the Saudi Irrigation Organization (SIO) will be targeted by a workshop / training focused on implementing water savings in irrigation and on the urban and agricultural reuse of reclaimed water including international case studies and good practices. They will then provide related on-the-job training to at least one local community in Al Ahsa where women and youth will be actively engaged. The lessons learnt will then be used to enhance the training, upgrade it, and upscale it nationwide.

planEntities.name: Enhanced capacities to measure e-commerce and digital trade to empower digital economy policymaking
planEntities.parentName: Enhanced collection, provision, and dissemination of reliable and transparent data in accordance with International standard to support evidence-based decision and policy making
planEntities.description: The project aims to establish the evidence base needed to understand the current “state of play” regarding e-commerce in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia (KSA) and provide a baseline against which to monitor future developments and the impact of policy actions. It consists of two tracks – a “domestic” track focusing on Saudi businesses as key actors in the e-commerce landscape with a view to assessing the degree of uptake of e-commerce and the value of business transactions facilitated by e-commerce in the Kingdom, and an “international track” supporting the development of internationally agreed guidelines and recommendations on measuring e commerce value through the UNCTAD Task Group on Measuring E-commerce Value (TG eCOM). The international track also includes the development of training materials based on those guidelines and recommendations, as well as the delivery of two regional training workshops to support their implementation across countries. The international track offers an opportunity for KSA to make the priority given to e-commerce measurement visible on the international stage and to cement a position among the leaders in this area, building upon previous initiatives such as the “Roadmap toward a common framework for measuring the digital economy” developed under the 2020 Saudi Arabian Presidency of the G20.

planEntities.description:
UNESCO plays a pivotal role in advancing the teaching profession globally, regionally, and nationally. In the Arab Region, UNESCO supports teacher policies, professional development, and inclusive education systems, working closely with Member States to address teacher shortages and improve quality education. Globally, UNESCO leads initiatives such as the International Task Force on Teachers for Education 2030, which promotes sustainable solutions to teacher challenges worldwide.
Saudi Arabia is an active member of the Teacher Task Force and has demonstrated strong commitment to global education efforts. Notably, the Kingdom supported the translation of UNESCO’s "Global Report on Teachers: Addressing Teacher shortages and transforming the Profession" into Arabic, facilitating broader regional engagement. The Arabic edition of the report was officially launched in Riyadh in May 2025, marking a significant milestone in regional collaboration for teacher development.

planEntities.name: Technical support provided for the establishment of UNESCO designated sites (MAB program or Geoparks) for inclusive and integrated management approaches linking biodiversity conservation and sustainable socio-economic development.
planEntities.parentName: Enhanced sustainable natural resources management system (water, forest, marine) to safeguard natural resources, preserve biodiversity, and maintain ecological balance in KSA.
planEntities.description:
KSA’s National Center for Wildlife acts as focal point for the UNESCO Man and the Biosphere Programme and has developed a management plan for the 2021–2023 period driven by the KSA’s aim to sustainably manage its natural resources and diversify its income generation away from the oil revenues by developing its emergent tourism sector. UNESCO is supporting the efforts of KSA through the organization of training, as well as through technical guidance.
In June 2022, Harrat Uwayrid was nominated as the second UNESCO Biosphere reserve in the country. KSA Natcom is heading the joint committee for MAB and Geoparks programs. KSA Natcom is also a member of the executive board of the ARABMAB network, headed by the UAE. To mark the International Day for Biosphere Reserves, 3rd November 2024, UNESCO, together with the National Center for Wildlife and Saudi Natcom, co-hosted the 1st Edition of the ARABMAB Youth Forum. 
Saudi Arabia submitted the nomination dossier for Imam Turki Bin Abdullah as the 3rd biosphere reserve in the kingdom. The MAB secretariat confirmed acceptance of the nomination dossier. The AlUla oasis also has great potential to join the UNESCO BR network. This is a subject that is currently at the heart of discussions between UNESCO and the Royal Commission AlUla (RCU), which has shown great interest in submitting a nomination dossier for the AlUla oasis as a UNESCO BR. In a strategic partnership being initiated between UNESCO and RCU, a global alliance will be launched to safeguard and sustainably develop oases worldwide. The proposed alliance aims to address these challenges by fostering international collaboration and sharing knowledge to protect, regenerate, and sustainably develop oases across the globe, capitalizing on the lessons learned from oases designated as UNESCO biosphere reserves. This alliance, led by AlUla Oasis, will create a platform for connecting oases worldwide, enabling them to benefit from collective expertise in heritage conservation, sustainable agriculture, water management, biodiversity preservation, and climate resilience.
UNESCO continues to promote the geopark concept in Saudi Arabia.  Two UNESCO Global Geoparks were designated in April 2025 by the UNESCO’s Executive Board: the Geological Park in Northern Riyadh, 120 kilometers from the capital, and the Salma Geological Park in Hail, northern Saudi Arabia.  
UNESCO, National Center for Vegetation Cover Development and Combating Desertification (NCVC) and the Saudi Natcom organized a regional training on Geoparks program, in November 2024. NCVC expressed interest in hosting the second edition of the regional training to foster collaboration among Arab countries, exchange best practices and promote the concept of UNESCO Geoparks in the region.

As a first step, UNESCO conducted a mapping of the integration of climate change education in the education system in the Gulf States and is ready to develop joint programming with the MOE and the NatCom in KSA.

UNESCO is working in KSA on building capacities on preservation, digitalization and access to documentary heritage, building capacity on AI for civil servants and for judges, access to information trainings for civil servants and OER and IFAP program (IFAP Symposium and IFAP national commission) and MIL and AI literacy. 

On 16 August 2024, The Government of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia decided to present its candidature to the IFAP Council, at the elections to be held during the 43rd session of the General Conference of UNESCO in November 2025. UNESCO is currently in discussion with the KSA National Commission to organize a conference on the IFAP programme that will be followed by the establishment of a national committee for the IFAP. 

UNESCO is supporting KSA to improve its representation in the Memory of the World International Registry. Saudi Arabia has two inscriptions in the Memory of the World International Register:  Earliest Islamic (Kufic) inscription: The Inscription of Zuhair, 2003 and Arabian Chronicles in Stone: Jabal Ikmah, 2023 

Through the Royal Commission for AlUla, Saudi Arabia has committed to promoting documentary heritage from AlUla (ongoing) and Saudi Arabia in general through a contribution of USD 2,595,850 (2.59M) to the Memory of the World Programme of UNESCO.  The flagship activity under the AlUla MoW project i.e. Kingdom’s Institute Platform Conference for Innovating the Preservation of documentary heritage, was hosted in April 2025 at UNESCO HQ to create a stable dialogue mechanism open to the Arab region, which will act as a public sphere for discussion and presentation of best practices and novelties related to documentary heritage in the Arab world.

The limited availability of data impedes advocacy efforts and opportunities for leveraging additional resources. The project number is 230141 ( and not 182259). This project aims at supporting the institutional capacity of the National Industrial and Mining Information Center (NIIC) of the Ministry of Industry and Mining (MIM) in Saudi Arabia, in collecting and analysing statistical information for informing policy decisions in a timely and sustainable manner. This in light of the enhanced data needs to support the implementation of the National Industrial Strategy (NIS).
The project overall objective is to strengthen the availability and quality of manufacturing and mining data at National Industrial and Mining Information Center (NIIC) of the Ministry of Industry and Mining (MIM) in Saudi Arabia, to support the implementation and monitoring of the National Industrial Strategy (NIS) and related policies. It also seeks to enhance coordination within the national statistical system and promote the use of industrial performance indicators for policy guidance.

planEntities.name: National capacities supported and strengthened to effectively prevent, suppress and punish trafficking in persons in accordance with international standards and best practices, and to achieve sustainable impact through implementation of the National Action Plan against TiP
planEntities.parentName: Strenghtened policy and legal frameworks in the labor sector to protect workers' rights and support equitable employment opportunities and safer labour migration
planEntities.description:
UNODC has been engaged with the Saudi Human Rights Commission (HRC), as chair entity of the National Committee to Combat Human Trafficking (NCCHT) since February 2020 in a multi-phased project of technical cooperation in the field of combating trafficking in persons (TiP). Therethrough, UNODC supports national efforts spearheaded by the HRC/NCCHT in preventing and combating TiP through a victim-centred approach that upholds the rights of trafficked and potential victims to protection, support, and care in line with international standards and norms and best practices.
Achievements under Phase I (February 2020 - August 2022) include the launch of the National Referral Mechanism (NRM) on 31 March 2020 which is currently managed by a central team in Riyadh together with 13 sub-teams in all regions across the Kingdom for effective coordination in dealing with TiP cases; the establishment of TiP specialized courts in all regions of the Kingdom with 124 prosecutors; the creation of the first-ever anti-TiP specialized Prosecution Unit on 30 July 2022; the creation of a specialized TiP Data Management Team; the development and adoption of the National Action Plan to Combat TiP (2021-2023); the legislative review and reform of the Kafala sponsorship system; and the delivery of 33 capacity-building activities that benefited over 1,600 officials within government entities, institutions, and CSOs.
Phase II (3 years, launched in March 2023) focuses on sustaining the outcomes of Phase I and further supporting the Kingdom through the implementation of the National Action Plan (NAP) against TiP. Activities include reviewing and updating the NRM; developing the electronic format of the NRM to support the availability, accuracy, and timeliness of TiP-related data; building monitoring and evaluation capacities for the implementation of the NAP; raising awareness of labour dispute committees, the media, the private sector and through religious authorities; conducting legislative and policy reviews; strengthening national capacities of law enforcement and criminal justice for the investigation, prosecution, and adjudication of TiP cases; supporting the creation of a national training resource/hub on preventing and combating TiP; and promoting the creation of partnerships for knowledge and best practices exchange.

planEntities.name: Advancing Human Capital Development in Tourism
planEntities.parentName: Increased knowledge and skills of population, especially women, girls and the most vulnerable groups, to enable them to participate in labor market, civic engagement and decision making
planEntities.description: Since 2024, the Ministry of Tourism of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, in collaboration with UN Tourism, is strengthening human capital development through e-learning, workforce research, and education quality enhancement, ensuring a skilled and inclusive tourism workforce. A key initiative was the development of ten new Massive Open Online Courses (MOOCs), covering destination marketing, event management, digital transformation, and hospitality operations, and providing scholarships for Saudi residents, prioritizing accessibility, including for women. Addressing workforce challenges, the Tourism Labour Market Observatory (TLMO) is formulating a Comprehensive Labour Market Report and an AI Impact Analysis on Tourism Jobs, offering data-driven insights to shape policies that foster diversity and inclusion. Additionally, the UN Tourism.TedQual Certification is supporting Saudi institutions to align with global quality standards, reinforced by mentoring and quality assurance programs. The Tourism Faculty Development Programme (TFDP) further enhances curriculum design and modern teaching methodologies, equipping educators - particularly women - with advanced skills to lead in tourism education. Through these efforts, the Ministry of Tourism and UN Tourism are enhancing Saudi Arabia’s leadership role in tourism education and workforce development, fostering sustainable growth, innovation, and gender inclusivity in the sector. To support the tourism industry at the global level, the Ministry of Tourism of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia requested UN Tourism to make the MOOCs available in the UN Tourism Online Academy and that these are delivered in Arabic, English, Spanish, French, and Chinese.

planEntities.parentName: Enhanced access to essential inclusive social and protection services for all, based on principles of human rights, gender equality, and inclusion of the most vulnerable populations.
planEntities.description: The establishment of the Tourism Law Observatory for the Middle East through the UN Tourism Regional Office in Riyadh represents a milestone in strengthening legal and institutional frameworks for tourism in the region. Building on the success of the first Observatory in Latin America and the Caribbean, this initiative provides a digital knowledge hub to collect, analyse, and disseminate tourism-related laws and regulations, while fostering dialogue among governments, experts, and academia. For Saudi Arabia, hosting the Observatory reinforces its leadership role in regulatory innovation and governance, in line with Vision 2030’s objective to create a competitive and transparent business environment that supports sustainable tourism growth. The initiative also enhances the Kingdom’s capacity to influence regional harmonisation of tourism law, attract investment through legal security, and position Riyadh as a centre of excellence and cooperation for tourism governance in the Middle East.

planEntities.name: Regional Conference on Inclusive Tourism in the Middle East - Creating Accessible, Equitable, and Competitive Destinations
planEntities.parentName: Enhanced access to essential inclusive social and protection services for all, based on principles of human rights, gender equality, and inclusion of the most vulnerable populations.
planEntities.description: The Regional Conference on Inclusive Tourism in the Middle East will be organised through UN Tourism’s Regional Office for the Middle East. The conference responds to Member States’ priorities of building more inclusive, equitable, and competitive tourism destinations, with a focus on accessible tourism, senior tourism, and women’s empowerment in tourism. It brings together government representatives, international organisations, the private sector, and civil society leaders to exchange experiences, identify challenges, and showcase policies and initiatives that advance inclusivity. The conference provides the Kingdom with visibility as a champion of accessibility and gender empowerment, while highlighting ongoing national efforts such as accessibility initiatives in Hajj and Umrah, transport systems, and hospitality services. This conference will also help the Kingdom to attract global attention and reinforce Saudi Arabia’s capacity to shape the inclusivity agenda in tourism. Moreover, with Saudi experts and institutions featured as speakers and moderators across multiple panels, the event supports domestic capacity building, strengthens collaboration with international partners, and enhances the Kingdom’s reputation as a forward-looking, socially responsible tourism destination.

planEntities.description: Under this sub-output, UN Women aim to strengthen the women’s movement and civil society engagement in advancing Gender Equality and Women’s Empowerment (GEWE) and ending Violence Against Women and Girls (VAWG) and Harmful Practices (HP) by providing integrated technical and financial support to grassroots and women’s rights organizations to implement evidence-based advocacy aligned with the Spotlight Initiative theory of change; enhancing the capacity of marginalized women’s groups to participate in inclusive chiefdom and district-level development planning and influence gender-responsive policies and budgets; building civil society competencies to effectively implement, monitor, and report on gender-transformative legal and policy frameworks such as the GEWE Act; facilitating the meaningful participation of women’s movements including those representing intersecting forms of discrimination—in key national, regional, and global platforms to amplify their voices and influence policy discourse; strengthening community-based organizations’ capacity for knowledge generation, documentation, and dissemination of best practices for advocacy; and undertaking a comprehensive mapping of the women’s movement landscape to inform the development of a coordinated, inclusive, and sustainable movement-building strategy that enhances collective action and advocacy impact

planEntities.name: Comprehensive beneficiary mobilization methodology developed, operationalized to facilitate beneficiary selection for inclusive job creation for youth and women in climate-smart agriculture value chains and waste management.
planEntities.parentName: Farmers, fisherfolks, and nature-based SMEs adopt sustainable practices and standards and benefit from increased access to technology, finance, information, and facilities for improved income, livelihoods, and production of diverse, safe and nutritious food
planEntities.description:
This methodology outlines a structured, inclusive, and participatory approach to identify, verify, and prepare Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) and Male Champions as project beneficiaries across Sierra Leone’s Southern, Eastern, and Western Area regions. The strategy prioritizes transparency, gender equity, Environmental and Social (E&S) Considerations with a strong cost efficiency approach and focus on engaging women- and youth-led enterprises. UN Women will employ evidenced based approach, levering on existing top-performing MSMES and cooperatives data bases to participate in the selection process. Clear criteria and standardized screening forms are established to identify, assess, and verify candidates for participation in the project. Mobilize women, youth, and Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises as beneficiaries of the WOKDONCAM Project according to the project appraisal report will include;
1. To identify, verify, and mobilize beneficiaries engaged in agriculture, fisheries, and waste management within the designated project locations.
2. To compile and submit a list of qualified potential beneficiaries for consideration and approval by the project team.
3. To conduct awareness-raising activities targeting beneficiaries and local authorities to ensure understanding and support for the project.
4. To inform beneficiaries of training logistics, including date, venue, and participant allocation per enterprise, group, or association, in alignment with the program’s training schedule.
5. To identify and engage male champions at the community level who will advocate for women’s economic empowerment.

planEntities.name: Strengthen agro-processing across rice value chains, mechanization and processing, and poultry and livestock subsectors to enhance productivity, value addition, and sustainable livelihood opportunities.
planEntities.parentName: Farmers, fisherfolks, and nature-based SMEs adopt sustainable practices and standards and benefit from increased access to technology, finance, information, and facilities for improved income, livelihoods, and production of diverse, safe and nutritious food
planEntities.description: This sub-output focuses on strengthening agro-processing systems across rice value chains, mechanization and processing, and poultry and livestock subsectors through targeted investments, capacity development, and technology adoption. It includes the provision and operationalization of appropriate processing equipment, promotion of climate-smart and efficient production techniques, and enhancement of post-harvest handling and value addition practices. The intervention also supports skills development for beneficiaries, particularly women and youth in processing, packaging, quality assurance, and agribusiness management. In collaboration with relevant stakeholders and market actors, the approach facilitates improved market linkages and access to value chains. As a result, the initiative contributes to increased productivity, reduced post-harvest losses, enhanced product quality, and expanded income-generating opportunities, ultimately promoting sustainable livelihoods and inclusive job creation.

planEntities.name: The institutional capacity of local councils and key Ministries Department and Agencies (MDAs) strengthened to effectively deliver inclusive and gender-sensitive services that uphold the leave no one behind (LNOB) principles for underserved communities
planEntities.parentName: Democratic institutions at all levels are strengthened to be inclusive, accountable, transparent, gender-responsive and rights compliant for enhanced rule of law, equity, and peaceful coexistence.
planEntities.description:
Under this output, the project will scale up investment in the five piloted local councils and one additional district to further strengthen their capacities in gender mainstreaming across development planning, monitoring, and implementation. The planned scale-up of gender-responsive budgeting (GRB) capacity is both timely and aligned with ongoing national efforts. While pilot Ministries Department and Agencies (MDAs) are already operating under GRB obligations and some local councils have undertaken gender-budget analyses, implementation at the local level remains inconsistent and limited. The project’s support, comprising web-based monitoring and reporting platform, training, tools, mentorship, and peer learning, will therefore be critical in helping councils institutionalize GRB practices and achieve more inclusive, gender-sensitive resource allocation. The Minister of Gender has expressed a strong need to strengthen the capacity of ministry staff to effectively implement national laws, including the GEWE Act 2022 and related legislation, to ensure professional, consistent, and gender-responsive service delivery across all levels. The local councils and key Ministry staff require structured training, practical tools, and opportunities for peer learning to operationalize gender-responsive governance, planning, budgeting, service delivery, monitoring, and advocacy.
Building on existing gains, the project will equip staff on key gender related topics and resource mobilization strategies, including proposal writing, donor engagement, and public-private partnerships and leverage innovative tools, partnerships and develop accredited training modules building on the induction manuals created by UN Women and UNICEF for the Ministry of Gender and Children’s Affairs (MOGCA). Standardized toolkits, peer learning exchanges, and technical mentorship will enable rapid replication and adaptation of gender-responsive practices across councils. Priority areas include Prevention of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse/Harassment (PSEA/H), GBV protection protocols, disability, child protection, advocacy, communication, leadership and governance skills.
Additionally, the project will strengthen monitoring, reporting, and accountability mechanisms by establishing a decentralized web-based Monitoring, Evaluation and accountability platform with user-friendly dashboards, real-time data collection, and interoperability. This will be aligned with the National Monitoring and Evaluation Authority (NaMEA) and integrated existing national systems. Using the UN Results-Based Management approach, the project will integrate gender-responsive indicators and adaptive monitoring into local and national planning processes.This will improve the availability and use of disaggregated data, including sex, age, and disability, for evidence-based decision-making.
The project will also build on existing work by development partners such as the World Bank and UNDP, which have supported local governance reforms and M&E strengthening. Lessons from their performance assessment systems, digital tools, and capacity-building initiatives will be incorporated to reinforce complementarities, avoid duplication, and accelerate the adoption of transparent and gender-responsive M&E practices across councils and ministries.

planEntities.name: Increased public awareness, mobilization to preventing and responding to violence against women and girls in targeted communities
planEntities.parentName: People, especially marginalized and vulnerable groups in hard-to-reach communities, benefit from coordinated and effective implementation of policies and strategies enabling social cohesion and economic transformation.
planEntities.description: Under this sub-output, UN Women will support coordination through the Ministry of Gender and Children’s Affairs (MoGCA) and its partners for continued public awareness raising on gender related laws and policies and public service provision. The project will support the commemoration of key international and national days dedicated to promoting gender equality and ending violence against women and girls. Activities will be tailored to the national and district specific context and will include innovative approaches including town hall meetings and AI and media supported content to raise awareness on existing SGBV response mechanisms and frameworks, while fostering community involvement in prevention and response efforts. Key stakeholders will include local councils, traditional and religious leaders, legal aid personnel, police (including community policing units), medical staff, civil society organizations, and community members—women, men, boys, and girls. In addition, the project will leveraging digital advocacy through social media platforms to disseminate informative content, graphics, and videos that educate the public on different forms of violence, warning signs, and available support services for survivors, recognizing the urgent need for prevention and survivor-centered support.

planEntities.name: Strengthen social protection and response structures for improved access to inclusive, gender related information and services for women, youth and girls, particularly marginalized groups
planEntities.parentName: People, especially marginalized and vulnerable groups in hard-to-reach communities, benefit from coordinated and effective implementation of policies and strategies enabling social cohesion and economic transformation.
planEntities.description:
UN Women will strengthen social protection and response structures by expanding access to information, improving service delivery, and enhancing real-time responsiveness for marginalized and digitally excluded populations. User-friendly digital tools such as Unstructured Supplementary Service Data (USSD) and Interactive Voice Response (IVR) systems would be employed to scale the use of mobile phone communication (analog phone) accessible by members of rural communities. By embedding this element into a local government service delivery framework, the initiative would seek to bridge the gap between policy and practice, ensuring no one is left behind to achieve protection, dignity and equal opportunity. This would also aid understanding of national policies and cultural appropriate information and foster access to information in local dialects.

The project will further Strengthen Community-Based referrals and Redress Mechanisms for Gender-Based Violence (GBV) through the development of strong community-based redress mechanisms to address discrimination, violence, and non-compliance with gender laws, responding to GBV issues especially for marginalized groups in the local communities. The project will leverage existing community structures to serve as safe homes through rehabilitation, coordination and logistical support for effective and efficient service delivery to SGBV victims, while simultaneously carrying out a study on best practices and developing a business case for sustainability of safe spaces in Sierra Leone.

planEntities.name: 2.2.11 Joint Programme (IOM) Strengthening Migration Governance and Asylum Systems in Serbia: Enhancing policies, Protecting Rights
planEntities.parentName: Output 2.2. Public policies and legislative reform, aligned with EU standards, are accelerated through institutional capacity building to ensure sustainable economic growth, protect labour rights, promote safe and regular migration, address wage gaps, advance the ‘silver economy’, address the economy of care and enhance labour force participation, especially among women, youth and vulnerable groups.
planEntities.description:
National stakeholders in Serbia are supported to develop evidenced-based migration policies in line with adopted EU and other international standards and commitments
National and local strategic and normative framework for migration governance strengthened and SCRM knowledge and skills strengthened for better policy development, planning, implementation, monitoring, reporting and information sharing and facilitated international cooperation in line with EU accession commitments.

The overarching goal of the project is to enhance national authorities' capacities to achieve effective and efficient migration governance and protection of rights of individuals in need of international protection, as well as other vulnerable individuals within mixed movements in Serbia.
This objective is anchored in the principles of rights-based and route-based approaches, ensuring that the most vulnerable receive the protection and assistance they need, as well as promoting regular migration pathways for safe, regular, and orderly migration. In this context, the terms ‘individuals in need of international protection’ refers to refugees or asylum seekers while ‘other vulnerable individuals’, refers to migrants in vulnerable situation, i.e. individuals who may face significant risks or vulnerabilities without necessarily seeking asylum, including victims of trafficking or unaccompanied and separated children (UASC). The long-term impact of the project is the creation of a more robust and rights-sensitive migration and asylum management systems in Serbia. This system will be better equipped to address the complexities of mixed movements, ensuring that individuals in need of protection are identified and assisted promptly, while also supporting their long-term integration into society.

planEntities.description:
The overarching goal of the project is to enhance national authorities' capacities to achieve effective and efficient migration governance and protection of rights of individuals in need of international protection, as well as other vulnerable individuals within mixed movements in Serbia.
This objective is anchored in the principles of rights-based and route-based approaches, ensuring that the most vulnerable receive the protection and assistance they need, as well as promoting regular migration pathways for safe, regular, and orderly migration. In this context, the terms ‘individuals in need of international protection’ refers to refugees or asylum seekers while ‘other vulnerable individuals’, refers to migrants in vulnerable situation, i.e. individuals who may face significant risks or vulnerabilities without necessarily seeking asylum, including victims of trafficking or unaccompanied and separated children (UASC). The long-term impact of the project is the creation of a more robust and rights-sensitive migration and asylum management systems in Serbia. This system will be better equipped to address the complexities of mixed movements, ensuring that individuals in need of protection are identified and assisted promptly, while also supporting their long-term integration into society.

planEntities.description:
U PRO PLUS focuses its work on enhancing territorial development management, supporting economic growth, and improving social infrastructure and cohesion. 
Within efforts to Improve development planning and introduce integrated territorial investment concept, the Programme supports development of Sustainable Urban Development (SUD) and Integrated Territorial Investment (ITI) strategies using EU territorial mechanisms. The key beneficiaries are local self-governments and regional development agencies, along with institutions at institutions at local and regional levels. The Programme also supports design of the national model for integrated and sustainable territorial development at the national level, in partnership with the Ministry of European Integrations. 

In 2023, development of 12 territorial strategies is planned to be completed, and a grant scheme for implementation of projects deriving from these strategies launched. Additionally, EU PRO Plus will implement a number of capacity building activities for stakeholders at all levels. 

Equal opportunities and representation of women in activities related to capacity building are supported by inclusion elements of gender equality in the Plan for building the capacity of national institutions for the introduction of instruments of integral territorial development.

Public policies and legislative reform, aligned with EU standards, are accelerated through institutional capacity building to ensure sustainable economic growth, protect labour rights, promote safe and regular migration, address wage gaps, advance the ‘silver economy’, address the economy of care and enhance labour force participation, especially among women, youth and vulnerable groups.
planEntities.description:
The EU Support to Integrated Sustainable Territorial Development – EU INTEGRA is a flagship initiative funded by the European Union (EU) to advance integrated territorial development in Serbia. The Programme supports the implementation of the EU Cohesion Policy 2021–2027 by enhancing governance, reducing regional disparities, and preparing Serbian institutions for future structural and investment funding. With a total budget of 15 million Euros, the Programme is implemented under the strategic leadership of the Ministry of European Integration (MEI), and delivered through two complementary components: The Standing Conference of Towns and Municipalities (SCTM) is responsible for implementing a project worth 12 million Euros, which includes managing a 10.14 million Euro grant scheme aimed at supporting integrated development projects and strengthening local capacities for territorial governance.
UNOPS manages 3 million Euros to strengthen the institutional framework, build capacities, and support the development and implementation of territorial strategies at the national, regional, and local levels. EU INTEGRA builds on the experiences of previous EU-funded Programmes, including the EU PRO Plus, scaling up Serbia’s readiness for future EU Cohesion Policy funding and reinforcing territorial development efforts.

Implemented in cooperation with Frontex, the Ministry of Interior of Serbia and the Serbian Border Police, the project focuses on enhancing surveillance along Serbia’s green and blue borders to prevent irregular migration and combat organised crime. The action combines infrastructure upgrades, procurement of advanced surveillance equipment, and specialised training. planEntities.name: Powering Eswatini’s Delivery Engine: The Citizen‑Centred UniPod Total
planEntities.parentName: Enhanced enabling environment and systems that facilitate economic growth and create equitable access to decent jobs, sustainable livelihoods, and foster entrepreneurship, particularly for youth and vulnerable populations
planEntities.description:
The overarching objective of the UniPod project is to establish a vibrant and sustainable innovation hub at the university, designed to accelerate youth and graduate-led entrepreneurship. The project seeks to bridge the gap between academic knowledge and market application by providing innovators with access to technology, mentorship, and business development support. The project addresses structural barriers to innovation by creating a "one-stop shop" where young entrepreneurs can develop, prototype, and scale their ideas. It aims to foster a culture of innovation within the university, strengthen the national innovation ecosystem, and create meaningful employment opportunities for youth.
Expected results include:
•	An operational UniPod facility with digital fabrication tools and co-working spaces.
•	A robust pipeline of youth-led innovations and startups in strategic sectors.
•	Strengthened capacity of innovators in business management, intellectual property (IP) protection, and market readiness.
•	Formalized partnerships between the university, the private sector, and government agencies to support the innovation ecosystem.
•	An effective IP management framework, developed in collaboration with the host university and national IP authorities, to ensure innovators can protect and commercialize their creations.

planEntities.name: UNESCO_“Africa-Europe Partnerships for Culture: Promoting Culture and Heritage-based Sustainable Tourism in Southern Africa
planEntities.parentName: Enhanced enabling environment and systems that facilitate economic growth and create equitable access to decent jobs, sustainable livelihoods, and foster entrepreneurship, particularly for youth and vulnerable populations
planEntities.description:
The project “Africa-Europe Partnerships for Culture: Promoting Culture and Heritage-based Sustainable Tourism in Southern Africa”, a European Union project implemented by UNESCO, will contribute to strengthening the contribution of culture and heritage to sustainable development, notably through enhancing culture and heritage-based tourism development, diversifying tourism products and delivering high-quality visitor experiences at selected UNESCO-designated sites and cities. These activities aim to contribute to improving livelihoods of the communities in the region, including youth, women and indigenous peoples, through capacity building and the creation of opportunities for income-generation and jobs.

Through innovative partnerships, the project will invest in the development of engaging storytelling, the production of meaningful digital content and authentic, relevant products incorporating new narratives. It will enhance cultural production capacities to develop community-based programming and tourism offers at the participating UNESCO-designated sites and cities. At the same time, the project presents a unique occasion to promote international cooperation and peer-to-peer learning opportunities among the six target Southern African countries, namely Botswana, Eswatini, Lesotho, Namibia, South Africa and Zimbabwe, as well as with European Union countries, to foster regional integration and social cohesion.

planEntities.name: Return and Rebuild: Advancing Voluntary Returns and Sustainable Reintegration for Syrians
planEntities.parentName: Output 3.1: Supporting the capacities of government institutions and of returnees and affected communities, in particular vulnerable groups to ensure the provision of and access to legal and administrative services aimed at facilitating the reintegration of returnees.
planEntities.description: The intervention focuses on four areas: The of intervention that enable forcibly displaced persons to overcome their specific vulnerabilities and host communities to pursue their own development efforts in transformed environments. These are: education and learning; employment; protection; and critical infrastructure. This country project entitled "Return and Rebuild: Advancing Voluntary Returns and Sustainable Reintegration for Syrians" aims to support durable solutions for Syrian refugees and Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs). These objectives will be achieved through supporting an enabling environment for return and reintegration in Syria.

planEntities.name: EU Support for Safe Returns and a Stable Future for Syrian Returnees.
planEntities.parentName: Output 3.4: Enhancing the safety and dignity of voluntary returns through technical advice on policies and legislation ,and facilitating procedures and measures for their implementation.
planEntities.description: With financial support from the European Union, this programme supports the safe, voluntary, dignified, and sustainable reintegration of returning Syrian refugees, while strengthening national capacities to manage return and recovery and to support access to decent work. The programme is implemented jointly the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) the International Organization for Migration (IOM) and ILO, in cooperation with national authorities, linking humanitarian assistance with early recovery and employment support. In Syria, the programme helps address legal and administrative barriers that affect returnees’ access to civil documentation, services, and employment. It provides reintegration support for returning families, including financial assistance and housing and shelter support for the most vulnerable, enabling returnees to meet immediate needs and start rebuilding their lives. The programme promotes livelihoods through skills development, developing public work schemes, job matching, and support to local employment initiatives aligned with local economic priorities, contributing to community stabilisation and social cohesion. It also strengthens coordination and information systems that support return and reintegration, including cooperation with neighbouring countries where relevant.

planEntities.description:
IOM Syria’s health programming will focus on strengthening national and local health systems through targeted support in three key areas: health system strengthening, border health, and technical assistance through the temporary return of qualified Syrian health professionals. IOM will:
In coordination with the Ministry of Health and other relevant authorities, support procurements, training and institutional development to enhance disease surveillance, emergency preparedness, and health service delivery in underserved and high risk areas;
Improve border health capacities by supporting health screening, referral mechanisms, and coordination at key points of entry to help prevent cross-border disease transmission. This will be complemented by community event surveillance at borders; and
Facilitate the temporary return of skilled Syrian health professionals from the diaspora, enabling them to contribute to the recovery of essential health services through technical placements, knowledge transfer, and mentoring of local staff.

planEntities.name: Transitional Justice programming including Housing, Land and Property (HLP) rights
planEntities.parentName: T-Pillar5 Output
planEntities.description:
IOM plays a global role in supporting post-conflict societies and governments in designing and implementing comprehensive Transitional Justice (TJ) frameworks, focusing on safeguarding Housing Land and Property (HLP) rights and ensuring victims' access to reparations. Based on IOM’s work to safeguard the HLP rights of Syrian households since 2021, the proposed interventions will integrate multidisciplinary solutions to address HLP restitution, compensation, psychosocial rehabilitation, and other reparative mechanisms tailored to local needs. IOM will:
Conduct baseline assessments, engaging communities, developing tailored frameworks, documenting and safeguarding HLP claims securely;
Design efficient claim processing systems; and
Build the capacity of local actors, including the provision of policy guidance, expert advice, and technical assistance for civil, mental health and psychosocial support assistance, legal assistance, and HLP rights, and to implement reparations and manage grievances effectively guided by psychosocial considerations.
