planEntities.name: UNICEF Output 2.1: Education systems and institutional capacity strengthened for improved evidence and risk-informed legislation, policies, partnerships and stakeholder support networks
planEntities.parentName: Output 4.1: Enhancing the technical and institutional capacities to plan and design responsive, evidence-based, quality, and inclusive services that improve participation and resilience of people and sustain peace.
planEntities.description: The project strengthens the education system by supporting a national study on out‑of‑school children (OOSC) to inform evidence‑based planning. It contributes to the development of a Strategic Framework for Alternative Education Pathways and supports the Ministry of Education in establishing national SOPs for the Safe Schools Initiative. The project further enhances policy and planning capacities through technical assistance in rolling out M&E systems and supports the development and endorsement of the national Teacher Professional Development (TPD) framework and guidelines.

planEntities.name: UNICEF Output 2.2: Children’s learning outcomes are improved in more effective, safe, and inclusive  learning environments
planEntities.parentName: Output 1.1. Enhancing access to quality formal and non-formal education services, including rehabilitation, equipment to ensure facilities are functional, safe roads to schools and building skills of adolescents and youth
planEntities.description: The project strengthens quality, inclusive learning by supporting the development and dissemination of Teaching at the Right Level (TaRL) content for foundational literacy and numeracy, including assessment tools and SOPs. It builds the capacities of teachers and education personnel to enhance instructional quality and promote children’s wellbeing. The project also supports the rollout of the Safe Schools Initiative in formal and non‑formal settings, provides technical assistance for intersectoral Inclusive Education guidelines and upgraded learning materials, and contributes to operationalizing the ECD strategy through a roadmap for free, compulsory pre‑primary education and provision of ECE supplies. Additionally, it supports revising and rolling out learning packages such as the Better Learning Programme, the teacher–student wellbeing package, and the Social Emotional Learning curriculum.

planEntities.name: UNICEF Output 2.3: Out-of-school children,  and children affected by emergencies  participate in an increased number of learning platforms for education and life skills development.
planEntities.parentName: Output 1.1. Enhancing access to quality formal and non-formal education services, including rehabilitation, equipment to ensure facilities are functional, safe roads to schools and building skills of adolescents and youth
planEntities.description: he project expands inclusive learning opportunities for vulnerable and out‑of‑school children by providing technical support to partners to deliver digital learning through electronic platforms for learners with limited access to education. It rehabilitates classrooms and supplies schools to ensure safe, inclusive, child‑friendly environments. The project implements inclusive non‑formal education, digital learning, school readiness, and skills‑building programmes, including support to ILCs. It also delivers the national Back to Learning campaign, community‑based activities for OOSC in formal education, and compensation programmes for learning loss. Additional support includes provision of national textbooks, emergency preparedness and response to maintain safe learning access, and assistance to national exam processes.

planEntities.name: UNICEF Output 3.1: Legislative, policy and administrative frameworks, accountability and national institutional  capacity are strengthened to prevent and respond to violence, abuse, neglect and exploitation of children.
planEntities.parentName: Output 4.1: Enhancing the technical and institutional capacities to plan and design responsive, evidence-based, quality, and inclusive services that improve participation and resilience of people and sustain peace.
planEntities.description: The project strengthens national child protection systems by supporting the Government to align legislation, policies, and plans with international standards. It enhances the capacity of national institutions to assess and analyse the situation of the most vulnerable children to inform evidence‑based programming and responses. The project reinforces the social service workforce through standard setting, quality assurance, and technical guidance. It advances the children and armed conflict agenda by supporting the development and implementation of action plans to protect children. Additionally, the project provides technical assistance on alternative care, protection of children in street situations, birth registration, and access to justice, contributing to a more inclusive, accountable, and rights‑based child protection system.

planEntities.name: UNICEF Output 3.2: Girls, boys, and women at risk of violence and exploitation will have equitable access to quality integrated child protection and GBV [gender-based violence] prevention and response services
planEntities.parentName: Output 4.3: Integrating right-based, inclusive, gender equality, protection and social cohesion for community resilience and well-being of vulnerable groups
planEntities.description: The project strengthens child protection systems by establishing specialized responses for vulnerable children, including reintegration support for children affected by conflict and provision of case management and referral services. It builds the capacities of governmental and non‑governmental partners on core child protection areas, including the Child Protection Minimum Standards, case management, MHPSS, EORE, Parenting, PSEA, GBV risk mitigation, and community‑based reintegration. Through strengthened workforce skills and coordinated, survivor‑centred services, the project enhances national ability to prevent and respond to violence, exploitation, abuse, and neglect, ensuring that at‑risk children are identified, supported, and safely reintegrated into their communities.

planEntities.name: UNICEF Output 3.3: Children, parents and communities have increased knowledge, motivation and capacity to promote and apply practices to protect themselves and reduce violence
planEntities.parentName: Output 4.3: Integrating right-based, inclusive, gender equality, protection and social cohesion for community resilience and well-being of vulnerable groups
planEntities.description: The project strengthens child protection and wellbeing by developing and delivering specialized MHPSS programmes for children and caregivers, including tailored interventions for those at heightened risk. It promotes gender‑sensitive GBV prevention and empowerment activities and supports risk‑education awareness through the development of training manuals and structured sessions. The project raises community awareness on key child protection concerns such as child marriage and child labour, and enhances positive caregiving through evidence‑based parenting programmes. To safeguard the frontline workforce, the project implements a wellbeing programme for humanitarian workers, enabling them to provide safe, ethical, and effective services.

planEntities.name: UNICEF Output 3.4: Girls, boys and women affected by humanitarian crisis, are protected from all forms of violence and receive quality child protection and GBV services
planEntities.parentName: Output 4.1: Enhancing the technical and institutional capacities to plan and design responsive, evidence-based, quality, and inclusive services that improve participation and resilience of people and sustain peace.
planEntities.description: The project strengthens national and sub‑national child protection systems by enhancing coordination structures, building capacities of governorate‑level actors, and improving information management to ensure timely, evidence‑based decision‑making. It supports national authorities, including MoSAL, in monitoring the situation of vulnerable children and assessing the impact of the crisis to inform responsive programming. Technical assistance is provided to government and partners to strengthen policies, planning, and institutional mechanisms for child protection. By improving coordination, data systems, and institutional capacities, the project contributes to more effective and accountable services that prevent and respond to violence, exploitation, and neglect of children.

planEntities.name: UNICEF Output 4.1:  Mechanisms and systems are strengthened to plan, budget, coordinate and implement gender-responsive, equitable, inclusive, resilient and safely managed WASH services
planEntities.parentName: Output 1.3: Increasing access to improved water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) systems and services
planEntities.description: The project strengthens WASH systems by updating the national WASH infrastructure assessment and expanding its scope to include the sanitation sub‑sector. This includes providing IT equipment, software, data systems, and specialized consulting services to ensure accurate data collection and analysis. The project also supports the development of simplified Standard Operating Procedures and an e‑learning platform to enhance the capacities of WASH technicians and operators, promoting more efficient, reliable, and sustainable WASH service delivery.

planEntities.name: UNICEF Output 4.2:  Water and sanitation systems that are gender-responsive and resilient are restored, giving improved, inclusive
planEntities.parentName: Output 1.3: Increasing access to improved water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) systems and services
planEntities.description: The project improves access to safe and sustainable WASH services by supporting the rehabilitation of existing water‑supply infrastructure and, where applicable, providing solar power systems to ensure uninterrupted operation. It extends support to the rehabilitation and operation and maintenance of sanitation infrastructure to enhance service reliability. The project also strengthens water‑quality management through the provision of disinfectants, testing reagents, and laboratory equipment. Additionally, it rehabilitates WASH facilities in institutions and promotes hygiene awareness, complemented by the provision of essential WASH supplies to create safe, healthy environments.

planEntities.name: UNICEF Output 4.3:  Water and sanitation operators have strengthened capacity for sustainable, shock-resilient, climate-resilient water and sanitation systems.
planEntities.parentName: Output 4.1: Enhancing the technical and institutional capacities to plan and design responsive, evidence-based, quality, and inclusive services that improve participation and resilience of people and sustain peace.
planEntities.description: The project strengthens climate‑resilient WASH systems by developing national WASH climate‑risk indicators and a climate rationale to improve risk‑informed planning and service delivery. It enhances emergency preparedness by supporting WASH Sector coordination, improving partner capacities, and providing technical guidance to ensure timely, harmonized responses during crises. Through capacity‑building, data improvement, and sector‑wide collaboration, the project enables national and sub‑national actors to anticipate, respond to, and manage climate‑related WASH risks while advancing sustainable, reliable WASH services for vulnerable communities.

planEntities.name: UNICEF Output 4.4:  Children and families in humanitarian situations have equitable access to basic inclusive water, sanitation and hygiene services and supplies
planEntities.parentName: Output 1.3: Increasing access to improved water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) systems and services
planEntities.description: The project provides life‑saving WASH support during emergencies by ensuring access to safe water and sanitation services for affected populations in camps, health facilities, IDP centres, collective shelters, and host communities. It supplies emergency WASH NFIs and essential materials needed to restore basic hygiene and sanitation conditions. The project also implements hygiene‑awareness interventions to promote safe practices, improved water management, and positive behaviour change, in close coordination with SBC efforts to strengthen community resilience and reduce public‑health risks.

planEntities.name: UNICEF Output 5.1: Young People-focused, evidence-based policies and strategies are in place to support Young People development
planEntities.parentName: Output 4.1: Enhancing the technical and institutional capacities to plan and design responsive, evidence-based, quality, and inclusive services that improve participation and resilience of people and sustain peace.
planEntities.description: The project strengthens the learning‑to‑earning transition for young people by supporting Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) schools under the Ministry of Education, Ministry of Higher Education, and Ministry of Social Affairs and Labour. It enhances the capacities of ADAP partners and youth volunteers to improve the quality and relevance of services delivered to adolescents and young people. The project also advances evidence generation by supporting documentation, analysis, and knowledge sharing on youth needs, skills pathways, and outcomes. Through stronger institutional capacity, improved TVET delivery, and youth‑centered data systems, the project promotes more inclusive, market‑relevant, and sustainable opportunities for young people.

planEntities.name: UNICEF Output 5.2: Young People have access to age and gender-sensitive learning and skills-building opportunities for improved learning, capacities and employability
planEntities.parentName: Output 1.1. Enhancing access to quality formal and non-formal education services, including rehabilitation, equipment to ensure facilities are functional, safe roads to schools and building skills of adolescents and youth
planEntities.description:
Provide access to services and skills-building for young people for enhanced employability (Basic, Advanced and Functional Literacy and Numeracy, Life Skills and Citizenship Education, Entrepreneurship Training, and Technical Vocational Education and Training/TVET).
Support the integrated platforms and learning centres, and youth centers.

planEntities.name: UNICEF Output 5.3: young people are increasingly aware of their rights to participate and have meaningful engagement and systematized participation
planEntities.parentName: Output 4.3: Integrating right-based, inclusive, gender equality, protection and social cohesion for community resilience and well-being of vulnerable groups
planEntities.description: The project strengthens young people’s social, civic, and digital engagement by fostering volunteerism, community participation, and social cohesion initiatives, including youth‑led climate‑action activities and meaningful involvement in advocacy, data collection, and evidence generation. It also promotes sport for development and peacebuilding by supporting school‑ and community‑based sports programmes that build teamwork, resilience, and positive social norms while creating safe, inclusive spaces for youth engagement.

planEntities.name: UNICEF Output 5.4: Young people are protected, supported and mobilized in humanitarian setting and participate in resilience-building programmes
planEntities.parentName: Output 4.3: Integrating right-based, inclusive, gender equality, protection and social cohesion for community resilience and well-being of vulnerable groups
planEntities.description: Building the capacity of young people to cope with emergencies, and mobilizing them to prepare, implement and monitor emergency response plans.

planEntities.name: UNICEF Output 6.1:  National and subnational capacities for monitoring child poverty and for designing and implementing integrated and child-sensitive social protection programmes and public finance management are strengthened.
planEntities.parentName: Output 4.1: Enhancing the technical and institutional capacities to plan and design responsive, evidence-based, quality, and inclusive services that improve participation and resilience of people and sustain peace.
planEntities.description: The project strengthens national social protection systems by providing technical support to government counterparts on multidimensional poverty measurement, evidence‑based policymaking, and the development of effective, inclusive strategies. It builds institutional and technical capacity across ministries and social workers to promote disability‑inclusive social protection, including support to develop the National Disability Strategy and the Terms of Reference for the National Steering Committee on Disability Inclusion. The project enhances data and evidence generation through comprehensive assessments on poverty, disability, MIS systems, and public financing for children. It also strengthens public financial management and resource mobilization for social sectors, and conducts post‑distribution monitoring (PDM) to assess the impact of humanitarian social protection interventions

planEntities.name: Output 6.3: Humanitarian social protection interventions have reduced socio-economic vulnerability of children and their families
planEntities.parentName: Output 2.2: Supporting social protection systems to ensure vulnerable populations have access to social assistance, services, and insurance
planEntities.description: The project supports vulnerable households through a Cash Transfer Programme for Basic Needs, helping families secure essential goods and services. It also provides referral and case‑management support through NGO partners to ensure households are linked to appropriate health, protection, and social services, strengthening their wellbeing, resilience, and access to assistance.

Syrian Arab Republic.name: United Nations Office for Project Services
Syrian Arab Republic.organizationType: Multilateral - UN organizations excluding pooled funds

planEntities.name: Supporting Children's hospitals in northern Syria with specialized medical equipment for intensive care, cardiac care and surgeries
planEntities.parentName: Output 1.2. Enhancing access to quality formal and community-based health and nutrition services, including establishment, rehabilitation, equipment to ensure facilities are functional and service provision
planEntities.description: The project aims at strengthening the resilience of the Syrian healthcare system by enhancing access to health services for children and improving child health outcomes. This will be achieved through the provision of urgent medical equipment and supplies to specialized pediatric hospitals and the department of pediatrics in general hospitals in Aleppo and Hama Governorates.

planEntities.name: The Nexus Response Mechanism (NRM) in Syria
planEntities.parentName: Output 1.3: Increasing access to improved water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) systems and services
planEntities.description: The Nexus Response Mechanism (NRM) aims to strengthen the humanitarian-development-peace nexus in Syria by addressing immediate needs while building long-term resilience among conflict-affected populations, including displaced persons, host communities, and returnees. The NRM focuses on reducing vulnerabilities through capacity development, preparedness for future shocks, and promoting human rights-based approaches. By linking relief efforts with early recovery and sustainable development, the NRM facilitates transitions from emergency assistance to durable solutions, particularly in protracted displacement settings and areas affected by inter-communal violence. Special emphasis is placed on empowering women and the most vulnerable while ensuring interventions align with due diligence criteria to foster security, stability, and resilience in conflict-affected regions.

planEntities.name: Strengthening Disaster Management and Emergency Response Capacity in Syria
planEntities.parentName: Output 4.1: Enhancing the technical and institutional capacities to plan and design responsive, evidence-based, quality, and inclusive services that improve participation and resilience of people and sustain peace.
planEntities.description: This project strengthens Syria’s disaster resilience by enhancing DRR and response capacities. Aligned with the Sendai Framework, it equips the MoEDM with environmental monitoring and a multi-hazard early warning system, while building sustainable capacity to improve hazard identification, coordination, and protection of vulnerable populations.

Syrian Arab Republic.name: The United Nations Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees in the Near East
Syrian Arab Republic.organizationType: Multilateral - UN organizations excluding pooled funds

planEntities.name: Crisis-affected Palestine refugees are provided with employment opportunities and Livelihoods support
planEntities.parentName: Output 2.1: Enhancing access to sustainable incomes and decent employment opportunities
planEntities.description: UNRWA supports Palestine refugees through Cash-for-Work (CfW) opportunities and livelihoods interventions. A total of 800 beneficiaries are provided with short-term CfW placements. In addition, 3,000 vulnerable small business owners receive conditional cash grants of up to US$ 5,000, complemented by mentoring, coaching and skills training, while 1,000 entrepreneurs, particularly women and female-led businesses, receive tailored business development support. Beneficiaries are selected based on vulnerability criteria and enterprise feasibility assessments.

planEntities.name: Palestine refugees are able to meet their essential needs and cope with sudden crises in dignity MPCA
planEntities.parentName: Output 2.2: Supporting social protection systems to ensure vulnerable populations have access to social assistance, services, and insurance
planEntities.description:
Vulnerable Palestine refugees are provided with multi- purpose cash assistance:
UNRWA aims to maintain MPCA as a core pillar of its 2026 humanitarian response in Syria. The Agency will extend MPCA support to 7,000 Palestinian refugee households (24,500 individuals), primarily those residing in Yarmouk, Ein el-Tal, and Dera’a camps, identified as most vulnerable through needs-based targeting.

- Shock-affected Palestine refugees are provided with emergency multi-purpose cash assistance (EMPCA):
To support households affected by new humanitarian shocks including armed conflict, climate-related events and situations of unrest, the Agency will provide EMPCA to 3,000 affected households (10,500 individuals). Each family will receive US$ 150 per month for three months to stabilize household economies following a crisis and help them meet essential needs.
- Palestine refugee returnee households are provided with a reintegration grant:
In 2026, UNRWA will also support dignified, sustainable and voluntary return through targeted support for Palestine refugees. A total of 6,500 cross-border returnee and internally displaced households (22,750 individuals), moving to their areas of origin or return will receive a one-off payment of US$ 600, intended to cover basic return and reintegration needs for an initial four-month period, equivalent to four months of the EMPCA transfer (US$ 150), in line with the Cash Working Group (CWG) guidance and harmonized with similar UNHCR support for Syrian returnees.

planEntities.name: Contribute to a protective environment for  Palestine refugees by maintaining access to basic service
planEntities.parentName: Output 1.2. Enhancing access to quality formal and community-based health and nutrition services, including establishment, rehabilitation, equipment to ensure facilities are functional and service provision
planEntities.description:
, UNRWA health facilities are expected to handle at least 900,000 health consultation supported by HA funding. 
Drawing on lessons from 2025, when subsidised hospitalization targets could not be met due to funding constraints, the Agency will reinstate partial coverage for hospitalization costs, ranging between 75 to 95 per cent depending on the specific treatment and circumstances. This will enable 5,000 subsidised hospitalizations and referrals to secondary and tertiary care at partner and public hospitals, with full coverage for eligible new arrivals.
Approximately 20,000 Palestine refugees, including both cross-border and internally displaced returnees, including around 200 persons with disabilities, will receive MHPSS services. Areas that have long been hard to reach will also be prioritized in light of improved humanitarian access with one mobile health team in Duma, expected to provide 4,000 primary health care consultations to communities heavily affected by conflict and displacement.
UNRWA will rehabilitate a total of five conflict-damaged health premises across its areas of operation in 2026, including Health Centers in Lattakia, Muzaireeb (Dera’a), Homs, Khan El-Shieh and Sbieneh (in Rural Damascus). In addition, UNRWA will repair and maintain all 23 health facilities.

planEntities.name: UNRWA students are  provided with quality,  inclusive and equitable  education
planEntities.parentName: Output 1.1. Enhancing access to quality formal and non-formal education services, including rehabilitation, equipment to ensure facilities are functional, safe roads to schools and building skills of adolescents and youth
planEntities.description:
UNRWA will continue to deliver quality, inclusive and equitable elementary and preparatory education to approximately 52,000 Palestine refugee students enrolled across 100 schools in Syria. To address capacity constraints resulting from conflict damage and population movements, particularly in Yarmouk camp, the Agency will operate around 58 double-shift schools, utilizing both UNRWA facilities and premises provided by the Ministry of Education.
To support learning continuity, around 5,500 students will benefit from catch-up classes, while all students will receive back-to-school kits and participate in at least one recreational or extra-curricular activity during the academic year. In addition, 3,000 students will participate in summer recreational programmes.
UNRWA will also rehabilitate or reconstruct five conflict-damaged schools across its areas of operation in 2026, including in Yarmouk, Khan El-Shieh, Hussienieh, and Dera’a. Furthermore, the Agency will undertake the repair and maintenance of all 36 school premises to ensure safe and functional learning environments.
TVET: UNRWA’s TVET programme will offer long and short-term courses for 1,930 trainees in its vocational training centres (VTCs)

planEntities.name: At-risk Palestine refugees continue to receive protection support
planEntities.parentName: Output 3.1: Supporting the capacities of government institutions and of returnees and affected communities, in particular vulnerable groups to ensure the provision of and access to legal and administrative services aimed at facilitating the reintegration of returnees.
planEntities.description:
UNRWA will prioritize addressing protection risks that threaten returns processes, both for cross-border 
returnees and internally displaced persons on the move, to heavily conflict-affected areas of return with limited 
services, infrastructure and ERW threats. The Agency will extend EORE to 51,350 individuals focusing on areas of 
heightened ERW risk and deliver PSS services to 11,360 Palestine refugees to mitigate the impact of trauma associated 
with years of conflict, socioeconomic hardship and repeated displacement.
Legal aid will be provided to some 4,000 Palestine refugees to secure relevant civil documentation to facilitate access 
to critical health and education services, housing, land and property rights, as well as support for securing protective 
legal rights for gender-based violence (GBV) survivors, as referred by a UNRWA social worker via case management. 
Where relevant, referrals to external partners will be facilitated, through lawyers and UNRWA social workers.
Social workers will handle high-risk protection cases through case management, with emergency cash for protection 
provided to 600 persons faced with immediate consequences of a protection incident or threat involving violence, 
coercion, depravation and/or abuse. Moreover, 2,000 assistive devices will be distributed to persons with a disability 
or mobility needs. To strengthen community-based protection, UNRWA will expand Area Protection Committees and 
engage volunteers in awareness-raising activities.

planEntities.name: Crisis-affected Palestine  refugees have access to safe  and dignified shelter and  associated NFIs
planEntities.parentName: Output 1.4: Increasing access to civil infrastructure and housing for increased resilience and security
planEntities.description:
The Agency will facilitate shelter repairs through the self-help approach primarily in Dera’a, Ein el-Tal, and Yarmouk camps.

UNRWA will also maintain contingency NFIs to support crisis-affected families in the event of sudden-onset emergencies. These will include essential items such as blankets, hygiene kits, jerry cans, kitchen sets, and mattresses.

planEntities.name: UNRWA installations repaired, rehabilitated or maintained for continued service provision
planEntities.parentName: Output 1.4: Increasing access to civil infrastructure and housing for increased resilience and security
planEntities.description: UNRWA will rehabilitate, reconstruct and maintain installations across Syria, including schools, health centres, community centres, distribution centres and area offices, to ensure continued access to essential services. Interventions prioritize conflict-affected areas and locations with high returnee populations, particularly in Yarmouk, Ein el-Tal, Dera’a and Khan El-Shieh.

planEntities.name: UNRWA ensures security  compliance for its personnel,  partners, programmes and  assets
planEntities.parentName: Output 4.1: Enhancing the technical and institutional capacities to plan and design responsive, evidence-based, quality, and inclusive services that improve participation and resilience of people and sustain peace.
planEntities.description: UNRWA strengthens operational safety and security by facilitating emergency humanitarian field operations, conducting compliance assessments of installations, and training personnel on security and risk management.

planEntities.name: Improved access to bread through bread subsidy project
planEntities.parentName: Output 2.2: Supporting social protection systems to ensure vulnerable populations have access to social assistance, services, and insurance
planEntities.description: Bread is a central component of the Syrian diet, accounting for around one third of daily caloric intake, yet worsening food insecurity affecting over 9 million people and shortfalls in national wheat production have made affordable bread increasingly difficult to access, with recent subsidy reductions driving sharp price increases and deepening hardship among vulnerable families. In response, WFP, in partnership with the Government of Syria through the Ministry of Economy and Industry, launched the Subsidized Bread Programme in 2025 to stabilize access, reduce household economic pressure, and support national food security by supplying WFP provided wheat flour to selected bakeries, enabling 2 million people in the most food insecure areas to purchase fortified bread at a fixed subsidized price that covers only operational costs while safeguarding access to a daily staple.

planEntities.name: National Annual Food Security Assessment
planEntities.parentName: Output 4.1: Enhancing the technical and institutional capacities to plan and design responsive, evidence-based, quality, and inclusive services that improve participation and resilience of people and sustain peace.
planEntities.description: Food Security Assessment aimed at analyzing the food security situation, identifying vulnerabilities, and understanding the needs of affected populations. This process supports evidence-based decision-making, and provides technical assistance to field teams to maintain the quality and reliability of findings.

planEntities.name: Support diversified and sustainable livelihoods and food systems at household, community and national level.
planEntities.parentName: Output 2.3: Supporting the protection and restoration of natural resources, productive infrastructure, and assets for sustainable food production
planEntities.description: The project focuses on rehabilitating and improving irrigation systems and communal agricultural assets to enable smallholder farmers to resume cultivation, increase productivity, and revive local markets. In parallel, it restores and strengthens the bread value chain as a strategic pillar for sustainable, nutrition-sensitive access to food. By improving the availability and quality of bread, the project supports job creation and local economic recovery. Interventions span the full value chain, from direct support to farmers to the rehabilitation of silos, mills, and bakeries, alongside technical assistance and capacity strengthening to advance a national wheat flour fortification policy.

planEntities.name: Mobile food security monitoring (mVAM)
planEntities.parentName: Output 4.1: Enhancing the technical and institutional capacities to plan and design responsive, evidence-based, quality, and inclusive services that improve participation and resilience of people and sustain peace.
planEntities.description: Remote Mobile Food Security Assessment to monitor and analyze food security conditions, identify vulnerabilities, and assess priority needs. It informs evidence-based decision-making, provides near real time monthly updates, and complements annual assessments.

planEntities.name: Drought response
planEntities.parentName: Output 2.3: Supporting the protection and restoration of natural resources, productive infrastructure, and assets for sustainable food production
planEntities.description: Severe drought conditions during the 2024 to 2025 season, confirmed through vegetation monitoring, significantly affected farming households across multiple governorates. The drought response targeted smallholder farmers and rural communities whose livelihoods were directly disrupted by crop failure and reduced agricultural productivity. Support was delivered through a combination of cash and in-kind assistance, calibrated to the level of impact across locations and aligned to ensure continuity of support throughout the critical period. This approach allowed WFP to respond quickly, bridge immediate consumption gaps, and help stabilize vulnerable households facing prolonged climate-related shocks.

planEntities.name: Agro-inputs support to crisis-affected smallholder famers
planEntities.parentName: Output 2.3: Supporting the protection and restoration of natural resources, productive infrastructure, and assets for sustainable food production
planEntities.description: Under WFP’s project to support wheat farmers in Swida governorate, implemented with the Ministry of Agriculture and in partnership with SARC, assistance is being provided to farmers affected by drought and recent violence to restore production and safeguard rural livelihoods. The project targets 10,504 farmers across 94 villages, covering more than 270,000 dunams of rainfed and irrigated land, with WFP covering 50 percent of their wheat seed and fertilizer needs based on land size. Inputs are delivered in phases aligned with the agricultural calendar, with seeds and superphosphate provided ahead of planting and urea supplied during the crop growth stage, ensuring timely support that strengthens productivity and local food availability.

planEntities.name: Nutrition-sensitive social protection cash-based transfers T-ANMU
planEntities.parentName: Output 2.2: Supporting social protection systems to ensure vulnerable populations have access to social assistance, services, and insurance
planEntities.description: WFP, in partnership with the Ministry of Social Affairs and Labour, co-designed Syria’s first transitional cash-based social protection programme, Transitional Anmu, targeting 2,200 households. The initiative lays the foundation for a nationally led system that bridges humanitarian assistance and longer term social protection. The project also includes dedicated capacity strengthening support to promote government ownership and ensure the long term sustainability of the programme.

planEntities.name: Unconditional resource transfer to food-insecure households
planEntities.parentName: Output 1.2. Enhancing access to quality formal and community-based health and nutrition services, including establishment, rehabilitation, equipment to ensure facilities are functional and service provision
planEntities.description: This activity ensures that crisis-affected and food-insecure populations, including host communities, internally displaced persons and returnees across all governorates in the Syrian Arab Republic, are able to meet their basic food and nutrition needs throughout the year. Households identified as in need based on WFP vulnerability and targeting criteria are eligible for general food assistance. In response to sudden onset emergencies, including new displacement, eligibility is assessed case by case. Where affected populations lack access to cooking facilities or require immediate support, WFP provides ready to eat or pre prepared rations to cover urgent food needs.

planEntities.name: Provide nutrition assistance to prevent chronic and acute malnutrition
planEntities.parentName: Output 1.2. Enhancing access to quality formal and community-based health and nutrition services, including establishment, rehabilitation, equipment to ensure facilities are functional and service provision
planEntities.description: Under this activity, WFP implements a supplementary feeding programme to prevent malnutrition among children aged 6 to 23 months from eligible households receiving general food assistance, through the distribution of medium quantity lipid based nutrient supplements. In collaboration with UNICEF, the programme integrates counselling on infant and young child feeding and promotes improved complementary feeding practices, including guidance on dietary diversity and age appropriate food quantities. In targeted locations, pregnant and lactating women and girls who are enrolled in general food assistance also receive cash based transfers to support improved dietary diversity and nutrition outcomes.

planEntities.name: Provide nutrition assistance to treat moderate acute malnutrition.
planEntities.parentName: Output 1.2. Enhancing access to quality formal and community-based health and nutrition services, including establishment, rehabilitation, equipment to ensure facilities are functional and service provision
planEntities.description: Underthis activity, WFP implements a community based management of acute malnutrition programme in partnership with UNICEF and the World Health Organization, in close coordination with the Ministry of Health. The programme provides specialized ready to use supplementary food, including large quantity lipid based nutrient supplements, for the treatment of children and pregnant and lactating women and girls with moderate acute malnutrition. It also includes community outreach and awareness activities that promote early detection, appropriate care practices, and shared parental responsibility for the health and well being of children.

planEntities.name: Provide humanitarian air services to humanitarian partners
planEntities.parentName: Output 3.2: Enhancing access to enable the provision of basic and protection services and reintegration support to returnees and receiving communites.
planEntities.description: The United Nations Humanitarian Air Service enables the inter agency humanitarian response by providing passenger and light cargo air transport services to partners across sectors. It enhances access to beneficiaries and project areas, supports the movement of essential humanitarian cargo, and maintains medical and emergency evacuation capacity to ensure continuity of operations in hard to reach locations.

planEntities.name: Ensure surveillance capabilities for rapid detection, investigation, identification, and response to disease outbreaks.

planEntities.description:
WHO will be supporting the implementation of effective national integrated disease surveillance (IDS) systems by the end of 2025. The project for strengthening surveillance system in Syria.
WHO supports different surveillance visits including collecting samples and samples transportation, provision of lab equipment's and reagents.

planEntities.name: Technical support to MoH for integrated health and nutrition service delivery, including workforce development, mental health, clinical guidance, essential supplies, and system strengthening.

planEntities.description: Technical support to MoH for integrated health and nutrition service delivery, including health system strengthening.workforce development, mental health, clinical guidance, and essential supplies.

planEntities.name: Rehabilitate and provide equipment to health and nutrition facilities for better inclusive access to health and nutrition services
planEntities.parentName: Output 1.2. Enhancing access to quality formal and community-based health and nutrition services, including establishment, rehabilitation, equipment to ensure facilities are functional and service provision
planEntities.description:
WHO in close coordination with MoH, will support the rehabilitation and equipping of public Health facilities across Syria including: 
Laboratories: Rehabilitation of public health labs in Daraa ($230,000) and Damascus ($300,000).
Malnutrition Treatment Centers: WHO will rehabilitate three Severe Acute Malnutrition Treatment Centers with complications in hospitals located in Daraa, Idleb, and Deir Ez Zor, at a total cost of $75,000. in addition to continue to Support equipment of 1043 HC with scales, stadiometers, (2000 scales and 1000 stadiometers /3 years) printings, data collection and analysis.  
-Continue to Support equipment and supplies of 25 stabilization centers (therapeutic formula, beds, refrigerators, tables …etc.). and reinhabitation of 3 SC's 
-create breastfeeding corners in 23 SC’s 
Specialized Departments in Hospitals: WHO planned to rehabilitate the Burn Unit in Latakia National Hospital and the ICU unit in Hama National Hospital ($ 1,000,000).
In Homs governorate, efforts are focused on rehabilitating the psychiatric ward. The project is budgeted at $105,000
PHC centers: 
Three PHC centers are currently under rehabilitation and will be delivered in 2026:
Albwaida Alshrqiya in Homs ($129,595), AlFtira in Idlib ($152,008), Kafr Sajna ($108,429), in addition to,  Alqatra PHC in Idlib, is planned for rehabilitation in 2026.

planEntities.name: Appuyer la mise en oeuvre de la Budgétisation Sensible au Dividende Démographique (BSDD)
planEntities.parentName: Les capacités d’organisation et de plaidoyers des institutions publiques (nationales et locales), du secteur privé, des OSC, de la Diaspora et des PTF sont renforcées en vue de diversifier et mieux coordonner les partenariats au service du développement durable inclusif
planEntities.description:
L'approche BSDD vise une réallocation efficace des ressources dans les secteurs porteurs du dividende démographique tels que le développement du capital humain (éducation, santé), l'entrepreneuriat et l'emploi, comme stipulé dans la feuille de route de l'Union Africaine de 2017 sur l’exploitation du dividende démographique grâce à des investissements massifs dans la jeunesse. 
L'intégration de l'approche BSDD dans les processus de planification et de programmation budgétaire permet également de créer des conditions favorables à la réalisation des Objectifs de Développement Durable (ODD) à la faveur des allocations budgétaires significatives aux secteurs porteurs, augmentant ainsi la capacité du pays à répondre à la demande sociale croissante : ODD 3 (Bonne santé et bien-être), ODD 4 (Éducation de qualité) et l'ODD 8 (Travail décent et croissance économique), qui ont des effets d'entraînement et de retombées significatifs sur d'autres ODD

planEntities.description: L’activité contribue au renforcement des capacités managériales et entrepreneuriales des acteurs ciblés (groupements et coopératives), ainsi qu’à l’amélioration de leur accès aux marchés, y compris à travers l’éducation financière. Elle comprend le développement de compétences en gestion d’entreprise, gouvernance organisationnelle, analyse des coûts et de la rentabilité, ainsi que l’appui à la compréhension des services financiers, de l’épargne et du crédit. En facilitant l’accès à l’information sur les marchés, la structuration des relations commerciales et la professionnalisation des pratiques, cette activité permet aux acteurs des chaînes de valeur de renforcer leur compétitivité, de sécuriser leurs revenus et de saisir durablement les opportunités économiques locales.

planEntities.description: L’activité vise à appuyer l’acquisition d’intrants agricoles performants ainsi que de matériels et d’équipements modernes de production et de transformation, respectueux de l’environnement, au profit des acteurs ciblés. Elle comprend la facilitation de l’accès à des intrants de qualité, aux technologies adaptées aux besoins des filières, ainsi que la promotion de pratiques de production et de transformation durables et climato‑intelligentes. En améliorant la productivité, la qualité des produits et la valeur ajoutée locale tout en réduisant l’empreinte environnementale, cette activité renforce la compétitivité des acteurs, soutient le développement des chaînes de valeur et favorise une croissance économique locale durable

Elle comprend la réalisation d’infrastructures répondant aux normes techniques, sanitaires et environnementales, adaptées aux besoins des acteurs locaux et aux spécificités de la production, de la transformation et de la commercialisation de la tomate. En renforçant les capacités de production, en réduisant les pertes post récolte et en améliorant la qualité et la conservation des produits, cette activité contribue à accroître la valeur ajoutée locale, la compétitivité des acteurs de la filière tomate et la création d’opportunités économiques durables au profit des communautés

Program objectives are (1) to strengthen national legislation, policies and regional frameworks for the protection of women migrant workers, children and other vulnerable groups in line with international standards; (2) to improve national and regional prevention and protection mechanisms to reduce rights’ violations against migrant women, children, and other vulnerable groups, including victims of trafficking and smuggled migrants; and (3) to increase the access of at-risk groups, women migrant workers and children to information, social and legal services, counselling, and association to prevent abuse, exploitation, harassment, violence, and trafficking in human beings.

planEntities.description:
WE RISE Together aims to facilitate more equal market opportunities for women entrepreneurs by advancing gender-responsive procurement in the Mekong subregion, and Thailand is a core implementation country for this work. In this phase, the project will systematically mainstream gender equality, disability and social inclusion (GEDSI) across implementation to ensure women-owned businesses and gender-responsive enterprises, including disabilities, rural entrepreneurs, ethnic minorities can participate and benefit more equitably from procurement opportunities. Building on collaborations and lessons from Phase 1 (2022–2025), and working through the existing management and coordination structure.

The project will consolidate and expand partnerships with both public and private sector actors to strengthen commitment and adopt the gender responsive procurement concepts into their policy and practices.

planEntities.name: Address marine hypoxic zones by curbing coastal nutrient pollution from tourism, agriculture, and fishing ports and seafood processing in Thailand.

planEntities.description: The project will work at national level and aim to address marine hypoxic zones by curbing coastal nutrient pollution from tourism, agriculture, and fishing ports and seafood processing in Thailand. planEntities.parentName: Capacities for low carbon society, resilience, post-COVID 19 and disaster recovery with capability to adapt and reduce the risks of disasters are enabled and strengthened.
planEntities.description: This sub-output consolidates five former sub-outputs: "Improving national capability to prepare, prevent, detect and respond to public health emergencies (PHE)" (ID 82366); "Regional health security and national risk assessment capacities strengthened" (ID 207683); "Emergency response operations and mass gathering preparedness supported" (ID 207684); "National health security capacities and IHR systems strengthened" (ID 207685); and "Risk communication and community-based emergency preparedness strengthened" (ID 207686). WHO supported the establishment of the Secretariat for the ASEAN Centre for Public Health Emergencies and Emerging Diseases (ACPHEED) and strengthened national surveillance by integrating the Quick and Immediate Risk Assessment (QIRA) tool into the Standard Operating Procedures of National Situation Awareness Teams. Emergency response capacity was bolstered through procurement of essential supplies for the cholera response to spillover cases from Myanmar, the provision of shelter and psychosocial support materials for the border conflict response, and support to the Ministry of Public Health for mass gathering preparedness during the SEA Games. National preparedness was further enhanced through implementation of the Hospital Safety Index across Ministry of Public Health hospitals, strengthened provincial Emergency Operations Center capacities, upgraded Event-Based and genomic Surveillance for respiratory pathogens in high-tourism locations, and establishment of the National IHR Authority. Risk communication was advanced by piloting the Information Environment Assessment to address infodemics and by strengthening linkages between the Public Health Emergency Operations Center's risk communication channels and Village and Migrant Health Volunteer networks.

planEntities.description: This sub-output consolidates two former sub-outputs: "Advance digital health and innovation for equitable service delivery" (ID 182897) and "Digital Health Platforms and Health Information System (HIS) is strengthened" (ID 82410). The digital health ecosystem was strengthened through improved governance, legislation and compliance with Health Information Exchange standards and cybersecurity protocols, alongside support to the Global Initiative on Digital Health architecture and promotion of safe, equitable use of artificial intelligence. A national strategy to standardize health data collection across public and private facilities was introduced, complemented by an Open Data approach enabling real-time public health data sharing among researchers and policymakers, as well as development of interoperability standards, health data governance frameworks, and virtual hospital and telemedicine platforms.

planEntities.name: Health and well-being improved through a transformed workforce and integrated action on the social, behavioural and environmental determinants of health,  including evidence-based parenting, violence prevention, road safety, healthy ageing, healthy cities, digital mental health services and NCD risk reduction.
planEntities.parentName: Accessibility, responsiveness, and quality of public services as enablers for Thailand’s transformation are improved.
planEntities.description: This sub-output consolidates five former sub-outputs: "Facilitate and enhance integrated care for older people through the use of mobile health technology" (ID 82412); "Progressive development of legislation on control of marketing of food and non-alcoholic beverage for children" (ID 82467); "Health policies and collective action against NCDs... (Strategies 1 and 2)" (ID 82468); "Evidence-based parenting and violence prevention programs scaled up" (ID 207692); and "Urban governance for Healthy Cities strengthened" (ID 207695). Integrated care for older people was advanced through mobile health technology, complementing broader NCD policy work that promoted increased investment in NCDs through targeted communication strategies based on Thailand's scale-up findings, aligned with NCD Strategies 1 and 2. Legislative development on marketing controls for food and non-alcoholic beverages targeting children was progressed through technical support and policy advocacy, contributing to the wider NCD risk-reduction agenda. Child protection and development were fostered through the scale-up of evidence-based parenting programmes and high-level advocacy, complemented by the 2nd global survey on Violence Against Children to generate data for policy formulation. Urban health governance was strengthened through capacity building for local authorities, with the Healthy Cities approach recognized through awards to four Thai cities for their commitment to health-promoting urban environments.

planEntities.name: Disease burden reduced through strengthened antimicrobial resistance surveillance and stewardship, accelerated neglected tropical disease elimination efforts, and implementation of evidence-informed policies and multisectoral actions for noncommunicable disease prevention and control.
planEntities.parentName: Accessibility, responsiveness, and quality of public services as enablers for Thailand’s transformation are improved.
planEntities.description: This sub-output consolidates eight former sub-outputs: "Promoting evidence-based advocacy and implementing robust health and economic monitoring mechanisms for managing NCDs... (Strategies 3, 4 & 5)" (ID 82469); "Improve the quality and reach of essential health services" (ID 182895); "National workforce strategies strengthened and National Health Assembly resolution 2024 on transforming workforce for healthy society" (ID 207682); "Antimicrobial Resistance (AMR) surveillance and stewardship enhanced" (ID 207687); "Neglected Tropical Disease elimination and treatment supported" (ID 207690); "Mental health promotion, surveillance, and digital services expanded" (ID 207691); "Healthy ageing and integrated care for older people promoted" (ID 207696); and "NCD risk factor reduction policies and enforcement mechanisms strengthened" (ID 207697). Multisectoral action on NCDs was enhanced through improved partnerships facilitated by the UN Thematic Working Group, aligned with NCD Strategies 3, 4 and 5, complementing the workforce strengthening achieved through enhanced HRH provider registries and a landscape analysis of the community non-professional workforce. Antimicrobial Resistance (AMR) management was advanced through co-hosting a Multi-Country Meeting on AMR and Primary Health Care, a Point Prevalence Survey on healthcare-associated infections across 100 hospitals, and development of a national AMR burden methodology and antimicrobial stewardship tools. Progress towards elimination of Neglected Tropical Diseases was supported through provision of diagnostic test strips for Lymphatic Filariasis and sustained treatment of leprosy cases through procurement and distribution of essential medication. Mental health services were expanded through the nationwide scale-up of the "Step-by-Step" digital application, the "Tor term Jai" platform, and the WHO LIVE LIFE suicide prevention package, alongside capacity building through the 3rd International Mental Health Workforce Training. Healthy ageing was promoted through implementation of the Integrated Care for Older People (ICOPE) approach with Siriraj Hospital, alongside advocacy to address social isolation among older persons. NCD risk factor reduction was advanced through sustained advocacy for "Best Buys" policies, including health taxes, e-cigarette bans, food reformulation, Milk Code enforcement, and alcohol control policy assessment.

planEntities.name: Migrant health equity advanced through strengthened migrant health management systems, improved health literacy, and multisectoral action to support inclusive and people-centred health services for migrants and non-national populations.
planEntities.parentName: An enabling, rights-based, inclusive environment to address inequalities, support equal opportunities and reduce poverty are provided.
planEntities.description: This sub-output consolidates two former sub-outputs that together form WHO's Migrant Health Initiative: "Strengthening migrant health management system" (ID 82490) and "Improving the health literacy among migrants and their communities" (ID 82497), which receive an equal proportion of funding. Access to health services for migrants was improved through advancement of the Migrant Health Strategy and expansion of the HINT data platform to include migrant populations, alongside strengthened health literacy among migrants and their communities, including workplaces, through policy advocacy, networking, social movement and policy research to advance health equity for migrants and non-national populations. Operational capacity was further strengthened through field visits, training and improved human resource management for migrant health.

planEntities.name: Thailand’s role in shaping key global health agendas and advancing sustainable health development strengthened through enhanced leadership, knowledge sharing, evidence-informed decision-making, and international collaboration, while supporting implementation of national health priorities and Country Cooperation Strategy outcomes.
planEntities.parentName: Good governance, rule of law and social contract are enhanced for SDG acceleration
planEntities.description: This sub-output is carried forward from the former sub-output: "Promoting the demonstrated collective leadership and contributions of Thailand in global health" (ID 90382), under the CCS EnLIGHT priority area of the 2022-2026 Country Cooperation Strategy. It enhances Team Thailand's collective capacity for international engagement in global health governance, focusing on two core functions: advancing key global health agendas and supporting other Country Cooperation Strategy programmes and partner agencies. This is achieved through four strategic actions: evidence generation, capacity development, international engagement, and knowledge management, including the establishment of resource centres and platforms and effective policy communication to support policy decisions.

planEntities.name: Advanced resilient, evidence-informed and environmentally sustainable health systems through strengthened governance, health technology assessment, and progress towards universal health coverage, while integrating climate adaptation, air pollution control, sustainable waste management and biodiversity protection into national health policies and programmes.
planEntities.parentName: Capacities for low carbon society, resilience, post-COVID 19 and disaster recovery with capability to adapt and reduce the risks of disasters are enabled and strengthened.
planEntities.description: This sub-output consolidates three former sub-outputs: "Strengthen public health resilience to climate and environmental risks" (ID 182894); "Universal Health Coverage and health systems governance advanced" (ID 207700); and "Health technology assessment and economic evidence generation supported" (ID 207701). Climate and environmental health resilience was strengthened through advancement of the Green Climate Fund (GCF) project, building health systems resilient to climate change impacts and integrating environmental considerations into health planning, alongside continued community-based air pollution interventions and mercury reduction efforts. Universal Health Coverage (UHC) and health systems governance were advanced through co-development of a National Health Assembly resolution on proactive health systems amid geopolitical turbulence, with continued technical support to refine and sustain UHC policies. The interface between science, health and the economy was strengthened through support to the "Science for Health and Economic Development" initiative, including development of frameworks to assess the economic impact of health policies.

planEntities.name: Improved equitable access to quality essential health services through strengthened immunization and disease surveillance systems, and implementation of evidence-based strategies for communicable and noncommunicable disease prevention, control and elimination.
planEntities.parentName: An enabling, rights-based, inclusive environment to address inequalities, support equal opportunities and reduce poverty are provided.
planEntities.description: This sub-output consolidates four former sub-outputs: "National Tuberculosis control strategy and data usage improved" (ID 207688); "Malaria elimination strategies for Vivax malaria implemented" (ID 207689); "NCD management practices and monitoring frameworks improved by documenting best practices in the Diabetes Remission Initiative" (ID 207698); and "Immunization coverage and vaccine-preventable disease surveillance enhanced" (ID 207703). Tuberculosis control was advanced through the 1st National TB Conference, a comprehensive review of Thailand's TB epidemiological data, and piloting of AI-powered computer-aided detection for TB and early cancer detection in resource-limited settings. Malaria elimination efforts targeting Vivax malaria were advanced through the funding and introduction of a 7-day Primaquine and Tafenoquine treatment protocol, complemented by novel G-6PD deficiency testing to ensure safe treatment administration. NCD management and monitoring were strengthened by documenting best practices under the Diabetes Remission Initiative, developing a draft health-economics Monitoring and Evaluation framework, and implementing the WHO SEAHEARTS technical package in Lampang and Chiang Mai to improve hypertension management in primary health care. Immunization coverage was enhanced through the Vaccine Avengers Programme, which boosted measles-rubella coverage in low-performing provinces, alongside strengthened community outreach, real-time tracking dashboards, Adverse Events Following Immunization (AEFI) surveillance, and continued support for Measles and Rubella elimination and Polio-free status by 2026.

planEntities.name: Equitable access to quality, integrated and people-centred health services improved for women, children, migrants and vulnerable populations through strengthened primary health care, gender-responsive and safeguarding approaches, disease prevention, and continuity of care.
planEntities.parentName: Accessibility, responsiveness, and quality of public services as enablers for Thailand’s transformation are improved.
planEntities.description: This sub-output consolidates four former sub-outputs: "Maintaining the Triple elimination of mother-to-child transmission (EMTCT) and optimized prevention cascades for key populations" (ID 207673); "Maternal and child health policies and quality of care improved" (ID 207694); "Prevention of sexual exploitation and gender equality capacity strengthened" (ID 207699); and "Migrant health strategy improved and the HINT data platform to include migrant populations expanded" (ID 207702). Leadership on the triple elimination of mother-to-child transmission (EMTCT) was sustained through revitalization of the National Validation Committee, with interventions optimizing the prevention cascade, including maternal syphilis treatment at the primary health care level and strengthened comprehensive prevention programmes for young people. Maternal and child health policies were strengthened through successful advocacy for extending maternity leave to 120 days, high-level engagement on preterm birth management, leadership on breastfeeding in ASEAN and global forums, and strengthened hospital surveyor capacity for assessing youth-friendly sexual and reproductive health services. Institutional capacity for gender equality and safeguarding was strengthened through advocacy on Prevention of Sexual Exploitation, Abuse and Harassment (PRSEAH) with the Ministry of Public Health, alongside enhanced gender mainstreaming capacity among implementing partners. Access to health services for migrants was improved through advancement of the Migrant Health Strategy and expansion of the HINT data platform, supported by the Thailand Migration Report 2024 analyzing healthcare access for 5.3 million non-Thai residents, and strengthened operational capacity through field visits, training and human resource management.

planEntities.name: Strengthened country capacity to address environmental determinants of health through mercury reduction and community-based air pollution interventions.
planEntities.parentName: Green growth: An inclusive and sustainable economic growth premised on Thailand’s bio-circular-green model is supported.
planEntities.description: This sub-output consolidates two former sub-outputs: "Conducted a national landscape assessment and developed an implementation plan to reduce dental amalgam use and mercury waste emissions" (ID 207704) and "Pioneered community-based air pollution interventions, including 'clean air shelters' and alternative crop promotion" (ID 207705). WHO collaborated with Thailand's Department of Health to implement the WHO-UNEP Global Environment Facility (GEF) project, accelerating national implementation of the Minamata Convention's dental amalgam provisions through a comprehensive assessment of policies, regulatory frameworks and waste management practices. In parallel, WHO supported the Government in promoting community-based air pollution interventions in high-risk regions, including Bangkok and Chiang Rai, where respiratory diseases linked to air quality are a major public health concern. This included the establishment of "clean air shelters", health literacy promotion and the encouragement of alternative crops to reduce community burning.

planEntities.name: Road safety strengthened, with a particular focus on motorcycle users, through a national master plan, strengthened road safety cooperation mechanisms, laws and policy implementation, and enhanced capacity of stakeholders and actors to address road safety challenges.
planEntities.parentName: Accessibility, responsiveness, and quality of public services as enablers for Thailand’s transformation are improved.
planEntities.description: This sub-output consolidates two former sub-outputs: "A national master plan for motorcycle safety developed" (ID 199373) and "Road safety enhanced with a particular focus on motorcycle users... (RSF)" (ID 210025). WHO supported the development of Thailand's first national Master Plan focused specifically on motorized two-wheeler safety, in response to the country's high rate of road traffic fatalities, of which nearly 80 per cent involve motorized two-wheelers, in partnership with the Department of Disease Control (DDC) and the Department of Disaster Prevention and Mitigation. This was complemented by road safety initiatives advanced through engagement with the Parliamentary Advisory Committee, implementation of the UN Road Safety Fund project, and improved hospital injury surveillance systems to inform road safety interventions.

In 2026: 
- To strengthen national capacities in the target countries for the development of comprehensive digital governance policies to better plan and manage integrated power systems for an inclusive and gender-responsive sustainable digital transformation of the energy sector. 
The project is grounded in the understanding that many countries with special needs face fragmented governance systems, outdated and/or damaged infrastructure, and limited technical capacity to integrate digital technologies into power systems. Without structured and inclusive policy frameworks, efforts to deploy smart grids and decentralized renewable energy technologies often remain ad hoc, vulnerable to rebound effects, and unable to ensure interoperability with legacy systems. Additionally, the digital divide, cybersecurity risks, and underrepresentation of women and marginalized groups in energy decision-making processes further hinder the inclusiveness and sustainability of the energy transition. 
To address these challenges, the project will support target countries – Belarus, Tajikistan, Egypt, Jordan, Mongolia, and Georgia – to develop national digital governance frameworks tailored to their energy system contexts (OP1.1). These frameworks will be complemented by capacity-building workshops (OP1.2) and the creation of a harmonized policy toolkit (OP1.3), helping policymakers and regulators apply digital governance principles in planning, managing, and regulating smart grid systems. 
In parallel, the project will facilitate increased cross-country cooperation through the establishment of a regional platform for knowledge exchange on digital energy governance (OP2.1). This platform will foster peer learning, mentorship, and the sharing of best practices among national institutions, regional actors, and the private sector. Policy briefs and country case studies (OP2.2) will summarize key insights and inform ongoing reforms, while national training events (OP2.3) will reinforce technical capacity and promote a responsible and inclusive digital transition. 
- Strengthening Sustainable Critical Raw Material Production in Central Asia. The project’s objective is to improve governance, accountability, and sustainability of critical raw material (CRM) supply chains in Central Asia to support socio-economic development and the energy transition.

planEntities.description:
In a letter dated 25 December 2023, H.E. Mr Zavqizoda Zavqi Amin, Minister of Economic Development and Trade of Tajikistan, requested UNIDO’s technical assistance to support the digital transformation of the national economy. Following consultations with the Ministry, UNIDO explored opportunities for technical assistance to strengthen the national digital innovation and entrepreneurial ecosystems in line with Tajikistan’s strategic priorities for digital economy development.

UNIDO subsequently developed the current project to support the implementation of the National Development Strategy 2030 and the Mid-Term Programme for the Development of the Digital Economy in Tajikistan for 2021 to 2025. The project strengthens the Government’s digital transformation efforts through two main intervention areas. The first focuses on free economic zones, industrial clusters and small and medium-sized enterprises in selected priority sectors. The second supports key public sector initiatives to facilitate technology and knowledge transfer, enhance public sector efficiency, increase small and medium-sized enterprise productivity and international competitiveness and foster a digital and innovation-driven entrepreneurial ecosystem.

Through these interventions, the project seeks to facilitate Tajikistan’s integration into the wider Eurasian economic landscape by strengthening linkages and accelerating the transition towards a more digital and innovative economy.
