planEntities.name: Support to Strengthening National Crop Monitoring through Remote Sensing Technology
planEntities.parentName: Circularity and resource efficiency concepts are mainstreamed into policy and practice
planEntities.description:
The project will provide technical and institutional support to the Ministry of Agriculture and its Land Resources Service to reform and upgrade its national crop monitoring systems using remote sensing technology. 
The project aims to strengthen Turkmenistan’s crop monitoring system by introducing remote sensing technologies to improve efficiency, accuracy, and reliability, while ensuring long-term sustainability through institutional capacity building. Implemented collaboratively with the Ministry of Agriculture, related institutions, academia, civil society, and the private sector, the project will be guided by a Project Steering Committee and supported by a Technical Working Group. Through FAO-led technical assistance under the TCP, stakeholders will gain advanced skills in remote sensing, GIS, land use monitoring, and improved business processes for crop forecasting and reporting, with practical testing at pilot sites. A comprehensive training and lifelong learning program, including integration into university curricula, will support lasting knowledge transfer. By enabling early detection of crop stress, precision agriculture, and evidence-based policy-making, the project will enhance agricultural productivity, resilience, and sustainability, with findings and policy recommendations widely disseminated to ensure broad ownership and long-term impact.

planEntities.name: Establishing a national strategy for the National Animal Identification and Traceability System (NAITS)
planEntities.parentName: Circularity and resource efficiency concepts are mainstreamed into policy and practice
planEntities.description:
The Project aims to prepare a national strategic plan and roadmap for animal identification and traceability system.
The project seeks to establish a strategic plan and roadmap for implementing a National Animal Identification and Traceability System (NAITS) in Turkmenistan by strengthening the knowledge and capacities of government institutions, competent authorities, producers, and livestock service providers through the use of specialized software. Following project completion, the Government of Turkmenistan is expected to independently manage and sustain NAITS, including providing animal movement data for regional analysis, while the State Association of the Livestock and Poultry Industry will serve as the primary beneficiary by gaining hands-on experience to support nationwide rollout. Effective implementation of NAITS will significantly enhance animal disease control and eradication, protect livelihoods, improve disaster risk management, and safeguard the national livestock sector. Equipped with a robust strategy, the government will also be positioned to seek international financial support to strengthen animal health and husbandry systems, meet international production and SPS standards, and access global markets.

planEntities.name: Strengthening technological innovation and research capacities for sustainable and climate-resilient cotton production
planEntities.parentName: Climate change adaptation and mitigation measures are implemented in accordance with the Paris Agreement
planEntities.description:
To support the adoption of sustainable agricultural practices, green technologies and innovative digital tools, resulting in improved cotton productivity, resource efficiency and resilience to climate change impacts.
The project ensures long-term sustainability by strengthening national capacities for resilient cotton improvement through an integrated approach combining capacity building, digital tools, innovative technologies such as marker-assisted selection (MAS) and high-throughput phenotyping (HTP), and collaborative institutional engagement. By training researchers, extension services, farmers, and policymakers, and embedding modern crop improvement methods into academic curricula and lifelong learning systems, the project develops a skilled workforce capable of independently applying and advancing these approaches. Strong collaboration among key national institutions, guided by FAO through coordinated governance structures, fosters ownership, effective decision-making, and policy integration. The project’s emphasis on continuous learning, participatory implementation, and wide dissemination of research findings and policy recommendations ensures that outcomes are embedded within national agricultural frameworks, ultimately enhancing cotton productivity, resilience to climate and environmental stresses, and the sustainability of Turkmenistan’s agri-food system.

planEntities.name: Support for the Improvement of Pest Management Capacities for Cereal Crops
planEntities.parentName: Circularity and resource efficiency concepts are mainstreamed into policy and practice
planEntities.description:
To support enhancement of the capacities of stakeholders, farmers, and researchers to effectively adopt and implement integrated pest management practices for controlling the most prevalent pests and diseases in cereal crops.
The project’s sustainability is ensured by its focus on strengthening Turkmenistan’s national Integrated Pest Management (IPM) system through long-term capacity building, institutional development, and broad stakeholder engagement. By enhancing technical, operational, and decision-making capacities across government institutions, research bodies, farmers, and extension services, the project embeds IPM practices into national agricultural systems, education curricula, and lifelong learning frameworks. Its collaborative implementation, guided by a Project Steering Committee and a Technical Working Group, fosters national ownership and coordinated action, while FAO provides technical oversight and international expertise. Through continuous training, integration of modern crop monitoring techniques, and wide dissemination of policy recommendations, the project promotes resilient, sustainable cereal production, supports sound agricultural policymaking, and contributes to long-term food security and environmental sustainability in Turkmenistan.

planEntities.name: Support for Adaptation and Promotion of Sustainable Soil Management Practices
planEntities.parentName: Climate change adaptation and mitigation measures are implemented in accordance with the Paris Agreement
planEntities.description:
To assist the Government of Turkmenistan in improving and promotion and adoption of modern crop management techniques characterized by higher productivity and cropping system diversification, while mitigating/preventing further land degradation, ensuring the environmental services that healthy agro-ecosystems provide, and minimizing climate change adverse effects.
The project’s sustainability will be ensured by combining practical demonstrations, capacity building, and policy support to promote long-term adoption of sustainable soil management in Turkmenistan. Demonstration sites will showcase effective practices such as crop diversification, crop rotation, and soil fertility enhancement, encouraging farmers to replicate them. Comprehensive training for farmers, extension officers, researchers, and technicians will build local expertise in sustainable soil management and soil quality analysis, enabling continued monitoring and improvement beyond the project’s lifespan. At the policy level, the project will raise awareness among decision-makers and provide technical recommendations to integrate sustainable soil management into national agricultural strategies. Together, strengthened local capacity, ongoing soil health monitoring, and supportive policies will help sustain project outcomes, improving soil health, agricultural productivity, and resilience to environmental challenges.

planEntities.name: Strengthening the capacity of Turkmenistan to comply with the Enhanced Transparency Framework under the Paris Agreement
planEntities.parentName: Climate change adaptation and mitigation measures are implemented in accordance with the Paris Agreement
planEntities.description:
Strengthening the capacity of Turkmenistan to comply with the ETF under the Paris Agreement.
The Paris Agreement, adopted at COP 21 in December 2015 and entering into force in November 2016, established a global framework requiring all Parties to implement robust measurement, reporting, and verification (MRV) systems to transparently communicate climate actions and support. In line with these obligations, the Global Environment Facility (GEF) approved on 18 October 2023 a Project Identification Form and Project Preparation Grant submitted by FAO for the project “Strengthening the capacity of Turkmenistan to comply with the Enhanced Transparency Framework under the Paris Agreement.” Funded under the CBIT program and GEF-8, and implemented by FAO with the Interstate Commission on Sustainable Development as executing partner, the project aims to strengthen Turkmenistan’s national capacities to meet Enhanced Transparency Framework requirements for tracking climate change mitigation and adaptation actions, as well as support received, particularly in sectors covered by the country’s nationally determined contributions.

planEntities.name: Catalysing Nature-Positive transformation of agriculture in Turkmenistan for enhanced resilience
planEntities.parentName: Circularity and resource efficiency concepts are mainstreamed into policy and practice
planEntities.description:
To enable a transformative shift towards nature-positive, resilient and sustainable management of natural resources, especially the holistic integration of NBS practices at the different connected landscapes, in order to improve biodiversity conservation and environmental sustainability of food systems in Turkmenistan.
The project aims to support a sustainable and climate‑resilient transformation of Turkmenistan’s agricultural sector—particularly in Lebap Province—by addressing land degradation, water scarcity, and biodiversity loss exacerbated by climate change. It seeks to promote sustainable land and water management through nature‑based solutions, innovative and water‑saving technologies, and improved farming practices that protect ecosystems while maintaining productivity of key crops such as cotton and wheat. The project will strengthen institutional capacities, harmonize environmental and agricultural policies, and enhance governance and stakeholder collaboration, including farmers and local communities. As part of the Central Asia Water and Land Nexus Program, it will contribute to regional cooperation within the Amu Darya basin, improving water security, ecosystem health, and rural livelihoods.

planEntities.name: Improving the capacity of Turkmenistan to access climate finance through capacity building and strategic frameworks
planEntities.parentName: The business climate in Turkmenistan supports structural transformation of the economy, growth and increased competitiveness of the private sector
planEntities.description:
Enhancing the capacity of the government of Turkmenistan to facilitate the access to climate finance and to improve compliance with the national targets under the Paris Agreements while promoting cross-sectoral collaboration and the engagement of diverse stakeholders in the integrated manner.
The aim of the proposal is to strengthen Turkmenistan’s capacity to implement coordinated, climate‑resilient and low‑carbon development by addressing critical institutional, technical, and financing gaps, with a particular focus on highly vulnerable areas such as the Aral Sea region. It seeks to enhance cross‑sectoral and inter‑ministerial coordination, improve monitoring, reporting, and transparent climate finance tracking systems, and develop NDC implementation, investment, and private sector engagement roadmaps to unlock public and private climate finance. By aligning mitigation and adaptation priorities with national development strategies and applying gender‑responsive, inclusive approaches, the project aims to enable effective climate action, attract investment, and support sustainable, resilient development in Turkmenistan.

planEntities.name: Coordinated approach for Land Restoration in Vulnerable Ecosystems of Central Asia
planEntities.parentName: Circularity and resource efficiency concepts are mainstreamed into policy and practice
planEntities.description:
Coordinated approach for Land Restoration in Vulnerable Ecosystems of Central Asia.
The Program Coordination (PC) project under the Central Asia Water and Land Nexus (CAWLN) Program aims to drive a strategic shift toward coordinated, integrated, and evidence-based management of shared water and land resources in the Amu Darya and Syr Darya river basins. It seeks to enhance regional water security, ecosystem resilience, and rural livelihoods by strengthening transboundary and cross-sectoral cooperation, improving policy dialogue and governance, harmonizing Earth Observation data for informed decision-making, and building institutional and technical capacity for integrated watershed management. By coordinating regional initiatives, piloting integrated water–land nexus approaches, mainstreaming climate-smart and biodiversity-friendly practices, engaging the private sector, and promoting gender-sensitive knowledge sharing, the project addresses environmental degradation, climate vulnerability, and socio-economic pressures while reinforcing existing regional mechanisms to enable sustainable and scalable solutions across Central Asia.

planEntities.name: Strengthening Integrated Water Management in Amu Darya, Zarafshon and Panj River Basins
planEntities.parentName: Circularity and resource efficiency concepts are mainstreamed into policy and practice
planEntities.description:
Strengthening Integrated Water Management in Amu Darya, Zarafshon and Panj River Basins.
The Amu Darya Basin Child Project (ADB-CP), under the Central Asia Water and Land Nexus (CAWLN) Program, seeks to tackle mounting environmental degradation and socio‑economic vulnerabilities in the Amu Darya River Basin by addressing systemic imbalances in water and land use caused by weak coordination, fragmented institutions, data gaps, limited stakeholder engagement, and unsustainable practices. Guided by Integrated Watershed Management, the project promotes a coordinated and resilient approach to managing the Water‑Land Nexus through strengthened transboundary cooperation, improved basin‑wide monitoring, and national‑level actions aligned with regional objectives. Implemented across Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, and Uzbekistan, the ADB‑CP responds to upstream‑downstream dynamics and builds on each country’s policy commitments, ensuring coherence with national development goals while collectively addressing shared environmental and climate risks in the basin.

planEntities.name: Improving adaptive capacity and resilience of local communities to climate change induced water shortages and land degradation in two climate affected regions of Turkmenistan
planEntities.parentName: Climate change adaptation and mitigation measures are implemented in accordance with the Paris Agreement
planEntities.description: Turkmenistan with its highly arid climate and scarce water resources is particularly vulnerable to the adverse impacts of climate change. The adverse effects of climate change, such as water shortages and land degradation, contribute to economic decline and job loss in the agricultural sector, serving as a push factor of migration from the primary sector dependent regions of Turkmenistan, mainly Dashoguz and Lebap. In these regions, land degradation and shortage of irrigation water for agriculture affect agricultural productivity and, accordingly, quality of life of the local communities, forcing them to migrate. However, for some vulnerable groups, primarily families of migrants left behind and women-led households, migration is not an option because they do not have economic and other resources. In this regard, the project will prioritize adaptation in-situ to build resilience of these vulnerable groups and promote their climate resilient development through demonstration of the efficient use of water resources, use of innovative “green” technologies in land and water use, water-smart practices for greater access to safe drinking water and irrigation, raising public awareness to encourage responsible water consumption, promoting stakeholder interaction and cooperation for better adaptation planning at the local level, and enhancing the knowledge and capacity of targeted vulnerable groups as well as local administrations through education and training.

planEntities.name: Procurement for clinical laboratory services in Turkmenistan
planEntities.parentName: Health policies,  financing, institutional and human capacities strengthened to ensure universal access to quality health services for all
planEntities.description:
The Government of Turkmenistan is strongly committed to protecting health of the people. Since 2023, the Ministry of Health and Medical Industry of Turkmenistan (MOHMI) and UNDP have been implementing a project to strengthen laboratory services for the diagnosis of various diseases, with a budget of 18 million USD. As part of the laboratory project, 121 laboratories across the country have been modernized to deliver the essential clinical analyses. 
Referring to the successful implementation of a project, the MOHMI and UNDP have initiated a new two-year project for ensuring the sustainable provision of high-quality medical services, achieve a long-term impact of the project and further strengthening of the laboratory diagnostic of diseases, with a focus on primary healthcare facilities. 

The goal of the project “Strengthening clinical laboratory services in Turkmenistan in 2026-2027” is to strengthen the potential of national healthcare system in the field of clinical laboratory diagnostic of diseases. 

The project will support healthcare services to ensure the availability, accessibility, reliability and modern laboratory analyses for accurate and timely diagnosis of the most common illnesses, including infectious and noncommunicable diseases, surgery, emergency, maternal and child healthcare and others. The project will focus on laboratory capacity in primary healthcare facilities, but will also support secondary and tertiary care facilities.

planEntities.name: Procurement of health products for diagnostics and treatment of noncommunicable diseases (NCD)
planEntities.parentName: Health policies,  financing, institutional and human capacities strengthened to ensure universal access to quality health services for all
planEntities.description:
The Government of Turkmenistan is strongly committed to protecting health of the people. Control of noncommunicable diseases (NCDs) and reducing their economic burden is a top priority on the national development agenda. Since 2021, the Ministry of Health and Medical Industry of Turkmenistan and UNDP implemented two NCD projects with total budget of more than $92 mln. Implementation of the joint projects ensured availability of high quality, affordable and free-of-charge medicines for treatment of major NCD and rare diseases, maternal and neonatal health, as well provided technical assistance and capacitating health workforce for management of NCDs, and overall strengthening of the national health system. 
Based on the successful implementation of the NCD projects and to ensure continuous provision of the quality health services and achieve long-term impact, MOHMI and UNDP initiated a new 2-year project on strengthening integrated health services on lab diagnostics and treatment of the NCD, rare diseases, maternal and neonatal health, with focus on primary health care facilities.
The overall aim of the project will be to improve health outcomes for NCDs, rare diseases, maternal and neonatal emergencies, through improving access to equitable, quality and affordable essential health services for all.

planEntities.name: Adherence support of MDR-TB patients
planEntities.parentName: Health policies,  financing, institutional and human capacities strengthened to ensure universal access to quality health services for all
planEntities.description:
By the end of 2027, the National Tuberculosis Programme of Turkmenistan plans to complete a full transition to domestic funding and exit from Global Fund support. 
In this context, adherence support for multidrug-resistant tuberculosis (MDR-TB) patients remains significantly important. MDR-TB treatment involves prolonged regimens (often 9–24 months) with second-line drugs that frequently cause severe adverse effects, leading to high risks of treatment interruption or default. Incomplete adherence is the primary cause of further drug resistance, including progression to extensively drug-resistant TB (XDR-TB), which carries substantially worse outcomes and higher costs. Sustained high treatment success rates — particularly for MDR-TB — are therefore essential to protect the epidemiological gains already achieved (low mortality and declining incidence) and to ensure the long-term sustainability of the national TB response under full domestic financing.

planEntities.name: Monitoring and evaluation of health services
planEntities.parentName: Health policies,  financing, institutional and human capacities strengthened to ensure universal access to quality health services for all
planEntities.description: In the framework of the Health projects, monitoring and evaluation of health services constitute a systematic and integral component aimed at ensuring the effective, transparent, and sustainable delivery of interventions. This process encompasses regular tracking of medicine distribution, storage conditions, expiration management, and rational dispensing across national, regional, city, and district levels through dedicated regional coordinators. It further includes assessment of coverage rates, uninterrupted availability of free medicines to registered patients, adherence to updated national treatment protocols, and the functionality of digital tools such as warehouse management systems and patient-facing applications. This approach supports accountability to the Ministry of Health and Medical Industry, Global Fund and UNDP HQ.

planEntities.name: Infection control and waste management
planEntities.parentName: Health policies,  financing, institutional and human capacities strengthened to ensure universal access to quality health services for all
planEntities.description:
Infection control and waste management are critical components in UNDP-supported health projects in Turkmenistan, as they directly safeguard patient safety, protect healthcare workers, and prevent the spread of infections within and beyond healthcare facilities. In projects focused on procurement of essential medicines for non-communicable diseases, maternal and child health, tuberculosis, HIV, viral hepatitis and other infectious diseases as well as in laboratory strengthening, these measures minimize the risk of healthcare-associated infections, particularly in settings treating chronic and drug-resistant conditions where patients may have prolonged hospital stays or compromised immunity. Effective infection prevention protocols, including the provision of personal protective equipment (PPE), biosafety equipment, and ventilation systems, combined with rigorous waste management practices, reduce cross-transmission of pathogens, prevent amplification of antimicrobial resistance, and maintain the integrity of treatment outcomes.
Proper waste management — encompassing safe segregation, collection, decontamination (e.g., through units such as Sterilwave SW100 and Medister 160), and environmentally sound disposal of infectious, sharp, pharmaceutical, and chemical waste — eliminates secondary hazards to the community and the environment. These activities ensure compliance with international biosafety standards, protect vulnerable populations (including remote residents and low-income households), and support the sustainability of health system investments during the transition to full domestic funding. By mitigating occupational and environmental risks, infection control and waste management contribute to the overall resilience, equity, and long-term effectiveness of national health programmes in alignment with SDG 3 targets.

planEntities.name: Digital solutions in health services
planEntities.parentName: Health policies,  financing, institutional and human capacities strengthened to ensure universal access to quality health services for all
planEntities.description:
Digital solutions in health projects play a pivotal role in improving access, adherence, and overall management of health services in Turkmenistan.
In these initiatives, a bilingual mobile application has been developed and deployed to enable registered patients to view their prescribed medicines, access detailed treatment information, and better adhere to therapy regimens. Concurrently, digital warehouse management systems have been introduced to facilitate real-time monitoring of medicine distribution, storage conditions, expiration dates, and rational dispensing practices across all levels of the health system. For tuberculosis control efforts, piloting of advanced digital adherence tools includes Video Supported Treatment (VST) and smart pillboxes, while the rollout of an electronic TB register (TB-RRIS) has commenced to enhance case management, surveillance, and reporting accuracy. These digital innovations reduce geographic and logistical barriers, strengthen patient-centered care, minimize treatment interruptions, support evidence-based decision-making, and contribute to more efficient and sustainable health service delivery as the country advances toward full domestic funding and self-reliance. Additionally, in Turkmenistan, CAD4TB has been implemented through UNDP-led initiatives supported by the Global Fund to Fight AIDS, Tuberculosis and Malaria. As of late 2025, portable X-ray units equipped with CAD4TB are deployed to expand TB screening, particularly in remote areas, by bringing diagnostic services directly to communities. Artificial intelligence rapidly analyzes images for TB signs, enabling timely detection and reducing barriers such as travel to centralized facilities. National medical personnel receive comprehensive training to maximize effectiveness, aligning with WHO recommendations for AI-assisted screening in adults and contributing to strengthened national TB control efforts. This technology transforms traditional screening into a mobile, efficient, and accessible process, supporting early diagnosis and program scalability in the transition toward domestic funding.

planEntities.name: Technical assistance (capacity building of health specialists, updating national protocols and technical assistance of international experts) including through WHO and UNFPA
planEntities.parentName: Health policies,  financing, institutional and human capacities strengthened to ensure universal access to quality health services for all
planEntities.description:
Technical assistance, encompassing capacity building of health specialists, updating of national protocols, and engagement of international experts (particularly through WHO and UNFPA), is of paramount importance in UNDP-supported health projects in Turkmenistan for several fundamental reasons.
First, it ensures the adoption of evidence-based, internationally aligned clinical practices in a context where drug-resistant tuberculosis, non-communicable diseases, and other priority health conditions require precise, standardized, and high-quality management. Continuous training of healthcare professionals — delivered by WHO experts — equips clinicians with up-to-date knowledge on diagnostics, treatment regimens (including shorter DR-TB regimens), adverse effect monitoring, and patient-centered care, thereby directly improving treatment success rates and reducing morbidity and mortality. Second, systematic updating of national treatment protocols, guided by WHO recommendations and UNFPA technical input on maternal and child health, guarantees that clinical decision-making reflects the latest global standards, enhances treatment efficacy, minimizes risks of resistance amplification, and promotes rational use of medicines — all essential for long-term epidemiological control and cost-effectiveness. Third, the involvement of international experts provides objective, specialized guidance during critical phases of programme design, implementation, and transition to domestic funding, strengthening national ownership while bridging technical gaps.

planEntities.name: Knowledge of national institutions is strengthened to improve their capacities to respond to climate change impact on cryosphere and related water systems
planEntities.parentName: Climate change adaptation and mitigation measures are implemented in accordance with the Paris Agreement
planEntities.description: The headwaters of the main river systems in Central Asia heavily depend on the seasonal melting of the cryosphere, with little additional precipitation input in their lower reaches. These rivers sustain the lives and livelihoods of people and support economic development across the region, including in Turkmenistan. However, glaciers in Central Asia are experiencing a rapid loss of mass. Changes in glacier extent and volume will have significant impacts on associated water systems and on the large populations that depend on them. It is therefore essential to understand the impacts of climate change on the cryosphere in Central Asia. The project aims to foster regional cooperation on adaptation strategies, validated through scientific assessments of snow, glaciers, permafrost, and available water resources.

planEntities.parentName: Disaggregated and reliable data is available to inform policymaking and monitor progress towards the SDGs
planEntities.description:
Development of a national, multi-sectoral strategy or framework that promotes demographic resilience in Turkmenistan.
A demographic resilience strategy (DRS) is defined as a forward-looking, evidence-based policy document that:
- Responds to the country’s population dynamics (age structure, fertility, mortality, migration, urbanization, etc.) and megatrends (climate change, digitalization, economic transformation, and labor shifts).
- Provides strategic policy directions, promotes legal frameworks, and identifies programmatic interventions aimed at maximizing the demographic dividend and promoting human capital development.
- Envisages gender-transformative and rights-based approaches, ensuring that reproductive rights, gender equality, and youth empowerment are central to the framework.
- Promotes intersectoral coordination among key ministries (e.g. economy, health, education, youth, labor, statistics, environment, digital development, and social protection), with a mechanism for implementation, monitoring, and accountability.

planEntities.name: Reforming disability determination, assessment, and referral system in line with the principles of ICF and development of cross-sectoral disability inclusive services
planEntities.parentName: The education system, from pre-primary to tertiary, provides quality, inclusive and safe learning opportunities for all children and young people, including children with disabilities
planEntities.description:
Disability determination, assessment, and referral system including medical-social expertise under the MoHMI and medical-pedagogical commissions under MoE will be revised in line with principles of the International Classification for Functioning, Disability and Health (ICF) to facilitate inclusive support, prevention of institutionalization, deinstitutionalization and overall social inclusion for children and adults with disabilities. Specific interventions will include capacity development for ICF, revision of the mandates of the medical-social expertise and medical-pedagogical commissions and piloting a new ICF based cross-sectoral model for disability determination, assessment, and referral (with the new data management) to cross-sectoral support services for further institutionalization.

Cross-sectoral support services will be developed to facilitate disability inclusion and inclusive education pathways for children and adults with disabilities. Specific intervention will include capacity development for multi-disciplinary professionals including psychologists, speech therapists, physical and occupational therapists, pedagogues, pediatricians, social workers in early intervention and multi-disciplinary support, parental empowerment; pre-and in-service training for the above disciplines, development of referrals and standards of services.

planEntities.name: Implementation of inclusive education policy for children and adults with disabilities
planEntities.parentName: The education system, from pre-primary to tertiary, provides quality, inclusive and safe learning opportunities for all children and young people, including children with disabilities
planEntities.description:
Implementation of the inclusive education policy for children with disabilities in line with the national concept of inclusive education. Expansion of inclusive education model (with focus on provision of continuous multi-disciplinary support and inclusive learning for children with disabilities, provision of assistive devices, accessibility improvements and building supportive environment) to mainstream kindergartens and schools nation-wide to achieve 2030 target. Transformation of residential care and rehabilitation facilities into inclusive resource centers to facilitate inclusive education and deinstitutionalization reform.
Specific interventions will include promoting a multi-sectoral system for modern assistive technologies and products and development of a standard methodology for school accessibility improvements, capacity development in early identification and intervention, multidisciplinary support, inclusive education, assistive technologies and products, social work case management, institutional capacity development for residential care and rehabilitation facilities to become inclusive resource centers.

planEntities.name: Institutional strengthening is undertaken for the HCFC phase-out management plan (HPMP)
planEntities.parentName: Climate change adaptation and mitigation measures are implemented in accordance with the Paris Agreement
planEntities.description:
The Executive Committee reviewed the report submitted with the request for renewal of the institutional strengthening project for Turkmenistan, phase V, and noted with appreciation that the country continued the process of ratifying the Kigali Amendment, amended the national law on ozone-depleting substances (ODS), maintained a robust licensing and quota system for hydrochlorofluorocarbons (HCFCs), raised public awareness on ozone layer protection, and reported 2018 and 2019 country programme implementation data and Article 7 data to the Multilateral Fund and Ozone Secretariats, respectively, indicating that the country is in compliance with the Montreal Protocol.

The Executive Committee also noted the submission of the hydrochlorofluorocarbon phase-out management plan (HPMP), stage II, together with the request for renewal of the institutional strengthening project, and the approval of the final tranche for stage I of the hydrochlorofluorocarbon phase-out management plan. The Executive Committee therefore expressed confidence that the Government of Turkmenistan will continue implementing activities to enable the country to meet the Montreal Protocol targets.

planEntities.name: The hydrofluorocarbon (HFC) implementation plan is developed in Turkmenistan
planEntities.parentName: Climate change adaptation and mitigation measures are implemented in accordance with the Paris Agreement
planEntities.description: The project includes a strategy for the phase-down of hydrofluorocarbons (HFCs) and a plan of action for the refrigeration servicing sector to enable Turkmenistan to meet the targets of the Montreal Protocol, while enhancing sectoral energy efficiency and minimising climate impact. The plan covers policy development and implementation, the upgrading of refrigeration and air-conditioning training programmes and manuals, training of technicians and customs officers, measures to prevent illegal trade in hydrofluorocarbons, improvements in servicing tools, recovery and recycling of hydrofluorocarbons, and the reduction of safety risks associated with low-global-warming-potential alternative refrigerants through the training of trainers.

Las instituciones nacionales responsables de implementar políticas sobre cambio climático (Comité nacional de cambio climático NDA, Comité de FVC) mejoran sus capacidades para acceder a la financiación climática, reforzar la gobernanza climática y elaborar políticas, planes y programas nacionales de mitigación y adaptación al cambio climático.
planEntities.description:
"Los principales objetivos del proyecto son los siguientes:
• Desarrollar un mecanismo de coordinación apropiado del GCF y fortalecer la capacidad de la NDA para supervisar adecuadamente las actividades apoyadas por el GCF a nivel nacional. Esto incluye fortalecer las capacidades de las instituciones candidatas para la acreditación como Entidades de acceso directo (DAE) para cumplir y mantener los estándares de acreditación del GCF, desarrollar una cartera de proyectos, implementar de manera efectiva las actividades financiadas por el GCF y desarrollar las capacidades de las partes interesadas para apoyar la planificación, programación. y la implementación de actividades financiadas por el FVC.
• Desarrollar, en coordinación con el MINEC, el Comité Nacional del GCF y la Comisión Presidencial para el Cambio Climático, un Programa País del GCF, basado en la NDC, para identificar oportunidades de inversión para el desarrollo resiliente al clima y bajo en carbono, asegurando la complementariedad con otros inversiones climáticas nacionales en curso.
• Incrementar la participación de las partes interesadas en la programación y diseño de proyectos financiados por el GCF, considerando la inclusión del enfoque de género y la perspectiva de grupos vulnerables."

planEntities.name: Acciones interseccionales para fortalecer iniciativas de inclusión, género, y discapacidad para un Desarrollo Sostenible en Venezuela
planEntities.parentName: 1.3.1. planEntities.description:
Breve descripción 
Venezuela enfrenta importantes desafíos para garantizar el ejercicio pleno de los derechos de las mujeres y de grupos históricamente excluidos, como personas con discapacidad, juventudes, pueblos indígenas, población LGBTIQ+ y personas afrodescendientes. Si bien existen marcos normativos, políticas públicas y avances institucionales, persisten brechas estructurales de desigualdad, discriminación y exclusión que requieren el fortalecimiento de capacidades nacionales desde un enfoque interseccional, basado en derechos humanos y gobernanza inclusiva.
En este contexto, resulta prioritario reforzar las capacidades institucionales, comunitarias y de las personas, así como los mecanismos de articulación entre actores, para avanzar hacia un desarrollo sostenible que no deje a nadie atrás. El PNUD, con mandato transversal en derechos humanos, igualdad de género y gobernabilidad democrática, y con presencia y reconocimiento global en más de 170 países, propone la consolidación de una Unidad de Inclusión e Igualdad de Género como plataforma técnica interna para transversalizar estos enfoques en la programación del PNUD Venezuela, apoyar a instituciones nacionales, contrapartes y otras agencias del Sistema de las Naciones Unidas, y promover acciones estratégicas, programáticas e innovadoras.
Esta iniciativa se enmarca en la Estrategia Global de Igualdad de Género 2022–2025 del PNUD, la agenda regional para América Latina y el Caribe centrada en inclusión estructural e igualdad sustantiva, y la Estrategia de Igualdad de Género del PNUD Venezuela 2024–2026. Asimismo, se articula con los Portafolios Interagenciales del PNUD y con el Documento de Portafolio del ODS 5 sobre Igualdad de Género y Empoderamiento de las Mujeres, fortaleciendo la coherencia metodológica, las sinergias interinstitucionales y el alineamiento con las políticas nacionales en materia de inclusión social, igualdad de género, discapacidad, juventudes e interculturalidad.
La Unidad también impulsará la implementación de la Estrategia de Inclusión de Personas con Discapacidad, en alineación con la Disability Inclusion Strategy del Sistema de Naciones Unidas, capitalizando la experiencia del Plan de Inclusión de la Discapacidad 2024–2026 del PNUD Venezuela, y contribuyendo al cumplimiento progresivo de los estándares UNDIS.
Durante un período de dos años, este proyecto busca fortalecer la inclusión en la toma de decisiones, equiparar el acceso a derechos y oportunidades, y ampliar las capacidades para la autonomía de poblaciones en situación de vulnerabilidad, con énfasis en mujeres, personas con discapacidad, juventudes y pueblos indígenas. Para ello, propone acciones estratégicas organizadas en seis ejes: (i) igualdad sustantiva y fortalecimiento institucional; (ii) garantía de derechos con enfoque prioritario; (iii) empoderamiento económico y social; (iv) fortalecimiento del liderazgo político y comunitario; (v) transversalización interna de enfoques interseccionales e inclusivos; y (vi) promoción de alianzas con el sector público, sociedad civil, sector privado y academia.
Estas acciones sentarán las bases para una Unidad de Inclusión e Igualdad de Género en el PNUD Venezuela con capacidad de generar impactos sostenibles, replicables y escalables, contribuyendo a un desarrollo más justo, inclusivo y resiliente en el país.

planEntities.name: Strengthening the capacities of public institutions in Venezuela to consolidate inclusive policies
planEntities.parentName: 3.1.1. Las capacidades técnicas de las instituciones públicas a nivel nacional, regional y local y el marco normativo, son fortalecidas para garantizar el disfrute de derechos sociales, civiles, laborales, económicos, ambientales, culturales y políticos con especial énfasis en las personas en situación de vulnerabilidad y asegurando el enfoque de género.
planEntities.description:
En Venezuela, los servicios sociales vinculados a los sistemas de protección social, cuidados y justicia representan el principal punto de interacción entre las instituciones públicas y la ciudadanía, y un espacio determinante para el ejercicio efectivo de los derechos. No obstante, la existencia de marcos normativos, políticas públicas y programas no garantiza, por sí sola, un acceso equitativo, digno y oportuno a dichos servicios. Persisten brechas en la calidad de la atención, barreras administrativas y prácticas institucionales desiguales que limitan la experiencia de las personas usuarias y debilitan la confianza ciudadana, afectando de manera desproporcionada a mujeres —especialmente aquellas con responsabilidades de cuidado—, juventudes, personas con discapacidad, personas adultas mayores y otros grupos en situación de vulnerabilidad.
El proyecto tiene como objetivo fortalecer las capacidades de las instituciones públicas subnacionales para traducir principios de igualdad, no discriminación, rendición de cuentas y enfoque centrado en las personas en prácticas concretas, medibles y sostenibles de prestación de servicios sociales inclusivos. A través de un enfoque basado en derechos humanos, igualdad de género e interseccionalidad, la intervención combina diagnósticos participativos, asistencia técnica especializada, procesos de formación híbrida y el desarrollo de herramientas operativas orientadas a mejorar la experiencia usuaria, la accesibilidad, la gestión de información desagregada y la toma de decisiones basada en evidencia.
Adicionalmente, el proyecto promueve la articulación efectiva entre instituciones públicas, organizaciones de mujeres, juventudes y redes comunitarias, fortaleciendo la coproducción de soluciones, el espacio cívico y los mecanismos de participación social a nivel territorial. Esta articulación busca asegurar que las reformas institucionales respondan a las necesidades reales de la población y refuercen la legitimidad de la acción pública.
La iniciativa contribuye a una gobernanza local más inclusiva, eficiente y resiliente, alineada con los resultados globales del PNUD en materia de fortalecimiento del sector público, prestación de servicios, inclusión social, igualdad de género y cohesión social, generando impactos sostenibles en la reducción de brechas estructurales y en el ejercicio efectivo de derechos.

planEntities.name: Biodiversity Finance Plan Venezuela
planEntities.parentName: 2.4.1. Las instituciones del Estado, las comunidades, los gobiernos regionales y locales y las entidades del sector privado fortalecen sus capacidades para la planificación de l desarrollo territorial con enfoque demográfico y ambiental en el marco de la nueva agenda urbana
planEntities.description: El Fondo para el Medio Ambiente Mundial (FMAM) creó un programa global para ayudar a los países a diseñar un Plan Nacional de Financiamiento de la Biodiversidad. Este Plan incluye un análisis de sistemas de la economía de un país, incluido el mapeo de los mecanismos de financiamiento existentes, los subsidios con posibles impactos dañinos en la naturaleza, los factores que impulsan la pérdida y ganancia de la biodiversidad, los gastos públicos y privados comprometidos con los objetivos de la biodiversidad y las necesidades financieras nacionales de un país para la biodiversidad[1]. El plan de financiación de la biodiversidad debe incluir una serie de acciones con el objetivo de aumentar significativamente la financiación disponible a través de la creación o fortalecimiento de mecanismos de financiamiento, reformar o eliminar gradualmente los flujos financieros perjudiciales y mejorar la eficacia de los gastos disponibles. El programa permite el intercambio activo de experiencias entre países e incluye una plataforma de intercambio de conocimientos.

planEntities.name: UMBRELLA PROGRAMME TO SUPPORT NBSAP UPDATE AND 7th NATIONAL REPORTS
planEntities.parentName: 2.4.1. Las instituciones del Estado, las comunidades, los gobiernos regionales y locales y las entidades del sector privado fortalecen sus capacidades para la planificación de l desarrollo territorial con enfoque demográfico y ambiental en el marco de la nueva agenda urbana
planEntities.description: Este programa apoya a 139 Partes elegibles para el GEF  para actualizar y preparar sus Planes de Acción Nacionales de Biodiversidad (PNB) para la implementación de los mismos, que reflejen el Marco de Acción de Kunming Montreal y sus objetivos globales. También se brinda apoyo técnico y financiero para la elaboración de los Séptimos Informes Nacionales  para el Convenio sobre la Diversidad Biológica (CDB), elaborados con datos de alta calidad y con perspectiva de género. Hasta 2027, aprovechando las sinergias del proyecto de Apoyo a la Acción Temprana y del Programa Paraguas sobre Financiación de la Biodiversidad, los Ministerios de  Ambiente prepararán políticas y mecanismos de seguimiento para la adopción de medidas urgentes que detengan y reviertan la pérdida de biodiversidad, contribuyendo así al logro de la Visión 2050 para la Diversidad Biológica y los Objetivos de Desarrollo Sostenible. El programa también fomentará la cooperación y la coordinación entre los diferentes sectores y partes interesadas para garantizar su participación efectiva y apoyará las sinergias entre las políticas de naturaleza, clima y desarrollo.

planEntities.name: Voces y Partituras: Multiplicando el Impacto de El Sistema para la Inclusión Social.
planEntities.parentName: 1.3.1. Capacidad reforzada de las instituciones nacionales para hacer frente a las disparidades sociales, en los planos nacional y local, desde un enfoque de gestión pública que responda a las necesidades de cobertura y disponibilidad de la atención a grupos más vulnerables.
planEntities.description: El objetivo del Proyecto es apoyar la consolidación nacional de El Sistema, a través del fortalecimiento de sus núcleos y módulos incorporando de manera transversal y explícita el enfoque de derechos humanos, de inclusión intersectional e igualdad de género. En este contexto se pretende: Mejorar las capacidades operativas y apoyar la obtención, fortalecimiento y mantenimiento de las competencias organizacionales y del personal fundamentales para establecer y alcanzar los propios objetivos de desarrollo de El Sistema a lo largo del tiempo, como política de inclusión y protección social. Así mismo, el proyecto contempla el apoyo para la expansión internacional de la metodología implementada por El Sistema, el cual utiliza la música como herramienta de inclusión y transformación social, a fin de contribuir al desarrollo humano a nivel nacional y mundial para llevar “Música para Todos”.

planEntities.name: Comprehensive Disaster Participatory Preparedness focused on highly Vulnerable Communities
planEntities.parentName: 1.4.1. Fortalecidas las capacidades institucionales, sectoriales y comunitarias para la gestión integral de riesgos a nivel nacional, regional , municipal y comunitario
planEntities.description: Disasters in Venezuela are associated with intensive and extensive risk conditions resulting from high levels of vulnerability and natural, socio-natural, and manmade hazards. These high-risk conditions threaten to aggravate the impact of the protracted socioeconomic crisis. This joint project aims to improve disaster preparedness in hard-to-reach areas across Amazonas, Apure, Delta Amacuro, Sucre, Táchira and Zulia states. UNICEF will strengthen critical services like health, nutrition, WASH, and child protection within education circuits that connect schools with local service providers. Through a joint participatory risk analysis, UNICEF will establish a common understanding of disaster risks and management approaches among stakeholders (R1-UNICEF). This analysis will inform the development of preparedness plans and the implementation of agreed-upon anticipatory actions (R2-UNICEF). UNICEF will promote risk management alternatives, through capacity building of key DRM actors (R4-UNICEF). UNHCR's role complements UNICEF's efforts by focusing on building community resilience and empowering community structures to identify and manage risks (R3-UNHCR). Agencies will work to strengthen Venezuela's response capacity to climate adversities by enhancing institutional mechanisms for disaster preparedness with a participatory approach. This project operates as an iterative process, where learning happens alongside implementation, fostering resilience and preparedness in disaster-prone areas. The project also includes Accountability to Affected Population actions to ensure meaningful community participation and culturally adapted feedback mechanisms, focusing on Indigenous communities.

planEntities.description:
El proyecto promoverá el desarrollo integrado y sostenible de la cadena de valor, con la participación de los agentes a lo largo de las cadenas de valor, para lograr una mayor producción y rentabilidad y, de este modo, facilitar la sustitución de importaciones y el acceso a nuevos y mejores mercados. Aumento de la producción y del valor añadido en 7 cadenas de valor seleccionadas y aumento del consumo de productos agrícolas locales.
Resultados esperados:
1. Identificación de oportunidades de acciones concretas para el desarrollo de 7 cadenas agroindustriales.
2. Establecimiento de una herramienta analítica para el seguimiento continuo de costes y precios en la cadena de valor.
3. Mejora de la coordinación e integración entre los agentes de cada una de las cadenas de valor.
4. Institucionalización del apoyo al desarrollo de la cadena de valor y creación y fortalecimiento de capacidades para su prestación a través de los servicios públicos.
5. Ejecución de acciones críticas de desarrollo de la cadena de valor y creación de capacidades.
6. Gestión, seguimiento y comunicación del proyecto.

planEntities.parentName: Resilience [Enhanced capacity and gender-responsive policies to identify and reduce climate risks, respond to disasters and build the resilience of vulnerable populations]
planEntities.description:
The overall objective of the proposed project is to reduce vulnerability to climate change in the Greater Mekong Sub-region. This objective will be achieved through three complementary outcomes: 
(1)	Climate change adaptation interventions, particularly EbA, implemented by vulnerable communities in the GMS to manage climate change impacts, particularly droughts and floods;
(2)	Enhanced knowledge and awareness of adaptation measures, including EbA, to shared climate change impacts in different ecosystems to promote regional cooperation, planning and implementation of adaptation in the GMS; and 
(3)	Strengthened regional cooperation.

planEntities.name: Enhancing sustainability of the Transboundary Cambodia - Mekong Delta Aquifer
planEntities.parentName: Natural Resources [Strengthened institutional capacity and actions from all stakeholders for sustainable management and use of natural resources and effective conservation of biodiversity and ecosystems]
planEntities.description:
The project is a groundbreaking initiative addressing critical challenges in the Lower Mekong Basin—a vast hydrological, ecological, and socio-economic system that supports nearly 70 million people and some of the world’s most diverse freshwater ecosystems. Lying beneath the fertile soils and floodplains of Cambodia and southern Vietnam, the transboundary Cambodia-Mekong Delta Aquifer (CMDA) is a vital underground reservoir that sustains the region’s agriculture, drinking water, and biodiversity. It faces mounting threats from over-extraction, land subsidence, saline intrusion, and pollution, all compounded by climate change and rapid socio-economic transitions. This makes coordinated transboundary management essential for securing its future.
By leveraging science-based assessments, innovative approaches to groundwater management, and inclusive stakeholder engagement, the CMDA project aims to safeguard water security, protect fragile ecosystems, and promote equitable resource use through a gender equality and ethnic minority perspective.

planEntities.description: Smallholder and commercial farmers supported with temporary and fixed grain storage solutions—including sleeves and modular storage units (MSUs)—to mitigate post-harvest losses and restore agricultural value chains in war-affected oblasts of Ukraine. This intervention aimed to address the acute shortage of storage infrastructure caused by the war, which led to a 9% reduction in cultivated grain and oil crop areas nationally

planEntities.name: Smallholder farmers and agri-enterprises in Ukraine are supported with matching grants to restore production, invest in value chains, and enhance resilience through inclusive and climate-smart agriculture.
planEntities.parentName: 2.7 Businesses, entrepreneurs and Agri-food enterprises, especially those led by women, benefit from policies and instruments that increase productivity, innovation, and competitiveness and support integration with EU and global markets
planEntities.description:
FAO, in partnership with the European Union, Italian government, and the Government of Ukraine, launched a multi-cycle grant program to support smallholder farmers and agri-enterprises in war-affected oblasts. Through the State Agrarian Registry (SAR), eligible applicants could access grants of up to USD 10,000 for individual producers and USD 25,000 for micro and small enterprises . The grants were designed as matching investments, requiring a minimum 10% contribution from recipients .

The program prioritized value chains such as fruits, vegetables, berries, beekeeping, wine production, and small ruminants

planEntities.name: Rural households and farmers strengthen technical, entrepreneurial, and financial capacities to improve livelihoods and access value chains.
planEntities.parentName: 2.6 Active labour market measures  are strengthened to increase participation rates of vulnerable groups
planEntities.description:
FAO aims to strengthen gender equality in Ukraine’s agricultural sector through a multi-pronged approach. This includes:

National Advocacy and Community Engagement: FAO will launch a nationwide campaign to improve women’s access to agricultural support, especially in frontline oblasts.

Gender Mainstreaming Trainings: At the request of the Ministry of Agrarian Policy and Food of Ukraine (MAPF), FAO is conducting strategic sessions and workshops to build capacity among policymakers and practitioners. These sessions explore practical tools, challenges, and best practices for integrating gender into agricultural policy.

Country Gender Assessment (CGA): FAO is updating its CGA to reflect the evolving roles of women in agriculture since the full-scale war and displacement began in 2022. The assessment applies an intersectional lens and will offer gender-transformative recommendations to guide future programming and investments. It is scheduled for completion by September 2025.

Gender-Responsive Policy Development: FAO is training at least 40 MAPF staff (with 50% female participation) to enhance gender-sensitive policy formulation and implementation .

Inclusive SAR Registration: FAO is working to identify and address barriers that prevent women—who currently represent less than 5% of registered users—from accessing the State Agrarian Register (SAR). This includes targeted outreach and platform accessibility studies .

Operational Gender Sensitivity: All implementing partners are trained on SEA prevention, GBV principles, and gender-sensitive communication. Project data is disaggregated by sex, and monitoring tools ensure equitable treatment throughout the project cycle .

Field-Level Inclusion: In grain storage operations, FAO prioritized women-led applications and engaged female laborers in post-harvest activities. For example, 65% of laborers hired during the Canadian fiscal year were women

planEntities.name: Forest ecosystems in Ukraine restored and sustainably managed through enhanced governance, policy modernization, and stakeholder engagement, including the establishment of the Forestry Advisory Network (FAN), to improve biodiversity resilience and strengthen the livelihoods of rural communities affected by conflict and climate change
planEntities.parentName: 3.2 State institutions have strengthened legislative and policy frameworks to implement and monitor sustainable practices  in line with circular economy principles (focus:  industrial, water, waste, agriculture, and forestry sectors)
planEntities.description: FAO is implementing a multifaceted forestry intervention in Ukraine that combines ecosystem restoration, policy reform, and institutional capacity building. Central to this effort is the establishment of the Forestry Advisory Network (FAN), a technical body designed to support evidence-based policymaking and alignment with EU forest regulations, including the European Deforestation Regulation (EUDR) . FAN engages national and international experts to advise on sustainable forest management, biodiversity conservation, and forest-based value chains, while also facilitating legislative development and stakeholder consultations . Complementing FAN, FAO’s broader strategy includes restoring war-damaged forests, promoting climate-smart practices, and improving rural livelihoods through inclusive governance and targeted support to forest-dependent communities . Together, these initiatives reinforce Ukraine’s resilience and readiness for EU integration.

Technical and policy support will be provided to help both countries develop effective domestic policies that support the apiculture sector. These efforts will be guided by sustainability principles and aligned with international best practices. Additionally, the initiative will promote ecosystem-based management of living resources ensuring that beekeeping contributes not only to economic development but also to environmental protection and biodiversity.

planEntities.name: War-affected agricultural lands are mapped and people are prioritized for mine action and livelihood support  Prioritization and Mapping of Agricultural Land for Recovery
planEntities.parentName: 2.1 Communities have increased, safe access to their homes, critical infrastructure, and agricultural land through mine action
planEntities.description: FAO applies a standardized methodology to assess and prioritize rural farms and household plots in conflict-affected settlements, in coordination with local authorities and through community consultations. FAO identifies uncontaminated arable land for immediate support and maps hazardous areas for future clearance, ensuring inclusion of the most vulnerable households. This targeting enables the selection of smallholder farmers for livelihood restoration, supports food security, and revitalizes rural economies. It also includes monitoring EO-related damage across affected oblasts, as requested by the Government of Ukraine, to inform evidence-based recovery planning and investment.

planEntities.name: Crisis-affected communities benefit from resource transfers, capacity and skills strengthening, to restore assets for improved livelihoods.
planEntities.parentName: 2.1 Communities have increased, safe access to their homes, critical infrastructure, and agricultural land through mine action
planEntities.description: As land is assessed and cleared for use, targeted smallholder farmers and rural households receive tailored support packages—including cash-based transfers, vouchers, training, and other context-specific assistance—to sustain or resume agricultural and business activities. This integrated support offsets income losses due to reduced productivity and promotes self-sufficiency, reducing reliance on government or humanitarian aid. Livelihood packages are defined through needs assessments and community engagement, ensuring alignment with the UN Food Security Cluster and relevant national agricultural programmes. Linkages with WFP and FAO interventions are explored, with increasing emphasis on product traceability within WFP procurement chains for food assistance in Ukraine and abroad.

planEntities.name: Fisheries policy, research and digital monitoring systems strengthened for sustainable management of aquatic biological resources
planEntities.parentName: 3.2 State institutions have strengthened legislative and policy frameworks to implement and monitor sustainable practices  in line with circular economy principles (focus:  industrial, water, waste, agriculture, and forestry sectors)
planEntities.description: FAO supports the modernization of Ukraine’s fisheries sector by strengthening legal and policy frameworks, scientific research capacity and digital monitoring systems in line with European Union practices and circular economy principles. The support helps state institutions promote the sustainable use of aquatic biological resources, improve evidence-based management, and strengthen transparency, traceability and monitoring across the sector. FAO focuses on supporting fisheries policy reform, applied research, sustainable catch-level assessments, monitoring of fish populations, habitats and environmental conditions, and the further digitalization of fisheries governance through e-Fish. It also contributes to restoring the capacity of national research institutions through equipment, machinery and technical support needed for field expeditions, ecological and biological assessments, and responsible fisheries management. This support strengthens the capacity of the Ministry of Economy, Environment and Agriculture, the State Agency for the Development of Melioration, Fisheries and Food Programs, and national fisheries research institutions to implement and monitor sustainable practices, advance EU-aligned reforms and support long-term recovery of the fisheries sector.

planEntities.name: Digital public goods and agriculture registries strengthened for transparent, EU-aligned service delivery
planEntities.parentName: 3.2 State institutions have strengthened legislative and policy frameworks to implement and monitor sustainable practices  in line with circular economy principles (focus:  industrial, water, waste, agriculture, and forestry sectors)
planEntities.description:
FAO supports the continued digital transformation of Ukraine’s agriculture sector by strengthening the State Agrarian Registry (SAR) and expanding digital public goods for transparent targeting, faster service delivery and EU-aligned governance. SAR remains a core digital entry point for farmers to access state and donor-funded support, building on its role in channelling agricultural assistance and its more than 200 000 registered users.
FAO focuses on the operationalization of the updated SAR, development of geospatial analysis modules and additional sector-specific registers, including the Vineyard–Winery Registry. Support also strengthens data management, mapping, secure exchange with state registers and evidence-based decision-making across the agriculture sector. FAO also works to make SAR more accessible and responsive to women farmers and entrepreneurs, including through inclusive application processes and targeted access to support programmes.

planEntities.description:
Purpose: Strengthen gender-responsive employment systems and improve women’s access to decent work, particularly for vulnerable groups.

Scope: National level institutional support alongside targeted interventions in priority regions (including Kyiv, Bila Tserkva, Dnipro, Kharkiv, Mykolaiv, Zaporizhzhia, Lviv, Kryvyi Rih, Khmelnytskyi, and Cherkasy).

Main activities: Conduct gender audits and provide technical guidance to state institutions to enhance gender-responsive service delivery; and deliver market-relevant re- and upskilling programmes for vulnerable women aligned with labour market demand, including in traditionally male-dominated sectors such as transportation.

Target beneficiaries: Government institutions and vulnerable women across priority regions, particularly those facing barriers to employment.

Expected results: Strengthened institutional capacity to deliver gender-responsive services; increased employability and workforce participation of women; and expanded access to decent work opportunities, including in non-traditional sectors.

planEntities.name: Women entrepreneurs benefit from initiatives and instruments that increase their access to resources, innovation, competitiveness, sustainability and support integration with EU markets
planEntities.parentName: 2.7 Businesses, entrepreneurs and Agri-food enterprises, especially those led by women, benefit from policies and instruments that increase productivity, innovation, and competitiveness and support integration with EU and global markets
planEntities.description:
Purpose: Promote women’s economic empowerment and gender equality in business by strengthening entrepreneurship, improving workplace practices, and generating evidence for responsive policymaking.

Scope: Nationwide, covering women entrepreneurs, public and private sector enterprises, and policy stakeholders across key sectors such as agriculture and energy.

Main activities: Deliver integrated enterprise development support (training, mentorship, networking, advocacy) to help women start and grow businesses; strengthen gender-responsive practices in enterprises through technical guidance and implementation of the Women’s Empowerment Principles (WEPs); and generate evidence on gendered economic challenges (e.g., energy crisis, care burden) and effective approaches to support women’s participation.

Target beneficiaries: Women entrepreneurs and aspiring business owners; public and private sector enterprises; and policymakers and stakeholders using gender data for decision-making.

Expected results: Increased capacity of women to establish and scale sustainable businesses; improved gender equality practices within workplaces and business operations; and enhanced evidence base to inform gender-responsive economic policies and programmes.

planEntities.name: Government institutions at all levels are strengthened to develop, implement, monitor, and coordinate Ukraine’s national and international commitments through gender responsive laws, plans, and budgets, especially to advance recovery and EU accession.
planEntities.parentName: 4.5 State institutions have increased capacity to develop and implement policies and legal frameworks for a gender-responsive and inclusive recovery and reform agenda, in a participatory manner
planEntities.description:
Purpose:
To integrate gender equality into Ukraine’s recovery and EU accession processes by strengthening policies, institutions, coordination, and evidence-based decision-making in line with EU and international standards.
Scope:
National and local levels, engaging key ministries, the national gender machinery, regional/municipal authorities, coordination bodies, and partners including women’s rights organizations (WROs) and development actors.
Main activities:
•	Provide policy advice and technical assistance to embed gender equality in laws, policies, and budgets.
•	Build institutional capacities using gender-responsive tools (analysis, audits, GRB).
•	Facilitate multi-stakeholder coordination and dialogue through formal platforms.
•	Generate and disseminate data and evidence on gender gaps and intersecting discrimination.
Target beneficiaries:
Government institutions (national and subnational), national gender machinery, coordination bodies and indirectly women and girls, especially those facing multiple and intersecting forms of discrimination.
Expected results:
•	Gender-responsive recovery and EU accession frameworks and budgets.
•	Strengthened institutional capacity to apply gender tools.
•	More inclusive and effective coordination mechanisms.
•	Enhanced availability and use of gender data to inform policies and programmes aligned with the EU acquis.

planEntities.name: Women leaders and WROs at all levels have strengthened capacities to express their agency, voice, and leadership to meaningfully engage in decision-making and participate in political life.
planEntities.parentName: 4.4 People, especially women, young people and vulnerable groups, are able to participate meaningfully in decision making and public policy processes
planEntities.description:
Purpose: Strengthen women’s leadership and inclusive participation in decision-making processes at the national and local levels, as well as in processes linked to recovery and EU accession.

Scope: Nationwide, covering national, regional, and local levels, engaging women’s rights organizations (WROs), women leaders, and government counterparts, with a focus on diverse groups facing discrimination.

Main activities: Provide financial and technical support to WROs through the Women, Peace and Humanitarian Fund; deliver leadership training, mentorship, and networking programmes for women (including IDPs, veterans, rural women, and women with disabilities); and convene structured dialogue platforms connecting women leaders, WROs, and government to influence gender-responsive policies and budgets.

Target beneficiaries: WROs and women across Ukraine, especially those facing intersecting forms of discrimination, as well, as government institutions benefiting from more inclusive engagement.

Expected results: Increased leadership capacity and political participation of women; stronger and better-resourced WROs; and more inclusive, gender-responsive decision-making processes and policies aligned with the EU acquis.

planEntities.description:
Purpose: Strengthen women’s participation and leadership in decision-making and security-related sectors by advancing implementation of NAP 1325 and promoting inclusive gender norms. 

 

Scope: National and regional levels, with a focus on priority regions (Kyiv, Kharkiv, Dnipro, Chernihiv, Sumy, Mykolaiv), engaging women, WROs, and key ministries and agencies in social policy, internal affairs, communications, and economic sectors. 

 

Main activities: Provide training, mentorship, and technical support to women and WROs to enhance advocacy and engagement in local decision-making linked to NAP 1325 and recovery plans; strengthen institutional capacity of national and regional authorities through advisory support and gender-responsive tools for effective localization, budgeting, implementation, and monitoring of NAP 1325 and related strategies; and implement research and awareness initiatives to address stereotypes limiting women’s participation in security, defense, and law enforcement. 

 

Target beneficiaries: Women across Ukraine and WROs, particularly in priority regions, as well, as national and regional authorities responsible for implementing NAP 1325 and related policies. 

 

Expected results: Increased capacity of women and WROs to influence decision-making; strengthened institutional capacity to implement the NAP 1325; greater inclusion of women in security and governance sectors; and reduced discriminatory attitudes toward women’s roles.

planEntities.description: UN Women’s CRSV programme in Ukraine strengthens national and community-based CRSV response mechanisms, in line with the 2022 UN–Government Framework of Cooperation. The programme builds institutional capacities of state authorities and civil society, while working with survivor-led networks and women’s CSOs to ensure survivors’ voices drive policy and programme design and implementation. Through psychosocial, legal, and economic support, it helps survivors access justice, rebuild their lives, and contribute to Ukraine’s broader recovery and reconstruction.

planEntities.name: Supporting people living with and affected by HIV (key populations - men who have sex with men (MSM), people who use drugs (PWUD), individuals in closed settings and recently released, and sex workers (SW)) in Ukraine in accessing HIV services during times of crisis
planEntities.parentName: 1.1 Health care services are strengthened to ensure access to quality services including for war-related needs and priorities (inclusive, culturally sensitive, gender and age-appropriate)
planEntities.description: The UNAIDS Humanitarian Programme for Ukraine (2026) aims to ensure continuity of HIV and SRHR services for people living with or at risk of HIV/TB, including targeted support for veterans affected by trauma and substance use, people who use drugs, individuals engaged in chemsex, and people released from prisons, affected by war, displacement, poverty, stigma, substance use and mental health issues and disruption of health and social services. The programme combines humanitarian assistance, shelter support, psychosocial services, and linkage to HIV/SRHR care. By addressing urgent humanitarian needs such as food, hygiene, temporary accommodation, psychosocial support, and restoration of personal documents, the programme will help beneficiaries remain adherent to treatment and engaged in HIV care, while reducing interruptions in ART and other essential services. The programme is expected to provide approximately 60,000 humanitarian service contacts annually, support 1,400 beneficiaries through shelter services, provide food assistance to 20,000 beneficiaries annually, hygiene support to 17,000 beneficiaries, psychosocial support to 7,000 people annually, and referrals to SRH/HIV services for at least 3,000 beneficiaries.

This effort is crucial in supporting Ukraine’s transition to a low-carbon, climate-resilient economy.

RDOs will be further empowered and capacitated to act as focal points for local authority planning and delivery of the early recovery effort.

planEntities.name: Enhanced administrative, emergency, and social service systems strengthen the resilience, safety, and inclusion of war‑affected communities through improved service delivery, accessibility, and institutional capacity.

planEntities.description: UNDP expands support to Administrative Service Centres, emergency responders, police, and social service providers to ensure accessible, integrated, and people‑centred services. Assistance includes infrastructure, equipment, mobile and modular solutions, training on digital and gender‑responsive approaches, and strengthening coordination mechanisms across local and national institutions. These efforts will improve service availability and quality for IDPs, veterans, persons with disabilities, and other affected populations, promoting safe returns, social inclusion, and resilient community‑based support systems.

planEntities.name: People who are most affected by war, including veterans, people with disabilities (PwD), women, the elderly, and others, have access to rehabilitation and social services and economic opportunities to enable them to live a decent life
