planEntities.description: UNDP focuses on ensuring that people most affected by the war gain equitable access to rehabilitation, social services, and economic opportunities that enable them to live dignified and self-sufficient lives. Efforts under this sub-output will strengthen modern, needs‑based rehabilitation and social service approaches to better respond to the physical, psychological, and social challenges experienced by war‑affected populations. This includes promoting inclusive, accessible environments and supporting social inclusion to ensure that women and men, including veterans and their families, can fully participate in community and economic life without barriers.

planEntities.name: Enhanced healthcare and mental health services address the needs of veterans, persons with disabilities, and other war-affected populations
planEntities.parentName: 1.4 People affected by the war on Ukraine enjoy access to safe, inclusive and quality mental health and psycho-social services and care
planEntities.description: UNDP supports local authorities in expanding decentralized health services by strengthening primary health care coverage, community‑level public health systems, home‑based palliative care, and gender‑sensitive service delivery. UNDP will scale integrated palliative care models and inclusive public health approaches that combine medical, psychological, social, and legal support for people affected by the war. UNDP will also expand community capacities to deliver mental health and psychosocial support and continue enhancing rehabilitation services for veterans and civilian war casualties. In addition, the Programme will invest in local medical colleges with equipment and training to address critical workforce shortages and increase the number of qualified nurses, paramedics, and other medical professionals entering the health system.

planEntities.name: Strengthened provision of social services promotes inclusion based on national reform priorities
planEntities.parentName: 2.3 Communities enjoy safe physical environments in which housing, utilities, social and cultural infrastructure are built back better to support psychosocial well-being, livelihoods, production, and economic growth
planEntities.description: UNDP supports local authorities in strengthening community‑based social services by enhancing institutional capacity, improving coordination among administrative, legal, and social functions, and expanding integrated service models tailored to IDPs, persons with disabilities, veterans, and other groups. The Programme will scale multifunctional and mobile service formats, invest in the professional development of frontline social workers, and promote gender‑responsive, trauma‑informed, and veteran‑sensitive approaches to service delivery. UNDP will further expand inclusive social care and supported living models, ensuring improved access to essential services for people with limited mobility and those disproportionately affected by caregiving burdens.

planEntities.name: A conducive environment for recovery and growth is enhanced and labour-force participation and productivity increased
planEntities.parentName: 2.4 The vocational education and training system offers skills demanded by the labour market with a focus on women, young people, veterans, persons with disabilities, IDPs, returnees and the Roma community
planEntities.description: UNDP supports the expansion of livelihood and economic opportunities by promoting entrepreneurship, facilitating access to finance, and providing tailored training and advisory services for veterans, women, youth, persons with disabilities, and other vulnerable groups. The Programme strengthens re‑skilling pathways aligned with labour‑market needs, modernizes vocational education institutions, and enhances the capacity of the State Employment Service to deliver inclusive, gender‑responsive employment services. UNDP also advances veteran economic reintegration through veteran‑friendly business support teams, recognition of prior learning and qualifications, and mentorship and networking opportunities for veteran‑led enterprises. In addition, the Programme promotes local‑level public‑private partnerships by supporting feasibility studies, PPP model development, and catalytic financing to de‑risk private investment in war‑affected communities.

planEntities.name: Human capital development and socio-economic recovery are enhanced.
planEntities.parentName: 2.6 Active labour market measures  are strengthened to increase participation rates of vulnerable groups
planEntities.description: Human capital is strengthened, and socio-economic recovery is enhanced through improved access to quality public services and increased Labour force participation and productivity.

planEntities.name: BIOFIN process implemented to strengthen biodiversity finance planning and mobilization in Ukraine

planEntities.description: UNDP Ukraine supports launching and implementing the full BIOFIN process, including assessments of biodiversity expenditures, financial needs, and appropriate finance solutions. This expansion enables to develop evidence‑based finance plans aligned with global biodiversity commitments. Through knowledge transfer and technical assistance, Ukraine will enhance the capacity to mobilize and manage financing for biodiversity and SDG‑related priorities.

planEntities.name: Community‑led biodiversity and climate initiatives in Ukraine are strengthened through the effective implementation of the GEF Small Grants Programme Operational Phase 8, enhancing local action, governance, and environmental resilience
planEntities.parentName: 3.2 State institutions have strengthened legislative and policy frameworks to implement and monitor sustainable practices  in line with circular economy principles (focus:  industrial, water, waste, agriculture, and forestry sectors)
planEntities.description:
UNDP Ukraine supports civil society organizations, community‑based groups, and Indigenous and local communities to design and implement innovative environmental projects aligned with the GEF Small Grants Programme Operational Phase 8 guidelines, which provide the policy and governance framework for all SGP operations. 
Through capacity development, inclusive decision‑making structures such as National Steering Committees, and clear grant administration procedures, the programme empowers communities to deliver measurable biodiversity, climate, and land‑degradation benefits at the local level. 
This approach strengthens Ukraine’s ability to mobilize community‑driven solutions that contribute to national environmental priorities and GEF‑8 programming objectives

planEntities.name: Ukraine establishes a fully functional and internationally aligned carbon market infrastructure that meets UNFCCC Article 6 requirements and strengthens national systems for transparent, high‑integrity mitigation outcome tracking
planEntities.parentName: 3.2 State institutions have strengthened legislative and policy frameworks to implement and monitor sustainable practices  in line with circular economy principles (focus:  industrial, water, waste, agriculture, and forestry sectors)
planEntities.description: UNDP Ukraine supports the development and operation of the National Carbon Registry, ensuring its integration with core national digital systems to enable secure and transparent Article 6 transactions. The project strengthens institutional capacities to oversee, report, and engage in bilateral cooperation under future carbon market mechanisms. These efforts enhance Ukraine’s readiness for international carbon market participation while upholding robust transparency, environmental integrity, and safeguard standards.

planEntities.name: Local authorities have strengthened their capacity to design, implement, and manage RES sub-projects, contributing to long-term energy sustainability and effective local energy governance.

planEntities.name: Ukrainian municipalities, local public administrations, regional and communal enterprises, village communities and the central governmental bodies of Ukraine, its local state administrations, bodies of local self-government, and state and communal enterprises have strengthened capacities to affect an energy transformation in a gender-responsive way
planEntities.parentName: 3.5 State institutions and the private sector have enhanced capacities to accelerate decentralization and decarbonization of the energy system and implement energy efficiency measures.
planEntities.description: UNDP aims to bolster the resilience, energy efficiency, and operational continuity of Ukraine's district heating sector through a multifaceted approach, leveraging strategic partnerships between UNDP, the European Investment Bank (EIB), Financial Intermediaries, and local municipalities (Final Beneficiaries). This strategic plan focuses on providing the technical assistance necessary to modernize and rehabilitate critical heating assets, ensuring sustainable development and the reliable provision of essential public services in the face of conflict and economic challenges

planEntities.name: Improved legal aid services support safe communities and enable returns
planEntities.parentName: 4.1 The judicial system has strengthened capacities to operate in an independent, impartial and transparent manner
planEntities.description: UNDP supports expanding access to justice as a cornerstone for the recovery and development of war‑affected communities in Ukraine, ensuring people can claim their rights, access compensation, overcome legal barriers to return and reintegration, and benefit from justice reforms linked to EU integration. The Programme focuses on rehabilitating court infrastructure, strengthening court security, and building the capacities of local courts to improve public trust. UNDP also continues its support to the state-run Free Legal Aid System and community paralegals to ensure vulnerable groups receive qualified legal assistance and are informed about their entitlements.

planEntities.name: Community-based reintegration model for veterans is implemented based on national policy and priorities
planEntities.parentName: 4.2 State institutions and communities have increased capacities, tools and knowledge to sustain and enhance trust, social cohesion and cultural fabric and diversity, addressing challenges related to different experiences of the war
planEntities.description: UNDP supports a community‑led and nationally aligned model of veteran reintegration that empowers local authorities, civil society, and veteran groups to design and deliver sustainable, gender-responsive services for veterans and their families. Building on years of partnership with the veteran community and the Ministry for Veterans Affairs, the Project strengthens local capacities, develops data-driven policies, and expands integrated veteran hubs as one‑stop spaces for psychosocial, legal, employment, and reintegration support. Through participatory planning, peer learning, and national‑local coordination, UNDP helps ensure that effective community solutions inform and reinforce the national veteran reintegration ecosystem.

planEntities.name: Veterans, internally displaced persons, women, youth, persons with disabilities, and other vulnerable groups benefit from improved living conditions and strengthened social cohesion

planEntities.description: UNDP supports communities across Ukraine to implement a comprehensive, gender-responsive veteran reintegration model by developing local reintegration plans, strengthening veteran CSOs, establishing Veteran Hubs, and providing policy support to the Ministry of Veterans Affairs. UNDP also empowers civil society, youth, and community groups to lead inclusive recovery through participatory planning, oversight of reforms, community-driven initiatives, and the establishment of sustainable community and youth centres. In addition, UNDP strengthens inter-community solidarity by supporting displaced populations, assisting regional administrations, promoting joint community projects, and generating evidence to enhance social cohesion and integration across regions.

planEntities.name: Communities and civil society across Ukraine are empowered to drive inclusive veteran reintegration, strengthen social cohesion, and support accountable, gender-responsive recovery
planEntities.parentName: 4.2 State institutions and communities have increased capacities, tools and knowledge to sustain and enhance trust, social cohesion and cultural fabric and diversity, addressing challenges related to different experiences of the war
planEntities.description: UNDP strengthens community resilience and social cohesion by supporting locally driven reintegration of veterans, empowering communities to design inclusive programmes, establish Veteran Hubs, and align services with national policies and gender-responsive standards. UNDP enables civil society, youth groups, and community platforms to lead participatory recovery efforts, improve accountability of local reforms, implement community-driven initiatives, and sustain vibrant community and youth centres as hubs for civic engagement and leadership. To foster unity across regions, UNDP supports displaced communities and regional administrations with services, skills and cultural preservation, co-designs inter-community recovery initiatives, and advances evidence-based understanding of social cohesion and vulnerabilities.

planEntities.name: The capacities and knowledge of parliaments are strengthened to enable them to fulfill their  institutional responsibilities and work more effectively in partnership.

planEntities.description: UNDP aims to support the Verkhovna Rada of Ukraine and enhance its legislative and oversight capacities as well as improve institutional coordination with the executive branch. These efforts will contribute to more coherent, inclusive, and accountable governance, ensuring continuity of democratic process and advancing recovery, reform, and long-term sustainable development objectives

planEntities.name: War‑affected communities are equipped with the core capacities needed for data‑driven, well‑coordinated, and investment‑ready recovery aligned with national reforms and EU integration requirements.
planEntities.parentName: 4.5 State institutions have increased capacity to develop and implement policies and legal frameworks for a gender-responsive and inclusive recovery and reform agenda, in a participatory manner
planEntities.description: UNDP supports communities in war‑affected regions to strengthen their capacities across the recovery ecosystem, including data systems, planning, coordination, public investment management, and loan absorption. Through an area‑based approach, the programme helps local authorities lead evidence‑based, participatory recovery processes, backed by improved socio‑economic data, digital tools, and integrated public investment systems. UNDP further enhances the ability of local and regional structures to manage reconstruction funds, prepare high‑quality project documentation, and meet national reform and EU alignment requirements. This support ensures that even the most affected hromadas can effectively plan, finance and implement recovery and development initiatives, while increasing readiness for future investments and financial facilities.

planEntities.name: Infrastructure resilience is strengthened and the delivery of accessible public services is enhacned in targeted communities through support to the proper implementation of EIB-funded Ukraine Recovery Programme, contributing to the restoration of critical infrastructure, economic transformation and maintenance of social fabric in war-affected regions
planEntities.parentName: 3.5 State institutions and the private sector have enhanced capacities to accelerate decentralization and decarbonization of the energy system and implement energy efficiency measures.
planEntities.description: UNDP provides comprehensive technical assistance to advance infrastructure recovery sub-projects in target communities across Ukraine, working in close coordination with the European Investment Bank, MDCT, Ministry of Finance, subnational authorities, and local stakeholders.

planEntities.name: Strengthened capacity of the healthcare facilities to serve the increasing needs of the war-affected population in Ukraine
planEntities.parentName: 2.3 Communities enjoy safe physical environments in which housing, utilities, social and cultural infrastructure are built back better to support psychosocial well-being, livelihoods, production, and economic growth
planEntities.description: The project will strengthen the capacity of health authorities and service providers to deliver accessible, inclusive, and responsive ophthalmic healthcare services for conflict-affected communities by assessing institutional needs, defining priority interventions, and establishing a structured implementation framework. It will support the procurement of specialized ophthalmic equipment and provide targeted training for healthcare practitioners to enhance the quality of care through gender-sensitive and inclusive service delivery approaches.

planEntities.name: Public finance institutions increasingly design and implement gender-responsive and inclusive fiscal policies, supported by strengthened institutional capacities, evidence-based decision-making, and reform processes that advance gender equality, women’s economic empowerment, and the development of inclusive care systems.
planEntities.parentName: 2.5 Authorities at national and local levels and the private sector have increased capacity to promote women’s access to decent work, equal pay, family care services, and productive assets.
planEntities.description: The EQUANOMICS project supports the Government of Ukraine in advancing gender-responsive public finance reforms by strengthening the integration of gender equality considerations into fiscal policy, taxation, public expenditure, and debt management. Through targeted technical assistance, evidence generation, and policy dialogue, the project aims to promote women’s economic empowerment, reduce economic and gender inequalities, and align public finance systems with national gender equality priorities.

planEntities.name: National and subnational institutions in Ukraine effectively prevent and respond to conflict-related sexual violence (CRSV) through strengthened leadership, coordinated implementation of policies and frameworks, institutionalized survivor-centered capacities, and expanded access to inclusive services for survivors.
planEntities.parentName: 4.1 The judicial system has strengthened capacities to operate in an independent, impartial and transparent manner
planEntities.description: The project aims to strengthen the capacity of national institutions to prevent and respond to CRSV through a coordinated, survivor-centred, and gender-sensitive approach. It will support the operationalization of national policies and coordination mechanisms, enhance institutional capacities of justice and security actors, and strengthen referral pathways and service provision systems to ensure accessible, quality assistance for survivors.

planEntities.name: National law-enforcement and justice institutions are better equipped, skilled, and coordinated to respond to the needs of returned children in a human-centred, gender-sensitive, trauma-informed, and sustainable manner, reducing risks of re-traumatisation while improving protection and accountability outcomes.
planEntities.parentName: 4.1 The judicial system has strengthened capacities to operate in an independent, impartial and transparent manner
planEntities.description: The project is designed to strengthen Ukraine’s national capacity to safely identify, reunify, and support children who have been deported or forcibly transferred as a result of the war. It focuses on reinforcing the role of national law-enforcement and justice institutions as first responders and coordinators in child return and accountability processes.

planEntities.name: National stakeholders’ capacities and partnerships are strengthened to advance electoral preparedness and position a coordinated, well-informed framework for future electoral assistance in Ukraine.
planEntities.parentName: 4.5 State institutions have increased capacity to develop and implement policies and legal frameworks for a gender-responsive and inclusive recovery and reform agenda, in a participatory manner
planEntities.description:
The project responds to this emerging policy and institutional landscape by supporting early analytical, coordination, and resource mobilization efforts required for future electoral assistance. It is firmly 
aligned with Ukraine’s national recovery and development priorities, which emphasize resilience, institutional strengthening, and progress toward EU accession. Conducting elections in line with EU democratic standards will be a key milestone in Ukraine’s accession process and requires early alignment of legislation, institutional arrangements, and operational capacities with the EU acquis.

planEntities.description: Evaluate several PPP and infrastructure projects at various implementation stages with the active engagement of public officials in Ukraine using the PIERS methodology. The projects will be selected in consultation with public officials, in priority sectors. The evaluations will assess whether the selected projects are aligned with the SDGs with the aim of improving their performance before and during implementation. planEntities.name: Capacity strengthened for the management of waste and hazardous waste in Ukraine, including asbestos-containing debris.
planEntities.parentName: 3.2 State institutions have strengthened legislative and policy frameworks to implement and monitor sustainable practices  in line with circular economy principles (focus:  industrial, water, waste, agriculture, and forestry sectors)
planEntities.description: Specialized training, technical guidance, and targeted support enhanced Ukraine’s overall waste management capacity, including asbestos-containing debris. Initiatives included asbestos management training for the State Emergency Service (SESU), a feasibility study for establishing a national waste management association, and measures to ensure the safe and effective management of asbestos-contaminated debris through adaptation of analytical standards, evaluation of laboratory capabilities, determination of optimal handling approaches, strengthening of legal frameworks, and increased public and institutional awareness. These efforts collectively improve safe collection, handling, and disposal practices, protecting public health and reducing long-term environmental risks.

planEntities.name: Capacity enhanced for monitoring and assessment of war-related environmental impacts in Ukraine
planEntities.parentName: 3.3 State institutions have increased capacities to generate and analyse disaggregated data and to report on environmental sustainability, climate change, disaster risk reduction and energy efficiency
planEntities.description:
This sub-output strengthens monitoring, documentation, and assessment of war-related environmental impacts in Ukraine to inform recovery and policy. It combines visual media—photographs, videos, and interviews—with statistical data on ecosystem degradation, resource loss, and infrastructure damage, providing qualitative and quantitative evidence to raise awareness and mobilize international support.

Systematic monitoring frameworks track impacts on ecosystems, air, water, and soils, while data are consolidated through the ECODOZOR platform to support response measures and green recovery planning. The initiative advances practical environmental standards for sustainable mine action, undertakes a targeted assessment of selected war-impacted sites in Kyiv oblast, and generates policy-relevant data on the Black Sea and coastal areas to inform national recovery strategies, including the Green Recovery Platform.

planEntities.name: Platform for Action on the Green Recovery of Ukraine developed
planEntities.parentName: 3.1 State institutions have capacities to design and implement effective and sustainable financial mechanisms for an inclusive green recovery
planEntities.description: The Platform for Action on the Green Recovery of Ukraine serves as a high-level international initiative bringing together the Ukrainian government, international organizations, and development partners. Through this platform, comprehensive technical support will be provided for screening preparation, including legal approximation assessments, institutional capacity analysis, and the preparation of documentation required under Chapter 27 of the EU–Ukraine accession negotiations. Another key focus of the initiative is to explore and enhance the integration of Ukrainian veterans into the green labour market by assessing the current landscape of green jobs, identifying opportunities and barriers to their participation, and developing actionable recommendations to support their transition. In parallel, the platform seeks to empower children and youth as active contributors to environmental protection and Ukraine’s green recovery, combining creative expression with practical capacity-building to foster engagement and sustainable impact.

planEntities.name: Sustainable Energy solutions advanced for Ukraine
planEntities.parentName: 3.5 State institutions and the private sector have enhanced capacities to accelerate decentralization and decarbonization of the energy system and implement energy efficiency measures.
planEntities.description: The main objective of this initiative is to empower Ukraine and Ukrainian cities to harness its sustainable energy potential by developing and implementing integrated energy systems tailored to the country's unique circumstances, fostering investment and accelerating the deployment of innovative energy solutions across the nation.

planEntities.name: Enhanced protected areas network for biodiversity conservation and development
planEntities.parentName: 3.4 State institutions have stronger policy and legal frameworks and implementation capacities for effective environmental governance and DRR strategies and plans that are gender-sensitive and inclusive
planEntities.description: This sub-output strengthens Ukraine’s protected areas network to support biodiversity conservation and sustainable development.

planEntities.name: Integrating Biodiversity Conservation into Upstream Planning of Linear Transport Infrastructure in Ukraine
planEntities.parentName: 3.4 State institutions have stronger policy and legal frameworks and implementation capacities for effective environmental governance and DRR strategies and plans that are gender-sensitive and inclusive
planEntities.description: This sub-output supports the integration of biodiversity conservation into the planning of linear transport infrastructure in Ukraine.

Ukraine.organizationType: Multilateral - UN organizations excluding pooled funds

planEntities.name: Preserving documentary heritage at risk in Ukraine, in particular Jewish documentary heritage, honouring collective memory, enhancing knowledge and access to archives while promoting intercultural dialogue
planEntities.parentName: 4.2 State institutions and communities have increased capacities, tools and knowledge to sustain and enhance trust, social cohesion and cultural fabric and diversity, addressing challenges related to different experiences of the war
planEntities.description: This sub-output is linked to two projects: "Preserving Ukraine’s Jewish documentary heritage, honouring collective memory, enhancing knowledge and access to archives while promoting intercultural dialogue" and "Preservation and digitization of documentary heritage at risk in Ukraine". The projects will support the promotion of access to and protection of documentary heritage in Ukraine, including through digitization. The first project is specifically dedicated to the preservation of the cultural and documentary heritage of the Jewish community in Ukraine as a key source of prevention of anti-Semitism, education about the Holocaust and genocides, and strengthening respect for human rights. The first project also aims to facilitate access to this heritage and aims to raise awareness of Jewish cultural heritage in Ukraine. Thus, the main objective of the activities carried out under this project is to preserve and ensure access to the Jewish cultural and documentary heritage, while promoting the recognition of such cultural heritage and its valuable contribution to the diversity of expression and the history of Ukraine.

planEntities.name: Strengthening the resilience of Ukrainian learners through living heritage and inclusive education
planEntities.parentName: 1.3 The education system is strengthened to offer safe and inclusive lifelong learning opportunities for individual empowerment and participation in Ukraine’s recovery
planEntities.description:
This sub-output is linked to two projects "Supporting the resilience of Ukrainian school children through enhancing awareness of their living heritage. Phase II: Preparing for the scaling up at the country level" (implemented under HEF),  and "Pushing the Boundaries: Cultivating Inclusion in Ukrainian UNESCO Associated Schools" (implemented under Participation Program). 
Under these projects it is planned:
1.100 teacher-trainers, from 60 schools in different parts of Ukraine will be trained and will implement small pilot projects in their schools. Furthermore, an existing online platform will be identified in consultation with local partners and adapted for the needs of primary and secondary school teachers. The platform in Ukrainian will become a ‘one-stop-shop’ with all the information needed to teach about and with living heritage in Ukraine, including links to other resources, such as e.g. the UNESCO Clearinghouse on ICH and Education.
2. Present the learning strategies of four Ukrainian Learning Cities to demonstrate how inclusive, community-driven education planning empowers both youth and adults to contribute meaningfully to resilience, reconstruction, and social cohesion.

planEntities.name: Supporting urgent needs of media professionals to promote Freedom of Expression and Safety of Journalists in Ukraine
planEntities.parentName: 4.2 State institutions and communities have increased capacities, tools and knowledge to sustain and enhance trust, social cohesion and cultural fabric and diversity, addressing challenges related to different experiences of the war
planEntities.description:
This sub-output is linked to three projects: 1. "Supporting urgent needs to promote Safety of Journalists and Freedom of Expression in Ukraine" (implemented with the support from Japan), 2. "Emergency support to journalists in Ukraine", and "Fostering MIL capacities of youth in Ukraine". These projects will contribute to the following outcomes:
1. The safety of Ukrainian and international journalists on-and offline in Ukraine is reinforced, with a gender-responsive focus on protection, psychological support and capacity-building.
2. Ukrainian media outlets and journalists continue their operations within Ukraine providing conflict-sensitive and gender-sensitive reporting with improved digital safety and enhanced media and information literacy skills.
3. Independent and investigative reporting in view of recovery and judicial and historical reprocessing as well as an independent judicial sector in line with international standards is strengthened.
4. The media and information literacy of Ukrainians, especially young people, is strengthened, including literacy in the field of artificial intelligence and fact-checking.

planEntities.name: Promoting Inclusion and Gender Equality in the Ukrainian Media Environment
planEntities.parentName: 4.4 People, especially women, young people and vulnerable groups, are able to participate meaningfully in decision making and public policy processes
planEntities.description: This sub-output is related to two projects: "Media without barriers: inclusivity solution for the Ukrainian media environment" (implemented by Hromadske Radio), "The power of gender diversity"(implemented by Media Center UA). The projects aims to strengthen Ukrainian media capacity to ensure inclusion, equality and non-discrimination in the media. The activities will include research and analysys, training, and guiding materials development. The projects will be guided by the principles of diversity, gender equality and social inclusion, with a strong focus on women and war-affected media professionals with disabilities among the target audience.

planEntities.name: Culture for Peace and Resilience: Creation of a Culture Hub in Lviv
planEntities.parentName: 4.2 State institutions and communities have increased capacities, tools and knowledge to sustain and enhance trust, social cohesion and cultural fabric and diversity, addressing challenges related to different experiences of the war
planEntities.description: The project envisages the creation of a Culture Hub in L'viv, Ukraine, make it sustainable and operational, as well as run a series of pilot activities to strengthen the capacity of government actors at all levels, communities, stakeholders and professionals in the cultural and creative industries. The Culture Hub will be a unique venue, conceptualized to serve as a centre of excellence for capacity-building in the field of culture and cultural policy research. It will serve also as a platform to demonstrate the role of culture as a source of resilience and recovery for the communities, in line with the strategic vision of the Ukraine's National Recovery Plan.

planEntities.name: Preserving cultural heritage in Ukraine: Reinforcing monitoring, emergency response and preparedness at damaged cultural and natural heritage sites in Ukraine, including the World Heritage property ‘The Historic Centre of Odesa’
planEntities.parentName: 2.3 Communities enjoy safe physical environments in which housing, utilities, social and cultural infrastructure are built back better to support psychosocial well-being, livelihoods, production, and economic growth
planEntities.description: The main purpose of the project is to enable the people of Ukraine, including cultural heritage professionals and volunteers, to reinforce the protection of cultural heritage through systematic monitoring and assessment of damage, as well as effective emergency response, in the context of increasing damage to cultural heritage, while integrating the protection of cultural heritage into recovery plans.

planEntities.name: Supporting the digital transformation of Ukraine in the field of culture
planEntities.parentName: 4.2 State institutions and communities have increased capacities, tools and knowledge to sustain and enhance trust, social cohesion and cultural fabric and diversity, addressing challenges related to different experiences of the war
planEntities.description:
"Supporting the digital transformation of Ukraine in the field of culture
This sub-output is linked to two projects: 1. ""Supporting the digital transformation of Ukraine in the field of culture (phases I & II, funded by the UNESCO Heritage Emergency Fund-HEF) and 2. ""Advancing Digital Integration: Enhancing Ukraine's State Register of Movable Properties through Museum Digitization" (funded by the Government of Flanders). The project aims to safeguard Ukraine's movable cultural heritage during the war and establish sustainable management. By digitizing and standardizing inventory processes, it will improve accessibility, interoperability with government databases, and align with international digital heritage standards. "

planEntities.name: Integrating culture into socio-economic recovery plans and raising public awareness
planEntities.parentName: 4.2 State institutions and communities have increased capacities, tools and knowledge to sustain and enhance trust, social cohesion and cultural fabric and diversity, addressing challenges related to different experiences of the war
planEntities.description: This component, implemented under the Special Account for Post-Crisis Situations Response Activities in and for Ukraine (PCPD), supports initiatives led by the UNESCO Antenna in Ukraine that reinforce the role of culture in socio-economic resilience and post-war recovery. It supports strengthening the managerial capacities of cultural institutions through the dedicated programme in cooperation with the Kyiv School of Economics, and aligning Ukrainian legislation on cultural property with EU standards, as part of Ukraine's EU accession process. The component also promotes gender equality as a contribution to recovery, by enhancing the professional capacities of Ukrainian female artists and cultural professionals and supporting their access to national and international platforms, including through support for the Women in Arts Award in partnership with UN Women.

planEntities.name: Strengthening resilience of education system in Ukraine in emergencies
planEntities.parentName: 1.3 The education system is strengthened to offer safe and inclusive lifelong learning opportunities for individual empowerment and participation in Ukraine’s recovery
planEntities.description: This project contributes to strengthening the resilience of national education system through policy formulation, specialized technical assistance, capacity development, relevant training for education professionals, and equipment provision to enhance Ukraine's capacity to effectively respond to urgent needs and lay a strong foundation for the recovery of the education sector.

planEntities.name: Strengthening Physical Safety in Educational Institutions
planEntities.parentName: 1.3 The education system is strengthened to offer safe and inclusive lifelong learning opportunities for individual empowerment and participation in Ukraine’s recovery
planEntities.description:
The primary goal of the project is to strengthen the resilience of Ukraine’s education system by rehabilitating damaged educational infrastructure, particularly 18 kindergartens, and ensuring safe, inclusive, and quality face-to-face education for children amidst the ongoing war:  
- Rehabilitate Infrastructure: Restore damaged and destroyed kindergarten infrastructure in prioritised regions based on detailed needs and structural assessments to facilitate safe learning environments. 
- Equip Safe Classrooms: Procure and install necessary furniture and equipment to create secure and functional classrooms and campuses for in-person education. 
- Enhance Shelters: Build or improve shelters in kindergartens to meet government safety requirements, increasing the capacity for face-to-face education and ensuring a secure, inclusive learning environment. 
- Support Winterization: Provide heating and insulation for kindergartens and shelters to ensure year-round usability and comfort. 
- Ensure Accessibility and WASH Facilities: Install facilities for people with disabilities and provide water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) infrastructure in kindergartens and shelters to promote inclusivity.

planEntities.name: Preserving the Crimean Tatar language and supporting its youngest learners
planEntities.parentName: 1.3 The education system is strengthened to offer safe and inclusive lifelong learning opportunities for individual empowerment and participation in Ukraine’s recovery
planEntities.description:
The multimedia project BULBUL aims to preserve the Crimean Tatar language and provide support to its youngest learners. The expected result is original 10 animated 2D cartoons, 10 audio stories, and 10 songs. This content is based on traditional symbols, images, and national music. 

Project Goals:
1. Educate children about the traditions and culture of Crimean Tatars.
2. Support preschoolers in learning the Crimean Tatar language through engaging cartoons.
3. Foster the development of speech and fine motor skills by incorporating fingerplay and interactive elements into the cartoons.
4. Cultivate emotional intelligence by using the mother tongue to name feelings and encourage dialogue that teaches how to express emotions effectively.
5. Enrich children's sensory experience through immersive experiences.
6. Expand the viewers' Crimean Tatar vocabulary through accompanying flash cards, activity sheets, and a collection of children’s songs.

planEntities.name: Supporting Ukraine's education sector by mitigating the negative consequences of war
planEntities.parentName: 1.3 The education system is strengthened to offer safe and inclusive lifelong learning opportunities for individual empowerment and participation in Ukraine’s recovery
planEntities.description: The project aims to mitigate the adverse impact of war on the mental health of the Ukrainian educational community through policy transformation, capacity building of key education stakeholders, and improvement of mental health and psychosocial support services (MHPSS), as well as enhancing the safety and inclusivity of Ukrainian educational institutions.

planEntities.name: Addressing the long-term impacts of the Kakhovka Dam destruction on water resources management options
planEntities.parentName: 3.3 State institutions have increased capacities to generate and analyse disaggregated data and to report on environmental sustainability, climate change, disaster risk reduction and energy efficiency
planEntities.description: The project aims to develop a rapid water security assessment, including a mapping of local water resources, and assess the long-term impacts of Kakhovka Dam destruction in freshwater systems and ecosystems. Further, the project aims to identify potential adaptation actions through the tailored application of UNESCO’s acknowledged Climate Risk Informed Decision Analysis (CRIDA).

planEntities.name: Introducing Action plan for Ukraine Scientific sector
planEntities.parentName: 4.2 State institutions and communities have increased capacities, tools and knowledge to sustain and enhance trust, social cohesion and cultural fabric and diversity, addressing challenges related to different experiences of the war
planEntities.description: Under this sub-output UNESCO will implement a number of measures under the Action plan for Ukraine Scientific sector, including conducting high-level science event in Kyiv to present Action plan for Ukraine Scientific sector. The project aims to support the stabilization and resilience of Ukraine’s scientific system in response to the severe disruptions caused by the ongoing war. Building on UNESCO’s Action Plan for Science and evidence gathered through studies on the impact of the war on Ukrainian researchers and research institutions, the project will provide rapid support to scientists through remote access to advanced research infrastructures under the UNESCO Remote Access to Lab Equipment (UNESRALE) initiative, strengthen international research collaboration through cooperation with laboratories, research institutions and other stakeholders globally, in particular with the Port of Antwerp-Bruges, APEC and the broader Flemish innovation ecosystem, including the engagement of Flemish universities and research institutions, upgrade marine water monitoring laboratories in line with Ukraine’s recovery and EU accession priorities, and establish a multi-stakeholder coordination platform through the Ukrainian Scientific Forum to support evidence-based policymaking, reform development, and the long-term recovery of Ukraine’s science, research and innovation ecosystem.

planEntities.name: Introducing the Artificial Intelligence Readiness Assessment Methodology (RAM) and follow-up activities in Ukraine
planEntities.parentName: 4.5 State institutions have increased capacity to develop and implement policies and legal frameworks for a gender-responsive and inclusive recovery and reform agenda, in a participatory manner
planEntities.description: The project is designed to assist countries around the world to translate the Recommendation into national institutional and regulatory frameworks and to build a national consensus on the shared vision for AI. Through this project, PMCG applies UNESCO’s Readiness Assessment Methodology (RAM) to evaluate Ukraine's preparedness for the ethical and responsible use of AI. The assessment examines legal and regulatory frameworks, technical infrastructure, economic and scientific capacity, educational readiness, and the social and cultural context. It identifies opportunities, gaps, and priority reforms to guide a comprehensive, ethical national AI strategy. Implementation of follow-up activities including training and capacity building in AI for key stakeholders is also planned under the project.

planEntities.name: Enhancing Resilience, Wellbeing and Viability of Ukrainian Media Professionals at Wartime contributing to sustainable recovery
planEntities.parentName: 4.2 State institutions and communities have increased capacities, tools and knowledge to sustain and enhance trust, social cohesion and cultural fabric and diversity, addressing challenges related to different experiences of the war
planEntities.description:
This sub-output is linked to four projects: 1."Recovery Window Media Network: supporting media viability and peer-to-peer learning"; 2."Resilience and Wellbeing of Ukrainian Media Professionals at Wartime"; 3."Media Recovery and Research: Strengthening Ukraine’s Independent Journalism for Sustainable Reconstruction"; 4. "Kyiv Media Hub — Professional Resilience, Peer Learning and Community Building"; 5. "Kyiv Media Hub — Professional Resilience, Peer Learning and Community Building".
The first project implemented by NGO Eastern Vairant to support the viability of media outlets in Ukraine. The second project implemented by NGO Social Perspective addresses the urgent need to strengthen the resilience, empowerment, and professional capacity of Ukrainian journalists and media professionals, particularly women and persons with disabilities affected by Russia’s armed aggression. Under the third project, UNESCO, in partnership with Lviv Media Forum, will conduct an activity to support recovery of the Ukrainian media sector. Building on data from the RDNA4, regular research will be conducted to update damage, loss, and recovery needs, ensuring an evidence-based approach to media reconstruction. Based on identified needs, the project will provide targeted capacity-building programs for local and regional independent media, including financial sustainability training, journalism education, and strategies for audience engagement. Additionally, it will facilitate knowledge-sharing between Ukrainian and international media experts to strengthen the sector’s role in promoting transparency in the recovery process. The fourth project implemented in cooperation with Media in Cooperation and Transition (MiCT) will support operations of Kyiv Media Hub as a safe and fully equipped workspace for Ukrainian and international journalists at the same time delivering  practical capacity-building sessions on media viability, digital security, AI for journalism, investigative reporting, cross-border cooperation, and mental health.

Ultimately, the projects will contribute to a more resilient, inclusive, and gender-equal media environment in Ukraine, strengthening journalists as agents of positive change during wartime and in post-war recovery.

planEntities.name: Emergency protection of cultural heritage in Ukraine
planEntities.parentName: 2.3 Communities enjoy safe physical environments in which housing, utilities, social and cultural infrastructure are built back better to support psychosocial well-being, livelihoods, production, and economic growth
planEntities.description: The war in Ukraine has had massive repercussions on the Ukrainian cultural and creative industries. According to the National Council for the Recovery of Ukraine, State and local funding for culture has been drastically reduced, notably causing a brain drain. This sub-output is linked to three projects: 1. "Emergency protection of cultural heritage" (implemented under UNESCO Special Account); 2. "Enhancing urgent protective measures for Odesa historic sites and Viazivka Church in Zhytomyr Oblast"  (implemented under UNESCO Heritage Emergency Fund); 3. Restoration of the monumental painting of Saint-Sophia Cathedral (implemented under  World Heritage Fund). The projects focus on the implementation of urgent protection, key emergency interventions, stabilization works and studies for cultural heritage preservation, meant to support urgent actions that might emerge to ensure timely protection of cultural heritage, access and re-functionalization of cultural heritage properties by users and communities.

planEntities.name: Strengthening safeguarding and preparedness measures for the Odesa Archaeological Museum
planEntities.parentName: 4.2 State institutions and communities have increased capacities, tools and knowledge to sustain and enhance trust, social cohesion and cultural fabric and diversity, addressing challenges related to different experiences of the war
planEntities.description: The project is implemented with the support of UNESCO Goodwill Ambassador Marc Ladreit de Lacharrière to improve the conservation of Odesa’s archaeological museum collections. Under the first phase of the project, UNESCO supported the updating of inventories, digitization of its collections strengthening security protocols and strengthening capacities of youth to support the museum in the digitization process. In addition, UNESCO is also supporting the museum in the procurement of storage equipment to further strengthen their storage systems. Building on the first phase, the second phase is structured around additional conservation measures and educational outreach:  essential conservation measures to ensure the protection and longevity of the stone sculptures located in the courtyard, including conducting condition assessments, implement preventive conservation interventions, and arrange an appropriate storage and display solution to safeguard the sculptures from environmental damage. The establishment of a storage area will improve the organization, protection, and accessibility of the sculptures for future research, exhibition, and conservation work; educational programme designed specifically for young audiences, with the aim to foster greater awareness and appreciation of cultural heritage by engaging youth through interactive learning, guided visits, workshops, and interpretive materials. By creating accessible and dynamic educational experiences, the programme will encourage younger generations to connect with the historical and artistic significance of the site while promoting long-term stewardship of cultural heritage.

planEntities.name: The Hague Convention of 1954 and its Protocols: opportunities for use and promotion
planEntities.parentName: 4.4 People, especially women, young people and vulnerable groups, are able to participate meaningfully in decision making and public policy processes
planEntities.description: The project will familiarise Ukrainian citizens with the basic principles of protecting cultural property and combating illicit trafficking in cultural property in times of war and to develop and implement information materials (videos) for different target audiences on international standards and best practices in the implementation of the Convention and its two Protocols.

planEntities.name: Guiding Human Rights and Social Engagement through Arts and Humanities
planEntities.parentName: 4.2 State institutions and communities have increased capacities, tools and knowledge to sustain and enhance trust, social cohesion and cultural fabric and diversity, addressing challenges related to different experiences of the war
planEntities.description: This sub-output is linked to the project "Art-Lab Ukraine Phase II: Guide for Human Rights and Social Engagement through Arts & Humanities and Establishment of a Culture & Human Rights Cohort". Following Phase I of the activity concluded in 2024 with the support of Spain, and building on a UNESCO-supported report which revealed the urgent need to strengthen the cultural sector’s capacity to promote cultural rights and social transformation, the present Phase II funded by the HEF aims to a) establish a Culture and Human Rights Cohort composed of five NGOs that will be trained on Human Rights Based Approach (HRBA) principles and receive support for their own HRBA-based activities; and b) produce a Guide for Human Rights and Social Engagement through Arts & Humanities offering strategies for cultural actors to integrate HRBA principles and promote cultural rights, inclusivity, and resilience, to be accompanied by targeted communication and advocacy campaigns to amplify impact.

planEntities.name: Providing regular water quality testing in educational institutions in Mykolaiv
planEntities.parentName: 1.7 People have increased access to equitable and safely managed water, sanitation, and hygiene services
planEntities.description: The project aims to conduct official laboratory water quality testing every two weeks in 42 educational institutions in Mykolaiv City and provide reports with results and recommendations to local authorities.

planEntities.name: Safeguarding Independent Media and Information Integrity in Ukraine: Emergency Response and Sustainable Recovery
planEntities.parentName: 4.2 State institutions and communities have increased capacities, tools and knowledge to sustain and enhance trust, social cohesion and cultural fabric and diversity, addressing challenges related to different experiences of the war
planEntities.description:
The main goal of this project is to support new critical and emerging needs in the fields of safety of journalists, media viability, and access to trustworthy information in Ukraine – including on recovery efforts. Beyond the tragic loss of life, the war continues to destroy media infrastructure, disrupt income sources, affect journalists’ livelihoods and equipment, and cause staffing shortages. Many journalists have been displaced, and media professionals, especially women, are dealing with gender-based threats, both online and offline. To address the urgent needs identified, work will be conducted under the following three outcomes: 
Outcome 1: The safety and resilience of journalists, media workers, and freedom-of-expression defenders are strengthened through emergency assistance, psychological support, with a strong gender-sensitive approach.
Outcome 2: The viability of Ukrainian media outlets is advanced through support for sustainable business models development and tailored audience outreach.
Outcome 3: Access to reliable information is reinforced through the promotion of international standards on freedom of expression, information integrity, and enhanced media and information literacy, with a particular emphasis on civil servants and judicial actors.

By continuing supporting the safety of journalists and the recovery of the media sector, the project will help ensure that the Ukrainian people receive reliable information in the times of war.

planEntities.name: Creating Safe, Supportive and Inclusive Education Environment in Ukraine
planEntities.parentName: 1.3 The education system is strengthened to offer safe and inclusive lifelong learning opportunities for individual empowerment and participation in Ukraine’s recovery
planEntities.description: The proposed project aims to mitigate these adverse mental health outcomes in the Ukrainian education community by transforming policies, building the capabilities of key educational stakeholders, and improving Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS) services through enhanced safety and inclusivity in educational institutions. This project builds on UNESCO's existing efforts to transform MHPSS in the education sector. Specifically, this project aims to contribute to further MHPSS policy reform; train education actors from various sectors on concepts and interventions on inclusive and trauma-informed MHPSS provision and the creation of a safe and inclusive education environment for children and young people in communities, strengthening capacity of education institutions and Inclusive Resource Centers (IRCs).

planEntities.name: Enhancing protection of cultural heritage in Ukraine: from emergency response to recovery
planEntities.parentName: 2.3 Communities enjoy safe physical environments in which housing, utilities, social and cultural infrastructure are built back better to support psychosocial well-being, livelihoods, production, and economic growth
planEntities.description: This sub-output aims to support the safeguarding of Ukraine’s cultural heritage in the context of the ongoing war by addressing urgent protection needs and ensuring that culture and heritage are systematically integrated into recovery planning processes. It will support the systematic monitoring and verification of war-related damage to cultural heritage, including World Heritage properties, through remote and satellite imagery analysis complemented by field verification, and will enable timely emergency stabilization and repair interventions at war-damaged cultural properties to prevent further deterioration. In parallel, the project will support the development and promotion of policy guidance, planning tools, and regulatory frameworks to ensure that cultural heritage and the culture sector are effectively reflected in national and local recovery and reconstruction frameworks.

planEntities.name: Implementing emergency measures at Khortytsia National Reserve
planEntities.parentName: 2.3 Communities enjoy safe physical environments in which housing, utilities, social and cultural infrastructure are built back better to support psychosocial well-being, livelihoods, production, and economic growth
planEntities.description: The project aims at supporting the safeguarding of the Khortytsia National Reserve in Zaporizhzhia oblast, one of Ukraine’s most significant cultural and natural heritage sites affected by the war and the destruction of the Kakhovka Dam. The project will support urgent repairs to museum facilities, expansion of climate-controlled storage for rescued artefacts, archaeological rescue missions and ecological monitoring of the island. The initiative also includes capacity-building activities for Ukrainian professionals through apprenticeships, university partnerships, and specialized cooperation with the Vasa Museum (Sweden) in the field of underwater archaeology and conservation, contributing to the long-term preservation and recovery of Ukraine’s cultural heritage.

planEntities.name: Fostering social cohesion and community recovery through cultural exchanges and support to the literature sector in Ukraine
planEntities.parentName: 4.2 State institutions and communities have increased capacities, tools and knowledge to sustain and enhance trust, social cohesion and cultural fabric and diversity, addressing challenges related to different experiences of the war
planEntities.description: The project aims to foster social cohesion and community recovery through culture by strengthening literary cooperation between Ukraine and Flanders and expanding access to books, libraries and culture for communities affected by the ongoing war. The initiative combines international literary exchange with culture-based recovery actions. Planned activities include a Ukrainian–Flemish literary translation and professional exchange programme; the organization of Crossroads literary events in Brussels; a literary residency at Passa Porta for two Ukrainian authors; a creative recovery programme for veterans; and a pilot initiative to expand access to books, literary activities and library services in frontline and war-affected communities through mobile library and literary outreach activities. Together, these interventions aim to strengthen professional networks, promote contemporary Ukrainian literature internationally, enhance the role of libraries as inclusive community spaces, and support social cohesion, well-being and community resilience through culture.

planEntities.name: Strengthening the fight against illicit trafficking of Ukrainian cultural property through a data-driven approach

planEntities.description: Upon the request of the Ukrainian authorities, this project aims to strengthen baseline data, address the most urgent needs of archaeological sites and museums in the frontline areas, and improve the clarity and comprehensiveness of information on online trafficking trends in the context of the ongoing war. planEntities.name: Supporting reform of the MHPSS system in the education sector of Ukraine
planEntities.parentName: 1.3 The education system is strengthened to offer safe and inclusive lifelong learning opportunities for individual empowerment and participation in Ukraine’s recovery
planEntities.description: Sweden's contribution will enable UNESCO to support the ongoing reform of the mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS) system in Ukraine's education sector over the next three years. UNESCO is a key partner of the Ministry of Education and Science of Ukraine in advancing this reform, which aims to ensure that mental health and psychosocial support is fully integrated into the education system. The reform will strengthen support for both learners and educators, establish a clear referral system, and ensure that school psychologists receive high quality pre service and in service training, professional supervision, career development opportunities, and continued professional support. The contribution will also allow UNESCO to engage technical experts to develop the comprehensive normative framework, policy instruments, implementation guidelines, and technical documentation needed to institutionalize and sustain the reform.

planEntities.description:
This UN Interagency Project operational since 2023 till mid 2026 is co-implemented by UNFPA, UNODC, UN Women, WHO, UNDP and IOM in cooperation with Government Commissioner for Gender Equality Policy of Ukraine (project’s beneficiary) and Deputy Prime Minister’s Office for European and Euro-Atlantic Integration of Ukraine to address the gaps, challenges and needs pertinent to CRSV identified jointly with the Government of Ukraine and civil society.
Coordination with five other UN agencies and government counterparts is ensured by UNFPA (as the project lead) to align CRSV response interventions; service mapping and needs assessments are conducted; response actors (inclduing state and non-state healthcare, social, GBV specialized, civil servants) are capacitated through offline and online tailored CRSV training jointly with designated government institutions; the online psychotherapeutic support platform for CRSV survivors is strengthened; a rehabilitation programme for female survivors and their families is available, with pre-, during- and post-programme case management support (in-person and online); high-level advocacy amplifies survivor voices and awareness-raising among affected population improved; legal reform is advanced through support to the adoption of thematic legislation; and survivor-led groups and local CSOs are engaged in programme design, implementation, and oversight.

planEntities.name: The Ukrainian health system has updated, harmonized, evidence-based, inclusive and human centred healthcare policies aligned with national recovery goals.
planEntities.parentName: 1.1 Health care services are strengthened to ensure access to quality services including for war-related needs and priorities (inclusive, culturally sensitive, gender and age-appropriate)
planEntities.description:
Working at the national and local levels under the Policy output, the programme will strengthen sector governance which has children’s interests and needs at its core and complies with EU standards. UNICEF’s policy advice and technical assistance will focus on strengthening policy and regulatory frameworks, compliance mechanisms and technical capacities and providing data and evidence for evidence-based planning and management of HC sector, including in humanitarian contexts. In partnership with key central healthcare institutions, UNICEF will work towards the following systemic changes: 

National regulatory framework (including guidelines and standards) is harmonized and used for provision of inclusive, human-centered, gender-transformative quality integrated maternal, newborn, child health and developmental services. 

National EPI system functions based on updated policies, includes new vaccines, and improves vaccine forecasting and procurement supported by regularly monitoring of the stock levels. 

Health system has unified functional MIS producing quality data and evidence that is used for decision making process at central and decentralized levels (to improve access and quality of MHC services, development of continuous improvement plans (CIP) for effective vaccine management (EVM), forecasting and monitoring of immunization).

planEntities.name: Healthcare system at national and sub-national level has strengthened capacities to deliver life-cycle appropriate quality, accessible and equitable health, immunization, nutrition, development, PMTCT, perinatal care and MHPSS services, especially for the most vulnerable.
planEntities.parentName: 1.1 Health care services are strengthened to ensure access to quality services including for war-related needs and priorities (inclusive, culturally sensitive, gender and age-appropriate)
planEntities.description:
Under the Programme output, UNICEF will deliver direct support, life-saving supplies and services and rehabilitation of facilities to affected populations while providing technical assistance and policy advice to build national and local capacities for efficient and equitable integrated MNCHN, immunization and MHPSS services to safeguard children's health and wellbeing, especially in humanitarian contexts. Working mostly at decentralized level, UNICEF will strive to achieve the following systemic changes: 

Health care facilities, supported by local authorities, especially in the frontline and those affected by war/emergencies are equipped to provide safe and quality human-centered, MNCHN/MHPSS services through facility-based and home-based services. 

Health facilities have appropriate storage conditions to provide safe and quality immunization services. 

Health workers have enhanced skills and knowledge to ensure provision of continuous quality of MNCHN/MHPSS and immunization services. 

Resilient community-based and outpatient services are available at the local authorities - hromada (community), level to provide essential cross-sectoral rehabilitation services to vulnerable children, especially those in humanitarian contexts. 

Ministry of Digital transformation has scalable, evidence-based model solutions to improve peer mental health services for young people.

planEntities.name: Communities, families, young people and caregivers of children have strengthened capacities to transform gender and social norms and are empowered to seek and utilize quality human-centred health, immunization, nutrition, development, HIV, MHPSS and perinatal care services and implement nurturing care practices.
planEntities.parentName: 1.1 Health care services are strengthened to ensure access to quality services including for war-related needs and priorities (inclusive, culturally sensitive, gender and age-appropriate)
planEntities.description:
UNICEF will provide technical assistance, policy advice and advocacy to rights-holders and duty-bearers to foster age-appropriate and gender-transformative capacities, knowledge, practices and behaviors on MNCHN, nutrition, HIV and mental health, foster nurturing care and parenting and empower children and young people, their families, communities and caregivers to uphold children’s right for health, especially for children affected by humanitarian contexts. 

The output will be implemented primarily at the local level with national outreach and scalability and will contribute to the following systemic changes: 

There is a comprehensive parenting system to ensure improvement of Parents/caregivers demand for and engagement in early health and development of young children. 

Parents caregivers and adolescents have increased knowledge and engagement leading them to adopt healthy behaviors and practices related to people centered MNCHN/MHPSS and seek adequate MNCHN/MHPSS and immunization services.
