planEntities.parentName: 1.3 The education system is strengthened to offer safe and inclusive lifelong learning opportunities for individual empowerment and participation in Ukraine’s recovery
planEntities.description:
The national-level interventions under the Policy output will address systemic inefficiencies causing inadequate quality and access of education for all children, especially the most vulnerable, including those affected by humanitarian contexts. The output will foster resilient, inclusive and gender-transformative educational policies, standards and frameworks, supported by quality disaggregated data and evidence on early childhood, primary and secondary education/vocational education and training, and strengthened digital learning ecosystems anchored in UNICEF’s normative agenda for the protection of children’s rights. 

UNICEF will provide technical assistance, policy and advocacy support work to key educational institutions at national and local levels to achieve the following systemic changes: 

Education system has an enabling normative framework for inclusive ECE services (Policy, curriculum framework, minimum quality service standards), which are accountable to the communities they serve. 

The education system is strengthened to provide learning recovery programmes that enable students to catch-up with learning losses and continue formal education.  

Effective system for provision of additional support measures for children with disabilities to facilitate their transition from institutions and inclusion in mainstream schools. 

Knowledge, Attitude, beliefs and behaviour data on student learning and skills development, inclusive education, positive parenting is available and used to inform an equity-driven roll-out of the New Ukrainian School curriculum reform, including the equitable child-focused education recovery plans and budgeting.  

Education system is strengthened to provide for continuity of learning during humanitarian crises. 

General Secondary Schools curricula & assessment frameworks comprehensively address/integrate transferable skills. 

Comprehensive & transparent education data systems are available to inform equity-based decision making at school, hromada, oblast (region) and national levels for implementation of the learning recovery plan and for monitoring and assessment of students learning. 

There is an enabling national-level coordination framework and strategy, aligned with EU systems, to facilitate young people’s transition from school to work.

planEntities.name: Education service providers have strengthened capacities to deliver effective education and training opportunities which foster children's well-being
planEntities.parentName: 1.3 The education system is strengthened to offer safe and inclusive lifelong learning opportunities for individual empowerment and participation in Ukraine’s recovery
planEntities.description:
Working with authorities and education service providers primarily at local level, the output will tackle the gaps in the access and quality of educational services which affect learning and skills development, especially for vulnerable children, including those affected by humanitarian contexts. Through technical assistance, modelling, capacity building and direct support and financing for the delivery of supplies and rehabilitation, UNICEF will support the delivery of comprehensive programmes and service packages, strengthening local education systems’ capacities, mechanisms and structures at central and local levels that respond to humanitarian and long-term recovery needs to achieve the following systemic changes:
•	Cost-effective, inclusive early childhood education models are available for implementation in diverse community settings.
•	There is a scalable model supporting young people's transition from learning pathways to first job experiences.
•	Student learning support services are integrated within the General Secondary Education system, providing adaptive remedial education interventions at scale.
•	Teacher training service providers are able to deliver on inclusive education reform.
•	A safe and inclusive digital learning environment supports children, including adolescents, acquisition of learning and skills, including climate action and environmental sustainability.
•	Safe and inclusive learning environments are accessible for conflict affected children.
•	Career-guidance systems within formal and non-formal education and training services (formal and alternative learning pathways) are labour market-informed, stigma-free and gender transformative and facilitate young people's transition from learning to earning.
•	Demonstration of youth skills development approaches within human capital development priority for Ukraine's recovery plan.
•	Increased opportunities for children and youth to choose their preferred career path within Ukraine.

planEntities.name: Children and young people, their caregivers, and communities, especially the most vulnerable, have strengthened capacities and motivation to practice positive parenting and nurturing care and utilise inclusive education and training services.
planEntities.parentName: 1.3 The education system is strengthened to offer safe and inclusive lifelong learning opportunities for individual empowerment and participation in Ukraine’s recovery
planEntities.description:
This output addresses harmful social, cultural and gender norms that perpetuate discrimination, exclusion and vulnerability of children and limit their meaningful participation in learning. Through technical assistance, SBC and advocacy UNICEF will promote the uptake of positive social, cultural and gender norms and practices and foster participation of children, young people, their families and communities in decision-making to uphold children’s and adolescents’ right to education and employment.
•	There is a comprehensive parenting support system to ensure improvement of parents/ caregivers' awareness, demand for and engagement in children's stimulation and learning.
•	There is a community-based demand and support for inclusive education services to support the successful implementation of the Government's Better Care reform efforts. 
•	There is a decrease in the stigma towards children with disabilities in education institutions and communities.
•	There is an increased support within families and communities for children and youth to choose their preferred career path within Ukraine.
•	There is an increased awareness around and demand for stigma-free, gender-transformative and labour-market informed career choices for young people.

planEntities.name: Institutional capacities are strengthened to reform, adopt and implement legislative, regulatory, budgetary and coordination frameworks that enable a quality, risk-informed, age-appropriate, gender-transformative inclusive and shock-responsive child protection system, especially for vulnerable groups.
planEntities.parentName: 4.5 State institutions have increased capacity to develop and implement policies and legal frameworks for a gender-responsive and inclusive recovery and reform agenda, in a participatory manner
planEntities.description:
The national-level interventions under the Policy output will address the systemic gaps and inefficiencies that prevent the child protection system from protecting the Ukrainian children, especially the most vulnerable, including those affected by humanitarian contexts. The outcome will focus on supporting the care reform, fostering mechanisms and policies for child-centered justice and protection and mobilizing partnerships and finance for children to uphold children’s rights in line with UNICEF’s normative agenda. Working with the key state institutions at the national and local levels, UNICEF will spearhead high level policy dialogues and provide technical assistance, policy and advocacy support, evidence generation and knowledge sharing, as well as capacity development to achieve the following systemic changes:
•	There is a nationally owned reform strategy and plan for child protection sector reform that is supported by and contributes to humanitarian response, recovery, reconstruction, return and reintegration. 
•	Data and evidence is available to inform child protection and justice sector reforms, policies and programmes and guide Programmes and People agendas.
•	Justice system is equipped with child-centered specialized justice professionals, legislation and referral  and is aligned with the EU standards to protect children in contact with the law.
•	There are frameworks and regulations for effective and shock responsive CPiE and GBViE, including MHPSS and case management, at national and sub-national levels.
•	Monitoring and Reporting Mechanisms are available to inform advocacy/dialogues on grave violations of children’s rights, including the right for family in line with the EU standards.

planEntities.name: National and local institutional and community capacities are strengthened to provide quality risk- informed, gender-transformative inclusive and shock-responsive child protection and social services for vulnerable children
planEntities.parentName: 4.5 State institutions have increased capacity to develop and implement policies and legal frameworks for a gender-responsive and inclusive recovery and reform agenda, in a participatory manner
planEntities.description:
Through the Programme output, UNICEF will work to close the gaps in service provision and strengthen institutional and community capacities for the delivery of quality, gender- and shock-responsive child protection services and monitoring children’s rights especially for children affected by armed conflict and other humanitarian contexts. Focusing on the implementation of decentralized scalable demonstration models, capacity strengthening, advocacy and policy advice, the output will be implemented primarily at the local level with national outreach and scalability on aim at the following systemic changes:
•	There are tested scalable models for the provision of continuum of care, ECI and support to CwD, their parents/caregivers and service frontline workers.
•	There is an improved availability and state capacity to undertake regular monitoring of children in family-based alternative care.
•	There are established operational mechanisms and packages for the implementation of Minimum Integrated Social Service and Benefits package, including diverse specialized services such as CPiE and GBViE, return and reintegration, children in contact with law, MHPSS and resilience services and the like.

planEntities.name: Girls, boys, women, families and communities have increased knowledge and capacities to adopt inclusive, gender-sensitive and stigma-free practices and demand child protection and social services, especially for the most vulnerable.
planEntities.parentName: 1.6 Participatory mechanisms that guide social services and protection systems are strengthened to enhance the voice of rights holders, especially from vulnerable groups, and the accountabilities of duty bearers
planEntities.description:
Under the People output UNICEF will work with the rights-holders and duty-bearers to address harmful social and cultural norms and practices and stigma. UNICEF will combine technical assistance, funding, advocacy support, knowledge and evidence generation and best practices with mass communication, advocacy campaigns and SBC to increase participation and engagement of parents and caregivers, children and adolescents and national and local authorities in upholding children’s rights and interests and seeking child-centered services. The output will also be implemented at the local level with national outreach and scalability and will contribute to the following systemic changes:
•	There is a package of evidence and guidance to address the prevailing social norms, practices and beliefs normalising violence against girls, boys, and women (VAGBAW) and institutional care and to monitor grave violations of children’s rights.
•	There is a comprehensive parenting services/system for improved engagement in positive nurturing care.
•	Parental knowledge and skills on positive parenting practices are improved and there is an increased culture of respect and trust in children.
•	There is an increased knowledge among children and families on available child protection services and how to seek and access them.

planEntities.name: The WASH sector has strengthened capacities to develop and manage evidence-based policies, budgets and programmes for affordable, sustainable, inclusive, and shock-resilient services, that factor in the needs of children and support recovery goals.
planEntities.parentName: 1.7 People have increased access to equitable and safely managed water, sanitation, and hygiene services
planEntities.description:
Through national-level interventions under this Policy output, the strengthen the WASH sector governance which has children’s interests and needs at its core and complies with EU standards.  UNICEF will generate and share evidence, knowledge and best practices, provide technical assistance, direct investments and capacity building support to strengthen policy and regulatory frameworks, compliance mechanisms and technical capacities and providing data and evidence for evidence-based planning and management of WSS sector, especially during humanitarian crises. The output aims to achieve the following systemic changes:
•	Data and evidence are available to inform and contribute to national recovery and sector policies.
•	Regulatory and governance frameworks are conducive for the provision of quality, resilient, safe and equitable water supply, wastewater treatment and sanitation services compliant with EU standards and mainstreaming children’s interests and needs, based on scalable pilots.
•	There are technically sound policies and capacities, which are conducive to efficiently funded and monitored WASH/IPC in health and education facilities to ensure safe and healthy care and environment for children.
•	Disaster risk preparedness and child focus are prominent in climate resilience plans and policies (across Environment, WASH, Health, Education sectors).

planEntities.name: Local governments, utilities, educational and health-care institutions have increased capacities to provide quality and sustainable WASH services to vulnerable children and communities.
planEntities.parentName: 1.7 People have increased access to equitable and safely managed water, sanitation, and hygiene services
planEntities.description:
This Programme output delivers direct support and life-saving supplies and services to affected populations while building national and local capacities for efficient and equitable WASH services, response to climate change and environmental sustainability and equipping institutions with capacities and infrastructure to safeguard children's health and wellbeing, especially in humanitarian contexts. Under this output, UNICEF will provide evidence-based policy advice, technical assistance and modeling as well as direct support and financial assistance at central and decentralized levels to achieve the following systemic changes:
•	Innovative pilots for the provision of quality and equitable water supply services are implemented and available for scaling up.
•	National and local capacities are enhanced for efficient and equitable management of wastewater treatment, sanitation and water supply services empowering children with a safe environment, including in humanitarian contexts. 
•	Key institutions for children have child-friendly, disability-inclusive and gender-responsive WASH infrastructure with appropriate maintenance in the long-term.
•	National and local capacities are enhanced for efficient and equitable response to climate change and environmental sustainability to safeguard children's health and wellbeing.

planEntities.name: Children, adolescents, their caregivers and communities have developed age-appropriate and gender-responsive WASH knowledge and practices promoting climate action, sustainable development, and resilience to disasters and shocks.
planEntities.parentName: 1.7 People have increased access to equitable and safely managed water, sanitation, and hygiene services
planEntities.description:
The People output aims to foster age-appropriate and gender-responsive WASH knowledge, behaviors and positive practices for climate action, sustainable development, and resilience to disasters and shocks and encourage participation of children, young people, their families and communities in decision-making to uphold children’s rights. Implemented primarily at the local level with national outreach and scalability the output will deliver technical assistance, evidence and know-how, cocreate platforms and education and communication tools to foster behavioral change at the community level towards the following systemic changes:
•	Families, youth and communities are equipped with knowledge and awareness, to demand and adhere to social accountability frameworks for safe drinking water supply services and are better informed, prepared and adequately supported to cope with the effects of climate change and environmental shocks.
•	There is Increased awareness and adherence to social and behavioural norms, such as enhanced recycling and environmental consciousness, resulting in a more responsible approach to addressing sewage, solid waste and wastewater impacts for the safety of children/families.
•	Children and practitioners are better informed about positive WASH-related beliefs and behaviours, including in humanitarian contexts and in response to disease outbreaks, enabling them to and make healthier choices for improved well-being.

planEntities.name: Government has strengthened capacity to reform, adopt and coordinate effective, inclusive, participatory and sustainable shock-responsive social protection policies and budgets for vulnerable children, young people and families.
planEntities.parentName: 1.2 People have access to more cohesive, equitable, and shock responsive social protection and care systems that are inclusive and that respond to life cycle vulnerabilities and covariate shocks, including through digital service delivery
planEntities.description:
Through national-level interventions under this Policy output, the programme will focus on systemic inefficiencies that contribute to poverty and vulnerability of Ukrainian children and young people, especially those affected by humanitarian contexts. The programme will focus on strengthening of the Social Protection System of Ukraine, by fostering family-friendly policies, standards and frameworks, supported by quality disaggregated data and evidence on multidimensional and monetary child poverty and sustained by child-centered private and public finance, anchored in UNICEF’s normative agenda for the protection of children’s rights. Working with the key state institutions at the national level, UNICEF will provide technical assistance, policy and advocacy support, evidence generation and capacity development to achieve the following systemic changes:
•	There is quality disaggregated data on monetary and multi-dimensional child poverty and deprivations to inform and advocate for child-friendly policies, prioritize children in national budgets and enact and implement inclusive and gender-transformative social protection in Ukraine.
•	The Government is able to draft and enact relevant legislation in line with the EU Chapter on Social Policy, develop flexible and shock-responsive financial mechanisms and operational guidelines for the expansion of SP programmes during the transition phase, design SP programmes that contribute to poverty reduction and an inclusive socio-economic recovery agenda and adopt family friendly policies enabling caregivers to participate in the labour market and contribute to economic recovery while ensuring children’s wellbeing and care.
•	Key financial decision-makers are prepared to prioritize children’s needs, include child-sensitive programmes in national and local budgets and external contributions and make sufficient and sustainable contributions to a child-centred recovery agenda.
•	Interinstitutional coordination is improved for a more effective use of resources within the SPS and with the humanitarian system.
•	Effective and sustainable standards and policies (e.g., youth guarantee, digital MOYS platform, etc.) are available and financed to increase young people’s meaningful participation in line with EU youth strategy.

planEntities.name: National and local authorities have strengthened capacities for enhanced delivery of quality, shock-responsive, inclusive, participatory and gender-transformative social protection services for children, young people and their families.
planEntities.parentName: 1.2 People have access to more cohesive, equitable, and shock responsive social protection and care systems that are inclusive and that respond to life cycle vulnerabilities and covariate shocks, including through digital service delivery
planEntities.description:
Working at the national and sub-national levels, the output will address the gaps in the access and quality of social services that affect quality of life and exacerbate poverty and vulnerability. In partnership with the national and local authorities, the Programme will focus on improving the delivery of comprehensive programmes and services at central and local levels that respond to humanitarian and long-term recovery needs by strengthening local social protection capacities, mechanisms and structures while delivering essential social assistance. Through the provision of technical assistance and operational support, capacity strengthening, and advocacy support the Programme will ensure the following systemic changes:
•	The Government has increased capacities to operationalize and manage improved social protection programmes that effectively contribute to reduce poverty, integrate and support vulnerable populations (displaced/returnee, Roma) in a gender-responsive and age-appropriate manner, prevent de-institutionalization, and respond to humanitarian crises.
•	Local authorities have improved capacities to plan, finance, implement and monitor child-sensitive, gender-responsive and age-appropriate integrated programmes and have effective and sustainable standards and scalable models for young people’s meaningful participation anchored in the national youth policy and EU youth strategy.
•	The Social Protection System and humanitarian cash actors have enhanced delivery mechanisms at their disposal to provide flexible and shock-effective social assistance during humanitarian emergencies.

planEntities.name: National and local authorities have strengthened capacity to develop, collect, monitor and use child-centered data and evidence at national and local levels.
planEntities.parentName: 1.5 Social sector ministries and sub-national authorities have improved capacity to develop and implement evidence-driven frameworks and gender responsive plans and budgets
planEntities.description:
Under this Output UNICEF will work towards the following systemic changes:
•	National and local statistical institutions have increased capacity to regularly produce child-related data and evidence including updated SDG data.
•	Improved quality and availability of statistics and evidence on children to inform child-friendly policies and improve evidence-based decision making, investments and accountability.
The output will address the bottlenecks and barriers related to the still prevalent lack of quality data, due to limited capacity to collect and analyze data at all levels and due to the lack of sufficient data interoperability and exchange among data-producing entities. There is also insufficient capacity to design evidence-based policies and limited effectiveness and efficiency of national and local coordination and monitoring mechanisms for children's rights, that prevent policy makers from fostering data-driven and inter-sectoral approaches in addressing the needs of children and advocating for child-centered policies in compliance with children’s rights. It will do so through technical assistance, capacity building and advocacy to improve skills for child-related data collection, evidence generation and analysis by national stakeholders and use of data and evidence in decision making. It will design this work based on capacity assessments and develop capacity building activities at all levels, in conjunction with planned national evaluation capacity development (NECD) work, to strengthen the ability of national and local institutions to generate and use timely, disaggregated data and evidence. UNICEF also plans to improve availability of recent data on children through support to conduct a MICS, to provide a large household-level dataset which will include internationally comparable estimates of about 130 indicators to assess the situation of children, women and men in the areas of health, education, and child protection. MICS also collects information on about 40 SDG indicators so is a central component to monitoring of SDGs around children. Finally, UNICEF will support a Situation Analysis for Children in preparation for the next country programme cycle, with the aim for joint management and national ownership.

planEntities.name: Ukrainian authorities have strengthened capacities to develop, coordinate and manage a comprehensive, cross-sectoral monitoring system to uphold children’s rights
planEntities.parentName: 1.5 Social sector ministries and sub-national authorities have improved capacity to develop and implement evidence-driven frameworks and gender responsive plans and budgets
planEntities.description:
Under this Output, UNICEF will work towards the following systemic changes:
•	Nationally owned CRM system to coordinate cross-sectoral monitoring of child rights to ensure children's interests and rights are protected and objectively reflected in decision-making and investments. 
•	Improved skills for evidence-based decision-making investments and independent child rights monitoring.
It will do so through advocacy to establish and strengthen coordination and monitoring mechanisms at national and local levels, and technical assistance to develop frameworks, guidance, standards, tools and standard operating procedures for the cross-sectoral monitoring mechanism. The presence of a fully functional CRM coordinating and monitoring mechanism is key to ensure fulfillment of obligations to implement CRC concluding observations and recommendations. UNICEF will work with government partners to both advocate for establishing and operationalizing the committee and to provide technical assistance to capacitate the committee including standards setting and guidance. The programme will support strengthening of national and local-level capacities and mechanisms for child-rights monitoring and coordination to help the country comply with the CRC recommendations and foster child-centered development.
For both outputs, UNICEF recognizes and supports the need for increased awareness and capacity of rights holders and duty bearers to uphold children’s rights and ensure their realization. This recognizes the role that different segments of society play to ensure the realization of child rights, whether it is the commitment to uphold children’s rights, or the promise to advocate and hold rights holders to account for monitoring and implementing these rights. UNICEF will work across its capacities in child rights monitoring, social and behavior change and communications and advocacy to ensure a coordinated approach to this work.
The outcome operates under the assumption that the achievement of the results will be conditional on the regular production of child-related data by the State Statistics Service, including production of SDG data and updating of the TransMonEE database. It’s also contingent on the commitment of the government to maintain the harmonized/cross-sectoral child-related data management system and to establish and maintain a national CRM system at all levels. Risks specific to this outcome include de-prioritization of evidence and statistics functions within the limited fiscal space and resulting lack of adequate buy-in and resourcing in data and evidence systems. Other risks are that the constraints on statistical functions related to martial law impact the conduct of household surveys such as MICS.

Ukraine.organizationType: Multilateral - UN organizations excluding pooled funds

planEntities.name: The reconstruction and development of industrial sectors in Ukraine is supported by fostering digital transformation and the innovation ecosystem
planEntities.parentName: 2.7 Businesses, entrepreneurs and Agri-food enterprises, especially those led by women, benefit from policies and instruments that increase productivity, innovation, and competitiveness and support integration with EU and global markets
planEntities.description: To support the reconstruction and development of industrial sectors in Ukraine, the central objective of the project is to enhance the economic competitiveness of priority industrial sectors by fostering digital transformation and strengthening the innovation ecosystem. The project objectives are aligned with the Digital Europe Programme and reflect the needs and priorities of the Ministry of Economy, Environment and Agriculture of Ukraine and the Ministry of Digital Transformation of Ukraine, as articulated to UNIDO.

planEntities.name: Green industrial recovery is fostered through municipality-based development
planEntities.parentName: 2.2 Policy frameworks, regulations and implementation capacities at national and local levels are strengthened to rehabilitate critical infrastructure damaged as a consequence of the war (energy, heating, transport, telecoms and other sectors)
planEntities.description:
In 2023, UNIDO received funding from the Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development of Germany to implement the project “Industrial capacity-building, policy advice and diagnostics for the green recovery of Ukraine”. The overall objective of the project was to provide technical support to the Government of Ukraine in conceptualising and operationalising a strategic approach to green industrial reconstruction and development through a coherent, evidence-based and results-oriented green industrial recovery programme.

This project represents a spin-off initiative that builds on earlier results by promoting a municipality-based approach to green recovery.

planEntities.name: Women and youth entrepreneurship is promoted in western Ukraine
planEntities.parentName: 2.4 The vocational education and training system offers skills demanded by the labour market with a focus on women, young people, veterans, persons with disabilities, IDPs, returnees and the Roma community
planEntities.description:
The ongoing war in Ukraine has had a disproportionate impact on vulnerable communities, including youth, women and internally displaced persons. Economic disruption, combined with large-scale internal displacement and refugee flows, has resulted in significant declines in employment and household incomes.

Within the framework of UNIDO’s green industrial recovery programme for Ukraine 2024-2028, the project aims to foster self-employment opportunities for youth and women in a selected oblast of western Ukraine. It seeks to increase economic engagement and income-generating opportunities through targeted technical support at the meso and micro levels, thereby contributing to inclusive and resilient local economic recovery.

planEntities.name: Green industrial recovery is facilitated through technology transfer from and co-creation of new businesses with Japan's private industries
planEntities.parentName: 2.7 Businesses, entrepreneurs and Agri-food enterprises, especially those led by women, benefit from policies and instruments that increase productivity, innovation, and competitiveness and support integration with EU and global markets
planEntities.description: This large-scale project, funded by the Government of Japan, supports the green industrial recovery of Ukraine by promoting technology transfer from Japanese private industries and the co-creation of innovative businesses between Ukrainian and Japanese partners. It facilitates collaboration across a wide range of industrial sectors, including agribusiness, circular economy, digital technologies, sustainable energy, hydrogen, and micro, small and medium-sized enterprise productivity enhancement. Through skills development, knowledge transfer and dedicated grant and matchmaking mechanisms, the project fosters the creation of new businesses, job creation and the development of a national innovation ecosystem, thereby contributing to inclusive and sustainable industrial development in Ukraine.

planEntities.name: The quality infrastructure and standards compliance are strengthened in the berries and nuts industry
planEntities.parentName: 2.7 Businesses, entrepreneurs and Agri-food enterprises, especially those led by women, benefit from policies and instruments that increase productivity, innovation, and competitiveness and support integration with EU and global markets
planEntities.description: The overall objective of the project is to promote Ukraine’s economic development through integration into regional and global trade by strengthening the national quality infrastructure system serving the berries and nuts value chains and by enhancing the competitiveness of micro, small and medium-sized enterprises in meeting market requirements. The project also supports strategic activities in the wood sector to ensure the effective completion of support provided under the first phase of the project.

planEntities.name: The concept of eco-industrial parks is promoted and institutionalized in Ukraine
planEntities.parentName: 3.2 State institutions have strengthened legislative and policy frameworks to implement and monitor sustainable practices  in line with circular economy principles (focus:  industrial, water, waste, agriculture, and forestry sectors)
planEntities.description: Under the second phase of the Global Eco-Industrial Park Programme, implementation of tailored eco-industrial park country-level interventions will be continued. The interventions deliver two main outcomes. First, eco-industrial parks are incentivised and mainstreamed in relevant policies and regulations, leading to an increased role of eco-industrial parks in environmental, industrial and other related national policies. Second, eco-industrial park opportunities are identified and implementation is initiated, with environmental, economic and social benefits achieved by enterprises being demonstrated and confirmed.

planEntities.name: Investment is facilitated to scale up innovative cleantech solutions for low-carbon economy and climate action
planEntities.parentName: 3.5 State institutions and the private sector have enhanced capacities to accelerate decentralization and decarbonization of the energy system and implement energy efficiency measures.
planEntities.description: The main objective of the project is to accelerate investments in and uptake of low-carbon and clean technologies in Ukraine by supporting the development of innovative green financial and market mechanisms for start-ups and small and medium-sized enterprises. The project promotes the transformation of early-stage cleantech solutions into commercially viable products and services, mobilises investment for piloting and scale-up, and strengthens the national cleantech innovation and entrepreneurship ecosystem through policy support, institutional capacity-building and dedicated acceleration and post-acceleration services.

planEntities.name: The environmentally sound management and final disposal of polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs) is advanced in Ukraine
planEntities.parentName: 3.2 State institutions have strengthened legislative and policy frameworks to implement and monitor sustainable practices  in line with circular economy principles (focus:  industrial, water, waste, agriculture, and forestry sectors)
planEntities.description: The project establishes an environmentally sound management system for polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs), strengthens compliance with PCB-related obligations under the Stockholm Convention and promotes the local application of non-combustion technologies for the disposal of 3,000 tonnes of PCB-contaminated equipment.

planEntities.name: Energy management system standards are introduced in Ukraine's industry
planEntities.parentName: 3.5 State institutions and the private sector have enhanced capacities to accelerate decentralization and decarbonization of the energy system and implement energy efficiency measures.
planEntities.description: The project supports the Government of Ukraine’s efforts to mitigate climate change by promoting energy efficiency in industry through the systematic introduction of energy management systems in line with the international standard ISO 50001. It strengthens national policies, institutions and technical capacities to enable enterprises to reduce energy consumption, lower greenhouse gas emissions and improve competitiveness. The project focuses in particular on energy-intensive industrial sectors, supports the development of monitoring, reporting and verification systems and facilitates the uptake of best available technologies and practices, thereby contributing to long-term decarbonisation of the Ukrainian economy.

planEntities.name: Circular economy and pollution reduction are fostered in the Eastern Partnership countries
planEntities.parentName: 3.2 State institutions have strengthened legislative and policy frameworks to implement and monitor sustainable practices  in line with circular economy principles (focus:  industrial, water, waste, agriculture, and forestry sectors)

planEntities.name: Implementation of the Biosafety Mechanism in Uzbekistan in accordance with the Cartagena Protocol
planEntities.parentName: Strengthened national and local capacities and enhanced policy and regulatory frameworks for sustainable, integrated management of agrifood systems, cultural and natural resources and biodiversity.
planEntities.description:
The export-oriented and industrialization centered agricultural strategy of Uzbekistan favors a limited number of standard and uniform varieties of fruits and vegetables. Along with threats posed by climate change and land degradation, it puts traditional local varieties at risk of disappearance. While gaps in the identification and monitoring of the components of agrobiodiversity used on-farm limit their potential for conservation and sustainable use. Altogether, this threatens national food sovereignty, food security and rural livelihood and disrupts the climate change adaptation potential the diversity of local varieties represents.

Following the same chain of thought, it is essential for the country to implement the Cartagena Protocol on Biosafety at the national level. The Cartagena protocol aims to protect biological diversity from the potential risks posed by living-modified organisms (LMOs) resulting from modern biotechnology. The potential risks include transgene flow to wild relatives, loss of genetic diversity, invasiveness, changes in agricultural practice that may be unsustainable, and changes in ecosystem landscape and functions, among others, the preservation and maintenance of local and wild varieties not only important nationally but also globally.

planEntities.name: Regional analysis and evidence for migration policy to improve the effectiveness of humanitarian and development efforts on migration and human mobility, collect and analyze information on human mobility in, to and from the country, and to contribute to evidence-based humanitarian and development programming in Uzbekistan.
planEntities.parentName: Strengthened, responsive national and local governance systems that leverage data-driven decision making to serve all people with a long-term impact.
planEntities.description:
Regional Evidence for Migration Analysis and Policy (REMAP) project was developed in response to the critical need to collect and analyze information on (protracted) displacement and human mobility in, to and from Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Pakistan, Tajikistan and Uzbekistan and to contribute to evidence-based humanitarian and development programming in these countries and in the region. The data collected will serve as a foundation for determining the numbers, locations, vulnerabilities, and basic needs of diverse mobile populations, which encompass internal and international migrants, Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs), returnees, and host communities within the target countries. This information will be invaluable for informing future humanitarian and development planning and policy. 

REMAP’s overall objective is to improve the effectiveness of humanitarian and development efforts on migration and displacement in Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Pakistan, Tajikistan, and Uzbekistan. To achieve this, it harnesses the Displacement/ Mobility Tracking Matrix (DTM/MTM) developed by the International Organization for Migration (IOM), a proven system that has been successfully employed in more than 121 countries since 2004 for tracking and monitoring displacement and population mobility. By deploying the MTM as its primary data collection methodology, the current project strives to advance the comprehension of displacement, migration, and return dynamics in the target countries. Furthermore, it seeks to promote regional interoperability and harmonization of displacement, and population mobility data collection initiatives as well as improve the generation, utilization, and management of such data.

planEntities.parentName: Strengthened national and local capacities and enhanced policy and regulatory frameworks for sustainable, integrated management of agrifood systems, cultural and natural resources and biodiversity.
planEntities.description: This pilot project under the Peace Forest Initiative (PFI) in Central Asia aims to serve as a springboard for designing a new regional programme that is context-relevant, adaptive to emerging climate and socio-political challenges, and attractive for long-term investment and partnerships. By testing nature-based solutions such as riparian restoration, reforestation, and sustainable agriculture in select sites across Kyrgyzstan, Turkmenistan, and Uzbekistan, the initiative will generate early results, build local ownership, and demonstrate scalable approaches that link climate resilience with social cohesion and regional cooperation, contributing to the PFI objectives.

planEntities.name: Strengthening Urban Resilience to Climate Risks in Central Asia
planEntities.parentName: Innovative, sustainable climate change adaptation and mitigation strategies, along with just energy transition initiatives, are designed and implemented at national and local levels across all sectors.
planEntities.description: The overall objective of the project is to support Central Asian countries in building climate resilience, focusing on urban areas. The project will specifically focus on enhancing regional cooperation and partnership through the existing coordination platforms, while introducing innovative approaches in urban planning based on practical experiences from other countries, including Japan. New approaches to integrated climate and disaster risk assessment will transform urban planning from resilience lenses, while considering future intensity and magnitude of natural hazards due to the changing climate. Knowledge base and capacity building efforts will be institutionalized in the region to ensure sustainability of interventions beyond the project cycle. The project promotes a people-centred, gender sensitive and climate risk-informed holistic approach to break siloes in urban planning efforts.

planEntities.description: This project will promote a transition to a circular economy in Uzbekistan by addressing upstream system gaps in policy, financing, and innovation, while empowering women and youth as key actors. Implemented in Tashkent, Angren and Nukus, the project will: (i) strengthen institutional knowledge and capacity for circular economy planning through municipal plastic inventories and training (≥50% women participants); (ii) support operationalization of Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) and Deposit Return Scheme (DRS) systems and pilot a light-touch Municipal Circular Innovation Facility to co-fund six small-scale municipal circular economy initiatives (approx. USD 10–15k each); (iii) support the creation of women- and youth-led circular micro-enterprises (e.g. buy-back depots, repair/reuse hubs, upcycling workshops) anchored in local mahallas; and (iv) run large-scale awareness campaigns and a youth innovation platform to build public support and generate new solutions. The project will complement existing downstream collection-focused initiatives by targeting the upstream enabling environment, and will allocate ≥1% of the budget to Monitoring & Learning and $3,000 to communications and visibility

planEntities.name: Empowering and nurturing leadership skills of youth through climate action education in Uzbekistan
planEntities.parentName: More inclusive, equitable, and competency-based teaching and learning environments in preschool and general secondary education.
planEntities.description:
This three-year joint initiative by UNDP, the “Education Above All” Foundation (EAA-Qatar), and Ministry of Pre-school and School Education of the Republic of Uzbekistan aims to equip 1.3 mln school students and youth across the Republic of Karakalpakstan, Bukhara, Navoiy, Khorezm, Samarkand, Kashkadarya and Surkhandarya regions with climate knowledge, leadership capacities and “green” skills.

By integrating climate change education into the formal school curriculum and training 50,000 teachers, the project ensures that every student gains access to interactive learning tools. This will help students explore key climate change topics, build understanding of climate science, adaptation and mitigation strategies, environmental sustainability, and practical actions individuals and communities can take to address climate crisis.   

Concurrently, the project establishes a network of 800 Young Green Ambassadors who, together with other youth in their communities, co-design and implement 48 community-led climate actions —ranging from planting drought-resilient species in Moynak to launching sustainable aquaculture initiatives.  

Finally, in partnership with 12 vocational training centers, the project offers two specialized courses to 4,000 young people – one on renewable energy and the other on climate-smart agriculture. These courses help improve job prospects while promoting low-carbon livelihoods. The project also emphasizes gender balance, with at least 48%women participation, and uses digital tools to enhance learning.  Overall, the project supports Uzbekistan’s commitments under the Paris Agreement, the National Green Economy Strategy, and contributes to global goals on quality education, clean energy, decent work, and climate action (SDGs 4, 7, 8 and 13).

planEntities.name: Inclusive information society with accountable institutions and strengthened rule of law
planEntities.parentName: Increased civil society and people’s participation in decision making for improved public oversight.
planEntities.description:
The project aims to contribute to building a more resilient, inclusive and informed society in Uzbekistan by enabling citizens to exercise their rights to access public information and by strengthening the rule of law and better journalism education. It also aims at enhancing media and information literacy. From three different perspectives, namely freedom of expression and access to information, media development, and media & information literacy, the project addresses the importance of freedom of expression and information as a pubic good and a vital element of democratic governance that contributes to citizen empowerment and collective action. A resilient information society requires three elements: a) empowered citizens who can demand and manage relevant information, b) robust and independent media that can produce quality content, and institutions guided by the rule of law that uphold freedom of expression as a human right, and c) a strategy to embed media and information literacy into the social and educational fabric of the country, involving educators, parents, children, and policymakers alike. 
(Project title: "Empowering the Government and Citizens of Uzbekistan by Strengthening Access to Information, Accountability of Institutions and Media Competence")

planEntities.name: Remote sensing and geographical information systems are applied for the Aral Sea ecosystem restoration and industrial revitalization
planEntities.parentName: Strengthened national and local capacities and enhanced policy and regulatory frameworks for sustainable, integrated management of agrifood systems, cultural and natural resources and biodiversity.
planEntities.description:
The Ministry of Ecology, Environmental Protection and Climate Change has approached UNIDO to explore opportunities for the application of geoinformation systems to monitor environmental parameters around the Aral Sea, and to promote digital innovations to combat desertification, restore ecosystems, prevent sand and dust storms, and implement smart and precision agriculture practices.
The project aims to establish a centralized Situational and Data Analytics Centre combining expertise in geodata analysis, drone technology and satellite imagery. The Centre will generate high-quality data on soil composition and other environmental parameters to support regional policymakers with evidence-based insights. By building a robust technological infrastructure for real-time monitoring and data-driven decision-making, the project will strengthen national capacities in data analytics, geospatial intelligence, remote sensing and smart ecosystem management.
The project will contribute to a knowledge-based economy by creating capacity-building opportunities, driving local technological innovation and generating new business prospects, particularly in smart agro-processing and manufacturing. The integration of digital tools will not only enhance ecosystem restoration but also support sustainable economic and industrial development in the region.

planEntities.name: PHC-integrated immunisation quality and safety system institutionalised nationwide
planEntities.parentName: Strengthened capacities of the health system to deliver quality, people-centered services across the life course at all levels, aligned with the primary healthcare approach.
planEntities.description:
Immunisation is delivered as a standardised, safe, people-centred PHC service with routine quality improvement, strong cold-chain integrity, and functional vaccine safety (AEFI) governance—embedded in PHC management and accountability arrangements.
Institutionalised supportive supervision as a PHC quality cycle: Convert the 2024–2025 large-scale supervision model into an annual national cycle with: (i) minimum coverage thresholds for facilities/vaccination points; (ii) corrective action tracking facility → district → region; (iii) supportive mentorship competency standards; Integrate supervision outputs into district PHC performance reviews (not parallel reporting); 
Cold-chain and vaccine management assurance (routine, not campaign-only):- Standard operating standards for storage, temperature monitoring, stock management, open-vial policy, and waste management, aligned with updated national norms and operational guidance; Expand use of remote temperature monitoring as a management tool (exception reporting, response times, accountability). 
Vaccine safety/AEFI governance fully operational: Implement the sequenced reform package identified through the 2024 system assessment: clarified roles, standardised case definitions/classification, causality assessment procedures, single reporting pathway and database, routine performance indicators, and tested crisis communication SOPs; Ensure alignment with WHO global vaccine safety strategic directions.

planEntities.name: “Data for action” immunisation system strengthened for equity, life-course coverage, and outbreak resilience
planEntities.parentName: Strengthened capacities of the health system to deliver quality, people-centered services across the life course at all levels, aligned with the primary healthcare approach.
planEntities.description:
A coherent immunisation intelligence approach is used at PHC and district levels to identify missed populations, reduce drop-outs, and sustain high coverage, supported by fit-for-purpose digital systems and people-centred community engagement.
EIR governance and interoperability for management use (not only reporting): Establish and enforce data quality rules (unique identity and deduplication, denominator coherence, completeness and timeliness), with routine dashboard review mandated in district management cycles; Progress interoperability with core national digital systems where feasible (PHC registers and civil registration/ID services), ensuring privacy and role-based access.
Equity-oriented microplanning institutionalized: Institutionalise micro-mapping and targeted planning as routine PHC practice: ‘who is missed, where, and why’ translated into outreach plans, defaulter tracing, and supervision follow-up; Apply lessons from documented antigen gaps (e.g., availability constraints and missed opportunities) to strengthen service integration and counselling at PHC points.
Integrated VPD risk signals for sustained measles and rubella control: Implement elimination-standard measles and rubella surveillance improvements (case classification, laboratory linkages, and CRS surveillance description and reporting) in line with RVC feedback and WHO/Europe guidance; Use EIR and surveillance outputs jointly for risk-based targeting through district dashboards integrating coverage, drop-out, and outbreak signals.
People-centred demand and confidence (behavioural insights to scalable tools): Translate behavioural insights work (e.g., COM-B-informed analyses) into PHC-ready counselling aids, refusal follow-up scripts, and targeted community engagement packages.

planEntities.name: Strengthened national regulatory governance and policy coherence for medicines and medical devices
planEntities.parentName: Enhanced, evidence-based and inclusive health governance and policy development ensuring greater efficiency, accountability, and informed decision-making.
planEntities.description:
Achieve sustained improvement in national regulatory authority (NRA) maturity using the WHO GBT framework; Institutionalise transparent, evidence-based regulatory decision-making and enforcement mechanisms; Strengthen separation of regulatory, promotional, and industrial policy functions.
Finalise and implement a WHO GBT Institutional Development Plan (IDP), endorsed at ministerial level; Clarify mandates and coordination mechanisms between the Center for Pharmaceutical Products Safety, the GxP Centre, the Procurement Center, and the Pharmaceutical Industry Development Agency through formal regulatory instruments; Introduce formal scientific advice and regulatory consultation procedures, modelled on international regulatory authorities, with publicly available SOPs; Review and modernise the regulatory fee system to support sustainable financing of core regulatory functions; Strengthen enforcement frameworks by introducing a transparent offence–responsibility–penalty matrix aligned with international practice.

planEntities.description: To strengthen public health emergency preparedness and response, WHO will support the Government in enhancing health security measures in accordance with the IHR (2005), the WHO Strategy and Action Plan on Health Emergency Preparedness, Response and Resilience (Preparedness 2.0), and Uzbekistan’s National Action Plan for Health Security (NAPHS), which was developed and endorsed using the findings of the recent Joint External Evaluation (JEE) and the States Parties Self‑Assessment Annual Report (SPAR). This includes enhancing surveillance and early warning systems, improving emergency response coordination, and strengthening laboratory and diagnostic capacities to better detect and contain public health threats.

planEntities.description: With climate change posing growing risks to health and well-being, WHO will support Uzbekistan in building a climate-resilient health system by integrating environmental health risks into national policies, strengthening preparedness for climate-related challenges, and ensuring sustainable water and sanitation systems with a focus on implementing the UNECFE-WHO Regional Office for Europe Protocol on Water and Health. Additionally, WHO will assist the Government of Uzbekistan in developing national health adaptation plans, reducing the environmental impact of the health sector while promoting the greening of health facilities and mobilizing resources for climate resilience and mitigation.

planEntities.name: Expanded preventive public health interventions for all hazards, through a multisectoral One  Health approach including AMR, food safety and zoonoses.
planEntities.parentName: Empowered communities, individuals, and civil society are equipped to demand equitable, timely, and informed access to health services while addressing the broader determinants of health.
planEntities.description: A key focus under this priority is the operationalization of the One Health approach in Uzbekistan, shifting from a human health–centred response to an integrated model that includes animal, plant and environmental health. The Government's commitment to this strategic shift is reflected in its plans to develop a 5-year One Health Strategy and Operational Plan. WHO will support the Government of Uzbekistan in developing and implementing this Plan by strengthening the National One Health coordination mechanism and embedding One Health principles into national policies and action plans. Key priorities will include expanding AMR surveillance beyond human health to encompass animal and environmental sectors, strengthening food safety systems and laboratory capacity, and improving infection prevention and control across both human and animal health sectors.

In response to the acute needs of displaced and vulnerable migrants in Cabo Delgado, IOM is currently implementing a comprehensive and integrated Health, WASH, CCCM, DTM, MHPSS, and Shelter intervention. The overall objective of the ongoing project is to ensure dignified, safe, and secure living conditions and access to essential services for populations affected by disasters driven by natural hazards and conflict, while contributing to empowered and resilient individuals and communities across northern Mozambique. This intervention forms part of IOM’s broader multi-donor, multisectoral humanitarian response in the region, which has reached an estimated 784,319 IDPs as of February 2022.

The project is being implemented within the framework of the Humanitarian–Development–Peace Nexus (HDPN), aimed at reducing overall vulnerability, decreasing unmet needs, strengthening risk management capacities, and addressing the root causes of fragility and displacement. Through this integrated approach, the project simultaneously responds to urgent humanitarian needs while supporting recovery, resilience-building, and pathways toward durable solutions. Please note that while the project is operational until March 2027, for the purposes of the current CF submission, the end date will be set as 31 March 2026

planEntities.name: Facilitating Cross Border Mobility and Small-Scale Cross Border Trade through Implementing a Mobile Border Pass System along Mozambique/Malawi Borders
planEntities.parentName: Output 1.2: Vulnerable and marginalized people, including refugees and IDPs, are empowered to access and utilize essential social services and protection systems they need, across the life course
planEntities.description: Malawi and Mozambique are countries of origin, transit, and destination for different categories of migrants and goods. Trade, migration, and cross-border human mobility are inherently interconnected; without people, the vast majority of goods and services would be unable to cross borders and contribute to economic development. In the case of border communities, the link between people and goods becomes unavoidable in the totality of the cases. As Malawi, Mozambique, and the African Union (AU) Member States move towards the implementation of the African Continental Free Trade Agreement (AfCFTA), the importance of effective border management policies increases as countries require measures that facilitate and expedite the movement of persons, goods, and services across borders while ensuring that important security concerns are addressed. Free Movement Protocols promulgated by the Regional Economic Communities (RECs), such as the Southern African Development Community (SADC) Protocol on the Facilitation of Movement of Persons, set out a series of measures related to a facilitated border management approach, which include visa liberalization, travel documentation, border residency arrangements among others aimed at simplifying and facilitating trade between and amongst neighbouring countries within the region and continent. In this regard, facilitating regular cross-border movement to promote trade is key for the achievement of Malawi’s and Mozambique’s development priorities. As part of efficient border management, it has a positive impact on trade, as trade agents, from small-scale traders to multinational companies, will benefit from swift, transparent, and well-organized processes at border posts (BP) and therefore, trade agents might be encouraged to increasingly use the Trade Corridors with efficient border management in place or individual men and women might be encouraged to engage in cross-border trade. This strongly contributes to increased revenues for the respective governments, creates job opportunities and contributes to economic development in general.

planEntities.parentName: Output 3.1: Policies, strategies, laws and regulations for the use of environmental & natural resources, climate and disaster resilience are developed and strengthened based on good practices and standards and are gender transformative and include the needs of refugees and IDPs.
planEntities.description: In displacement settings, internally displaced persons (IDPs) face significant challenges due to limited access to cooking fuel, lighting, electricity, and other essential energy services. This lack of energy access exacerbates hardships, increases risks of gender-based violence (GBV), puts strain on nearby host communities, and threatens local environmental ecosystems. While the humanitarian sector is beginning to prioritize sustainable energy access, data on current access levels remains scarce. Most displaced individuals in camps rely heavily on traditional biomass for cooking and have negligible or no access to electricity. IOM project aims to address these critical issues by scaling up the implementation of efficient cookstoves, integrating nature-based solutions, and expanding solar energy systems. By doing so, we seek to provide more reliable and sustainable energy sources, thereby reducing dependency on traditional biomass. This approach not only improves energy access but also allows displaced individuals greater dignity and flexibility in choosing their energy solutions.

planEntities.name: Support to IOM Mozambique Crisis Response Plan (Jan-Dec 2026)
planEntities.parentName: Output 1.2: Vulnerable and marginalized people, including refugees and IDPs, are empowered to access and utilize essential social services and protection systems they need, across the life course
planEntities.description: Mozambique continues to face various crisis such as climate shocks and conflict. Most recently, heavy rains caused flood and destructions in central and southern Mozambique. Since mid-January 2026, severe flooding has affected more than 724,000 people, prompting the Government to declare a nationwide Red Alert and activate large-scale evacuation and emergency operations. At the height of the disaster, approximately 100,000 individuals were hosted in around 100 accommodation centres, while hundreds of thousands more remained displaced in host communities and spontaneous sites with extremely limited services. This project will respond to the urgent humanitarian needs of flood-affected populations, using a multi-sectoral approach. The sectors involved include Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM), Camp Coordination and Camp Management (CCCM), Shelter/Non-Food Items (NFIs, Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH), Protection and Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS), Health, and Prevention of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA). The proposed intervention is in line with the IOM Flash Appeal for the flood response in Central and Southern Mozambique which is aiming to mobilize USD 38,400,000 to assist 150,000 individuals between January and December 2026.

planEntities.name: Multi-sectoral assistance for conflict and flood-affected populations in northern and southern Mozambique
planEntities.parentName: Output 1.4: Policy, regulatory and legal frameworks to enhance access and utilization social and protection services are improved.
planEntities.description: The project aims to respond to urgent humanitarian needs of people affected by conflict in northern Mozambique and by flooding in central and southern regions, through an integrated, multi‑sectoral approach that prioritizes safety, dignity, and equitable access to assistance. It focuses on providing emergency shelter and essential household items, including context‑appropriate shelter kits, support for rapid repairs, and guidance on safer construction to enhance resilience in disaster‑prone environments. At the same time, it strengthens camp coordination and site management by improving service delivery, enhancing collaboration between stakeholders, and promoting community participation through small‑scale, community‑led improvements that reinforce ownership and accountability. The intervention also addresses water, sanitation, and hygiene needs by distributing hygiene kits, promoting key practices such as handwashing and safe water use, and improving environmental health conditions in communal spaces. In addition, it delivers protection and psychosocial support through awareness‑raising, monitoring of risks, referral services, and provision of mental health care, ensuring that vulnerable individuals receive appropriate and confidential support. Complementing these efforts, the project provides essential health services, including primary health care and disease surveillance, while strengthening the capacity of local health systems to respond effectively to emergencies. Throughout all components, the project adopts a protection‑centred, gender‑responsive, and conflict‑sensitive approach, with particular attention to the needs of vulnerable groups, ensuring inclusive and meaningful assistance for affected communities.

planEntities.name: Multi-Sectoral Response in Northern Mozambique
planEntities.parentName: Output 1.2: Vulnerable and marginalized people, including refugees and IDPs, are empowered to access and utilize essential social services and protection systems they need, across the life course
planEntities.description: The province of Nampula in northern Mozambique is confronting a convergence of climate, health, and conflict-driven crises that threaten public health, social stability, and long-term recovery and development. Recurrent cyclones have devastated critical water and sanitation infrastructure, leaving displaced and vulnerable communities reliant on contaminated sources. These conditions have precipitated persistent and severe cholera outbreaks, which disproportionately affect marginalized populations, including internally displaced persons (IDPs). The fragile health and water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) systems are further strained by limited outbreak preparedness, inadequate community hygiene awareness, and weak cross-sector coordination. This vulnerability is compounded by active and escalating conflict, as evidenced by recent attacks in Memba district. According to IOM DTM Emergency Tracking reports (November 2025), these attacks have forcibly displaced over 66,000 people into Erati district, overwhelming reception sites and creating acute protection and service gaps. The potential spill-over of an ongoing Mpox outbreak from Niassa Province could further complicate the health emergency. Together, these shocks are eroding community resilience and creating conditions that heighten the risk of exploitation and recruitment by non-state armed groups (NSAGs), particularly among disenfranchised youth. The project aims to address the interconnected health, social, and economic vulnerabilities in Nampula Province, thereby promoting community stability and resilience. Through a comprehensive and context-specific intervention across the WASH and Health sectors, it will employ a joint WASH-Health approach, combining water and sanitation infrastructure rehabilitation with health system strengthening. This way, individuals will be protected and empowered to live their lives with dignity, thereby promoting greater community stability and societal resilience.

Targeting 9,000 households (approximately 45,000 individuals), the response begins with rapid shelter and NFI needs assessments in the affected areas to identify priority gaps and inform an evidence-based distribution plan. Based on assessment findings, the project will procure and distribute emergency shelter kits and essential non-food item (NFI) kits, with a strong focus on reaching the most vulnerable households, including women, children, older persons, persons with disabilities, and female-headed households. The intervention will ensure that families whose homes and belongings have been damaged or destroyed can meet their immediate shelter needs and restore basic living conditions.

planEntities.name: Saving Lives Through Anticipatory Action: Cyclone Preparedness and Response in Mozambique
planEntities.parentName: Output 1.2: Vulnerable and marginalized people, including refugees and IDPs, are empowered to access and utilize essential social services and protection systems they need, across the life course
planEntities.description:
The Shelter component will provide targeted, needs-based assistance through rapid household assessments to inform the distribution of Non-Food Items (NFIs). Beneficiary eligibility will be validated in close collaboration with local authorities and communities, with particular attention to vulnerable groups, including older persons, people with disabilities, and female-headed households. Implementation will be closely coordinated with the Shelter Cluster, which leads needs assessments, gap analysis, and pipeline stock management, to prevent duplication and ensure complementarity with other partners. Pre-positioned NFIs, such as tarpaulins and shelter repair kits, will be mobilized to high-risk districts. Accessible distribution points will be established to ensure equitable access, and distributions will be accompanied by awareness session and demonstrations on the correct use of items to maximize effectiveness and durability of assistance.  

Ahead of cyclone events, CCCM teams will work with government counterparts and the CCCM Cluster to assess, verify, and prepare priority accommodation centers and pre-position items. Support will be provided to the National Institute for Disaster Risk Reduction and Management (INGD) and Local Committees for Disaster Risk Reduction and Management (CLGRD) to establish safe evacuation centers, identify safe evacuation routes, and strengthen basic infrastructure to ensure protection and safety. This includes improvements to roads, drainage, sanitation facilities, pathways, and lighting, as well as the pre-positioning of essential items such as first aid kits and solar lights. 

Early warning messages from the National Institute of Meteorology will be disseminated to at-risk communities through community meetings, door-to-door outreach, and megaphone announcements led by community leaders and CLGRD members. Following cyclone impact, CCCM mobile teams will be rapidly deployed to assess site conditions and priority needs. Within 48 hours, teams will collect data on damages and displacement to inform coordination and support the government's response for internally displaced persons (IDPs), both within and outside formal accommodation centers. 

Post-impact support will include accommodation center/site management, site maintenance, rehabilitation of damaged infrastructure, debris clearance, service coordination, and community engagement. Information desks will be established to improve communication on available services and to strengthen access to complaints and feedback mechanisms and CCCM teams will facilitate access to assistance and services through coordination with district and local authorities, UN agencies, INGOs, and local organizations. Community participation will be promoted through regular consultations, operation of feedback mechanisms (including the Zite Manager platform), proactive information sharing and community-led projects.

Cross-cutting: Prevention of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA): In line with IOM's zero-tolerance policy on sexual exploitation and abuse (SEA), PSEA measures will be integrated across all activities. This includes SEA risk mitigation, capacity strengthening of national and local actors, awareness-raising among affected populations on their rights to free assistance and reporting mechanisms, and referral information for survivor support services.
