planEntities.parentName: Output 3.3: Governmental and non-governmental organizations, including forcibly displaced led organizations, have effective and inclusive tools to enhance productivity and revenues through improved sustainable management of environment and natural resources, climate and disaster resilience, and value chains for environmental and natural resources, goods and services.
planEntities.description: IOM Mozambique is attempting an ambitious and innovative initiative of empowering displaced communities through energy in the central provinces of Mozambique. Recognizing the critical need for sustainable energy solutions for Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs) in Mozambique, the project aims to revolutionize energy access through a groundbreaking approach. Traditional delivery models have yielded minimal impact and scale, prompting the exploration of more frugal innovations driven by the communities themselves. The project introduces a pioneering model that places the IDPs at the core of the solution development process, empowering them to actively participate in crafting and implementing sustainable energy solutions. This approach not only addresses immediate energy challenges but also ensures the longevity of impact by fostering community-led innovations. The project's focal point is to create an ecosystem where the IDPs are not passive beneficiaries but active contributors to the development and maintenance of the Energy Mesh Network. By championing a community-centric and innovative model, the project seeks to not only improve energy access but also empower displaced communities to take ownership of their energy solutions, fostering sustainability, reliability, and affordability for all.

planEntities.name: Bridging Borders for Women Entrepreneurs in Trade Corridors in Mozambique
planEntities.parentName: Output 2.2 More people, including refugees and IDPs, especially women and youths, have improved access to income generation opportunities, technical and vocational education and training, and financial and business development and extension services.
planEntities.description: Serving as a critical trade and mobility route along the border between Mozambique, Malawi and Zambia, the Nacala corridor plays a key role in the region's economic development, income growth and employment creation. The corridor serves an important trade route, including for Informal Cross-Border Trade (ICBT) which is a heavily feminized economic activity. Evidently, informal cross-border trade is important to national economies and livelihoods in the SADC region. Despite its potential for fostering economic diversification and growth through intra-regional trade and investment, women engaged in small-scale cross-border trade (SSCBT) face significant challenges that hinder their economic activities and jeopardize their safety. These challenges include limited access to finance, inadequate infrastructure, and cumbersome border procedures, compounded by widespread corruption and gender-based discrimination. These aspects not only hamper their economic activities but also expose them to risks of sexual assault, exploitation, harassment as well as health risks at border crossings. Other major challenges include inefficiency of customs and immigrations procedures and the lack of proper infrastructure and facilities at border crossing points. The project has three components, contributing to the overall objective of providing integrated support to enable safe and prosperous cross-border trade at the Zobué Border Cross Point, thereby promoting gender-inclusive economic growth.

planEntities.name: Integrated Multisectoral Emergency Response to Conflict and Climate Shocks to Affected Populations in Northern Mozambique
planEntities.parentName: Output 1.2: Vulnerable and marginalized people, including refugees and IDPs, are empowered to access and utilize essential social services and protection systems they need, across the life course
planEntities.description: With this grant, IOM will continue to respond to crises arising from the ongoing conflict and recurrent disasters affecting Mozambique. Under this project, IOM will provide humanitarian assistance through the deployment (1) an Integrated Multi-sectoral Settlements Approach (SA) in the districts identified as having a high concentration of multisectoral humanitarian needs, including of Quissanga, Macomia, Metuge and Mocimboa da Praia (Cabo Delgado Province) and (2) sectoral responses (non-SA) in other districts with high sectoral-specific humanitarian needs in other locations , including Nangade, Ibo, Muidumbe, Pemba Districts (Cabo Delgado Province), and any other district/province across the country in case humanitarian needs arise.

planEntities.name: IOM Flash Appeal - Flood response in Central and Southern Mozambique
planEntities.parentName: Output 1.2: Vulnerable and marginalized people, including refugees and IDPs, are empowered to access and utilize essential social services and protection systems they need, across the life course
planEntities.description: Mozambique continues to face various crisis such as climate shocks and conflict. Most recently, heavy rains caused flood and destructions in central and southern Mozambique. Since mid-January 2026, severe flooding has affected more than 724,000 people, prompting the Government to declare a nationwide Red Alert and activate large‑scale evacuation and emergency operations. At the height of the disaster, approximately 100,000 individuals were hosted in around 100 accommodation centres, while hundreds of thousands more remained displaced in host communities and spontaneous sites with extremely limited services.    This project will respond to the urgent humanitarian needs of flood-affected populations, using a multi-sectoral approach. The sectors involved include Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM), Protection and Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS), Health, and Prevention of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA). The proposed intervention is in line with the IOM Flash Appeal for the flood response in Central and Southern Mozambique.

planEntities.name: IOM – Multi Country Humanitarian Assistance – 2026
planEntities.parentName: Output 1.2: Vulnerable and marginalized people, including refugees and IDPs, are empowered to access and utilize essential social services and protection systems they need, across the life course
planEntities.description: IOM provides coordinated humanitarian assistance and protection to vulnerable populations affected by displacement and crises in Mozambique. The project focuses on delivering targeted, context-specific interventions to address urgent needs, improve access to essential services, and strengthen the protection, safety, and dignity of affected communities, particularly in areas impacted by conflict and climate-related shocks in northern Mozambique.

planEntities.name: IOM Mozambique Flood Response
planEntities.parentName: Output 1.2: Vulnerable and marginalized people, including refugees and IDPs, are empowered to access and utilize essential social services and protection systems they need, across the life course
planEntities.description:
The proposed interventions are aligned with the IOM Flood Flash Appeal for the response in Central and Southern Mozambique and prioritize the use of data to enable life-saving and well-coordinated humanitarian action. IOM will deploy the Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM) as a cross-cutting operational service to support sectoral response efforts throughout the flood emergency and early recovery phase.

DTM will provide timely, location-specific information on displacement, returns, population profiles, and priority needs across accommodation centres, host communities, and flood-affected districts. By systematically tracking mobility trends and evolving vulnerabilities, DTM will support evidence-based decision-making and allow partners to adjust interventions as conditions change, including in areas affected by residual and localized secondary flooding.

DTM data and analysis will be regularly shared with Shelter/NFI, CCCM, WASH, Health, Protection/MHPSS, and Rapid Response Mechanism partners to strengthen targeting, reduce duplication, and improve operational efficiency. This shared information base will enhance inter-sectoral coordination and support the delivery of safe, accountable, and responsive assistance to flood-affected and displaced populations.

planEntities.name: Strengthening community policing activities and border security systems
planEntities.parentName: Output 4.1: More people, especially the most vulnerable and marginalized and those affected by conflict, including refugees and IDPs, are empowered to actively participate in and lead conflict prevention, community-led stabilization, social cohesion, peacebuilding, and recovery initiatives
planEntities.description: Cabo Delgado in northern Mozambique has been significantly impacted by a severe context over the past seven years, driven by the Non-State Armed Groups (NSAG) linked to the Islamic State. This violence resulted in the displacement of over 720 thousand people, with many fleeing to neighboring provinces and across borders into Tanzania. The insurgency has been marked by brutal attacks, including beheadings, kidnappings, and destruction of infrastructure, causing widespread fear and trauma among the local population. Allegations of human rights abuses by security forces have further eroded trust between communities and authorities, with concerns that heavy-handed responses may push more people toward supporting the insurgents. IOM’s proposed project focuses on strengthening community resilience, improving border management, and enhancing law enforcement capacity in Cabo Delgado. The project will work on three main fronts: 1) establishing community structures that link to law enforcement, creating a two-way information-sharing system; 2) building trust between law enforcement and communities through positive engagement and capacity-building; and 3) upgrading police stations and border crossing infrastructure to boost operational capacity and security. By adopting this integrated approach, the proposed project aims to contribute to effective and inclusive law enforcement services by creating a collaborative environment where safety concerns can be effectively addressed, bridging communication gaps and enhancing community engagement.

planEntities.name: Mainstreaming Human Mobility into Climate Change Policies in Mozambique
planEntities.parentName: Output 1.3: Capacities of national systems including domestic financial capacity and institutions to deliver human rights-based, people centered, comprehensive essential social services and protection systems for all are enhanced.
planEntities.description: This project aims to enhance community resilience to climate change in Mozambique through effective government interventions that integrate human mobility (Objective), through the Government of Mozambique strengthening national and local climate change policy frameworks by integrating human mobility considerations, informed by community experiences with displacement, migration or planned relocation (Outcome 1). This will be achieved through gender-sensitive research and policy gap analysis on human mobility and climate change made available to inform government and stakeholder decision-making (Output 1.1), a contextualised gender-sensitive toolkit, made available to equip government and key stakeholders to integrate the human mobility and climate change nexus into Local Adaption Plans, (LAPs) (0utput 1.2), enhanced knowledge and skills of government officials and key stakeholders to design and implement climate change adaptation interventions that address human mobility (Output 1.3), two updated LAPs incorporating human mobility considerations submitted to national government for endorsement, (Output 1.4) and two co-designed projects integrating human mobility considerations made available for funding (Output 1.5).

planEntities.name: Comprehensive multisectoral humanitarian assistance for crisis-affected people in Mozambique
planEntities.parentName: Output 1.2: Vulnerable and marginalized people, including refugees and IDPs, are empowered to access and utilize essential social services and protection systems they need, across the life course
planEntities.description:
The intervention combines life-saving assistance with resilience-building through a multi-sectoral approach. Key activities include: primary healthcare via mobile/static clinics and community health workers; robust PSEAH measures; accountability and data collection through DTM; and a Crisis Modifier for rapid Shelter/NFI distribution and Build Back Safer (BBS) training. Environmental and climate considerations are integrated to ensure sustainability, alongside strong coordination with authorities and partners to align with national priorities.  
The project contributes to humanitarian appeal objectives by addressing the ongoing health, protection and displacement-related needs of conflict-affected populations in northern Mozambique, while moving beyond emergency relief through community-based health systems strengthening, preparedness measures and resilience-building interventions that reduce future vulnerabilities.

planEntities.name: Multisectoral humanitarian-development-peace nexus response in Mozambique
planEntities.parentName: Output 1.2: Vulnerable and marginalized people, including refugees and IDPs, are empowered to access and utilize essential social services and protection systems they need, across the life course
planEntities.description: To address these urgent and interconnected crises, IOM proposes a phased, integrated intervention that bridges emergency response, recovery, and resilience building, in line with the Humanitarian, Development and Peace Nexus (HDPN) and Solutions Agenda. The initiative will be anchored in a single overarching outcome: crisis-affected communities in northern Mozambique receive evidence-based, timely, and coordinated humanitarian assistance, protection, and recovery support that meets urgent needs, strengthens local capacities, and contributes to long term resilience and stability throughout the 2025 to 2026 period.

planEntities.name: Community stabilization for conflict-affected communities in northern Mozambique
planEntities.parentName: Output 4.1: More people, especially the most vulnerable and marginalized and those affected by conflict, including refugees and IDPs, are empowered to actively participate in and lead conflict prevention, community-led stabilization, social cohesion, peacebuilding, and recovery initiatives
planEntities.description:
For six years, the province of Cabo Delgado in northern Mozambique has experienced attacks by armed groups affiliated with the Islamic State causing over 709,529 people to be internally displaced and leaving many communities affected by loss, destruction, as well as negative economic and social impact. The insecurity in northern Mozambique is multi-faceted with many drivers including perceptions of historical marginalization and lack of economic opportunities.
This project will seek to promote community stabilization and preventing violent extremism in Northern Mozambique, particularly in communities affected by conflict with a specific focus on youth, women and girls.
In pursuit of this objective, IOM will build upon its previous work supporting community-led conflict prevention and creating a conducive environment for communities to live peaceful and productive lives through income generation activities, school-based peace clubs, community-based projects prioritized by communities and support to the Government of Mozambique to discuss mechanisms and frameworks for reintegration of former and eligible non-state armed group (NSAG) members.

planEntities.name: Improving access to energy in displacement settings
planEntities.parentName: Output 1.2: Vulnerable and marginalized people, including refugees and IDPs, are empowered to access and utilize essential social services and protection systems they need, across the life course
planEntities.description: This project aims to enhance access to clean and affordable energy for internally displaced persons (IDPs) in central Mozambique by expanding community mesh grids, also known as crowd-sourced grids. These interconnected solar home systems (SHSs) enable households to share power, thereby enhancing energy capacity and benefiting a greater number of individuals. The project builds on IOM's previous initiatives in Sofala Province, leveraging successful pilot projects funded by Innovation Norway. By expanding these efforts, the project aims to create a sustainable and inclusive energy market for displaced populations and host communities.

planEntities.name: Promoting gender-inclusive empowerment and social cohesion in displacement-affected communities in northern Mozambique
planEntities.parentName: Output 2.2 More people, including refugees and IDPs, especially women and youths, have improved access to income generation opportunities, technical and vocational education and training, and financial and business development and extension services.
planEntities.description:
For over six years, northern Mozambique has faced attacks by Non-State Armed Groups (NSAG) allegedly linked to the Islamic State, resulting in widespread displacement and a complex crisis with dire humanitarian implications. Among the Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs) in the country—545,870 out of a total of 721,348—women and girls are disproportionately affected, facing heightened risks of gender-based violence, exploitation, and barriers to accessing essential services. The Northern provinces, where the majority of IDPs are located, struggle to support 55% of these individuals hosted in communities, while over 600,000 persons have returned to their places of origin, often to areas with inadequate infrastructure and limited resources.
To address this, IOM applies a Humanitarian-Development-Peace Nexus (HDPN) approach to this complex crisis in Northern Mozambique. Through the HDPN, IOM simultaneously responds to the direct humanitarian needs that emerged as a result of conflict and displacement and seeks to address the drivers of conflict and related displacement effects.

With this intervention, IOM will support selected displacement-affected communities by providing them with multi-sectoral assistance, enhancing their resilience and social cohesion, promoting women’s empowerment and gender equality, and facilitating their access to durable solutions in collaboration with a Japanese non-governmental organization (NGO), Peace Winds Japan, in Mocimboa da Praia.

planEntities.name: Rapid Response Fund (RRF) – localization fund – programme responding to emergency and recovery needs of disaster- and conflict-affected populations in Mozambique
planEntities.parentName: Output 1.2: Vulnerable and marginalized people, including refugees and IDPs, are empowered to access and utilize essential social services and protection systems they need, across the life course
planEntities.description: Mozambique is grappling with a multitude of humanitarian challenges across the country. Since 2017 the conflict has displaced over 1M people across the Northern provinces, worsening living conditions of displaced and resident communities due to the damaging/destruction of the already limited infrastructures. In addition to conflict-related displacements, cyclical extreme climate events are becoming more severe and intense, affecting communities across the country, especially in Central and Southern Provinces. International Humanitarian partners have been present in the country for decades, supporting the government and providing regular life-saving assistance to communities affected by the conflict and disasters. Recognizing the importance of localization in effectively addressing these issues and increasing the sustainability of the response and country resilience, the proposed project by IOM seeks to address humanitarian action by empowering Local and National Partners (LNAs) in Mozambique. As the first line of support for affected communities, these organizations will be allocated resources and dedicated mentoring to take ownership of interventions and lead them in accordance with the needs of their communities.

planEntities.name: Integrated shelter and camp coordination and camp management support for displacement-affected communities in Cabo Delgado
planEntities.parentName: Output 1.2: Vulnerable and marginalized people, including refugees and IDPs, are empowered to access and utilize essential social services and protection systems they need, across the life course
planEntities.description: This project aims to provide coordinated assistance to 25,000 individuals in Cabo Delgado, focusing on two primary intervention components: Shelter and Non-food Items (NFI) and Camp Coordination and Camp Management (CCCM). The intervention will target four vulnerable districts including Chiure, Ancuabe, Muidumbe, and Macomia. Through CERF funding, IOM intends to deliver life-saving support to those displaced—many of whom are currently in transit centers and relocation sites. The response will address urgent shelter needs and provide NFIs, while also ensuring effective coordination and management of displacement sites through CCCM activities.

planEntities.name: Strengthening Public Health Preparedness and Cross-Border Surveillance at Mozambique’s Priority Points of Entry Using a One Health Approach
planEntities.parentName: Output 4.2: State institutions and decentralized governance bodies are inclusive and have strengthened capacities and policies to operate in line with national, regional and international standards, to ensure rights-based, gender transformative, transparent, and accountable governance;
planEntities.description:
The project “Strengthening Public Health Preparedness and Cross-Border Surveillance at Mozambique’s Priority Points of Entry Using a One Health Approach” aims to enhance Mozambique’s capacity to prevent, detect, and respond to public health threats at key border crossings, airports, and ports. Implemented by the International Organization for Migration (IOM) in partnership with government institutions and health partners, the project will strengthen disease surveillance, emergency preparedness, and cross-border coordination in line with the International Health Regulations (IHR). Using a One Health approach that recognizes the interconnected health of people, animals, and the environment, the project will address emerging health risks linked to mobility, climate-related disasters, and infectious disease outbreaks.
Key activities include conducting risk assessments at priority points of entry, improving operational procedures and preparedness systems, mapping population mobility patterns to better understand disease transmission risks, and strengthening collaboration between health, immigration, border management, and local authorities.The project will directly benefit travellers, cross-border traders, transport operators, border officials, and surrounding communities, contributing to stronger health security systems, safer mobility, and more resilient border regions across Mozambique.

planEntities.parentName: Output 3.4: People's voices and capacities, in particular those of women and youth and the most vulnerable forcibly displaced persons, are enhanced to participate in public and private decision-making and governance systems for the management of environment and natural resources and for climate and disaster resilience building;
planEntities.description: The Local Climate Adaptive Living Facility (LoCAL)  was designed to provide solutions and access to climate finance for Mozambican local governments in 2014. Since then, with generous support from Belgium, Sweden, Switzerland, the European Union and the Region of Catalonia, around 100 adaptive development infrastructures have been financed in 54 of the 154 districts in Mozambique during the implementation of the LoCAL Mechanism. To date, LoCAL has directly benefited approximately three million people in the country - almost 10% of the Mozambican population - and channeled approximately US$25 million directly to local governments in Mozambique.

planEntities.name: MERCIM - Building Local Climate Resilience in Mozambique
planEntities.parentName: Output 3.4: People's voices and capacities, in particular those of women and youth and the most vulnerable forcibly displaced persons, are enhanced to participate in public and private decision-making and governance systems for the management of environment and natural resources and for climate and disaster resilience building;
planEntities.description: MERCIM uses UNCDF methodologies that strengthen the capacity of local governments to improve the delivery of basic climate-resilient services to communities and to enhance decision-making processes based on local knowledge. This means providing training and technical assistance to governments so that communities can genuinely participate in planning, budgeting and other local governance processes. MERCIM channels, through the national public finance management system, climate finance to local government authorities for locally-led adaptation, using Performance-Based Climate Resilience Grants. These grants provide additional decentralized resources to finance local climate-resilient investments. The annual performance of local authorities determines their budget allocation for the following year.

planEntities.name: Informal Economy Project
planEntities.parentName: Output 2.1: Legal frameworks targeting productive capacity, competitiveness, infrastructure, trade and investment, information and communications are strengthened, gender sensitive and include the needs of refugees and IDPs, and new digital technologies are inclusive and more accessible.
planEntities.description:
The project will strengthen informal firms' ecosystem, and increase their ability and willingness for growth and formalization.
The expected outcome of the project is to support and enable informal enterprises transition towards sustainable growth and formalization in Mozambique. 
The main objective of the project is to facilitate informal firms’ growth and formalization in the following four main results areas:
(1)	Create an enabling regulatory environment for informal enterprises through the promotion of an integrated policy framework for the formalization of informal enterprises in Mozambique; 
(2)	Facilitate access to finance through the development and promotion of new financial services, and the expansion of capitalization opportunities for financial intermediaries;
(3)	Build capacity among informal economy intermediaries and informal enterprises and promote digital finance technology use.
(4)	Foster collective and mutually reinforcing action and innovations to address gaps in selected sectors through the establishment and operationalization of an agricultural commercialization sector collective action platform. This platform will contribute to identifying and addressing systemic gaps in this particular sector of the Mozambican economy.

planEntities.name: Immediate Stabilization and Recovery in Cabo Delgado Province, Mozambique
planEntities.parentName: Output 4.1: More people, especially the most vulnerable and marginalized and those affected by conflict, including refugees and IDPs, are empowered to actively participate in and lead conflict prevention, community-led stabilization, social cohesion, peacebuilding, and recovery initiatives
planEntities.description:
Since 2017 the Province of Cabo Delgado in Mozambique has been facing an escalating conflict, including armed violence compounded by terrorism and connections to extremist cells in East Africa and the confluence of various economic interests in the Mozambique Channel, the occurrences of socio-economic inequalities and expectations related to the exploitation of natural resources, especially among local youth and the perception of political exclusion, and few economic opportunities, affecting in particular young people, consecutive climatic shocks, and recurrent disease outbreaks. Currently, at least  1.5 million people are in need of urgent humanitarian aid1.  It is estimated that in November 2021, over 735,000 internally displaced people were located in relocation camps or informally hosted by communities across the Provinces of Cabo Delgado, Nampula, and Niassa. 

According to the Northern Resilience and Integrated Development Program (PREDIN), by the end of September 2021, attacks resulted in the loss of life of more than 2,000 citizens and forced the displacement of more than 817,000 people.   

Violent attacks by insurgents have significantly heightened protection risks, especially for women and girls. The government of Mozambique, with the strengthening of regional and international cooperation in the field of defense, including with the arrival of troops from the Republic of Rwanda and the SADC Standby Force (SAMIM), reclaimed a number of areas which had been occupied by insurgents. Prior to the arrival of the first Foreign troops on the ground in July 2021, UNDP had initiated stabilization interventions to assist the government of Mozambique in its efforts to re-establish the presence of the State in the reclaimed areas, paving the way for reconstruction and a subsequent safe and voluntary return of IDPs to their areas of origin. UNDP is already working in the districts of Macomia, Quissanga, Mocimboa da Praia and Palma. Benefiting from decades of experience in stabilization activities elsewhere on the continent and in the world, and with an office fully established in Pemba in 2021, UNDP is well positioned to support the government in three interrelated and complementary dimensions as part of stabilization: 

OUTPUT 1: Community security is improved with a focus on Rule of Law and Access to Justice, creating the foundation for social cohesion, peace and development  

OUTPUT 2: Basic services and infrastructure are rehabilitated, functional, and accessible and the capacity of local authorities are developed to improve access to service delivery 

OUTPUT 3: Socio-economic support is provided to individuals and communities, including immediate livelihood support for affected populations 

The support provided by UNDP is aligned with PREDIN's vision to restore and consolidate peace and promote sustainable socio-economic development in the Northern Region of Mozambique, particularly with its pillars 1 (Restoration and consolidation of peace and security) and 3 (Recovery, Reconstruction and socio-economic development and resilience). 

While humanitarian support continues to be provided to populations across the province of Cabo Delgado, the stabilization interventions of UNDP are meant to increase basic state service delivery capacities in areas where security has been restored to allow for the safe return of populations. UNDP supports immediate return of State presence in conflict-affected areas through rehabilitation of damaged infrastructure and institutional capacity building for the restoration of basic services as fundamental conditions for socio-economic recovery. UNDP will ensure a conflict-sensitive, human rights-based and gender-sensitive approach through its response to build forward better, laying the foundations for peace and rule of law, as emphasized by PREDIN.  

UNDP’s stabilization engagement in Mozambique is part and parcels of the Government’s priorities in Cabo Delgado, as embodied in the reconstruction plan (PRCD), and contributing to the Northern Resilience and Integrated Development Program (PREDIN). Along those lines, the present programme is fully integrated with other components of UNDP cooperation in country, as part of its new 2022-2026 programme cycle, with particular complementarity with UNDP’s decentralization programming, as well as with its social cohesion and peacebuilding work. 

UNDP’s stabilization engagement is also grounded in two of the foundational elements of UN wide engagement on internal displacement in which UNDP is called on to a critical role: on the one hand, the 2011 decision on Durable Solutions adopted by the UN Secretary-General, and the accompanying Preliminary Framework on Ending Displacement in the Aftermath of Conflict; on the other hand, the recommendations of the report of the United Nations Secretary-General’s High-Level Panel on Internal Displacement, released in September 20212. As such, the proposed programme builds on the call for development and peace actors to predictably and coherently engage as early on as possible on solutions for displacement. Although it should not be understood as a  peacebuilding intervention, stabilization is conceived as responding to the immediate and critical step on the way to building and sustaining peace, as part of the humanitarian, development and peace engagement (HDP Nexus). UNDP will ensure it engages adequately as part of the existing humanitarian and wider coordination platforms, and will work with sister agencies on the ground.

planEntities.description: Programme is an extrabudgetary programme created in 2003. It is based on the understanding that education reforms will not be effective if countries lack the capacities to make them operational. With an overarching capacity development approach, CapED seeks to improve the quality of education and increase learning opportunities, especially for girls and women and disadvantaged population groups. Under "Literacy skills for girls' and women's empowerment", CapED assists countries craft non-formal education policies and develop, implement and scale up good quality, relevant and innovative adult education programmes targeting girls and women.

Within the implementation of the joint UN program, "Action for the Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights of Girls and Young Women in Mozambique - Phase II", funded by the Swedish International Development Cooperation Agency (SIDA), UNESCO is leading efforts to implement Comprehensive Sexuality Education (CSE). planEntities.name: By 2026, girls, boys and adolescents, and their families and communities have increased knowledge and awareness and are better equipped to prevent violence and harmful practices
planEntities.parentName: Output 1.1: Mechanisms and capacities of community actors and institutions, including in refugee and IDP hosting areas, to address discriminatory gender and social cultural norms, and prevent and respond to violence and harmful practices are strengthened.
planEntities.description: Harmful social norms continue to take a heavy toll on child protection efforts in Mozambique. The prevention of violence through the promotion of positive social norms and behaviour change is a slow process that requires long term commitment and steady engagement with a wide range of partners and with communities, families, adolescents and children. The implementation of the VAC school-based referral mechanism is a landmark achievement and the roll-out of the operational plan to implement the mechanism will be a priority in the new Country Programme, working across sectors, under the leadership of the Education team.  Work with C4D, will focus on triggering behavioural change with and within communities, addressing harmful effects of social (and negative gender) norms and practices that act as socio-cultural barriers towards positive social change. Initiatives will aim to break the culture of silence that continue to hamper reporting and denunciation of acts of violence committed against children, including child marriage. A wide range of Communication for Development methodologies and tools will be developed and used to ensure a multi-level, multi-sectoral, participatory and inclusive social change process, using gender-transformative approaches to ensure gender differences and inequalities are addressed. Activities for prevention of violence and harmful practices will comprise of two inter-connected pillars: social behaviour change communication and parenting skills. Close collaboration  with social protection will ensure that vulnerable children and families do not fall through the social safety.

planEntities.parentName: Output 4.2: State institutions and decentralized governance bodies are inclusive and have strengthened capacities and policies to operate in line with national, regional and international standards, to ensure rights-based, gender transformative, transparent, and accountable governance;
planEntities.description: While Mozambique has made significant strides in establishing a progressive legal framework and policies that conform with core international standards, there are a number of gaps that have prevented implementation, including the need for additional regulations, standards and guidelines. In particular, there is a lack of reliable systematic administrative data on child protection and insufficient overall investment in child protection. Efforts are needed in the collection of data to inform prevention and response to violence against children. There is also a need to invest at national and subnational levels in budget review and introduce a child-rights perspective into the budgeting process with clear allocations and specific indicators for children in the relevant sectors and agencies, combined with a tracking system to monitor and evaluate the adequacy, efficacy and equitability of the distribution of resources allocated for child protection priorities.

planEntities.parentName: Output 2.3 The primary sector is more sustainable, productive, value-adding and inclusive of forcibly displaced persons and incorporating circular, regenerative and gender transformative practices.
planEntities.description: As a follow-up to the official request from the Ministry of Industry and Commerce, Republic of Mozambique, UNIDO has formulated a technical assistance project aimed at increasing local capacities, technology upgrading, and know-how transfer for strengthening agribusiness models and contributing to the development of the agro-industry in Mozambique. Agro-industry development has been understood as the primary driver of structural transformation in rural areas of Mozambique. In cooperation with the local institutions, agricultural aggregation points, processing facilities, and related services for agricultural enterprises are strategic for supporting the Government of Mozambique in its efforts toward a sustainable and inclusive agro-industry development. The project will be implemented in Manica, and Cabo Delgado Provinces and will work in close cooperation with the donor (AICS), and other initiatives funded by the Italian Agency for Development and Cooperation – AICS - and/or partners in the target areas. As a scaling up of the project N°170217, funded by the Italian Agency for Development Cooperation (AICS), the project will be focusing on promoting value addition and improving agro-processing performances in horticulture, coffee and grains productions

planEntities.name: Implementation of the "Maputo Roadmap" of UNODC engagement in Mozambique
planEntities.parentName: Output 4.2: State institutions and decentralized governance bodies are inclusive and have strengthened capacities and policies to operate in line with national, regional and international standards, to ensure rights-based, gender transformative, transparent, and accountable governance;
planEntities.description: Upon invitation of Mozambique to establish a presence in the country, UNODC worked closely with the Government to establish a roadmap of UNODC engagement for the coming years. Called the ‘Maputo Roadmap’, this strategy focuses on four thematic pillars, namely: criminal justice response to fight transnational organized crime, promotion of health-based approaches, prevention of terrorism and the improvement of justice and integrity measures. The overall objective of UNODC’s engagement in Mozambique is to assist the authorities in having a holistic, effective and pragmatic response to drug use, drug trafficking, illicit trafficking, organized crime, corruption and terrorism, through both a national and regional perspective. This will help strengthen the rule of law in Mozambique and restore the confidence of populations towards their criminal justice system. UNODC intends to strengthen the capacities of relevant national authorities through legislative assistance, technical assistance on criminal justice and law

planEntities.name: Assisting Mozambique to strengthen criminal justice responses to terrorism, including capacities for collecting, preserving and sharing of evidence in line with human rights standards
planEntities.parentName: Output 4.2: State institutions and decentralized governance bodies are inclusive and have strengthened capacities and policies to operate in line with national, regional and international standards, to ensure rights-based, gender transformative, transparent, and accountable governance;
planEntities.description: UNODC is the primary provider of technical assistance to the Government in Mozambique to counter the threat of terrorism in full respect of international human rights standards. UNODC capacity-building efforts address key aspects of the criminal justice response to terrorism. This includes strengthening investigative techniques and the effective handling of evidence—from its collection and analysis to preservation, exploitation, and admissibility in court. UNODC work also covered prosecutorial strategies specific to terrorism-related cases, relevant legal frameworks and procedures, and mechanisms to enhance inter-agency cooperation.

The project aims to promote social cohesion and local peace between IDPs, returnees and host communities in Cabo 
Delgado supporting the Government and the communities in the achievement of durable solutions to displacement 
through equitable, inclusive and peaceful natural resource access and management, in particular land and water. It 
focuses on addressing the root causes of conflict and fragility associated with access and distribution of the 
resources, experience and access to resources by different groups, preventing secondary conflicts and displacement, 
and improving security of tenure, participation in decision making and increase in livelihoods for these populations

planEntities.description: The project aims to support eight national governments fulfill essential communication requirements to the Climate Convention and the Paris Agreement; and is in conformity with Objective 3 of the GEF-7 Climate Change Focal Area, which focuses on fostering enabling conditions for mainstreaming mitigation concerns into sustainable development strategies.

planEntities.name: Ecosystem conservation and community livelihood enhancement in North Western Zambia
planEntities.parentName: Planet Output 4.2 People in Zambia, particularly the marginalized, including the most vulnerable groups, have improved knowledge and capacities to demand, adopt and implement  environmentally friendly, gender responsive and climate-smart sustainable natural resource management practices, and utilize basic services and infrastructure
planEntities.description: The Project aims to address the barriers to sustainable land management and to biodiversity conservation at three project sites in three districts in the Northwestern Province in the Republic of Zambia. It will carry out activities to develop systems of community management of forests and other natural resources, and to develop and extend sustainable agricultural technologies. The leading causes of forest loss are clearing for agriculture and over-exploitation of wood and non-woody forest products. The key barrier to sustainable agriculture is the shortage of tested, proven sustainable agricultural technologies with high rates of farmer adoption.

planEntities.description: Amélioration de la sécurité alimentaire et de la nutrition des femmes rurales et de leurs ménages, contribuant à des systèmes alimentaires équitables et durables. (2220 femmes et 660 hommes) - Les femmes rurales ont des compétences et des capacités accrues pour augmenter la production d'aliments nutritifs, la qualité des aliments et les réserves locales de sécurité alimentaire, réduire les pertes et les déchets alimentaires et améliorer le régime alimentaire des ménages. Les revenus, le travail décent et l'autonomie économique des femmes rurales sont accrus afin de garantir leurs moyens de subsistance et de renforcer leur résilience. (2220 femmes et 660 hommes) Les femmes rurales peuvent davantage s'exprimer et agir pour participer pleinement et sur un pied d'égalité à la vie de leur foyer, de leur communauté, de leur organisation et de leur système de gouvernance. (2220 femmes et 660 hommes) Les cadres juridiques, les politiques et les institutions sensibles au genre sont renforcés afin de créer un environnement favorable aux femmes rurales pour garantir leurs moyens de subsistance, leurs droits et leur résilience. (2220 femmes et 660 hommes)

planEntities.description: The project aims to improve local water governance in Tunisia, in order to ensure a transparent and equitable distribution of water resources, in the face of growing tensions due to their unequal management between the North and the South of the country. In response to climate challenges, including reduced rainfall and increased droughts, it promotes sustainable and efficient water use through appropriate techniques and a change in user behavior.

planEntities.parentName: Produit 3.6 : Des approches multisectorielles et innovantes sont consacrées à des problématiques prioritaires de la santé et du bienêtre sont mises en œuvre avec un engagement actif de la population et la participation de toutes les parties prenantes
planEntities.description: This project aims to support human and animal health sectors under the "one health" approach to fight against epidemics and contribute to the global effort in reducing epidemic and pandemic risks through effective prevention and preparedness. The goal is to bring Tunisia's national health systems including the animal health sector up to IHR and international standards requirements.

planEntities.name: SoilFER-VACS Framework - Enhancing Integrated Soil-Crop Management for Sustainable Food Systems in Africa
planEntities.parentName: Produit 4.2 : Les acteurs concernés sont outillés pour développer et mettre en œuvre une approche territoriale favorisant une gestion intégrée des écosystèmes et des ressources naturelles, tenant compte des effets du changement climatique
planEntities.description: The objectives of the Project are designed to address low soil fertility and productivity challenges by improving decision-making for crops, fertilizers and soil management practices at various scales, thereby increasing yields and improving food security, particularly for smallholders. The project focuses on producing detailed maps of soil health and fertility status to enable strategic national-level decisions on policies. It also aims to strengthen institutional capacities in soil analysis and data interpretation and establishing a decision support framework, and facilitate decision-making for crop selection, fertilizer use, and SSM practices to optimize agricultural productivity at the local level.

planEntities.name: Boosting evidence on biodiversity and gender for sustainable livestock transformation
planEntities.parentName: Produit 1.1 La vision 2030, la planification stratégique et les politiques publiques y afférentes sont centrées sur l’atteinte des ODD et ont corrigé les écarts socio-économiques et environnementaux
planEntities.description: This project aims to fill a critical gap in the availability of harmonized data on the performance of pastoralism in biodiversity and the role women play into the livestock sector. Harmonized data, in this context, refers to data that is consistent across different methodologies and ensures comparability and reliability in assessing the pastoral production systems in biodiversity and gender.

planEntities.name: Renforcement des systèmes de prévention et de contrôle des maladies aquatiques à l'ère des changements climatiques
planEntities.parentName: Produit 4.4 : Les acteurs publics, privés et de la société civile disposent de capacités et d’outils permettant de réduire et de gérer les risques de crises
planEntities.description: Le projet cible la promotion de l'utilisation durable et la conservation des ressources halieutiques en Tunisie, tout en renforçant les capacités de contrôle des maladies des organismes aquatiques. Il a pour objectifs d'améliorer la biosécurité et la gestion dans l'aquaculture, contribuant ainsi à la sécurité alimentaire durable et à la résilience des écosystèmes. Les résultats attendus incluent la certification du secteur, le renforcement des capacités des laboratoires pour un diagnostic précoce, le développement de méthodes de surveillance moins invasives et la digitalisation des bases de données épidémiologiques. Le projet intégrera également des considérations de genre pour garantir une participation équitable et renforcer la résilience des communautés.

planEntities.description:
The overall objective of the SEMPA project is to protect the biodiversity of the Mediterranean Sea and support the achievement of its Good Environmental Status.
The specific objectives of the two projects components are: a) Support the implementation of the Post-2020 Strategic Action Programme for the Conservation of Biodiversity and Sustainable Management of Natural Resources in the Mediterranean Region and b) Continue support on IMAP implementation with a particular focus on biodiversity & NIS , Hydrography & coast and interlinkages with climate change, expanding the scope of the support to SEIS  implementation and its related indicators to biodiversity and climate change.

planEntities.parentName: Produit 4.1 : Les acteurs publics, privés et de la société civile disposent des outils et des capacités en matière de gouvernance durable, équitable et participative des ressources naturelles, des écosystèmes et des services environnementaux
planEntities.description: The objective of the Special Programme is to support country-driven institutional strengthening at the national level, in the context of an integrated  to address the financing of the sound management of chemicals and wastes, taking into account the national development strategies, plans and priorities of each country, to increase sustainable public institutional capacity for the sound management of chemicals and wastes throughout their life cycle. Institutional strengthening under the Special Programme will facilitate and enable the implementation of the Basel, Rotterdam and Stockholm conventions, the Minamata Convention and the Strategic Approach to International Chemicals Management (SAICM).

planEntities.description: The GEF/UN Environment “Mediterranean Sea Programme (MedProgramme): Enhancing Environmental Security” (2019-2024) represents the first GEF programmatic multi-focal area initiative in the Mediterranean Sea aiming to operationalize priority actions to reduce major transboundary environmental stresses in its coastal areas while strengthening climate resilience and water security and improving the health and livelihoods of coastal populations. The MedProgramme is implemented in nine beneficiary countries sharing the Mediterranean basin: Albania, Algeria, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Egypt, Lebanon, Libya, Montenegro, Morocco and Tunisia.

planEntities.parentName: Produit 1.1 La vision 2030, la planification stratégique et les politiques publiques y afférentes sont centrées sur l’atteinte des ODD et ont corrigé les écarts socio-économiques et environnementaux
planEntities.description:
Le projet s'est initialement concentré sur le Plan de développement 2023-2025 avec le Ministère de l'Économie et de la Planification, mais après une réorientation des priorités du projet a été proposé.
Le projet concerne la conception et la mise en œuvre du Plan de développement 2026-2030: l'équipe s'engage dans la gestion du changement et les domaines prioritaires du Plan (par exemple, la croissance économique, l'inclusion sociale, etc.). L'UNOPS soutient également la structuration de l'investissement public en Tunisie, en ajoutant une base de données pour soutenir la planification, l'exécution et le suivi.
Les activités comprennent :
Proposition et développement d'un nouveau cadre structurel sur l'investissement public en Tunisie pour le Plan national de développement (PND) 2026-2030.
Amélioration des capacités internes du MEP pour le suivi et l'évaluation du PND.
Renforcement des capacités du personnel du MEP chargé du suivi et de l'évaluation du Plan.
Appui à la conception, à la planification, au suivi et à l'évaluation de la mise en œuvre du PND.
Appui à l'institutionnalisation de la mise en œuvre et de la révision du budget économique.

planEntities.name: Micro, pequenas e médias empresas fortalecidas em empreendedorismo, capacidade técnica e acesso a financiamento adequado para sistemas agroalimentares sustentáveis
planEntities.parentName: Produto 2.1.2: As pequenas e médias empresas são integradas nas cadeias verde, azul e de valor, suas capacidades produtivas e acesso a serviços financeiros e não financeiros são fortalecidos e soluções de mercado, baseadas na natureza e com eficiência energética (no setor privado) são promovidos.
planEntities.description:
No âmbito do projeto de Promoção do Empreendedorismo na Economia Azul (GCP/CVI/051/SPA), estão previstas as seguintes atividades, a serem implementadas por meio de um protocolo de acordo assinado com a PROEMPRESA:
1. Formação de Empreendedores: Realização de ações de formação para micro e pequenos empreendedores, com um foco especial na inclusão de pelo menos 40% de mulheres. As formações abrangerão os diferentes ofícios e serviços necessários para a melhoria das cadeias de valor na economia azul.
2. Capital Semente: Alocação de capital semente para cinco projetos empresariais, com a garantia de que ao menos 40% dos projetos sejam liderados por mulheres, promovendo a equidade de gênero no setor.
3. Base de Dados de Consultores: Criação de uma base de dados/bolsa de consultores especializados em diversas áreas da economia azul. Esta base terá como objetivo reunir profissionais capazes de contribuir para a melhoria das cadeias de valor, abordando todos os aspectos técnicos e serviços relevantes.
4. Concurso de Empreendedorismo: Organização de um concurso nacional de empreendedorismo em economia azul (PROMEB III), com o objetivo de reunir projetos inovadores nas áreas de produtos, embalagens, mercados e serviços. Os melhores projetos serão premiados, incentivando a inovação e a competitividade no setor.
5. Assistência Técnica: Oferta de assistência técnica contínua a empreendedores, por meio de capacitação, treinamento, e apoio à adoção ou ao acesso a inovações. Isso será facilitado por consultores especializados e sessões de mentoria, visando fortalecer as capacidades empreendedoras e a implementação de soluções inovadoras na economia azul.

Objetivo da Ação: A ação visa fortalecer as capacidades técnicas e organizacionais dos atores em horticultura, proteção vegetal, produção animal e cultivo de algas para alimentação.

Capacitações Previstas Através do projeto de Cooperação Sul-Sul com a China, estão previstas formações em: 
a) Gestão de Água, Solos e Fertilizantes para Horticultura.
b) Produção e Reprodução Animal.
c) Epidemiologia Veterinária
d) Controle Biológico de Pragas e Doenças do Solo
e)Controle Integrado de Pragas e Doenças do Milho.
f)Fisiologia e Ecologia de Algas Marinhas.

Projeto de Cooperação Técnica:  Através do projeto de cooperação técnica, a equipe de proteção vegetal do Ministério da Agricultura e Ambiente será capacitada no controle da atual epidemia de Paracoccus marginatus e percevejos-verdes (Nezara viridula), com o objetivo de reduzir as perdas económicas sofridas pelos agricultores.

planEntities.description:
No âmbito do projeto regional de cooperação técnica (i.e TCP/SFW/4002) serão organizadas de sessões de capacitação sobre o reconhecimento da HPAI e alerta precoce a nível nacional e na fronteira. Prevê-se fortalecer a capacidade dos técnicos laboratoriais para diagnóstico rápido e identificação de cepas do vírus HPAI, com envio dos técnicos para laboratórios regionais de referência e fornecer kits, reagentes, equipamentos de amostragem e EPIs para fortalecer a capacidade de resposta rápida dos laboratórios veterinários. Será recrutado um consultor nacional para apoiar o desenvolvimento e/ou atualização do Plano de Resposta de Emergência à Gripe Aviária.

A FAO irá também apoiar na operacionalização do Sistema Nacional de Identificação e Registo Animal (SNIRA).

No âmbito do projeto GCP/GLO/1140/USA, será reforçada a vigilância sanitária, a biossegurança e os sistemas de alerta precoce ao longo das cadeias de valor alimentar, por meio do fortalecimento de sistemas de dados e da capacitação nacional e comunitária.

planEntities.name: SIDS Adapt - O Projeto “Adaptação dos Pequenos Estados Insulares em Desenvolvimento da África Ocidental e Central (SIDS Adapt) – Reforço da Resiliência dos Sistemas Agrícolas às Alterações Climáticas” em Cabo Verde, Guiné-Bissau e São Tomé e Príncipe
planEntities.parentName: Produto 2.2.4: Os atores têm melhor acesso ao conhecimento, técnicas e tecnologias inovadoras para um planeamento territorial integrado sensível ao género, incluindo a tomada de decisões sobre o uso da terra e do mar, o funcionamento saudável dos ecossistemas e o aumento sustentável dos serviços prestados.
planEntities.description:
O programa tem duração de 6 anos, foi lançado em abril de 2025 em Praia, no Cabo Verde, e se trata de um dom regional por parte do Fundo de Adaptação, que promoverá um sistema resiliente às alterações climáticas que combina as capacidades de absorção, adaptação e transformação dos sistemas socioecológicos de Cabo Verde, Guiné-Bissau e São Tomé e Príncipe - pequenos estados insulares. O programa apoiará os sistemas agrários a recuperar de choques e pressões climáticas, ao mesmo tempo que reforça a sua capacidade de resistir positivamente aos efeitos das alterações climáticas.

O programa será estruturado em três componentes mutuamente complementares:
(i) implementação de práticas agrícolas resilientes ao clima;
(ii) reforço das capacidades para sustentar as intervenções do projeto;
(iii) monitorização, avaliação e aprendizagem.

Ao longo da planificação e da implementação de cada atividade no âmbito destes componentes, haverá uma partilha regular de informações e experiências com as diferentes partes interessadas envolvidas na resiliência climática da agricultura em Cabo Verde, Guiné-Bissau e São Tomé e Príncipe. Isto permitirá assegurar a aprendizagem contínua durante a execução do programa e que cada país beneficie das experiências e dos conhecimentos dos outros.

É importante salientar que determinadas subatividades terão lugar apenas em países específicos, como a dessalinização piloto ou as técnicas de half-moon.

planEntities.name: Políticas e programas coerentes e integrados de transição para a formalidade e trabalho digno e reforço de capacidades dos mandantes da OIT
planEntities.parentName: Produto 2.1.1: As estruturas institucionais são reforçadas e mais inclusivas, e os responsáveis ​​têm capacidades fortalecidas para um melhor ambiente de negócios, sistemas nacionais de qualidade, integração regional, uma maior contribuição da diáspora para a economia e a proteção dos direitos dos trabalhadores.
planEntities.description:
RESULTADO 1 – Os pré-requisitos para a formalização do negócio aprimorados
Produto 1.2 – Uma proposta de um sistema integrado de incentivos à formalização é validada pelas partes interessadas e implementada
Será realizado um estudo de operacionalização dos incentivos à formalização das MPE, a ser validado num workshop com a participação dos principais atores do ecossistema de formalização, incluindo os parceiros sociais. Será elaborado um roteiro para a implementação dos incentivos definindo as responsabilidades institucionais, com medidas de simplificação de procedimentos e de melhoria da comunicação. Será implementado um caso prático de operacionalização de um incentivo prioritário.

Produto 1.3 – Os indicadores sobre o setor informal são integrados nos sistemas nacionais de recolha de dados existentes
Será elaborado um Guia Metodológico dos Indicadores do Setor Informal em Cabo Verde, que irá dar diretrizes e contribuir para harmonizar o processo de coleta e análise dos dados sobre a informalidade em Cabo Verde. O mesmo será validado num workshop com as instituições produtoras de estatísticas e dados administrativos sobre o mercado de trabalho. Base empírica das políticas públicas de transição da economia informal à formal  reforçada.
Produto 1.5 - O regime jurídico especial das micro e pequenas empresas (REMPE) é reformado
Apoio técnico ao Governo no processo de aprovação do diploma que aprova a revisão do REMPE, contribuindo para reforçar a equidade fiscal, a governança e a sustentabilidade do regime. Um projeto de proposta de lei elaborada no ano de 2025).

RESULTADO 2 – A oferta de serviços de formalização de empresas é melhorada
Produto 2.1 – Uma plataforma digital de formação e informação sobre a formalização de empresas é integrada nos dispositivos digitais das instituições responsáveis pela formalização de empresas e das Câmaras de Comércio e de Turismo
Será desenvolvida integrada nos digitais das instituições do ecossistema de formalização er e operacionlizar uma plataforma digital nacional sobre formalização de empresas, com conteúdos de formação, informação prática e ferramentas de apoio, que virá reforçar a oferta de serviços de formalização.
Produto 2.2 – A Pró Empresa e outros prestadores de serviços às empresas integram o programa "Formalize a Sua Empresa" FSE nos serviços nacionais
Concluir a certificação de formadores e transferir os direitos de propriedade do programa à Pró Empresa e às Câmaras de Comércio, visando a sua institucionalização e a integração noss currículos dos cursos de empreendedorismo. Serão estabelecidos mecanismos de governança e de sustentabilidade do programa.
Produto 2.3 – As empresas informais especialmente nos municípios da Praia, Santa Catarina e Mindelo são apoiadas no seu processo de formalização
No ano de 2026, o projeto irá expandir e escalar o modelo integrado de serviços de formalização, com a oferta de serviços de proximidade e através de diversos canais, visando a formalização de no mínimo 2.000 unidades económicas nos concelhos da Praia, Santa Catarina e Mindelo. 

RESULTADO 3 – As organizações de empregadores estão em condições de influenciar a melhoria do ambiente de negócios através da advocacia, bem como de apoiar as empresas no seu processo de formalização
Produto 3.1 – As Câmaras de Comércio e de Turismo melhoram a sua capacidade de análise do ambiente empresarial e de advocacia	
As Câmaras de Comércio e de Turismo serão capacitadas em matéria de advocacy e apoiadas na realização de duas ações de plaidoyer e de diálogo público-privado a favor da melhoria do  ambiente de negócios, tendo por base o Plano de Ação com  as reformas prioritárias do ambiente empresarial.

Produto 3.3 – Os serviços oferecidos pelas Câmaras de Comércio de Sotavento e Barlavento e pela Câmara de Turismo em matéria de formalização de empresas são melhorados
As Câmaras de Comércio são apoiadas institucionalmente, nomeadamente com a certificação de formadores do programa de formação FSE, para implementar serviços integrados de apoio à formalização de 1,000 empreendedores. 

RESULTADO 4 – As organizações de trabalhadores melhoram a sua capacidade para promover o trabalho digno e apoiam os seus membros na formalização das empresas e dos seus trabalhadores
Produto 4.3 – Uma campanha nacional de sensibilização para a formalização das empresas e dos seus trabalhadores será levada a cabo
Uma campanha de sensibilização de âmbito nacional sobre os benefícios da formalização será realizada pelas duas Centrais Sindicais nacionais em parceria com o INPS e outros atores relevantes do ecossistema. Serão priorizados os grupos mais vulneráveis da população, com mensagens segmentadas e adaptadas a cada grupo. Serão utilizados canais de comunicação de massa, combinados com atividades de comunicação de proximidade.

RESULTADO 5 – A Inspeção Geral do Trabalho e a Direção Geral do Trabalho asseguram um melhor cumprimento da legislação
Produto 5.2 – A IGT é apoiada na implementação das suas atividades de promoção da Agenda para o Trabalho Digno
A IGT será apoiada no seu processo de transformação digital, com o desenvolvimento de novas funcionalidades do seu sistema de informação, contribuindo para modernizar a oferta e melhorar a oferta e qualidade dos serviços que presta. Alguns serviços passarão a estar disponíveis nos seus canais digitais, de forma acessível e inclusiva.
Produto 5.3 – Uma campanha nacional de sensibilização sobre os benefícios da formalização das empresas e dos seus trabalhadores será implementada em parceria com as duas centrais sindicais
A IGT irá desenvolver uma campanha de sensibilização, através da implementação de dois projetos-piloto setoriais de formalização nas ilhas de S. Antão no setor do aguardente, visando a formalização dos empregos, e S. Vicente visando a formalização das empresas nas áreas da mecânica e marcenaria. A abordagem  será preventiva e pedagógica com o intuito de promover uma cultura de conformidade e de cumprimento da legislação laboral.

planEntities.name: Erradicar a Pobreza Extrema através da Inclusão Socioeconómica
planEntities.parentName: Produto 2.1.1: As estruturas institucionais são reforçadas e mais inclusivas, e os responsáveis ​​têm capacidades fortalecidas para um melhor ambiente de negócios, sistemas nacionais de qualidade, integração regional, uma maior contribuição da diáspora para a economia e a proteção dos direitos dos trabalhadores.
planEntities.description:
Implementado conjuntamente pela Organização Internacional do Trabalho, o Programa das Nações Unidas para o Desenvolvimento e o Banco Mundial, o projeto tem por objetivo contribuir para acelerar a erradicação da pobreza, extrema, reforçando a inclusão económica e a estabilidade dos rendimentos das pessoas em situação de pobreza extrema, através do acesso aos mercados de trabalho e às oportunidades de autoemprego. 

Resultado (ILO): As microempresas que operam no sector informal beneficiarão de apoio à transição para o sector formal.
As Unidades de Produção Informal (UPI) tanto no meio urbano, como nas zonas rurais serão apoiadas no processo de transição da economia informal à formal, contribuindo assim para a promoção do trabalho digno. Será seguida uma abordagem integrada do processo de formalização, testada pela OIT em vários países, que inclui a componente de (i) sensibilização, (ii) formação/desenvolvimento de competências empresariais, (ii) apoio à criação e/ao registo das suas empresas (iii) assistência técnica após a formalização das suas empresas e no acesso aos incentivos, nomeadamente à proteção social.
Nesse quadro, está prevista a criação de uma base de dados administrativa, a ser alojada e gerida pela Pró Empresa em parceria com os municípios e os atores do ecossistema de formalização, com o objetivo de cartografar as UPI existentes, por ramo de atividade, permitindo obter um conhecimento aturado da problemática da informalidade, essencial para traçar estratégias de intervenção ajustadas.
Serão priorizados os grupos mais vulneráveis da economia informal. Promover-se-ão sinergias com o projeto Form@empresa, o qual trabalha ao nível da transição da economia informal à formal.

planEntities.description: O documentário incluirá uma visão histórica dos fluxos migratórios cabo-verdianos, reconhecendo as realizações mais relevantes do Governo em parceria com diferentes partes interessadas ao longo dos últimos anos. Irá também promover uma reflexão sobre a atual governação das migrações e as políticas de envolvimento da diáspora em Cabo Verde, os seus desafios e potencialidades, e também apontar alguns vectores para o futuro, com a intenção de combinar esforços e sinergias, a fim de promover o desenvolvimento sustentável

planEntities.parentName: Produto 1.1.1: As instituições nacionais, os parceiros sociais e as organizações da sociedade civil, têm maiores e melhores capacidades para fornecer, inovar e fazer parcerias para a protecção social e a proteção das crianças e adolescentes, os serviços essenciais, e sistemas de dados, monitorização e informação.
planEntities.description:
O objetivo deste programa é promover a sensibilização e a defesa da relevância da abordagem SEGURANÇA HUMANA da no contexto das múltiplas crises vividas a nível mundial, regional e nacional, numa altura em que se assiste simultaneamente a um retrocesso no desenvolvimento do processo de desenvolvimento humano humano, colocando desafios sem precedentes à humanidade. 
O UN-HABITAT promove a ampliação da metodologia desenvolvida e testada com sucesso para o programa anterior, para incorporar agora uma análise de projeto de habitação social na integra.

planEntities.description: O objetivo é implementar as recomendações para melhoria das receitas locais, traduzidas em medidas ou iniciativas que visem melhorar a conformidade voluntária, o reforço da capacidade institucional e o quadro normativo;

planEntities.name: Fontes de receita municipal e introdução  de taxas de serviços relacionados com resíduos e mecanismos de fiscalização avaliados
planEntities.parentName: Produto 2.1.1: As estruturas institucionais são reforçadas e mais inclusivas, e os responsáveis ​​têm capacidades fortalecidas para um melhor ambiente de negócios, sistemas nacionais de qualidade, integração regional, uma maior contribuição da diáspora para a economia e a proteção dos direitos dos trabalhadores.
planEntities.description: Será realizada uma avaliação detalhada das receitas locais com incidência nos quadros jurídicos, práticas institucionais e sistemas de dados, visando identificar o potencial inexplorado e lacunas no registo, avaliação, conformidade e fiscalização no município da Boa Vista. A avaliação culminará em recomendações para informar estratégias de aumento de receitas, incluindo potenciais taxas relacionadas com os resíduos. O objetivo geral é garantir que a Câmara Municipal da Boa Vista terá capacidade financeira para participar de forma sustentável na Parceria Público Privada.

planEntities.name: Plano de melhoria da gestão de resíduos elaborado e adotado com base nas conclusões da ferramenta Waste Wise Cities.
planEntities.parentName: Produto 2.2.3: Os quadros jurídicos e de planeamento são melhorados e melhor implementados com abordagens participativas na gestão do ambiente e dos recursos naturais, incluindo energia limpa acessível e preparação e resposta a choques.
planEntities.description: Com base na ferramenta Waste Wise Cities, será realizada uma avaliação do sistema de resíduos sólidos da ilha da Boa Vista, abrangendo a geração de resíduos, a recolha, as práticas de eliminação e a fuga para o ambiente. A avaliação produzirá dados que servirão de base para (i) o estudo de viabilidade para a criação de uma PPP e promover a economia circular na ilha; (ii) a adoção de medidas destinadas a melhorar a prestação de serviços, a recuperação de recursos e minimizar impactos no ambiente.
