planEntities.name: 2.1.1.18 Strengthening Digital Solutions and technologies for Innovative, Resilient and Climate-smart , nutrition sensitive and inclusive agrifood systems
planEntities.parentName: Output 2.1.1: Institutions and Small-holder Farmers and Processors Strengthened to Deliver Sustained Food Production Systems that are Innovative, Resilient and Climate-smart for Enhanced Access to Food and Prevent Malnutrition, Especially within Vulnerable Communities.
planEntities.description: This involves harnessing information and communication technologies (ICTs), data-driven tools, and precision agriculture applications to enhance productivity, improve climate adaptation, and optimize resource use along agricultural value chains. By integrating weather advisory services, market information systems, e-extension platforms, digital financial services, and early warning systems, farmers and agri-entrepreneurs—especially women and youth—can make informed decisions, access vital services, and build resilience against climate shocks. These digital innovations also support nutrition-sensitive agriculture by promoting diversified and sustainable food production practices, ultimately contributing to improved food security and livelihoods in rural communities.

planEntities.name: 2.2.1.18 Building the Capacity of Public Institutions  and farmers organizations to Implement National Adaptation Plan.
planEntities.parentName: Output 2.2.1: Human and Institutional Capacities of Public and Private Institutions at Federal, State and LGA Levels Strengthened to Develop and Implement Risk Management and (National) Adaptation Plans to Mitigate for Impact of Climate Change.
planEntities.description: This involves strengthening institutional frameworks, policy alignment, and operational systems at national, state, and local levels to mainstream climate adaptation priorities into agricultural and rural development programmes. Equally important is equipping farmers' organizations with the knowledge, tools, and leadership skills to actively participate in policy dialogues, advocate for their needs, and implement climate-resilient farming practices. Through tailored training, strategic partnerships, and inclusive platforms, this capacity-building effort ensures that both government institutions and community-based groups can collaboratively drive climate adaptation actions, enhance food security, and protect livelihoods, particularly for vulnerable populations.

planEntities.description:
The Internal Displacement Solutions Fund (IDSF) is a newly designed program that has the explicit objective to support authorities in achieving Solutions for their displacement affected communities. The launch of the program in Nigeria coincides with the launch of the State Action Plans, offering an opportune set-up for the IDSF to support the Federal and State authorities in operationalizing the State Action Plans. 
IOM will be contributing to -	Data stewardship for evidence-based government interventions

planEntities.name: 4.1.1.2b Social cohesion platforms and peace committees established to promote reintegration and reconciliation process of the former low-risk associates to Non State Armed Groups (NSAGs) (IOM)
planEntities.parentName: Output 4.1.1: Strengthened Systems, Institutions, and Capacities for Humanitarian Action and Transitioning to Development Solutions, and for Inclusive and Gender Responsive Peace Building.
planEntities.description:
The project contribute to the successful inclusive and gender-responsive community-driven reintegration and reconciliation of former armed non-state combatants and Boko Haram associates (men, women, and children) in the North-East of Nigeria.
The Project  emphasizes the importance of resolving the backlog of cases of over 4,200 former members of Boko Haram who are currently in detention in a timely manner, ensuring accountability for the most serious offenses according to UN and international standards.
IOM is actively involved in community sensitization and reconciliation efforts

It seeks to enhance labour migration governance, improve protection mechanisms for Nigerian migrant workers abroad, and facilitate safe, orderly, and regular migration pathways.

planEntities.parentName: Output 1.2.2 Strengthened Capacity of Public and Private Sectors, and Civil Society Organisations to Implement Responsive Employment Programmes and Initiatives Including on Digital Skills and Green Economy.
planEntities.description: This activities aim to strengthen labour migration governance and ethical recruitment systems by fostering partnerships among government institutions, private sector actors, destination countries, and training institutions; enhancing the capacities of labour recruitment and oversight institutions to promote compliance with ethical recruitment standards and protect migrant workers' rights; engaging employers and businesses to adopt responsible labour practices and human-rights-based approaches; and strengthening TVET institutions through institutional, infrastructural, and curriculum improvements to align skills development with labour market needs and create sustainable pathways to traineeships and employment opportunities.

planEntities.name: 1.2.3.5-Strengthen the capacity of MRCs in irregular migration hotspots in the Northern region of Nigeria and provide additional support to MRCs in Abuja, Lagos, Edo and Nasarawa States, so they can better respond to training needs, skills development and placement, and facilitate information on regular migration opportunities.
planEntities.parentName: Output 1.2.3: Improved Access to Markets and Financial Services for Women, Youth, Older Persons, Persons with Disabilities and Other Vulnerable Groups.
planEntities.description: This activity promotes the rights of migrants and potential migrants by strengthening access to accurate information, skills development opportunities, and employment support through Migration Resource Centres (MRCs). By enhancing the capacity of MRCs, the activity contributes to informed decision-making, reducing migrants' vulnerability to exploitation, trafficking, abuse, and unsafe migration practices. Services are delivered in a non-discriminatory and inclusive manner, ensuring that women, men, youth, persons with disabilities, and other vulnerable groups have equitable access to information and support. The activity empowers individuals to exercise their right to make informed choices about migration and livelihoods while strengthening access to services that support safe, orderly, and regular migration pathways. Accountability and referral mechanisms are integrated to ensure that migrants can access appropriate protection and support services when needed.

planEntities.description: The project “Circular and POPs-free Plastics in Africa” is a regional UNEP project funded by the Global Environment Facility (GEF). This project is to be implemented in Nigeria, Kenya, South Africa, Uganda, and Zimbabwe. The objective of the project is to reduce the use of persistent organic pollutants (POPs) in plastics-containing products and unintentional persistent organic pollutants (uPOPs)  generation by applying circular economy approaches through the development of strategies targeting plastics containing POPs, circular economy practices to reduce pollution from plastics containing POPs, environmental sound management of plastics containing waste and Knowledge management, capacity building, and communication. The implementation of this project is anticipated to begin in Nigeria in 2025, and it is currently in project preparation.

planEntities.description: The Africa POPs in plastics project aims to reduce the releases of Persistent Organic Pollutants (POPs) from plastic products in the African continent. Three sectors were prioritized in five countries: automotives (Kenya, South Africa), construction (Zimbabwe) and electronics (Nigeria, Uganda). Project interventions intend to reduce the import, production and use of POPs in plastic-containing products, and the generation of POPs and greenhouse gases (GHG) in these sectors. The project will work with governments to adopt and enforce upstream policies and financial instruments; with plastic product designers, manufacturers and assemblers to implement circular economy practices and eliminate/replace problematic products with more sustainable alternatives; and with recyclers and collectors to separate hazardous plastics fractions and increase awareness.

planEntities.parentName: Output 3.2.1: Education Systems Capacity is Strengthened to Plan, Implement and Monitor the Delivery of Basic Quality Inclusive Education for Skills and Knowledge Acquisition Including in Humanitarian Situations.
planEntities.description:
Beyond the effect of COVID-19, inclusion in education is further challenged in Nigeria due to emerging insecurities that have threatened the safety of schools and ultimately denying some learners their right to education. As a result of the crises of insecurity, children of school age in some parts of Nigeria, particularly the Northern region have limited and in some cases no access to school. More worrisome, is the plight of learners with special needs, as infrastructure/equipment to aid their learnings are not available. The increasing emergencies that interrupt school systems and ultimately learning requires systemic preparedness that will ensure that learning continues without leaving anyone behind.

 It is in this regards that the implementation of the right to education, including creating lifelong learning opportunities will be pursued within the 42 C5 programmes and activities. To achieve this, UNEESCO will strengthen partnerships and networks to promote cross-sectoral collaboration that will stimulate technical dialogues, policies and practices that assures the learning needs of marginalized groups.
ICH will be addressed through Education, and States including the FCT, would be engaged to review ESP to ensure inclusive education is mainstreamed and budgeted for. Cross-sectoral collaboration with health, nutrition and social protection will be encouraged.

With number of crises affected areas increasing, there is need to apply the inclusive approach to education system and ensure no one is left behind. UNESCO is committed to taking concerted action to eliminate all forms of exclusions and marginalization, to uphold the right to education for all, to address disparities and inequalities in access, and in quality of learning, as well as to build education systems that are resilient and responsive to contemporary challenges. It implies focusing on those at greatest risk of being left behind and addressing inequalities in the education policies and practices. In view of this, UNESCO Abuja would:

i.      Support multistakeholder dialogues on facilitating inclusive education in Nigeria.
ii.    Work with the Nigeria’s Governors forum to advocate for policies and practices that promotes inclusive education in all states of the federation.
iii.   Support technical dialogues for addressing the learning needs of marginalized groups through inclusive policies.
iv. Support states to review and or development an ESP that ensures that inclusion is mainstreamed and budgeted for.

planEntities.name: 2.1.2.1; Establishment of Bio-buisnesses and GEBR livelihoods in two Biosphere Reserves and one protected site in Nigeria (Oban Biosphere Reserve, Omo Biosphere Reserve (BR) and Shere Hills Forest Reserve
planEntities.parentName: Output 2.1.2: Control of Desertification, Degradation and Ensuring Sustainable Forest Management.
planEntities.description:
The goal of the project is to reduce poverty and contribute to sustainable development and biodiversity in Omo Biosphere Reserve, Oban Biosphere Reserve in Nigeria, and Shere Hills Reserve through the establishment of green economy activities, with a focus on youth and women. Objectives are to -
1) Diversify and improve local economy through improved and alternative green biodiversity related livelihoods.
2) Build the capacity of communities in a holistic manner to ensure the sustainability of the biodiversity businesses,
3) Enable completion of nomination dossier for Shere Hills Reserve to join the World Network of Biosphere reserve

The project will be articulated along one outcomes and several outputs and activities, as described below.
 
Outcome 1: Reduce anthropogenic pressure on the forest, preserve biodiversity, diversify the local economy and improve biodiversity-related livelihoods.
 
This outcome will be achieved through the following outputs and activities.Output 1.1:   strengthened capacity of the Ministry of Environment, Forestry Research institute of Nigeria, National MAB committee, National Park Service and indeed other relevant stakeholders  to continue to provide support to community partners even after the end of the project funding.
 
Activity 1.1.1:   Inauguration of Project
Activity 1.1.2:   Capacity building on GEBR and conservation concepts 
 
Output 1.2:  Improved knowledge on socio-economic, biodiversity and market aspects available to stakeholders
 
Activity 1.2.1:  Stakeholder mapping, Community consultation and needs assessment;
Activity 1.2.2 : Socio-economic survey/Inquiry;
Activity 1.2.3:  Biodiversity  inventory (Biosphere Reserve/Protected area);
Activity 1.2.4:  Market Survey and Product analyses;
Activity 1.2.5: Validation workshop.
 
Output 1.3: Local communities have enhanced capacity to reduce their environmental impact, develop alternative livelihood activities, and manage their biodiversity businesses including accounting, product marketing, packaging, sales and use and maintenance of simple business equipment.
 
Activity 1.3.1: Training on environmental education - management and biodiversity conservation.
Activity 1.3.2:  Training on business management, processes and bookkeeping.
Activity 1.3.3:  Small business incubation support through hands-on training and coaching on business start-up processes.
Activity 1.3.4: Technical training on the use and maintenance of simple biodiversity business equipment.
 
Output 1.4 :  Alternative livelihoods established and economy diversified
 
Activity 1.4.1: Procurement of tools and appliances, or simple inputs for the establishment of selected biodiversity livelihood activities;
Activity 1.4.2:  Facilitation for the establishment of selected biodiversity livelihoods in target areas (at least 30% Female and 20% youth);
Activity 1.4.3: Comprehensive start-up business incubation services, coaching and mentoring of project participants on the management of their biodiversity livelihood activities.
Activity 1.4.4. Support business networks development, including towards access to micro-finance, cooperatives, development of sales channels, profit re-investment, and knowledge of vendors and providers for inputs.
 
Output 1.5 :  Designation of Shere Hills Reserve as a Biosphere Reserve in the World Network of Biosphere Reserve (WNBR)  
Activity 1.5.1: Production of zonation Maps  
Activity 1.5.2:  Consultations with the communities
Activity 1.5.3 Completion and processing of Biosphere reserve nomination dossier
Implementation strategy.
Activity 1.1.1-2 Inauguration and capacity building at National authorities’ level
 At inauguration, the project will be presented to the relevant stakeholders and partners; while also receiving inputs on strategies of implementation and their roles. Following the inauguration, the next activity will be a capacity building on the concept of GEBR; for the Ministry of Environment, Forestry Research institute of Nigeria, National MAB committee, National Park Service and indeed other relevant stakeholders to continue to provide support to community partners even after the end of the project funding. This will ensure sustainability of the project activities.
Activities 1.2.1-4:  Mapping and assessments
 The mapping and assessment is aimed at ensuring the full involvement of the target communities in the framework of the opportunities offered by the natural environment in the selected areas. This first activity is about identifying and bringing together community partners and all relevant stakeholders, to discuss and develop a shared vision for the whole project and the prospective biodiversity business. Stakeholder aspirations, roles, responsibilities and capacities in the project will be reviewed. The project will take stock of the indigenous knowledge of the communities, and this will be an invaluable tool for the choice of the biodiversity businesses.
 
The second activity will be a socio-economic survey and needs assessment. The main objective of the study is to provide baseline data on the socio-economic status of the local communities, which will serve as the benchmark for measuring the project impacts[1]. Information on livelihoods, gender perspectives and natural resource utilization in the target sites will be gathered.
 
The third activity will be the Biosphere Reserve Assessment and Inventory. An in-depth assessment and biological inventory exercise will be carried out for all the target intervention areas with the specific aim of obtaining the biodiversity index of the park.  The results of the inventory will guide the choice and design of biodiversity business initiatives in the different areas. It will also guide the delineation of the proposed biosphere reserve (core, buffer and transition zones), which will be instrumental for the Biosphere Reserve nomination dossiers.
 
The fourth and last activity is Market Survey and Product Analyses. This activity is aimed at ensuring that careful analyses of the opportunities and limitations involved with the biodiversity business are carried out.  This would include the review of markets, availability and sustainability of resources, environmental, infrastructural and policy and other barriers to the development of the business. Special attention will be given to the involvement of the private sector, of business intermediaries and on the logistic aspects of the market analysis.
 
Activity 1.2.5: Validation/launch workshops
After the start-up phase and studies, 2 validation workshops will be organized (one per site) to bring together all relevant stakeholders to validate the results of all socio-economic, market and biodiversity studies. Community leaders and potential community partners and project beneficiaries will be sensitized and confirm their engagement in the implementation of project activities. During the workshop, the selection of the livelihood business will be confirmed by all stakeholders.
  
Activities 1.3.1-4:  Capacity building at community level
As emerges from the livelihood analysis, capacity building is an important element in supporting new and improved livelihoods for local communities.  Communities in both sites will be trained in a variety of practical skills for the development and management of their selected biodiversity businesses. In addition to the skills necessary to undertake production, community partners will acquire skills in the fields of accounting, marketing, packaging of their products, managing their business and re-investing their business profit. Different training sessions will be organized on the following topics:
1.	Environmental and biodiversity conservation education;
2.	Accounting, marketing and packaging;
3.	Hands on training on implementation of alternative livelihood activities;
4.	Technical training on the use and maintenance of the equipment.
 To ensure that capacity is strengthened at different levels, additional training materials would be developed in a language and style that corresponds to the literacy level of stakeholders and community partners. Ultimately, communities will be trained to monitor and manage the natural resources on which their business depends. Conservation and environmental education will therefore be an integral part of this project. This will ensure that the link between biodiversity conservation and development is maintained. Community members will also learn to continuously re-invest part of their income to ensure the sustainability of their subsistence revenues.
 
Activities 1.4.1-4:  Implementation of green economy activities. 
A business implementation structure will be drawn up and the service or production will be rolled out. The community partners and beneficiaries will be provided with start-up support and inputs for their businesses in the form of tools and equipment. Relevant items will be purchased and distributed and community partners will receive training on how to use them. For example, those who will choose a livelihood such as beekeeping will receive improved hives, protective clothing and other tools for harvesting honey.
 
The plan will also include various approaches towards attracting other investors. Suitable assessed Green businesses mostly preferred by women and the youth will be targeted so that at least 30% of community partners are female and 30% are youth. Incentives and benefit sharing mechanisms will be developed and will be engrained in the business structure and model of the enterprises that will be run by community partners in the form of cooperatives, or of small family businesses. This will ensure that hard working individuals are not only remunerated but are also incentivized. Project beneficiaries will be encouraged to form Cooperative Associations based on their livelihoods to ensure accountability, ownership and sustainability of their businesses.
 
Activity 1.5.1-3
Biosphere reserves promote solutions reconciling the conservation of biodiversity with its sustainable use. They are learning areas for sustainable development under diverse ecological, social and economic contexts, touching the lives of people that leave within its vicinity. Biosphere Reserves allow through research, the recreation of landscapes that have been affected by human activity, identify species that have disappeared, monitor climate change processes, for seeking recovery of ecosystems and their components and make better decisions. Considering that framework of Biosphere Reserve can guide and reinforce and sustain projects that enhance livelihoods, it will be useful to designate the Shere Hills Reserve as a Biosphere reserve. SHR is already a protected area and as such the project team with work with the Nigeran National MAB committee to use exiting and approved Guidelines to process the designation of SHR as a Biosphere reserve. This process include producing zonation maps (Maps of the core, buffer and transition zones), holding at least 4 consultation meetings and thorough completion of the Biosphere reserve nomination forms

planEntities.name: 2.1.2.2; Support  Nigeria to complete and submit dossier for designation of  biosphere reserves; in order to increase the number of BRs for sustainable development
planEntities.parentName: Output 2.1.2: Control of Desertification, Degradation and Ensuring Sustainable Forest Management.
planEntities.description:
Rationale 
Halting biodiversity loss is a Sustainable Development Goal (SDG 15), one that is strongly linked to all other SDGs. Keeping ecosystems resilient and safeguarding the planet’s biodiversity is fundamental to poverty eradication, human health and wellbeing.   The UNESCO  MAB Programme and the World Network of Biosphere Reserve (WNBR) aligned closely with the functions of BRs as set out in the Statutory Framework aligned closely with the functions of BRs as set out in the Statutory Framework aligned closely with the functions of BRs as set out in the Statutory Framework aligned closely with the functions of BRs as set out in the Statutory Framework serve this vision both within and beyond the boundaries of biosphere reserves. The Hangzhou MAB Strategic Action Plan for 2026– 2035 articulates this vision through four main approaches.  Biosphere reserves provide opportunities for local communities to experiment with sustainable development and conservation (5). Experiences from BRs can help shape national policy and contribute to learning for GBF implementation across territories and designations. As unique institutional infrastructures all over the world, BRs are suitable places for monitoring and testing indicators for target follow-up within a global network to mobilize knowledge for impact. Biosphere Reserves can be round table institutions which bring multiple actors to work together for conservation and sustainability in their territories. As such, Biosphere Reserves are well-positioned places to contribute to achieving the GBF targets by providing innovative solutions that balance ecological integrity with human well-being. The GBF objectives of (1) working to reduce threats to biodiversity (Targets 1-8), (2) meeting people’s needs through sustainable use and benefit t-sharing (Targets 9-13) and (3) providing tools for implementation and mainstreaming of biodiversity (Targets 14-23) are aligned closely with the functions of BRs as set out in the Statutory Framework. The designation of more BRs will certainly enhance Nigeria’s implementation of the KGBF. 
Geopark provides bottom-up approach by combining conservation with sustainable development while involving local communities is becoming increasingly popular. 2024-2025 biennium (42 C/5) provided a valid platform for Nigeria to start up activities towards the possibility of applying for a UNESCO Global Geopark (UGGp) as well as participate in IGCP projects. UNESCO worked with the Nigerian National Commission for UNESCO (NatCom-UNESCO) to Inaugurate the International Geoscience and Geopark Programme – Nigeria National Committee (IGGP-NNC), as a first principal and necessary step to enable application for geopark. The capacity of members of the IGGP-NNC was strengthened on the fundamentals of UNESCO Global Geoparks concept and International Geoparks Programme (IGGP), as well as on the operational Guidelines applications for UNESCO Global Geoparks.  The IGGP-NNC supported the submission of research proposal by Nigerian geo-scientists for the UNESCO IGCP programme funding, and thankfully one has been approved tiled “Hydrogeological and Climate Impact Assessment of Groundwaters and Ecosystems in Dahomey Basin and West Africa“  by Prof. Moshood Tijani o University of Ibadan- Nigeria. in 43 C/5 it will be apt to scale up actions that will enable Nigeria to undertake a Geo-heritage survey which is a prerequisite for identifying sites for geopark and a necessary document in the application for Geoparks. 

Description of workplan 
Overriding objective 
Biosphere Reserves and Global Geoparks as drivers of sustainable development and global climate action
The overriding objective of the workplan is to support actions geared towards nomination of Biosphere Reserves for fast tracking Nigeria’s implementation of the Kunming Global Biodiversity Framework (KGBF) well as kick start activities required for application of a geopark 
 
Activities 
The workplan comprise two activities
i)	UNESCO Man and Biosphere Workshop 
-	Validate Nomination dossier for two (2) proposed biosphere reserves – Gashaka Gumti National Park and Okumo Nationla Park 
-	Fund mobilisation for Biodiversity Businesses in Biosphere reserves 
-	Presentation of zero draft nomination dossier for Old Oyo National Park 

ii)	Support an enlarged meeting of International Geoscience and Geopark Programme – Nigeria National Committee (IGGP-NNC),
-	Development of plan and strategy IGGP-NNC activities including Geo-Heritage survey 
-	Fund mobilization for Geo-heritage survey and green activities in identified Geo-sites

planEntities.name: 2.1.4.1; Supporting Water security in Nigeria, based on Science for Mitigation, Adaptation, and Resilience
planEntities.parentName: Output 2.1.4: Improvement of the Capacity to Ensure Integrated Water Resource Management at all Levels Including Transboundary Cooperation or Restoration of Water Related Ecosystems.
planEntities.description:
Citizen science approaches and Climate Risk Informed Decision Analysis (CRIDA) methodology for sustainable water management under climate change, 

The Activity aim to strengthen the sustainable water management of the Kaduna River Basin and Lower Benue Basin by Integrating the Climate Risk Informed Decision Analysis (CRIDA) methodology with citizen science to help strengthen capacity for addressing extreme climate risks, monitor water quality, and fill data gaps for sustainable water management. in the Kaduna River Basin and/or Lower Benue Basin
Two main activities will be implemented
1) IHP committee, stakeholder and local community engagement on sustainable water management under climate change as well capacity building on CRIDA; and
2) Mini Pilot CRIDA vulnerability assessment using the Kaduna river and/or lower Benue Basin - Application of CRIDA Methodology

nstitutional capacity for hydrological data collection in Nigeria is often stretched across large basins. By utilizing a "bottom-up" vulnerability approach, the UNESCO CRIDA methodology will help identify where the system breaks under climate uncertainty (such as extreme dry spells or flash floods) without needing massive computational power. Citizen science, on the other hand, fills the local data gaps, turning river users and residents into active stakeholders and fostering sustainable water malmanagement. The workplan will focus on the Kaduna River Basin and/or Lower Benue Basin which are impacted by climate change. The kaduna River Basin and/or Lower Benue Basin support livelihood and agricultural activities, as such, climate impact could result to food scarcity and loss of livelihoods



The Workplan aim to strengthen the sustainable water management of the Kaduna River Basin and/or Lower Benue Basin by Integrating the Climate Risk Informed Decision Analysis (CRIDA) methodology with citizen science to help strengthen capacity stakeholders and local community for addressing extreme climate risks, monitor water quality, and fill data gaps for sustainable water management. in the Kaduna River Basin and/or Lower Benue Basin   

Two main sub-activities  will be implemented 
1) IHP committee, stakeholder and local community engagement on sustainable water management under climate change as well capacity building on CRIDA; and 

2) Mini Pilot CRIDA vulnerability assessment using the Kaduna river and/or lower Benue Basin - Application of CRIDA Methodology

planEntities.name: 2.1.4.4. Supporting Ground Water Governance and IWRM in Nigeria
planEntities.parentName: Output 2.1.4: Improvement of the Capacity to Ensure Integrated Water Resource Management at all Levels Including Transboundary Cooperation or Restoration of Water Related Ecosystems.
planEntities.description:
UNESCO Abuja is joining efforts with the National Water Resources Institute, Kaduna, Nigeria, to implement the project “Improving Groundwater Governance towards achieving Sustainable Water Security for Human Settlements in Nigeria” in the framework of UNESCO/K-FIT Project “Water Security for Human Settlements in Developing Countries under Climate Change”. 

The project has the overall objective of improving knowledge-based management and governance of groundwater resources to support Nigeria in achieving sustainable water security for human settlements as well as build resilience to the impact of climate change. 

Specific objectives include: 
a)	 A desktop review of studies on the effects of climate change on the Nigeria’s Ground water resources ((effect of climate change on quality and availability; implications  for human settlements; and suggestions  of climate friendly infrastructure); 
b)	Develop guidelines and tools for improving groundwater governance for water security and building resilience of urban Human settlement against the impact of climate change 
c)	Strengthen the human resources capacity of the Nigerian groundwater experts on the tools developed (Strategy/guidelines and plans) so as to ensure sustainability of the project beyond UNESCO's support. 
a)	Produce publication with main results of the project for dissemination beyond the proposed capacity building and workshops.  

The Specific objectives are the following  
a)	A desktop review of studies on the effects of climate change on the Nigeria’s Ground water resources ((effect of climate change on quality and availability; implications  for human settlements; and suggestions  of climate friendly infrastructure); 
In achieving this objective, all relevant stakeholders will be brought together in an inception meeting to introduce the project and also gather information and inputs that will help in the successful implementation of the project. Drawing from the inception activities, a TORs will be developed for comprehensive desktop review of studies that has been done on comprehensive desktop review of studies that has been done on effect of climate change on quality and availability of groundwater; with respect to its implications for human settlements; and suggestion on sustainable and climate friendly infrastructure- such infrastructure that will enhance sustainability. The report of this review/information will be very useful for the development of methods for tools and guidelines as well as contribute to achieving Output 1  
b)	Develop guidelines and tools for improving groundwater governance for water security and building resilience of Human settlement against the impact of climate change 
In addition to the important report of Output 1, a baseline documentation/report of exiting National Frameworks on Groundwater governance in Nigeria, will be commissioned at the end of which a comprehensive report will be obtained. This report together with report of Output 1, will form the basis of the Development of tools that can be implemented on the groundwater resources on Nigeria; in order to build resilience of Human settlement against the impact of climate change. These tools which contributes to achieving output 2, will complement and upgrade/improve existing ones in the country and will include i) strategy/guidelines to improve governance and ii) recommendation on Infrastructures for sustainable management of Groundwater iii) recommendation of future work. In order for the tools to have national acceptability, it will be validated in a national expert meeting.
c)	Strengthen the human resources capacity of the Nigerian groundwater experts on the tools developed (Strategy/guidelines and plans) so as to ensure sustainability of the project beyond UNESCO's support. 
To achieve this objective a comprehensive training will be organised for Groundwater experts, Water engineers, decision and policy makers in the water sector. 20 participants will be drawn per city for the 8 cities: totalling 120. Consideration will be given to gender; ensuring the participation of women experts. The participants will be trained on the guidelines and tools (Strategy/guidelines and plans) developed. At the end of the training output 3 will be achieved – “Capacity of the 160 Nigerian groundwater experts from the focused towns   strengthened, to use the Guidelines and tools developed   so as to ensure sustainability of the project beyond UNESCO's support” Produce publication with main results of the project for dissemination beyond the proposed capacity building and workshops. 
d)	Produce publication with main results of the project for dissemination beyond the proposed capacity building and workshops
The result of the work will be put in a publishable format, that can be disseminated; thus, enabling the result of the project to be shared and referenced   

To allow for effective monitoring, there will be bimonthly meeting of the [project team to review progress  

Outcome N°1: Nigeria Groundwater governance improved to achieve water security for Human settlements as well as build their resilience against climate change.

Output N°2:  Guidelines and Tools for improving groundwater governance for water security and building resilience against the impact of climate change.

To promote the implementation of the UNESCO 2021 recommendation on Open Science as well as Establish protocols and build trust that can facilitate establishment of platforms for Scientific knowledge sharing under the context of Open Science and strengthened STI Policy 

Description 
In Nigerian, it has been observed that access to scientific literature, data, and tools is often restricted, thus hindering the progress of research and development of industry that can enhance job creation. Embracing open science can break down these barriers by making information freely available, leveling the playing field for researchers in the country. This democratization of knowledge can empower Nigerian scientists to tackle local challenges, such as public health issues and environmental concerns, with the support of a broader scientific community, as well as strengthen the production sector for new job for teaming young professionals in the country. 

To this end the Workplan, “Strengthening the implementation of 2021 UNESCO recommendation on Open Science, for jobs of the future and sustainable development in Nigeria”, will be implemented within the framework of the UNESCO  C/5  programme. Activities will be implemented to Promote a common understanding of Open Science among Nigerian STI experts, enable the right STI policy environment for the implementation of Open Science and having initial actions for creating a Nigerian wide platform for knowledge sharing under the context of Open Science; as well as strengthen Nigerian STI Policy Implementation

planEntities.name: 2.1.4.5b: Reducing Risks of Floods, Drought, and Biodiversity disruption in Nigeria
planEntities.parentName: Output 2.1.4: Improvement of the Capacity to Ensure Integrated Water Resource Management at all Levels Including Transboundary Cooperation or Restoration of Water Related Ecosystems.
planEntities.description:
The activity aim to strengthen information, preparedness, and institutional capacities in Nigeria to reduce the risks and impacts of floods, drought, and biodiversity disruption, with focus on high-risk states and frontline communities.

The workplan combines knowledge generation, capacity development, and multi-stakeholder engagement, leveraging SC approaches to disaster and climate risk reduction

I-	Rationale  

Nigeria faces increasing climate-related hazards, with floods, drought, and biodiversity disruption threatening millions of people, livelihoods, and ecosystems. Over the past decade, floods have affected over 7 million people, causing fatalities, displacement, and infrastructure damage. Niger State, along the Niger River basin, is particularly vulnerable. On 28–29 May 2025, flash floods in Mokwa caused 206 deaths, 1,000 missing persons, and displaced 3,000 residents, disrupting transport links and markets critical for local livelihoods.

Drought and land degradation have impacted 43% of Nigeria’s landmass (~923,000 km²), disrupting the livelihoods of over 40 million Nigerians, increasing resource-based conflicts (e.g., farmer-herder clashes), and negatively affecting biodiversity. Despite government efforts, gaps remain in early warning interpretation, community awareness, preparedness, and integration of climate risk into policies and local development planning.

With the rainy season, recurrent floods, droughts, and biodiversity disruptions present a heightened emergency risk. This workplan addresses these risks by strengthening relevant capacities, promoting resilient communities, and linking local preparedness with national policy and SDG targets.

II-	Objective

To strengthen information, preparedness, and institutional capacities in Nigeria to reduce the risks and impacts of floods, drought, and biodiversity disruption, with focus on high-risk states and frontline communities.

 Iii  Sub Activities 
•	Supporting Awareness and Community Dialogue
•	Fostering local ownership and participation in climate risk reduction projects. -– Develop a project for Adaptation fund
•	Capacity Development and Proactive Risk Management

Expected Results :
1) Enhanced preparedness and capacity of Nigerian experts and institutions to mitigate floods, drought, and biodiversity disruption.
2) Strengthened community awareness and participation in climate risk reduction initiatives.
3) Improved integration of early warning systems into policies and local response planning.
4) Mobilization of at least one national project for implementation and funding

planEntities.name: 2.1.4.5c: Strengthening flood resilience in Nigeria to foster long-term societal stability – Focus on Niger State
planEntities.parentName: Output 2.1.4: Improvement of the Capacity to Ensure Integrated Water Resource Management at all Levels Including Transboundary Cooperation or Restoration of Water Related Ecosystems.
planEntities.description:
Strengthening flood resilience in Nigeria to foster long-term societal stability – Focus on Niger State

This project is designed as a short-term, non-infrastructure intervention focused on strengthening flood preparedness, institutional coordination, and climate-informed decision-making in Niger State, with a particular focus on Mokwa Local Government Area. The intervention prioritizes capacity

Outcome 1: - Enhanced resilience and adaptive capacity in Niger State through strengthened institutional capacities and community preparedness for flood risk management, leading to reduced loss of life, protection of livelihoods and infrastructure, and improved investment decisions for long-term resilience.

Output 1.1: Community awareness and local capacity for flood preparedness strengthened.
- Activity 1.1.1: Inception meeting at state and federal levels to formally launch the project, ensure stakeholder buy-in, and clarify institutional roles and coordination mechanisms.
- Activity 1.1.2: Flood awareness campaigns conducted in flood-prone communities, including Mokwa and surrounding LGAs, using simple visual materials to communicate flood risks, early warning signals, and safe response measures, with particular attention to displaced youth and vulnerable groups.
- Activity 1.1.3: Training of youth, teachers, and local volunteers as community focal points to support basic rainfall and river monitoring and to relay early warning messages through trusted local channels.

Verifiable outputs: One inception workshop conducted; awareness campaigns delivered; trained community focal points actively engaged

Output 1.2: Institutional coordination on flood early warning and preparedness strengthened.
- Activity 1.2.1: Organization of one technical dialogue at state and national levels, bringing together relevant government agencies, technical institutions, the Ecological Project Office, development partners, and selected private sector actors to review recent flood impacts, identify preparedness and financing gaps, and agree on priority flood resilience actions.
- Activity 1.2.2: Preparation of a concise, investment-oriented technical note outlining at least two priority flood resilience initiatives, designed to inform future funding decisions and partnerships.

Verifiable outputs: One multi-stakeholder technical dialogue conducted; one validated investment-oriented note produced

Output 1.3: Climate Risk–Informed Decision Analysis (CRIDA) conducted on a pilot basis and translated into actionable guidance.
- Activity 1.3.1: Training of a core group of researchers and technical staff in Niger State on the CRIDA methodology and its application to flood risk management.
- Activity 1.3.2: Application of the CRIDA methodology to assess past flood events, current exposure, and future climate risks in the Mokwa pilot area, with results synthesized into decision-relevant guidance for authorities.
- Activity 1.3.3: Design and guidance for community-based demonstration activities on very low-cost, community-managed nature-based solutions—such as riverbank and floodplain vegetation restoration and vegetated buffer zones—aimed at reducing surface runoff and localized flood impacts.

Verifiable outputs: Trained CRIDA core team; completed pilot CRIDA analysis with actionable recommendations; implemented pilot nature-based solutions

TARGETS AND INDICATORS:
By the end of the project, at least five communities and approximately 500 people will have enhanced flood preparedness awareness, with at least 40% women and 30% youth participation. One validated coordination and investment note will be produced. Up to 30 national experts will be trained on CRIDA, and one pilot CRIDA application will be completed in Mokwa.

-	Enhanced government capacity for coordination, leadership, and resource mobilization on the federal, state and local levels; (UNDP)

planEntities.name: 4.1.1.10d Joint Durable Solutions MPTFO Project under ASG Robert Piper. (UNICEF)
planEntities.parentName: Output 4.1.1: Strengthened Systems, Institutions, and Capacities for Humanitarian Action and Transitioning to Development Solutions, and for Inclusive and Gender Responsive Peace Building.
planEntities.description:
The Internal Displacement Solutions Fund (IDSF) is a newly designed program that has the explicit objective to support authorities in achieving Solutions for their displacement affected communities. The launch of the program in Nigeria coincides with the launch of the State Action Plans, offering an opportune set-up for the IDSF to support the Federal and State authorities in operationalizing the State Action Plans. 
Concretely, the IDSF in Nigeria has 3 thematic focuses:
-	Enhanced government capacity for coordination, leadership, and resource mobilization on the federal, state and local levels; (UNDP)
-	Data stewardship for evidence-based government interventions (IOM)
-	A more effective state government IDP approach through enhanced protection support. (UNHCR)
-	UNMAS, FAO and UNICEF to complement each pillar

planEntities.name: 4.3.2.6b Joint Programme on the Elimination of Female Genital Mutilation: Delivering the Global Promise to End FGM (UNICEF))
planEntities.parentName: Output 4.3.2: Strengthened Mechanisms and Capacities of Actors and Institutions (Government and Non-government) to Address Discriminatory Gender and Social Norms, and Harmful Practices, Including Child Marriage and Female Genital Mutilation.
planEntities.description: The Joint Programme aimed at ending the practice of FGM in Nigeria and globally. The programme addresses FGM as a harmful violation of human rights. It combines advocacy, community engagement, and policy reforms to promote gender equality and women and girl’s empowerment. The programme works closely with governments, civil society organizations, and local communities to raise awareness, implement legal frameworks, and provide services for the protection of girls at risk. By strengthening social and institutional mechanisms, it addresses behavioural change and shifts social norms to accelerate the abandonment of FGM.

planEntities.name: 2.2.1.12 Promoting Small Hydropower Development and Circular Economy Approaches in Nigeria
planEntities.parentName: Output 2.2.1: Human and Institutional Capacities of Public and Private Institutions at Federal, State and LGA Levels Strengthened to Develop and Implement Risk Management and (National) Adaptation Plans to Mitigate for Impact of Climate Change.
planEntities.description: The EU-funded project on "Advancing Nigeria's Green and just transition to Net Zero through Circular Economy" in Nigeria was officially signed in December 2023. However, the project activity implementation will commence in March 2024 after the official project launch. About four states will be selected as core partners while two states will be associate partners. Therefore, a total of six states will benefit from the project. The 6 states will be selected after the project launch based on set criteria The main objective of the project is to improve the management of used off-grid energy equipment and plastics through circular economy practices for mitigation of pollution and Green House Gas emissions. Generally, the project will also promote circular economy practices to combat pollution and climate change in Nigeria.

planEntities.name: Capacities of national authorities, communities and other key stakeholders strengthened, stigma and discrimination among KVP are reduced and the protection and promotion of human rights among all target groups are upheld through strategic partnerships and technical assistance to mitigate the risk an dimpact of HIV on those furthest behind in line with the 10-10-10 targets
planEntities.parentName: Inequalities in all sectors are addressed by equitable distribution and effective management of resources including through the use of innovation and technology
planEntities.description:
In 2025, the Joint UN Team on AIDS (JUTA) supported Ghana in strengthening national and community capacities to address HIV-related stigma, discrimination and human rights barriers affecting key and vulnerable populations, in line with the global 10-10-10 targets.

Through strategic partnerships with government institutions, civil society organisations and community networks, UN partners provided technical assistance to strengthen national frameworks and institutional capacities for protecting the rights of people living with HIV and key populations. Engagement with national authorities contributed to reinforcing governance and accountability mechanisms addressing stigma and discrimination within the HIV response, while promoting the integration of human rights approaches into national HIV programming.

At the community level, targeted initiatives strengthened the capacity of networks of people living with HIV and key population organisations to engage with institutions, monitor rights violations, and advocate for equitable access to health and social services. Community actors were supported to enhance peer outreach, awareness raising and referral mechanisms that enable affected populations to access services without fear of stigma or discrimination.

Technical assistance and partnership efforts also supported dialogue and collaboration between community organisations and public institutions, helping to foster trust and strengthen mechanisms for addressing discrimination and other structural barriers to HIV services. These initiatives contributed to improving the enabling environment for HIV prevention, treatment and care while reinforcing community leadership within the national response.

Collectively, these interventions contributed to advancing a rights-based HIV response in Ghana, strengthening institutional and community capacity to prevent and respond to stigma and discrimination, and supporting progress towards achieving the 10-10-10 targets.

planEntities.name: FAO:  Enhancing Land Consolidation in North Macedonia
planEntities.parentName: Output 2.1: Economic Enabling Environment
planEntities.description:
Under this sub-output, FAO, with support from the European Union, has assisted the Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Water Economy to continue the implementation of the National Land Consolidation Programme. Key achievements include adoption of the National Land Consolidation Strategy and Action Plan 2025–2035, establishment of a Permanent Advisory Group on Land Consolidation, preparation and adoption of the land consolidation plan for Chiflik village, and completion of agricultural infrastructure works in Dabjani village. The project has also strengthened stakeholder capacities and public understanding of land consolidation.
Under the planned no-cost extension until 31 March 2027, remaining activities will include  targeted trainings for MAFWE, the National Extension Agency and the Agency for Real Estate Cadastre, focusing on multi-purpose land consolidation, cadastral registration and farmer engagement. A public awareness campaign will also be conducted to promote the National Land Consolidation Strategy and Action Plan 2025–2035 and opportunities for farmers to participate in future land consolidation projects. Infrastructure works originally planned for Chiflik and subsequently redirected to Logovardi will not be implemented.

planEntities.name: FAO: Enhanced One Health surveillance, early warning, and laboratory capacities to detect and manage antimicrobial resistance and zoonotic and transboundary diseases, protecting animal and human health
planEntities.parentName: Output 2.1: Economic Enabling Environment
planEntities.description: This sub-output will strengthen national One Health capacities for early warning, surveillance, and laboratory diagnostics to detect, monitor, and manage antimicrobial resistance and zoonotic and transboundary diseases. It will support a coordinated approach across the human, animal and environmental health sectors by enhancing digital surveillance systems, laboratory networks, information management, data analytics, biosafety and biosecurity standards, and field epidemiology competencies. The intervention will be implemented in close partnership with the Food and Veterinary Agency as the lead national counterpart, and in coordination with the Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Water Economy to ensure alignment with national veterinary, food safety and agrifood sector priorities. Through integrated system strengthening, this sub-output will improve national preparedness, rapid detection and response capabilities, contributing to a more resilient health and agrifood system.

planEntities.name: FAO: Strengthened country capacities and developed strategic frameworks for building low-carbon and climate-resilient society through strategic engagement with the Green Climate Fund
planEntities.parentName: Output 3.1: Climate Action and Resilience to Disaster and Humanitarian Risks
planEntities.description: This project represents the third national initiative supported under the GCF Readiness and Preparatory Support Programme and implemented by FAO. It supports the strengthening of the institutional and technical capacities of the National Designated Authority (NDA) for the GCF and the institutions comprising the national GCF Country Coordination Mechanism to more effectively steer climate action and access to climate finance in North Macedonia. The project enhances the systems that enable these institutions to fulfil their roles and policy requirements by improving inter-institutional coordination, establishing knowledge management tools, and ensuring continuous capacity development. It also facilitates strategic private sector engagement in climate action, builds the capacities of direct access entities to meet and maintain GCF accreditation standards, and enables them to develop and implement high-quality GCF-funded projects. Furthermore, the project supports the updating of the national GCF Country Work Programme in line with national priorities and climate strategies, and contributes to the preparation of strong, nationally endorsed GCF concept notes and pre-feasibility assessments for priority climate investments.

planEntities.name: FAO: Support country decarbonization process through integrated management of forest fires and strengthening climate information sharing
planEntities.parentName: Output 3.3: Environmental Protection and Natural Resource Management
planEntities.description:
Through this GCF Readiness project GCP/MCD/012/GCR, FAO supports the implementation of North Macedonia’s Enhanced NDC by strengthening institutional and technical capacities for integrated forest fire management and by improving national systems for collecting, analyzing, and sharing climate, greenhouse gas (GHG), and air-quality information. The forestry sector—traditionally the country’s main carbon sink—has become increasingly vulnerable to wildfires and land-use change, leading to rising GHG emissions and periodic deterioration of air quality with impacts on public health and ecosystems. 
The project strengthens integrated forest fire management through capacity development of key institutions, upgrading the Macedonian Forest Fire Information System (MKFFIS), and introducing technologies for near-real-time fire detection and monitoring in selected pilot areas. It develops forest vulnerability assessments, predictive fire-risk models, and national methodologies for fire prevention and mitigation, while supporting the preparation of a National Plan for Forest Fire Protection aligned with national climate mitigation goals. In parallel, the project enhances climate and environmental observation systems by strengthening the National Hydrometeorological Service’s capacities to monitor GHG emissions and air quality, particularly in forest-fire-prone areas. By improving climate observation, data transparency, and information sharing, the project enhances national preparedness, supports evidence-based mitigation action, reduces emissions linked to forest fires, improves understanding of fire-related air-pollution impacts, and contributes directly to North Macedonia’s decarbonization goals.

planEntities.name: FAO: Support to developing effective NDC 3.0 Climate Finance Strategy and Action Plan, to accelerate North Macedonia’s transition to a low-carbon, climate-resilient economy
planEntities.parentName: Output 3.1: Climate Action and Resilience to Disaster and Humanitarian Risks
planEntities.description: This project aims at supporting the Government of North Macedonia to develop an effective NDC 3.0 (2025–2035) and a Climate Finance Strategy and Implementation Action Plan. It provides targeted technical analysis on climate finance landscapes, past and ongoing climate finance flows, institutional readiness, and opportunities for climate co-financing. These assessments will serve as the analytical foundation for developing the new NDC 3.0 and aligning national climate finance priorities with the upcoming NDC cycle. The project will work closely with the Ministry of Environment and Physical Planning and all relevant national institutions, ensuring inclusive stakeholder engagement and adequate participation of women and under-represented groups. The support will reinforce national capacities for mobilizing, managing, and deploying climate finance, contributing to a more ambitious, low-carbon, and climate-resilient development pathway for North Macedonia.

planEntities.name: FAO: Support to resolving private-public co-ownership to improve agricultural land management and land tenure in the Pelagonija region
planEntities.parentName: Output 2.1: Economic Enabling Environment
planEntities.description: Under this sub-output, FAO will continue supporting the Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Water Economy to improve land tenure and utilization in the Pelagonija region by addressing private–public land co-ownership affecting over 2,000 landowners and 10,000 ha—currently limiting effective land use and contributing to conflicts, particularly on land under long-term lease. This will be achieved through policy and legal recommendations within the broader land policy framework, and by piloting an integrated voluntary land consolidation approach to enable more efficient and productive agricultural land use.

planEntities.name: FAO: Stakeholders trained in climate mitigation and climate-smart landscape fire management through structured training programmes
planEntities.parentName: Output 2.2: Vocational Training and Skills Development
planEntities.description: Under the GCF project “Support the decarbonization process of North Macedonia through integrated management of forest fires and strengthening climate information sharing” (GCP/MCD/012/GCR), FAO is strengthening stakeholders’ capacities to manage landscape fires and safeguard forests’ climate mitigation potential. A structured training curriculum will guide five one-day sessions for up to 100 participants from relevant public institutions, forestry services, local communities and civil society. Demonstration equipment and training materials will support practical learning and continued delivery beyond the project, helping address skills needs in climate-resilient forest management.

planEntities.name: FAO: Veterinary and public health workforce capacities strengthened in animal disease surveillance, antimicrobial resistance (AMR), laboratory diagnostics and emergency preparedness through structured training and skills development programmes
planEntities.parentName: Output 2.2: Vocational Training and Skills Development
planEntities.description: Under the Pandemic Fund-supported project "Strengthening One Health capacities for pandemic prevention, preparedness and response", FAO is implementing a set of interlinked workforce development and capacity building interventions targeting public institutions and civil society in the animal and public health sectors. FAO will review animal health training needs across the three KAM countries (North Macedonia, Albania, Kosovo) and develop and deliver a Training of Trainers (ToT) programme for veterinary services, covering animal disease surveillance, antimicrobial resistance (AMR), biosecurity, and diagnostics. This will build sustainable institutional training capacity within national veterinary services. FAO will also establish a continuous professional development programme through accredited short courses for veterinary and public health professionals, with a focus on field epidemiology, outbreak investigation, foodborne disease surveillance, and data analysis. Additionally, structured laboratory training on the diagnosis of zoonotic diseases in livestock and wildlife, including AMR diagnostics (bacterial isolation, identification and antimicrobial susceptibility testing), will be delivered to strengthen the qualified laboratory workforce. Joint outbreak simulation exercises will be conducted with WHO for public health and veterinary personnel to build cross-sector emergency preparedness and response competencies. FAO will also strengthen the capacities of community-based non-governmental organizations working with marginalized and vulnerable populations to improve One Health literacy and AMR awareness, contributing to inclusive skills development for civil society actors.

planEntities.name: FAO: Capacities of the National Hydrometeorological Service improved for air quality monitoring and data sharing through upgraded and integrated observation equipment
planEntities.parentName: Output 3.2: Pollution Action
planEntities.description:
As part of the GCF Readiness project GCP/MCD/012/GCR, FAO supports the strengthening of national capacities of the National Hydrometeorological Service (NHMS) to enhance climate and air quality monitoring, expand and upgrade the observational network, and improve the use of climate and air quality data for mitigation in line with NDC commitments. This support includes an assessment of existing observational capacities and development of a technical proposal for an integrated network for sub-national and local GHG emissions estimation and air-quality monitoring, prioritizing co-location of monitoring systems and use of existing infrastructure.
In close cooperation with NHMS, the project will also support climate information-sharing mechanisms in at least three municipalities. Standardized reporting procedures and visual formats will translate locally relevant atmospheric and climate data into actionable recommendations for municipal authorities and stakeholders. Complemented by awareness-raising campaigns, these activities will strengthen capacities to interpret, communicate and use climate information for evidence-based mitigation decisions.

planEntities.name: FAO: Strengthening Climate-Resilient Land Consolidation and Investment Readiness for Sustainable Agriculture
planEntities.parentName: Output 2.1: Economic Enabling Environment
planEntities.description: Under this sub-output, FAO will support MAFWE and partner institutions to strengthen climate-responsive land management, agricultural investment readiness and policy development in North Macedonia. Support will include developing and testing a multi-purpose land consolidation model in Bitolsko Pole, including feasibility assessment, participatory re-allotment planning and support for approval and registration; preparing technical designs and supporting studies for climate-resilient agricultural and water investments; establishing a Land Management Innovation and Knowledge Hub with the Faculty of Civil Engineering to strengthen applied learning, professional skills and knowledge exchange; and developing recommendations, a catalogue of climate-responsive measures and guidance for integrating climate adaptation and mitigation into agricultural support programmes. These interventions will strengthen institutional capacities and create conditions for improved farm structures, more efficient land and water use, and future climate-resilient investments, with inclusive participation of women, young people and vulnerable groups.

planEntities.name: FAO: Emergency Response to Sheep Pox and Goat Pox outbreak in North Macedonia
planEntities.parentName: Output 2.1: Economic Enabling Environment
planEntities.description:
Under this sub-output, FAO will support the Food and Veterinary Agency and MAFWE to control sheep pox and goat pox in North Macedonia, following the first confirmed outbreak in January 2026 and a sharp increase to over 90 confirmed outbreaks by September 2026. Emergency assistance will enable timely vaccine procurement while national procurement procedures are pursued, helping contain the outbreak and reduce the risk of further spread within the country and across borders.
Support will include vaccines and essential supplies for an emergency vaccination campaign targeting 200,000 sheep and goats, awareness raising, post-vaccination monitoring, strengthened passive surveillance and updated contingency, vaccination and surveillance plans. By protecting livestock assets, agricultural productivity and smallholder incomes, the intervention will help maintain an enabling environment for sustainable economic activity and decent work in the livestock sector, particularly for vulnerable rural households.
Practical training, simulation exercises and locally adapted technical learning materials will strengthen professional skills and institutional capacities for early detection, vaccination, biosecurity and effective outbreak response, supporting continuity of livestock production and greater resilience to future animal disease shocks.

planEntities.name: ILO: National OSH framework conducive to the promotion of a safe and healthy working environment is in place
planEntities.parentName: Output 2.1: Economic Enabling Environment
planEntities.description:
The ILO will support the development of a sound, gender-sensitive national legal- and policy framework as the critical starting point for ensuring a safe and healthy working environment. To this end, the ILO will support stakeholders to effectively engage in the legislative and policy processes needed to bring the legal and policy frameworks in line with International Labour Standards and the related EU acquis. A comprehensive gap analysis of the harmonisation of the national OSH legislation (laws and bylaws) with ratified ILO conventions and the EU OSH Directives will be conducted. The ILO Support Kit for Developing Occupational Safety and Health Legislation will be used to prepare all necessary changes to align the legislation. The ILO will also assess the current system of employment injury compensation and insurance and develop recommendations for possible system redesign. 
A gender sensitive national OSH Profile will be developed/updated as an important step towards building a solid OSH policy and a new National Strategy on OSH which addresses the different risks and health needs of women and men. National OSH Policy and Strategy will be developed in line with the EU Strategic Framework on Health and Safety at work 2021-2027. The OSH Profile is an instrument which entails a systematic review and evaluation of the national situation with respect to occupational accidents and diseases as well as of the entire range of instruments and resources available in the country to implement the OSH Policy. It will identify strong points, weak points and gaps in North Macedonia’s OSH system and will be used to identify priority issues for the national OSH Policy.

planEntities.name: ILO: Systems and procedures for improved labour inspection services are in place
planEntities.parentName: Output 2.1: Economic Enabling Environment
planEntities.description:
With the ILO support, the State Labour Inspectorate (SLI) will be transformed and modernized. The SLI plays a crucial role in securing a safe and healthy working environment in North Macedonia. The ILO will support the revision/development and digitalisation of all inspection processes, reporting procedures, analytical functions, and planning. To this end, the SLI information management system will be upgraded. The ILO will support development of methodology and software for risk assessment in planning the inspection visits. ILO will support development a training curriculum for labour inspectors, based on the preceding LI training needs assessment. In cooperation with the Government, a SLI training and education centre will be established and equipped. Furthermore, we will upgrade the ILO-supported SLI learning platform for the labour inspectors in North Macedonia, by developing new learning modules and specific trainings (for instance, on OSH data analysis). SLI will, moreover, be granted the access to all ILO tools and methodologies that will support its transformation in a modern and efficient labour inspectorate.
The ILO will support the participation of national stakeholders in various EU-OSHA and ILO surveys. Targeted training for the staff of the Ministry of Economy and Labour and the State Labour Inspectorate will ensure that these institutions have the critical staff to respond to the obligations in the area of OSH, stemming from the EU negotiations process and later from the EU membership.

planEntities.name: ILO: Improved OSH Information system and procedures are in place
planEntities.parentName: Output 2.1: Economic Enabling Environment
planEntities.description:
A key enabler for the progressive improvement and resilience of occupational safety and health frameworks is the development of evidence-based research, coupled with a mechanism for the collection and analysis of occupational safety and health data. In addition to developing national recording and notification systems on occupational injuries and diseases, the ILO will support robust research on occupational safety and health, thereby fostering a proactive approach to the prevention of hazards and mitigation of risks.
ILO will support building of the evidence base effectively feeding the processes of design, monitoring and evaluation of legislation, policies and interventions. Comprehensive and accurate data will strengthen the occupational safety and health system at national level and within enterprises and will facilitate effective allocation of scarce public resources. Following an assessment of the current situation, the ILO will implement combined actions at national and workplace level to improve the data collection, reporting and notification on work-related accidents, occupational injuries, and occupation diseases, in line with the European Statistics on Accidents at Work and European Occupational Diseases Statistics methodologies. The ILO will support preparation of the necessary legal framework for the information system and will develop the web-based OSH information system for collecting, recording, processing, and reporting on occupational accidents and diseases. The online OSH information system platform is aimed at revolutionizing workplace safety management in North Macedonia. By providing real-time data on the number of workers, companies, workplace accidents, specific risks, industry-wide hazards, health trends, and related costs, this platform will empower North Macedonia to continuously monitor and improve its occupational safety landscape. The insights gained will support the development of effective safety and health strategies, targeted action plans, and timely preventive measures, ultimately benefiting all citizens and enhancing workplace safety standards nationwide.

planEntities.name: ILO: National capacities to promote a safe and healthy working environment for all workers are strengthened
planEntities.parentName: Output 2.1: Economic Enabling Environment
planEntities.description: Social partners are at the core of building a culture of OSH prevention. ILO will work closely with them to improve their capacity and assist them in providing timely support and modern services to their members.  ILO will provide manuals on labour inspection, OSH rulebooks, and will provide trainings on OSH for employers and workers. The activities supported will entail development of OSH services for members, incentives for micro, small and medium size enterprises to engage in and successfully implement OSH measures, awareness raising and promotional OSH activities, seminars, conferences, development and dissemination of OSH related materials.

planEntities.name: ITU Regional CyberDrill 2026
planEntities.parentName: Output 4.1: Good Governance:
planEntities.description:
The ITU Cybersecurity Forum and CyberDrill for Europe and the Mediterranean will take place in Skopje, in October 2026. 

Combining a Cybersecurity Forum, technical trainings, and CyberDrill exercises, this event aims to enhance the communication and incident response capabilities of participating teams from European countries. It also seeks to foster collective and collaborative efforts to mitigate cyber threats among Computer Security Incident Response Teams (CSIRTs) from both Europe and the Arab regions of the Mediterranean.

This event continues ITU's tradition of organizing regional CyberDrills to build cybersecurity capacity and capability through collaboration and cooperation.

The primary objectives are to strengthen the cybersecurity readiness and resilience of the CSIRT community across Europe and the Mediterranean region. Specifically, to:
	•	Enhance cybersecurity capacity and capability through regional cooperation.
	•	Assist Member States in developing and implementing operational procedures to improve responses to various cyber incidents.
	•	Identify areas for improvement in future planning and CIRT processes at the national level.
	•	Strengthen international cooperation between Member States.
	•	Promote knowledge sharing to foster a regional culture of cybersecurity preparedness.

planEntities.description: Under this sub-output, the action will strengthen institutional and human capacities to effectively advance Gender-Responsive Budgeting and Gender Equality and Women’s Empowerment (GEWE) commitments at both central and local levels. It will build the capacities of budget users to apply GRB within programme-based budgeting processes, while strengthening central-level gender mechanisms to carry out effective, results-based monitoring and reporting on progress towards GEWE commitments. The action will support the full operationalization of the Resource Centre on Gender-Responsive Policy Making and Budgeting as a hub for knowledge, tools, and technical assistance, and will further enhance local-level implementation by supporting LSGUs through peer-to-peer learning, Training of Trainers, and the delivery of a structured training and mentoring programme, ensuring sustainable and scalable GRB practice.

planEntities.name: UNDP: Climate Promise II – Revision of the National Determine Contributions - NDC 3.0
planEntities.parentName: Output 3.1: Climate Action and Resilience to Disaster and Humanitarian Risks
planEntities.description:
The project "Climate Promise II – Revision of the National Determine Contributions – NDC 3.0" focuses on revising the National Determined Contributions in North Macedonia as a comprehensive national strategy aimed at accelerating climate action and sustainable development. The project aims to raise the country’s ambition for reducing greenhouse gas emissions, in line with the Paris Agreement and European Union climate policies. This means setting stronger targets for emission reductions and integrating climate action into the country’s broader economic, social, and environmental development plans. 

A key aspect of NDC 3.0 is its inclusive approach where the process involves active participation from government institutions, civil society, youth, women, and vulnerable groups, ensuring that climate action is fair, transparent, and leaves no one behind. The project also emphasizes sustainable management of natural resources, where efforts are directed at pollution control, biodiversity protection, sustainable agriculture, and improved waste management. 

Institutional strengthening is another major focus of the project, with measures to improve coordination among ministries, build capacity at the local level, and ensure effective governance of climate policies. The main goal is to establish transparent systems for monitoring, reporting, and verifying progress.

planEntities.name: UNDP: Development of North Macedonia's BTR1 and BTR2/NC5
planEntities.parentName: Output 3.1: Climate Action and Resilience to Disaster and Humanitarian Risks
planEntities.description: The objective of this project is to assist the Republic of North Macedonia in the preparation and submission of its First Biennial Transparency Report on Climate Change and a combined Second Biennial Transparency and Fifth National Communication Report (BTR1 and BTR2/NC5) for the fulfillment of the obligations under the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) and the Paris Agreement (PA), in line with the Modalities, Procedures and Guidelines (MPGs) for the transparency framework for action and support referred to in Article 13 of the Paris Agreement (Decision 18/CMA .1) and the guidance on operationalizing the MPGs as per Decision 5/CMA.3. The project will support the Republic of North Macedonia in achieving its global environment concerns and commitments to international conventions, and to integrate climate change considerations in national development planning and policy through ensuring continuity of the institutional and technical capacity building, partly initiated, and consequently sustained by reporting instruments under the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC).
