planEntities.description: The initiative “Global Programme on National Biodiversity Finance Plans” is an enabling activity that directly supports the implementation of the new biodiversity targets under the new Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF), specifically it will focus on providing support to countries in developing: a) a national biodiversity finance policy and institutional review; b) an expenditure review to assesses spending related to biodiversity across all relevant sectors; c) an assessment of financial needs required to achieve the targets of the GBF; and, d) a National Biodiversity Finance Plan. This is underpinned by a transformational process to develop a shared vision and action agenda on financing nature in the country, closely involving the finance sector.

planEntities.name: UNDP: EU For Prespa - Infrastructure Improvements in the Prespa Area
planEntities.parentName: Output 3.3: Environmental Protection and Natural Resource Management
planEntities.description:
The Project “EU for Infrastructure Improvements in the Prespa Area” is an important part of the broader “EU for Prespa” Action, aiming at promoting the Green Agenda for the Western Balkans in the transboundary Prespa Lake area in line with the principle of "leaving no persons and regions behind."
The Project comprises a set of interrelated capital investments for infrastructure development and accompanying measures with far reaching beneficial impacts for the entire transboundary Prespa Lake basin/Prespa Park area.
The Project will contribute to the preservation and improvement of the ecological system in the Prespa Lake area through a series of interlinked capital investments to be implemented within the boundaries of the Municipality of Resen and accompanying capacity development measures. These initiatives are designed to enhance municipal wastewater and solid waste management systems, redirecting harmful pollutants away from natural ecosystems. The Municipality of Resen and the public utility “Proleter” will benefit from carefully planned capacity development efforts, ensuring the sustainability of the newly introduced systems, and resulting communal wastewater and solid waste management services.
Furthermore, the Project will contribute to enhancing transboundary cooperation and improving connectivity and mobility around the lake, through the opening of a new border crossing point with Greece, at Markova Noga. This, in turn, is expected to boost socio-economic and tourism development while fostering cooperation among the nations sharing the lake basin. All of this aligns with the main provisions of the International Agreement for the Protection and Sustainable Development of Prespa Park and the trilateral Strategic Action Plan for Prespa Park. 
The partners and beneficiaries of the Project are the Customs Administration (for the border crossing), the Municipality of Resen, the public utility "Proleter" as well as communities, households, and businesses benefiting from the newly introduced systems. The Project shall be implemented in close collaboration with the Ministry of Environment and Physical Planning and multiple other stakeholders at national and local levels.

planEntities.name: UNDP: EU for Prespa - Restoration of natural resources and enhancing sustainable agriculture and tourism
planEntities.parentName: Output 3.3: Environmental Protection and Natural Resource Management
planEntities.description:
The objective of the overall Action “EU for Prespa” is to promote the Green Agenda for the Western Balkans in the transboundary Prespa Lake area in line with the “no persons and regions left behind”. 
The Specific Objective of the Project “Restoration of natural resources and enhancing sustainable agriculture and tourism” is to instigate a significant change in practices and behaviour among policy makers at local level, farmers, private sector, CSO and citizens regarding the management of and the sustainable use of natural resources in the Prespa region which will result in improved quality of life and contribute to economic development by emerging “green” pathways to growth.
The EU investments will contribute to the preservation of the natural capital and restore the damaged ecosystem of Macro Prespa Lake to good ecological status, in line with EU standards. The measures will address the pollution of water and soil, protect endangered species and encourage the sustainability of the local economic and agricultural practices. The farmers, households, and small businesses will be supported to apply good agricultural practices, create small chain value, and invest in sustainable tourism services and products respectively. The Project shall also enhance the cross-border cooperation by supporting the creation of a new vision for sustainable development of the Prespa Lakes region. 

This overall goal of the Project will be achieved through three outcomes: 
Outcome 1: The ecological system in Prespa Lake area preserved and improved
Outcome 2: Sustainable economic activities in Prespa area boosted
Outcome 3: Enhanced cross-border cooperation

The main Project partners and beneficiaries are the Municipality of Resen, farmers and farmer associations, households and entities engaged in sustainable tourism from the Prespa region.
The Project shall be implemented in close collaboration with the Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Water Economy, the Ministry of Environment and Physical Planning and the Prespa Park Management Committee.

planEntities.name: UNDP: Green Finance Facility to Improve Air Quality & Combat Climate Change in North Macedonia
planEntities.parentName: Output 3.2: Pollution Action
planEntities.description: The Green Finance Facility (GFF) is an innovative financial mechanism that enables affordable finance to small and medium sized enterprises (SMEs) and marketable but underserved households to adopt renewable energy (RE) and efficient energy (EE) technology solutions. The facility provides loans for RE and/or EE through partner financial institutions, supported by technical assistance and ex-post performance-based payments for completed and verified RE and/or EE projects. GFF enabled adoption of RE and EE solutions will contribute to reduction of greenhouse gas emissions and air pollution and will strengthen the local ecosystem for RE & EE green finance. Outcome 2: Target groups, especially women and female headed households have greater access to finance for accelerating a transition to renewable energy and energy efficiency solutions. For households, the facility will provide US$ 6.5 million in loans through local banks, with an expected IRR of 5 - 6%. This will be complemented by performance- based payments equal to up to 30% of the original loan amount. Outcome 2 specifically targets female-headed households, single-parents, households with PWD, Roma households, and employees who were affected by COVID-19. To tap into remittances, the project also targets remittance recipients and returning migrants.

planEntities.name: UNESCO: Cultural Heritage Resilience in North Macedonia
planEntities.parentName: Output 3.1: Climate Action and Resilience to Disaster and Humanitarian Risks
planEntities.description:
UNESCO and UNDP are jointly developing CHERISH – Cultural Heritage Resilience in South-East Europe, a regional climate-resilience initiative spanning the Western Balkans and including North Macedonia. The programme responds to rising climate impacts – droughts, floods, heatwaves, wildfires, and land degradation – that are eroding cultural landscapes, traditional water systems, and heritage-based rural economies. CHERISH positions cultural and natural heritage as a climate-relevant asset and aligns with national adaptation priorities, NDCs, and EU Green Deal processes.

As the project is still in development, the initial phase will focus on establishing key baselines, mapping priority heritage systems, and preparing a full climate-finance proposal. The long-term vision is to restore and climate-proof heritage systems, support community-led adaptation mechanisms, strengthen climate-resilient tourism and green enterprises, and integrate heritage-based adaptation into national and local planning. This joint effort offers a scalable regional model for resilience and sustainable development.

planEntities.name: UNIDO: The Kigali Implementation Plan to phase down hydrofluorocarbons (HFC) in North Macedonia is developed and implemented
planEntities.parentName: Output 3.1: Climate Action and Resilience to Disaster and Humanitarian Risks
planEntities.description:
Following the outcomes of the 80th meeting of the Executive Committee of the Multilateral Fund for the Implementation of the Montreal Protocol, and pursuant to decision 80/50(d), funding was approved for North Macedonia to support activities related to the phase-down of hydrofluorocarbons (HFC). These activities aimed to facilitate early ratification of the Kigali Amendment.

The main objective of the project was to prepare North Macedonia for the ratification and early implementation of the Kigali Amendment to the Montreal Protocol, taking into account the country’s prevailing HFC consumption patterns. Project activities focused on the development of legal and regulatory instruments, stakeholder engagement and awareness-raising initiatives. These efforts contributed directly to the ratification of the Kigali Amendment in February 2020.

planEntities.parentName: Output 1.2: Inclusive, Quality Education:
planEntities.description:
This initiative has trained 50 school specialists and 150 teachers from 50 primary schools across the country who will work with adolescents over the next two school years to implement the programme. The programme aims to strengthen the social and emotional skills of students aged 10 to 14. The training sessions were held from 27 October to 14 November 2025, in both Macedonian and Albanian languages, in the cities of Skopje, Strumica, Štip, Prilep, Kočani, and Gostivar.
The implementation of the programme will include the training of teachers and school specialists who will deliver the programme, the evaluation of the programme through pre- and post-testing of students and process evaluation among the teachers, as well as the translation and cultural adaptation of the materials into Macedonian and Albanian languages.
UNODC: More than a training, the “Skills for Adolescence” programme is a strategic investment in the wellbeing and resilience of young people. It empowers them to make healthy choices while building essential life skills (communication, critical thinking, conflict resolution and others) to prevent tobacco, alcohol, and drug use through evidence-based approach. It equips students with tools to resist peer pressure, make responsible decisions, and build positive and supportive relationships.

planEntities.name: Transforming Inland Fisheries and Aquaculture in Kazakhstan to Ensure Environmental Sustainability
planEntities.parentName: Output 3.1. National and local actors have the enhanced capacity, tools and knowledge to effectively design, implement, and monitor age and gender-sensitive environmental policies across all sectors.
planEntities.description: The objective of the project (GCP /KAZ/11373/GFF) is to support the country to realise the goals of the Kazakhstan Fisheries Development Programme (2021-2030). It is anticipated that the project will: 1) Strengthen policy, legal, regulatory, and strategic planning frameworks to ensure that the aquaculture and culture-based fisheries production sectors develop in accordance to the principles of an ecosystem approach to aquaculture (EAA), and based on the precautionary approaches to fisheries, aquaculture, and culture-based fisheries development. 2) Strengthen management systems and tools to ensure the adoption of international best practice and standards to promote climate resilient and ecologically sustainable aquaculture and culture-based fisheries sector development. 3) Introduce key technology transfers to support climate-smart, water saving production technologies, diversify production systems and culture species, and optimise exiting production systems to promote ecological sustainability, and enhance production, social and economic outcomes.

planEntities.name: Sustainable land management and restoration of degraded lands mainstreaming biodiversity conservation and ecosystem services in the Southern region of Kazakhstan (FSP)

Alignment with the overarching the Central Asia Water and Land Nexus (CAWLN) approach aims to catalyze sustained environmental change at regional, national, and subnational levels. The project emphasizes cross-sectoral coordination, participatory governance, and evidence-based sustainable pasture management.

planEntities.name: Strengthening the capacity of Kazakhstan to comply with the ETF under the Paris Agreement
planEntities.parentName: Output 3.1. National and local actors have the enhanced capacity, tools and knowledge to effectively design, implement, and monitor age and gender-sensitive environmental policies across all sectors.
planEntities.description: The project's (GCP /KAZ/11938/GFF) main goal is to provide the Government of Kazakhstan with the technical support for strengthening the national institutional and technical capacities of the country to comply with the enhanced transparency framework (ETF) for climate change mitigation and adaptation actions. The proposed project will support the Capacity Building Initiative for Transparency (CBIT) of GEF-8 CBIT Focal Area. After completion of the project, Kazakhstan will be capable of building institutional and technical capacities to meet the enhanced transparency requirements in the Paris Agreement through: (i) coordinated and strengthened national institutional effort on ETF, (ii) enhanced technical capacity of the stakeholders and packaged set of tools for tracking the Nationally Determined Contributions (NDC) adaptation actions, (iii) enhanced technical capacity of the stakeholders and packaged set of tools for the consistent GHG inventory preparation and tracking the NDC mitigation actions, and (iv) enhanced technical capacity of the stakeholders and packaged set of tools for tracking the climate finance (domestic and international) and support received for NDC actions.

planEntities.name: Coordinated approach for Land Restoration in Vulnerable Ecosystems of Central Asia
planEntities.parentName: Output 3.1. National and local actors have the enhanced capacity, tools and knowledge to effectively design, implement, and monitor age and gender-sensitive environmental policies across all sectors.
planEntities.description: The project's (GCP /SEC/11379/GFF) primary objective is to strengthen regional-level WLN approaches and coordination for their implementation. This aims to enhance water security, bolster resilience, and improve rural livelihoods within the Amu Darya and Syr Darya river basins. The project's primary objective is to strengthen regional water-land nexus (WLN) approaches and their implementation, thereby enhancing water security, building resilience, and improving rural livelihoods. This will be achieved through a transformative strategy encompassing four key pathways: (1) fostering transboundary and cross-sectoral coordination to establish an enabling policy environment for integrated natural resource management; (2) enhancing data-driven decision-making through regional harmonization of EO technologies and targeted capacity-building; (3) promoting integrated watershed management (IWM) practices across borders by developing a model framework and strengthening the engagement with the private sector; and (4) supporting gender-sensitive knowledge management and the dissemination of lessons learned

planEntities.name: Strengthening Integrated Water Management in Syr Darya and Naryn River Basins

planEntities.description: The project’s (GCP /SEC/11381/GFF) primary objective is to enhance water security and climate resilience in the region through the integration of Water-Land Nexus (WLN) approaches. This means addressing the interdependencies between water and land management to achieve more sustainable outcomes. By improving transboundary cooperation and introducing innovative monitoring technologies, the project strives to foster collaborative governance and evidence-based decision-making. The goal is to enhance water security and climate resilience in the Syr Darya and Naryn River Basins by mainstreaming the Water-Land Nexus (WLN) through strengthening transboundary cooperation, advancing integrated watershed management practices and employing innovative monitoring technologies.

An evidence-based approach will be taken by establishing a better understanding of the brucellosis epidemiological, management, and legislative landscape at the regional and national level during the first phase of the project. This project will strengthen the capacities of national authorities, as well as the farming community, in all aspects related to the management of brucellosis (i.e. reporting, detection, field and laboratory diagnosis, control and biosecurity).

This tool, called “E-Collab.OSH”, serves as a digital tool and has a broader scope of application, it combines the functions of a repository of OSH-related standards, documents and practices, with a competence-building training segment. planEntities.parentName: Output  2.1. Government and other institutions’ capacities are strengthened to design, implement and monitor policies for sustainable and inclusive economy, trade and transport connectivity, energy efficiency, fundamental labour principles and rights, dynamic entrepreneurship environment
planEntities.description: Mining represents an important source of income worldwide and the influence of the mining and metallurgical industry (MMI) on the macroeconomic performance of the country is substantial. However, the largest number of those working in unfavourable working conditions in all aspects falls on the mining industry of the country. For the last decade there were over 150 fatalities in mining sector and over 600 workers were injured. To address the challenges with occupational hazards, deceases and mortality as well as to bring the national legislation in compliance with international labour standards, ILO jointly with national tripartite constituents in Kazakhstan signed the Roadmap on decent work promotion in June 2024. as part of this roadmap implementation, the national project "Enhancing Occupational Safety and Health through Social Dialogue in Mining Sector in Kazakhstan" was officially launched in December 2024. The project contributes to strengthening fundamental principles and rights at work in mining sector by enhancing application of core ILO Conventions on freedom of association (C87), collective bargaining (C98), and occupational safety & health (OSH) (C155 and C187) as well as Labour Inspection Conventions (C81 and 129). The project anticipates the ILO support to the government in addressing compliance gaps identified by the ILO Committee of Experts and in preparation to ratification of C102 on minimum social standards, C176 on safety in mines and C190 on prevention and countering violence and harrassment at workplace.

planEntities.name: The legislative framework and the capacities of national constituents are strengthened to ensure effective governance of Occupational Safety and Health and to promote a preventive culture and the right to a safe and healthy working environment
planEntities.parentName: Output  2.1. Government and other institutions’ capacities are strengthened to design, implement and monitor policies for sustainable and inclusive economy, trade and transport connectivity, energy efficiency, fundamental labour principles and rights, dynamic entrepreneurship environment
planEntities.description: In the previous period, ILO provided significant assistance and support to the national constituents in the area of Occupational Safety and Health (OSH).    With the support of ILO, the update of the National OSH Profile was initiated, to be used as a foundation for assessing the strengths and weaknesses of a KAZ OSH system, for identifying priority areas for improvement, and guide the development of strategies and interventions to enhance occupational safety and health outcomes.      The mining has been identified as the particularly vulnerable sector in relation to OSH, characterized by number of work-related accidents. In addition, Gap-Analysis on the C176 was prepared to provide relevant information and guides to the national authorities and social partners, to assist the process of ratification of C176 on OSH in mining.     ILO will continue to providing technical assistance, guidance and support to the process of reforming the OSH system in the country, and shifting toward the risk-oriented approach and in building the preventive culture, by also promoting in the same time an effective social dialogue in this area.

planEntities.name: The institutional capacities of labour inspection are strengthened to enhance workplace compliance and ensure effective enforcement of labour legislation aligned with International Labour Standards
planEntities.parentName: Output  2.1. Government and other institutions’ capacities are strengthened to design, implement and monitor policies for sustainable and inclusive economy, trade and transport connectivity, energy efficiency, fundamental labour principles and rights, dynamic entrepreneurship environment
planEntities.description:
In the area of Labour inspection, Kazakhstan is still facing many challenges and situations that create/represent obstructions to the labour inspectors in their work and in ensuring higher level of compliance with the labour legislation.  There are still number of restrictions and limitations, included in the current legislation and regulations, regarding the powers of inspectors to freely conduct inspections without notifications of employers or other gov. institutions, and to conduct the inspections as often and as thoroughly as is necessary, and to undertake appropriate measures/actions to ensure effective compliance.   The challenges are also in the area of the capacities and available resources (human, technical, financial) of the labour inspectorate. There have been, however, a positive developments noted in 2024 when the Government adopted the Decree formally establishing the State Labour Inspection Committee (SLIC) within the Ministry of Labour and Social Protection of the Population, together with the establishment of 20 territorial divisions of the SLIC. With this, the labour inspection in Kazakhstan was officially transferred from the authority of local executive bodies, under the (central) authority.   
Substantial efforts have been invested in the previous period in providing support, advice and guidance to the national constituents in this area. However, ILO need to continue to provide the necessary assistance, technical expertise and further capacity building of the labour inspection system in Kazakhstan, with the aim of bringing the national legislation and practice in line with the ILS.

planEntities.description:
Kazakhstan is highly water-stressed. Over 40% of its water resources originate outside the country, leaving it dependent on inflows from China, Kyrgyzstan, and Russia. Domestic challenges—inefficient irrigation, outdated infrastructure, water losses, and pollution—exacerbate scarcity.
PAGE agencies are joining forces in 2026 to respond to the request of the Government of Kazakhstan for support in assessing the feasibility of blue finance. The ILO leads the assessment of the labour and social dimensions of blue finance, with special attention on impact on women and women entrepreneurship. The objective is to ensure that the transition to blue finance promotes decent work, skills development, and gender equality, all elements linked to enhancing the water productivity ecosystem in the selected areas. This work will support the revision of outdated related labour regulations and the compliance with ILO Conventions such as C131 on minimum wage (ratified on December 19, 2025).

planEntities.description:
The ILO contribution to the PAGE Blue Finance Assessment lays the social and labour groundwork necessary to ensure that Kazakhstan’s ambitious blue finance agenda achieves a sustainable, equitable, and people-centred transition. By integrating skills development, job quality, inclusion, innovation and social dialogue from the start, the intervention contributes to unlock the full potential of the Caspian Sea, Aral Sea and Lake Balkhash regions to act as catalysts for inclusive and resilient development.
The beneficiaries are government departments, workers’ and employers’ organizations, sector associations, SMEs, and community stakeholders in the participant regions: Caspian Sea, Aral Sea, Balkhash Lake.

The project aims to advance gender equality and strengthen women’s empowerment in Kazakhstan by addressing systemic challenges and leveraging existing opportunities. It responds to barriers to gender equality in Kazakhstan and addresses the need for more coordinated capacity-building, improved legal protection for women, strengthened gender equality mechanisms, and greater public awareness and engagement. The project aligns with national priorities, the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development - specifically SDGs 5, 16, and 17 and supports the implementation of Kazakhstan’s Family and Gender Policy Concept until 2030. The project’s Overall Goal (Impact) is to contribute to improved well-being for all people in Kazakhstan - especially the most vulnerable - through inclusive, effective, and accountable institutions that provide equal access to age- and gender-responsive, increasingly digitalised public and private services.

planEntities.description:
This project covers twelve countries situated in three geographical regions, i.e., in the Caucasus, and in Asia and the Pacific, which have taken some steps towards the digitalisation of their government operations and processes and for the delivery of public services to business and citizens, however in a varying degree. Moreover, most of them have also embraced the notion of digital transformation and of digital governance in their development strategies, although much still needs to be done towards their goal for digital transformation; incorporating the latest digital technologies, i.e., evidence-based policy formulation and implementation by harnessing abundant “big data”, or for the provision of proactive, efficient, and effective public services digitally.
Hence, this project – fully recognising the value of digital transformation and of digital governance – aims at further developing the capacities of public servants at different levels of government by transferring knowledge and experience enabling them to implement initiatives that will advance digital transformation and digital governance in their countries. It is expected that such knowledge and experience sharing will assist the participating countries to further develop policies initiatives that will allow them to establish data-driven public sectors for evidence-based policy making and implementation, and to introduce digital open governments that are proactive and user-driven resulting to efficient and effective public service provision and an increase of trust in government. Ultimately, utilising digitalisation for shaping public governance outcomes will be beneficial for their citizens.

planEntities.parentName: Output 4.2. Policies, systems and capacities enhance the civic space allowing all people to genuinely participate in public decision-making, and engage in constructive dialogue to achieve social cohesion, justice and equality for all, including the increased representation of women, youth and other groups in decision-making.
planEntities.description: Contemporary governments and public administration systems face immense and unique challenges that seriously threaten the peace and prosperity of our world. These challenges, in most instances, are interconnected, span across many different policy domains, and happen faster and on a much bigger scale than the past. Furthermore, as many of these policy issues are interlinked, and they tend to amplify one another, policy responses are much harder to anticipate, and more forceful in their impact. In this setting, governments, and public administration systems, vested with the responsibility to design, formulate, and implement public policy, they nowadays need to be able to predict, face and react to, and operate in the new reality that is characterised by considerable levels of volatility, uncertainty, complexity, and ambiguity, all amid rising geo-political tensions. Consequently, public administrations play a paramount role in coping with such complex and intertwined policy issues that put to test the capacity and ability of existing governance structures and organisational arrangements, as well as the adequacy of the competencies and skills of public administrators in coping with them. In addressing these concerns, the Government of the Republic of Kazakhstan, together with UNDP created the Astana Civil Service Hub (ACSH) - currently supported by 43 participating countries and 90 regional and international organisations. Since 2013, the ACSH operates as a multilateral and networking platform promoting supporting public service excellence, by assisting the efforts of the participating countries’ governments – particularly those in the immediate region – in building institutional and human capacity to cope with contemporary challenges and issues through three main pillars: (i) partnerships and networking; (ii) capacity building and peer-to-peer learning; and (iii) research and knowledge creation and management. It is worth noting that all ACSH activities are shaped by a flexible demand-driven agenda, which has proved its relevance in regional and international development cooperation over the years. The quality of its work has been highly acclaimed by the United Nations and its sister agencies, as well as by the European Union, and the Organisation for Economic Development and Cooperation and by many participating countries. The vision and mandate of this fourth phase of the project is to continue contributing to the establishment of modern, effective, efficient, and sustainable governance, public administration, and civil service systems in its participating countries and beyond, which meet society’s expectations for responsive, accountable, and transparent public institutions; in congruence with the SDG 16 and 17 objectives.

Identifying the regions’ development potential and growth points will be done through testing the best global and domestic practices (including by transferring successful cases from one region to another) to demonstrate the most optimal and economically feasible solutions, including on the basis of advanced water and energy saving technologies, use of environmentally friendly materials, technologies and knowledge to improve labour productivity, and production of high value-added products. Specific emphasis will be put on development of technical solutions that support planning, prevention, preparedness and response to flood emergencies in the regions.
Additionally, IP will support the Government in preparation for the Voluntary National Review on the SDGs in 2025 to conduct a comprehensive review of Kazakhstan progress towards the SDGs, SDG 5 being one of top priority SDGs, identify gaps and challenges, and develop strategies and action plans to accelerate progress towards achieving the goals.

The overall aim of the activities is to modernize and upgrade virological and bacteriological laboratories, including the repair of utility networks at NPCSEM, and to renovate and equip a virological laboratory in Turkestan. This will be done in line with SMART facility principles and green technologies. Furthermore, the project will enhance laboratory facilities across the Ministry of Health's sub-regions and modernize sanitary and quarantine checkpoints, ultimately improving disease surveillance, strengthening control measures, and ensuring sustained readiness to tackle public health challenges nationwide.

planEntities.description:
Kazakhstan's Family and Gender Policy 2030, alongside sectoral protocols, address domestic violence. The legislative changes enacted in 2023, granting law enforcement officers the authority to intervene in domestic violence cases without the survivor's statement, as well as the adoption of a law criminalizing domestic abuse in Kazakhstan (April 2024) represent a stride in combating GBV. However, further efforts are needed to ensure the effective implementation of the latter law to protect survivors and hold perpetrators accountable.
As a pioneering effort in Central Asia, Kazakhstan established the National Commission on Women, Family, and Demographic Policy to promote gender equality, further reinforced by constitutional guarantees of equal rights and freedoms for all citizens, irrespective of gender. This dedication is complemented by proactive measures to address gender stereotypes and promote women's rights through partnerships with religious leaders, grassroots organisations, and youth-friendly health centres.
National strategies such as the Kazakhstan-2050 Strategy and the updated Concept of Family and Gender Policy until 2030 aim to improve women’s leadership, access to employment, and protection from violence.

planEntities.parentName: Output 3.2. All people , especially children, youth, women have enhanced skills, knowledge, values, and engagement for more resilient and sustainable environment.
planEntities.description: BIOFIN supports countries with a methodology that provides innovative steps to measure current biodiversity expenditures, assess financial needs, identify the most suitable finance solutions, and provides guidance on how to implement these solutions to achieve their national biodiversity target. The 2nd phase of BIOFIN in Kazakhstan will be built on the lessons learned from the 1st phase and will aim to test six finance solutions: (1) subsidizing game breeding, (2) creating a basis for certification in the field of ecotourism, (3) capacity building of protected areas to improve financing, (4) biodiversity offsets, (5) carbon offsetting through an internal emission trading system (ETS) and (6) attracting foreign investment to implement projects to absorb greenhouse gases by forest ecosystems. The Phase II aims to establish the institutional and legal basis that will allow mobilizing financial resources for biodiversity through new financial solutions. Implementation of new finance solutions will be based on changing existing and preparing new legal standards, testing, studying the experience of other countries, approaches, capacity building of industry experts, providing extensive information on the problems and possibilities of biodiversity financing. The NAP project in the Republic of Kazakhstan addresses the urgent need to enhance resilience against the impacts of climate change. Focused on four priority sectors—agriculture, forestry, water management, and civil protection/disaster risk reduction – the project aims to establish clear mandates, coordination mechanisms, and standard procedures for climate adaptation at both national and sub-national levels. planEntities.name: Flood Control Using Integrated Dam Management System (01004180)
planEntities.parentName: Output 3.3. National and local actors, including communities, have enhanced disaster risk management capacities
planEntities.description:
The flood situation in 2024 was an unprecedented event. Frozen soil, sudden temperature rise and rainfall in conjunction with a considerable snow layer resulted in extremely high flows in the north and west of Kazakhstan. Many rivers experienced all-time high water levels and flood defence structures could not cope with the extreme flood volumes. The flood inundated large areas including settlements and agricultural zones and Aktobe was one of the hardest-hit cities in Kazakhstan.
This unprecedented flood revealed that preparedness, as part of efficient flood management, was not developed as it was supposed to be. The flood early warning systems to provide sufficient lead time did not exist. Specifically, dams did not have early warning systems which means preparation and foresighted flood operation are either not in place or just based on estimations and experiences of dam operators. However, the operators lack experience in addressing the increase in flow intensity, flow variability and speed floods developed in recent years due to climate change.
All in all, dams need urgent modernization in terms of three pillars: (1) Dam integrity; (2) Monitoring and dam surveillance; (3) Operation to enhance the flood management strategy in Kazakhstan, protect downstream riparians and ensure the full potential of flood attenuation of dams. Therefore, dams must be embedded into the national flood management concept of Kazakhstan as best as possible requiring the enhancement of early warning, dam monitoring, the rehabilitation of outdated structures and an update of operation rules.
The project aims to enhance flood resilience in Kazakhstan by strengthening dam safety and flood preparedness, directly supporting the disaster risk reduction and water priority sectors outlined in Kazakhstan's updated Nationally Determined Contributions (NDC). The updated NDC includes a dedicated chapter on climate change adaptation, emphasizing the importance of water resources management and disaster risk reduction as national adaptation priorities. This project aligns with these goals by improving infrastructure and preparedness measures to mitigate flood risks. Additionally, it complements the UNDP's ongoing initiative to integrate national adaptation plans into regional development strategies, ensuring a unified and comprehensive approach to climate resilience and sustainable development throughout Kazakhstan.

planEntities.description: UNODC’s global projects on the treatment of drug use disorders (DUD) are being implemented with the overall goal of improving the quality of drug dependence treatment worldwide and increasing access to drug dependence treatment for all those in need, thus reducing the adverse health and social consequences of drug dependence. The global projects include the following lines of action:  enhancing data,  capacity building on evidence-based drug dependence treatment approaches to improve the quality of drug dependence treatment services, systematic advocacy to promote a sound understanding of drug dependence and its treatment and to counteract stigma and discrimination, and support to the respective governments in developing national networks of community-based drug dependence treatment centers and social service providers, for a continuum of care approach.

planEntities.description: The Regional Youth Network for Central Asia (RYNCA) is a UNODC-supported platform that brings together youth leaders and youth organizations from Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan and Uzbekistan. Its aim is to promote prevention of drug use, healthy lifestyles, and youth participation in addressing global drug-related challenges. The Network was established in November 2021 in Samarkand following regional consultations supported by the Government of the Russian Federation.

planEntities.name: Regional Working Group on Precursor Chemicals (RWGP) "Strengthening Regional Cooperation and Regulatory Efforts against Precursor Chemicals”
planEntities.parentName: Output 4.1. Human rights, law enforcement and justice institutions have enhanced capacities to ensure fair age and gender-sensitive justice, rule of law and equity for all people in line with international law as well as standards and norms
planEntities.description: Precursor chemicals, often used for legitimate industrial and medical purposes, are frequently diverted and misused in the illicit manufacture of drugs. This diversion poses significant public health, safety, and security risks, particularly in the context of regional and global drug trafficking networks. As precursor chemicals are often traded across borders, regional collaboration is essential to effectively monitor, control, and prevent their diversion and misuse. The regional working group meeting on precursor chemicals offers a vital opportunity for countries in the region to collaborate, share best practices, and develop effective strategies to address the growing threat posed by precursor chemical diversion. By fostering strong partnerships between governments, international and regional organizations, the meeting aims to build a unified regional response to this pressing issue, strengthening the overall effort to prevent the misuse of precursor chemicals in illicit drug production.

planEntities.name: Supporting Central Asia to address the threats posed by online and prison-based radicalization to violent extremism, with a focus on Islamic State in Iraq and the Levant-Khorasan (ISIL-K)
planEntities.parentName: Output 4.1. Human rights, law enforcement and justice institutions have enhanced capacities to ensure fair age and gender-sensitive justice, rule of law and equity for all people in line with international law as well as standards and norms
planEntities.description: The Islamic State in Iraq and the Levant-Khorasan (ISIL-K) has become the most pressing terrorist threat in Central Asia, leveraging increased freedom of movement in Afghanistan and intensifying its violent rhetoric and targeted propaganda campaigns throughout 2024–2025. The group has tailored multilingual digital content—disseminated across online platforms—in different languages, aimed at radicalizing and inciting youth to violence both within Central Asia and globally. Central Asian nationals have been increasingly involved in ISIL-K-linked attacks, raising concerns about regional recruitment. However, efforts to counter the group throughout the criminal justice pathway - including through prevention, investigation, prosecution, incarceration and rehabilitation - face serious challenges. This project aims to strengthen the ability of key stakeholders in Central Asian Member States to detect, prevent, and respond to online and offline terrorist threats, as well as the recruitment and radicalization efforts of active groups in the region, with a particular focus on protecting and empowering youth targeted by violent extremist narratives.

planEntities.description:
The project focuses on three priority areas, seeking to achieve the following outputs:
1. Develop and strengthen institutional capacities of border control agencies in achieving international standards and best practices to ensure national, regional and global security. 
2. Facilitate the cooperation between law enforcement agencies and border guards agencies, and support law enforcement agencies and evidence-based investigations, specifically in dealing with detection and investigation of cross-border crime. 
3. Improve the living conditions in border areas through local economic development, with a focus on human rights, gender equality and groups in vulnerable situations.

planEntities.name: Valuation-to-Financing Framework for Biodiversity: A National Biodiversity Index developed to inform Ecological Fiscal Transfers (EFTs) and a Payment for Ecosystem Services (PES) scheme established and operationalised.
planEntities.parentName: Targeted institutions and communities protect, restore and sustainably use and manage terrestrial and aquatic ecosystems.
planEntities.description: BIOFIN is piloting an integrated Valuation-to-Financing Framework for Biodiversity. This framework establishes a national Biodiversity Index, which serves as a scientific "health scorecard" to measure ecosystem vitality and inform two complementary financing mechanisms. First, it guides Ecological Fiscal Transfers (EFTs), enabling the national government to reward local districts and communities that demonstrate strong biodiversity performance with increased budget allocations. Second, it supports the development and operationalization of a Payment for Ecosystem Services (PES) scheme, where downstream beneficiaries such as urban populations or private enterprises compensate upstream communities for maintaining essential ecosystem services like water purification and flood control. By creating a direct economic link between conservation and community livelihoods

planEntities.name: Strengthening country, community and household long term resilience via delivery of integrated insurance, risk finance and investment solutions
planEntities.parentName: Targeted institutions and communities are mitigating and adapting to climate change and disaster risks
planEntities.description: The financial impact of disasters on countries and communities can be devastating, with the burden of managing these risks often falling directly on national governments, local communities, and businesses. This is particularly acute in developing countries, where fiscal shocks can reverse development gains. This initiative aims to enhance resilience across multiple levels by ensuring that households, businesses, and food systems are better prepared to withstand climate and economic shocks. The focus is on building resilient nations and communities, safeguarding natural ecosystems, and incentivizing sustainable development. Through strategic advocacy, innovative partnerships, and the deployment of cutting-edge financial tools, the programme will strengthen the financial resilience of communities and smallholder farmers. Key to this effort is increasing the uptake of risk insurance and finance products, while simultaneously supporting governments in adopting comprehensive national risk financing and agricultural insurance programmes.

planEntities.name: Enhancing conjunctive management of surface and groundwater resources in selected transboundary aquifers in the Nile Basin
planEntities.parentName: Targeted institutions and communities protect, restore and sustainably use and manage terrestrial and aquatic ecosystems.
planEntities.description: The programme's strategic outcome is to achieve more effective utilisation and protection of shared aquifers in selected sub-basins within the Eastern Nile and Nile Equatorial Lakes region. This will be accomplished by improving the understanding of available groundwater resources and demonstrating conjunctive management approaches that optimise the coordinated use of surface and groundwater. The challenges addressed by the programme stem from a critical lack of knowledge regarding aquifer systems and their geographical extent. This is compounded by the absence of clear groundwater policies, poor management practices that lead to pollution, and limited application of techniques to enhance natural storage. Furthermore, over-exploitation of resources persists due to inadequate enforcement controls and insufficient monitoring systems. The interventions are conducted in 05 countries, Uganda, Kenya, Tanzania, Burundi, and Rwanda.

planEntities.name: Enhancing the resilience and livelihoods of communities in target wetland catchments through the rehabilitation of degraded ecosystems, promotion of climate-smart agricultural practices and alternative livelihoods, and strengthening of climate information services, thereby ensuring sustainable wetland management and improved adaptive capacity to climate change
planEntities.parentName: Targeted systems for natural resources and environment management increase productivity and resilience in select primary growth sectors.
planEntities.description: This programme main outcome is to build the resilience of communities and ecosystems in critical wetland catchments across Uganda. It directly addresses the degradation of wetland hydrology and associated landscapes through the rehabilitation of over 64,000 hectares of wetlands and natural grasslands, alongside the restoration of more than 11,000 hectares of degraded catchment areas. By constructing rainwater harvesting structures, restoring water retention facilities, and strengthening wetland management policies and by-laws, the initiative aims to restore ecosystem functionality, reduce topsoil loss, and improve water infiltration. These efforts are integrated with the promotion of climate-smart agricultural practices and alternative livelihoods, targeting over 50,000 households with a strong focus on women to diversify incomes and reduce pressure on fragile natural resources. Complementing these on-the-ground interventions, the programme strengthens the enabling environment for climate adaptation by improving access to reliable climate information and early warning systems. This involves upgrading meteorological and hydrological monitoring infrastructure, building capacity for data interpretation, and disseminating tailored forecasts and advisories to reach last-mile users, including smallholder farmers. By ensuring that 85% of men and women in the project area have access to improved climate services, the programme empowers communities to make timely decisions for agriculture and disaster risk reduction. Ultimately, this integrated approach combining ecosystem restoration, sustainable livelihoods, and enhanced climate information seeks to safeguard development gains, foster adaptive capacity, and ensure the long-term health of wetland ecosystems for both people and nature.

planEntities.name: Enhancing multistakeholder collaboration in waste management and circular economy in Uganda
planEntities.parentName: Targeted institutions and communities promote equitable, inclusive, gender-responsive waste management, sustainable urbanization and management of natural resources particularly of the extractive sector.
planEntities.description: Uganda is facing a growing waste management crisis due to rapid urbanization, increased consumption, and inadequate infrastructure, with projections indicating a 70% rise in waste generation by 2050. Current systems are overstretched, especially in cities like Kampala, leading to environmental and public health issues. Existing policies are fragmented and lack effective coordination. To address these challenges, the project proposes establishing a National Multistakeholder Platform for Waste Management, combining a physical convening body with a digital, GIS-enabled data hub. This platform will facilitate real-time data sharing, coordinated planning, and inclusive governance by integrating government, private sector, civil society, academia, and informal waste workers. The initiative will also drive innovation through a national circular economy challenge, supporting pilot projects and business models across multiple regions, with a focus on creating green jobs for women and youth. Additional components include awareness campaigns, training, and toolkits to promote behavioral change and improve waste management standards.

planEntities.name: Ecosystems restored and community livelihoods strengthened through wetland rehabilitation and nature-based enterprises.
planEntities.parentName: Targeted systems for natural resources and environment management increase productivity and resilience in select primary growth sectors.
planEntities.description: UNDP supports Uganda’s implementation of the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (KMGBF) by advancing sustainable development, biodiversity conservation, and inclusive governance through integrated technical assistance, capacity building, and financing solutions. Through the BIOFIN initiative and in partnership with NEMA, the programme focuses on implementing the National Biodiversity Finance Plan (NBFP) aligned with Uganda’s NBSAP III, targeting key KMGBF goals such as expanding protected areas (Target 3), enhancing access to biodiversity knowledge (Target 21), promoting inclusive participation (Target 22), and strengthening gender equality in biodiversity management (Target 23). planEntities.parentName: Output 3.2: People, especially the most vulnerable and marginalized including women, girls, adolescents and youth are empowered to contribute to and benefit from productive and decent work opportunities.
planEntities.description: Increased employment opportunities among youth and women through skills training, increased productivity, market linkages and entrepreneurship in selected agricultural value chains.  The objective is to increase employment opportunities among youth and women through skills training, increased productivity, market linkages and entrepreneurship in selected agricultural value chains. Specifically, the project is aimed at (i) building critical skills for productivity through TVET institutions in the agricultural sector, (ii) support work integrated learning (WIL) through internships and job placements and (iii) link on-farm production and private off takers for the youth and women around the targeted TVET institutions. This will be achieved by: (i) strengthening the capacity of Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) training systems though curricula review to align with the demands of the private sector. (ii) training and/or reskilling male and female youth in entrepreneurship and climate smart agribusiness, horticulture, aquaculture and livestock skills; and (iii) work-based learning involving onsite internships, apprenticeships and other forms of dual learning.

planEntities.name: Strengthening Protection, Safety and Wellbeing of Unaccompanied Minors and Separated Children in Zimbabwe
planEntities.parentName: Output 1.2: People, especially the vulnerable, marginalized, women,  adolescents and youth are more knowledgeable and empowered to utilize quality basic social and protection services, having strengthened engagement and participation in and skills for their own development.
planEntities.description:
The primary overall of the JP is to strengthen the protection, safety and wellbeing of unaccompanied minors and separated children in Zimbabwe. The project will focus on CoM at the Beitbridge, Plumtree and Chirundu reception and support centres. These are the border posts that account for the vast majority movement of these vulnerable groups. The JP seeks to employ a “Prevention, Protection and Empowerment” framework using a three-pronged approach based on four interrelated outcomes to strengthen unaccompanied minors and separated children and reintegration support and promote social well-being. The following deliverables will be achieved: 
Output 1.1 CoM accessed dignified and humane protection services at the Reception and Support Centres in Zimbabwe (IOM-UNICEF)
Output 1.2 Migration Reception Support Centers are refurbished to meet the basic minimum international standards. (IOM)
Output 2.1 Escorts, Reception Centre Staff, and frontline officials are capacitated on the National Referral Mechanism, child protection and cross border case management for Vulnerable Unaccompanied Minors and Separated Children, Migration Policy, GBV risk mitigation and Protection from Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA). (UNICEF-IOM)
Output 2.2 Cross Border Traders and Transporters (taxi drivers, truck, and bus drivers) are sensitized Child Safe Migration. (IOM-UNICEF)
Output 2.3 Sub-national child protection structures have strengthened capacity to protect children in communities adversely impacted by migration (UNICEF-IOM)
Output 3.1 Strengthened and promoted household livelihoods and resilience to address some of the drivers of migration and mitigate the risk of engaging in secondary irregular migration (IOM-UNICEF)
Output 3.2 Parents/caregivers and children supported to acquire civil registration documents including birth certificates. (IOM, UNICEF)
Output 4.1 Data collection, analysis and reporting on Unaccompanied minors and Separated children in Zimbabwe is strengthened. (IOM-UNICEF)
Output 4.2. Strengthen the technical working group on Mixed and Irregular migration. (IOM-UNICEF)
Output 4.4. Expand and strengthen the bilateral Cross Border Coordination mechanism and foster an enabling regional legal and policy framework that promotes protection and child friendly migration. (IOM-UNICEF)

planEntities.name: Harare Urban Economic Resilience Builiding
planEntities.parentName: Output 1.1. Government and non-government institutions and systems are strengthened at national and sub national levels to effectively manage and deliver sustainable and inclusive quality social and protection service
planEntities.description: The world is facing a series of interconnected crises, including the COVID-19 pandemic, climate change, natural disasters, and conflicts. These crises have severe socio-economic impacts on cities, particularly vulnerable communities, and hinder progress towards the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Local governments are facing fiscal constraints, making it challenging to build urban resilience and access funds for response and recovery plans. The project aims to address these challenges by strengthening the capacity of selected cities to design and implement inclusive and resilient economic and financial responses to crises. In Harare, the project will enhance the cities' capacity to engage with donors and international financial institutions, resulting in concrete projects and programs supporting urban resilience. By the project's end, the target cities are expected to have the capacity to prepare project pipelines and engage directly with financial institutions. Activities will include capacity-building, identification of financing sources for the cities’ projects and support with those projects' development. It also emphasizes continued support and knowledge exchange among the pilot cities globally.

planEntities.name: HIV prevention for AGYW supported by CIDCA
planEntities.parentName: Output 1.2: People, especially the vulnerable, marginalized, women,  adolescents and youth are more knowledgeable and empowered to utilize quality basic social and protection services, having strengthened engagement and participation in and skills for their own development.
planEntities.description:
The project, “Addressing High HIV Prevalence among Adolescent Girls and Young Women (AGYW) in Key Provinces in Zimbabwe,” aims to reduce new HIV infections among AGYW by 10% in four high HIV-burden provinces—Matabeleland South, Matabeleland North, Midlands, and Mashonaland Central—over a 24-month implementation period (2026–2028). The project will address key drivers of HIV infection, including limited access to HIV and sexual and reproductive health (SRH) services, adolescent pregnancies, early and forced marriages, school dropout, and sexual and gender-based violence (SGBV). Major interventions include HIV self-testing and linkage to care, demand creation for HIV and SRH services, provision of sanitary packs, peer-led awareness campaigns, community mobilization, male engagement as agents of change, strengthening community-led responses, and advocacy with traditional, religious, and political leaders to address harmful social norms. 
The project will utilize the Sister-to-Sister (Sista2Sista) model to empower AGYW through peer mentorship, link them to integrated HIV, SRH, and GBV services, and support informed reproductive health decision-making. It will also apply the SASA! (Start, Awareness, Support and Action) model to mobilize communities and address the root causes of gender-based violence through social norm change and engagement across all levels of society. The primary target population comprises adolescent girls and young women aged 10–24 years, including in-school girls, out-of-school girls, young single women, and married young women. The project is expected to reach 863,250 direct beneficiaries, primarily women and adolescent girls, while an additional 863,256 people will benefit indirectly, bringing the total beneficiary population to 1,726,506 people

The project aims to support Zimbabwe to turn its Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) pledges into action towards net-zero, climate resilient and sustainable development pathways. Building on the
results, experience and momentum of the first phase, the initiative aims to scale-up support to deliver and track ambitious climate action across sectors and thematic areas to achieve the bold targets set
forth in revised and enhanced NDCs. Climate Promise supports countries to mobilize both public and private investments to realize NDC targets while also simultaneously achieving the UN Sustainable
Development Goals. A key lesson from Climate Promise 1 was that more include NDCs tend to be more ambitious. Inclusive stakeholder engagement and strong partnerships will help deliver on NDCs while supporting all actors to be agents of change and continuing to advocate for ambition. The project will also empower marginalized groups, such as women and youth, to bring their unique voices, leadership, and skills to NDC implementation.

planEntities.name: Zimbabwe Resilience Building Fund 2 - UNDP
planEntities.parentName: Output 2.2: People especially the vulnerable and marginalized including women, girls, adolescents and youth are empowered to cope with climate change and build resilience for household food, and nutrition and water security demonstrating optimal attitudes, knowledge and attitudes.
planEntities.description: The overall objective of the programme is to build resilience capacities of vulnerable rural communities, by ensuring sustainable natural resources management for climate action, improving food and nutrition security, and lower the impact of natural disasters in at-risk communities in Zimbabwe. This will be achieved through layering, sequencing and integration of 1: Evidence generation and capacity built for key institutions, systems, and communities for policy and programming that promote community stewardship on sustainable natural resources management and livelihood options. 2: Improved natural resources management, utilization, and environmental protection to promote sustainable food systems within functioning ecosystems for sustainable resilience to multiple shocks. 3: Enhanced sustainable, diversified livelihoods options for rural inclusive economic growth for at-risk communities. 4: Strengthened climate and disaster risk governance for resilience (early warning, and early action -Crisis Modifier) to cushion and protect developmental gains for at-risk communities. The implementation methodology of ZRBF Phase 2 will be anchored on two main approaches the landscape approach and programmatic approach. The Landscape Approach, a holistic and integrated method for land, resource, and ecosystem management. This approach is particularly suited to the diverse ecological, social, and economic contexts of the two targeted landscapes. In addition to the landscape approach, the programme will adopt a Programmatic Approach to ensure that activities are layered, sequenced, and integrated with other resilience-building efforts in the landscapes and beyond. The programmatic approach will allow for the coordination of ZRBF Phase 2 activities with ongoing government programmes, other donors and ongoing initiatives in the geographical areas.  The above four components are interconnected and are going to be implemented in an integrated and complimentary manner using a multilayered and multisectoral approach that address context specific development challenges. Given that resilience is dynamic and context specific interventions will be risk informed and embed DRM as the foundation for building resilience. The implementation approach ensures transformative change, sustainability and greater impact.

planEntities.name: Eighth Operational Phase of the GEF Small Grants Programme (Part 1) – SGP OP8-Part 1
planEntities.parentName: Output 2.1: Strengthened capacity of government and non-government institutions at national and subnational levels to sustainably manage and protect natural resources, the environment and promote climate change resilience
planEntities.description:
SGP-OP8 builds on 30 years of successful experience in empowering local CSOs and CBOs in community driven initiatives that have enhanced wellbeing, increased awareness and resilience, and generated global environmental benefits. With economic development pressures intensifying in the developing world and the associated rising inequalities, local communities, particularly vulnerable and disadvantaged groups are becoming increasingly marginalized. The objective of Part 1 of SGP OP8 is to engage local CSOs/CBOs in landscape-seascape approaches across the 99 participating countries, providing them access to knowledge and information, capacitating them through learning-by-doing, skills development, and delivering technical and grant assistance for interventions that enhance socioeconomic conditions and generate global environmental benefits. In line with the GEF-8 SGP Implementation Arrangements Paper, core SGP resources are to be allocated equally among all eligible countries.
The proposed strategy, elaborated through four complementary outcomes, reflects the key features of GEF Small Grants Programme 2.0, including new approaches to support youth, women and Indigenous Peoples, linking up with complementary partnerships, cooperating with the two additional GEF agencies, and leveraging opportunities with other GEF programs. SGP-OP8 will facilitate opportunities for innovation and scaling up, catalyze multi-stakeholder alliances, and leverage dialogue platforms for greater impact.
An important comparative advantage of SGP is the focus on social inclusion and vulnerable groups, including women, Indigenous Peoples, persons with disabilities, the elderly and youth. Expected results under OP8-Part 1 include 225,000 ha of land and ecosystems under restoration, 3,800,000 ha of landscapes under improved practices, 90,000 ha of marine protected areas under improved management, 270,000 ha of marine habitat under improved practices, and 500,000 direct beneficiaries, of whom 250,000 are women.

planEntities.description:
Zimbabwe has made commendable progress in its climate action journey, including the submission of its updated NDC and LT-LEDS. However, several systemic challenges persist in fu lly operationalizing these commitments. These include limited institutional coordination mechanisms, insufficient capacity for climate technology assessment and tracking, and underdeveloped private sector engagement models.
This Readiness project will strengthen national systems for transparency and coordination, conduct a comprehensive Climate Technology Needs Assessment (TNA), and develop a private sector engagement strategy to unlock investment aligned with Zimbabwe's NOC and climate-resilient development priorities. The project aligns with GCF Readiness outcomes under Result Areas 1.1, 1.3, 2.1, and 2.2.

Zimbabwe faces fiscal constraints and high poverty rates, particularly in rural areas dependent on rain-fed agriculture. The project responds to these challenges by pro-moting low-cost and yet reliable, scalable technologies, open-source tools, and community-led solutions that are resilient to economic and environmental shocks. planEntities.name: UNESCO_Ecosystem Restoration and Community Development in Protected Areas Programme
planEntities.parentName: Output 2.1: Strengthened capacity of government and non-government institutions at national and subnational levels to sustainably manage and protect natural resources, the environment and promote climate change resilience
planEntities.description: The Ecosystem Restoration and Community Development Programme supports Zimbabwe by strengthening conservation and sustainable development in the Chimanimani Biosphere Reserve, an area of exceptional biodiversity that faces increasing pressures from climate change, floods, landslides, small-scale mining, and ecosystem degradation. These challenges threaten both ecological integrity and the livelihoods of local communities that depend on natural resources. The programme aims to restore ecosystems, improve biodiversity conservation, and enhance community resilience while promoting sustainable economic opportunities. Key activities include participatory environmental diagnostics, strengthening governance and institutional capacity of the biosphere reserve, restoring degraded ecosystems through reforestation and assisted natural regeneration, and installing monitoring systems to improve environmental management. The project will also support community cooperatives, develop local value chains, and promote indigenous knowledge and sustainable practices. Through training and capacity-building for park authorities, NGOs, women and youth, the programme will improve conservation management and community participation. Expected results include improved ecosystem health, strengthened biosphere reserve governance, increased income-generating opportunities for local communities, and enhanced long-term sustainability of the Chimanimani Biosphere Reserve as a model site for integrated conservation and development.

planEntities.description: The output is under the Joint Program on Gender Equality, Women’s Rights and the Empowerment of Women, Young Women and Adolescent Girls which seeks to ensure that women and girls realize their full potential in a gender-just society free from all forms of violence and where women and girls fully contribute towards the attainment of an upper middle-income society by 2023. It is aligned to the vision of the High-Level Political Compact on Ending Gender-Based Violence & Harmful Practices (2021-2030), which is a significant achievement of the Zimbabwe Spotlight Initiative Country Program, and which provides the fundamentals of this joint proposal to sustain the gains of the Zimbabwe Spotlight Initiative (2019-2023). UNFPA's key contribution to the output is to strengthen Gender equality and GBV coordination at national, provincial and district level.

planEntities.name: UNHCR- OA 11 Education - Supporting access to primary, secondary and tertiary education for refugees and asylum seeker children in Zimbabwe.
planEntities.parentName: Output 1.1. Government and non-government institutions and systems are strengthened at national and sub national levels to effectively manage and deliver sustainable and inclusive quality social and protection service
planEntities.description: UNHCR contributes to the fulfilment of the fundamental right to education for refugee and asylum seeker children at Tongogara refugee camp in Zimbabwe. This is done through payment of school fees, incentives to staff, funding infrastructural development, promotion of digital learning and procurement of stationery for children enrolled at both the primary school and its early childhood development centre as well as the secondary school at the camp. Support is also provided towards tertiary education.

planEntities.name: UNHCR- OA 1 Access/ Doc -Supporting access to status determination and civil registration documentation for refugees and asylum seekers in Zimbabwe.
planEntities.parentName: Output 1.3: A strengthened gender responsive policy, regulatory and budgeting environment is in place to promote equitable utilization of social and protection services
planEntities.description: UNHCR supports access to documentation for refugees and asylum seekers by funding mobile registration clinics for provision of birth certificates, marriage certificates and identity documents as well as United Nations Convention travel documents for refugees that may require to travel abroad.

planEntities.name: UNHCR- OA6 Justice - Social inclusion of vulnerable refugees and asylum seekers through promoting child protection, youth empowerment and social justice.
planEntities.parentName: Output 4.2: People especially the vulnerable and marginalized  including women, girls, adolescents and youth are empowered to effectively participate, claim their rights  and benefit from service delivery by institutions at national and sub national levels (Executive, legislative and judiciary)
planEntities.description: UNHCR's protection work targets vulnerable groups among refugees and asylum seekers and has specific programmes for such groups as single women, girls, youths, persons with disability and the elderly. Interventions are done through implementing partners that work on specific solutions that meet the different needs to ensure refugees enjoy their rights and protection during their stay in Zimbabwe as the host country. UNHCR advocates for the inclusion of refugees and asylum seekers in national programmes to encourage their inclusion in the national system, foster integration and enhance livelihood activities. Advocacy targets legislative reforms of the refugee laws and policies in Zimbabwe.

Output 2.1.1: Increased capacity of emergency preparedness and response mechanisms at all levels
Output 2.1.2: Increased capacity of coordination and surveillance capacity at national, subnational and community levels
2.2 Increased risk perception and adoption of protective practices among communities at risk
Output 2.2.1: Increased system capacity to disseminate culturally appropriate, gender- and age-sensitive multi-hazard risk information and promote protective practices at all levels
Output 2.2.2: Enhanced enabling environment for most at risk children, adolescents, women to adopt protective practices at all levels

UNICEF specific interventions 
"Key Intervention 1.2.1 Strengthen the use of the Expanded Programme on Immunization as preparedness tool to public health emergencies                                                                         
Key Intervention 1.2.2 Emergency preparedness and response is enhanced through procurement and supply chain management                                                                                     
Key Intervention 1.2.3 Emergency Preparedness, Response and Mitigation Capacity Building are strengthened through improved Surveillance, Case Management and IPC measures                                                                                        
Key Intervention 1.2.4 System to ensure immunization data is fully analyzed to support detection of PHE, especially at the primary health care level is developed"



2.3 Sustained performance of essential service delivery in all emergencies
Output 2.3.1: Strengthened climate change -informed programming at decentralized (PHC-level)
Output 2.3.2: Increased institutional capacity and management capacity on business continuity planning and emergency response service delivery
Output 2.3.3: Scaled-up micro-nutrient supplementation and essential medicines services for children, adolescents, and women through multiple platforms during emergency situations
